Route review: blocks batch only when their spans nest, and window blocks do not

22 September 2026 · Route review of odd-prime-clause-transfer · The recorded batch theorems need spans nested modulo annihilators; window blocks are not; next: test a reuse-free gluing. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

The line's general claim. After the common weight, the window blocks can be removed together, at a cost that grows more slowly than their number. What the goal needs is that polynomially many window blocks cost \(o(n)\) degrees in the final replay. Theorem NDX′ reaches the linear ceiling of one-at-a-time removal. The last review asked whether two blocks can ever cost less than the sum, and whether derivation order breaks the circular dependency between their first stages. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer.

Falsification attempt: does the record contain a batched mechanism?

Yes, and it answers the two-block question. The historical nested-span theorem removes a chain of blocks with input spans \(V_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq V_s\) for one charge \((p-1)\delta\), whatever its length. Its target form, the batch modulo target annihilators (TAB), needs nesting only modulo a space \(H\) with \(tH\) cheaply derivable. The historical core–residual theorem relaxes nesting to nested cores, at a multiplier that grows with the residual rank. These theorems break the circular dependency by nesting. When the current input \(f\) lies in every later block's span, every later block can be specialized to the product \(1-\alpha^{-1}f\) at once. Its companions then become field consequences, not axioms that still need removing. So two blocks cost one charge when their spans nest modulo \(H\), and every recorded argument charges the sum otherwise.

Window blocks do not nest, for two reasons.

  • What an annihilator space can absorb. After the map, \(H\) must satisfy \(fH\subseteq\mathcal C_c(\Gamma_H)\) for the weight \(f\). It contains the PHP consequences of low degree, which the quotient rank already factors out. For one matching monomial, the affine annihilators are exactly the recorded space \(H_M\), by the rigidity theorem (MAR) of the TAB entry. If \(H\) lies in the PHP consequences plus affine forms, then \(V_a\subseteq V_b+H\) forces the nonlinear quotients to nest. For a window block these have rank up to about \(r^2/2\) at nonlocal dimension \(r\). The record does not characterize nonlinear annihilators of the weight, but nothing in it makes the nonlinear parts of two random dense lines nested modulo annihilators.
  • Derivation order does not create nesting. Over \(\mathbb F_3\), resolving on equations \(L_A=0\) and \(L_B=0\), with \(L_A,L_B\) affine, produces \(\alpha L_A+\beta L_B=0\) with \(\alpha,\beta\ne0\). Since \(\alpha^2=\beta^2=1\), its selector is \(1-(\alpha L_A+\beta L_B)^2=(1-L_A^2)+(1-L_B^2)-1-2\alpha\beta L_AL_B\). The product \(L_AL_B\) is not in general in the span of the premises' selectors. So a resolvent's span lies in the sum of its premises' spans, the constants and the one product \(L_AL_B\). It drops the resolved selectors, so in general it neither contains nor is contained in a premise's span. Only weakening steps, which add equations, give nested spans.

So the record's batched mechanisms apply exactly to nested or low-residual families, and dense window lines are neither.

What completeness leaves open

Observation CR refutes every block-count-independent PC lag over PHP, because the compiled refutation reuses lines. It does not refute a reuse-free statement. The NS test found that fresh blocks add nothing at the Nullstellensatz level in all 53 small cases, where PC gains. The binary form of that statement is the open level-one conjecture. CR's argument does not apply to an NS form as it stands: it uses the PC compilation, whose degree bound relies on reuse. Whether completeness refutes an NS form independent of the block count depends on the NS degree of compiled refutations, which grows with how deeply lines are reused. Nothing recorded bounds it. If such a statement held, it would batch window blocks for free, but only where they are used without PC reuse. Its possible use is therefore an endpoint in which the cost depends on how deeply window lines are reused, not on how many there are. That use is not formulated yet, and the conjecture is unproved even for one binary block.

Assessment of this line

Weak. Per-block removal is at its ceiling (Theorem NDX′). The recorded batch theorems need nesting, which window blocks lack, and derivation order does not supply it. Max-type weights and restrictions fail on window blocks (last review, F3). The one statement these arguments do not reach is reuse-free gluing. It is a conjecture with small-case support, and it would reach only window lines that are not reused deeply. The user overrode the earlier pause, so window work continues. This review recommends that the next window cycle test that one open possibility, and that the scope-and-review write-up of the partial endpoints (Corollaries ND and NDp, Propositions MX″ and MXp, Theorems Y and NDX′, Lemma WE) be scheduled as the thread's productive alternative.

Next step on the highest-risk item

Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. Formulate the reuse-free gluing precisely and test it before any use. The statement is a mixed one: a PC-closed old base, with window blocks used in NS form. The cost to count is the unfolding of window-dependent reuse in the compiled refutation. First check it against completeness: some compiled refutation must lie outside its reach at every size. Then test it at the smallest nonvacuous size against the NS test's bases, stating the count first. If it fails, or its unfolding cost is linear in the number of window lines anyway, recommend the write-up.

Sheaf check

Nested spans are exactly a sheaf condition that glues for free: along a chain, each section restricts to the next, and one global charge covers the chain. Window blocks form an antichain, so there is nothing to glue along. The reuse-free statement is the only remaining gluing that the completeness argument does not reach. At the NS level, sections over different blocks do not interact through reuse.

Verification gate. No result is claimed. Re-read the nested-span and core–residual theorems, the target-annihilator batch theorem with its annihilator rigidity, Observation CR, the NS test and the level-one conjecture's registry record. The two remarks are elementary: the first is linear algebra, and the second expands a square. Searched the record for nested-span, core and target batching, and for antichains and chain covers of blocks; nothing states a batched mechanism for non-nested dense blocks. No computation was run.

Reuse-free gluing would reach only window lines near the conclusion, and it implies a linear depth bound

22 September 2026 · Negative analysis · Unfolding reuse costs about \(2p\) degrees per inference below a window line; the window line's last open possibility gives no size bound. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The batching review left one gluing statement that the completeness argument does not reach: fresh blocks used without PC reuse add nothing, independently of their number. It asked to formulate that statement, check it against completeness, and find what it costs to use. The stated rule was to recommend the write-up if the cost of use turned out to be linear.

Formulation

Let \(\mathcal G\) be an old base and \(\mathcal W\) the axioms of fresh one-level blocks. Write \(\mathrm{NS}_d(\mathcal W)\) for combinations \(\sum_Ag_AA\) with \(A\in\mathcal W\) and \(\deg(g_AA)\le d\). The mixed statement (MNS) is: for every old \(t\), if \(t\in\mathcal C_d(\mathcal G)+\mathrm{NS}_d(\mathcal W)\), then \(t\in\mathcal C_{d+c}(\mathcal G)\), with \(c\) independent of the number of blocks. The base may be used with PC reuse; the blocks may not. The NS test supports its pure-NS case at small sizes. The open binary level-one conjecture is a PC statement for one fresh block over level-one bases. The batching review called it the binary form of this statement; more precisely, MNS asks less of each block, which may not be reused, but asks it for any number of blocks. The ternary PC form, Conjecture C3, is refuted.

How a compiled refutation unfolds

The selector compiler works inference by inference. For a resolution step with premises \(A\), \(B\) and conclusion \(T\), it derives \(P_T\) from the completed premise lines through \[ P_T=R_A+r_ft_fR_B+r_fr_gQ,\qquad R_A=P_AP_T+\sum_jr_{A,j}t_jP_T, \] and similarly for \(R_B\). So \(P_A\) enters multiplied by \(P_T\), of degree at most \(p\), and \(P_B\) multiplied by \(r_ft_fP_T\), of degree at most \(2p\). Weakening multiplies the premise by \(P_T\) in the same way. The PC refutation avoids accumulation because it multiplies the completed premise lines, not their derivations. Rewriting it with no reuse of block-dependent lines substitutes each premise's expression into its uses. Along a path of \(\ell\) inferences the multipliers then multiply, so the resulting degree is at most about \(2p\ell\) plus the compiler's ceiling \(4p-1\). This is the standard PC-to-NS conversion, which costs degree times depth; nothing better is recorded.

Check against completeness

Apply MNS with \(\mathcal G=F_N\) and all blocks of a compiled refutation of depth \(h\). The unfolded refutation puts \(1\) in \(\mathcal C_{4p-1}(F_N)+\mathrm{NS}_{O(ph)}(\mathcal W)\). MNS would give \(1\in\mathcal C_{O(ph)+c}(F_N)\). The matching barrier puts \(d_N\) above \((N+1)/2\). So MNS implies that every \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\) refutation of PHP, of any size, has depth \(\Omega(N/p)\). Completeness refutes MNS if some refutation is shallower than that; otherwise this argument does not decide it. A linear depth bound is plausible. Closure arguments, recorded for linear systems over \(\mathbb F_2\) on the bit encoding, keep systems of rank below \(cN\) consistent with a partial matching. A form over \(\mathbb F_p\) for unary PHP is not recorded. So MNS is at least as strong as an unrecorded depth lower bound, and its consistency with completeness is open, not settled.

What it would give

Suppose MNS held. After the common weight, the narrow blocks are mapped and may be reused. Every line that depends on a window block has to be unfolded, and each inference between a window line and the empty clause adds about \(2p\) degrees. After the map these degrees are multiplied by \(T_n\approx\sqrt n\) against a budget of about \(\lambda n\). So MNS would batch only window lines within about \(\lambda n/(2pT_n)=\sqrt n/\operatorname{polylog}n\) inferences of the conclusion, together with the \(Cn\) lines of Theorem NDX′ anywhere. A polynomial-size refutation can place its window lines deep in the derivation, and then the unfolding cost is linear in its depth. So the endpoint would be a new special class, of shallow window lines, and not the unrestricted statement. A small computation cannot change this, because the limit is in the unfolding, not in MNS. No computation was run.

Assessment

The last open possibility on the window line does not lead to the goal. It is a conjecture at least as strong as an unrecorded depth lower bound, and even if proved it would reach only window lines near the conclusion. By the rule the review set, the unfolding cost is linear, so this entry recommends the scope-and-review write-up. The window line's prospects remain weak. Every recorded route to it is now closed or conditional:

  • weights and restrictions, heuristically;
  • per-block removal, at its linear ceiling;
  • nesting-based batching, which window blocks lack;
  • reuse-free gluing, which is limited by depth.

Sheaf check

At the Nullstellensatz level, sections over different blocks do not interact, which is why the test found no loss. The sections still have to be glued along the derivation. Each inference contributes a multiplier, and the gluing cost is the length of the path, not the number of pieces. The window problem needs gluing along arbitrary DAGs at a cost independent of their depth, and no recorded object does that.

Next step

Next step (scope-and-review): write up the partial endpoints as one statement set:

  • Corollaries ND and NDp;
  • Propositions MX″ and MXp;
  • Theorems Y and NDX′, with Lemma WE;
  • the linear ceiling of per-block removal.

Check each against the ordering and mixed-interface controls, as the route item requires, and list exactly what remains open: refutations with superlinearly many lines of nonlocal dimension above \(n^{1/(p-1)-\varepsilon}\). Restart the window line on any of three events:

  • a batched mechanism for non-nested dense blocks;
  • a proof of the level-one conjecture together with a depth-independent way to use it;
  • outside work on DAG-like proofs with dense linear lines.

Verification gate. No result is claimed. Re-read the selector compiler's resolution and weakening steps, the batching review, the NS test, the level-one conjecture's record, the matching barrier and Theorem NDX′. The implication from MNS to a depth bound uses only the compiler's local form and the barrier. The unfolding bound is the standard conversion and is stated as an upper bound for this compiler, not as a lower bound for every conversion. Statement set: what is proved about \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\) refutations of unary PHP, checked against the controls

22 September 2026 · Consolidation · Every recorded endpoint in one list, checked against the ordering and mixed-interface controls, with the exact open case. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. Route item: scope-and-review. The reuse-free gluing analysis closed or made conditional the last recorded route to the window and recommended a write-up of the partial endpoints. The consolidation of the same day predates the mixed endpoints, the all-prime extensions and the exceptional-line theorems. This entry replaces its list. It states each endpoint once with its hypotheses, checks each against the two controls the route item names, and states exactly what remains open. No new result is claimed.

Conventions

The object is ordinary unary \(\mathrm{PHP}^{n+1}_n\) and, where stated, its functional variant. Refutations are standard syntactic \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\) refutations, with size measured in lines, and with no restriction on width, depth or sharing unless stated. "Excluded" means that for every fixed \(c\), refutations with at most \(n^c\) lines do not exist for large \(n\). Forms are taken modulo the linear row equations. A form is local if it is supported in one row or one column. A line's nonlocal dimension is the dimension of the span of the linear parts of its nonlocal equations. Its cell support is the union of the supports of its forms. Every endpoint compiles the refutation by the complete-board transfer or its weak-base form, one block per line, and ends at a PHP-specific barrier, such as the matching filtration or the separation of a fixed robust graph.

Endpoints in which every line lies in one class

  • Local lines, \(p=3\): every form row- or column-local (local corollary). It is the case of nonlocal dimension zero of the next item, which holds for every odd \(p\).
  • Low nonlocal dimension, every odd \(p\): nonlocal dimension at most \(n^{1/(p-1)-\varepsilon}\) (Corollary NDp).
  • Probes plus row remainders, every fixed \(p\): each line has \(O(\log n)\) affine probes, and each form is a probe combination plus a remainder on \(n^\alpha\operatorname{polylog}n\) rows, \(\alpha<1\) (remainder exclusion). It contains the row-support class.
  • Column occupancy, every fixed \(p\), weak base: each form is a global affine column-occupancy statistic plus a perturbation inside one column (occupancy exclusion).
  • Subquadratic cell support, every fixed \(p\): cell support at most \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\operatorname{polylog}n\) (cell-support exclusion).

Endpoints that mix classes

  • Across lines, \(p=3\): each line lies in the row-support class with \(\alpha<1/5\), or has nonlocal dimension at most \(n^\eta\) with \(\eta<(1-\alpha)/8\) (Proposition MX). With probes and \(\alpha<1\), this is Proposition MX′.
  • Within lines: each line splits into a part with shared probes and row remainders and a part of nonlocal dimension at most \(n^\eta\). This is Proposition MX″ at \(p=3\), and Proposition MXp at every odd \(p\), with \(\eta<(1-\alpha)/(4(p-1))\).
  • The occupancy class does not join these mixtures by composition.

Endpoints that allow arbitrary lines

  • Theorem Y, every fixed \(p\): a polynomial-size refutation has more than \(\Theta(n^\beta)\) lines of cell support above \(n^{2-\varepsilon}(\log n)^A\), for \(\beta<\varepsilon/2\).
  • Theorem NDX′, every odd \(p\): a polynomial-size refutation has more than \(Cn\) lines of nonlocal dimension above \(n^{1/(p-1)-\varepsilon}\), with \(C\) depending only on \(p\). It supersedes Theorem NDX.
  • Both rest on removing blocks one at a time: the old-consequence transfer for Theorem Y, and Lemma WE for NDX′.

Limits of the methods

  • Observation CR: completeness of resolution refutes every bound on what compiled blocks add over PHP that does not depend on their number.
  • Per-block removal cannot pass a linear number of window lines (ceiling review); Theorem NDX′ reaches this ceiling up to constants.
  • The recorded batch theorems need spans nested modulo annihilators, which window blocks lack (batching review).
  • Reuse-free gluing would reach only window lines near the conclusion (analysis).
  • Common weights and restrictions are expected to fail on window blocks, heuristically (window review).

Check against the two controls

Ordering control. The balanced minimum source on the graph-ordering principle has one complete block for every node \(S\) of a balanced partition tree and every \(i\in S\): about \(n\log_2n\) blocks with affine inputs. Its source degree is \(O(h\log n)\), while the old PC degree of the expander ordering family is \(\Omega(n)\). So over a general base no elimination can be charged independently of the number of blocks. Every endpoint above ends at a PHP-specific barrier, not at a generic transfer, so the control does not apply to them. The two generic statements are consistent with it. Lemma WE with target one charges \((p-1)\sum_b\delta_b\), about \((p-1)n\log_2n\) on this source. So it bounds the old degree by the source degree plus that charge, which is above the \(\Omega(n)\) lower bound. Observation CR concerns PHP only. The control does add one fact to the limits above. A batched mechanism for window blocks cannot be generic: it must use PHP structure.

Mixed-interface control. The canonical-OR certificates give a binary helper block that gains one degree over a retained second-level base. That is within the per-block charge \((p-1)\delta=1\) of BC and Lemma WE at \(p=2\). The endpoints above remove only one-level compiled blocks, whose inputs are old, so the second-level base of the control does not arise in them. None of the listed statements asserts conservativity, so none is contradicted.

Relations

The line classes are pairwise incomparable, by the separating examples of the consolidation. Theorems Y and NDX′ are incomparable too. The forms \(x_{1,j}+x_{2,j+1}\), \(j<n\), have cell support \(2n-2\) and nonlocal dimension \(n-1\). Row-local forms \(\sum_ja_{i,j}x_{i,j}\) with all \(a_{i,j}\ne0\), one for each row \(i\), have nonlocal dimension zero and cell support \(n(n+1)\).

What remains open

  • The window. To escape every endpoint above, a polynomial-size refutation must have more than \(Cn\) lines of nonlocal dimension above \(n^{1/(p-1)-\varepsilon}\) (Theorem NDX′) and more than \(\Theta(n^\beta)\) lines of cell support above \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\operatorname{polylog}n\) (Theorem Y). It must also have lines outside the mixed and occupancy classes. No statement excludes such refutations. At \(p=3\) their typical dense lines have projected rank of order \(n\) spread over many rows. Nested chains and shallow placement of these lines would help only through arguments that are not proved (batching review, reuse-free analysis).
  • The occupancy class in mixtures.
  • Dense-rank criteria for \(p\ge5\). The graph-level dense side exists only at \(p=3\), and it has no proof-system form at any prime.
  • Verification. No endpoint is Lean-verified or independently checked for novelty. The endpoints depend on the working complete-board transfer and on the fixed-graph and quotient-rank chain, which have fresh-context reviews only.

Assessment

The thread has a coherent set of partial results. They exclude short refutations whose dense lines are few, local, low-dimensional, sparsely supported, probe-structured or mixtures of these. Up to constants they also give the exact number of dense lines that per-block methods tolerate. They do not give the goal, and every recorded route to the rest is closed or conditional. As a statement set it is ready for review. A publication would need an independent check of the complete-board transfer and the fixed-graph chain first.

Sheaf check

The statement set is the list of local sections the thread has: each endpoint is an exclusion on one class of lines, and the mixed propositions are the gluings that worked. The window is the region no local section covers. It is also where the recorded gluings fail: per piece at linear cost, by nesting, or by reuse-free assembly.

Next step

Next step (odd-prime-clause-transfer, thread level): a thread route review. It should ask whether any route item remains live. The window's routes are closed or conditional; same-graph composition is a bookkeeping item; this entry completes the scope-and-review write-up. If no item is live, the thread should wait for a user decision rather than produce further special cases. The options are an independent check of the complete-board transfer with the fixed-graph chain, toward publication; a Lean assignment; or a new window idea from outside the recorded mechanisms.

Verification gate. No result is claimed. Every endpoint was restated from its registered summary and anchor, with its prime range and parameters, and every anchor was checked to exist. The two controls were re-read in full, and the ordering source's block count, about \(n\log_2n\), was computed from its construction. The two incomparability examples for Theorems Y and NDX′ were checked against the definitions: support and nonlocal dimension. No computation or reviewer was needed.

What the goal needs is the case the statement set leaves open. A polynomial-size refutation can escape every endpoint only with more than \(Cn\) lines of nonlocal dimension above \(n^{1/(p-1)-\varepsilon}\), more than \(\Theta(n^\beta)\) lines of large cell support, and lines outside the mixed and occupancy classes. Route item under review: all three, starting from odd-prime-clause-transfer.

Falsification attempt: is any mechanism class unexamined?

Within the compile-and-exclude framework, a mechanism either charges blocks by a maximum or by a sum. Max-type charges come from a common weight or a common restriction. Both are expected to fail on window blocks: the weight heuristically, through the window review and the alignment tests, and the restriction through the dyadic calibration. Sum-type charges stop at a linear number of blocks (ceiling review), which Theorem NDX′ reaches. Between the two, batching needs nested spans, which window blocks lack (batching review). By the ordering control, any batching must use PHP structure. Reuse-free gluing is conditional and limited by depth (analysis). A different compilation does not help: sign variables that make selector false sets affine are definable and add nothing (window review, F4). Outside the framework, the published methods for dense linear lines cover regular or bounded-depth proofs only (lag review). No class of mechanism remains unexamined, and none reaches the open case.

  • scope-and-review: the statement set is written. One task remains: an independent check of the foundations. Every endpoint depends on the selector compiler and the complete-board transfer. The ND family also depends on the fixed-graph theorem, the two-level map and the quotient-rank theorem. All are working proofs, several produced by another agent, and the registry records no independent audit and no Lean coverage for any of them. An error there would affect every endpoint at once. This is the highest-value task that does not need a new idea.

Ask it to check the per-inference degree ledger for resolution, weakening, simplification and contraction; the initial-clause bridge for ordinary and functional PHP; the compression to a basis subset; and the claim that one block per line suffices. Independent audit: the selector compiler and the complete-board transfer are sound, with a sharper local ledger

22 September 2026 · Audit · Sound; no mathematical gap. Local ceiling \(\max(3p,4p-3)\); four statements made explicit. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. Route item: scope-and-review. The thread review found that every endpoint of the thread rests on two working proofs with no independent audit: the selector compiler and the complete-board transfer. This entry records such an audit. A fresh-context reviewer received only the full text of the two entries and the rule convention of the equation-clause audit, and was asked to break them.

What was checked, and passed

  • Compression. An omitted selector times \(P_C\) is a constant combination of companions. The inventory bound \(\binom{v+\delta}{\delta}\) holds, the zero selector is never in a basis, and an empty basis gives \(P_C=1\).
  • Initial clauses. The telescoping identity and \(\prod_i(1-t_i)=F_A^\delta\) are exact. The degree is \(p+a\delta\), and \(3p-2\) for Boolean, hole and row-exclusion initials. For the pigeon rows of the complete-board transfer, \(t_j-X_j\) is divisible by \(X_j^2-X_j\) for odd \(p\) and is zero for \(p=2\). The pigeon bridge costs \(2p-1\) and fails without the row equation, as the entry's own control states.
  • One-premise rules. Weakening, simplification and contraction reduce to \(P_T=P_AP_T+\sum_jr_{A,j}t_jP_T\), at degree \(2p\).
  • Resolution. The identity \(t_ft_g(1-t_h)=0\) holds for every \(p\) and all \(\alpha,\beta\), on all of \(\mathbb F_p^v\): if \(f=g=0\) then \(h=0\). The line \(Q\) is derived at degree \(4p-3\), and the final identity \(P_T=R_A+r_ft_fR_B+r_fr_gQ\) checks symbolically.
  • The DAG. Each completed line \(P_C\) has degree \(p\) and is reused, so degree does not accumulate along the DAG.
  • The end. The empty clause arises by simplification with \(P_\varnothing=1\), so the final line is a PC refutation.

Clarifications recorded here

The original entries are not rewritten; these statements hold for them as written.

  1. Sharper local ledger. In the resolution step, \(Q=t_ft_gP_T\) has degree \(3p-2\), and \(r_ft_fR_B\) and \(r_fr_gQ\) both have degree \(3p\). The line \(IP_T\) has degree \(4p-3\). So the local ceiling is \(\max(3p,4p-3)\): this is \(4p-3\) for \(p\ge3\), and \(6\) for \(p=2\). The compiler's ceiling \(4p-1\) is valid but loose. The sentence about reaching \(4p-1\) "even if its derivation previously reached \(4p-3\)" mixes a line's degree with its derivation's, and the reuse argument that follows it is the correct one. Every endpoint that uses \(4p-1\) stays valid.
  2. Boolean axioms. The certificate for \(IP_T\) uses \(x_i^2-x_i\) for every variable of \(f\) and \(g\). The base must therefore contain all \(v\) Boolean equations, whether or not the source uses their Boolean initials. The complete-board transfer's base contains them.
  3. Degenerate resolvents. If \(h\) is a nonzero constant, then \(t_h=0\) and \(I=t_ft_g\), which still vanishes on the cube. If \(\alpha=\beta=0\), then \(t_h=1\) and \(P_T\) is itself a combination of companions. If \(t_f\) coincides with a context selector, fix the designation once per inference. Either choice works: as context it gives \(r_f=0\) and \(R_A=P_T\); as pivot it gives the stated \(R_A\). If \(t_f\) is not in the chosen basis, then \(R_A=P_T\).
  4. Binary remark. The complete-board entry's binary sanity paragraph cites a local ceiling of five and a separate affine-DAG controller. That paragraph depends on the controller, and it is not checked here. The compiler's own \(p=2\) ledger is six. No odd-prime endpoint uses the paragraph.

The auditor also noted that for ordinary PHP the replay never uses row exclusions, so it lands in the weak linear-row base. The registry already records this.

Consequence

Every endpoint in the statement set starts from these two proofs, and they now have an independent audit. The sharper ledger \(4p-3\) would lower every "\(4p-1\)" in the endpoints by two degrees. No asymptotic statement changes, so the endpoints are not restated.

Next step

Next step (scope-and-review): audit the chain behind Corollary NDp and Theorem NDX′ in the same way:

  • the fixed-graph pair-counting lemma and theorem, with the graph class;
  • the two-level semantic map with its step 4;
  • the quotient-rank theorem with its basis conversion and rank-one step.

These are larger. Split the audit into the graph part and the map part, with one fresh reviewer each and excerpts in a scratch file.

Sheaf check

No gluing is involved; this audit checks the covering on which the thread's local sections are built.

Verification gate. The audit was run by a fresh-context reviewer given only the two entries and the rule convention, with six targeted checks. Its verdict: sound with fixes, and every fix presentational or a statement of scope. The degree ledger was recomputed independently: \(\deg Q=2(p-1)+p=3p-2\), \(\deg(IP_T)=3(p-1)+p=4p-3\), and the two terms of the final identity have degree \(3p\). No computation was run.

Independent audit: the fixed-graph chain and the two-level and quotient-rank maps are sound

22 September 2026 · Audit · Sound; no mathematical gap. Seven statements made explicit; one displayed formula does not render. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. Route item: scope-and-review. After the compiler audit, the rest of the chain behind Corollary NDp and Theorem NDX′ had fresh-context reviews only. This entry records an independent audit in two parts, each by one fresh-context auditor that read only a scratch file of excerpts and was asked to break the argument.

  • Graph part. The pair-counting and separation lemma, the fixed-graph theorem with its uniform range and graph class, and the maps it takes from the all-prime source exclusion. The imported Mikša–Nordström degree bound was taken as given, and its hypotheses were checked where it is applied.
  • Map part. The two-level semantic map with its step 4 and power-range corollary, the projection lemma, Theorem QRp with its basis conversion, the rank-one bridge, and the rank count of Corollary NDp.

What was checked, and passed

  • Pair counting. The conflict degree is at most \(2d\Delta-2<A_0\). Each step of the recurrence has \(x=A_0j/(s-j)\le1/3\), and \(\sum_{j<k}j/(s-j)\le k^2/s\), so \(i_k\ge e^{-2A_0k^2/s}\binom sk\). The containment probability is at most \((2k/s)^r\). The boundary-deletion union bound gives \(\xi/(1-\xi)\le1/3\), so at least two thirds of the independent sets are good.
  • Separation. The residual graph keeps left degree at most \(d\) and expansion \(\delta/2\), so the imported bound gives degree above \(\delta L/(4d)\), within its hypotheses. All \(2^k\) signed restrictions send the graph base to the same residual system, because the \(2k\) labels are distinct. The detector's CNF-to-linear-row transfer is valid at \(\max(B,d)\le\delta L/(4d)\), in every characteristic.
  • Fixed-graph theorem. The flat-restriction image bound \(\binom{s-r+k}k\le e^{-k(r-k)/s}\binom sk\) and \(r-k>4A_0k\) give \(e^{-4A_0k^2/s}\). The joint kernel is nonzero because \(e^{2A_0k^2/s}\ge256(M+1)^2>2M\). The maps have degree at most \(T=(p-1)R\), and the replay stays within \(TD+k\).
  • Graph class. Fewer than \(64t\) unique neighbours give a neighbourhood of at most \(96t\). The constant \(C=2e^{97}96^{32}\) is exact. The hole degrees have mean at most \(256\), with tail at most \((256e/Q)^Q\).
  • Two-level map. Used-bottom companions vanish on the whole cube, because \(\prod_{u\ne0}(1-uF)=1-F^{p-1}\) is an identity. Parent companions vanish where \(f\ne0\), because (LPF-value) is the indicator of the common zero set of the basis of \(V_a\), which equals that of the actual inputs. The coefficient fields vanish, and the Boolean division is certified through \(Te+k\) and \(pT+k\). The costs \(\delta(\ell_a-1)\) and \(T_A+1+\delta(\ell_a-1)\) match (LPF-map-cost). The power-range corollary holds with \(\rho+\sigma<1\).
  • Quotient rank. \(\varphi(P_q)=P_f+\sum_jt_jv_j\) with the error in \(I_{\delta+1}\), and the companion identity is certified through \(2\delta+1=2p-1\). The coefficient fields map correctly because \(\beta\in\mathbb F_p\). After restriction and projection, \(c_a\le r_a\).
  • Rank-one bridge. (RS-equality) and (RS-parent) are exact identities. The ceiling is \(\max(D,2p+1)\), also for mixed parents, and \(4p-1\ge2p+1\).
  • Rank count of NDp. Local selectors map to zero in \(Q_\delta/P_{\le1}\). The nonlocal ones lie in the span of monomials of degree \(2\) to \(\delta\) in a basis of \(U\), so the rank is at most \(\binom{r+\delta}\delta\le(2r)^\delta\).

Clarifications recorded here

The audited entries are not rewritten, and every statement below holds for them as written.

  1. Unused hypotheses of the pair-counting lemma. The proof never uses \(k\le m-L\), and it needs only \(\delta/2>0\), not \(\delta>1\). The first keeps at least \(L\) rows in the residual graph. Only that use could need it: if the imported expander definition presupposes that many rows. It is harmless in the asymptotic range, where \(L\le m/2\) and \(k=o(m)\).
  2. Proof degree. The fixed-graph theorem must be read without the step of the source exclusion that raises \(D\) to at least \(\max(16,p)\), because that would change \(TD+k\). A generator of original degree \(e>D\) is never used, and a used one costs at most \(Te+k\le TD+k\). So \(D<p\) needs no adjustment, and \(D\) enters only through \(TD+k\le\delta L/(4d)\).
  3. The graph-class sums. "The same geometric bounds as before" means the following. For \(t\le\sqrt N\) the terms are at most \((CN^{-15.5})^t\), with sum \(o(1)\). For \(\sqrt N<t\le\gamma N\) each term is at most \(8^{-t}\), with sum \(O(8^{-\sqrt N})\). The choice \(\gamma\le1/192\) gives \(96t\le N/2\), which the containing hole set needs.
  4. The uniform range. "\(\Delta=\operatorname{polylog}N\)" means one fixed bound for all graphs, such as \(\Delta\le\lceil(\ln N)^2\rceil\), which the graph class supplies. Uniformity over graphs needs a common bound.
  5. The row-local case of NDp. The passage from a row-local \(L\) to its representative \(L'\) on one row uses the same identity as the column case: \(L^\delta-L'^\delta=(L-L')\sum_aL^aL'^{\delta-1-a}\), where \(L-L'\) is a constant combination of row axioms, at degree \(\delta\).
  6. Order of steps in Theorem QRp. The ternary theorem states it and QRp inherits it. The basis conversion, which uses the \(I_\delta\) certificates, and the rank-one bridge are applied on the complete functional board, before restriction and projection. The restricted base is the graph base with its functional row and column exclusions, and the fixed-graph separation holds for exactly that base. The projection lemma's telescoping through degree \(2\) covers these generators, as checked for \(x_dx_e\) and \(x_d^2-x_d\).
  7. A formula that does not render. In section 3 of the two-level map, the prefix identity is written with a raw "<" before a letter. The HTML parser reads it as the start of a tag, so the displayed formula breaks. The intended identity, which the auditor checked, is \[ 1-B_{a,u}=\sum_tv_t\prod_{b<t}(1-v_bG_{j_b})\,G_{j_t}. \] A scan of the main notebook finds 30 raw "<" characters followed by a letter inside mathematics, all in older entries; the side notebooks have none. An in-place escape is a repair that the append-only check does not currently allow.

Consequence

The chain behind Corollary NDp now has independent audits from the compiler to the graph barrier. Theorem NDX′ uses the same chain together with Lemma WE. The imported Mikša–Nordström theorem remains a published dependency. The statement set's verification item is discharged for this chain. It remains open for the endpoints outside it, among them the removal mechanisms of the two arbitrary-line theorems: the old-consequence transfer behind Theorem Y, and Lemma WE with the exceptional-line assembly behind Theorem NDX′.

Next step

Next step (scope-and-review): audit the two removal mechanisms in the same way, with one fresh auditor each. The first is the old-consequence transfer with its three stages and the ledger \(\max(d+(p-1)\delta,d+k,pk)\), as Theorem Y uses it. The second is Lemma WE together with the assembly of Theorem NDX′. After that, the statement set needs a novelty check against the literature.

Sheaf check

No gluing is involved. The graph part checks the global object on which all local sections are compared: one fixed robust graph and one common weight. The map part checks the restriction maps from compiled blocks to that object.

Verification gate. The two auditors read only the excerpt files and ran no searches. Both verdicts: sound with fixes, where every fix is wording, a statement of scope or rendering. Independent audit: the removal mechanisms behind Theorems Y and NDX′ are sound

22 September 2026 · Audit · Sound; no mathematical gap. Old-consequence transfer, Theorem Y, Lemma WE and Theorems NDX and NDX′ checked; clarifications only. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. Route item: scope-and-review. The graph and map audit left unaudited the removal mechanisms of the two theorems that allow arbitrary lines. This entry records their audit, in two parts, each by one fresh-context auditor that read only a scratch file of excerpts and was asked to break the argument.

  • Theorem Y part. The old-consequence transfer (BC) with its later-dependency control, Theorem Y, the part of the cell-support exclusion that Theorem Y uses, and the statement of the matching barrier.
  • NDX′ part. BC, the degree analysis and proof of Theorem NDX, Lemma WE and Theorem NDX′. The chain audited in the two earlier audits was taken as given, and its hypotheses were checked where it is applied.

What was checked, and passed

  • BC, first stage. Setting \(r_{1,j}=\alpha^{-1}\) and every other coefficient to zero makes \(P_U=1-\alpha^{-1}f_j\) at every accuracy, and the field equations vanish. The identity \(\chi_\alpha(y)(\alpha-y)=y^p-y\) is exact, and \(\sum_{\alpha\ne0}\alpha\chi_\alpha(x)=x\) holds as polynomials, because both sides have degree at most \(p-1\) and agree on \(\mathbb F_p\). Multiplications by a coefficient variable become scalar multiples. Every weighted line stays within \(d+(p-1)\delta\), and so does the domain reduction, because a used companion forces \(d\ge\delta_i+h(\delta+1)\).
  • BC, second and third stages. The first-stage lines \(f_it\) are reused as finished lines, so the ceiling is \(\max(B_1,d+k)\). The steps \(t^2\to t^p\to t\) stay within \(pk\), and \(t=1\) gives \(d+(p-1)\delta\).
  • Theorem Y. Compiled inputs are selectors in the cell variables, so a removed block's coefficients occur neither in the base nor in any remaining block. This gives both BC's freshness and the later-dependency restriction. Each removal adds \((p-1)\delta\le(p-1)^2\), and no variable of a removed block survives. The replay of the cell-support exclusion has degree at most \(TD'\) for every \(D'\), not only polylogarithmic \(D'\). The constants of step 4 hold with \(B=\lfloor(N+1)/2\rfloor\): \(N\ge2B-1\), \(m=N+1\ge B\), \(TD'\le B\), and \(K_n=\Theta(n^\beta)\).
  • Lemma WE. Both identities of the first stage hold. The leaf is certified from the equations of \(Y\) alone, a field leaf vanishes, and a leaf of another block stays \(t\)-weighted, so the induction on the number of blocks is valid. In the second stage, the leaf \(twf_i\) comes from the first-stage line \(tf_i\) within its own degree. The charges add to \(d+(p-1)\sum_b\delta_b\), with nothing else accumulating.
  • Theorem NDX. A multiplication by a narrow coefficient in step 3 stays within \((4p-1)T_n+k_n\), and a wide axiom is fixed by \(\sigma\), so it enters only as \(fA\). The wide inputs lie in \(\mathbb F_p[Y]\) with degree at most \(\delta\), and their coefficient sets are private. BC's hypotheses hold at each removal. The rates of (FG-pairs), the bounds on \(k_n\) and \(T_A\), \(T_n=o(n)\) and \((4p-1)T_n+k_n\le B_H/2\) all check, and so does \(C=\lambda/(2\sqrt{c+2p})\).
  • Theorem NDX′. The derivation \(\pi_0\) is \(f\)-weighted with \(\mathcal G_0=\Gamma'_H\), and \(B_H<d_K\le B_H/2+K\delta^2\) gives \(K>B_H/(2\delta^2)\).

Clarifications recorded here

The audited entries are not rewritten, and every statement below holds for them as written.

  1. Where Theorem Y uses \(T\). Besides the two replay inequalities that Theorem Y names, the replay of the cell-support exclusion uses \(T\) in two more places. The multiplication step needs \(\deg\beta\le s_a\le T\), and old variables need substitution degree \(1\le T\). The fixed \(T=\max(1,2(k-1))\) covers both.
  2. Which degree is \(D'\). The certificate bound \(s_a+\delta+\delta_i\le Te_i\) is charged against the original companion degree \(e_i\le D'\). So \(D'\) is the degree of the eliminated refutation before the restriction.
  3. The barrier's conclusion. Theorem Y uses that the residual system has no refutation through \(B\); Theorem NDX′ uses the graph separation instead. This is the barrier's stability statement at degree zero. Under \(m\ge B\) and \(N\ge\max(1,2B-1)\) it gives \(\mathcal I_B\cap\mathcal P_{\le0}=\mathcal I_0=\{0\}\) and \(\mathcal C_B=\mathcal I_B\), so \(1\notin\mathcal C_B\).
  4. Unused hypotheses. BC never uses completeness of the removed block, as Lemma WE's entry already notes for Lemma WE. Theorem Y's restriction \(\varepsilon\le1\) keeps the statement nontrivial and is not used by the proof, as the remark after the proof says.
  5. Degrees in Lemma WE. The leaf bound uses \(\deg P_U=h(1+\max_i\deg f_i)\), which holds because the coefficient variables are distinct, and additivity of total degree in \(\mathbb F_p[Y,R]\). A nonzero constant input is covered, since then \(\chi_\alpha\) is constant and \(\deg P_U\ge1\) still holds.
  6. Variables in NDX step 3. The substitution \(\sigma\) replaces every variable that the narrow conversion introduces, not only the narrow coefficients. A stray variable could also be set to zero, a ring map that does not raise the degree.
  7. Constants of NDX and NDX′. The lower bound on \(k_n\) in step 6 of NDX is not needed: \(\delta^2\) is a constant, so \(\max(\delta^2,k_n)\le\sqrt{(c+2p)n\ln n}\) for large \(n\) anyway. In NDX′, Lemma WE is applied at most \(K\) times. Since \(d_K\ge d_0\ge k_n\) and \(d_K\ge2\), the assumption \(d_K\le B_H\) would put \(B=d_K\) in the separation range. The constant \(\gamma\) of the graph class is absolute, so \(C=\gamma/(18\delta^2)\) depends only on \(p\).

The excerpt file for the Theorem Y part ended before step 4 of the proof and the remark after it, through an extraction error made here. The auditor rechecked the constants of step 4 independently. It also asked that step 4 name \(B\) and that the remark treat \(\varepsilon>1\) as the trivial case. The entry does both.

Consequence

The chains of Corollary NDp and of both theorems that allow arbitrary lines, Theorem Y and Theorem NDX′, now have independent audits, from the compiler to the barrier. The imported Mikša–Nordström theorem and the matching barrier are the dependencies they take as given. The statement set made publication wait for an independent check of the complete-board transfer and the fixed-graph chain, and that condition is met. Still unaudited are the full restriction argument of the cell-support exclusion, the remainder and occupancy exclusions and the mixed propositions.

Next step

Next step (scope-and-review): a novelty check of the statement set against the literature. The 22 September search looked for mechanisms, not for prior versions of these endpoints. Search for superpolynomial lower bounds for DAG-like \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\), or for \(\mathrm{Res}(\oplus)\) restricted by line structure, rank or support, on PHP or on any formula, from 2018 to 2026. Compare the results found with Corollary NDp and Theorems Y and NDX′, and with this project's own binary result. Record the sources, what each proves, and whether any endpoint is known, implied or new. Audit the remaining endpoints afterwards.

Sheaf check

No gluing is involved. The audited mechanisms are the per-piece gluing maps of the thread: each removes one piece at a constant cost, relative to a fixed global section, the weight \(f\) or the target \(1\).

Verification gate. The two auditors read only the excerpt files and ran no searches. Verdicts: sound with wording fixes (Theorem Y part) and sound (NDX′ part). Independently rechecked here: the identity \(\chi_\alpha(y)(\alpha-y)=(\alpha-y)+(y-\alpha)^p=y^p-y\); \(B_H=\lfloor\lfloor\gamma n\rfloor/8\rfloor\ge\gamma n/9\) for large \(n\), from \(\delta_H/(4d)=1/8\); the number \(s=127(n+1)\) of nondistinguished edges; the barrier's stability statement for every \(0\le t\le B\) in its living summary; and that the entry's step 4 and remark, missing from the excerpt, state what the auditor asked for. No computation was run.

Novelty check: no prior DAG-like \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\) lower bound for PHP was found, restricted or not

22 September 2026 · Literature review · None of the thread's endpoints found or implied in the sources checked; closest relatives recorded; novelty is not certified. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. Route item: scope-and-review. The removal audit completed the independent audits of the chains behind Corollary NDp and Theorems Y and NDX′. The statement set still lacked a novelty check: the search of 22 September looked for mechanisms, not for earlier versions of the endpoints. This entry asks, for each endpoint, whether it is known, implied by a known result, or not found.

Method

Two fresh-context searchers received a short file with the endpoints and their definitions, and read primary sources: abstracts and the relevant theorems. The first covered resolution over linear equations over fields other than \(\mathbb F_2\), and polynomial calculus with extension variables. The second covered resolution over parities and the linear branching programs and parity decision trees used for it. Both were asked to mark what they could not open. The closest relatives were then opened again here.

What the literature proves

Over fields other than \(\mathbb F_2\).

  • Raz and Tzameret (arXiv 0708.1529, APAL 2008) work over \(\mathbb Z\). They give polynomial-size \(\mathrm{R}^0(\mathrm{lin})\) refutations of PHP, so PHP is easy in characteristic zero, and prove an exponential bound for \(\mathrm{R}^0(\mathrm{lin})\) on clique-colouring.
  • Part and Tzameret (arXiv 1806.09383, Comput. Complexity 2021) prove exponential tree-like \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_F)\) bounds for PHP over every field, and DAG-like \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb Q})\) bounds for subset sum.
  • Khaniki (ECCC TR20-034, ToCL 2022) studies \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{PC}_d)\) over finite rings. It proves nearly quadratic DAG-like bounds for Tseitin mod \(q\) and random \(k\)-CNFs, and tree-like bounds for PHP. Its method passes from lines to extension variables, width and PC degree. This is the closest precedent of the thread's compilation.
  • Part (arXiv 2202.08214, version 3, April 2026) proves bounds for subset sum in \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_q})\), \(\operatorname{char}\ge5\), in a regular DAG-like fragment and tree-like.
  • Polynomial calculus with extension variables over \(\mathbb F_p\). Impagliazzo, Mouli and Pitassi (CCC 2023) allow extension variables of arity \(O(\log n)\). Dahiya, Mahajan and Mouli (SAT 2024) allow \(N^{1+\varepsilon(1-\delta)}\) extension variables of arity at most \(N^{1-\varepsilon}\), and prove \(\exp(\Omega(N^{\varepsilon\delta}/\operatorname{polylog}N))\) for XOR-ified generalized PHP formulas. Alekseev (CCC 2021) shows that extension PC with radicals over \(\mathbb Q\) simulates \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin})\).

Over \(\mathbb F_2\).

  • Krajíček (arXiv 1611.08680, J. Math. Log. 2018), section 4, translates a line \(\{f_1,\ldots,f_k\}\) to \(\prod_i(1-f_i)\). With Razborov's degree bound, every \(\mathrm{R}(\mathrm{LIN}/\mathbb F_2)\) refutation of unary functional PHP with linear row clauses then has a line with at least \(n/2\) equations. No size bound follows. Section 4 was read here in full.
  • Tree-like \(\mathrm{Res}(\oplus)\): unary PHP needs size \(2^{\Omega(n)}\) (Itsykson and Sokolov; their pages could not be opened, and the statement comes from citing papers). Oparin (SAT 2016) gives a matching upper bound \(2^{O(n)}\).
  • Regular and bounded-depth \(\mathrm{Res}(\oplus)\):
    • Efremenko, Garlík and Itsykson (STOC 2024): bit PHP. Their Theorem 5.5 gives every DAG-like refutation a line of rank at least \(n/4\).
    • Bhattacharya, Chattopadhyay and Dvořák (CCC 2024).
    • Alekseev and Itsykson (STOC 2025).
    • Efremenko and Itsykson (CCC 2025, STOC 2026).
    • Bhattacharya, Chattopadhyay and Byramji (STOC 2026): depth up to \(N^{2-\varepsilon}\).
    • Byramji and Impagliazzo (arXiv 2511.20023): bit PHP at depth up to \(N^{2-\varepsilon}\). They also show that the block-lifted unary functional PHP needs \(\exp(\Omega(n^2/D))\) at depth \(D\).
  • Read-once linear branching programs: Gryaznov, Pudlák and Talebanfard (CCC 2022), and Li and Zhong (CCC 2024).
  • This project's preprint (arXiv 2609.23015): unrestricted DAG-like \(\mathrm{Res}(\oplus)\), bit PHP.

Verdict for each endpoint

  • Restricted line classes: local lines, Corollary NDp, probes with row remainders, occupancy, cell support and the mixtures. Not found and not implied. Every published bound found for resolution over linear equations is tree-like, restricts the shape of the DAG (regularity, depth), concerns another formula or field, or is at most nearly quadratic. None restricts what the lines contain. The nearest statements find one wide line. Krajíček finds \(n/2\) equations in some line over \(\mathbb F_2\), and Efremenko, Garlík and Itsykson find rank \(n/4\) in some line for bit PHP. These exclude refutations whose every line is narrow, at every size. They do not imply Corollary NDp, which bounds only the nonlocal part of a line and leaves its number of local equations free.
  • Cell support. The nearest statement is Dahiya, Mahajan and Mouli. Their arity \(N^{1-\varepsilon}\) resembles cell support \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\), which is about \(N^{1-\varepsilon/2}\) in the \(N\approx n^2\) cell variables. But they bound the number of extension variables by \(N^{1+\varepsilon(1-\delta)}\), where the thread allows \(n^c\) lines, and their formula is different. Not implied.
  • Counts of exceptional lines: Theorem Y and Theorem NDX′. Not found. The known arguments find one wide or high-rank line; none counts such lines in a short refutation.
  • Binary analogues. The \(\mathbb F_2\) literature restricts DAG-like proofs only by regularity and depth, never by the structure of the forms in a line.
  • Upper bounds. No DAG-like refutation of unary PHP shorter than tree-like size was found, in \(\mathrm{Res}(\oplus)\) or in \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\). Over \(\mathbb Z\), polynomial-size refutations exist, so the analogues of the endpoints fail in characteristic zero. The thread's compiler uses the finite field through the selectors \(1-L^{p-1}\).

The translation of lines into polynomial calculus has precedents: Krajíček's section 4, Khaniki, and Part and Tzameret. The thread's contributions are, as far as this search shows, the complete-block compiler with its degree ledger and the exclusions of compiled sources. That includes the counts of exceptional lines, for which no analogue was found even over \(\mathbb F_2\).

A correction to the search brief

The brief given to the searchers attributed this project's binary unary result to its preprint arXiv 2609.23015. That is wrong. The preprint proves a lower bound for the bit encoding of PHP, and its introduction says it does not address unary PHP. The unary binary theorem is the separate working theorem of the main notebook, which its registry record already describes as separate from the preprint. The record is consistent; only the brief was wrong.

Consequence

No source checked contains or implies any endpoint of the statement set. As far as this search shows, they are the first superpolynomial size lower bounds for classes of DAG-like \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\) refutations of PHP at an odd prime, and the first counts of exceptional lines in any \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_F)\). Novelty is not certified. The search is bounded, several sources were read only through abstracts, and some pages could not be opened. So Corollary NDp and Theorems Y and NDX′ are registered here as novelty candidates for review, not as established new results. Two gaps remain before the statement set could be published: an expert review, and audits of the endpoints not yet audited.

Next step

Next step (scope-and-review): audit the remaining endpoints of the statement set, with one fresh auditor each for two parts. The first part is the full restriction argument of the cell-support exclusion and the remainder exclusion. The second is the occupancy exclusion and Proposition MXp. Then the thread waits for a user decision on the statement set, publication or a restart condition of the window.

Sheaf check

No gluing is involved. The check asks whether any published local section already covers one of the thread's line classes; none was found.

Verification gate. The two searchers ran their searches independently and marked unopened sources: the Itsykson–Sokolov pages, the journal version of Part–Tzameret, the ACM pages of STOC 2026 and Garlík–Kołodziejczyk. Opened again here: the Dahiya–Mahajan–Mouli abstract, the Khaniki abstract, the abstract and version dates of Part's preprint, and section 4 of Krajíček's paper in full, which confirms the statement above. Both searchers found the brief's misattribution independently. No computation was run.

Independent audit of the remaining endpoints: cell support, remainders, occupancy and the mixed propositions

22 September 2026 · Audit · Remaining endpoints sound; two stated bounds of MX″ and MXp corrected, with no change to any conclusion; the whole statement set is now audited. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. Route item: scope-and-review. After the novelty check, the statement set still had four endpoints without an independent audit. This entry records their audit in three parts, and a fourth for Proposition MX′, each by one fresh-context auditor that read only a scratch file of excerpts and was asked to break the argument. Cited endpoints outside a part were taken as given, and their hypotheses were checked where they are applied.

  • Part A. The full cell-support exclusion and the remainder exclusion, with the statements of the row-local and probe endpoints it composes with.
  • Part B. The occupancy exclusion, with the column-state reduction and the column freezing map.
  • Part C. Propositions MX, MX″ and MXp.

Part A: cell support and remainders

Verdict: sound with fixes; no step fails. Checked:

  • The surviving row and column sets are independent and uniform, and the survival probability of a \(k\)-matching is right. The tail \(n^{-k(\varepsilon-2\beta)+o(1)}\), with \(\beta<\varepsilon/2\) and \(k(\varepsilon-2\beta)>c+1\), gives the union bound, and the residual cover satisfies \(s_a\le2(k-1)\).
  • The partition identity lies in \(I_s\). Row exclusions are used only after the base is strengthened to functional. The certificates hold at the stated degrees: \(P'-V\in I_{s+\delta}\), \(g_iV\in I_{s+\delta_i}\), \(g_iP'\in I_{s+\delta+\delta_i}\), and the field certificate within \(ps\). The replay through \(TD\) is valid, and the barrier applies with \(N\ge2B-1\).
  • The compiler corollary preserves support and does not raise the degree, and \(\varepsilon\le1\) admits the pigeon clauses.
  • In the remainder exclusion, compression costs no degree. A fixed \(u>(C+1)/(1-\alpha-\beta)\) makes the tail \(n^{-u(1-\alpha-\beta)+o(1)}\) cover every support. The row equations and the source hypothesis survive the restriction, and the probes keep their number.

Clarifications:

  1. The remainder exclusion applies the probe endpoint on the residual board with \(n_1=\lceil n^\beta\rceil\). Its constants in \(n_1\) are \(M\le n_1^{c/\beta}\), \(t_a\le(c_0/\beta)\log_pn_1\), at most \(u-1\) local rows, so \(\alpha=0\), and \(D=\operatorname{polylog}n_1\). "Sufficiently large" is taken in \(n_1\).
  2. The paragraph "All parameters still fit" quotes the degree ledger \(D_*=\max(TD,2\max(p-1,R,1)+1)\) and \(sD_*=n^{\alpha+o(1)}\). The ledger is recorded in the composition section of the probe endpoint's entry, not in its statement. The conclusion needs only the statement.
  3. Each input of the remainder exclusion is an old selector \(1-L^{p-1}\), with \(L\) an old affine form. Its compiler is the complete-board transfer, which gives accuracy-one blocks whose inputs are the selectors of the clause's own forms. A form that becomes constant under the restriction gives an input \(0\) or \(1\). Such an input fits the probe endpoint with empty row support, or its block is removed by the unit map.
  4. In the cell-support exclusion, \(\delta\) is the largest actual degree of a nonzero input, so \(\deg P_a=h_a(\delta+1)\) exactly, as in the removal audit. Also \(Te_i\le TD\), because only generators of degree at most \(D\) occur in a proof of degree \(D\).

Part B: occupancy

Verdict: sound with fixes. The auditor made its verdict conditional on one point: the final endpoint must accept blocks that mix affine inputs from different columns. That point is settled below. Checked:

  • The pigeon-row bridge satisfies \(t_j-X_{ij}\in I_{p-1}(\mathrm{Bool})\). The hole and Boolean initials hold through \(3p-2\).
  • The freezing map \(\Phi\) is an affine substitution of variables, hence a ring map. Every \(\sigma_j\) becomes \(0\) or \(1\), and the distinguished row equation holds because \(K+1=0\). The certificates for Booleanity of \(q_j\) and for \(y_{ij}q_j\) hold through degree \(2\). The residual board has \(N=\lfloor n/(p-1)\rfloor-1\) holes and \(N+1\) pigeons. The inputs become affine in one column each, modulo a residual row combination, and each input may use its own column.
  • The column-state identity is exact, with bounds \(\max(3,p+1,2p-1)=2p-1\) for every \(p\ge2\). All coefficient fields are kept, and the base is strengthened to functional only after \(\Phi\).

Resolved here:

  1. The final endpoint. "The all-prime affine endpoint" is the all-prime unary affine source exclusion. Its statement admits any complete one-level family whose inputs are affine in the old cells over \(\mathbb F_p\), at every accuracy, on the weak or functional base, with polynomial inventory and polylogarithmic degree. So blocks that mix single-column inputs from different columns are covered, and so are constant inputs, through the zero and unit spans. The degree excluded is \(\max(4p-1,2p-1)=4p-1\). The auditor observed that at \(p=2\) such an endpoint would cover every \(\mathrm{Res}(\oplus)\) refutation, and concluded that it must be restricted. It is restricted only by inventory and degree. At \(p=2\) it gives exactly the recorded binary unary theorem, so the observation is consistent with the record.
  2. The weak-base compiler. The compiler's compression uses literal polynomial spans of degree at most \(\delta\), with "no Boolean quotient" (selector compiler). So compression and the source spans of weakening and simplification use no base generator, and no functional identity precedes \(\Phi\). The ceiling \(4p-1\) for the local rules is that of the selector compiler. Its local steps use only the Boolean equations, which the weak base contains, as the compiler audit requires.
  3. Lines and inventory. Compression leaves at most \(\binom{v+p-1}{p-1}\) actual inputs per block, whatever a line's number of disjuncts. So the inventory is polynomial in the number of lines, as the endpoint requires.

Part C: the mixed propositions

Verdict: sound with fixes. Checked:

  • In MX, the exponent \(\beta\) exists exactly when \(\alpha<1/5\) and \(\eta<(1-\alpha)/8\), and \(n^\alpha=o(N)\) because \(\beta>\alpha\). The type-(i) companion identity is exact and lies in \(\mathcal I_{C+t+2}\).
  • (SPLIT) is exact. Costs add everywhere and multiply only by the constant \(D\).
  • In MXp, the union bound over branches is \(n^Kp^t\le n^{K+c_0}\). Parameters with \(\delta\eta<\beta_1\beta_2\sigma\), \(\beta_1<1-\alpha\), \(\beta_2<1/4\) and \(\sigma<1\) exist exactly when \(\eta<(1-\alpha)/(4\delta)\). The boundary cases \(\alpha=0\), \(\eta=0\), \(t=0\) and \(r<\delta\) hold.

Corrections to stated bounds. They change no conclusion.

  1. The degree of \(P_{\mathcal B}\). MX″ and MXp state \(\deg P_{\mathcal B}\le T+1\). But \(P_{\mathcal B}=1-\sum_{\mathcal B}\Theta(r_j)q_j\), with \(\deg\Theta(r_j)\le T\) and \(\deg q_j\le\delta\), so the bound is \(T+\delta\): \(T+2\) at \(p=3\). This was checked here from the definitions. So \(T+1\) becomes \(T+\delta\) in four places: the coefficient-image degree \(T+\delta+d+s\), the replay term \(D(T+\delta+d+s)+k\), the \(\mathcal A\)-companion term \(D_{\mathcal A}+T+\delta+k\), and the \(\mathcal A\)-field term. The field term is \(p(T+\delta+d+s)+k\), since every replayed axiom image carries the weight \(f\). Every term remains \(o(N)\), because \(T=o(N)\), \(d=O(\log N)\), and \(s\) and \(\delta\) are constants.
  2. The type-(ii) rank in MX. The bound \(r_a\le n^{2\eta}\) should read \(r_a\le(2r)^2\le4n^{2\eta}\), which is MXp's count at \(p=3\). Since the condition \(2\eta<\beta\sigma\) is strict, \(4n^{2\eta}\le N^\sigma\) for large \(n\), and nothing changes.

Clarifications:

  1. Mixed blocks. The compiled refutation is not rewritten for a block whose forms fall into both parts. \(\Theta\) substitutes that block's coefficients directly. The certificate of \(f\,q_jP_{\mathcal B}\) is a polynomial identity: a polynomial that vanishes on the cube plus old-ideal terms. It uses (LPF-value) and the pointwise argument of step 4 of the two-level map for the \(\mathcal B\)-subtuple's inputs. It does not need the subtuple to be a block of the compiled refutation, and the graph and map audit confirmed that this pointwise conclusion concerns only the image polynomials.
  2. The degree \(D_{\mathcal B}\). MX″ takes \(D_{\mathcal B}\) from MX′'s \(\mathcal B\)-certificate. Whether it is of order \(Te+k\) or \(DT+k\), it is \(o(N)\).
  3. "\(D=4p-1\), polylog" in MXp's table. The compiler's degree is the constant \(4p-1\). It lies in the polylogarithmic range that the cited endpoints assume, and no polylogarithmic factor enters \(D\).
  4. The separation. MXp's final contradiction is with the fixed-graph separation that Theorem QRp uses, with its linear range. The graph and map audit checked it at every prime. The ternary dense graph criterion, which has no \(p\ge5\) analogue, is not used.
  5. The constants \(m\) and \(C_0\). The \(m\) in MXp's \(C=\max(\delta,m-1)\) is MX′'s fixed integer \(m>C_0/(1-\alpha-\beta_1)\). It bounds the rows that a nonconstant branch input reads after the second restriction. \(C_0\) is MX′'s support-count exponent. It is fixed for each \(p\), because the compressed inventory is at most \(n^{K+2\delta+1}\), as MXp's table says.

Proposition MX′. MX″ runs the proof of MX′, which was outside the excerpt of part C, so a fourth fresh auditor checked MX′ alone. Verdict: sound with fixes. The range check and the formula for \(s\) are correct. Clarifications:

  1. Two constants named \(C\). MX′ uses \(C\) both for the support-count exponent and for the expansion degree \(C=\max(2,m-1)\). They are different constants. The support exponent is \(C_0\), as MXp renames it, and with that reading \(m>C_0/(1-\alpha-\beta_1)\) is not circular. The exponents \(\beta_1,\beta_2,\sigma\) are positive.
  2. The support count. The union bound runs over the one chosen remainder of each kept input, not over every representation modulo rows. With at most \(n^K\) blocks and polynomially many kept inputs per block, a fixed \(C_0\) exists, for example \(K+2\delta+1\), as in MXp.
  3. The switching count. \(n^K3^t\) counts one branch disjunction per line and branch. This holds because each line compiles to one block, and the reader switches the whole branch disjunction. A polynomial factor more would raise only the constant \(s\).
  4. Empty branches. A branch whose inputs have all become zero selectors has an empty disjunction. The empty-aware reader handles it as an empty leaf.
  5. The branch product. \(P_u=1-\sum_iR_{u,i}q_{u,i}\) is the product of (PL-map) in the probe endpoint. It is linear in the formal \(R\), and its old part has degree \(\delta=2\). After the reader substitution of degree \(s\), its image \(P'\) has degree at most \(s+2\), which the bounds \(\mathcal I_{d+s+4}\) and \(\mathcal I_{C+s+2}\) need. The term \(d+s+4\) is absorbed by \(d+C+s+2\) because \(C\ge2\).
  6. The replay bound. It must also carry the type-(ii) certificate degree \(D_{\mathcal B}\) of step 4, as MX″ writes it: \(B\le11\max(T,d+s)+\max(D_{\mathcal A},D_{\mathcal B})+k\). The weight degree is \(k=O(\sqrt{N\log N})\) on the final board, by the fixed-graph formula with inventory polynomial in \(n=N^{O(1)}\), as in step 6 of Theorem NDX. So every term is \(o(N)\).

Thread route review: the statement set is complete; bounded-depth closure is the one outside mechanism not yet tested at odd primes

22 September 2026 · Route review of the odd-prime thread · Window weak; write-up awaits a user decision; next: test an \(\mathbb F_p\) closure lemma for unary PHP, the first step of a bounded-depth endpoint. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

The thread's general claim. Superpolynomial lower bounds for \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\) refutations of unary PHP, at every odd prime, follow by compiling a refutation into complete selector blocks over PHP and excluding the compiled source. What the goal needs is the case the statement set leaves open: refutations with more than \(Cn\) window lines, of nonlocal dimension above \(n^{1/(p-1)-\varepsilon}\), outside every recorded class. Since the last thread review, the statement set has been audited end to end, the last step being the affine endpoint audit, and the novelty check found none of its endpoints in the literature. Route items under review: all three.

Falsification attempt: is a restart condition met?

The statement set named three restart conditions for the window.

  1. A batched mechanism for non-nested dense blocks. None was found. The audits confirm the recorded limits: per-block removal is linear (Theorem NDX′), and the batch theorems need nesting.
  2. A proof of the level-one conjecture with a depth-independent use. No progress; the reuse-free analysis showed that any use is limited by depth.
  3. Outside work on DAG-like proofs with dense linear lines. The novelty check found work that the lag review had not listed. Bhattacharya, Chattopadhyay and Byramji (STOC 2026) and Byramji and Impagliazzo (arXiv 2511.20023) prove bounds for \(\mathrm{Res}(\oplus)\) up to depth \(N^{2-\varepsilon}\), for bit PHP and for a block-lifted unary functional PHP. These are DAG-like proofs with arbitrary dense lines, restricted only in depth, at a depth far beyond the earlier \(O(n\log n)\). They work over \(\mathbb F_2\), on other encodings. Like every closure method, they follow one path of the proof, as F4 of the ceiling review recorded. So the condition is not met for the unrestricted goal.

One fact changes the assessment of the third condition. These bounds are the only recorded mechanism that handles dense lines of the window's rank in DAG-like proofs of large depth. None of the thread's endpoints admits more than \(Cn\) window lines at any depth. So a bounded-depth endpoint for \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\) on unary PHP would be the first odd-prime statement that admits arbitrarily many window lines. It would still not be the goal: depth is a restriction, and the gap between depth-restricted and DAG-like proofs is exactly what closure methods do not cross.

Assessment of each route item

  • odd-prime-clause-transfer (the window): weak, unchanged. No mechanism within the compile-and-exclude framework; the audits add confidence in the partial results, not a route to the rest.
  • same-graph-composition: bookkeeping; nothing open.
  • scope-and-review: complete up to external review. Every endpoint and dependency is independently audited, except for the imported theorems, and the novelty check found none of the endpoints in the literature. Whether to write the statement set up for expert review, or as a preprint, is a publication decision that belongs to the user. Separately, the binary unary theorem of the main notebook lacks only an audit of its own CNF compiler; that is a main-notebook task.

A candidate line and its first obligation

A bounded-depth endpoint at odd primes would need two pieces. The first is an \(\mathbb F_p\) closure lemma for unary PHP. Given a linear system over \(\mathbb F_p\) in the cell variables of rank \(a\), it would find a partial matching on \(O(a)\) rows and holes after which the system is implied, while PHP on the remaining board stays hard, with degree about \(n/2-O(a)\). The second is a path argument that keeps the rank of the system along a path below the depth bound. The record has the first piece only over \(\mathbb F_2\) and for bit labels (Corollary SL), and the matching filtration over every field. Two obstructions must be checked first. Over \(\mathbb F_p\), sums of row equations count modulo \(p\): onto-PHP is refuted at once by comparing row and column sums, so the closure must not introduce onto-type column equations. And a dense form over \(\mathbb F_p\) can take \(p\) values, so closure must handle equations \(L=u\) for every \(u\), not only parities.

Next step

Next step (odd-prime-clause-transfer): test the first obligation of the bounded-depth line. Read the closure lemma of Byramji and Impagliazzo (arXiv 2511.20023) and of Efremenko, Garlík and Itsykson, and state its exact \(\mathbb F_p\) analogue for ordinary unary PHP. Check it against the two obstructions above: modular counting of row sums, and multi-valued dense forms. Then either prove it at rank \(a\le cn\) or find the obstruction. If the closure lemma fails at odd primes, record why and close the line. The write-up of the statement set waits for a user decision, which this review surfaces.

Closure methods glue along one path: each node's linear system restricts to its successor's, and the section is a partial matching that extends along the path. That is why they reach bounded depth and not DAGs, where a node has several parents whose closures need not agree. The thread's endpoints glue across the covering by compiled blocks, at a cost per block. The two gluings are complementary, and neither reaches the window.
