The low-or-dense graph criterion at every odd prime: a dense side for \(p\ge5\)

22 September 2026 · Working proof · Theorem GCp: the ternary graph criterion at every odd prime, with Lemma HDH in the dense step; the \(p\ge5\) window runs from \(R\) to about \(N^{p-3/2}\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The head-count entry proved the counting step of a dense side for \(p\ge5\) and listed the other \(p\)-dependent steps of the ternary low-or-dense graph criterion. This entry checks each against its source. A complete transcription gives \(p\ge5\) a dense side, which the statement set lacks. A step that fails would locate a prime-specific obstruction.

Setting

Fix an odd prime \(p\) and put \(\delta=p-1\). Take the graph \(H\), the \(s=15(N+1)\) nondistinguished coordinates \(Y\) and the space \(W_k\) of the separated-space lemma. Its statement holds over every field: \(\dim W_k\ge\frac12e^{-5k^2/N}\binom sk\), and \(W_k\cap\mathcal C_B(\Gamma_H)=\{0\}\) for \(\max(k,8)\le B\le N/10^6\). Here \(\Gamma_H\) is functional graph PHP with linear row equations. Restrict every cell outside \(H\) to zero, and replace each distinguished cell in the block inputs by \(1\) minus the other cells of its row. This changes each input \(g\) to some \(g'\) with \(g-g'\) in the ideal of the row equations, certified through \(\delta\). With the same coefficients, \(P-P'=\sum_ir_i(g'_i-g_i)\) is certified through \(\delta+1\). So \(gP-g'P'=(g-g')P+g'(P-P')\) is certified through the companion degree \(2\delta+1\), and the source transfers at its original ceilings.

Consider \(M\) complete accuracy-one blocks whose inputs are old polynomials of degree at most \(\delta\), such as selectors \(1-L^\delta\), with all coefficient fields. The companion degree is \(2\delta+1=2p-1\). Fix a requested PC degree \(D\ge2p-1\). For block \(a\), let \(V_a\) be its input span, and let \(r_a\) be the dimension of \(V_a\) in \(\mathcal P_{\le\delta}/I_\delta(\Gamma_H)\) modulo the affine image, after the restriction and projection. Put

\[ \Lambda=\log(64(M+1)),\quad k=\lceil\sqrt{N\Lambda}\rceil,\quad H_*=\Bigl\lceil k+\frac sk\Bigl(\Lambda+\frac{5k^2}N\Bigr)\Bigr\rceil, \] \[ Q^{(p)}_*=\Bigl\lceil2^\delta\,\delta\binom s\delta\Bigl(\frac{\delta-1}s+\frac{5k}N+\frac{\Lambda+1}k\Bigr)\Bigr\rceil,\qquad T=(p-1)(H_*+\delta R)+p . \]

Theorem GCp

Assume a polynomial inventory, so that \(\Lambda=O(\log N)\) and \(k=O(\sqrt{N\log N})\) as the separated-space lemma requires, and let \(N\) be sufficiently large. Assume \(k\le s/4\), that every block has \(r_a\le R\) or \(r_a\ge Q^{(p)}_*\), and \(TD+k\le N/10^6\). Then the source has no ordinary PC refutation through \(D\). Since \(T\ge(p-1)\delta R\), the budget needs \(RD\le c_pN\). For polylogarithmic \(D\) it holds eventually with \(R\le N^\sigma\operatorname{polylog}N\), \(\sigma<1\), as in the ternary criterion. For bounded \(D\), such as the compiler degree \(4p-1\), it holds with \(R\le c_pN\). Then \(H_*=O(\sqrt{N\log N})\) and \(Q^{(p)}_*=O_p(N^{p-3/2}\sqrt{\log N})\). At \(p=3\) this is the ternary criterion, with slightly different constants in \(Q_*\) and \(T\).

Proof

Dense heads. Let block \(a\) have \(r_a\ge Q^{(p)}_*\). Its inputs are polynomials in \(Y\) after the projection \(\Pi\), which substitutes each distinguished cell. For every \(e\), \(e-\Pi(e)\) is a multiple of row equations certified through \(\deg e\), so \(\Pi(I_\delta)\subseteq I_\delta\). And \(v=e+a\) with \(e\in I_\delta\) and \(a\) affine gives \(v=\Pi(e)+\Pi(a)\). So \(r_a\) is also the dimension of \(V_a\) in \(\mathcal P_{\le\delta}(Y)\) modulo \(\Pi(I_\delta)+\mathcal P_{\le1}(Y)\). This matters at \(\delta\ge3\): an element of \(I_\delta\) with a head in \(Y\) can carry lower nonlinear monomials in distinguished cells. Work in \(\mathcal P_{\le\delta}(Y)\) with the degree-compatible order used for the later reduction. Row-reduce the nonlinear coefficient columns of \(V_a\), the monomials of degrees \(2\) to \(\delta\), modulo the nonlinear parts of \(\Pi(I_\delta)\), keeping all affine tails. The rank of this reduction is \(r_a\). It supplies \(r_a\) polynomials \(y_h=v_h-e_h\), with \(v_h\) a constant combination of actual inputs and \(e_h\in\Pi(I_\delta)\) certified through \(\delta\). Their leading monomials are distinct squarefree subsets of \(Y\), of sizes \(2\) to \(\delta\), because Booleanity removes squares. No affine equation is subtracted. Reducing degree-\(\le k\) monomials by the \(y_h\) and Booleanity, in a degree-compatible order, keeps the degree ceiling. By Lemma HDH and the head-count entry's arithmetic, its image has dimension at most \(4\binom sk e^{-5k^2/N-\Lambda}=\frac{\frac12e^{-5k^2/N}\binom sk}{8(M+1)}\). A kernel element has the form

\[ f=\sum_ic_ig_i+E,\qquad\deg c_i\le k-2,\qquad E\in I_{k+\delta-2}(\Gamma_H),\tag{GCp-membership} \]

with \(g_i\) the actual inputs. A head of degree \(d\) gets a multiplier of degree at most \(k-d\le k-2\), and \(e_h\) is certified through \(\delta\), so \(E\) is certified through \(k+\delta-2\). At \(p=3\) this is \(k\), as in the ternary criterion.

Affine cores. For a block with \(r_a\le R\), apply the all-prime degree-certified basis conversion of Theorem QRp. Its new inputs are affine representatives \(F_1,\dots,F_b\) of the affine part of \(V_a\), taken in \(Y\) by applying \(\Pi\), and at most \(r_a\) actual inputs \(G_j\). Every source axiom image is certified through the original companion degree \(2p-1\le D\), and coefficient fields map by Frobenius. After zero and unit cleanup, call the span of the \(F\)s the core. A proper core of rank at least \(H_*\) restricts to its common zero flat by substituting pivot coordinates, with image in multilinear polynomials of degree at most \(k\) in the other coordinates. That image has dimension at most \(\binom sk\exp[-k(H_*-k)/s]\le\frac{\frac12e^{-5k^2/N}\binom sk}{32(M+1)}\), as in the ternary criterion. None of this depends on the field. Its kernel elements have the form \(f=\sum_jc_jF_j+B\) with \(\deg c_j\le k-1\) and \(B\) a Boolean multiple in the free coordinates.

One weight. The images of all blocks together have dimension below \(\dim W_k\). So some nonzero homogeneous \(f\in W_k\) lies in every kernel.

Dense map. Map the coefficient of \(g_i\) to \(\beta_i=f^{p-2}c_i\), of degree at most \((p-1)k-2\). The product becomes

\[ 1-\sum_i\beta_ig_i=1-f^{p-1}+f^{p-2}E,\qquad f\,g_iP(\beta)=g_i(f-f^p)+f^{p-1}g_iE . \]

The polynomial \(f^p-f\) vanishes on the Boolean cube, since \(f\) takes values in \(\mathbb F_p\), so the first term has a Boolean certificate through \(pk+\delta\). The second has an old certificate through \(pk+2\delta-2\), within \(T(2p-1)+k\). The weighted field image \(f(\beta_i^p-\beta_i)\) vanishes on the cube, through \(p(p-1)k+k\).

Low map. The affine part is normalized to a product \(A\):

  • A high proper core maps \(t_j\mapsto f^{p-2}c_j\), so \(A=1-f^{p-1}+f^{p-2}B\), with coefficient degree at most \((p-1)k-1\).
  • A core of rank \(h<H_*\) uses the exact Fermat zero indicator \(A=\prod_{j\le h}(1-F_j^\delta)\). This is \(1-\sum_jF_j\cdot F_j^{\delta-1}\prod_{i<j}(1-F_i^\delta)\), with coefficient degree below \((p-1)H_*\).
  • A unit core has product zero, and an empty core has \(A=1\).

For the nonlinear inputs, the exact prefix \(\beta_j=A\,G_j^{\delta-1}\prod_{i<j}(1-G_i^\delta)\) telescopes to the product \(A\prod_j(1-G_j^\delta)\). Its coefficient degree is at most \((p-1)H_*+(p-1)\delta R\le T\). At every Boolean point with \(f\ne0\), each companion image vanishes:

  • \(G_j(1-G_j^\delta)=G_j-G_j^p=0\);
  • \(F_jA=0\), for a small core by the zero indicator, and for a high core because \(f^{p-1}=1\) and \(B=0\) there.

So every weighted companion image vanishes on the cube, and Boolean division certifies it at its actual degree, at most \(T+2p-1+k\le T(2p-1)+k\). Weighted coefficient fields vanish on the cube, through \(pT+k\).

Replay. All maps use old coordinates only and share the weight \(f\). Old axioms stay legal weighted multiples. Every weighted source-axiom image is certified through \(Te+k\) for its original degree \(e\le D\). Fields cost at most \(pT+k\), which is below \(TD+k\) because \(D\ge2p-1\ge p\). Substituting and weighting the PC proof therefore derives \(f\) over \(\Gamma_H\) through \(TD+k\le N/10^6\). This contradicts the separation of \(W_k\), since \(\max(k,8)\le TD+k\) because \(T\ge p\) and \(D\ge2p-1\). \(\square\)

Scope

  • Theorem GCp is the ternary criterion transcribed. Six things change with \(p\): the degree of heads (Lemma HDH); taking heads in \(Y\) modulo the projected ideal; the certificate degree \(k+\delta-2\) of \(E\); the power \(f^{p-1}\) in the maps; the Fermat indicators of degree \(p-1\) per form; and the cost \((p-1)\delta\) per nonlinear input. The graph, the separated space and the affine-core bound do not.
  • Corollary NDp bounds a block's rank on the full functional base by \(\binom{v+\delta}\delta\) for nonlocal dimension \(v\). Restriction to \(H\) maps the full base's ideal into \(I_\delta(\Gamma_H)\), \(\Pi\) maps that into itself, and both keep affine polynomials affine. So the rank after restriction and projection is at most the full-board rank. For bounded \(D\) the low side then covers \(v\) up to about \(N^{1/(p-1)}\), and the dense side needs \(v\) of at least about \(N^{1-1/(2(p-1))}\). At \(p=3\) the window is \([N^{1/2},N^{3/4}]\) in these terms; at \(p\ge5\) it is wider.
  • Structured blocks such as the sunflower family, with span dimension up to about \(N^2\), cannot reach the dense threshold at \(p\ge5\). The ternary clique-head refinement is not transcribed here.
  • With the complete-board compiler at degree \(D=4p-1\), a polynomial inventory and \(R=c_pN\), a polynomial-line \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\) refutation must, on the supplied graph, have a block with \(R<r_a<Q^{(p)}_*\). This is a necessary condition, not a lower bound for refutations containing such blocks.

Checks

map_identities.py checks the \(p\)-dependent identities exactly, modulo Booleanity, over \(\mathbb F_3\), \(\mathbb F_5\) and \(\mathbb F_7\). It uses random instances in six Boolean variables with deterministic seeds. It checks the dense product and companion identities, the telescoping of the zero indicator and of the prefix, and the high-core product with \(B=0\). All hold in all twelve trials, four per prime. In this Boolean-reduced arithmetic \(f^p\equiv f\), so its vanishing checks for \(g(f-f^p)\) and for the fields are automatic, and it checks no degree bound. The degree ledger rests on the proof.

Assessment and next step

The transcription went through without a prime-specific obstruction. Every odd prime now has a low-or-dense criterion, and the statement set gains a dense side at \(p\ge5\). The window is wider there and still open, and the goal is not reached.

Next step (odd-prime-clause-transfer): transcribe the clique-head refinement to every odd prime. At \(p\ge5\) a head family containing all \((p-1)\)-subsets of a set \(M\) needs \(|M|\) of order \(\sqrt{N\log N}\), as at \(p=3\). So the rank needed would drop from about \(N^{p-3/2}\) to about \((N\log N)^{(p-1)/2}\). Then update the statement set's \(p\ge5\) lines with Theorem GCp.

Sheaf check

One section, the weight, glues across all blocks by dimension counting, now at every prime. The local conditions differ only in degree: heads of degree up to \(p-1\), and Fermat indicators of degree \(p-1\).

Clique heads at every odd prime: random dense blocks at \(p\ge5\) are excluded from rank about \((N\log N)^{(p-1)/2}\)

22 September 2026 · Working proof · Theorem CHp adds clique-covering blocks to Theorem GCp at every odd prime; random dense blocks qualify above about \((N\log N)^{(p-1)/2}\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. Theorem GCp gives every odd prime a dense side, but at \(p\ge5\) its threshold \(Q^{(p)}_*\approx N^{p-3/2}\) comes from the worst-case head count. At \(p=3\) the clique-head refinement lowered the threshold from \(N^{3/2}\) to \(N\log N\) for blocks whose heads cover all pairs of a coordinate set. Does the same work with heads of degree \(\delta=p-1\)? The test ends with a transcribed theorem and a count for random dense blocks, or with the step that fails.

Lemma CH\(_\delta\) (a clique of heads of degree \(\delta\))

Let \(2\le\delta\le m\), and \(k,m\le s/4\). Let a family of subsets of \([s]\) contain every \(\delta\)-subset of a set \(M\) of size \(m\). Then the number of sets of size at most \(k\) that contain no member satisfies

\[ J_{\le k}\le2C_\delta\binom sk\exp\Bigl(-\frac{mk}{2s}\Bigr),\qquad C_\delta=\sup_{x\ge0}(1+2x)^{\delta-1}e^{-x/2}=(4(\delta-1))^{\delta-1}e^{1/4-(\delta-1)}. \]

Proof. Such a set contains at most \(\delta-1\) points of \(M\). So the number of such \(j\)-sets is at most \(\sum_{i<\delta}\binom mi\binom{s-m}{j-i}\). Since \(m+j\le s/2\), \(\binom{s-m}{j-i}\le\binom{s-m}j(2j/s)^i\). Also \(\binom mi\le m^i/i!\le\binom{\delta-1}i m^i\), so the sum is at most \(\binom{s-m}j(1+2mj/s)^{\delta-1}\), and \(\binom{s-m}j\le\binom sj e^{-mj/s}\). Call this bound \(T_j\). For \(j<k\), \(T_j/T_{j+1}\le\frac{j+1}{s-j}e^{m/s}\le\frac13e^{1/4}<0.43\). So the sum over \(j\le k\) is at most \(2T_k\le2\binom sk e^{-x}(1+2x)^{\delta-1}\) with \(x=mk/s\), and \((1+2x)^{\delta-1}e^{-x/2}\le C_\delta\). The maximum is at \(1+2x=4(\delta-1)\). \(\square\)

At \(\delta=2\), \(C_2=4e^{-3/4}<4\), and the bound is the ternary (CH-count) \(8\binom sk e^{-mk/(2s)}\), with a better constant.

Theorem CHp

Keep every parameter of Theorem GCp, and replace its rank hypothesis by a trichotomy: every block has \(r_a\le R\), or \(r_a\ge Q^{(p)}_*\), or satisfies (CH\(_\delta\)-hyp) below. Put

\[ m^{(p)}_*=\Bigl\lceil\frac{2s}k\Bigl(\frac{5k^2}N+\Lambda+\log\frac{C_\delta}2\Bigr)\Bigr\rceil=O_p(\sqrt{N\log N}), \]

and assume \(m^{(p)}_*\le s/4\). The third kind of block is one admitting a set \(M\subseteq Y\) of size \(m^{(p)}_*\) for which, in the monomial order that compares first by degree, then by the additive weight \(w_M\) giving each coordinate of \(M\) weight one and every other coordinate weight zero, and then lexicographically,

\[ \binom M\delta\subseteq\operatorname{in}\bigl(\operatorname{span}(\Pi(g_i))+\Pi(I_\delta)\bigr)_\delta ,\tag{CH\(_\delta\)-hyp} \]

where \(\Pi\) is the projection of Theorem GCp and \(g_i\) are the block's actual inputs. Then the source still has no ordinary PC refutation through \(D\).

Proof. Multilinearize by Booleanity first, so that no squares remain. This is needed before heads are taken: \(w_M\) is additive and counts multiplicities, so a non-squarefree degree-\(\delta\) monomial in \(M\)-coordinates has the same weight \(\delta\) as a \(\delta\)-subset of \(M\) and can beat it lexicographically.

Full reduced row echelon form on the \(\binom m\delta\) columns indexed by \(\delta\)-subsets of \(M\) gives, for each such subset \(S\), a polynomial \(y_S=\sum_i\lambda_i\Pi(g_i)-e_S\) with \(e_S\in\Pi(I_\delta)\), whose leading monomial is \(S\): full reduction clears every other column of \(\binom M\delta\), and every remaining degree-\(\delta\) monomial has strictly smaller weight. Reduce degree-\(\le k\) monomials by these \(\binom m\delta\) polynomials and Booleanity, in this degree-compatible order. All heads have degree exactly \(\delta\), so the multipliers have degree at most \(k-\delta\) and the degree ceiling \(k\) is kept. A normal form is supported on sets containing no \(\delta\)-subset of \(M\), so by Lemma CH\(_\delta\) the image has dimension at most \(2C_\delta e^{-m^{(p)}_*k/(2s)}\binom sk\le4\binom sk e^{-5k^2/N-\Lambda}\), by the choice of \(m^{(p)}_*\). That is the share Theorem GCp allots to a dense block.

A kernel element \(f\) therefore satisfies (GCp-membership). Each \(g_i-\Pi(g_i)\) is a multiple of row equations certified through \(\delta\), so writing the combination in the actual inputs changes \(y_S\) by an element certified through \(\delta\), which joins \(e_S\) in the old residual. Hence \(f=\sum_ic_ig_i+E\) with \(\deg c_i\le k-\delta\) and \(E\in I_k(\Gamma_H)\subseteq I_{k+\delta-2}(\Gamma_H)\), and \(\deg\beta_i=\deg f^{p-2}c_i\le(p-1)k-\delta\). Theorem GCp's dense map, its identities and its certificates apply unchanged, a fortiori. The sum of all image dimensions stays below \(\dim W_k\), so a common nonzero weight \(f\in W_k\) exists, and the replay derives it over \(\Gamma_H\) through \(TD+k\), contradicting separation exactly as in Theorem GCp. \(\square\)

Remark: the old relations alone never satisfy (CH\(_\delta\)-hyp). Keep the order \((\deg,w_M,\text{lex})\) throughout; the reduction needs only that \(w_M\) is additive and that each reducer is \(w_M\)-largest at its head, and Lemma CH\(_\delta\)'s count does not depend on the order. Let \(M'\subseteq M\) have size \(m\), and suppose every \(\delta\)-subset of \(M'\) were a head of \(\Pi(I_\delta)\). A subset of \(M'\) inherits this, so we may take \(m=m^{(p)}_*-c\) for any \(c\le m^{(p)}_*-\delta\); then \(\delta\le m\le m^{(p)}_*\le s/4\) and Lemma CH\(_\delta\) applies. Reduce multilinear polynomials of degree \(k\) by those reducers, with multipliers of degree at most \(k-\delta\). Each step subtracts \(\mu g\) with \(g\in\Pi(I_\delta)\subseteq I_\delta(\Gamma_H)\) and \(\deg\mu\le k-\delta\), so it stays inside \(I_k(\Gamma_H)\). The image has dimension at most \(2C_\delta\binom sk e^{-mk/(2s)}\le4\binom sk e^{-5k^2/N-\Lambda}e^{ck/(2s)}\), which is below \(\dim W_k\ge\frac12e^{-5k^2/N}\binom sk\) as soon as \(e^{ck/(2s)}<8(M+1)\), that is

\[ c<\frac{2s}k\log\bigl(8(M+1)\bigr)=O_p(\sqrt{N\log N}). \]

Some nonzero \(f\in W_k\) would then lie in \(I_k(\Gamma_H)\subseteq\mathcal C_B(\Gamma_H)\), where \(\max(k,8)\le B=TD+k\) since \(k=\lceil\sqrt{N\Lambda}\rceil\ge8\) in this range, against the separated-space lemma. So (CH\(_\delta\)-hyp) cannot be met by the old relations alone: the block's inputs must contribute a head.

Random dense blocks

Choose \(M\) in advance, of size \(m=m^{(p)}_*\), in distinct rows of \(Y\); this is possible because \(Y\) has \(15\) coordinates in each of the \(N+1\) rows and \(m^{(p)}_*=O_p(\sqrt{N\log N})\). Consider a block whose \(h\) inputs are selectors \(1-L^\delta\) of independent uniform forms \(L=\sum a_ux_u\). Graph restriction and row projection replace the coefficient of a cell \(u\) by \(a'_u=a_u-a_{d(r_u)}\), where \(d(r_u)\) is the distinguished cell of \(u\)'s row. Since \(M\) meets each row at most once, the \(a'_u\), \(u\in M\), stay independent and uniform.

After multilinear reduction, the coefficient of \(\prod_{u\in S}x_u\), for a \(\delta\)-subset \(S\) of \(M\), in \(\Pi(1-L^\delta)\) is \(-\delta!\prod_{u\in S}a'_u=\prod_{u\in S}a'_u\), by Wilson's theorem, because only the term \(T=S\) of the expansion contributes to a squarefree monomial of this degree. So (CH\(_\delta\)-hyp) holds as soon as these projected vectors span \(\mathbb F_p^{\binom M\delta}\). They fail to span only if some nonzero \(B\) makes the multilinear polynomial \(\sum_SB_S\prod_{u\in S}a'_u\), of degree \(\delta\), vanish at all \(h\) samples. A nonzero multilinear polynomial of degree \(\delta\) vanishes at a uniform point of \(\mathbb F_p^m\) with probability at most \(\varepsilon_p=1-(1-1/p)^\delta\); this follows by induction, splitting off one variable at a time. A union bound over \(B\) gives failure probability at most \(p^{\binom m\delta}\varepsilon_p^h\le e^{-\Lambda}\) once

\[ h\ge\frac{\binom m\delta\ln p+\Lambda}{\ln(1/\varepsilon_p)} . \]

The factor \(\ln p/\ln(1/\varepsilon_p)\) is about \(3.05\) at \(p=5\) and \(3.85\) at \(p=7\). This number of inputs is \(\Theta_p((N\log N)^{\delta/2})\), against \(Q^{(p)}_*=O_p(N^{p-3/2}\sqrt{\log N})\). At \(p=5\) that is about \(N^2\log^2N\) instead of \(N^{3.5}\). At \(p=3\) it matches the ternary \(\Theta(N\log N)\), with a weaker constant than the ternary stratified count. The threshold is proved sufficient for the full-spanning route; a smaller \(h\) is not excluded, since \(\Pi(I_\delta)\) may already supply some subsets \(S\).

Scope

  • For random dense blocks the window at \(p\ge5\) narrows to \([R,\ c_p(N\log N)^{(p-1)/2}]\) in the number of inputs, as the ternary refinement narrowed it at \(p=3\). It is still far wider than at \(p=3\), and no window closes: the dyadic random inventory still has blocks in the window at every prime.
  • Common-factor blocks are not covered from the input side. In the recorded sunflower control \(q_{ij}=1-z^\delta-(y_i+y'_j)A-y_iy'_jB\), where \(z^\delta,A,B\) are polynomials in the coordinates of \(Z\) of degrees \(\delta,\delta-1,\delta-2\), and \(y_i,y'_j\) and \(Z\) lie in \(Y\), so \(\Pi\) fixes each input. Hence every degree-\(\delta\) monomial of every element of the span, before and after multilinearization, has at least \(\delta-2=p-3\ge1\) of its coordinates in \(Z\) at \(p\ge5\), and every \(\delta\)-subset \(S\subseteq M\setminus Z\) has coefficient zero throughout the input span. That alone does not refute (CH\(_\delta\)-hyp): \(S\) could still head a sum whose two parts cancel above \(S\), and this entry does not decide it. What the remark does give is that the old relations cannot supply every \(\delta\)-subset on their own, so such a block's inputs would have to head the sum through cancellation. These blocks stay open here and remain one-probe cases, as recorded.
  • Nothing here reaches the goal, which needs all window blocks at once.

Checks

clique_head_check.py checks the entry's countable steps exactly. For all \(1135\) admissible tuples with \(8\le s\le40\), \(m,k\le s/4\) and \(2\le\delta\le\min(m,6)\), the exact count \(J_{\le k}=\sum_{j\le k}\sum_{i<\delta}\binom mi\binom{s-m}{j-i}\) lies below Lemma CH\(_\delta\)'s bound, the largest ratio being \(0.479\); the closed form agrees with brute-force enumeration of all subsets on the smallest boards. For the vanishing bound, every nonzero homogeneous multilinear form of degree \(\delta\) in \(m\) variables is enumerated for five \((p,m,\delta)\) triples and sampled with deterministic seeds for five more: none vanishes at more than the fraction \(\varepsilon_p\) of \(\mathbb F_p^m\), and a single monomial attains \(\varepsilon_p\) in every case, so the test is tight and a wrong exponent would show. Möbius inversion of \(1-L^\delta\) on the cube confirms the Wilson coefficient \(\prod_{u\in S}a_u\) at \(p=3,5,7\), and a separate check confirms that the projection replaces \(a_u\) by \(a_u-a_{d(r_u)}\). These are finite checks of the counting and coefficient steps; the degree ledger and the kernel argument rest on the proof.

Assessment and next step

The clique-head refinement transcribes to every prime with one new constant, \(C_\delta\). The random-block count replaces the ternary quadratic-form zeros by a multilinear Schwartz–Zippel bound. With Theorems GCp and CHp, the statement set's \(p\ge5\) exclusions now parallel \(p=3\), with wider windows. This line of work, all-prime transcription, is complete. It narrows the random-inventory window at \(p\ge5\), as the ternary refinement did at \(p=3\), but closes no window at any prime, and the route item's missing implication is unchanged: a batched mechanism for many non-nested dense blocks.

Next step (odd-prime-clause-transfer): a route review of the window at every prime. It should weigh the statement set's restart conditions against what the all-prime criteria add: they fix the window's ends at every prime, but give no mechanism inside it. It should decide whether any line remains for the window, or whether the thread's work should now go to the write-up that awaits the user's decision.

Sheaf check

The weight is one section glued across blocks by dimension counting. A clique of heads makes a block's local condition act like an affine core of rank \(m\), at every prime. The gluing is unchanged.

Searches with tools/search-claims.py for clique heads at degree \(\delta\), for weight-order head selection, for multilinear Schwartz–Zippel spanning and for the reduction-image technique returned only those four records, all cited here. clique_head_check.py was run; all its checks pass. Correction: what the clique-head checks actually cover, and three clauses of Theorem CHp

22 September 2026 · Correction to the clique-head entry · The finite checks are narrower than its Checks section claimed; three proof clauses are added. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

What is corrected. A review of clique_head_check.py arrived after that entry was committed. It confirmed every function and every number, and found no error in Lemma CH\(_\delta\), Theorem CHp, the remark or the random-block count. It did show that the entry's Checks section describes the evidence more strongly than the runs support, and it asked for three clauses in the proofs. Both are recorded here; the earlier entry stands otherwise.

The checks are narrower than claimed

  • Over the whole sweep \(m,k\le s/4\le10\), so \(mk/(2s)\le s/32\le1.25\) and \(e^{-mk/(2s)}\ge e^{-1.25}\). The \(1135\) cases therefore exercise essentially the constant \(C_\delta\) only, whereas at the point of use \(m^{(p)}_*k/(2s)=5k^2/N+\Lambda+\log(C_\delta/2)\), about \(6\Lambda\). The sweep is a check of the constant, not of the exponential regime.
  • The sweep covers \(\delta\le6\), that is \(p\le7\), not every odd prime.
  • In the five sampled \(\varepsilon_p\) cases the extremal single monomial is appended to the sample by construction, so "attained" is not a finding there; attainment is a finding only in the five exhaustive cases, and "within bound" in the sampled cases is a random probe. The sharp value of \(\varepsilon_p\) for multilinear forms is the Alon–Füredi bound.
  • No case has \(\delta=p-1\) at \(p=7\); the on-parameter pairs tested are \((p,\delta)=(3,2)\) and \((5,4)\).
  • The enumerated forms are homogeneous of degree exactly \(\delta\). That is the case the random-block count uses, and it is the hypothesis under which \(\varepsilon_p\) is stated here.
  • The projection check compares two rearrangements of the same sum, so it tests the sign convention of \(a'_u=a_u-a_{d(r_u)}\), not the projection step itself.

Three clauses in the proofs

  • In the remark, the reduction multilinearizes each product \(\mu g\); the Boolean axioms lie in \(I_2(\Gamma_H)\subseteq I_k(\Gamma_H)\), so multilinearization stays inside \(I_k(\Gamma_H)\) and the image count, which counts multilinear monomials, applies.
  • The remark's deletion needs \(c\le m^{(p)}_*-\delta\) as well as \(c<(2s/k)\log(8(M+1))\). These are compatible: \(\log(8(M+1))=\Lambda-\log8\), so \(m^{(p)}_*-(2s/k)\log(8(M+1))\ge(2s/k)(5k^2/N+\log(4C_\delta))\), and \(\log(4C_\delta)\ge\log(16e^{-3/4})>2\) for \(\delta\ge2\), so the difference exceeds \(\delta\) in the range of use.
  • In the common-factor bullet, that \(y_i,y'_j\) and \(Z\) lie in \(Y\), so that \(\Pi\) fixes each input, is a condition the construction is chosen to satisfy; it is not part of Observation SH as recorded.

Sheaf check

Nothing glues here: this is a correction to an evidence description and three clauses of an existing argument.

Verification gate. The corrections come from a fresh-context reviewer briefed on the revised remark, the revised scope bullet and the script, with the dependency excerpts in a scratch file. Every item it required is recorded above; none strengthens a claim, and it confirmed the mathematics of the corrected entry. No new computation was run, and no claim metadata changes, since no new statement is made.

Restriction mixtures of endpoint designs reduce to one input count: the top-size lemma

22 September 2026 · Conditional result: an elementary lemma, applied under a typicality hypothesis · The mixture lead reduces to a one-count design problem and gives no mechanism for it. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The sheaf entry proposed mixtures \(\Lambda=\sum_\rho w_\rho\,\lambda_\rho\circ\mathrm{res}_\rho\) of pulled-back endpoint designs whose errors cancel. The Macaulay-ceiling entry found its simplest case vacuous, because elimination removes a single band block, and parked the lead until it could be tested against a thick inventory. The window's missing implication is one design for polynomially many window blocks with different input spans. Mixtures could supply something new only by using the sizes at which a window block is easy: dense below its band and low above it. The user asked for a short cycle on this lead. It tests whether a successful mixture on a thick inventory must still solve a window problem without help from any endpoint. The test ends with a reduction of that kind or with a mixture pattern that avoids it.

What the record already gives

If a component at size \(L\) handles a block \(b\), meaning that its pullback annihilates what \(b\) contributes, then only components at sizes in \(b\)'s band can carry errors on \(b\), and those errors must cancel among themselves. This is the band-cancellation condition in the sheaf entry's dyadic test. It holds for every block and needs no new lemma. What it leaves open is normalization: the band components' weights might sum to zero, so that each block is cancelled by a zero-sum combination while the total weight sits elsewhere. The lemma below rules this out for the blocks whose band starts at the largest size the mixture uses.

The top-size lemma

Let each component have a residual size \(|\rho|\) and a normalized local functional, \(\lambda_\rho(1)=1\), and let \(\sum_\rho w_\rho=1\). Put \(W(L)=\sum_{|\rho|=L}w_\rho\), let \(\mathcal L=\{L:W(L)\ne0\}\), which is nonempty, and let \(L_{\max}=\max\mathcal L\). Let \(U\) be a subspace of polynomials and \(I\) a set of sizes with \(L_{\max}\in I\), \(I\cap\mathcal L=\{L_{\max}\}\), and such that every component with \(|\rho|\notin I\) has a pullback annihilating \(U\). If \(\Lambda\) annihilates \(U\), then \[ \Lambda_I=W(L_{\max})^{-1}\sum_{|\rho|\in I}w_\rho\,\lambda_\rho\circ\mathrm{res}_\rho \] is normalized and annihilates \(U\), together with every subspace that all the pullbacks annihilate.

Proof. The sizes in \(I\) other than \(L_{\max}\) have \(W=0\), so \(\Lambda_I(1)=W(L_{\max})^{-1}\sum_{L\in I}W(L)=1\). For \(u\in U\), the components outside \(I\) vanish on \(u\), so \(0=\Lambda(u)=W(L_{\max})\Lambda_I(u)\). The last clause holds because \(\Lambda_I\) is a combination of the components. \(\square\)

The lemma is elementary linear algebra. Its only content beyond band cancellation is that the size-\(L_{\max}\) components carry nonzero total weight, and the components at the other sizes in \(I\) have zero total weight at each size.

Application to a thick inventory

Write \(n\) for the board size, \(L\) for a residual size and \(\Lambda_M=\log(64(M+1))\) for the criterion's count parameter, where \(M\) is the number of blocks. Take as components the sheaf entry's local sections: at residual size \(L\), a design that annihilates the residual closure through \(D\) of the source without its band blocks, those whose projected rank at that restriction lies strictly between \(R(L)=L/(4.4\times10^7)\) and the dense end \(Q(L)\). Here \(Q(L)\) is an integer threshold at or above which the clique extension handles a tuple. The recorded value for random tuples is about \(1.6\times10^4L\Lambda_M\) (the dyadic band). Fix \(Q\) at every size \(2\le L\le n\) so that \(Q(L)-Q(L-1)\ge1\) and \(Q(L-1)>R(L)\). The linear threshold \(1.6\times10^4L\Lambda_M\) satisfies both at every size. Designs exist only above the nonvacuity threshold \(L\ge4\times10^{18}\Lambda_M\).

The calibration inventory has \(n\) independent tuples of \(h\) uniform random forms for every integer \(h\le Q(n)\). That is about \(1.6\times10^4\Lambda_Mn^2\) blocks, polynomially many. Write \(B_h\) for the tuples with \(h\) forms. The application assumes the following.

(T) At every component used, at size \(L\), each tuple of \(B_h\) with \(h\ge Q(L)\) has projected rank at least \(Q(L)\).

The low side needs no hypothesis, because the rank is at most \(h\). For one fixed restriction, (T) holds with high probability, since restriction leaves the coefficients uniform (the two-size control). The mixture's restrictions may be chosen after the inventory and may be exponentially many, however, and the recorded failure bound, about \(e^{-\Lambda_M}\) per restriction, admits no union bound over such a family. So (T) is an unproved hypothesis, and everything below is conditional on it.

Take \(h\) an integer with \(Q(L_{\max}-1)\le h<Q(L_{\max})\); it exists because \(Q(L_{\max})-Q(L_{\max}-1)\ge1\), and it lies in the inventory because \(h<Q(L_{\max})\le Q(n)\). Let \(I=\{L:R(L)<h<Q(L)\}\). Then \(L_{\max}\in I\), because \(h\ge Q(L_{\max}-1)>R(L_{\max})\), and no size \(L\le L_{\max}-1\) is in \(I\), because \(Q(L)\le Q(L_{\max}-1)\le h\). Hence \(I\cap\mathcal L=\{L_{\max}\}\). Let \(U=C_D(\Gamma+B_h)\), the degree-\(D\) PC closure of the old base \(\Gamma\) with the blocks of \(B_h\).

A component with \(|\rho|\notin I\) has every tuple of \(B_h\) outside its band: below \(R\) automatically, above \(Q\) by (T). Its design therefore annihilates the residual closure of \(\Gamma|_\rho\) with \(B_h|_\rho\). Restriction maps a degree-\(D\) derivation to a residual derivation of the same degree, so \(F\in C_D(\Gamma+B_h)\) implies \(F|_\rho\in C_D((\Gamma+B_h)|_\rho)\). This is the pullback step of the sheaf entry. So the pullback annihilates \(U\). A successful PC mixture annihilates \(C_D\) of the whole source, which contains \(U\).

Conclusion, under (T). Every normalized restriction mixture of these endpoint designs that annihilates the source's closure through \(D\) contains a normalized sub-mixture \(\Lambda_I\) that is a degree-\(D\) PC design for \(\Gamma+B_h\), where \(h\) is determined by the largest size used. The design is for the \(n\) random tuples of one input count, and no component of \(\Lambda_I\) is required to handle \(B_h\). Only components outside \(I\) are guaranteed to handle it, and those do not enter \(\Lambda_I\).

What this does to the lead

Under (T), the mixture lead on this inventory reduces to the one-count problem: build a PC design for the old base plus \(n\) independent random window tuples of one input count, as a combination of designs that are not required to handle them. The one-count problem is a special case of the window problem, whose general form has polynomially many different input spans, so it may be easier. Nothing recorded solves it. The lemma asserts that the sub-mixture exists; it does not construct it. This does not refute mixtures. My judgment is that mixtures contribute no mechanism for this problem and that the lead adds no leverage beyond it, and it stays parked with that problem as its restart condition. The sheaf entry's claim that unconstrained mixtures restate the problem is not used here. It needs the empty restriction, or \(S^\perp\subseteq W\), and the sub-mixture here uses only endpoint designs at sizes in \(I\).

Besides (T) and the conditions on \(Q\), the reduction needs only one inventory feature: for the largest size \(L_{\max}\) that the mixture uses, some input count \(h\) with \(Q(L_{\max}-1)\le h<Q(L_{\max})\) must carry \(n\) tuples. A sparser inventory, such as the dyadic one, can miss that interval, and then this argument says nothing. The dyadic inventory is already handled by elimination.

Verification gate. Re-read from the notebook: the sheaf entry's mixture criterion (MX), the pullback argument and the dyadic test with its band-cancellation display; the dyadic band paragraph of the clique entry; and the Macaulay-ceiling entry's dyadic paragraph and quick error-cancellation check. My claim searches covered restriction mixtures, cancellation, sheaf, localization, pullback designs and the thick dyadic calibration, and the reviewer ran one for mixture restriction cancellation localization. None records this lemma. A narrowly briefed fresh-context reviewer found the first draft's lemma correct but its induction redundant, since separation is needed only at the largest size, and found its conclusions overstated. It required the following, all adopted. A second focused pass on the strengthened PC step confirmed it under (T) and required small additions, also adopted: the in-inventory check for \(h\), \(Q\) fixed at every size, and "not required to handle" in place of an unproved in-band claim. The first pass required:

  • separate the recorded band cancellation from the lemma's only new content, normalization at the top size;
  • take \(U\) to be the PC closure, with the restriction-of-derivations step, so that the conclusion is a PC design;
  • weaken the hypothesis (T) to the dense side and make the application conditional on it;
  • drop "restates the problem" and "as hard as the window";
  • state the lead's closure as a judgment;
  • fix \(Q\) exactly, with unit gap \(\ge1\) and \(Q(L-1)>R(L)\);
  • remove a misplaced elimination remark;
  • rename the clashing symbols.

No computation was run, since no finite size is nonvacuous: the criterion needs \(L\ge4\times10^{18}\Lambda_M\).

Family compatibility through affine conditioning: a wide-conditioning conjecture and its quadratic ceiling

22 September 2026 · Route review of the \(p\)-complex family line, with a conjecture, a counting ceiling and a control · The family question is reduced, not answered. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The \(p\)-complex line gives designs that extend under wide conditions: the amplitude theorem, the two-form lift, the one-predicate theorem and the ternary pair theorem. The three-selector control refuted assembling them from pairs, but only for the stronger aim of extending every functional that satisfies the active equations. The window needs one normalized design for polynomially many blocks. The user asked for a short cycle on family compatibility. This cycle states the family target as existence and tests its most direct family form: one affine conditioning that serves every block. It ends with the reach of that form, compared with polynomially many window blocks.

The target is existence

In the three-selector control, the forms \(a,b,a+b\) are all nonzero exactly when \(a=b\ne0\). The control's own degree-two design \(\lambda_{1,1}\) gives \(q_1,q_2,q_3\) the values \(0,0,1-4=0\) in \(\mathbb F_3\), so it is a design for the triple, though only through degree two. The compiler needs \(4p-1=11\), and existence there is not shown. The control therefore refutes extension of the signed functional \(\mu\), not the existence of a family design. Family compatibility should be asked as existence: given a family of blocks, does some normalized design annihilate the closure through the required degree?

The transversal special case of Lemma K

The recorded constant-row clamp (Lemma K) substitutes constants for the coefficient rows of complete first-level blocks, over any prime. The substitution maps each product \(P_b\) to \(Q_b=\prod_u(1-\lambda_{b,u})\), with \(\lambda_{b,u}\) in the block's span. So the blocks have no degree-\(D\) PC refutation if the old base with the axioms \(g_{b,i}Q_b\) has none. A transversal is the choice, in each block \(b\) of the weak-base compiler, of one input \(L_b^*=L_{b,i^*(b)}\). The special case sets \(r_{b,i^*}\mapsto1\) and the other coefficients \(\mapsto0\). This assumes the ordinary compiler, without the optional rank-one bridge; with the bridge and \(r\mapsto0\), the axiom \(LP\) becomes \(L\), a further conditioning. Then \(Q_b=(L_b^*)^{p-1}\), and the companion images are \(g_{b,i}(L_b^*)^{p-1}\), each saying "\(L_b^*=0\) or \(L_{b,i}\ne0\)". The stronger system \(\{L_b^*=0\}\) derives every such image at degree \(2p-2\le D\). So a degree-\(D\) refutation of the source gives one of the old base plus \(\{L_b^*=0\}\). This step is lossy: a design for the affine conditioning gives a design for the source, but not conversely. Neither completeness of the blocks nor any PHP property is used.

So a transversal whose affine conditioning keeps the base hard at \(D=4p-1\) excludes the whole inventory. Up to linear rank this is no gain over the record. The affine-flat conditioning theorem gives only a certificate-or-hardness dichotomy: for the full functional base with \(N\ge2B-1\) and \(\tau=(p-1)r\le B/2\), either a Nullstellensatz refutation through \(\tau\) or none in PC through \(D\) with \(D+\tau\le B\). No transversal is shown to fall on the good side. The recorded linear exceptional-lines theorem and the bottom-count lift, whose reach is linear in the number of distinct bottom input spans, already cover linearly many blocks directly.

A conjecture beyond linear rank, and a control

Work modulo the row equations. A linear part is \(\sum_i\sum_jf_i(j)X_{ij}\), each \(f_i\) defined up to a constant. It is active on row \(i\) when \(f_i\) is nonconstant, and \(Q\)-robust there when \(f_i\) differs from every constant on more than \(Q\) labels.

The wide-conditioning conjecture. For each odd \(p\) and each \(D\) there are \(t\) and \(Q\) with the following property. Take the ordinary unary PHP base and an affine system whose linear parts are independent modulo the rows. If every nonzero coefficient combination of those linear parts is \(Q\)-robust on at least \(t\) rows, the base plus the system has no degree-\(D\) PC refutation. The only rank bound is the automatic \(d_t\) below.

The recorded results give special cases only at their own parameters. For one form the one-predicate theorem with \(A=\{\alpha\}\) needs \(t\ge2B-1\) and robustness through \(3B-1\), on the functional base. For two forms the two-form lift needs \(2d+2p-1\) active rows and robustness through \(3d+3p-1\) deletions, for every direction of the pencil over the algebraic closure. The three-selector control uses the two-form case only at degree two. Many forms would need an \(r\)-parameter lift. The projective proof does not port: the topological entry notes \(H^2(\mathbf P^2,\mathcal O(-3))\ne0\) in characteristic three. The conjecture is a statement about affine systems, not about sources. It does not exclude refutations of PHP itself, so completeness does not bear on it.

Width alone is not enough. Take the column occupancies \(C_j=\sum_iX_{ij}\) and the system \(C_j=1\) for \(j<N\). Its linear parts are independent modulo rows. A combination \(\sum_{j<N}c_jC_j\) has row function \(c_j\) on \(j<N\) and \(0\) at \(N\), which is nonconstant on every row unless \(c=0\). So the system has the largest possible width, \(N+1\). Yet the row equations give \(C_N=2\) at degree one. Booleanity and the collisions give \(C_N^2-C_N\in I_2\), and \[ C_N(C_N-2)-(C_N^2-C_N)+(C_N-2)=-2 \] is a nonzero constant for odd \(p\). That is a degree-two refutation. Robustness fails here: \(\sum_{j<N}C_j\) has row function \(1_{j<N}\), one label from constant, and each single \(C_j\) is non-robust too. The recorded forced-cells lemma made the same point with a thin rank-one equation; this control shows that width does not rescue it.

The quadratic ceiling of the width hypothesis

Dimension bound. The linear parts modulo rows form a space of dimension \(\mathcal D=(N+1)(N-1)\). Those supported on a fixed set of \(t-1\) rows form a subspace of dimension \((t-1)(N-1)\). A span \(V\) whose nonzero elements are all active on at least \(t\) rows meets that subspace only in zero, so \[ \dim V\le d_t=(N+2-t)(N-1)<N^2. \]

Random blocks. Consider \(M\) blocks with at most \(h\le N^{O(1)}\) inputs each, where inputs of different blocks are independent and uniform modulo the rows. Independence within a block is not used. This is the model of the dyadic and thick calibrations. A transversal whose span satisfies the width hypothesis lies in some \(d_t\)-dimensional subspace. There are at most \(2p^{d_t(\mathcal D-d_t)}\) such subspaces and \(h^M\) transversals, and a fixed transversal lies in a fixed subspace with probability \(p^{-M(\mathcal D-d_t)}\). Hence the probability that some transversal satisfies the width-\(t\) hypothesis, for \(t\ge2\), is at most \[ 2h^Mp^{-(M-d_t)(t-1)(N-1)}, \] which is negligible once \(M\ge(1+c\log_ph/N)\,d_t\) for a suitable constant \(c\). The robustness parameter plays no role here.

What the ceiling says. The conjecture, even if true, certifies no transversal for an inventory of about \(d_t<N^2\) or more random blocks. With \(N^3\) random window blocks, polynomially many, it certifies nothing. The ceiling does not show that the conditioned base is refutable, or that no transversal or other constant substitution gives a design. Lemma K's general substitutions give non-affine conditionings, \(g_{b,i}Q_b\), which this count does not cover. It limits a sufficient condition, not the mechanism.

What this does to the family line

This cycle has reduced the family question for transversal designs; it has not answered it. Below linear rank the reduction adds nothing to the record. Beyond it, the natural hypothesis is the wide-conditioning conjecture. That conjecture is unproved even at constant degree, and its width condition stops certifying transversals below \(N^2\) random blocks. The remaining family designs are these:

  • Lemma K's non-affine substitutions, for which the record's hypothesis is Question H with density \(M2^{-h}\) over \(\mathbb F_2\);
  • mixtures of substitution designs;
  • the \(p\)-complex's moment corrections applied block by block.

Combining them is the gluing problem, which the three-selector control and the top-size lemma leave without a mechanism. My assessment is that the \(p\)-complex stays a local correction tool, not a batching mechanism for polynomially many window blocks. The wide-conditioning conjecture is recorded for its own sake. If true, it would give quadratic reach, beyond the recorded linear endpoints, but still not the goal.

Route review of the \(p\)-complex family line

The line's general claim. The \(p\)-complex's local extension theorems assemble into one normalized design for every polynomial inventory of complete selector blocks, at the compiler's degree \(4p-1\). What the goal needs from it is that assembly for polynomially many window blocks with different input spans, on the ordinary unary base.

Falsification attempt. This cycle tried the most direct assembly: one affine conditioning that serves every block. Up to linear rank it adds nothing to the record. Beyond that it needs the unproved wide-conditioning conjecture, and width is necessary but not sufficient, as the column control shows. The conjecture's width hypothesis cannot certify any transversal for about \(N^2\) or more random blocks. The earlier three-selector control refutes assembling extensions pair by pair. Every other assembly is the gluing problem.

Assessment of this line only. Weak as a route to the goal. The line proved genuine local theorems: exactness, and one-form, two-form and pair lifts. Its three family forms, however, have each met a recorded limit or remain unproved: extension from pairs (refuted), common affine conditioning (conjectural and capped below \(N^2\)), and block-by-block correction (the gluing problem). No recorded ingredient scales with the number of blocks, and the window needs exactly that. The line remains a source of local tools.

Next step, on the highest-risk item (odd-prime-clause-transfer). Do not open a further \(p\)-complex cycle unless it comes with an \(r\)-parameter lift or a gluing mechanism that uses the block count. The thread-level decision is the statement set's choice, which awaits the user: park the thread, assign Lean work on the transfer, or bring a new idea for the window. The wide-conditioning conjecture could be tested at constant degree on small robust systems as a side question. It does not address the window.

Verification gate. Re-read from the notebooks: the amplitude theorem, the two-form lift, the one-predicate theorem and its source-interface section, the ternary pair theorem's assessment, and the three-selector control with its design \(\lambda_{\alpha,\beta}\). Also the working context's compiler summary, the affine-flat conditioning theorem, and the zero-substitution theorem. My claim searches covered transversal and zero substitution, common affine restriction, wide affine systems, safe systems over \(\mathbb F_p\) and point conditioning. A narrowly briefed fresh-context reviewer confirmed the substitution proof, the control's arithmetic for every odd \(p\), the dimension bound and the union bound. It required the following, all adopted:

  • label the reduction a special case of the recorded Lemma K, which I had missed, and note that it is lossy;
  • restrict "point designs" to transversal affine conditioning;
  • restate the ceiling as a limit of the conjectured hypothesis rather than of the mechanism;
  • drop "settled in both directions";
  • state the affine-flat result as a dichotomy for the functional base, and cite the bottom-count lift;
  • require independent linear parts in the conjecture;
  • give the one- and two-form special cases their actual parameters;
  • state the degree of the three-selector design;
  • sharpen the threshold to about \(d_t\);
  • note the unused hypotheses and the rank-one bridge;
  • shorten the status line.

These corrections weaken or rescope, so no second pass was run. No computation was run: the control is a hand refutation, and the ceiling is a count.

Random affine conditioning of unary PHP: quadratic thresholds that fit a dimension law, and the one-count problem

22 September 2026 · Finite check (\(D=2,3\), \(n\le10\)) and conjecture · The one-count problem reduces to a random-conditioning law. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The top-size lemma reduced restriction mixtures to the one-count problem: a degree-\(D\) PC design, \(D=4p-1\), for the base plus \(m\) independent random window tuples of one input count. The family review noted the transversal special case of the recorded constant-row clamp. Choosing one input per tuple reduces any inventory whose inputs are independent and uniform to PHP plus \(m\) uniformly random affine equations: if that system has no degree-\(D\) refutation, neither has the source. The recorded weight mechanism, the affine-flat conditioning theorem, reaches only rank about \(n/(4(p-1))\), because a weight supported on the solution flat has degree \((p-1)m\). The one-count problem with \(n\) tuples needs rank \(n\). The missing implication tested here is whether random conditioning keeps PHP hard up to linear rank or beyond. Its answer fixes the reach of the transversal mechanism for random inventories. The test ends at exact thresholds on boards large enough to separate linear from quadratic growth.

The computation

Work over \(\mathbb F_3\) in the multilinear ring on the \(n(n+1)\) cells of ordinary weak unary \(\mathrm{PHP}^{n+1}_n\). The generators are the row equations \(\sum_jX_{ij}-1\) and the column collisions \(X_{ij}X_{i'j}\). Add \(M\) affine equations with every coefficient and constant uniform in \(\mathbb F_3\). The degree-\(D\) PC closure is computed exactly by the closure routine of the ternary conservativity tester, run on multilinear monomials. For each seed one random sequence of equations is fixed, and bisection over its prefixes finds the least refuted \(M\); refutability is monotone in nested prefixes. At every listed \((n,D)\), PHP alone is not refuted, so the thresholds are nonvacuous.

Two predictions were on the table. The weight mechanism guarantees only linear rank, so a threshold growing linearly in \(n\) would leave the one-count problem out of reach. The wide-conditioning conjecture asserts hardness when every combination is \(Q\)-robustly active on at least some \(t\) rows. With the choice \(t=2D+1\) suggested by the family review, a random span keeps that width up to rank about \((n+2-t)(n-1)-\log_3\binom{n+1}{t-1}\): a union over row sets makes some set fail about \(\log_3\binom{n+1}{2D}\) equations before the generic count. The space of linear parts modulo rows has dimension \((n+1)(n-1)\). Recorded context: the bit-encoding Conjecture H1 conjectures PC degree at least \(c\min(n,\dim W/\ell)\) for a uniformly random affine subspace \(W\), with an elementary projection upper bound \(\lceil\dim W/\ell\rceil+O(1)\). The random-flat avoidance corollary proves hardness for \(M\le N/8\) random binary flats of logarithmic codimension.

At \(n=4\), degree three already refutes PHP alone, which matches the formula's value \(n+1-2D<0\) there.

What the thresholds show

  • Quadratic, not linear. At \(D=2\) the mean threshold grows as \(1,4.6,10.5,17.75,27,37,50,64\) for \(n=3,\dots,10\). Its second differences average about \(1.6\), consistent with the formula's \(2\). Every least refuted \(M\) lies between \(0\) and \(2\) above \((n+1-2D)(n-1)+1\), never below, at both degrees. The formula is met exactly at \(n=3\), in two \(n=4\) seeds, at \(n=10\) (all at \(D=2\)), and in one \(n=5\), \(D=3\) seed. At these sizes the weight mechanism's linear rank is not the limit of random conditioning.
  • Some row set against every row set. The projection of the flat \(A\) onto the coordinates of a row set \(T\) is onto exactly when no nonzero combination in the span is supported on \(T\). The width column therefore records when projection first fails for some set of \(2D\) rows, and the formula when it must fail for every such set. The first comes about \(\log_3\binom{n+1}{2D}\) earlier: that predicts \(58.7\) at \(n=10\), where \(58\) is observed. Refutation lags the first thin combination by \(2\) to \(9\) equations at \(D=2\) and by \(0\) to \(5\) at \(D=3\); one \(n=5\), \(D=3\) seed has both at \(M=1\). So at these sizes one or a few thin combinations do not refute. With \(t=2D+1\), the minimum-width hypothesis fails earlier than hardness does, by a lower-order \(O(D\log n)\) term. The data bear on the conjecture only under that choice of \(t\), and not on its robustness condition. The direction is sound: support on at most \(2D\) rows falsifies the hypothesis.
  • A dimension heuristic fits. The thresholds sit where the solution flat \(A\), of dimension \((n+1)(n-1)-M\) modulo rows, falls below \(2D(n-1)\). Below that dimension, projection onto a set of \(2D\) rows, whose coordinates have dimension \(2D(n-1)\), cannot be onto for any row set. This is a heuristic prediction: the projection count proves nothing about refutability. At \(M=0\) it predicts that PHP alone survives degree \(D\) while \(2D\le n+1\), consistent with Razborov's lower bound of about \(n/2+1\). The data confirm this only at \(n=3,4,5\). In this form each \(n-1\) random equations lower the refutation degree by about one half. It is the unary analogue of H1's projection bound, with each row contributing \(n-1\) coordinates in place of \(\ell\) bits, and here both sides fit, with constant \(1/2\).

The random-conditioning law (conjecture). Over \(\mathbb F_p\), let \(A\) be the solution flat of \(M\) independent uniformly random affine equations, of dimension \(a=(n+1)(n-1)-M\) modulo rows. With high probability the ordinary unary PHP base plus these equations has no degree-\(D\) PC refutation when \(a\ge2D(n-1)+c\), and has one when \(a\le2D(n-1)-c'\), for constants \(c,c'\) independent of \(n\). Over \(\mathbb F_3\) at \(D=2,3\) the data fit it with a hardness offset of \(0\) to \(2\): no margin is measured on the hardness side. Only the hardness side matters here. The law refines H1 in the ordinary unary encoding. The law is checked at small \(n\) and fixed \(D\) only. Its constants may depend on \(D\) and \(p\), and the boards are far below the degree \(4p-1\) at which it would be used.

What it gives, and what it does not

Suppose the law holds at \(D=4p-1\) for the relevant \(p\). Choose, by a fixed rule, one input per tuple, uniform over all affine forms on the \(n(n+1)\) cells with a uniform constant and independent across tuples. The transversal substitution sends a degree-\(D\) refutation of the source to one of PHP plus the \(m\) chosen equations: each substituted companion \(g_{b,i}(L_b^*)^{p-1}\) is \(L_b^*\) times a polynomial of degree \(2p-3\), derivable within degree \(2p-2\le D\). So with high probability over such an inventory, the one-count problem reduces to the law with \(m\) up to about \((n+1-2D)(n-1)\) less its constant. At \(p=3\), \(D=11\), that includes \(m=n\) once \(n\) exceeds about \(23\) plus the law's unknown constants. The same holds with high probability for any inventory of at most about \(n^2-2Dn\) blocks whose chosen inputs have this distribution, window or not.

It does not reach polynomially many blocks. The transversal system's rank is at most the dimension \((n+1)(n-1)\), and the quadratic ceiling already caps every point design of this kind. An inventory of \(n^3\) random window blocks, or the thick inventory with about \(1.6\times10^4\Lambda_Mn^2\) blocks, is beyond it. For those, a block's clause must be used as a clause, not replaced by one of its equations. Lemma K's non-affine constant substitutions, for example all coefficients equal to one, turn a block into the degree-\(2(p-1)\) constraints \(g_i\sum_{j\ne i}g_j=0\) rather than an equation. They are not capped by the dimension count, and they are the natural next object.

Assessment and next step

The one-count problem is reduced to the random-conditioning law, which has consistent small-board evidence over \(\mathbb F_3\) at \(D\le3\) and a precise form refining H1. Its constants may depend on \(D\) and \(p\), and it is untested near \(D=11\). The law is not on the critical path: even proved, transversals reach at most about \(n^2\) random blocks, and the goal needs polynomially many. Larger boards would sharpen its constants without moving the general implication, so none are planned.

The last three cycles share a pattern. Every mechanism that removes the blocks' fresh variables by substitution lands in a fixed old design space. Constant substitutions, transversals and point designs are all of this kind. The dimension of that space is about \(n^{O(Ds)}\) for substitution degree \(s\), and generic blocks consume it. The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer is the general statement behind this pattern, not more cases. One outcome is a capacity theorem: every substitution design of degree \(s\) handles at most \(n^{O(Ds)}\) generic window blocks, whatever the substitution. The other is a construction whose substitution degree grows with the inventory's polynomial degree, stays within PHP's degree barrier and keeps the companion images in the old ideal. The first would be an obstruction covering every substitution-based mechanism at once. The second is the missing mechanism.

Process. Two points. First, predicting the threshold before the runs, and computing each sample's actual width drop, located the width hypothesis as a lower-order \(O(D\log n)\) correction to the dimension count, where a single confirmation would have missed it. Second, the first \(n=7\), \(D=3\) run was launched single-threaded, with no time estimate and with collision monomials kept as columns. It was replaced by an exact reduced, incremental and parallel driver, about 8 times faster on the validation sizes. The launcher now requires an estimate and parallel threads for long runs.

Evidence. research/results/odd_prime_one_count_20260922/: random_conditioning.py, random_conditioning_fast.py (the collision quotient, incremental closure and OpenMP elimination; its fast_*.json outputs reproduce the plain thresholds) and width_drop.py, with seeds \(1000n+10D+s\), and every threshold_n*_D*.json, fast_n*_D*.json and width_n*_D*.json. The first \(n=7\), \(D=3\) run was interrupted and has no result file. Run each through the protected launcher with --n --D --seeds --out.

Substitution designs are not capped at a fixed polynomial: a capacity count and the partial-prefix conjecture

22 September 2026 · Heuristic count, one calibration check and a conjecture · The proposed capacity statement would not obstruct; partial prefixes are the construction to test. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The random-conditioning entry proposed a general statement behind its last three cycles. After substitution, a design lives in a fixed old design space of dimension about \(n^{O(Ds)}\), so every substitution design of degree \(s\) might handle only \(n^{O(Ds)}\) generic blocks. The missing implication is a mechanism for polynomially many window blocks. This cycle asks whether that capacity statement would be an obstruction or points to a construction. It ends with a count that settles which, and with the construction's precise form.

A correction to the framing

The \(n^2\) ceiling of the family review concerns the strengthened system \(\{L_b^*=0\}\). An affine system has rank at most \((n+1)(n-1)\), so it caps at about \(n^2\) blocks. The images that Lemma K's substitution actually produces are weaker. For the transversal they are \(g_{b,i}(L_b^*)^{p-1}\), \(i\ne i^*\): "\(L_b^*=0\), or every other input of the block is nonzero". These are clause-like, not affine, and no rank bound applies to them. The ceiling limits the strengthened conditioning, not substitution.

The capacity count

Write \(d_k=\dim\big(P_{\le k}/C_k(\Gamma)\big)\) for the degree-\(k\) quotient of the ordinary weak base, so a degree-\(D\) design is a functional on a space of dimension \(d_D\). A constraint polynomial \(c\) of degree \(e\) imposes the conditions \(\Lambda(mc)=0\) for \(\deg m\le D-e\), at most \(d_{D-e}\) of them. If the constraints of different blocks behave generically, \(M\) blocks with \(q\) constraint polynomials of degree \(e\) each exhaust the design space near \[ M\approx\frac{d_D}{q\,d_{D-e}}. \tag{CC} \] Since \(d_k\) grows like \(n^{2k}/k!\) while \(k\ll n\), (CC) is about \((D-e)!\,n^{2e}/(D!\,q)\). This is a heuristic: it assumes independence of constraints, and it ignores derivable clauses, which cost nothing, and forced contradictions, which cost everything.

Calibration against the measured law. For affine equations, \(q=1\) and \(e=1\), and (CC) is \(d_D/d_{D-1}\). One exact computation gives the quotient dimensions in the collision quotient:

\(D\)\(n\)\(d_{D-1}\)\(d_D\)\(d_D/d_{D-1}\)Measured law \((n+1-2D)(n-1)+1\)
24, 5, 6, 716, 25, 36, 4976, 220, 498, 9734.75, 8.8, 13.8, 19.94, 9, 16, 25
28, 9, 1064, 81, 1001720, 2826, 439026.9, 34.9, 43.936, 49, 64
35, 6, 7220, 498, 973656, 3067, 96613.0, 6.2, 9.91, 6, 13

The count has the measured quadratic growth, but its constant is off. The ratio of threshold to count is \(0.84,1.02,1.16,1.26,1.34,1.40,1.46\) at \(D=2\), \(n=4,\dots,10\), and \(0.34,0.97,1.31\) at \(D=3\), \(n=5,6,7\). It is still rising, and to leading order it tends to \(D\): (CC) is about \(n^2/D\), while the law is about \(n^2\). At the smallest boards the count lies above the law. One guess for the shortfall is that different equations' multiples overlap, which (CC) ignores; it is untested. (CC) is an order-of-magnitude guide for growth in \(n\), with an unknown constant factor.

What the count says about substitution

Take the transversal images at \(p=3\): \(q=h-1\) constraints of degree \(e=2(p-1)=4\). Then (CC) is about \(n^{8}/h\), far above the affine \(n^2\), though still a fixed polynomial. More generally, a substitution whose product image \(Q_b=1-\sum_j\beta_{b,j}g_{b,j}\) has degree \(s'\) gives constraints \(g_{b,i}Q_b\) of degree \(e=p-1+s'\), and (CC) is about \(n^{2(p-1+s')}/h\). The capacity rises with \(s'\) without bound. An inventory of \(n^K\) generic window blocks is within the count once \(s'\) is about \(K/2\), a constant. If the substituted coefficients \(\beta\) have degree \(\delta\), a line of degree at most \(D\) in the old variables and the \(r\)'s becomes one of degree at most \(D\max(1,\delta)\). The images are new axioms of degree \(e\). The substituted refutation therefore has degree at most \(\max(D\max(1,\delta),e)\): a constant, far below PHP's degree barrier of about \(n/2\).

So the capacity statement proposed last cycle, "every substitution design of degree \(s\) handles at most \(n^{O(Ds)}\) generic blocks", would not be an obstruction even if proved: \(s\) may be chosen as a constant depending on the inventory's exponent. Counting does not rule out substitution designs for polynomial inventories. It does not show that they work either. Non-generic behaviour, derivable clauses, and low-degree contradictions forced by one block's images together with PHP all remain possible obstructions. The question is whether suitable substitutions exist whose images behave generically.

The partial-prefix construction

For a block \(b\) and a set \(S_b\) of \(k\) of its inputs, substitute the exact prefix on \(S_b\) alone: \(\beta_{b,j}=\prod_{l\in S_b,\,l<j}(1-g_{b,l})\) for \(j\in S_b\), and \(\beta_{b,j}=0\) otherwise. Then \(Q_b=\prod_{j\in S_b}(1-g_{b,j})=\prod_{j\in S_b}L_{b,j}^{p-1}\), of degree \((p-1)k\), and the images are \[ g_{b,i}\prod_{j\in S_b}L_{b,j}^{p-1}\quad(i\notin S_b):\qquad\text{"if an input outside }S_b\text{ is zero, one in }S_b\text{ is zero".} \] The case \(k=h\) is the exact prefix, which leaves no constraints but costs degree \((p-1)h\). The case \(k=1\) is the transversal, whose \(\beta\) are constants. The field images \(\beta^p-\beta\) vanish modulo Booleanity: \(L^p=L\), so each \(L^{p-1}\) and each product of them is idempotent. Here \(\delta=(p-1)(k-1)\) and \(e=(p-1)(k+1)\). By Lemma K, a degree-\(D\) refutation of the source gives one of \(\Gamma\) plus the images of degree at most \(B_k=\max\big(D\max(1,(p-1)(k-1)),(p-1)(k+1)\big)\). The compiler degree is \(D=4p-1\), from the weak-base compiler.

The partial-prefix capacity conjecture. For each odd \(p\) and \(K\) there is \(k\), independent of \(n\) and of the block widths, with the following property. Take \(M\le n^K\) blocks of widths \(h_b\), with \(k<h_b\le n^{O(1)}\). Draw every input of every block independently as \(\sum_{ij}c_{ij}X_{ij}+c_0\), with all coefficients uniform in \(\mathbb F_p\). Take \(S_b\) to be the first \(k\) inputs of block \(b\), a rule fixed before sampling. Then, with probability tending to one as \(n\to\infty\), the ordinary unary base plus the partial-prefix images has no PC refutation of degree \(B_k\) with \(D=4p-1\). By (CC) one expects \(k\) of about \(K/(2(p-1))-1\), that is \(k=O(K/p)\). The width regime matters: for bounded widths the exact prefix already gives constant degree \(D(p-1)h\), and the conjecture would say nothing new. Its content is for widths that grow with \(n\), as window blocks do, where \(h=\Theta(n)\).

The conjecture uses the size, as a sufficient condition must: \(k\) grows with \(K\), and exponentially many blocks exceed every fixed capacity. That is consistent with the exponential refutations that completeness guarantees. It concerns random inventories, the calibration for the window, not arbitrary ones. The goal-level statement would add: for every inventory of at most \(n^K\) blocks, some choice of the subsets \(S_b\) keeps the images hard. That is stronger and untested.

Can it be tested?

At \(p=3\) the images have degree \(e=2(k+1)\ge4\). A test at degree \(D\ge e+1=5\) is nonvacuous only for refuting the images themselves, a weaker statement than the conjecture, which concerns the substituted degree \(B_k\). Even that needs PHP hard at degree 5, so \(n\ge9\). In the collision quotient that is about \(\binom{9}{5}10^5\approx1.3\times10^7\) columns: not feasible with dense elimination. The binary analogue is already on record. The random-clause Nullstellensatz check (check:unary-avoidance-ns-spaces) computed exact spaces over \(\mathbb F_2\) for the functional unary base with random clauses of \(h\le3\) parities, at degrees two to four on six to eight holes. Every clause added the predicted dimension increment, 1 entered only at exhaustion, and the recorded PC jumps were the forced falls. It confirmed the predicted Nullstellensatz dimension increments, not (CC)'s block-count threshold. That is consistent with the independence assumption behind (CC) at the Nullstellensatz level, for clause-like constraints over \(\mathbb F_2\). It is the related Conjecture SR regime of semi-regular behaviour. So no new binary test is needed, and the open point for odd primes is whether the partial-prefix images behave the same way, beyond the Nullstellensatz level.

Assessment and next step

The count reverses last cycle's proposed next step. That particular capacity statement is empty as an obstruction, though obstructions of other kinds remain possible. The construction direction has a concrete candidate that uses the size. What remains is the candidate's hardness. The recorded hardness results this cycle's searches found concern affine or single-predicate conditioning, apart from the binary Nullstellensatz check. The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer is to prove the hardness side of the conjecture for \(k=1\) at constant degree, or to find the obstruction that defeats it. The \(k=1\) images say "\(L_1=0\) or all other inputs nonzero". The natural tool is the \(p\)-complex's prescribed-moment extension with one conditioned form and one wide predicate family per block. The recorded binary random-clause check already supports (CC) for clause-like constraints at the Nullstellensatz level, so the proof attempt should aim at the polynomial-calculus side, where the check saw forced falls only.

Process. Checking what the proposed statement would give before trying to prove it saved a cycle: counting showed that it could not be an obstruction. The prior-record search then found the binary test I was about to propose, already done.

Evidence. research/results/odd_prime_substitution_capacity_20260922/: quotient_dims.py and quotient_dims.json, which reuse the fast driver's collision quotient. Run with --out PATH through the protected launcher.

Verification gate. Re-read from the notebooks: Lemma K's statement, the family review's transversal and ceiling, the random-conditioning entry's law and table, the weak-base compiler's degree, and the recorded random-clause check. Claim searches covered partial and exact prefixes, substitution capacity and clause conditioning. They found the binary random-clause check, now cited in place of a proposed test, and the related Conjecture SR. A narrowly briefed fresh-context reviewer confirmed the partial-prefix algebra, the idempotence of the substituted coefficients and the central point that the capacity statement cannot obstruct. It required the following, all adopted:

  • restate the calibration: the gap tends to a factor \(D\) rather than staying within 1.5, and the count lies above the law at small boards;
  • fix the conjecture's quantifiers: the input distribution, a fixed rule for \(S_b\), the limit \(n\to\infty\), and \(k<h\) independent of \(n\);
  • note that the conjecture is trivial for bounded widths;
  • derive the substituted degree \(B_k\) exactly from Lemma K, using one formula throughout;
  • correct the estimate for \(k\);
  • soften the obstruction claim, the reading of the binary check and a universal claim about the record;
  • say what a degree-5 test would and would not decide.

The corrections weaken or restate, so no second pass was run.

Route review: the random-calibration line is the odd-prime form of the recorded wide-clause line, parked at the relative-rank count

22 September 2026 · Route review with rediscovery labels · The next step targets the recorded degree-three obstruction with a rank-stratified first moment. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

The line's general claim. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. Random window inventories of every polynomial size are excluded at the compiler degree \(4p-1\) by substitution designs. By the constant-row clamp (lem:constant-row-clamp), a substitution turns each block into images added to the base, and the base stays hard under polynomially many generic images. The last three cycles built this: random affine conditioning, the capacity count and the partial-prefix conjecture, and the transversal reduction before them. What the goal needs is more: arbitrary inventories, the ones polynomial-size refutations actually produce, not random ones.

Rediscovery

This cycle opened on the \(k=1\) hardness of the partial-prefix conjecture. The route check read the main record's wide-clause line, which I had not read before designing the last two cycles. The index searches of those cycles used the thread's vocabulary (prefix, conditioning, capacity) and missed it. The same objects are recorded there over \(\mathbb F_2\):

  • The random-conditioning law is the odd-prime analogue of the proved uniform degree-two theorem (thm:uniform-parity-degree-two). That theorem shows the functional unary base keeps degree two under up to \(N^2-\sqrt2N^{3/2}(1+o(1))\) uniform parity constraints, matching the forced count. The odd-prime thresholds measured last cycle at \(D=2,3\) are the same phenomenon. They are new only as finite evidence at odd \(p\) and degree three.
  • The capacity count (CC) is the recorded forced-fall count \(M^*\approx\gamma_B/\gamma_{B-h}\) of Conjecture SR (conj:semi-regular-relative-to-base, obs:forced-degree-fall).
  • The partial-prefix conjecture is the wide-clause hardness statement, which says that generic clauses do no harm before the count forces a fall. Here it is written for substitution images at odd \(p\). The recorded point-support remark already explains why a design fixed before the clauses cannot work, which is the transversal and point-design ceiling seen here.

What the thread adds is the translation itself: through substitution, the random window inventory of the odd-prime problem becomes an instance of that line. The translation shows the odd-prime window, at the random calibration, needs nothing beyond the wide-clause statement at constant degree.

Falsification attempt

The recorded line was parked, with its reason (ctx:HW-parked-relative-rank-count). At level \(B\ge3\) a degree fall is an element of the degree-\(B\) part \(\bar K_B\) of the conflict ideal that vanishes on the annihilator \(U\) of the forms. It must lie outside the trivial part \(\bar W\wedge\bar K_{B-1}\). The event "vanishes on \(U\)" is dominated by that trivial part, so a first moment over \(\bar K_B\) needs a rank of \(B\)-forms relative to the ideal, and a count of the elements of low rank. None was known. The compiler degree is \(4p-1\ge11\), so the odd-prime random calibration sits squarely behind this obstruction. The measured \(D=3\) thresholds show the phenomenon persists at degree three, but they do not touch the missing count. The second recorded gap also applies unchanged: the clauses a proof produces are not random.

Assessment of this line

Weak for the goal, for the same two reasons as the recorded line. The counting evidence is consistent and now spans two characteristics and degrees two and three. But the proof technique for many wide forms at once stops at degree two, and nothing addresses proof-chosen clauses. The line's one genuinely new contribution is that the odd-prime window, at the random calibration, reduces to that line's missing step. It is not a separate problem.

Next step: a rank-stratified first moment at degree three

The obstruction asks for "a notion of rank of a \(B\)-form relative to the ideal and a count of the elements of low rank". The record already imports two relevant tools, used in the cubic polar-tensor line:

  • Janzer's bound (imp:Janzer-finite-field-partition-rank): partition rank is polynomial in analytic rank, uniformly in all dimensions, over every fixed finite field.
  • Kazhdan–Ziegler effective universality (imp:KZ-effective-affine-universality): families of high rank have equidistributed affine pullbacks.

The relative-rank theory of Lampert and Ziegler, rank relative to a collection of polynomials, is not in the record. The plan is to stratify the first moment over \(\bar K_B\) by partition rank \(r\) of \(\xi\) restricted to \(U\), and to compare two sides:

  • High rank. Bias bounds make vanishing on a random \(U\) improbable, with probability about \(q^{-c\,r}\) or better after Janzer's conversion.
  • Low rank. \(\xi\) is a short sum of products of lower-degree forms. The recorded decomposable computation, where vanishing forces a factor into \(\bar W\) and hence the trivial part, has to be generalized to sums of \(r\) products, with a count of such sums about \(q^{O(r\dim\bar K_{B-1})}\).

The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer is to write this balance at \(B=3\) over \(\mathbb F_p\) and decide whether it closes, as a theorem or as an explicit failure of the exponents. It should first be calibrated on the uniform degree-two theorem, whose proof is the \(B=2\) case with matrix rank. If it closes, it would give the first constant-degree hardness for many random wide forms, the missing step of the recorded line, and through transversals it would settle the one-count problem. The proof-chosen-clause gap would remain. If it fails, the failure names which exponent is wrong, and this route to the random calibration closes.
