Density is not what the thresholds follow: one constraint reduces to wide conditioning of one pattern, two kinds of deciding design are capped, and Conjecture SR's count fits the recorded thresholds

23 September 2026 · A working lemma, a control and observations · The density hypothesis is a surrogate; the count of Conjecture SR is the working heuristic. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The local-lift review asked for a density-weighted local-to-global principle, checked against the record. The implication at stake: the core statement's hypothesis that the total density of the forbidden sets is below one is what makes many wide constraints harmless. This cycle tests where density can act and ends with it replaced.

Setting

A constraint \(b\) has forms \(L_b=(L_{b,1},\dots,L_{b,k_b})\), affine over \(\mathbb F_p\), and a forbidden set \(F_b\subseteq\mathbb F_p^{k_b}\) of density \(\rho_b=|F_b|p^{-k_b}\). It is imposed by the equations \(\chi_v(L_b)=0\) for \(v\in F_b\), where \(\chi_v(L)=\prod_j\bigl(1-(L_j-v_j)^{p-1}\bigr)\) has degree \((p-1)k_b\). Two identities are used. First, \(\sum_{v\in\mathbb F_p^k}\chi_v(L)=1\) as polynomials, since \(\sum_{c\in\mathbb F_p}(1-(y-c)^{p-1})=1\). Second, \((y-v)\bigl(1-(y-v)^{p-1}\bigr)=y-y^p\) exactly, since \(v^p=v\). So \((L_j-v_j)\chi_v(L)\) is \((L_j-L_j^p)\) times a polynomial, of degree at most \((p-1)k+1\). And \(L^p-L=\sum_ia_i(x_i^p-x_i)\) for an affine form \(L=c+\sum_ia_ix_i\), with \(x^p-x=(x^2-x)(x^{p-2}+\dots+1)\), so Booleanity derives it at degree \(p\).

The planned test is vacuous

Every refutation and degree fall in the record has total density at least one:

  • random affine equations, each forbidding density \(1-1/p\);
  • the occupancy predicates of the symmetric-lift entry, each forbidding density \(1/3\);
  • the three-selector control, at total exactly one, which derives a consequence, not a refutation.

So the record cannot test a principle whose only extra hypothesis is density below one. The tests below replace it.

One constraint: density plays no role

Lemma (single-constraint dichotomy). Let \(B\) be any polynomial system containing the Boolean axioms, and fix affine forms \(L=(L_1,\dots,L_k)\). The PHP axioms are not used: part 1 uses nothing from \(B\), and part 2 uses only Booleanity.

  1. If \(B+\{L=v\}\) has no PC refutation of degree \(E\), then for every \(F\) with \(v\notin F\), \(B+\{\chi_w(L)=0:w\in F\}\) has none of degree \(E\).
  2. If \(B+\{L=v\}\) has a PC refutation of degree \(E'\) for some \(v\), then \(B\) derives \(\chi_v(L)=0\) at degree \(E'+(p-1)k\). So the constraint forbidding \(F=\mathbb F_p^k\setminus\{v\}\), of density \(1-p^{-k}<1\), is refuted at degree \(E'+(p-1)k\).

Proof.

  1. For \(w\in F\) choose a coordinate \(j\) with \(w_j\ne v_j\). The factor \(1-(L_j-w_j)^{p-1}\) of \(\chi_w\), taken modulo \(L_j-v_j\), becomes \(1-(v_j-w_j)^{p-1}=0\). So \(\chi_w=(L_j-v_j)h_w\) exactly, with \(\deg h_w<(p-1)k\). In a PC refutation of the constraint system, replace each axiom line \(\chi_w\) by its derivation from \(L_j-v_j\) by multiplications, of degree \(\deg\chi_w\le E\). This gives a refutation of \(B+\{L=v\}\) of degree \(E\).
  2. Multiply every line of a degree-\(E'\) PC refutation of \(B+\{L=v\}\) by \(\chi_v\). Linear combinations and multiplications by variables commute with this, and degrees rise by \((p-1)k\). Lines from \(B\) become multiples of axioms of \(B\). An axiom line \(L_j-v_j\) becomes, by the second identity, a multiple of \(L_j^p-L_j\) of degree at most \((p-1)k+1\), derivable from Booleanity. The last line becomes \(\chi_v\). So \(B\) derives \(\chi_v\) at degree \(E'+(p-1)k\). With the constraint equations, \(1=\chi_v+\sum_{w\ne v}\chi_w\) by the first identity. \(\square\)

So, over all forbidden sets \(F\ne\mathbb F_p^k\) on fixed forms \(L\), harmlessness of every such constraint is equivalent, up to \((p-1)k\) degrees, to hardness of the affine conditioning \(L=v\) for every pattern \(v\). Density plays no part beyond \(F\ne\mathbb F_p^k\). This is the question of the recorded wide-conditioning conjecture. The mechanism is the Fermat-selector dichotomy of the recorded retained affine-conditioning corollary (cor:retained-affine-conditioning-gap): either the selector lies in the base's ideal at its own degree, or conditioning preserves hardness. That corollary is for a complete affine layer over the full functional board; this lemma restates it for avoidance constraints on any Boolean base, so it is a refinement, not a new mechanism.

Robustness is necessary even at small density

Control (Boolean image). Take the occupancy forms \(C_1,\dots,C_k\), where \(C_s\) is the sum of column \(s\), and forbid \(F=\{0,1\}^k\), of density \((2/p)^k<1\). The weak base with this one constraint is refuted at degree \((p-1)k\).

Proof. By Booleanity and the collisions, \(C_s^2-C_s\) lies in \(B\) at degree two. The polynomial \(e_s=\chi_0(C_s)+\chi_1(C_s)-1\) has degree at most \(p-1\) and vanishes at \(0\) and \(1\), so \(e_s=C_s(C_s-1)q_s\). Then \(\sum_{v\in\{0,1\}^k}\chi_v=\prod_s(1+e_s)=1+\sum_{\emptyset\ne S}\prod_{s\in S}e_s\). Every term of the last sum is a multiple of some \(C_s^2-C_s\), of degree at most \((p-1)k\). Subtracting the constraint equations gives \(1=0\). \(\square\)

For \(k<N\) every nonzero combination of the \(C_s\) is active on every row (with all \(N\) columns, \(\sum_sC_s\) is constant modulo rows). But a single \(C_s\) has row function one label away from a constant, so the family is not robust. The recorded control \(C_j=1\) made the same point for affine equations at density above one; this one shows that density below one does not replace robustness.

Deciding designs are capped

Call a design deciding if it satisfies every constraint by conditioning on an event that implies it. The two kinds below stop short of polynomially many generic constraints. The constant-row clamp's non-affine substitutions and mixtures of designs are not covered.

  • Affine deciding. Conditioning on \(L_b=w_b\) for allowed joint patterns needs the joint span of the conditioned forms to be wide. Otherwise the wide-conditioning conjecture certifies nothing, and by the recorded dimension bound that caps it below \(N^2\). At full rank the cap is real, not only a limit of the conjecture; between the dimension bound and full rank nothing is shown. Observation: once the conditioned forms span all linear parts modulo rows, every cell is fixed to a constant modulo the row equations. The base axioms then become constants, and one of them is nonzero because PHP has no Boolean solutions. That is a refutation of degree at most two. Density enters the affine route only through a union bound over \(\mathbb F_p\): if each constraint's forms are independent modulo rows and constants, the joint allowed patterns in the image \(W\) of the joint linear map have density at least \(1-\sum_b\rho_b>0\). That is correct, but useful only below the cap.
  • Multiplier deciding. Conditioning a base design on the product \(\prod_b s_b\) of satisfaction indicators \(s_b=1-\sum_{v\in F_b}\chi_v\) is the recorded old-multiplier mechanism of the flat value-choice corollary (cor:rank-free-flat-value-choice). Its degree \(\sum_b(p-1)k_b\) plus the target degree \(D\) must stay below the base's own degree, about \(N/2\). So it reaches fewer than \(N/(2(p-1)k)\) constraints.

So a design for polynomially many generic constraints can be neither affine-deciding nor multiplier-deciding. The remaining candidates are non-deciding designs, which annihilate \(m\chi_v\) for low-degree \(m\) without conditioning on satisfaction, like the \(p\)-complex's moment corrections, and the clamp's non-affine substitutions and mixtures, which these caps do not cover.

Density does not govern the recorded thresholds; Conjecture SR's count fits them

Density below one is far from necessary. The recorded random-conditioning thresholds keep the base hard with many random affine equations, each forbidding density \(1-1/p\):

  • 13 equations at \(n=7\), \(D=3\), total density about \(8.7\);
  • 63 equations at \(n=10\), \(D=2\) (both seeds refuted from 64), total density 42.

What fits these thresholds is the semi-regular count of the recorded Conjecture SR (conj:semi-regular-relative-to-base), in the minimal-generator presentation: one linear generator \(L-c\) per equation. Let \(d_j\) be the dimension of the base's degree-\(j\) quotient (\(d_0=1\)), computed here exactly with the recorded driver. For the equations, all of degree \(h=1\), the count predicts the first refuted \(M\) as the least \(M\) with \(\sum_{i\ge0}(-1)^i\binom Mi d_{D-i}\le0\):

case\(d_1,d_2,d_3\)predicted crossingmeasured
\(n=10\), \(D=2\)100, 439064.264
\(n=7\), \(D=3\)49, 973, 9661about 14.414
\(n=6\), \(D=3\)36, 498, 3067about 8.17

The count depends on the presentation: with the \(\chi\) presentation an affine equation over \(\mathbb F_3\) has two generators of degree two, and the naive count is far too large. It also needs robustness: it predicts hardness for the Boolean-image control, which is refuted at once. So the working heuristic is Conjecture SR for collectively robustly wide constraints, in minimal presentation. Density enters it only through the number of generators, a factor small next to the degree ratio \(d_{D-h}/d_D\). For the logarithmic-prefix images, \(M=n^{O(1)}\) generators of degree about \((p-1)k\) with \(k=\Theta(\log n)\), the count leaves superpolynomial room at every polylogarithmic \(D\). So the core statement's density hypothesis is a union-bound surrogate, and the statement is best read as Conjecture SR for such constraints, as the random-calibration review already identified. This cycle adds that no density-based principle is a separate route, and that the count fits the affine thresholds with Koszul terms included (files: research/results/odd_prime_density_principle_20260923/).

Assessment and next step

The density-weighted principle is withdrawn as a formulation: density acts only in deciding designs, which are capped, and it is not what governs hardness. The line's target is Conjecture SR for robust wide constraints. The regime that matters first is \(D<2h\). There no product of two constraints fits in degree \(D\), so in the Macaulay-count heuristic a fall first shows as a rank deficiency of the multiplication map from \(\bigoplus_b(P/I)_{\le D-h}\,c_b\) to \((P/I)_{\le D}\). PC closure is not the Macaulay count, so this is the heuristic's form, not a proved equivalence. The question is of Hochster–Laksov type, relative to the base. Hochster and Laksov proved maximal rank one degree above the generators for generic forms in a polynomial ring; the record does not contain it. The recorded uniform degree-two theorem is its relative case \(h=1\), \(D=2\). The recorded degree-three obstruction concerns \(h=1\), \(D=3=h+2\).

The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer is the first new relative case, quadratic constraints at one degree above them: \(h=2\), \(D=3\) over \(\mathbb F_3\), with random selector constraints \(1-L^2=0\). The capacity count gives a prediction from the base quotient's dimensions \(d_1\) and \(d_3\). Compare it with the exact least refuted count on \(n=6,7\) using the recorded fast closure driver, whose \(D=3\) runs took about one and twelve minutes. Then read the proof of Hochster–Laksov for a step that transfers to the quotient by the PHP ideal. A selector constraint has one quadratic generator, and \(2h=4>3\), so the count predicts the first refuted \(M\) near \(d_3/d_1\): about 85 at \(n=6\) and 197 at \(n=7\). Those differ from the affine thresholds 7 and 14 and are below the trivial bound \(d_3\). At \(n=6\) a bisection over \(M\le200\) needs about eight closures, each close to the recorded one-minute \(D=3\) run, so it is reachable; \(n=7\) is optional. Agreement supports Conjecture SR one degree above quadratic generators; a clear early fall locates the first failure of the count. The cycle ends with the measured threshold against that prediction, and with the transfer point in the Hochster–Laksov proof or the step that fails relative to PHP.

Verification gate. Claim searches (old-consequence transfer, conjunction and normalization, occupancy Boolean pattern, one-predicate conditioning, weighted conditioning, single-constraint pattern conditioning, Hochster–Laksov and Fröberg) found the transfer lemma, the flat value-choice corollary, the retained affine-conditioning corollary, the one-predicate theorem, Conjecture SR and the semi-regularity source audit, and no statement of Hochster–Laksov. The quotient dimensions were computed exactly for this entry. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed both identities, the lemma's conclusions, the Boolean-image algebra and the union bound. It required: the proofs rewritten line by line for PC instead of as Nullstellensatz sums, the unused PHP hypotheses stated, the recorded retained affine-conditioning corollary cited as the same mechanism, the non-robustness witness corrected, the claim about non-deciding designs restricted to the two capped kinds, the affine cap qualified between the dimension bound and full rank, the capacity count stated with its presentation, robustness and predicted-versus-measured numbers and labelled as Conjecture SR, the maximal-rank statement weakened to heuristic form, and the next step's predictions computed. Quadratic selectors show no degree fall relative to PHP until the graded count forces one: the count with the Frobenius syzygy predicts every sampled threshold

23 September 2026 · Finite check · Selectors \(1-L^2\) over \(\mathbb F_3\) at degree three, \(n=6,7\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The density-principle entry read the core statement as Conjecture SR, relative semi-regularity (conj:semi-regular-relative-to-base), for collectively robustly wide constraints. It proposed the first new test one degree above the generators: random selector constraints \(1-L^2=0\) (that is, \(L\ne0\)) over \(\mathbb F_3\) at PC degree \(D=3\). The implication at stake is that the base with such constraints has no degree fall before the count forces one. For generic forms in a polynomial ring, the Hochster–Laksov theorem proves the one-degree-above case; the selectors here are squares of linear forms, a special family. The test ends with the measured thresholds and ranks against the count.

The count, corrected

The previous entry's predictions (85 at \(n=6\), 197 at \(n=7\)) used cumulative dimensions \(d_j\). The recorded forced-fall count uses the graded dimensions \(\gamma_j=d_j-d_{j-1}\) of the base quotient, and it must include the syzygies the field forces. Over \(\mathbb F_3\) with Boolean variables, \(L^3=L\) for every affine form, so \(L\cdot(1-L^2)\equiv0\). Each selector therefore has one trivial linear syzygy. Of its \(\gamma_1\) linear multipliers, only \(\gamma_1-1\) give new degree-three top parts. With \(2h=4>3\) there is no product of two constraints in degree three. The count assumes that the base's own degree-three closure has no fall; this is checked below. It predicts:

  • no degree fall while \(M(\gamma_1-1)<\gamma_3\);
  • closure rank \(\operatorname{rank}_0+(\gamma_1)M\) until then, where \(\operatorname{rank}_0\) is the base's own closure rank. That is one lower-degree row (the constraint) plus \(\gamma_1-1\) new top rows per constraint;
  • the first degree fall at \(M=\lceil\gamma_3/(\gamma_1-1)\rceil\), once the degree-three top part is exhausted. That refutation follows at the same \(M\) is an observed outcome, not a consequence of the count.

From the exact quotient dimensions of the previous entry: at \(n=6\), \(\gamma=(1,35,462,2569)\) and \(\operatorname{rank}_0=4571\), so the prediction is \(\lceil2569/34\rceil=76\). At \(n=7\), \(\gamma=(1,48,924,8688)\), so it is \(\lceil8688/47\rceil=185\). With graded dimensions, the affine thresholds of the previous entry become crossings 63.17, 13.35 and 7.15 (first predicted \(M\) 64, 14 and 8) against measured 64, 14 and 7. The affine case at \(n=6\) is refuted one equation early, so for affine generators there is a small early fall at that size.

Measurements

Exact PC closures over \(\mathbb F_3\) in the collision quotient, with the recorded fast driver. Each constraint is \(1-L^2\) for a uniformly random affine form \(L\) in the cells. The least refuted \(M\) was found by bisection on a fixed sequence of constraints per seed.

\(n\)predictedleast refuted \(M\)
67676, 76, 76 (seeds 9060–9062)
7185185, 185 (seeds 9070, 9071)

At \(n=6\), seed 9060, the closure was split by degree. In the reduced echelon form with degree-three columns first, the rows pivoting in degree three give the rank of the projection onto the degree-three part. The other rows give the dimension of the closure's degree-\(\le2\) part. A degree fall would raise the second count beyond \(280+M\).

\(M\)0205070747576
degree-3 projection4291497159916671680768416860
degree \(\le2\) part280300330350354355778

Through \(M=75\) the parts are exactly \(4291+34M\) and \(280+M\). The base's own values leave exactly \(\gamma_3=6860-4291=2569\) free top dimensions, and 280 is the base's degree-two closure rank, so the base has no fall of its own at degree three. So there is no degree fall before the count's crossing. At \(M=76\) the degree-three part is exhausted (6860 is every degree-three column), the degree-\(\le2\) part jumps, and the system is refuted. Files: research/results/odd_prime_selector_sr_20260923/ (selector_threshold.py, selector_threshold_lib.py, degree_split.py, selector_n6_D3.json, selector_n7_D3.json, degree_split_n6.json).

What this shows

On the sampled seeds the base with quadratic selectors is semi-regular at degree three, with the Frobenius syzygy as the only extra relation: random squares \(1-L^2\) have no unexpected linear syzygies modulo the PHP ideal before the count forces them. The earlier evidence for Conjecture SR was the affine case (degree-one generators: the recorded uniform degree-two theorem and the random-conditioning thresholds). This is the first check with nonlinear generators, and at these sizes the selector thresholds match with no slack. The occupancy predicates of the symmetric-lift entry fell far earlier, at 8 to 21 at \(D=2\). They are the low-dimensional control: their forms span only \(n-1\) dimensions modulo rows and constants, so they generate a small subalgebra.

Literature and the proof route

The selectors are squares of linear forms, whose top parts \(-\bigl(\sum_ic_ix_i\bigr)^2\) lie on the square variety, not generic quadrics. The closest classical setting is powers of general linear forms (Fröberg–Hollman, Iarrobino), where exceptions to the expected Hilbert function are known; those sources have not been read here. For generic forms, Hochster and Laksov (The linear syzygies of generic forms, Comm. Algebra 15, 1987) proved maximal rank one degree above generators of degree at least two. A recent preprint, Boij, Dannetun and Lundqvist, arXiv:2605.03872 (May 2026), reports Fröberg's prediction through degree \(d+2\) for any number of forms, and through \(2d-1\) when the number of variables is large. According to its HTML text, the method is Hochster–Laksov's. It stratifies multiplier tuples by rank, bounds the bad locus with the fiber-dimension theorem, and closes the count with Macaulay's bound on Hilbert-function growth, over an infinite field. These statements come from a summary of the paper and were not checked against its proofs. The relative transfer would do three things:

  • replace the polynomial ring by the associated graded algebra of the base quotient, which is standard graded, so Macaulay's growth bound still applies;
  • replace the fiber-dimension step by a first moment over \(\mathbb F_p\): the expected number of nontrivial linear syzygies, summed over multiplier tuples stratified by rank;
  • count the Frobenius syzygies \(L\cdot(1-L^{p-1})\) as expected.

The record's degree-three first moment failed on an entropy count for affine generators two degrees above them. One degree above is the regime where the recorded uniform degree-two theorem succeeded for affine generators. The reach is limited even if the transfer works. The logarithmic-prefix images need degree about \((4p-1)\) times their generator degree, beyond \(2d-1\). So a relative maximal-rank theorem for squares at one degree above would be the first nonlinear case of Conjecture SR, not the goal.

Assessment and next step

This is the strongest evidence yet for Conjecture SR relative to PHP with nonlinear generators. The prediction matched all five seeds at two sizes, and the degree split at one seed at \(n=6\) shows no fall before the crossing. The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer is to prove the relative maximal-rank statement for random selectors \(1-L^2\) over \(\mathbb F_3\) at degree three. It is a first moment over nonzero tuples \((a_b)\) of linear multipliers, taken modulo the Frobenius syzygies. The event is that \(\sum_ba_b\operatorname{top}(c_b)=0\) in the degree-three graded part, and \(\operatorname{top}(c_b)\) is a quadratic function of the uniform form \(L_b\), not uniform on a linear space. So the bound needs a Schwartz–Zippel or quadratic character-sum estimate for \(\sum_ba_b\,q(L_b)\). Stratify the tuples by the rank of that quadratic map, and compare the first moment with the prediction \(M(\gamma_1-1)<\gamma_3\). The recorded uniform degree-two theorem (thm:uniform-parity-degree-two) is the model only for its affine-generator part. The cycle ends with the theorem, or with the rank stratum where the first moment exceeds one.

The predictions use exact quotient dimensions. The rank equality \(4571+35M\) at five values is an exact check of the no-fall claim at \(n=6\), independent of the bisection. Claim searches (Hochster–Laksov, Fröberg, maximal rank, semi-regularity) found Conjecture SR, the forced-fall count and the semi-regularity source audit, and no prior selector test or Hochster–Laksov statement. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed the driver's construction and the bisection. It required: the stale docstring fixed, the no-fall claim measured by the degree split rather than the total rank, refutation at the crossing labelled as observed, the count's assumption stated and checked, the affine early fall noted, the selectors described as squares with the powers-of-linear-forms literature as the relevant analog, the next step's probability bound restated for a quadratic map, and the overclaims narrowed to the sampled seeds. All were adopted.

Selector degree falls: a kernel criterion, an exact first-moment identity, and a proof that the unconditioned moment is useless

23 September 2026 · Working lemma and an obstruction · The unconditioned first moment fails provably; a spread event is needed. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The selector check found no degree fall for random selectors \(1-L^2\) over \(\mathbb F_3\) at degree three until the graded count forces one. It proposed proving this by a first moment. The implication at stake is the relative maximal-rank statement, the first case of Conjecture SR with nonlinear generators. This cycle sets up the first moment exactly and tests whether it can be bounded by its typical value. It ends with the identity and with the form the proof must take.

Setting

Let \(J\subseteq P=\mathbb F_3[x_{ij}]\) be the homogeneous ideal generated by \(x_{ij}^2\), the collisions \(x_{ij}x_{i'j}\) and the row forms \(\sum_jx_{ij}\), and put \(A=P/J\) with graded dimensions \(\gamma_j\). When the base's own closure has no degree fall through degree three, \(A_j\) is the base's graded quotient in degrees \(j\le3\). The degree split checked this at \(n=6\). A selector \(c_b=1-L_b^2\) has linear part \(\ell_b\in A_1\) and top part \(-\ell_b^2\in A_2\). Define \[ \Phi:A_1^M\to A_3,\qquad(a_b)\mapsto\sum_ba_b\ell_b^2 . \] In characteristic three \(\ell^3=\sum_ia_i^3x_i^3=0\) in \(A\), so \(\ker\Phi\) contains the Frobenius kernel \(F_\ell=\{(\lambda_b\ell_b)\}\), of dimension \(M\) when every \(\ell_b\ne0\).

Kernel criterion

Lemma (selector kernel criterion). Suppose the base has no degree fall through degree three and \(\ker\Phi=F_\ell\). (This implies that the squares \(\ell_b^2\) are linearly independent in \(A_2\) when \(\gamma_1\ge2\): a relation \(\sum\alpha_b\ell_b^2=0\) would give the kernel tuple \((\alpha_ba)\) for any \(a\) not proportional to the \(\ell_b\).) Then adding the selectors causes no degree fall at degree three. The degree-three closure's part of degree at most two is the base's plus the span of the \(c_b\).

Proof. Let \(V\) be the span of the base's degree-three closure and the products \(mc_b\) with \(\deg m\le1\). It suffices to show that the part of \(V\) of degree at most two is the base's degree-two closure plus \(\langle c_b\rangle\), since then \(V\) is closed under multiplication by variables within degree three and is the closure. Because the base has no fall, the degree-three components of base-closure elements lie in \(J_3\), and a base-closure element of degree at most two lies in the base's degree-two closure. Take \(v=\sum_b(\alpha_b+a_b)c_b+\beta\) with \(\beta\) in the base's closure, \(\alpha_b\) constants and \(a_b\) linear, of degree at most two. Its degree-three part is \(-\sum_ba_b\ell_b^2\) plus an element of \(J_3\), so \(\sum_ba_b\ell_b^2=0\) in \(A_3\) and \((a_b)\in F_\ell\). So \(a_b=\lambda_b\ell_b+r_b\) with \(r_b\) in the span of the row forms. Write \(L_b=\ell_b+\kappa_b\). Then \(\ell_bc_b=L_bc_b-\kappa_bc_b\), and \(L_bc_b=L_b-L_b^3\) lies in the base at degree three: \(L^3-L=\sum_ia_i(x_i^3-x_i)\) for \(L=\kappa+\sum_ia_ix_i\) over \(\mathbb F_3\), and \(x^3-x=(x+1)(x^2-x)\). A row form \(R_i\) gives \(R_ic_b=(R_i-1)c_b+c_b\), again in the base plus \(\langle c_b\rangle\). So \(v\) lies in the base's closure plus \(\langle c_b\rangle\), and its base part has degree at most two. One level down, \(\sum_b\alpha_bc_b\) of degree at most one would need \(\sum_b\alpha_b\ell_b^2=0\) in \(A_2\), which is excluded. \(\square\)

An exact first-moment identity

Identity. For independent uniform \(\ell_b\in A_1\), \[ \mathbb E\,|\ker\Phi|=3^{M\gamma_1-\gamma_3}\sum_{\chi\in A_3^*}\pi(\chi)^M,\qquad\pi(\chi)=\Pr_{\ell}\bigl[\chi(a\ell^2)=0\ \ \forall a\in A_1\bigr]. \] Proof. \(\mathbb E|\ker\Phi|=\sum_a\Pr[\Phi(a)=0]\). Write the indicator of \(\Phi(a)=0\) as \(3^{-\gamma_3}\sum_\chi\omega^{\chi(\Phi(a))}\), and use independence over \(b\). Then note \(\sum_{a\in A_1}\omega^{\chi(a\ell^2)}=3^{\gamma_1}\cdot\mathbf 1[\chi(A_1\ell^2)=0]\), because \(a\mapsto\chi(a\ell^2)\) is linear. \(\square\)

Equivalently, \(\sum_\chi\pi(\chi)^M\) is the expected number of killers, the \(\chi\) vanishing on the image of \(\Phi\). If \(\ker\Phi=F_\ell\) with every \(\ell_b\ne0\), the number of killers is exactly \(\mathcal B=3^{\gamma_3-M(\gamma_1-1)}\). Otherwise it is at least \(3\mathcal B\): either the kernel is larger, or \(z\ge1\) of the \(\ell_b\) vanish and \(\dim\ker\Phi\ge M-z+z\gamma_1\ge M+1\). So \(\Pr[\ker\Phi\ne F_\ell]\le(\mathbb E[\#\text{killers}]-\mathcal B)/(2\mathcal B)\), and a proof along these lines would need \(\mathbb E[\#\text{killers}]=\mathcal B(1+o(1))\).

The unconditioned first moment is useless

Observation (column squares). If \(\ell=\sum_ia_ix_{ij}\) lies in the span of one column, then \(\ell^2=0\) in \(A_2\), by \(x^2=0\) and the collisions. Modulo rows the column forms of one column span at most \(n+1\) dimensions, so a uniform \(\ell\) is a column form with probability \(p\ge(1-o(1))\,n\,3^{n+1-\gamma_1}\). Let \(r_b\) be the rank of \(a\mapsto a\ell_b^2\). Then \(r_b\le\gamma_1-1\) when \(\ell_b\ne0\), \(r_b=0\) for column forms, and \(\operatorname{rank}\Phi\le\sum_br_b\). With the \(\ell_b\) independent, \[ \mathbb E[\#\text{killers}]=3^{\gamma_3}\,\mathbb E\,3^{-\operatorname{rank}\Phi}\ \ge\ 3^{\gamma_3}\prod_b\mathbb E\,3^{-r_b}\ \ge\ \mathcal B\,\bigl(1+n3^n(1-o(1))\bigr)^M . \] At \(n=6\), \(M=73\), that is about \(\mathcal B\cdot3^{557}\). So the killer moment is provably useless without conditioning. In particular the mean of \(\pi(\chi)\) is not about \(3^{-(\gamma_1-1)}\): it exceeds that by a factor of about \(n3^n\), coming from the rare \(\ell\) with small square rank.

Spread event. The bad \(\ell\) are exactly those whose square has a large annihilator: \(\dim\{a\in A_1:a\ell^2=0\}>1\). This covers column forms and also low-support forms such as \(x_{1j}+x_{2k}\), which \(e=x_{3j}\) kills. Define the spread event \(\mathcal S\) as: every \(\ell_b\) has \(\dim\operatorname{Ann}_{A_1}(\ell_b^2)=1\). Its complement has probability roughly \(M\,n\,3^{n+1-\gamma_1}\) (to be proved), negligible for \(M\) polynomial. Without it, the stratum of single-form tuples fails outright, with about \(Mn3^{n+1}\) expected bad tuples.

Proof plan

The recorded uniform degree-two theorem (thm:uniform-parity-degree-two) avoids the same problem in two ways:

  • it conditions on the event that the forms are independent;
  • it takes the first moment over the objects witnessing a fall, stratified by rank, with the low-rank strata counted separately.

The analog here, on the spread event and with every \(\ell_b\ne0\), is \(\Pr[\ker\Phi\ne F_\ell]\le\mathbb E\,|\ker\Phi\setminus F_\ell|/(2\cdot3^M)\). The expectation is a sum over fixed tuples \(a\) of \(\Pr[\Phi(a)=0,\ a\notin F_\ell]\); the event must exclude \(F_\ell\), since \(F_\ell\) depends on \(\ell\). Stratify the tuples as in Hochster–Laksov by \(t=\dim\operatorname{span}\{a_b\}\) and by the support size \(s\) of the coefficient matrix. For a tuple of span dimension \(t\) with basis \(e_1,\dots,e_t\), \(\Phi(a)=\sum_ke_kQ_k\) with \(Q_k=\sum_bc_{bk}\ell_b^2\). So the event is a linear syzygy of \(t\) terms among combinations of random squares. With \(N_{t,s}\) tuples in a stratum, the union bound closes if \(\sum_{t,s}N_{t,s}\,p_{t,s}=o(3^M)\), where \(p_{t,s}\) bounds the stratum's probability on \(\mathcal S\). At \(t=\gamma_1\) with full support, the count \(3^{M\gamma_1}\) against \(3^{-\gamma_3}\) gives \(3^{M\gamma_1-\gamma_3}\), which is \(o(3^M)\) exactly when \(M(\gamma_1-1)<\gamma_3\) with room: the graded count. The small-\(t\) strata are where the square structure of \(\ell_b^2\), not uniformity, decides the probability.

Assessment and next step

The cycle proved the reduction of "no fall" to a kernel statement and an exact identity, and proved that the natural moment of that identity is useless without conditioning. It named the spread event the proof needs. No stratum is bounded yet.

The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer is to bound the complement of the spread event, then the smallest strata, \(t=1\) and \(t=2\). For \(t=1\), bound \(\Pr[e\cdot\sum_bc_b\ell_b^2=0]\) for fixed \(e\in A_1\) and \(c\in\mathbb F_3^M\) through the rank of the quadratic form \(\sum_bc_b\ell_b^2\) restricted to the annihilator of \(e\). This covers the support of \(c\) being one, two or many forms. Then do the same for \(t=2\). The target is the exponent \(t(\gamma_1+M)\) with room. Compute the exact probabilities at \(n=6\) for supports one and two. Enumerate \(e\) up to the symmetry group \(S_{n+1}\times S_n\) of pigeons and holes. For each orbit representative, compute \(\operatorname{Ann}_{A_2}(e)\) and the distribution of the rank of a random square restricted to it by exact rank computations over \(\mathbb F_3\) in \(A_2\) (dimension 462), sampling \(\ell\) rather than enumerating all \(3^{35}\). The cycle ends with the two strata bounded, or with the stratum whose probability is too large, which would be a structural exception like those known for powers of linear forms.

Verification gate. Re-read: the selector check (its count and degree split), the uniform degree-two theorem's statement and proof (its two-form fall criterion, first moment over \(\bar K\) by rank, independence event), and the selector construction. The criterion and the identity are proved above. A fresh-context reviewer found the column-square obstruction, which replaced a Poisson heuristic, and required the spread event, the normalization of the union bound with the event \(a\notin F_\ell\), the criterion's independence hypothesis noted as implied, a non-circular spanning argument, the identity \(x^3-x=(x+1)(x^2-x)\), the case of vanishing \(\ell_b\) in the killer count, and the plan relabelled. All were adopted.

The spread lemma: four robust pigeons force the square's annihilator to be the form itself

23 September 2026 · Working lemma and a finite check · The spread event fails with probability at most \(M\cdot3^{-(1-o(1))n^2}\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The first-moment entry reduced the no-fall statement for random selectors \(1-L^2\) over \(\mathbb F_3\) at degree three to a kernel statement. It proved that the proof must condition on a spread event: every linear part \(\ell_b\) has \(\operatorname{Ann}_{A_1}(\ell_b^2)=\langle\ell_b\rangle\). This cycle determines which \(\ell\) fail it, proves a sufficient condition, and bounds the failure probability. It ends with that lemma, or with a family of bad forms of noticeable probability.

Setting

\(A=\mathbb F_3[x_{ij}]/(x_{ij}^2,\ x_{ij}x_{i'j},\ \sum_jx_{ij})\), with \(n\) holes and \(n+1\) pigeons. A linear form in \(A_1\) is a family of row functions \(f_i:[n]\to\mathbb F_3\), one per pigeon, each defined up to a constant: \(\ell=\sum_{i,j}f_i(j)x_{ij}\). Call \(f\) \(q\)-robust if it takes at least two values on every set of \(n-q\) labels.

The monomials and the row relations respect the multiset of pigeons, so \(A_3\) splits into components by pigeon multiset. For three distinct pigeons \(T=\{a,b,c\}\), the component is the space of functions on injections \(T\to[n]\) modulo the span of the functions that depend on only two coordinates. The relation \(R_a\,x_{bj}x_{cj'}\) is such a function, the collisions having removed \(j_a\in\{j,j'\}\). For three pairs of labels \(P_a,P_b,P_c\) with all six labels distinct, the mixed third difference \(\Delta_{P_a,P_b,P_c}\) (the alternating sum over the eight injections choosing one label from each pair) kills every two-coordinate function. For a product it is the product of the first differences \(\delta f(P)=f(j)-f(j')\).

The spread lemma

Lemma (spread lemma). Let \(n\ge8\) and \(\ell\in A_1\) with row functions \(f_i\). If at least four pigeons have \(6\)-robust row functions, then \(\operatorname{Ann}_{A_1}(\ell^2)=\langle\ell\rangle\).

Proof. Since \(\ell^3=0\), \(\ell\) annihilates \(\ell^2\). Let \(e\in A_1\), with row functions \(g_i\), satisfy \(e\ell^2=0\). Since \(\ell^2=2\sum_{u<v}\ell_u\ell_vx_ux_v\), the component of \(e\ell^2\) on a triple \(T=\{a,b,c\}\) is twice the function \(g_a\otimes f_b\otimes f_c+f_a\otimes g_b\otimes f_c+f_a\otimes f_b\otimes g_c\) on injections. Shifting any row function by a constant changes this only by two-coordinate functions. Its vanishing in \(A_3\) and the product rule give, for all disjoint pairs \(P_a,P_b,P_c\), \[ \delta g_a\,\delta f_b\,\delta f_c+\delta f_a\,\delta g_b\,\delta f_c+\delta f_a\,\delta f_b\,\delta g_c=0. \tag{SP} \] For a robust pigeon \(x\) and a pair \(P\) with \(\delta f_x(P)\ne0\), put \(r_x(P)=\delta g_x(P)/\delta f_x(P)\). Let \(x,y,z\) be robust and let \(P,P''\) be two pairs of \(x\) with nonzero differences. By \(6\)-robustness choose a pair \(Q_y\) of \(y\) avoiding the at most four labels of \(P\cup P''\), and a pair \(Q_z\) of \(z\) avoiding those and \(Q_y\), at most six labels, both with nonzero differences. Then (SP), divided by the three nonzero differences, gives \(r_x(P)+r_y(Q_y)+r_z(Q_z)=0=r_x(P'')+r_y(Q_y)+r_z(Q_z)\). So \(r_x\) is a constant \(\mu_x\), and \(\mu_x+\mu_y+\mu_z=0\) for every three robust pigeons. With four robust pigeons \(a,b,c,d\), the triples \(\{a,b,c\}\) and \(\{a,b,d\}\) give \(\mu_c=\mu_d\), and by symmetry all are equal to some \(\mu\); \(3\mu=0\) holds automatically in \(\mathbb F_3\).

Now let \(y\) be any pigeon and \(P\) any pair of its labels. Choose pairs of two robust pigeons \(b,c\ne y\) avoiding \(P\) and each other (at most four excluded labels), with nonzero differences. Then (SP) gives \(\delta f_b\,\delta f_c\,(\delta g_y+2\mu\,\delta f_y)=0\), that is \(\delta g_y(P)=\mu\,\delta f_y(P)\), since \(-2=1\) in \(\mathbb F_3\). This covers robust \(y\) at pairs with \(\delta f_y=0\), and non-robust or zero row functions. So \(g_y-\mu f_y\) is constant for every pigeon, and \(e=\mu\ell\) in \(A_1\). \(\square\)

The hypothesis may be far from necessary: the probes at \(n=6\), below the lemma's range, found no bad form among samples on three or more pigeons.

Failure probability. As in the first-moment entry, each linear part \(\ell_b\) is uniform in \(A_1\): its row functions are independent and uniform modulo constants, and robustness does not change under constant shifts. For a uniform row function, the probability of being constant on some set of \(n-6\) labels is at most \(\binom n6\,3^{7-n}\). The \(n+1\) row functions of a uniform \(\ell\) are independent, so fewer than four are \(6\)-robust with probability at most \(\binom{n+1}{3}\bigl(\binom n6\,3^{7-n}\bigr)^{n-2}=3^{-(1-o(1))n^2}\). A union over the \(M\) constraints gives \(\Pr[\mathcal S^c]\le M\binom{n+1}3\bigl(\binom n63^{7-n}\bigr)^{n-2}\), superpolynomially small for \(M=n^{O(1)}\). The bound says nothing at the checked size \(n=6\), which is below the lemma's range, and becomes meaningful from about \(n=16\).

Finite check at \(n=6\)

The script builds \(A\) exactly in degrees one to three: 6860 degree-three monomials, relation rank 4291, \(\gamma_3=2569\), \(\gamma_1=35\). It computes \(\dim\operatorname{Ann}_{A_1}(q)\) by one GF(3) rank per sample.

probesamples\(\dim\operatorname{Ann}\)
\(\ell^2\), \(\ell\) uniform1001 in all
\(\ell^2\), \(\ell\) on 1 pigeon201 (1), 2 (7), 3 (3), 14 (9)
\(\ell^2\), \(\ell\) on 2 pigeons201 (17), 2 (3)
\(\ell^2\), \(\ell\) on 3 to 7 pigeons20 each1 in all
\(\ell^2\), \(\ell\) a column form135 (\(\ell^2=0\))
\(\ell_1^2\pm\ell_2^2\), uniform1000 in all
\(\ell_1^2+\ell_2^2\), each on 1 or 2 pigeons20 each0 in 14 and 19; the rest 1 to 14
\(\ell_1^2+\ell_2^2\), each on 3 pigeons200 in all

The bad forms found were supported on at most two pigeons (not all such forms are bad), or had narrow row functions such as column forms, consistent with the lemma. The last rows are the stratum \(t=1\) with two terms of the kernel union bound: \(e(\ell_1^2\pm\ell_2^2)=0\) never occurs for uniform forms in these samples. Files: research/results/odd_prime_spread_event_20260923/annihilators.py, annihilators_n6.json.

Assessment and next step

The spread event is now proved to fail with probability at most \(M\cdot3^{-(1-o(1))n^2}\), and its proof gives a method: third differences on triple components turn annihilation in \(A_3\) into multilinear identities among row functions. The same method should handle the stratum \(t=1\) with support \(s\ge2\). There \(e\sum_bc_b\ell_b^2=0\) gives \(\sum_bc_b\sum_{\rm cyc}\delta g\,\delta f^{(b)}\delta f^{(b)}=0\), and for independent uniform \(\ell_b\) this should force \(e=0\).

The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer is to prove that, bound its failure probability, and count the stratum's contribution. Then extend to \(t=2\), where the identity has two unknown row-function families. The proof ends with those strata bounded, or with the smallest support where the triple method stops forcing \(e=0\).

Verification gate. Re-read: the first-moment entry (the spread event and the union-bound plan), the construction of \(A\) and its component split, and the selector check's dimensions, which the script reproduces (\(\gamma_1=35\), \(\gamma_3=2569\)). The third-difference product rule was checked numerically, 200 random instances at \(n=7\). A first proof draft used \(4\)-robustness, which does not leave room for the third pigeon's pair; the lemma now assumes \(6\)-robustness and \(n\ge8\). A claim search (annihilator, square, robust row functions, third difference, triple) found the ternary pair theorem and bit-annihilator lemmas, and no statement of this lemma. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed the component decomposition, the triple component of \(e\ell^2\), the label counts with \(6\)-robustness, the equality of the \(\mu\), the final step, the probability bound (first below one at \(n=16\)) and the table against the data. It required the bound stated as an upper bound for the union, the uniformity of the \(\ell_b\) cited, an undefined generalization removed, and the finite-check wording narrowed to the samples. All were adopted.

The span-one stratum: no single multiplier kills a combination of two to \(cn^3/\log M\) random squares, except on a rare event

23 September 2026 · Working proof, conditional above \(2\gamma_1\) on a multiplication bound. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The first-moment entry reduced the no-fall statement for random selectors \(1-L^2\) over \(\mathbb F_3\) at degree three to this: \(\ker\Phi\) contains only the Frobenius kernel. The spread lemma handled a single square. This cycle treats the kernel tuples of span dimension one, \(a_b=c_be\), with support \(S=\operatorname{supp}c\) of size \(s\ge2\). The event is \(eQ_c=0\) with \(Q_c=\sum_{b\in S}c_b\ell_b^2\). The cycle ends with the stratum bounded, or with the support size where the method stops.

Notation

As in the spread lemma, forms are families of row functions: \(\ell_b\leftrightarrow(f^b_x)_x\) and \(e\leftrightarrow(g_x)_x\), each defined up to constants. The triple component of \(eQ_c\) on pigeons \(\{x,y,z\}\) has third differences, over disjoint label pairs \(P_x,P_y,P_z\), \[ \sum_{\rm cyc}\delta g_x(P_x)\,C\bigl(u_y(P_y),u_z(P_z)\bigr)=0,\qquad u_x(P)=(\delta f^b_x(P))_{b\in S},\quad C(u,v)=\sum_bc_bu^bv^b . \tag{S1} \] The \(\ell_b\) are independent across \(b\) and uniform in \(A_1\), as drawn in the selector check; both probability bounds below use this. Write \(H_{yz}=\sum_bc_bf^b_y\otimes f^b_z\), a function on label pairs, for fixed representatives of the row functions (uniform ones in the probability parts). Then (S1) reads \(\sum_{\rm cyc}\delta g_x\,\Delta^2_{P_y,P_z}H_{yz}=0\).

Supports two to four

Call pigeon \(x\) good for \(S\) if the \(s+1\) functions \(\{f^b_x\}_{b\in S}\cup\{1\}\) are linearly independent on every set of \(n-8\) labels. Then the vectors \(u_x(P)\), over pairs \(P\) inside any such set, span \(\mathbb F_3^S\).

Lemma (small support). If \(2\le s\) and at least three pigeons are good for \(S\), then \(eQ_c=0\) implies \(e=0\), for every \(c\) with \(\operatorname{supp}c=S\) and every \(e\). With support one, \(e=\mu\ell_b\) is a solution, which the spread lemma handles.

Proof.

  • Each good \(g_x\) lies in the span of the \(f^b_x\). Let \(x,y,z\) be good. Choose disjoint pairs \(P_y,P_z\) with \(C(u_y,u_z)\ne0\), possible by spanning. For every pair \(P_x\) in the \(n-4\) remaining labels, (S1) gives \(\delta g_x(P_x)=\lambda(u_x(P_x))\) for a linear functional \(\lambda\). So \(g_x-\sum_b\lambda_bf^b_x\) is constant there. Any two labels lie in such a set. The coefficients are unique on the intersection of two such sets, which has at least \(n-8\) labels, by goodness. So \(g_x=\sum_b\kappa^b_xf^b_x+\text{const}\).
  • The coefficients vanish. Substitute into (S1) for good \(x,y,z\). The resulting trilinear form in \((u_x,u_y,u_z)\) vanishes on realizable triples, which span in each argument with the other two fixed. So it vanishes identically. For \(b\ne b_0\), the monomial \(u^b_xu^{b_0}_yu^{b_0}_z\) arises only from \(\kappa^b_xc_{b_0}\). Since \(s\ge2\), some \(b_0\ne b\) has \(c_{b_0}\ne0\), so \(\kappa^b_x=0\), and \(g_x\) is constant.
  • Other pigeons. For any pigeon \(w\), take two good pigeons \(y,z\ne w\). Then (S1) gives \(\delta g_w(P_w)C(u_y,u_z)=0\). Choosing pairs avoiding \(P_w\) with \(C\ne0\) gives \(\delta g_w=0\). \(\square\)

For uniform row functions, pigeon \(x\) fails to be good with probability at most \(\binom n8\,3^{s+9-n}\): there are \(3^s\) nonzero coefficient patterns, and each gives a constant on \(n-8\) labels with probability \(3^{1-(n-8)}\). So fewer than three pigeons are good with probability at most \(\binom{n+1}2\bigl(\binom n83^{s+9-n}\bigr)^{n-1}=3^{-(1-o(1))n^2}\) for \(s\le4\). A union over the at most \(M^4\) supports keeps this superpolynomially small. The event depends only on the \(\ell_b\), so it covers every \(c\) and \(e\) at once.

Supports five and more

Lemma (rank). Suppose that for every pigeon \(x\) there are pigeons \(y\ne z\), both \(\ne x\), such that \(H_{yz}\) has three \(5\times5\) blocks of rank \(5\). Each block has disjoint row and column label sets, and the three blocks use 30 distinct labels. Then \(eQ_c=0\) implies \(e=0\).

Proof. Suppose \(g_x\) is not constant, and choose \(P_x\) with \(\delta g_x(P_x)\ne0\). Take \(y,z\) as assumed, and a block \(R\times C\) of rank five avoiding the two labels of \(P_x\). By (S1), for pairs \(P_y\subseteq R\) and \(P_z\subseteq C\), which are disjoint from each other and from \(P_x\), \[ \Delta^2_{P_y,P_z}\bigl(H_{yz}+\delta g_x^{-1}(g_y\otimes\eta+\theta\otimes g_z)\bigr)=0, \] where \(\eta(j)=H_{xz}(p,j)-H_{xz}(p',j)\) and \(\theta(j)=H_{xy}(p,j)-H_{xy}(p',j)\) for \(P_x=(p,p')\). A function on \(R\times C\) whose second differences all vanish has the form \(a(j)+b(j')\). So \(H_{yz}\) restricted to \(R\times C\) has rank at most \(2+2=4\), for every choice of representatives, a contradiction. So every \(g_x\) is constant and \(e=0\). \(\square\)

For a fixed \((S,c)\) with \(s\ge5\), a block equals \(F_R\operatorname{diag}(c)F_C^{\mathsf T}\) with independent uniform \(5\times s\) matrices. If \(F_R\operatorname{diag}(c)\) has rank five, which happens with probability at least \(q_0=\prod_{i=1}^5(1-3^{-i})\approx0.561\), then the block is a uniform \(5\times5\) matrix and is invertible with probability \(q_0\). So each block has rank five with probability at least \(q_0^2>0.31\). Blocks on disjoint labels are independent. With \(\lfloor n/10\rfloor\) of them, a pair \((y,z)\) fails with probability \(3^{-\Omega(n)}\). Disjoint pigeon pairs are independent, so a pigeon \(x\) finds no good pair with probability \(3^{-\Omega(n^2)}\), and a union over the \(n+1\) pigeons keeps this bound.

Taking \(k\times k\) blocks with \(k=\lfloor n/12\rfloor\), five disjoint ones, improves this for large \(s\). Write \(A=F_R\operatorname{diag}(c)\). Then \(\Pr[\operatorname{rank}A=r]\lesssim3^{-(k-r)(s-r)}\), and given that rank, the block \(AF_C^{\mathsf T}\) has rank at most four with probability \(\lesssim3^{-(r-4)(k-4)}\). The sum over \(r\) is dominated near \(r\approx(s+4)/2\), which gives an exponent of \((s-4)(4k-s-12)/4\) for \(s\le k\). So a \(k\times k\) block has rank at most four with probability at most \(C\,k\,3^{-\frac34(k-4)(\min(s,k)-4)}\). So the failure probability for fixed \((S,c)\) is \(3^{-\Omega(n^2(\min(s,n)-4))}\). Against the \((2M)^s\) choices of \((S,c)\), the union bound closes for \(5\le s\le c\,n^3/\log M\) and some constant \(c>0\).

Supports above \(2\gamma_1\): conditional on a multiplication bound

For \(s\ge2\gamma_1+2\) the combination \(Q_c\) is nearly uniform on \(A_2\). The squares span \(A_2\), since \(\ell m=(\ell+m)^2-(\ell-m)^2\) over \(\mathbb F_3\). So a nonzero \(\chi\in A_2^*\) defines a nonzero quadratic form \(\ell\mapsto\chi(\ell^2)\) of some rank \(r\ge1\), and \(|\mathbb E\,\omega^{\chi(c_b\ell^2)}|=3^{-r/2}\). There are at most \(3^{r\gamma_1}\) forms of rank \(r\). For any subspace \(W\subseteq A_2\) of codimension \(k\), \[ \Pr[Q_c\in W]\le3^{-k}\Bigl(1+\sum_{r\ge1}3^{r\gamma_1-rs/2}\Bigr)\le2\cdot3^{-k}. \] Apply this to \(W=\operatorname{Ann}_{A_2}(e)\), whose codimension is \(\dim(eA_2)\), and take a union over the \(3^{\gamma_1}\) choices of \(e\) and the at most \(3^M\) choices of \(c\). The stratum closes for these supports if \[ k_{\min}=\min_{e\ne0}\dim(eA_2)\ \ge\ M+\gamma_1+\omega(1). \tag{MM} \] The two regimes overlap, because \(2\gamma_1\approx2n^2\) is below \(cn^3/\log M\) for large \(n\).

Evidence for (MM). At \(n=6\): \(\dim(eA_2)=266\) for a variable and for a column form, 461 for ten random \(e\), and 391 to 452 for ten forms on one pigeon. The bound needed near the threshold is \(M+\gamma_1\approx110\). A proof sketch by the same triple method: if \(g_x\) is not constant, then (S1) with \(Q\) in place of \(Q_c\) determines each pair component \(q_{yz}\) of \(q\in\operatorname{Ann}_{A_2}(e)\), \(y,z\ne x\). It fixes \(q_{yz}\) modulo row, column and diagonal parts from \(q_{xy}\) and \(q_{xz}\). The free data are the \(q_{xy}\), the row, column and diagonal parts, and the same-pigeon components \(\{y,y\}\), each \(O(n^3)\) in total. So \(\dim\operatorname{Ann}_{A_2}(e)=O(n^3)\), and \(k_{\min}\ge\gamma_2-O(n^3)\). Since \(\gamma_2\approx n^4/2\), this is above \(M+\gamma_1\) for \(M\) up to the threshold, which is about \(n^4/6\). The sketch is not yet written out, so this regime is conditional.

Finite check

At \(n=6\), \(\dim\operatorname{Ann}_{A_1}(Q_c)=0\) in all 20 samples for each support size 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 16, 35 and 70, with random nonzero \(c\). This is below the lemmas' ranges, which need \(n\) large. Files: research/results/odd_prime_span_one_20260923/ (support_probe.py, mult_dims.py and JSON outputs).

Assessment and next step

The span-one stratum is now proved for supports from two up to \(cn^3/\log M\), with failure probability \(3^{-\Omega(n^2)}\) after the union. It is conditional on (MM) above \(2\gamma_1\). The methods are the spread lemma's third differences, and a rank bound for the pair functions \(H_{yz}\).

The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer has two parts. First, write out the proof of (MM), the bound \(\dim\operatorname{Ann}_{A_2}(e)=O(n^3)\). Then extend the rank lemma to span dimension two, where \(e_1Q_1+e_2Q_2=0\) gives two terms per cycle of (S1). The rank argument should carry over with block rank six, because the right side then has rank at most \(2\cdot2+2\). The cycle ends with (MM) proved and the span-two stratum bounded, or with the obstruction.

Verification gate. Re-read: the spread lemma (component decomposition, third differences, robustness counting) and the first-moment entry (kernel criterion, strata). The block probability \(q_0\) was computed. A claim search (span one stratum, squares, annihilator, rank, block) found no restatement. The nearest record is the rank-one relative cubic-kernel exclusion, the first stratum of the degree-three question for affine generators over \(\mathbb F_2\) in exterior form. It is the analogue for different generators, not the same statement. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed (S1), the spanning, gluing and monomial steps, the rank-four derivation, \(q_0\), the Gauss-sum and rank-count bounds and the (MM) union. It found the \(k\times k\) block exponent too strong by \((s-4)^2/4\), now corrected with the sum over the rank of \(F_R\operatorname{diag}(c)\); the conclusions survive. It also required the support condition, independence across \(b\), fixed representatives, the union over \(x\), the meta and title qualified, and the (MM) count completed. All were adopted.

Route review: the selector line proves random cases one degree up; its deterministic core points to a structure-versus-randomness dichotomy

23 September 2026 · Route review · The line is productive but random; the next step states its deterministic conditions and matches their failures to recorded endpoints. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

The line's general claim. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. Since the density-principle entry, the thread reads its core statement as Conjecture SR, relative semi-regularity, for collectively robustly wide constraints. The last four cycles developed its first nonlinear case, random selectors \(1-L^2\) over \(\mathbb F_3\) at degree three:

  • exact thresholds with no early fall (selector check);
  • a kernel criterion and a union bound (first-moment entry);
  • the spread event (spread lemma);
  • the span-one stratum (span-one entry).

What the goal needs. The logarithmic-prefix reduction needs Conjecture SR at degree about \((4p-1)\) times the constraint degree \(h=(p-1)(k+1)\), not at \(h+1\). It also needs it for constraints whose forms come from a refutation and are not random. The prefix sets are the only choice left to us.

Falsification attempt

The proofs so far are deterministic statements under stated conditions, plus a probability bound for those conditions. The conditions used are:

  1. each constraint's row functions are robust on at least four pigeons (spread lemma);
  2. small groups of constraints have jointly robust row functions (supports two to four);
  3. the pair functions \(H_{yz}\) of every small combination have rank-five blocks (supports five and more);
  4. the squares are independent in \(A_2\);
  5. the multiplication bound (MM).

Every early fall in the record violates one of them:

  • the Boolean-image control violates robustness;
  • the occupancy predicates have forms in an \(n\)-dimensional subalgebra, so their squares become dependent in \(A_2\) after about \(n^2/2\) constraints (refuted from 8 to 21 at degree two);
  • column forms square to zero;
  • the three-selector control uses dependent forms.

No recorded example satisfies all five conditions and falls early. That is consistent with a dichotomy but does not prove one.

Assessment of this line

The line is productive: exact evidence, a working reduction, and two strata proved with new methods (third differences on triple components, and a rank bound for pair functions). But it proves only the random calibration, and only at one degree above the generators. The two gaps between it and the goal are untouched:

  • higher degree, where the kernel tuples become multipliers of degree \(D-h\) and the triple method would need higher mixed differences on larger pigeon sets;
  • adversarial families.

Continuing stratum by stratum at degree three would refine a random special case. The part of this line that bears on the second gap is that its proofs are deterministic under explicit pseudorandomness conditions. That suggests a structure-versus-randomness dichotomy. A family that satisfies the conditions has no early fall. A family that violates one has a structural feature: few robust pigeons, dependent row functions, low-rank pair functions, or a small span. Structural features of that kind are what the recorded endpoints exploit: low nonlocal dimension, narrow and literal-type blocks, the graph criteria. This is a new route for adversarial families, and the only one the thread has for them.

Next step: state the dichotomy at one degree above and test its structured side

The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer is to write the deterministic theorem at degree \(h+1\) for quadratic selectors: if a family satisfies conditions 1 to 5 for all small subfamilies, it has no degree-three fall. The spread and span-one proofs already give this for the strata done; the higher-span strata remain. Then classify the ways a family can violate each condition. For each violation, check against the record whether a recorded endpoint applies to the constraints involved, or whether it can be removed by choosing the prefix sets, the one freedom the reduction leaves. The cycle ends with the dichotomy stated and each violation type either matched to an endpoint or named as a new obstruction. A violation type no endpoint handles would be the thread's sharpest open case.

Verification gate. Re-read: the four entries of the line, the density-principle entry and the logarithmic-prefix reduction's degree requirement. The claim search for structure-versus-randomness or deterministic pseudorandomness conditions found nothing similar. This review proves nothing new and registers no claim.

Structured side, first test: every overloaded sub-span forces a fall, and at these sizes nothing else does

23 September 2026 · Finite check · Selectors over \(\mathbb F_3\) at degree three, \(n=6\), forms in random subspaces of dimension 5 to 20. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The selector-line review proposed a dichotomy. Families meeting the deterministic conditions of the selector proofs have no early fall. Families violating one have a structural feature, to be matched to the record. The first condition to test needs no randomness to violate: the forms spread over enough dimensions. A family whose forms lie in a small subspace \(V\) violates it, as the occupancy predicates do. How do such families fall: by a count relative to \(V\), which would make the structured side tractable, or with no count? The test ends with measured first falls and refutations against the relative counts.

Counts relative to a span

Let the linear parts \(\ell_b\) be uniform among the nonzero vectors of a random \(d\)-dimensional subspace \(V\) of cell forms, with random constants. For a subfamily \(T\) whose forms span \(V_T\), of dimension \(d_T\), the map \(V_T\otimes\operatorname{span}\{\ell_b^2\}_{b\in T}\to V_T^3\), \((a_b)\mapsto\sum a_b\ell_b^2\), has the Frobenius kernel \(\{(\lambda_b\ell_b)\}\) of dimension \(|T|\). By dimension count it has a larger kernel once \[ |T|\,(d_T-1)>\dim V_T^3,\qquad \dim V_T^3\le\binom{d_T+2}3-d_T, \tag{OV} \] the bound because every cube vanishes in \(A\) in characteristic three. Call such a \(T\) overloaded. For \(d_T=2\), (OV) is \(|T|\ge3\): three forms in a two-dimensional span, the recorded three-selector control. For \(d_T=3\) it is \(|T|\ge4\). The global count is \(M_3=\dim(A_1V^2)/(\gamma_1-1)\) from the selector check. The \(V\)-internal count, \(T\) the whole family, is forced from \(M_V^{+}=\lfloor\dim V^3/(d-1)\rfloor+1\).

Measurements

Exact at \(n=6\), \(D=3\). Dimensions are GF(3) ranks in \(A\). The fall excess \(E(M)\) is the dimension of the closure's part of degree at most two, minus its no-fall value \(280+M\), where 280 is the base's own value, recomputed. It was scanned linearly in \(M\) up to the first refutation. The table also records the smallest linearly dependent subset among the forms up to the first fall. The squares were independent in \(A_2\) at every first fall (rank \(=M\)).

The earlier runs, superseded_*.json, contained degenerate constraints (a zero linear part with constant 0 is the constraint \(1=0\)) and used a bisection for the fall that the excess, not being monotone, does not justify.

Reading

  • When no small subfamily is overloaded, the family collapses at a count. At \(d=20\) the global count \(M_3\) binds, and fall and refutation coincide at 76, as for uniform forms. At \(d=12\) the \(V\)-internal count binds, and fall and refutation coincide within one of its forced value 33, half the global one. This suggests, from two dimensions only, that the count to use is the minimum over the spans the family generates.
  • Every earlier fall comes with an overloaded small subfamily. The early falls at \(d=5\) and \(d=8\) start with a small excess (1 at first) and are preceded by a dependent subset of size 3 or 4. A dependent triple spans two dimensions and a dependent four-set spans at most three, both overloaded by (OV). At \(d=12\), seed 1, the smallest dependent subset has size five, spanning four dimensions, and (OV) needs six forms there; that run falls only at the whole-span count. At these sizes nothing else produced a fall. Two cautions: the table shows an overloaded subfamily exists before each early fall, not that it causes the fall, and \(\dim V_T^3\) was not computed for the subfamilies.
  • What this suggests for the reduction (heuristic). The structured side looks like "some subfamily overloads its own span". The logarithmic-prefix images have degree \(h\). The analogous overload at degree \(D\) needs about \(\dim V_T^{D}/\dim V_T^{D-h}\) images inside one span \(V_T\). That number is of order \(d_T^{\,h}\), which is \(n^{\Theta(\log d_T)}\) and so polynomial only for bounded \(d_T\). So an adversary can overload only spans of bounded dimension with polynomially many images. What their consequences are, and whether the base survives them, is the open structured case.

Assessment and next step

The structured side's first test supports the dichotomy's shape and sharpens it. The violation to study is an overloaded span of bounded dimension, of which the three-selector control is the smallest instance. A count relative to each span decides when it bites.

The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer is to plant \(t\) selectors whose forms lie in a fixed two-dimensional span \(\langle a,b\rangle\) into a uniform family at \(n=6\). Measure the consequences and the refutation threshold. The prediction: the overload's consequences stay inside the span. That means affine relations pinning \(a\) and \(b\) to values allowed by the planted constraints, since three or more selectors on a two-dimensional span leave few allowed value pairs. The rest of the family then behaves as a uniform family over the base conditioned on those at most two affine equations. So the refutation threshold should equal the graded count of the base conditioned on \(a,b\), computed from its own quotient dimensions. The uniform family's threshold is 76 (selector check). The conditioned count is below 76 by a computable amount. A threshold far below it would falsify the prediction and show that an overloaded span propagates beyond itself. The cycle ends with that comparison and, if it holds, a proof that the consequences of an overloaded bounded span are affine relations inside it.

Verification gate. Re-read: the selector-line review, the selector check, the three-selector control's identity, and the quotient-rank exclusion's statement as summarized in the working context. The relative counts are exact dimensions from the same algebra construction as the spread-lemma probes, which reproduce \(\gamma_1=35\) and \(\gamma_3=2569\). The no-fall value 280 is the base's degree-two closure rank from the degree split. A fresh-context reviewer found degenerate constraints in the first runs (a zero linear part with constant 0, and one vacuous constraint), a non-monotone excess under the bisection, an unsupported attribution of the early falls to triples, loose matching claims, reduction arithmetic that was off (\(d^h\) is polynomial only for bounded \(d\)), a letter-code name, and a next-step test whose outcomes were all compatible with it. The runs were redone with nonzero forms and a linear scan, the reading was rebuilt on the new data, and the test now has a quantitative prediction.

Constraints on a bounded span are equivalent to conditioning on their allowed patterns; a planted overload matches the conditioned count exactly

23 September 2026 · Working lemma and a finite check · Planted point-pin at \(n=6\), \(D=3\), two seeds. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The relative-span entry found every early selector fall preceded by an overloaded span. It predicted that an overloaded two-dimensional span only pins its own forms, so the rest of the family behaves as over the base conditioned on them. This cycle tests that prediction quantitatively and proves the mechanism. It ends with the comparison and the lemma.

Planted overload: measurement

At \(n=6\), \(D=3\), over \(\mathbb F_3\): take random cell forms \(a,b\) and a target \(v\in\mathbb F_3^2\). Plant the eight selectors \(1-(\alpha a+\beta b-c)^2\), one for each direction \((\alpha,\beta)\in\{(1,0),(0,1),(1,1),(1,2)\}\) and each value \(c\ne\alpha v_1+\beta v_2\). They forbid every value pair of \((a,b)\) except \(v\). Then add uniform selectors.

0both5353\(\lceil1682/32\rceil=53\)
1both535353

The conditioned base has quotient dimensions \(34,427,2109\) through degrees one to three, so graded dimensions \(\gamma'=(1,33,393,1682)\). Its count is \(\lceil\gamma'_3/(\gamma'_1-1)\rceil\), as in the selector check. In this run (\(n=6\), \(D=3\), two seeds, \(P\) a single point) the overload derives the affine relations at degree three, and the rest of the family is refuted exactly where the conditioned base's count says. Files: research/results/odd_prime_planted_overload_20260923/planted.py, planted_n6.json.

The mechanism

The mechanism is an elementary fact about functions of finitely many affine forms. It is stated here for use on the structured side, not as a new mechanism.

Lemma (bounded-span equivalence). Let \(y_1,\dots,y_d\) be affine forms in the Boolean variables over \(\mathbb F_p\). Take constraints \(c_j=c_j(y)\), polynomials of degree at most \(e\) in \(y\), and let \(P\subseteq\mathbb F_p^d\) be their common zero set, the allowed patterns. Then the base plus the constraints derives every polynomial \(f(y)\) vanishing on \(P\), of degree at most \((p-1)d\) in \(y\), in PC of degree at most \((p-1)d+e\). Conversely each \(c_j\) vanishes on \(P\). So at that degree the constraints are equivalent to the ideal \(I(P)\) of polynomials in \(y\) vanishing on \(P\). If \(P=\varnothing\) this is a refutation. If \(P=\{v\}\), it derives \(y_i-v_i\).

Proof. The ring \(R=\mathbb F_p[y]/(y_i^p-y_i)\) is the algebra of all functions \(\mathbb F_p^d\to\mathbb F_p\), a product of copies of \(\mathbb F_p\). So the ideal the \(c_j\) generate in \(R\) is the ideal of functions vanishing on their common zero set: \(f=\sum_jh_jc_j\) in \(R\), with each \(h_j\) reduced, of degree at most \((p-1)d\). In \(\mathbb F_p[y]\), \(f-\sum_jh_jc_j\) lies in the ideal of the \(y_i^p-y_i\). It has degree at most \(\Delta=(p-1)d+e\). Reduction by these generators does not raise degree, so its certificate has degree at most \(\Delta\). Substituting the affine forms, \(y_i^p-y_i=\sum_ka_k(x_k^p-x_k)\) is derivable from Booleanity at degree \(p\), since \(x^p-x=(x^2-x)(x^{p-2}+\dots+1)\). So the whole identity is a PC derivation of degree at most \(\Delta\). \(\square\)

For selectors, \(e=p-1\), so the degree bound is \((p-1)(d+1)\): six for \(d=2\) at \(p=3\). So the lemma gives the equivalence at degree six. That degree three already suffices in the planted runs is measured, not explained by the lemma.

What density limits

Pinning a bounded span costs density, but density below one does not forbid it. Two selectors on one form, \(L\ne0\) and \(L\ne1\), pin \(L=2\) at degree two with total density \(2/3\). The lemma applies to every allowed set \(P\), not only to the overloaded spans of the relative-span entry. What density limits is how much can be pinned. In the uniform measure on patterns of a span, the forbidden sets of the constraints on it must cover the complement of \(P\). Their densities therefore sum to at least \(1-|P|p^{-d}\), and a point-pin costs at least \(1-p^{-d}\ge2/3\). With total density below one, at most one form can be pinned to a point. Every other bounded span keeps an allowed set of positive density. This measure is on patterns of the span, not on Boolean points: a nonempty \(P\) does not by itself mean that some Boolean assignment realizes an allowed pattern.

The overloads of the relative-span entry need more. For selectors at \(p=3\) with \(d_T=2\), the condition \(|T|(d_T-1)>\dim V_T^3\) needs \(|T|\ge3\) when \(\dim V_T^3=2\) (the monomials \(a^2b,ab^2\); cubes vanish), which holds for generic \(a,b\) but is not proved here. That is total density at least one. For the logarithmic-prefix images no separate count is needed. An image whose forms all lie in a span of dimension \(d\) is a polynomial in the \(d\) forms, so modulo the Frobenius relations it is a function on \(\mathbb F_p^d\), whatever its degree \(h\). By the lemma, a family of images confined to one span is equivalent, at degree \((p-1)(d+1)\), to conditioning on its allowed set \(P\). The density bound above then applies: with total density below one, such families can pin at most one form to a point and otherwise leave positive-density pattern sets. A first draft of this paragraph estimated the images needed for an overload as \(d^h/h!\). That estimate was wrong: in \(A\) the span generates at most \(\mathbb F_3[y]/(y_i^3)\), which vanishes above degree \(2d\).

Assessment and next step

What this cycle establishes is scoped. Constraints on a bounded span are equivalent, at degree \((p-1)(d+1)\), to conditioning on their allowed patterns (lemma). A planted point-pin makes the rest of the family follow the conditioned count exactly (measured at \(n=6\)). For constraints confined to a bounded span, selectors or prefix images, density below one allows only positive-density pattern restrictions and at most one point-pin; the overloads found before the early falls need density at least one for selectors. So the structured side seen so far adds no new obstruction. The core statement's remaining content is its pseudorandom side at the degrees the reduction needs, \(D\approx(4p-1)h\), far above \(h+1\).

The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer is the pseudorandom side one step higher, at degree \(h+2\), for selectors at \(p=3\) (\(D=4\)). There the kernel tuples are quadratic multipliers. The triple method's analogue uses four-pigeon components of \(A_4\) and fourth mixed differences. This is also the degree where the recorded degree-three obstruction stopped the affine first moment. First measure the \(D=4\) thresholds for random selectors at the smallest board where the base survives degree four. By the random-conditioning law that is \(n\ge8\); the collision quotient there has about \(4.6\times10^5\) degree-four columns, so compute its size first and use \(n=8\) only if it fits. Compare with the graded count \(\gamma_4/\gamma_2\)-type prediction, with Frobenius and Koszul corrections. The cycle ends with that comparison, or with the size estimate showing it out of reach and the four-pigeon identity derived instead.

Verification gate. Re-read: the relative-span entry (the overload condition and its data) and the three-selector control's identity, which is the case \(d=2\) of the lemma. The lemma's proof uses only that finite function algebras are products of fields, degree-compatible reduction, and the Frobenius relations derived from Booleanity. The planted measurements are exact closures with the recorded driver. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed the lemma (a Nullstellensatz derivation from Booleanity only), the planted construction and all numbers. It found the density paragraph wrong: two selectors on one form pin it below density one, the overload condition gives no lower bound on \(|T|\) from an upper bound on \(\dim V_T^3\), and the union-bound measure is on patterns, not Boolean points. It also required the claims scoped to the runs, and the next step re-aimed, since the image arithmetic already decides the overload question. All were adopted.

At degree four, random squares follow the semi-regular count in a run up to the fill point, and the spread lemma extends to quadratic multipliers

23 September 2026 · Working lemma and a finite check · Selector squares over \(\mathbb F_3\) at degree four. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The planted-overload entry left the pseudorandom side of the core statement as its content, at the degrees the reduction needs, \(D\approx(4p-1)h\). The selector results so far are at degree three. This cycle goes one degree higher, to \(D=4\) over \(\mathbb F_3\), where the multipliers are quadratic. Its first question: does the exact semi-regular count, which gave the degree-three thresholds, still hold? The count is corrected for the Frobenius and Koszul syzygies. Its second question: does the degree-three spread lemma's method prove the single-square part of that count? The cycle ends with the comparison and with the lemma or the point where the method stops.

Size check

The PC closure at \(n=8\), \(D=4\), the smallest board where the base survives degree four, has \(502{,}435\) collision-free monomial columns, \(459{,}270\) of them in degree four. A dense GF(3) elimination of that size needs tens of gigabytes, beyond the 10 GB limit, so the refutation threshold itself was not measured. The graded question is smaller. \(A_k\) splits by the pigeon multiset of its monomials, and each component's relations \(R_i\cdot m\) stay inside it. So normal forms can be computed one component at a time: at most \(1680\) columns at \(n=8\), with no global elimination. This reproduces the recorded degree-three counts, \(\lceil\gamma_3/(\gamma_1-1)\rceil=76,185\) at \(n=6,7\).

The degree-four count and its test

For \(M\) linear forms \(\ell_b\) put \(\Phi_4:A_2^M\to A_4\), \((a_b)\mapsto\sum_ba_b\ell_b^2\). Since \(\ell_b^3=0\), its kernel contains the Frobenius syzygies \(\ell_bA_1e_b\). It also contains the Koszul syzygies \(\ell_c^2e_b-\ell_b^2e_c\). The semi-regular model says there are no others below the fill point, that is, \(\operatorname{rank}\Phi_4=\min\bigl(\gamma_4,\ M(\gamma_2-\gamma_1)-\binom M2\bigr)\). This is the \(t^4\) coefficient of \(\mathrm{HS}_A(t)\bigl((1-t^2)/(1-t^3)\bigr)^M\), whose \(t^3\) coefficient gives the degree-three count. The fill point is the least \(M\) at which that coefficient is nonpositive.

In one run at \(n=7\) (one seed, six values of \(M\)) the rank equals the model's value at every tested \(M\), through the fill point: \(34260\) at \(M=40\) and the full \(\gamma_4=34950\) at \(M=41\). So for \(M\le40\) the kernel has the dimension \(M\gamma_1+\binom M2\) that the Frobenius and Koszul syzygies would span if independent; their independence was not checked separately. At the fill point the kernel is larger, as it must be. For every sampled form \(\operatorname{Ann}_{A_1}(\ell)=0\), so \(\dim\ell A_1=\gamma_1\) (lin_ann.py, lin_ann.txt). So at \(n=7,8\) the sampled squares have \(\operatorname{Ann}_{A_2}(\ell^2)=\ell A_1\). At \(n=6\) each has six further annihilators, so the model already fails there at \(M=1\). This small-board effect lies below the lemma's range. The degree-four graded fill comes far earlier than the degree-three one. The refutation threshold at degree four was not measured (see the size check), and a graded fill is not by itself a refutation.
