Component identities

Notation as in the spread lemma: \(\ell\) has row functions \(f_i\), and \(\delta f(P)=f(j)-f(j')\) for a label pair \(P=(j,j')\). A quadratic \(q\in A_2\) has two kinds of components. On two distinct pigeons \(\{x,y\}\) the component is a function \(h_{xy}\) on injections \(\{x,y\}\to[n]\), modulo functions of one coordinate. Write \(H_{xy}(P_x,P_y)\) for its mixed second difference over disjoint pairs. On a repeated pigeon \(\{a,a\}\) the component is a function \(h_{aa}\) on 2-sets of labels, modulo the stars \(\{j,j'\}\mapsto\varphi(j)+\varphi(j')\), since \(R_ax_{aj}=\sum_{j'\ne j}x_{aj}x_{aj'}\).

In \(A_4\), the component on four distinct pigeons is the space of functions on injections modulo functions of three coordinates. The mixed fourth difference over four disjoint pairs kills the latter. The component on \(\{a,a,c,d\}\) is the space of functions of an \(a\)-edge and a label for each of \(c\) and \(d\). Its relations are stars in the edge and functions independent of \(j_c\) or of \(j_d\). The operator \[ \square(j_1,j_2,j_3,j_4)\,e=e(j_1j_2)-e(j_2j_4)+e(j_4j_3)-e(j_3j_1), \] on four distinct labels, kills stars. Applied with first differences in \(c\) and \(d\), it kills all these relations. On products, \(\square(f\otimes f)=\delta f(j_1,j_4)\,\delta f(j_2,j_3)\). Since \(\ell^2=2\sum_{u<v}\ell_u\ell_vx_ux_v\), expanding \(q\ell^2=0\) gives two identities. The first holds for distinct pigeons \(a,b,c,d\) and pairwise disjoint pairs: \[ \sum_{\{X,Y\}}H_X(P_X)\,\delta f_Y(P_Y)=0, \tag{I4} \] the sum over the three ways of splitting \(\{a,b,c,d\}\) into two pairs, each counted in both orders (six terms), with \(\delta f_Y\) the product of the two first differences. The common factor 2 is dropped here and in (IR). The second holds on \(\{a,a,c,d\}\), with \(P=(j_1,j_4)\), \(P'=(j_2,j_3)\): \[ \square h_{aa}\,\delta f_c\,\delta f_d+\bigl(H_{ac}(P,P_c)\delta f_a(P')+\delta f_a(P)H_{ac}(P',P_c)\bigr)\delta f_d+\bigl(H_{ad}(P,P_d)\delta f_a(P')+\delta f_a(P)H_{ad}(P',P_d)\bigr)\delta f_c+H_{cd}(P_c,P_d)\,\delta f_a(P)\,\delta f_a(P')=0. \tag{IR} \] Both were checked numerically against direct products at \(n=8\), in 200 random \((q,\ell)\). Both operators vanished on 200 sampled relation rows each; for \(\square\) these include 82 star relations \(R_a x_{aj}x_{cj_c}x_{dj_d}\) (check_identities.py, check_identities_n8.txt).

The degree-four spread lemma

Call a row function \(f\) \(\rho\)-robust if it is nonconstant on \([n]\setminus X\) for every label set \(X\) with \(|X|\le\rho\). So for every such \(X\) it has a pair outside \(X\) with nonzero difference.

Lemma (degree-four spread lemma). Let \(\ell\in A_1\). If at least seven pigeons have \(12\)-robust row functions, then \(\operatorname{Ann}_{A_2}(\ell^2)=\ell A_1\). (This forces \(n\ge14\). The proof never uses that there is exactly one more pigeon than holes, so it holds for any numbers of pigeons and holes.)

Proof. \(\ell A_1\subseteq\operatorname{Ann}(\ell^2)\) since \(\ell^3=0\). Let \(q\ell^2=0\). Let \(\mathcal R\) be the set of robust pigeons. A frame is \(F=(c,d,P_c,P_d)\) with \(c\ne d\) in \(\mathcal R\), \(P_c,P_d\) disjoint and \(\delta f_c(P_c)\,\delta f_d(P_d)\ne0\). Put \(L_F=P_c\cup P_d\), \(\Lambda_F=[n]\setminus L_F\), \(\Xi_F=\{\text{pigeons}\}\setminus\{c,d\}\).

Step 1 (local form). Fix a frame. For \(a,b\in\Xi_F\) distinct and disjoint pairs \(P_a,P_b\subseteq\Lambda_F\), divide (I4) by \(\Delta_F=\delta f_c(P_c)\,\delta f_d(P_d)\): \[ H_{ab}(P_a,P_b)=\kappa\,\delta f_a\delta f_b+u_a(P_a)\,\delta f_b(P_b)+\delta f_a(P_a)\,u_b(P_b), \] with \(\kappa=-H_{cd}(P_c,P_d)/\Delta_F\) and \(u_x(P)=-H_{xc}(P,P_c)/\delta f_c(P_c)-H_{xd}(P,P_d)/\delta f_d(P_d)\). Now \(H_{xc}(P,P_c)=\psi(j)-\psi(j')\) for \(\psi(j)=h_{xc}(j,c_1)-h_{xc}(j,c_2)\), so \(u_x=\delta\tilde u_x\) for a row function \(\tilde u_x\) on \(\Lambda_F\) that does not depend on the partner pigeon. Put \(g^F_x=\tilde u_x+2\kappa f_x\) (note \(4\kappa=\kappa\) in \(\mathbb F_3\)). Then \(H_{ab}\) is the mixed second difference of \(f_a\otimes g^F_b+g^F_a\otimes f_b\), the \(\{a,b\}\) component of \(\ell g^F\). No robustness of \(a,b\) is used. A function on injections into a label set of size at least four whose mixed second differences all vanish is separable. Indeed, \(h(j,k)-h(j',k)\) is then independent of \(k\) and additive in \((j,j')\), so it equals \(\alpha(j)-\alpha(j')\), and \(h-\alpha\) depends on \(k\) only. So on \(\Lambda_F\) the pieces \(h_{ab}\) and \((\ell g^F)_{ab}\) agree modulo separable functions, for all distinct \(a,b\in\Xi_F\).

Step 2 (uniqueness). Let \(\Lambda\) be a label set and \(\Xi\) a pigeon set containing three pigeons of \(\mathcal R\), with \(|[n]\setminus\Lambda|\le8\). Suppose row functions \(k_x\) (\(x\in\Xi\)) make \(f_a\otimes k_b+k_a\otimes f_b\) separable on \(\Lambda\) for all distinct \(a,b\in\Xi\). Then every \(k_x\) is constant on \(\Lambda\). Indeed, \(\delta f_a(P)\delta k_b(Q)+\delta k_a(P)\delta f_b(Q)=0\) for disjoint pairs in \(\Lambda\). For three robust \(a,b,e\in\Xi\) and pairwise disjoint pairs with nonzero differences, the ratios \(r=\delta k/\delta f\) satisfy \(r_a=-r_b=r_e=-r_a\). They exist since each pair avoids at most \(8+2+2=12\) labels. So \(r_a(P)=0\) for every such pair \(P\) of a robust \(a\). For any \(b\in\Xi\) and pair \(Q\subseteq\Lambda\), choose robust \(a\ne b\) and \(P\subseteq\Lambda\setminus Q\) with \(\delta f_a(P)\ne0\), avoiding at most 10 labels. Then \(\delta f_a(P)\delta k_b(Q)=-\delta k_a(P)\delta f_b(Q)=0\).

Step 3 (gluing). For frames \(F,F'\), apply Step 2 to \(k=g^F-g^{F'}\) on \(\Lambda_F\cap\Lambda_{F'}\) and \(\Xi_F\cap\Xi_{F'}\). The latter omits at most four pigeons, so it contains three of the seven robust ones. So \(g^F_x-g^{F'}_x\) is constant on \(\Lambda_F\cap\Lambda_{F'}\). For a pigeon \(x\), choose frames \(F_1,F_2\) avoiding \(x\) with \(L_{F_1}\cap L_{F_2}=\varnothing\); they exist by \(6\)-robustness. Set \(g_x=g^{F_1}_x\) on \(\Lambda_{F_1}\), and \(g_x=g^{F_2}_x+\mu_x\) on \(L_{F_1}\subseteq\Lambda_{F_2}\), with \(\mu_x\) the constant for which \(g^{F_2}_x+\mu_x=g^{F_1}_x\) on \(\Lambda_{F_1}\cap\Lambda_{F_2}\). For any frame \(F\) avoiding \(x\), \(g_x-g^F_x\) is constant on \(\Lambda_F\cap\Lambda_{F_1}\) and on \(\Lambda_F\cap\Lambda_{F_2}\). The two constants agree on the nonempty triple intersection, and these two sets cover \(\Lambda_F\). So \(g_x-g^F_x\) is constant on \(\Lambda_F\).

Step 4 (distinct pigeons). Put \(q'=q-\ell g\in\operatorname{Ann}(\ell^2)\). Let \(a\ne b\) and \(P,Q\) be disjoint pairs. Choose a frame \(F\) with \(c,d\notin\{a,b\}\) and \(L_F\cap(P\cup Q)=\varnothing\). This needs four robust pigeons and pairs avoiding at most six labels. On \(\Lambda_F\), \(h_{ab}-(\ell g^F)_{ab}\) is separable by Step 1. \((\ell(g-g^F))_{ab}\) is separable too, since \(g-g^F\) is row-constant there. So the mixed second difference of \(q'_{ab}\) at \((P,Q)\) vanishes. By the separability fact, every distinct-pigeon component of \(q'\) is zero in \(A_2\).

Step 5 (repeated pigeons). With every \(H'\) zero, (IR) for \(q'\) reads \(\square h'_{aa}(j_1,\dots,j_4)\,\delta f_c(P_c)\,\delta f_d(P_d)=0\). Choose robust \(c,d\ne a\) with pairs avoiding the four labels and each other. Then \(\square h'_{aa}=0\) for all four distinct labels. An edge function with all \(\square\) zero is a star when \(n\ge4\). Put \(\varphi(j)=\tfrac12\bigl(e(jk)+e(jm)-e(km)\bigr)\). It does not depend on \(k,m\), because the three pairings of any four labels have equal sums, and \(e(jk)=\varphi(j)+\varphi(k)\). So \(h'_{aa}=0\) in \(A_2\), hence \(q'=0\) and \(q=\ell g\). \(\square\)

Failure probability. For a uniform row function, the probability of being constant on some \((n-12)\)-set is at most \(\binom n{12}3^{13-n}\). As in the spread lemma, the row functions of a uniform \(\ell\) are independent and uniform modulo constants. So fewer than seven of the \(n+1\) are \(12\)-robust with probability at most \(\binom{n+1}{6}\bigl(\binom n{12}3^{13-n}\bigr)^{n-5}=3^{-(1-o(1))n^2}\). This bound first drops below one at \(n=31\), where it is about \(3.6\times10^{-6}\). For \(M\) squares a union bound multiplies it by \(M\). The constants 12 and seven are what this proof's label counts need, not optimized. The data at \(n=7,8\), below the lemma's range, already show \(\operatorname{Ann}_{A_2}(\ell^2)=\ell A_1\) for the sampled uniform forms.

Assessment and next step

At degree four the picture of degree three repeats, one level up. The exact semi-regular count with Frobenius and Koszul corrections holds, measured at \(n=7\) through the fill point. The single-square part of the count, the Frobenius exactness, is proved for spread forms. The proof's method is general: fix the pairs of two robust pigeons, read the identity as a local product, and glue. Fixing one pigeon's pair also gives a contraction identity. For a pigeon \(d\) and a pair \(P_d=(j,j')\) with \(c=\delta f_d(P_d)\ne0\), let \(\partial\) take the coefficient of \(x_{dj}\) minus that of \(x_{dj'}\), and then restrict: set pigeon \(d\)'s variables and the variables of holes \(j,j'\) to zero. Let \('\) denote the restriction alone. Both maps are well defined on \(A\), with values in the algebra \(A'\) of the board with \(n\) pigeons and \(n-2\) holes. They satisfy \(\partial(ab)=\partial a\cdot b'+a'\cdot\partial b\) and \(\partial\ell=c\). Applied to \(q\ell^2=0\), with \(q\) of degree \(k\), this gives \(\partial q\cdot\ell'^2+2c\,q'\ell'=0\), so \(q'-(\partial q/c)\ell'\) annihilates \(\ell'\) in \(A'\) (since \(1/(2c)=-1/c\) in \(\mathbb F_3\)). Single-square exactness at degree \(k\) is \(\operatorname{Ann}_{A_k}(\ell^2)=\ell A_{k-1}\). Its companion is \(\operatorname{Ann}_{A_k}(\ell)=\ell^2A_{k-2}\). On each restricted board the identity reduces the first to the companion, and vice versa. Reassembling the restrictions into a statement on the full board is the open gluing step. Since the smaller boards have more pigeons than holes plus one, the statements must be made for general pigeon and hole counts. The lemma's proof already allows this.

The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer is that induction. State the pair of single-square exactness statements for all \(k\le cn\) and prove them by contraction, with the gluing of Step 3 generalized to multipliers determined only modulo \(\ell^2A_{k-3}\). Test each statement at \(n=7,8\), \(k=2,3\) with the component code before relying on it. It ends with the induction proved, or with the degree at which the gluing fails and the data showing why. The multi-square strata, where the Koszul syzygies enter, come after.

Verification gate. Re-read: the spread lemma's statement and proof, its component split of \(A_3\) and its probability bound, and the selector check's count, which the component code reproduces. The count is \(\lceil\gamma_3/(\gamma_1-1)\rceil=76,185\). Before drafting, a claim search found no recorded degree-four statement. The searches used annihilator, square, quadratic, degree four, robust, fourth difference, four pigeons, Koszul and semi-regular. A reviewer given only the statement confirmed that the record neither states nor implies it. Checks: (I4) and (IR) against direct products, and both operators on relation rows, including star relations after a first version of the check skipped them. The linear annihilators \(\operatorname{Ann}_{A_1}(\ell)\) were computed for every sampled form. A fresh-context reviewer checked the component descriptions, both identities, the label counts, the separability and star facts, the gluing, the model's coefficients and all fill points, and found the proof correct. It required several corrections, all adopted. The first group scoped the evidence: one seed; no Frobenius-plus-Koszul claim at the fill point, where the kernel is larger; \(\dim\ell A_1\) computed rather than assumed; the \(n=6\) failure stated; and no refutation claimed from a graded fill. The second group concerned the lemma: the unused hypothesis \(n\ge14\) dropped, the probability bound located (below one from \(n=31\)), \(\partial\) defined explicitly, the general board shape of the contraction noted, the gluing named as open, and clashing symbols renamed.

Route review: single-square exactness is recorded at every degree; the selector line reduces to lifting over many forms at once

23 September 2026 · Route review with a working lemma and a finite check · Per-degree work stops; next, a truncated Dade lemma for many forms. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

The line's general claim. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. Since the selector-line review the thread has read the core statement's pseudorandom side as Conjecture SR for selectors \(1-L^2\) over \(\mathbb F_3\). It proved it degree by degree through kernel strata. The results so far are exact thresholds at degree three and the degree-four count. The single-square annihilators are handled by the spread lemma and its degree-four version. The previous entry proposed extending single-square exactness to every degree by a contraction induction.

What the goal needs. The logarithmic-prefix reduction needs Conjecture SR at degree about \((4p-1)h\) for polynomially many constraints whose forms come from a refutation. The count must hold jointly for all of them, up to the fill point.

Finding 1: the single-square part is recorded, in dual form

The amplitude theorem of 21 September states \(\ker D^a=\operatorname{im}D^{p-a}\) on the top moment-correction spaces \(K_d\) of functional matching boards, with \(D=\sum_i\delta_i\) the sum of weighted marginals. \(K_d\) is dual to the functional top algebra in degree \(d\), and \(\delta_i\) is adjoint to multiplication by the row-\(i\) part of \(\ell\). A complex of finite-dimensional spaces is exact exactly when its dual is. So at \(p=3\), \(a=2\) gives \(\operatorname{Ann}(\ell)=\ell^2A_{d-2}\), and \(a=1\) gives \(\operatorname{Ann}(\ell^2)=\ell A_{d-1}\), on functional boards at every degree \(d\). It needs \(2d+3-a\) active rows that stay nonconstant after deleting \(3d+2(3-a)\) labels. The robustness convention is the same as the spread lemmas' own. For uniform forms that range is roughly \(d\lesssim n/3\).

Consequences for the record:

  • The recorded theorem at \(d=1\), \(a=1\) gives the spread lemma for 7-robust forms, with four rows. The weak algebra maps onto the functional one, so an annihilator in the weak algebra is one in the functional algebra. The two algebras coincide in degree one, where the conclusion \(e\in\ell A_0\) lives. The spread lemma itself assumes only 6-robustness, so it refines the recorded case in robustness.
  • The degree-four spread lemma's functional part is the case \(d=2\), and the theorem's constants are better: six rows and 10-robustness, where the lemma asks for seven and 12. Its own content is Step 5, the repeated-pigeon components that the weak board adds.
  • So the spread lemma, and the degree-four lemma's functional part, rediscover recorded results; the registry now links them. The gate searches of those cycles used the multiplication words (annihilator, square). They missed the dual words (contraction, weighted marginal, amplitude). The verification gate in CLAUDE.md now asks for a search under the dual formulation.
  • The contraction induction proposed last cycle is not needed on functional boards.

Finding 2: exactness on the column tensor

Let \(T=\bigotimes_{j}C_j\), with \(C_j=\mathbb F_3\oplus V_j\), \(V_j^2=0\) and \(V_j=\langle x_{ij}\rangle_i\), be the collision algebra without row relations. Then \(A=T/(R_0,\dots,R_n)\).

Lemma (column-tensor exactness). Let \(\ell=\sum_jy_j\) with \(y_j\in V_j\), and let \(c\) be the number of columns with \(y_j\ne0\). Then \(\operatorname{Ann}_{T_k}(\ell)=\ell^2T_{k-2}\) and \(\operatorname{Ann}_{T_k}(\ell^2)=\ell T_{k-1}\) for all \(k<\lfloor c/2\rfloor\), and the second fails at \(k=\lfloor c/2\rfloor\).

Proof. \(H=\mathbb F_3[x]/(x^3)\) with \(x\) primitive is a Hopf algebra: \(\Delta(x^3)=x^3\otimes1+1\otimes x^3\) in characteristic three. Multiplication by \(\ell\) on \(T\) is the diagonal action of \(x\) on the tensor product of the \(H\)-modules \(C_j\), where \(x\) acts on \(C_j\) by \(y_j\). Write \(V_a[s]\) for the graded indecomposable \(H\)-module of length \(a\) starting in degree \(s\). If \(y_j\ne0\), then \(C_j=V_2[0]\oplus V_1[1]^{\dim V_j-1}\) (basis \(1,y_j\) and a complement); otherwise \(C_j\) is trivial. The rules are these. \(V_1[s]\otimes M=M[s]\). Free modules stay free under tensor products, since \(H\otimes M\cong H\otimes M^{\mathrm{triv}}\) for a Hopf algebra. Directly, \(V_2[0]\otimes V_2[0]=V_3[0]\oplus V_1[1]\): \(e_0e_0\mapsto e_1e_0+e_0e_1\mapsto2e_1e_1\) is a chain of length three, and \(x(e_0e_1-e_1e_0)=0\). By induction \(V_2[0]^{\otimes c}\) is free plus one summand \(N_c\). Here \(N_c=V_1[c/2]\) for \(c\) even and \(V_2[(c-1)/2]\) for \(c\) odd: tensoring \(N_{c-1}\) with \(V_2[0]\) gives \(V_3\oplus V_1\) or \(V_2\) at the stated shift. Expanding each nonzero column as \(V_2[0]\oplus V_1[1]^{\dim V_j-1}\), \(T\) is a sum over the sets \(S\) of columns that contribute their \(V_2[0]\). Each term is \(V_2[0]^{\otimes|S|}\) shifted by \(c-|S|\) (plus degree-zero trivial factors from the zero columns). Its non-free part \(N_{|S|}[c-|S|]\) starts in degree \(\lfloor|S|/2\rfloor+c-|S|\ge\lfloor c/2\rfloor\), with equality when \(S\) is all \(c\) columns. So the non-free part of \(T\) starts exactly in degree \(\lfloor c/2\rfloor\). Free summands \(V_3[s]\) satisfy both exactness statements. A summand \(V_1[s]\) or the bottom of \(V_2[s]\) is killed by \(\ell^2\) and is not in \(\ell T\). The top of \(V_2[s]\) is killed by \(\ell\) and is not in \(\ell^2T\). So both statements hold below \(\lfloor c/2\rfloor\), and the second fails there. \(\square\)

The lemma needs no robustness, only \(c\) nonzero columns. Column forms have \(c=1\), and there it fails at once (\(\ell^2=0\)). What it does not cover is the row relations. In the Nakayama sense of Finding 3, \(T\) is free over \(\mathbb F_3[\ell]/(\ell^3)\) through degree \(c/2\) for even \(c\) and \((c+1)/2\) for odd \(c\). The summand \(V_1[s]\) first breaks the isomorphism in degree \(s+1\), and \(V_2[s]\) in degree \(s+2\).

Finding 3: the weak board, measured

By graded Nakayama, \(A\) is free over \(\mathbb F_3[\ell]/(\ell^3)\) through degree \(D\) exactly when the Hilbert function of \(A/\ell A\) equals that of \(\mathrm{HS}_A/(1+t+t^2)\) through \(D\). Freeness through \(D\) gives \(\operatorname{Ann}_{A_k}(\ell)=\ell^2A_{k-2}\) for \(k\le D-1\) and \(\operatorname{Ann}_{A_k}(\ell^2)=\ell A_{k-1}\) for \(k\le D-2\). Likewise, with \(\gamma_k=\dim A_k\), the rows act freely on \(T\) through \(D\) exactly when \(\gamma_k=[t^k]\,\mathrm{HS}_T/(1+t+t^2)^{n+1}\) for \(k\le D\). 73degree 4: \(26316\) against \(26309\); \(\dim\operatorname{Ann}_{A_3}(\ell)=54\) against 47at least 44

These are two samples at \(n=6,7\) and one at \(n=8\); the computations stop at degree four. In the same Nakayama sense, the weak board stops no later than \(T\), and sometimes earlier. At \(n=7\) it fails in degree four, where \(T\) is still free. At \(n=6\), \(\operatorname{Ann}_{A_2}(\ell^2)\) is too large although \(T\)'s holds there. So the row relations cost exactness. The column-tensor lemma bounds what can be hoped for and does not explain where \(A\) stops. Finding 4: what the joint count needs

Let \(U=\bigotimes_b\mathbb F_3[y_b]/(y_b^3)\), acting on \(A\otimes N\), \(N=\bigotimes_bN_b\), \(N_b=\mathbb F_3[y_b]/(y_b^2)\). Here \(y_b\) acts on \(A\) by \(\ell_b\) and on \(N_b\) by its generator. \(U\) is cocommutative with antipode \(y\mapsto-y\), and \(A\) with \(\ell\mapsto-\ell\) is isomorphic to \(A\) by the degree sign. So \(A\otimes_UN\cong(A\otimes N)/U^+(A\otimes N)\), and \(A\otimes_UN=A/(\ell_1^2,\dots,\ell_M^2)\). Hence if \(A\otimes N\) is free over \(U\) through \(D\) (Nakayama sense), the selector count \(\mathrm{HS}_A\bigl((1+t)/(1+t+t^2)\bigr)^M\) holds through \(D\).

\(U\) is the group algebra of \((\mathbb Z/3)^M\). By Dade's lemma, with Carlson's rank varieties, a finite-dimensional \(U\)-module is free exactly when it is free over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3[z]/(z^3)\) for every nonzero \(z=\sum\beta_by_b\) with \(\beta\in\overline{\mathbb F}_3^M\). What the count needs is a truncated version: freeness through \(D\). The single-element test is computable on the row-free model \(T\otimes N\), acted on by the row generators and the selectors; on \(A\otimes N\) the rows act as zero. For \(z=\sum\beta_by_b+\sum\alpha_iR_i\), the tensor rules of Finding 2 apply. Each board column where the column part of \(z\) is nonzero contributes a \(V_2\), and so does each selector with \(\beta_b\ne0\). So single-element freeness on \(T\otimes N\) is governed by a column count: board columns plus selector support. It fails early only for combinations with small selector support whose forms nearly cancel, the overload structure of the relative-span entry. For uniform families one expects no early single-element failure over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\); this was not checked. Carrying single-element freeness from \(T\otimes N\) to \(A\otimes N\) is heuristic, since the rows themselves are not free on \(T\) at every size (the \(n=6\) row of the table).

Two limits. First, the truncated passage from single elements to the whole family must use the count. For uniform families the count fails at the fill point. So if, as expected, no single element fails early, any truncated local-to-global statement needs Hilbert-series positivity as a hypothesis. Second, the record has this passage only for two forms. The ternary projective-line lemma and the ternary pair theorem build a common lift from exactness in every pencil direction \(D_1+\lambda D_2\). That is a truncated rank-two Dade statement. The two-form corollary asks for \(2d+2p-1\) rows for a lift from \(K_d\) to \(K_{d+p-1}\), against \(2d+p-a\) for one form's exactness at degree \(d\). These are different statements, so how the cost grows with the number of forms is unknown. If it grew linearly, only \(O(n/p)\) selectors could be handled, far below the fill point.

Falsification attempt

The freeness route predicts that a single-element failure breaks the count exactly at the degree where freeness first fails. A linear dependency \(\sum_{b\in S}\beta_b\ell_b=0\) makes \(z=\sum_{b\in S}\beta_by_b\) act only on \(N_S\cong V_2^{\otimes|S|}\). Its non-free summand is \(N_{|S|}\). \(U\) is free over \(\mathbb F_3[z]/(z^3)\). A linear change of the generators \(y_b\) that makes \(z\) one of them keeps the ideal of cubes, because cubing is additive in characteristic three. So \(U\cong\mathbb F_3[z]/(z^3)\otimes(\text{the rest})\). Hence \(U\)-freeness of \(A\otimes N\) fails by degree 3 for \(|S|=3\) (summand \(V_2[1]\)) and by degree 4 for \(|S|=5\) (summand \(V_2[2]\)). The prediction was tested with \(\ell_S\) summing to zero and uniform other forms:

\(|S|=5\), degree 4, \(n=7\)fails by 4one short at \(M=5,10,20\) (e.g. \(4369\) against \(4370\))

In each case the count failed at the predicted degree, by one dimension. Each family was tested at one degree only. The three-term case has the explicit syzygy \(\ell_1^2\ell_2-\ell_2^2\ell_1-\ell_3^2(\ell_1-\ell_2)=0\) for \(\ell_3=\ell_1+\ell_2\). The prediction survived. So freeness is a sharp proxy for the count in these tests. Files: dependent_count.py, dependent_count_n6_s*.json, dependent3_deg3_n6.json, dependent5_deg4_n7.json.

Assessment

The selector line's per-degree cycles produced correct special cases. Their single-square core was already recorded in dual form, on functional boards, over a degree range of order \(n/3\). The line's actual open content is the joint statement for many forms. In the freeness picture that is a truncated Dade lemma for \((\mathbb Z/3)^M\) acting on \(A\otimes N\), with the Hilbert series' positivity as its hypothesis. It is the batched mechanism the remaining route names as missing, reached here from the algebra side. The record's rank-two case is the projective-line lemma. Further degree-by-degree strata do not move this.

Next step

On odd-prime-clause-transfer, first read the standard proofs of Dade's lemma and of rank varieties for elementary abelian groups, and determine which steps survive truncation to degrees at most \(D\). Then try to generalize the projective-line lemma from pencils to planes. The test is three forms: given exactness in every direction \(\sum\lambda_bD_b\), \(\lambda\in\mathbb P^2(\overline{\mathbb F}_3)\), at the needed degrees, when does a common lift exist? Determine the degree, row and robustness loss of the third form. Check candidates against three uniform selectors at \(n=7\), degree four, where the count is known to hold. The cycle ends with the rank-three lemma, or with a measured growth of the loss.

Verification gate. Re-read: the amplitude theorem's statement (spaces, operators, room and deletion hypotheses), the projective-line lemma's statement and the two-form corollary's summary. A reviewer given only the column-tensor statement found no record of it; the searches used tensor product, Hopf, Jordan block, amplitude, weighted marginal and collision algebra. Checks: \(\ell\)-exactness and row freeness computed exactly at \(n=6,7,8\) through degree four, and the dependency controls at degrees three and four. A fresh-context reviewer checked the entry and required changes, all adopted. Its main finding was that a first version misread the five-term dependency: its non-free summand breaks freeness only in degree four, not three. That version's conclusion, that freeness is more than the count needs, was withdrawn. The degree-four and three-term controls were then run, and they support the opposite reading. The reviewer also required:

  • the truncated claim stated against Dade's lemma, which holds for whole modules;
  • the single-element analysis placed on \(T\otimes N\), where the rows act;
  • the table compared in one sense, showing that the rows cost exactness;
  • a step added to the column-tensor proof for the extra column summands;
  • the spread lemma's robustness relation to the recorded theorem corrected;
  • the degree range of the amplitude theorem stated;
  • the growth of the lifting cost called unknown.

A focused second pass over the revised sections confirmed all numbers against the data. It required four precisions, all adopted: a conditional in the first limit, "fails by" instead of "first fails" in the controls, one tested degree per family, and the change of generators behind the freeness of \(U\) over \(z\).

A truncated Dade lemma needs more than single-element freeness and positivity: special position breaks it

23 September 2026 · Refutation and a finite check · Column tensors over \(\mathbb F_3\), complete and rank-one columns. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The column-tensor review read the joint selector count as freeness of a column tensor over \(u(\mathfrak g)=\mathbb F_3[z_1,\dots,z_r]/(z_i^3)\) through a degree \(D\). It asked for a truncated Dade lemma: single-element freeness, meaning freeness over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3[z]/(z^3)\) for every nonzero \(z\), together with nonnegativity of the predicted Hilbert function, should imply freeness through \(D\). This cycle tests that statement on the smallest structured models, where both hypotheses can be computed exactly. It ends with agreement over the tested range, or with a counterexample.

Models and equivalences

A column is \(L_c=\mathbb F_3\oplus V_c\) with \(V_c^2=0\), on which \(\mathfrak g\) acts through a linear map \(\varphi_c:\mathfrak g\to V_c\), sending \(1\mapsto\varphi_c(z)\). A column tensor is \(X=\bigotimes_cL_c\) with the diagonal action. The collision algebra \(T\) of the board is the case of complete columns, \(\varphi_j\) an isomorphism from the row span onto \(V_j=\langle x_{ij}\rangle_i\). Selector columns have rank one. By graded Nakayama, \(X\) is free through \(D\) exactly when \(\dim(X/\mathfrak gX)_k=W_k:=[t^k]\,\mathrm{HS}_X/(1+t+t^2)^r\) for \(k\le D\). So nonnegativity of \(W_k\) through \(D\) is necessary.

For a single element \(z\), let \(c(z)\) be the number of columns with \(\varphi_c(z)\ne0\). Each such column restricts to \(V_2\oplus(\dim V_c-1)\cdot\text{trivial}[1]\). So, as in the proof of the column-tensor lemma, \(X|_z\) is a sum of pieces \(V_2^{\otimes c'}[c-c']\otimes(\text{trivial})\) with \(c'\le c\), and the shift offsets the smaller \(c'\). Hence \(X|_z\) is free, in the Nakayama sense, exactly through \(c/2\) for even \(c\) and \((c+1)/2\) for odd \(c\). For rank-one columns only \(c'=c\) occurs. The minimum of \(c(z)\) over \(z\in\mathfrak g\otimes\overline{\mathbb F}_3\) is computable over \(\mathbb F_3\). For rank-one columns \(\varphi_c=\lambda_c\), the \(\mathbb F_3\)-points of an \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\)-hyperplane lie in an \(\mathbb F_3\)-hyperplane. So \(\min c(z)=m-\max_h\#\{c:\lambda_c\in h\}\) over the \(\mathbb F_3\)-hyperplanes \(h\).

The statement under test predicts freeness exactly through \(\min(\text{single-element range},\text{last }k\text{ with }W_k\ge0)\).

Test 1: complete columns

\(X=L^{\otimes m}\) with \(L=\mathbb F_3\oplus\mathfrak g\), for \(r=\dim\mathfrak g\le5\) and \(m\le8\). There are 35 cases, each computed up to degree \(m\) or until a degree had more than 40,000 basis elements. In all 35 the measured freeness degree equals the prediction, or reaches the last computed degree when the computation stopped first. Here the two bounds nearly coincide, so this test mainly confirms the single-element part.

Test 2: rank-one columns

This is the pure selector model: \(X=\mathbb F_3[t_1,\dots,t_m]/(t_c^2)\), with \(z_i=\sum_c\lambda_c(e_i)t_c\) for random \(\lambda_c\in\mathbb F_3^r\setminus0\). Modulo the \(z_i\), \[ X/\mathfrak gX\cong\mathbb F_3[s_1,\dots,s_{m-r}]/(\mu_1^2,\dots,\mu_m^2), \] with \(\mu_c\) the image of \(t_c\). This needs \(\operatorname{rank}\Lambda=r\), which follows from \(\min c(z)>0\); otherwise the prediction is freeness through degree 0 and nothing is tested. So the test asks for the Hilbert function of \(m\) squares of linear forms in \(m-r\) variables. In characteristic zero, the degree-two part of this question is the classical one: the squares are dependent exactly when the points \([\mu_c]\) fail to impose independent conditions on quadrics. From degree three on the characteristic-three problem differs. Every cube of a linear form lies in \((\mu_c^2)\), since \(\ell^3=\sum a_c^3t_c^3=0\) in \(X\). So \(W\) is not the characteristic-zero expected series: for \(r=6\), \(m=14\), \(W_3=14\), while \((1+t)^{14}(1-t)^6\) gives 8. Inverse systems in degree at least three would also need divided powers. Commands: ctf.py --rs 1,2,3,4,5 --ms 2,...,8 --maxcols 40000, rank1.py --rs 2,...,6 --ms 6,...,14 --trials 4 (seed 0) and rank1.py --rs 3,...,7 --ms 10,...,16 --trials 12 --seed 1. Computed: 100 instances with \(r\le6\), \(m\le14\), and 240 with \(r\le7\), \(m\le16\), each through the predicted degree plus one.

outcomeinstances
freeness exactly as predicted333
fails one degree early, at \(W_k=0\) (quotient 1, e.g. \(r=3\), \(m=6\), degree 2)6
fails one degree early with \(W_k>0\)1

Counterexample. Take \(r=6\), \(m=14\), with the \(\lambda_c\) stored in rank1_large.json. At most 9 of the 14 forms lie in one hyperplane, so \(c(z)\ge5\) for every \(z\ne0\). So \(X\) is free over every single element through degree 3. The predicted Hilbert function is \(W=(1,8,22,14,\dots)\), positive through degree 3. But \(\dim(X/\mathfrak gX)=(1,8,22,15)\): freeness fails in degree 3 by one dimension. An independent recomputation with plain NumPy elimination confirms the quotient dimensions and the hyperplane count (verify_instance.py, verify_instance.txt).

So, for general column tensors over \(\mathbb F_3\), the truncated Dade lemma is false in the form "single-element freeness through \(D\) plus \(W_k\ge0\) (even \(W_k>0\)) implies freeness through \(D\)". The counterexample uses rank-one columns. The version restricted to the board's own tensors, with complete row columns and selector columns, is untested beyond Test 1 and remains open. The six boundary failures, all in degree two, are the classical kind of special position. With \(r=3\), \(m=6\), the six squares \(\mu_c^2\) in three variables are dependent exactly when the six points \([\mu_c]\) lie on a conic. Over \(\mathbb F_3\) that is frequent. The strictly positive case is a degree-three defect of 14 squares in 8 variables, measured against the characteristic-three prediction \(W\); it has no direct fat-point counterpart. Files: research/results/odd_prime_truncated_dade_20260923/, ctf.py, ctf.json, rank1.py, rank1.json, rank1_large.json.

What this means for the route

In the freeness picture, the batched mechanism is not a consequence of single-element exactness, which is the recorded amplitude theorem's kind of statement, together with counting. It also needs a genericity hypothesis excluding special position. It is of the same type as Fröberg-type and fat-point interpolation statements, which are open in general. But the predicted series \(W\) differs from Fröberg's from degree three on, so no existing conjecture is the statement needed here. Two structural remarks bound where special position can hide:

  • Every finite instance has a bounded number \(m-r\) of quotient variables, so the defects above carry no information about growth by themselves. If a defect in the board setting comes from forms confined to a bounded span, the bounded-span equivalence resolves it as conditioning on allowed patterns, on the structured side. How \(m-r\) in this model translates into the span of board forms was not worked out.
  • For the goal, the forms come from a refutation, not from a random source. An adversary could aim for special position in a span whose dimension grows with \(n\). Whether such configurations exist in the board algebra with a positive predicted count is the open question. The uniform families measured so far show none, at degree three (\(n=6,7\)) and four (\(n=7\)).

Assessment and next step

The tested statement is refuted as stated. Single-element freeness plus positivity decided freeness in 333 of 340 random rank-one instances and in all complete-column cases. The failures are special-position defects in small spans. The missing hypothesis is a genericity condition, and the route now needs to know whether that condition can fail only through bounded-span structure.

The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer is the core test, on constructed special-position families with growing span. Candidates are forms from a conic or a rational normal curve, and Frobenius- or subspace-structured configurations, in \(v=m-r\) quotient variables for \(v\) from 9 to about 15, at degree three. Say a defect in degree \(k\) has a bounded core if a subset \(C\) of the forms, spanning at most \(d_0\) dimensions, already has a degree-\(k\) relation among the \(\mu_c^2\), \(c\in C\), beyond the Frobenius and Koszul ones. The hypothesis to test predicts that every defect has a bounded core with \(d_0\) independent of \(v\). Sizes: in the \(X\) model degree three has \(\binom m3\) basis elements (560 at \(m=16\), 4060 at \(m=30\)); in the quotient ring, at most \(\binom{v+2}3\) monomials (455 at \(v=13\)). Random frequencies are a secondary control only, since the goal's forms are adversarial. The step ends with a family that has a defect without a bounded core, which is a new obstruction for the structured side, or with the core found in every constructed defect.

Verification gate. Re-read: the column-tensor lemma's decomposition, which is the source of the single-element ranges, and the bounded-span equivalence's statement. The counterexample was recomputed by independent code. The complete-column predictions were rechecked after the positivity criterion was corrected from \(W_k>0\) to \(W_k\ge0\): a zero coefficient is allowed. A fresh-context reviewer reran the independent check and confirmed the refutation, the counts and the Nakayama and hyperplane reductions. It required corrections, all adopted: the single-element formula for columns of rank above one; the rank hypothesis; the interpolation analogy restricted to degree two, since cubes of linear forms vanish in characteristic three; the refutation scoped to general column tensors; the bounded-span remark weakened; and the next step rebuilt around constructed families, a defined core and stated sizes.

Special position against bounded cores: a pencil of quadrics gives defects whose only core spans almost every dimension

23 September 2026 · Finite check and a working lemma · Evidence against bounded cores, rank-one model, degree two. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The truncated Dade entry found that single-element freeness plus a positive predicted Hilbert function does not imply freeness: special position breaks it. Its next step asked whether every such defect has a bounded core: a subset of the forms, spanning a bounded number \(d_0\) of dimensions, whose squares already carry the extra relation. If so, the structured side could absorb special position through the bounded-span equivalence. The cycle ends with a constructed family that has a defect without a bounded core, or with a core found in every constructed defect.

Single-element failures always have a bounded core

In the rank-one model, \(X=\mathbb F_3[t_1,\dots,t_m]/(t_c^2)\) is acted on by generators \(z_i=\sum_c\lambda_c(e_i)t_c\). The quotient is \(X/\mathfrak gX\cong\mathbb F_3[s_1,\dots,s_v]/(\mu_1^2,\dots,\mu_m^2)\), with \(v=m-r\). Take the generators to be a basis of the linear dependencies (so \(\operatorname{rank}\Lambda=r\), and \(z\Lambda\ne0\) for \(z\ne0\)) \(\sum_ca_c\mu_c=0\) of the points \(\mu_c\in\mathbb F_3^v\). Every model with \(\operatorname{rank}\Lambda=r\) has this form, since the rows of \(\Lambda\) span the dependencies of the images \(\mu_c\).

Lemma (girth lemma). \(\min_{z\ne0}c(z)\), over \(z\in\mathfrak g\otimes\overline{\mathbb F}_3\), equals the girth of the configuration: the smallest number of the \(\mu_c\) carrying a nontrivial linear dependency.

Proof. \(c(z)\) is the number of columns with \(\lambda_c(z)\ne0\), the support of the vector \((\lambda_c(z))_c=z\Lambda\). As \(z\) ranges over \(\mathbb F_3^r\setminus0\), \(z\Lambda\) ranges over the nonzero dependencies, so the minimum over \(\mathbb F_3\) is the girth. Over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\), the zero set \(\{c:\lambda_c(z)=0\}\) is the set of columns \(\lambda_c\) in the hyperplane \(z^\perp\). These are \(\mathbb F_3\)-vectors, and \(\mathbb F_3\)-rank equals \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\)-rank, so they span at most \(r-1\) dimensions over \(\mathbb F_3\). Hence they lie in \(y^\perp\) for some nonzero \(y\in\mathbb F_3^r\), and \(\operatorname{supp}(y\Lambda)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(z\Lambda)\). So the minimum is the same. \(\square\)

The single-element range is \(\lceil c/2\rceil\), so a single-element failure at or below degree \(D\) needs \(c\le2D-2\): a circuit of at most \(2D-2\) forms, spanning at most \(2D-3\) dimensions. In that sense single-element failures are always localized in a small span. This is not a core in the degree-two sense used below, since a failure at degree above two is not a relation among squares.

A defect whose only core is everything

Construction (rejection sampling: up to 200 attempts per trial until a pencil with an extra \(\mathbb F_3\)-base point appears). Choose \(N=\binom{v+1}2-2\) points \(\mu_1,\dots,\mu_N\in\mathbb P^{v-1}(\mathbb F_3)\). They are taken from a random greedy cap, so no three are collinear. When the quadrics through them form a pencil, the \(N\) points impose independent conditions on quadrics. Add an \(\mathbb F_3\)-point \(\mu_{N+1}\) of the pencil's base locus not among them. The base point lies on every quadric of the pencil, so its square lies in the span of the other \(N\) squares in the space \(S_2\) of quadrics, of dimension \(\binom{v+1}2\). Hence the dependency space among the \(m=N+1\) squares is exactly one-dimensional and contains the added point in its support. The degree-two count predicts \(W_2=\binom{v+1}2-m=1\), but the quotient has dimension 2. The single-element range is at least 2, since distinct projective points have girth at least 3. The cap does not raise this: the base point can be collinear with two cap points, and the girth is 3 in 4 of the 5 instances where it was computed. What the cap prevents is a support of four collinear points. So this is a defect within the predicted range, with \(W_2>0\). So every subset of forms whose squares are dependent contains the dependency's support: that support is the only possible core.

\(v\)\(m\)support of the only dependency (3 trials)its span dimensiontensor-model quotient against \(W\)

51410, 10, 85, 5, 4\((1,5,2)\) against \((1,5,1)\)

The only core spans all \(v\) dimensions in 11 of 12 instances and \(v-1\) in the twelfth, and its size tends to grow with \(v\). This is evidence against bounded cores, not a refutation. It excludes \(d_0\le6\) only in the sampled instances, and a proof that the span grows with \(v\) is missing. Without the cap condition, random points over \(\mathbb F_3\) often give a line (support 4, span 2), and otherwise small supports: 6 and 7 points spanning 3 dimensions at \(v=5\), 8 spanning 4 and 12 spanning 6 at \(v=6\). Lines are the small-field effect behind the earlier boundary failures. Files: research/results/odd_prime_special_position_20260923/, pencil.py, pencil.json (random points), pencil_cap.json (caps), and xcheck.py, xcheck.txt for the tensor-model cross-check.

What such a defect is in the board

For selectors \(1-L_c^2\) with \(L_c=\ell_c+k_c\), a relation \(\sum_ca_c\ell_c^2=0\) among the squares in \(A_2\) means that \(\sum_ca_c\ell_c^2\) reduces, modulo the base at degree two (through \(x^2=x\), collisions and the row equations), to an affine function \(g\). Since \(1-L_c^2=1-k_c^2-2k_c\ell_c-\ell_c^2\), the linear combination \(\sum_ca_c(1-L_c^2)\) of the selectors gives at degree two the affine consequence \[ \textstyle\sum_ca_c(1-k_c^2)-2\sum_ca_ck_c\ell_c-g=0 . \] So a special-position defect of this kind is a fall to an affine equation among the forms. For homogeneous forms (\(k_c=0\)) it reads \(\sum_ca_c=g\), which is a refutation when \(g\) is a constant different from \(\sum_ca_c\). On patterns this is visible directly. In the rank-one model the relation is an identity of reduced polynomials in \(v\) variables, reduced because the degree two is below three, hence an identity of functions on \(\mathbb F_3^v\). This fails for products of squares, whose degree \(2w\ge4\) is not reduced under \(x^3=x\). So on the allowed patterns, those avoiding every forbidden hyperplane \(\{L_c=0\}\), the affine consequence must hold. A refutation means the \(m\) forbidden hyperplanes cover all patterns.

The constructed families have \(m\approx v^2/2\) selectors of density \(1/3\) each, so their total density is far above one. The route's constraints are wide, each of small density and the total below one. The planted-overload entry recorded that, for constraints on one bounded span, total density below one leaves allowed patterns of positive density and allows at most one point-pin. Whether special position without a bounded core can occur, or can matter, at total density below one is not settled by this model.

Assessment and next step

Single-element failures are localized in small spans (girth lemma). Special-position defects need not be, as far as the data go: a pencil of quadrics through a cap produces defects whose only core spans all or almost all of \(v\le7\) dimensions. So bounded spans alone are unlikely to close the structured side. The constructed defects have high density, and the goal's regime has low density.

The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer is to test low density directly, where a count rules out the pencil mechanism at the constraints' own degree. Total density below one with width \(w\) allows fewer than \(3^w\) constraints: at most 8 for \(w=2\) and 26 for \(w=3\). A degree-\(2w\) special position like the pencil needs about \(\dim S_{2w}=\binom{v+2w-1}{2w}\) constraints (15 at \(v=3\), \(w=2\)), so it is possible only for \(v\le3\). So low-density defects can only appear above degree \(2w\), through multipliers. The model: the truncated ring \(B=\mathbb F_3[s_1,\dots,s_v]/(s_i^3)\), where cubes of all linear forms vanish, with constraint tops \(\prod_{i\in T_b}\mu_i^2\), \(b\le M\), \(|T_b|=w\). The prediction is \(\mathrm{HS}_B\prod_b\bigl(1-t^{2w}/(1+t+t^2)^w\bigr)\), exact when all \(Mw\) forms are independent. A defect is a Hilbert-function value above the prediction's positive part in a degree where every lower value agrees. Smallest nonvacuous case: \(w=2\), \(M\le8\), \(Mw>v\), degrees 5 to 8. \(\dim B_k=[t^k](1+t+t^2)^v\) is at most about 3,000 for \(v\le9\), \(k\le8\). Search special configurations (forms on a conic, a quadric or a subspace) for a defect without a bounded core. The step ends with such a defect, or with the finding that every defect at \(M\le8\) has a core of bounded span.

Verification gate. Re-read: the truncated Dade entry's model, its equivalences and its core definition, and the bounded-span equivalence and density statements of the planted-overload entry. The degree-two defects were cross-checked in the tensor model at \(v=4,5,6\) (xcheck.txt). A fresh-context reviewer confirmed the table against the data and the affine-consequence algebra. It required changes, all adopted. The status is downgraded from refutation to evidence, since 12 instances cannot exclude every fixed \(d_0\). The girth lemma's \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\) step is made explicit, and its bounded-core claim is weakened to localization with exact bounds. The one-dimensionality of the dependency is proved, not observed. The girth statements about caps and the random-point supports are corrected. The degree-two limitation of the pattern argument is noted. The next step is rebuilt around the density count, with a model, a prediction and sizes.

At total density below one, random product-constraint defects come from overlapping subfamilies

23 September 2026 · Finite check · 144 random instances, \(v\le9\), degree at most eight. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The special-position entry gave evidence that degree-two defects of selector squares need not have a bounded core. Its families have total density far above one. The route's constraints are wide, with total density below one, and a count excludes the pencil mechanism there. Width-\(w\) constraints number fewer than \(3^w\), while a degree-\(2w\) pencil needs about \(\binom{v+2w-1}{2w}\) of them. So this cycle asks whether defects above the constraint degree, at density below one, still have bounded cores. It ends with a defect without a small core, or with the cores of all defects found.

Model

Take the truncated ring \(B=\mathbb F_3[s_1,\dots,s_v]/(s_i^3)\). Every cube of a linear form vanishes there, and it plays the role of \(u(\mathfrak g)\) with the forms as pseudo-independent variables. Constraint \(b\) has top \(P_b=\mu_{2b}^2\mu_{2b+1}^2\), with its two forms linearly independent. A proportional pair would give \(P_b=\mu^4=0\), a degenerate constraint, excluded. There are \(M\le8\) constraints, of density \(1/9\) each, so the total is at most \(8/9\), and \(2M>v\), so the forms are dependent. A linear change of variables is an automorphism of \(B\), since \((\sum a_is_i)^3=\sum a_is_i^3\) in characteristic three, so the ideal \((s_i^3)\) is stable under it. For independent forms the ideal of tops is therefore monomial after a change of variables: \(B/I\cong\bigotimes_b\mathbb F_3[x,y]/(x^3,y^3,x^2y^2)\otimes(\text{rest})\), with Hilbert function exactly \[ W=\mathrm{HS}_B\,\bigl(1-t^4/(1+t+t^2)^2\bigr)^M . \] Every tested instance has \(2M>v\), so there \(W\) is a heuristic prediction of Fröberg type, never exact. The expected Hilbert function is \(W\) truncated at its first nonpositive coefficient, zero from there on. A defect is the first degree where the Hilbert function \(H\) of \(B/(P_1,\dots,P_M)\) differs from it. Its core is a smallest subfamily \(S\) whose own quotient already has a defect by that degree; its span is the dimension of the span of its \(2|S|\) forms. A first run compared against \(\max(W,0)\), without truncation, and kept degenerate constraints. Both produced spurious defects, and it is kept only as products_small.json.

Results

There were 144 random instances, six for each of 24 pairs \((v,M)\) with \(4\le v\le9\), \(M\in\{3,4,5,6,8\}\), \(2M>v\), each computed through degree 8 (products.py, products.json).

All 53 defects are excesses, \(H\) above the truncated prediction. Their cores:

  • 43 are pairs spanning 3 dimensions, with the defect in degree 6.
  • 3 are pairs spanning 2 dimensions, in degree 4.
  • 4 are triples or quadruples spanning 3 dimensions, in degree 5 (3 and 1 cases).
  • 2 are triples spanning 4 dimensions, in degree 7. These are the two defects without an overlapping pair.
  • 1 is a family of seven spanning all four dimensions of a \(v=4\) instance, in degree 5. That is essentially the whole family, not a small core; the instance also contains an overlapping pair.

Every core's span is at most the defect degree, and the largest span is 4. The \(v=4\) row is largely vacuous. For \(M\ge4\) the truncated prediction is already zero from degree 6 (from degree 5 at \(M=8\)), so the degree-6 pair mechanism cannot show: 13 instances with an overlapping pair have no defect. At \(v\ge5\), every instance with an overlapping pair has a defect. At \(v=8,9\), with 10 to 16 forms, defects occur only in the one instance containing an overlapping pair. Otherwise the Hilbert function matches the truncated prediction through degree 8, although the forms are dependent.

Reading

The defects are small subfamilies of constraints whose forms overlap, so that their span \(d_S\) is below \(2|S|\). They fail in degrees near the top \(2d_S\) of their own small truncated ring. This matches the relative counts of the relative-span entry: a subfamily fails its own count before the whole family does. The mechanism the data show is at the top of the small ring. The subfamily's own prediction \(W_S\) turns negative at degree \(2d_S\), while its Hilbert function is at least 0, and the excess appears there. A heuristic first-moment reading: at low density a subfamily of large span cannot fill its middle degrees, since each width-\(w\) factor removes a proportion of order \(3^{-w}\) there. That count concerns \(H>0\), not excess syzygies, so it does not exclude defects in the middle degrees. This suggests a hypothesis: at total density below one, a defect in degree \(D\) has a core of span at most about \(D\). The present runs barely test it: with \(v\le9\) and \(D\) from 4 to 8, every span is at most \(v\), which is about \(D\) anyway. Only the span-3 cores in degree 6 and the span-4 cores in degree 7 carry content. A nonvacuous test needs \(v\) well above \(D\), for example \(v\ge2D\), with the truncated prediction positive through degree \(D\). The pencil family of the previous entry violates it only at high density. Cores of bounded span are the bounded-span structure that the bounded-span equivalence resolves as pattern conditioning.

Assessment and next step

In this model, at total density below one, in 144 random instances with \(v\le9\) and degrees at most eight, every defect found comes from an overlapping subfamily of span at most 4 and at most the defect degree. That supports the structure-versus-randomness dichotomy in the regime the goal needs. The instances are random, so an adversarial low-density family with a large-span defect is not excluded.

The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer is the first case, at \(w=2\). Lemma to prove: if a family of width-two product constraints has its first defect in degree at most 6, then it contains a pair of constraints whose four forms span at most 3 dimensions, or a degenerate or smaller overlap. For general \(w\) the pair's own prediction, \((1+t+t^2)^d-2t^{2w}(1+t+t^2)^{d-w}+t^{4w}(1+t+t^2)^{d-2w}\) with \(d=2w-1\), first turns negative at \(2d=4w-2\). So the general statement concerns degree \(4w-2\), and \(4w-2=2w+2\) only at \(w=2\). The enumerable part is the pairs and triples of constraints. Up to \(\mathrm{GL}_v(\mathbb F_3)\), a pair is determined by the linear relations among its four forms, and a triple by those among six forms spanning at most 6 dimensions. These are few orbits, which can be listed and checked in \(B\) with \(v=d_S\) through degree 8. The whole families cannot be enumerated: at \(v=6\) there are 364 projective points and about 66,000 constraints. Families would be tested by random and structured sampling in nonvacuous cases, \(v=5\), \(M\le4\) and \(v=6\), \(M\le8\), where the truncated prediction is positive at degree 6 and \(2M>v\). The proof would show that a degree-6 syzygy beyond the Koszul and Frobenius ones, in a family without an overlapping pair, is impossible. The step ends with that lemma, or with a family without an overlapping pair that has a defect in degree at most 6.

Verification gate. Re-read: the special-position entry (the core definition, the density count and the pencil families) and the relative-span entry's overload pattern. A first run was discarded and kept only as products_small.json: it compared against \(\max(W,0)\) and kept degenerate constraints. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed the model, the code's defect and core detection, and the table and the 53 cores against the data. It required corrections, all adopted: the \(M\) values stated; the change-of-variables step for the prediction, and its heuristic status when \(2M>v\); the vacuous \(v=4\) row noted; the seven-constraint core not called small; the hypothesis marked as barely tested, with a nonvacuous range; the first-moment reading separated from the excess mechanism; and the next step corrected to \(w=2\), with the general degree \(4w-2\), "contains a pair" wording and enumerable sizes.

Route review: the freeness line is a column-tensor analogue of the recorded r-parameter lift, and its form needs genericity

23 September 2026 · Route review with a finite check · The line re-derives the recorded obstruction; the next step moves to the board itself. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

The line's general claim. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. Since the column-tensor review, the thread has read the joint count for many constraints as freeness of a column tensor over \(u(\mathfrak g)\) through a degree \(D\). The step it needs is a truncated local-to-global lemma: single-element exactness plus positivity implies joint exactness. Three cycles tested that statement in toy models:

  • it fails in special position (truncated Dade entry);
  • at high density, special-position defects need not have a bounded core (special-position entry);
  • at total density below one, the random defects found have small overlapping cores (low-density entry).

What the goal needs. Joint exactness, or at least absence of refutation, for polynomially many wide constraints whose forms come from a refutation. This must hold relative to the PHP base \(A\) itself, at degree about \((4p-1)h\).

Relation to the record

The recorded wide-conditioning conjecture (22 September) states the affine case of this program. It adds unary PHP and an affine system whose nonzero combinations are all robust on many rows, and claims no degree-\(D\) refutation. Its claim-index assessment records that "the \(r\)-parameter lift it needs is unproved and the projective proof does not port". The truncated Dade lemma of the last three cycles is the column-tensor analogue of that \(r\)-parameter lift. Two correspondences, which are analogies rather than identities:

  • The conjecture's hypothesis, that every nonzero combination is robust, plays the role of the single-element hypothesis. It is combinatorial, and it yields single-element exactness or non-refutation only through the recorded one-form case.
  • Both pictures cap the number of forms, from different sources. The conjecture's dimension bound (a width-\(t\) span has dimension below \(N^2\)) limits how many random blocks can admit such a span. The freeness picture's positivity cap is a Hilbert-series condition, \(\mathrm{HS}_A/(1+t+t^2)^{\dim\mathfrak g}\ge0\) through \(D\). At degree four it allows only \(r\le5\) at \(n=7\), far below \(N^2\).

The record also has a proved positive case: the many-operator lift holds for symmetric targets on free modules. The local-lift review set that many-operator lift aside "for lack of a density mechanism". The special-position failure below lies outside that proved case. So the freeness line re-derived a recorded obstruction in another language.

What it adds to the record:

  1. The column-tensor form of the \(r\)-parameter lift is false. Single-element exactness plus positivity does not imply joint exactness; a genericity condition excluding special position is also needed.
  2. Single-element failures are localized: the girth lemma puts them in circuits.
  3. Special position at high density can involve the whole span.
  4. At total density below one, every special-position defect found, random or adversarial, contains an overlapping pair or triple; a search forbidding them found no defect.

None of this is about the PHP base. The toy models are the free ring \(\mathbb F_3[s]/(s_i^3)\) and rank-one column tensors. In the free ring \(B\), quotients by linearly independent linear forms are always exact. Since \((\sum a_is_i)^3=\sum a_i^3s_i^3\) in characteristic three, \(B=S(V)/(v^3:v\in V)\) does not depend on the basis, so \(B\) modulo independent linear forms is again a truncated polynomial ring. So special position of linear forms cannot arise there, and the affine case of the conjecture is invisible. The toy-model constraints were the nonlinear products \(\mu_a^2\mu_b^2\), which is where special position arose.

Falsification attempt

The low-density entry's working claim was tested adversarially: at total density below one, a defect needs an overlapping pair or triple. A subfamily \(S\) overlaps when its \(2|S|\) forms span fewer than \(2|S|\) dimensions. The search used \(v=8\), \(M=8\) width-two product constraints in the free ring. It forbade overlapping pairs and triples, and hill-climbed over single-form changes to maximize the total excess \(\sum_k\max(0,H_k-T_k)\) through degree 8.

  • Correct condition (every pair spans 4, every triple spans 6): three random restarts and three with all forms on a random quadric, 300 steps each, about 140 admissible evaluations per restart. No excess in any degree through 8.
  • A first, looser version forbade only triples spanning fewer than 5 dimensions, so it admitted overlapping triples (span 5). It found defects with excess 25 (first in degree 7), 3 and 1 (degree 8). Their minimal cores were 5 constraints spanning 5 dimensions, 4 spanning 5, and 5 spanning 6. Each contains overlapping triples, so these runs do not bear on the claim. Two further runs at \(v=10\) found no defect. They are kept, relabelled, as loose_triples_*.json.

So the narrow claim survived the adversarial search at \(v=8\). This is weak evidence: six local searches in a toy model. The broader form, that a core's span is at most the defect degree, was not tested. At \(v=8\) it holds automatically for degree-8 defects, and the \(v=10\) runs found no defect. Files: research/results/odd_prime_freeness_review_20260923/, adversary.py, adversary_v8.json, adversary_v8_quadric.json, adversary_cores.py, and the loose_triples_* files.

Assessment

The freeness line is not converging on a proof. It reformulated the recorded \(r\)-parameter lift and showed that its natural form needs a genericity hypothesis. It gathered evidence in toy models that at low density the genericity fails only through small overlapping subfamilies. An adversarial search forbidding overlapping pairs and triples found no defect at \(v=8\). That evidence is random or search-based, in a model without the PHP base, and it does not touch the step the recorded conjecture needs. Further toy-model cycles would add special cases. What remains untested is whether the PHP base itself produces special position for robust affine systems. The toy models cannot show this, and the recorded conjecture depends on it.

Next step

On odd-prime-clause-transfer, test the board version directly: special position of robust affine systems in \(A\). By graded Nakayama, \(A\) is free over \(u(\langle\ell_1,\dots,\ell_r\rangle)\) through \(D\) exactly when the Hilbert function of \(A/(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_r)\) equals \(\mathrm{HS}_A/(1+t+t^2)^r\) through \(D\). Fix \(t\) and \(Q\) first, and check that \(r\)-systems with every nonzero combination \(Q\)-robust on \(t\) rows exist at \(n=7\), \(r\le5\); the conjecture only asserts that some \(t\) and \(Q\) work. Then search, randomly and by hill-climbing, for such systems but whose quotient exceeds the prediction in a degree where the prediction is positive. Such a system is a PHP-specific special-position defect.

The smallest nonvacuous sizes, computed from the graded dimensions, are \(n=7\) with \(r\le5\) and \(n=8\) with \(r\le10\), at degree four. The prediction's degree-four coefficient is 490 at \(n=7\), \(r=5\), and 6557 at \(n=8\), \(r=10\). The rank computations are \(r\gamma_3\times\gamma_4\): \(5\cdot8688\times34950\) at \(n=7\), about 0.19 GB packed. At \(n=8\), \(10\cdot22929\times168147\approx3.9\times10^{10}\) entries need about 9.6 GB at two bits per entry, at the memory cap. So \(n=8\) needs streamed elimination, or only the rank of the image in \(A_4\) accumulated in blocks, or smaller \(r\). A defect in the homogeneous quotient is a necessary precondition for a fall of the affine system, not a refutation, and the conjecture is about refutation: for a defect found, check whether a fall and then a refutation follow. Degree four is far below the \((4p-1)h\) the goal needs, so a null result bounds only low degrees. The step ends with the search's outcome at both sizes.

Verification gate. Re-read: the wide-conditioning conjecture's statement and its assessment in the claim index, the remaining route's wording on the parked lines, and the low-density entry's definition of overlap. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed the run counts, the core descriptions and the nonvacuity coefficients (490; \(r=6\) gives \(-4011\); 6557; \(r=11\) gives \(-2485\)). Its main finding was that the first adversarial search used a looser triple condition than the low-density entry's definition. The "refutation" drawn from it was withdrawn, and the search was rerun with the correct condition, finding nothing. It also required:

  • the correspondences stated as analogies;
  • the recorded positive case of the many-operator lift noted;
  • free-ring exactness restricted to independent forms, with its reason;
  • the \(n=8\) memory estimate corrected to 9.6 GB, with methods that fit;
  • the next step weakened: a defect is a precondition for a fall, and degree four bounds only low degrees;
  • the quotation attributed to the claim index.

All were adopted.

On the board, column-type affine systems are special: robust on every row, yet non-free early and sometimes refuted at degree three

23 September 2026 · Finite check · Weak unary PHP over \(\mathbb F_3\), \(n=6,7\), degrees three and four. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The freeness-line review redirected the line to the board itself. Does the PHP algebra \(A\) put robust affine systems in special position? The hypothesis to meet is that of the recorded wide-conditioning conjecture: every nonzero combination is \(Q\)-robust on at least \(t\) rows. A defect is excess in the Hilbert function of \(A/(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_r)\) over \(\mathrm{HS}_A/(1+t+t^2)^r\), truncated. The cycle ends with the search's outcome and a first check of whether defects lead to refutations.

Three families at \(n=7\)

Robustness was checked over all nonzero \(\mathbb F_3\)-combinations, with \(Q=2\), \(t=5\).

  • Random: uniform forms, \(r=2,\dots,5\), three trials each. No defect through degree 3 in any of the 12.
  • Column-type: every row carries the same hole function \(\varphi_b\), so \(\ell_{\varphi}=\sum_j\varphi(j)C_j\) with \(C_j=\sum_ix_{ij}\). Every combination is again column-type, and it is \(Q\)-robust on all rows when its hole function is. Since \(\sum_j\psi(j)C_j\) lies in the row span exactly when \(\psi\) is constant, a column-type system is independent modulo rows exactly when no nonzero combination has a constant hole function, which the robustness check guarantees. Defects appeared in all six systems: degree-3 excesses of 47 to 69 at \(r=2\), and 147 at \(r=3\), with one extra dimension already in degree 2. No robust column-type system with \(r\ge4\) was found in 500 draws. A Hamming-bound count explains why: robust combinations need a ternary code containing the all-ones vector with minimum distance at least \(Q+1\), which caps \(r\) at 3 for \(n=7\), \(Q=2\).
  • Mixed: alternating column-type and uniform forms. Defects in all 12 systems, 2 to 154 in degree 3, and one extra dimension already in degree 2 at \(r=5\).

A single column-type form is already non-free. Through degree 4, two such forms gave excesses \((0,0,0,22,1138)\) and \((0,0,0,1,676)\), while a random form gave \((0,0,0,0,7)\). The 7 is the known degree-four failure at \(n=7\) from the column-tensor review.

Refutations at degree three

These are exact PC closures with the recorded affine-conditioning closure code, for PHP plus \(r\) column-type equations \(\ell_{\varphi_b}=c_b\), over every right-hand side \(c\). Each is compared with random affine systems of the same size. For each right-hand side the run also checks whether a Boolean occupancy vector \(y\in\{0,1\}^n\) exists with \(\sum_jy_j\equiv n+1\) and \(\sum_j\varphi_b(j)y_j=c_b\). The column sums \(C_j\) are Boolean modulo collisions at degree two, and the rows force \(\sum_jC_j=n+1\).

\(n\), \(r\)robustness \(Q\) of the systemcolumn-type right-hand sides refutedrandom systems refuted
6, 1 (two systems)2, 21 of 3 each (\(c=1\), resp. \(c=0\))0 of 3 each
6, 2 (two systems)1, 19 of 9 each0 of 9 each
7, 130 of 30 of 3
7, 212 of 9 (\(c=(0,2),(1,2)\))0 of 9

At \(r\le2\), every right-hand side, refuted or not, has a Boolean occupancy solution, so the check does not discriminate there and the occupancy reduction does not explain those refutations. In an earlier run at \(n=6\), occupancy_n6_D3.json, two \(r=3\) systems (robustness 1 and 0) were refuted for all 27 right-hand sides. Of these, 17 and 12 have an occupancy solution. At \(n=7\) the symmetric value \(c_b\equiv\tfrac{n+1}{n}\sum_j\varphi_b(j)\), \((2,1)\) there, is not refuted, but neither are six other right-hand sides. At \(n=6\) this value is undefined, since \(n\equiv0\pmod3\). Only the \(r=2\), \(Q=1\) rows are like-for-like between the sizes, and there the effect weakens from 9 of 9 to 2 of 9; the \(r=1\) rows compare \(Q=2\) with \(Q=3\). Plain PHP is not refuted at degree three at either size. Files: research/results/odd_prime_board_affine_20260923/, board_affine.py, n7_K3_*.json, n7_K4_*_r1.json, occupancy_refute.py, occupancy_n6_D3_rhs.json, occupancy_n7_D3.json. occupancy_n6_D3.json is the earlier run without per-right-hand-side detail, which includes the \(r=3\) systems.

A heuristic account

Column-type forms live in the subalgebra generated by the column sums, where \(C_j^2=0\) and \(\sum_jC_j\equiv0\) modulo rows. A model is \(R=\mathbb F_3[t_1,\dots,t_n]/(t_j^2,z)\) with \(z=\sum_jt_j\). For a hole function \(\varphi\), let \(c=n-\max_a\#\varphi^{-1}(a)\), the smallest column count in the pencil \(\langle z,\ell_\varphi\rangle\). By the definition of robustness, \(\varphi\) is \(Q\)-robust exactly when \(c\ge Q+1\). The column-tensor lemma does not cover the quotient by \(z\), so the model was computed directly (model_ring.py, model_ring_n7.json, model_ring_n8.json). For single forms the first excess of \(R/(\ell_\varphi)\) over \(\mathrm{HS}_R/(1+t+t^2)\) is in degree \(\lceil c/2\rceil+1\):

  • \(n=7\): degree 2 for \(c=1,2\), degree 3 for \(c=3,4\);
  • \(n=8\): degree 4 for the two \(c=5\) forms below, where the truncated prediction is already 0, and degree 2 for \(c=2\).

In \(A\), the two single forms (\(c=3,4\)) also first fail in degree 3. So for single forms the heuristic reads: a \(Q\)-robust column-type form is free through at least \(\lceil(Q+1)/2\rceil\), whatever \(n\). If this carries over to \(A\), the wide-conditioning conjecture's \(Q\) must be at least about \(2D\) for single column-type forms.

Three limits:

  • Systems can fail earlier. The \(n=7\), \(r=3\) column systems have \(c\ge3\) in every combination, yet show a degree-2 excess in \(A\). The model predicts none for them.
  • Non-freeness does not imply refutation. The \(Q=3\) single form at \(n=7\) is non-free in degree 3 but was never refuted at \(D=3\), so the heuristic makes no refutation prediction.
  • It assumes that \(A\) behaves like a free extension of the column subalgebra, which is unproved.

Assessment and next step

The board does produce special position for affine systems that the toy models could not show: occupancy (column-type) forms. They meet the row-robustness hypothesis of the wide-conditioning conjecture, fail freeness early, and give degree-three refutations that random systems do not. The refutations seen come from \(Q\le2\). For single forms, the model predicts that the freeness failures are a small-\(Q\) effect set by the value multiplicities of the hole functions, which would calibrate the conjecture, not contradict it.

The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer is to test the single-form prediction at \(n=8\), \(D=3\), where the heuristic makes a definite claim. Plain PHP should survive degree three there (random-conditioning law), and the run checks it. The closure has about \(4.3\times10^4\) columns. Compare single column-type forms with \(c=5\) (\(Q=4\), the maximum at \(n=8\), since some value occurs at least three times) against forms with \(c\le2\). Two examples with \(c=5\) are \(\varphi_1=(0,0,0,1,1,1,2,2)\) and \(\varphi_2=(0,1,2,0,1,2,0,1)\). Measure, for each form, the first excess degree of \(A/(\ell_\varphi)\) and the refutation count over the 3 right-hand sides.

The heuristic predicts a first excess in degree 4 for \(c=5\), and in degree 2 for \(c\le2\). An excess in degree 3 or lower at \(c=5\) falsifies the account. Refutations at \(c=5\) would mean \(Q\) must grow faster than about \(2D\). The pair \(\varphi_1,\varphi_2\), with every combination of multiplicities \((3,3,2)\), is a secondary test, since systems can fail earlier. The step ends with these degrees and counts.

Verification gate. Re-read: the wide-conditioning conjecture's statement, including its independence and robustness hypotheses; the recorded affine-conditioning closure code's interface and its base rows; and the column-tensor review's weak-board data. A fresh-context reviewer checked the robustness code against the definition, the Hamming bound and all numbers against the data. It required corrections, all adopted:

  • the occupancy claim restricted to \(r\le2\), with the \(r=3\) data reported;
  • the refuting \(Q\) corrected to at most 2;
  • the independence modulo rows made explicit;
  • the model-ring computation reported as a computation, not as a consequence of the lemma. It was reproduced independently: first excess in degree \(\lceil c/2\rceil+1\).
  • the heuristic restricted to single forms, with two limits: systems fail earlier, and non-freeness does not predict refutation;
  • the comparison between \(n=6\) and \(n=7\) confounded unless like-for-like;
  • the next step rebuilt around single forms at \(n=8\), with an explicit \(Q=4\) example and a falsifying outcome.

At \(n=8\), single column-type forms first fail exactly where the column-subalgebra model says

23 September 2026 · Finite check · Weak unary PHP over \(\mathbb F_3\), \(n=8\), freeness through degree four and refutations at degree three. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The column-type entry found that occupancy forms \(\ell_\varphi=\sum_j\varphi(j)C_j\) meet the row-robustness hypothesis of the wide-conditioning conjecture but fail freeness early and, at small robustness, give degree-three refutations. A model of the column subalgebra predicts that a single form first fails in degree \(\lceil c/2\rceil+1\), with \(c=n-\max_a\#\varphi^{-1}(a)\). A \(Q\)-robust \(\varphi\) has \(c\ge Q+1\). The test was set at \(n=8\), \(D=3\): an excess in degree 3 or lower at \(c=5\) falsifies the account. The cycle ends with the first excess degrees and the refutation counts.

First excess degrees

The Hilbert function of \(A/(\ell_\varphi)\) was computed through degree 4 and compared with \(\mathrm{HS}_A/(1+t+t^2)\), truncated (board_affine.py --phis, n8_K4_explicit.json). The degree-four rank needs \(22929\times168147\) entries. A first run built them densely, about 4 GB, and was stopped by the memory limit. The final run packs them in chunks of 2000 rows.

\((1,1,0,0,0,0,0,0)\)22\((0,0,1,125,4349)\)

All four match. A random form at \(n=8\) has no excess through degree four (column-tensor review). So on the board a single column-type form is free through degree \(\lceil c/2\rceil\) and not beyond, in these cases. Together with the two single forms at \(n=7\) (column-type entry), the formula now holds in six board cases, and in all eight model-ring cases computed.

Refutations at degree three

Exact closures of PHP plus the column-type equations over every right-hand side, with random affine systems of the same size for comparison. Plain PHP is not refuted at degree three at \(n=8\). The recorded closure routine multiplies 400 rows by all 72 variables at once, about 5 GB of dense integers at this size, and was stopped by the memory limit. The script now uses the same closure in chunks of 40 rows, converted to bytes per variable. This computes the same closure. Reducing modulo 3 per block equals reducing after stacking. The loop stops only after a full pass with no growth, so its fixed point is the least space closed under multiplying its part of degree at most \(D-1\) by variables, whatever the chunk size. The columns are ordered by degree, as in the original, so pivot degree is polynomial degree. As a control, the modified routine reproduced the recorded \(n=7\) two-form count exactly: 2 of 9, at \(c=(0,2)\) and \((1,2)\) (control_n7_pair_new_closure.json). Each single-form closure took about 30 seconds, each two-form closure about 100.

Nothing is refuted. Degree-three refutations of column-type systems were not observed at \(n=8\) in the systems tested: one pair each at \(Q=2\) and \(Q=4\), and single forms down to \(Q=1\). The two-form rows go from 9 of 9 at \(n=6\) (\(Q=1\)), to 2 of 9 at \(n=7\) (\(Q=1\)), to 0 of 9 at \(n=8\) (\(Q=2\)). \(Q\) changes along this sequence, and there is one pair per size. So the trend is suggestive, not like-for-like: an \(n=8\) pair with \(Q=1\) was not run. The \(c=2\) form is non-free already in degree 2 and yet not refuted, a further instance of non-freeness without refutation. Files: occupancy_n8_D3_phi1.json, occupancy_n8_D3_singles.json, occupancy_n8_D3_pairQ4.json, occupancy_n8_D3_pair_random.json, with the closure's control in control_n7_pair_new_closure.json.

Assessment and next step

At \(n=8\) the single-form freeness formula holds in all four cases. No degree-three refutation of a column-type system was observed at \(n=8\). So occupancy forms show no evidence against the wide-conditioning conjecture, which is about refutation. They calibrate the freeness route to it instead. A column-type form with column count \(c\) is free exactly through \(\lceil c/2\rceil\) in the cases computed. So a proof through freeness, such as the \(r\)-parameter lift, needs \(Q\) at least about \(2D-2\) for such forms. That is a constraint on the route, not on the conjecture: non-freeness does not imply refutation, as the \(c=2\) form shows.

The comparison with the recorded amplitude theorem crosses board types. The theorem is stated on functional boards, and every computation here is on the weak board, so it gives no bound on the computed \(A\). On functional boards it applies to column-type forms, since all rows are robust. Freeness over \(\mathbb F_3[\ell]/(\ell^3)\) needs \(a=1\) and \(a=2\) together, and the binding case \(p-a=2\) requires \(3d+4\le c-1\), that is \(d\le\lfloor(c-5)/3\rfloor\). Its degree \(d\) is the degree of the top algebra, the same grading as the Hilbert function of \(A/(\ell)\). At \(c=5\) this covers only \(d=0\), and for \(c\le4\) nothing, so at \(n=8\) the comparison is vacuous. Asymptotically it gives about \(c/3\) against the observed \(\lceil c/2\rceil\).

The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer is the upper bound, which is the calibration that matters. For every \(\varphi\), \(A\) should fail to be free over \(\mathbb F_3[\ell_\varphi]/(\ell_\varphi^3)\) through degree \(\lceil c/2\rceil+1\). Construct an explicit witness in the model ring \(R=\mathbb F_3[t]/(t_j^2,\sum_jt_j)\): a nonzero class of degree \(\lceil c/2\rceil+1\) in \(\ker\ell/\operatorname{im}\ell^2\) or in \(\ker\ell^2/\operatorname{im}\ell\). Build it from the value-class sums \(S_a=\sum_{\varphi(j)=a}C_j\), so that \(\ell_\varphi=S_1-S_2\). Then show it stays nonzero modulo the ideal of the board.

A proof bounds the freeness route at \(Q\ge2D-2\) for occupancy forms, for every \(n\). The lower bound, freeness through \(\lceil c/2\rceil\), would only sharpen the recorded \(c/3\) by a constant factor, off the critical path, and is not pursued. The step ends with the witness and its survival proved, or with the point where survival fails.
