A component hypothesis with local freeness would exclude low-degree refutations; Frobenius and Koszul syzygies lift, and an overlapping pair lifts exactly when its forbidden lines meet

23 September 2026 · Conditional result with a lemma and a finite check · Weak unary PHP over \(\mathbb F_3\), forbid-value constraints. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The board degree-six entry supports a split of the core statement's inductive step: bounded overlapping components, and genericity for the rest. Its next step asked what that split would give for the core statement, which is about PC refutations of affine constraints, not about Hilbert functions of their tops. The cycle ends with the derivation, or with the point where the link fails.

The link is recorded

Homogenize the base and the constraints with a variable \(z\), as in the marked presentation. The \(z\)-quotient of the homogenized base is its top algebra, here \(A=\mathbb F_3[x]/(x_{ij}^2,\ x_{ij}x_{i'j},\ \sum_jx_{ij})\). There are no degree falls through \(D\) exactly when \(z\) is injective below \(D\). Then bounded PC equals the Nullstellensatz span, and \(z^D\ne0\), so there is no refutation of degree \(D\).

The recorded filtered obstruction quotient identifies what can break injectivity. In the base's own \(z\)-injective range, the top syzygies \(\sum_ba_bP_b=0\) in \(A\) modulo the liftable ones are exactly \(\ker z\). Call a top syzygy \((\sigma_b)\) liftable if it has lifts \(\tilde\sigma_b\) with \(\sum_b\tilde\sigma_bg_b^{\mathrm h}=z\rho\), \(\rho\) in the constraint ideal. Equivalently, after subtracting \(z\) times a representation of \(\rho\), it is the reduction modulo \(z\) of an exact relation among the \(g_b^{\mathrm h}\). So no refutation of degree \(D\) follows from two conditions:

  • (a) the base is \(z\)-injective below \(D\);
  • (b) every top syzygy of degree at most \(D\) is generated by liftable ones.

The recorded quotient concerns the block tensor complex. The same two-term argument works for any presentation, and the direct proof below supplies it.

Which syzygies lift

Take constraints that forbid one value of a family of forms: \(g=\prod_{k=1}^w\bigl(1-(\ell_k-a_k)^2\bigr)\), with top \(P=(-1)^w\prod_k\ell_k^2\).

Lemma (Frobenius lift). On the weak unary base over \(\mathbb F_3\), \((\ell_k-a_k)\,g\) lies in the base ideal for every \(k\), at degree \(2w+1\). So the Frobenius syzygies \(\ell_kP=0\) of \(A\) lift, with zero correction. Koszul syzygies \(P_ce_b-P_be_c\) lift trivially.

Proof. In characteristic 3, \(\ell^3=\sum_ic_ix_i^3\) for \(\ell=\sum_ic_ix_i\). Booleanity gives \(x_i^3-x_i=(x_i+1)(x_i^2-x_i)\), so \(\ell^3-\ell=\sum_ic_i(x_i+1)(x_i^2-x_i)\) and \((\ell-a)^3\equiv\ell-a\) modulo the base ideal. Hence \((\ell_k-a_k)(1-(\ell_k-a_k)^2)\equiv0\), and \((\ell_k-a_k)g\) is a multiple of it. The derivation uses the Booleanity axioms times monomials of degree at most \(2w-1\), so it stays within degree \(2w+1\). \(\square\)

What remains are syzygies special to overlapping subfamilies, the component-local ones. They need not lift, and the smallest case already shows it. Take two constraints on pairs whose four forms span 3 dimensions, a component of the kind in the overlapping-pair lemma. Each forbids an affine line \(L_b\) of \(\mathbb F_3^3\). In the function ring \(\mathbb F_3[y_1,y_2,y_3]/(y_i^3-y_i)\), whose top algebra is the truncated ring, the Nullstellensatz span was compared with the no-fall value from the lemma's Hilbert function \((1,3,6,7,4,1,0)\). All configurations were checked, with the first pair fixed to \((e_1,e_2)\) and all right-hand sides (pair_lifting.py, pair_lifting.json).

  • In the 3,888 cases where \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) meet, there is no fall through degree 6. The pair's degree-6 top syzygy lifts in the function ring of the span.
  • In the 7,776 cases where they are disjoint, there is a fall of exactly 1 in degree 6. The ideal then contains every function vanishing off the 6 forbidden points. That space has dimension 6, while the tops predict 5.

The count explains it: the tops predict \(27-22=5\) independent conditions, and two lines forbid 5 points only if they meet. A fall inside a component is not a refutation, since the allowed set is nonempty. It means the component's constraints generate more than their tops show.

By the bounded-span equivalence, a component's constraints are equivalent, at bounded degree, to the ideal \(I(P_C)\) of functions of its span vanishing on its allowed patterns \(P_C\). A degree-compatible basis of \(I(P_C)\), one whose leading forms generate the leading-form ideal, has only liftable syzygies by construction. So the right local factor is that of \(I(P_C)\)'s leading-form ideal, not of the raw tops. The overlapping-pair lemma's \(+t^6\) is the factor only when the lines meet.

The local picture is not enough by itself. Its leading forms live in the graded ring \(\operatorname{gr}R_C=\mathbb F_3[y]/(y^3)\) of the span, and the natural map \(\varphi_C:\operatorname{gr}R_C\to A\) can have a kernel coming from the PHP relations. The reviewer's example: one constraint forbidding \(\ell=0\) for the narrow form \(\ell=x_{11}+x_{21}\). Its allowed set \(\{1,2\}\) is nonempty and its local basis is \(y^2-1\). But \(\ell^2=0\) in \(A\), by \(x^2=0\) and the collision, so the coefficient 1 is a top syzygy of none of the kinds above. It does not lift: modulo the base, \(g^{\mathrm h}\equiv z(z-\ell)\), and \(z-\ell\) is not in the ideal in degree 1. Here the base derives \(\ell=1\) at degree 2, a fall. Local freeness of \(A\) over each component's span, that is injectivity of \(\varphi_C\), must therefore be assumed. That is where width enters: narrow forms violate it, and so does the occupancy pair, whose span is not free in degree 3.

The component hypothesis and what it gives

Component hypothesis (conjecture). Let \(g_1,\dots,g_M\) be forbid-value constraints on the weak unary base. Group them into components along circuits of bounded size, and replace each component \(C\) by a degree-compatible basis of \(I(P_C)\) on its span. Assume that each component satisfies \((p-1)d_C+2w_C\le D\), where \(d_C\) is its span's dimension and \(w_C\) its largest width, and that \(\varphi_C\) is injective through degree \(D\) (local freeness). Then through degree \(D\), every syzygy of the resulting leading forms in \(A\) is generated by Koszul syzygies, Frobenius syzygies and component-local syzygies: the images under \(\varphi_C\) of syzygies in \(\operatorname{gr}R_C\).

Conditional result. Suppose the base is \(z\)-injective below \(D\), every component's allowed set \(P_C\) is nonempty, and the component hypothesis holds through \(D\), with its local-freeness and degree assumptions. Then the base plus the constraints has no PC refutation of degree \(D\).

Proof. By the bounded-span equivalence, a component's constraints and the basis of \(I(P_C)\) derive each other within degree \((p-1)d_C+2w_C\le D\), so the ceiling-\(D\) consequence space is unchanged. Nonempty \(P_C\) means the basis does not contain a nonzero constant. By the hypothesis, every top syzygy is generated by Koszul, Frobenius and component-local ones. The first two lift by the lemma. The component-local ones lift because a degree-compatible basis has lifting syzygies in the span's function ring, whose relations \(y^3=y\) homogenize through the Booleanity derivation of the lemma. So condition (b) holds.

Directly, without citing the obstruction quotient: let \(\bar A_0\) be the homogenized base algebra, and let \(u\in\bar A_0\) of degree \(k<D\) satisfy \(zu=\sum_bc_bg_b^{\mathrm h}\). Reducing modulo \(z\) gives a top syzygy \(\sum_b\bar c_bP_b=0\) in \(A\). By (b) it is a combination \(\sum_s\alpha_s\sigma_s\) of liftable syzygies, with lifts \(\sum_b\tilde\sigma_{s,b}g_b^{\mathrm h}=z\rho_s\), and \(c_b-\sum_s\tilde\alpha_s\tilde\sigma_{s,b}=zd_b\) for some \(d_b\). Then \(zu=z\bigl(\sum_s\tilde\alpha_s\rho_s+\sum_bd_bg_b^{\mathrm h}\bigr)\). By (a), from degree \(k\) to \(k+1\le D\), \(u\) lies in the constraint ideal. So \(z\) is injective below \(D\) on the full homogenized algebra. Then \(T_D=0\), and the socle criterion gives \(C_D=I_D\). Finally \(z^D\ne0\), since \(1\ne0\) in degree 0: no supplied generator is a nonzero constant. \(\square\)

The hypothesis is the Fröberg-type genericity the thread has circled: the model and board data of the last cycles are its only support. Its expected Fröberg-type consequence, not derived here, is that the Hilbert function of \(A\) modulo the leading forms equals \(\mathrm{HS}_A\) times the local factors, truncated. That would need exactness beyond the first syzygies. That is what the component correction, the board low-density entry and the board degree-six entry tested, with raw tops in place of pattern ideals. Those tests planted components whose tops happen to lift or did not examine lifting, so they bear on the hypothesis's Hilbert-function form, not on lifting.

Against the goal

  • A heuristic on size. The hypothesis concerns small constraints. The dimension ceiling of the wide-conditioning conjecture came from affine equations, each forbidding two thirds of a form's values. A forbid-value constraint on a width-\(w\) family forbids \(3^{-w}\) of its values. The prediction \(\mathrm{HS}_A\prod_b(1-t^{2w_b}/(1+t+t^2)^{w_b})\) stays positive through \(D\) roughly while the total density \(\sum_b3^{-w_b}\) is below one, the core statement's own condition. This is a heuristic reading of the product, not a computed bound, and it assumes local freeness throughout.
  • Condition (a) on the base. The base's \(z\)-injective range is not established here for the weak unary base at the degrees the goal needs, about \((4p-1)h\). It is a property of PHP alone. The recorded obstruction quotient uses it as a hypothesis too.
  • What is left. For forbid-value constraints, no refutation of degree \(D\) would follow from: the corrected hypothesis for the families a refutation produces, local freeness, nonempty allowed sets, spans of dimension at most about \(D/(p-1)\), and (a). The logarithmic-prefix images \(g_{b,i}\prod_{j\in S_b}L_{b,j}^{p-1}\) are not forbid-value products, so applying this to the core statement needs an adaptation. The hypothesis is open in the model and on the board, and random evidence cannot settle it for adversarial families.

Next step

The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer first adapts the constraint form: rewrite the logarithmic-prefix images \(g_{b,i}\prod_jL_{b,j}^{p-1}\) as forbid-value constraints, or extend the Frobenius lemma to them, since without that the conditional result does not reach the core statement. Then it tests the lifting side of the hypothesis on the board. Take components of the recorded kinds with both kinds of right-hand side: overlapping pairs with meeting and with disjoint forbidden lines, and a triple of each type in the catalogue. Plant them among random constraints at \(n=7\), degrees 4 and 5, and at \(n=8\), degree 6. Compare the full homogenized closure with the prediction built from \(I(P_C)\). The closure is needed here, not only the top algebra: that is the extension board_degk.cpp needs. Size it before coding. The step ends with the comparison, or with the size count if it does not fit.

Verification gate. Re-read: the socle criterion and its proof, the statement of the filtered obstruction quotient, and the bounded-span equivalence with its proof. Claim searches found the recorded obstruction quotient, which the reduction here follows, and no recorded Frobenius lift or component hypothesis. The pair computation enumerates all configurations up to the stated normalization. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed the Frobenius lemma, the induction and the pair data. It refuted the first formulation of the hypothesis with the narrow-form example above, which is now part of the entry. It required changes, all adopted:

Prefix images are families of forbid-value constraints; their components are whole blocks, so the component route meets the core statement's inductive step

23 September 2026 · Working lemma and analysis · Weak unary base over \(\mathbb F_p\), logarithmic-prefix images. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The component hypothesis is stated for forbid-value constraints \(\prod_k(1-(\ell_k-a_k)^{p-1})\). The goal's constraints are the logarithmic-prefix images \(g_iQ\), with \(g_i=1-L_i^{p-1}\), \(Q=\prod_{j\in S}L_j^{p-1}\), \(|S|=k\) of order \(\log n\), and degree budget \((4p-1)(p-1)k\). Can the hypothesis be applied to them? The cycle ends with the adapted statement, or with the obstruction.

The raw images are not forbid-value constraints

The top of \(g_iQ\) is \(-\prod_{j\in S\cup\{i\}}L_j^{p-1}\), the same as that of a forbid-value constraint on the same forms. But the Frobenius syzygies do not lift the same way. For \(j\in S\), \(L_j\cdot g_iQ\equiv L_j\,g_i\,Q_{S\setminus j}\) modulo the base, because \(L_j^p\equiv L_j\). The right side has degree \((p-1)k+1\) and vanishes on every allowed point, since \(g_iQ=0\) forbids \(L_i=0\) with all \(L_{j'}\ne0\). So the raw image derives a lower-degree consequence, a degree fall, whenever the top \(L_jL_i^{p-1}\prod_{S\setminus j}L^{p-1}\) is nonzero in \(A\). For \(i\) itself the lift is exact: \(L_i(1-L_i^{p-1})\equiv0\).

The rewrite

Lemma (prefix rewrite). On the weak unary base over \(\mathbb F_p\), the image \(g_iQ\) and the \((p-1)^{k}\) forbid-value constraints \[ G_a=(1-L_i^{p-1})\prod_{j\in S}\bigl(1-(L_j-a_j)^{p-1}\bigr),\qquad a\in(\mathbb F_p^\times)^S, \] derive each other in PC of degree at most \((p-1)(2k+1)\).

Proof. Every identity used is an identity of functions of single affine forms \(L\), in \(\mathbb F_p[L]/(L^p-L)\), and \(L^p-L\) follows from Booleanity at degree \(p\) (as in the logarithmic-prefix proof).

  • For \(a\ne0\), \(L^{p-1}(1-(L-a)^{p-1})\equiv1-(L-a)^{p-1}\), since both sides are the indicator of \(L=a\). So \(G_a\equiv g_iQ\cdot\prod_{j\in S}(1-(L_j-a_j)^{p-1})\), a multiple of \(g_iQ\) of degree at most \((p-1)(2k+1)\).
  • Conversely, \(L^{p-1}=\sum_{a\ne0}(1-(L-a)^{p-1})\) exactly as polynomials, since both sides have degree below \(p\) and agree as functions. Expanding \(Q\) gives \(g_iQ=\sum_aG_a\) exactly.

The multiples of \(L^p-L\) used in the first direction stay within degree \((p-1)(2k+1)\). \(\square\)

For \(k\ge1\) and \(p\ge3\) the bound is below the budget \((4p-1)(p-1)k\). So within the budget the prefix system is a system of forbid-value constraints on the same forms, with the same allowed patterns, and each \(G_a\) has value 0 on \(L_i\). This matches the component hypothesis's syntax. It does not remove falls: all \((p-1)^k\) of the \(G_a\) share the top \(\pm\prod L^{p-1}\), so each difference \(G_a\mp G_{a'}\) is itself a fall. Both kinds of fall are local to the block, and only replacing the block by a basis of its pattern ideal \(I(P_C)\) absorbs them. The Frobenius lemma, the conditional result and the degree condition were stated at \(p=3\), and the discussion below applies them there. Their odd-\(p\) versions, \((\ell-a)^p\equiv\ell-a\) at degree \((p-1)w+1\) and the bounded-span degree at general \(p\), are not checked here.

The components are blocks

Assume each \(G_a\)'s forms are independent, as the definition of a circuit requires. The \((p-1)^k\) constraints from one image share their \(k+1\) forms, and images \(i,i'\) of one block share the \(k\) forms of \(S_b\). Their families span at most \(k+2<2(k+1)\) dimensions, so they form circuits. So each block's constraints merge into one component, whose span is the block's whole input set, of dimension up to \(h_b\). The component hypothesis needs \((p-1)d_C+2w_C\le D\) for the bounded-span equivalence. That allows spans of order \((4p-1)k\), that is \(O(\log n)\) inputs per block. Compiled blocks have up to \(\binom{v+p-1}{p-1}\) inputs, the weak-base compiler's input bound, polynomial in \(n\), so for general inventories the local part is not bounded. Blocks sharing forms merge further.

What remains is a different split. The local part is one block: the constraints from one family of forms, with its own allowed-pattern set. Nothing recorded handles it in general. The one-predicate theorem concerns one old affine form with one predicate, on the functional base, with robust active rows. It does not cover a block with many inputs and a pattern set on the weak base. The global part is genericity across blocks: syzygies of the blocks' leading forms generated by Koszul syzygies between blocks and by syzygies inside each block. That is the inductive step of the core statement, adding one wide constraint to a system known to extend, in the language of syzygies. The core-statement review asked for it at a degree cost that does not grow with the number of constraints.

Assessment and next step

The adaptation succeeds for the constraint form's syntax, with the rewrite lemma, and fails for boundedness. The hypothesis's other conditions are also unmet in general. Local freeness fails for narrow blocks: the hole family's forms \(X_{jt}-1\) collide in \(A\). Nonempty allowed sets and the base condition (a) are separate requirements. In the goal's setting the components of the hypothesis are whole blocks, not bounded overlaps. The low-density evidence of the last cycles concerned constraints on 2 to 5 forms, and it supports Koszul-type genericity between small components. It does not address blocks with many inputs, or several blocks overlapping in forms. So the component line has reformulated the core statement's inductive step, with a conditional exclusion theorem attached. It has not proved it.

That makes the next cycle a route review of odd-prime-clause-transfer, before more component work. Five research cycles have passed since the affine-line review. The review should weigh the one-block local part, which nothing recorded covers for many inputs, against the cross-block genericity, which is open, and decide what to test or prove next. The step ends with that review.

Verification gate. Re-read: the odd-prime wide-clause statement and the reduction's form of \(g\), \(Q\), \(S_b\) and the budget, and the component hypothesis with its degree condition. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed the fall computation, the rewrite lemma, the budget check and the merging argument. It required changes, all adopted:

  • the fall stated as conditional on the top being nonzero in \(A\);
  • the claim that the rewrite cures falls withdrawn, since the \(G_a\) share one top;
  • the lemma's degree tightened, with the second direction exact;
  • the scope restricted to \(p=3\), where the hypothesis is stated;
  • local freeness and the other hypotheses stated as unmet in general;
  • the input bound attributed to the compiler;
  • the one-predicate theorem described correctly;
  • the independence assumption for circuits stated.

Route review: the component line gives a clean conditional theorem, but its conditions fail for the goal's blocks; the next cross-block case needs a proof

23 September 2026 · Route review · The component line restates the missing step precisely; the next step is a proof: the two-form lift extended to two width-two constraints. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

The line's general claim. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. Since the affine-line review, the thread has worked in the core statement's regime of small constraints. The claim is that the batched mechanism is syzygy genericity. Group the constraints into components, and replace each by its pattern ideal. Then every syzygy of the leading forms should be generated by Koszul, Frobenius and component-local ones. Given that, the recorded marked presentation excludes low-degree refutations: that is the conditional result of the component hypothesis.

What the goal needs. The odd-prime wide-clause statement of the logarithmic-prefix reduction. For \(M=n^K\) blocks, with \(M(1-1/p)^k<1\) and \(k\) of order \(\log n\), some choice of prefixes must leave the weak base plus the images with no PC refutation of degree \((4p-1)(p-1)k\).

What the line established

  • Every low-density defect seen in the model comes from a small overlap (component correction). On the board, at \(n=7\) in degree 5 and at \(n=8\) in degree 6, random constraints meet the prediction, and an overlapping pair adds exactly its model coefficient (\(n=7\), \(n=8\)).
  • Proved: the overlapping-pair lemma, the Frobenius lift and the prefix rewrite. There is also a C++ tool that makes degree-6 board tests at \(n=8\) take minutes.
  • The conditional result, with its hypotheses: the component hypothesis itself, local freeness, bounded spans, nonempty allowed sets, and the base \(z\)-injective.
  • In the goal's setting the components are whole blocks (prefix adaptation).

Falsification attempt

Can the hypothesis hold for the blocks a refutation produces? Its conditions fail in the recorded ways (prefix adaptation):

  • The degree condition \((p-1)d_C+2w_C\le D\) allows spans of \(O(\log n)\) forms. A block's span, the whole component in the goal's setting, can reach the compiler's polynomial input bound.
  • Local freeness fails for narrow blocks: the hole family's forms collide in \(A\).

If the degree condition were dropped, local freeness would still be capped. It needs \(\mathrm{HS}_A/(1+t+t^2)^{d_C}\) nonnegative through \(D\). The fill was computed only at \(D=3\) (\(r=8,14,22\) at \(n=6,7,8\), clause-transfer review), of order \((N+1-2D)(N-1)\). A span can reach \(\dim A_1=(N+1)(N-1)\).

The one-block local part is also not covered. The recorded weighted elimination removes compiled blocks with private coefficient variables from a weighted derivation, at additive cost \(d+(p-1)\sum_b\delta_b\). It does not apply to prefix-image axioms, which have no private variables, and nothing recorded covers one block with many inputs. What the goal needs is a cost that does not grow with the number of blocks.

What can computation test of the cross-block part? Let \(e\) be the initial degree of the blocks' leading-form ideals \(J_b\). The independence formula below predicts \(J_1\cap J_2=0\) in degrees below \(2e\), and the Koszul products only from degree \(2e\). So a test below \(2e\) can detect a non-Koszul interaction, a nonzero intersection, but it cannot test the Koszul-level prediction. The degree-6 families at \(n=8\) (several constraints with degree-4 tops) found no such low-degree interaction, and they did find the overlapping pair's local one. How large \(A_8\) is at \(n=8\) or \(9\), and so whether degree 8 is within reach, was not checked. Degree 8 needs at least 8 holes, and at \(n=9\) it is spanned by \(\binom98\cdot10^8=9\cdot10^8\) monomials before the relations. So the random small cases say nothing yet about Koszul-level behaviour in the goal's regime.

Assessment of this line

The line has made the missing step precise. There is a clean conditional theorem: syzygy genericity plus lifting excludes refutations. It has calibrated where small overlaps matter, with a proved local lemma. The evidence says random small constraints behave generically on the board. But the hypothesis's conditions fail for the goal's blocks, and its local freeness is capped by span, like the affine line. The cross-block genericity it needs remains a Fröberg-type statement, open. The random small cases that support it saw no low-degree interaction, but did not reach the degree where Koszul-level behaviour would show. For the goal as stated the line is weak. Its reusable part is the conditional theorem's shape. With the base \(z\)-injective, top syzygies generated by liftable kinds exclude refutations, and nothing in that shape needs freeness.

Next step: the smallest cross-block case, by proof

The smallest cross-block case already recorded is two single forms. The two-form lift gives a common polarized matching lift of two row-linear forms from \(K_d\) to \(K_{d+p-1}\). It needs every pencil direction over the algebraic closure to have at least \(2d+2p-1\) active rows and evaluation robustness through \(3d+3p-1\) deleted labels. It works on the functional base, requires supplied compatible polarized targets, and does not assemble a full source. The next case in the small-constraint regime is two width-two constraints, with tops \(\mu_1^2\nu_1^2\) and \(\mu_2^2\nu_2^2\). Call the four forms collectively wide when every nonzero combination over the algebraic closure satisfies the two-form lift's row and robustness conditions.

The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer attempts that two-product lift: a common extension for the pair, under collective width, through a degree linear in the width. The route is to read the two-form lift's proof (the projective-line lemma with the amplitude theorem) and extend its pencil argument from one form per constraint to a pair of forms. A proof would be the first cross-block case in the goal's regime. A failure would show which part of the two-form machinery does not extend to products, and that would redirect the line. The step ends with the proof or with that point.

The independence formula, \(\mathrm{HS}(A/(J_1+J_2))=\mathrm{HS}(A/J_1)\mathrm{HS}(A/J_2)/\mathrm{HS}_A\), equivalently \(\mathrm{HS}(J_1\cap J_2)=\mathrm{HS}(J_1)\mathrm{HS}(J_2)/\mathrm{HS}_A\), remains the heuristic Hilbert-function form of the target. Here \(J_b\) must be the full leading-form ideal of the block. For \(k=1\) it contains degree-3 forms \(L_1L_i^2\) beyond the raw tops.

The two-product lift needs the multi-operator step; for a pencil, joint freeness is a splitting-type condition on its kernel bundle

23 September 2026 · Working identity and a finite check · Weak unary PHP over \(\mathbb F_3\), \(n=8\), degree three; pencils of two forms. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The component review proposed extending the recorded two-form lift to two width-two constraints. The cycle ends with that lift, or with the point where the machinery fails.

Where the recorded machinery stops

The two-form lift applies the projective-line lemma. Given alternating exactness for every direction of a pencil of two commuting \(p\)-nilpotent operators, it lifts closed polarized targets. Its proof works on the projective line of directions. Two width-two constraints involve four forms, hence four operators \(D_{\mu_1},D_{\nu_1},D_{\mu_2},D_{\nu_2}\), and a joint lift needs conditions over all directions of their span. For four operators the directions form \(\mathbf P^3\). The record says the extension beyond two operators is not automatic but a proof obligation: the corresponding cohomology groups, such as \(H^2(\mathbf P^2,\mathcal O(-3))\), do not vanish, and characteristic three matters because the twist \(-p\) equals \(-3\). Stronger recorded results settle the naive form. The symmetric-lift entry shows that the closed-tuple form of the two-parameter lemma is false for three or more operators (obs:closed-tuple-lift-fails-three-operators). It proves a symmetric lifting lemma on free modules, with the obstruction for general modules an \(\operatorname{Ext}^1\) group (lem:symmetric-lift-free-modules). The truncated Dade entry shows that exactness along every direction does not imply the joint statement without a genericity condition. So the recorded machinery does not give the two-product lift. This is the recorded obstruction, not a new one.

A structural reading of the genericity condition for pencils

For two forms the missing condition can be identified exactly. Let \(G(w)=G_a+wG_b\) be the degree-\(k\) multiplication pencil from \(A_{k-1}\) to \(A_k\), \(N=\gamma_k\), with right minimal indices \(\varepsilon_i\). There are \(N-\rho\) of them, where \(\rho\) is the normal rank.

Lemma (pencil splitting identity). \(\#\{i:\varepsilon_i=0\}=\dim\bigl(A/(\ell_a,\ell_b)\bigr)_k\). The right kernel sheaf of \(G(w)\) on \(\mathbf P^1\) splits as \(\bigoplus_i\mathcal O(-\varepsilon_i)\) (the minimal-basis theorem of Forney, imported). It has rank \(N-\rho\) and degree \(-\sum_i\varepsilon_i=-(\rho-\sum_j\eta_j-k_{\mathrm{reg}})\), and the joint quotient in degree \(k\) is its number of trivial summands. If \(G(w)\) has rank \(\rho\) at every point of \(\mathbf P^1\), including \(\infty\), its fibres are the pointwise kernels.

Proof. The minimal indices of degree 0 count the constant vectors \(x\) with \(G_ax=G_bx=0\), the common right kernel of the two maps. That kernel is dual to \(A_k/(\ell_aA_{k-1}+\ell_bA_{k-1})\), and it has dimension \(N-\operatorname{rank}[G_a;G_b]\). The splitting of the kernel sheaf by the minimal indices is Forney's minimal-basis theorem, and the degree formula is the Kronecker count \(\rho=\sum\varepsilon_i+\sum\eta_j+k_{\mathrm{reg}}\). \(\square\)

So for two forms, freeness in degree \(k\) holds exactly when the number of trivial summands equals the prediction \([t^k]\,\mathrm{HS}_A/(1+t+t^2)^2\). A non-pointwise defect is then a change in splitting type at fixed rank and degree.

The Toeplitz ranks of the recorded pencil computation give the splitting types directly: \(\#\{\varepsilon\le d\}=N-(\operatorname{rank}T_d-\operatorname{rank}T_{d-1})\). At \(n=8\), degree 3, \(N=22929\), \(\rho=1655\) (pencil_closure.py, splitting_n8.json):

pencil\(\varepsilon=0\)\(\varepsilon=1\)\(\varepsilon=2\)
occupancy pair19685152564
two random pairs19682153161

For both, \(k_{\mathrm{reg}}=0\) and \(\sum\eta=2\) exactly, so both have \(\sum\varepsilon=1653\) and 21274 summands. The occupancy pair's bundle has 3 more trivial summands and 3 more summands \(\mathcal O(-2)\), and 6 fewer \(\mathcal O(-1)\), than the random pairs. The 3 extra trivial summands are its joint excess of 3. The random pairs have 19682 trivial summands, the prediction, so they are free in degree 3. Their splitting is not the balanced one, which would have only \(\mathcal O\) and \(\mathcal O(-1)\). Whether the free splitting type is unique was not shown.

Assessment and next step

The two-product lift is out of reach of the recorded tools: it needs the multi-operator step. For pencils, the genericity it needs has a precise form, a splitting-type condition on kernel bundles over \(\mathbf P^1\). For more forms the natural analogue is a family of sheaves over \(\mathbf P^{r-1}\) attached to modules over \(u(\mathfrak g)\). That is the setting of the theory of modules of constant Jordan type and their vector bundles. The record has used it only through a claim search in the symmetric-lift entry's gate, and through Dade's lemma, imported there.

The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer is a literature step, with web access. As pointers only: Carlson–Friedlander–Pevtsova, Modules of constant Jordan type (J. reine angew. Math. 2008); Friedlander–Pevtsova on the associated bundles; and Carlson–Friedlander–Suslin (Comment. Math. Helv. 2011) on modules of equal images and equal kernels. This also discharges the truncated Dade entry's pending literature step on Dade's lemma and rank varieties. Ask two questions:

  • Is there a freeness or projectivity criterion, or a statement about "equal images" or "equal kernels" modules, that controls the joint behaviour from pointwise data plus bundle invariants?
  • Does anything survive truncation to a degree range, which is what the thread needs?

Record the exact statements, their hypotheses and their field conventions, and test the most promising one against the occupancy pair's splitting data above. The step ends with the literature findings and that test.

A fresh-context reviewer confirmed the identity, its orientation and every number in the table. It required changes, all adopted:

  • the degree stated through \(\rho\) and \(\sum\eta\), which are not pointwise data;
  • the splitting cited to Forney's theorem, with no eigenvalue hypothesis needed for the count;
  • the freeness criterion limited to the count of trivial summands;
  • the recorded obstruction described accurately, with its stronger recorded forms cited;
  • the literature named as pointers only.

Constant Jordan type: pointwise data never control the bundles, so the missing genericity is not in the literature's criteria; r = 2 is recorded, r ≥ 3 is the open case

23 September 2026 · Literature step · Modules of constant Jordan type and their bundles; no new mathematics. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The pencil splitting entry read a non-pointwise defect as a jump in the splitting type of a kernel bundle. It asked whether the theory of modules of constant Jordan type gives a freeness criterion from pointwise data plus bundle invariants, and whether anything survives truncation to a degree range. The cycle ends with the findings.

Sources read and what they say

  • Carlson, Friedlander and Pevtsova, Modules of constant Jordan type, J. reine angew. Math. 614 (2008) 191–234, arXiv:0707.3845, read in the arXiv version. For a finite group scheme over a field of characteristic \(p\), a module has constant Jordan type if its Jordan type is the same at every \(\pi\)-point. For an elementary abelian \(p\)-group, the \(\pi\)-points are the points of the rank variety, that is the directions in \(\mathfrak g\) in the thread's notation. The class is closed under sums, summands, duals, tensor products and Heller shifts. Example 2.2 and Remark 2.3 recall Jantzen's example: for rank 2, \(kE/I^2\) and its dual have the same Jordan type at every point but are not isomorphic. That is the classical form of the thread's non-pointwise phenomenon. Section 7 derives a case of Macaulay's generalized principal ideal theorem from this theory. No statement in the paper concerns graded modules truncated to a degree range.
  • Benson and Pevtsova, A realization theorem for modules of constant Jordan type and vector bundles, arXiv:1007.3827, from the abstract and search summaries, not read in full. Functors \(\mathcal F_i\) send modules of constant Jordan type for a rank-\(r\) elementary abelian group to vector bundles on \(\mathbf P^{r-1}\). Every vector bundle of rank \(s\) is \(\mathcal F_1\) of some module of stable constant Jordan type \([1]^s\), up to a Frobenius twist when \(p\) is odd. For odd \(p\) the Chern numbers of such bundles are divisible by \(p\).
  • Carlson, Friedlander and Suslin on modules of equal images and equal kernels, Comment. Math. Helv. 2011. Located by search as a pointer, not read.
  • Chindris, Kang and Kline, The Jordan type of a multiparameter persistence module, arXiv:2510.22116. It concerns modules over posets, not polynomial rings or linear forms, and is not relevant.

What this means for the thread

For whole, finite-dimensional modules, Dade's lemma, imported in the symmetric-lift entry, already turns freeness at every point into freeness. The thread's problem is the truncated version, where it fails (truncated Dade entry). The literature explains why no pointwise criterion can replace it. By the realization theorem, fixing the Jordan types at all points leaves the bundles essentially arbitrary. Global information, the bundles, is not controlled by local information, the Jordan types. The pencil splitting identity says the same for two forms: pointwise freeness fixes the kernel bundle's rank and, with the left indices, its degree, but not its splitting type. So any genericity input must constrain bundle-level data directly. The sources read contain no criterion for graded, truncated modules.

Checked against the record, the two-form case is already covered under width. The two-form lift proves joint lifting for collectively wide pencils on the functional base. The occupancy pair falls outside it: its robustness condition \(3d+3p-1\) exceeds the 8 labels at \(n=8\). So for \(r=2\), width supplies the bundle genericity, by the recorded proof. The open case begins at \(r=3\), where bundles on \(\mathbf P^2\) need not split, and where the record shows that the closed-tuple form of the lift is false.

A small consistency check, not a test of any criterion. The degrees of the degree-3 kernel bundles in the pencil splitting entry are \(-1653=-3\cdot551\), divisible by \(p=3\), in line with the divisibility of Chern numbers for odd \(p\). The theorem concerns whole modules of stable constant Jordan type, not the truncated graded case, so this proves nothing.

Assessment and next step

The literature confirms the structural picture and gives vocabulary, but no tool the thread can apply. What remains is the \(r\ge3\) genericity for wide forms, the open core of the batched step.

The symmetric-lift entry proposed a concrete first case that was never carried out: decide by hand, at \(r=3\), \(p=3\), \(d=1\), whether symmetric tuples lift under the two-parameter lemma's hypotheses. That is the smallest place where the open case can be decided. There \(K_0=k\), and a symmetric 6-tuple splits into its moment part and a part in the common kernel. The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer takes it up. Re-read that entry's setup and its Ext identification, then decide the case by hand. The step ends with a proof that the window at \(r=3\), \(d=1\) is covered by the two-parameter hypotheses, or with a counterexample showing it must widen.

The Carlson–Friedlander–Pevtsova paper was read in its arXiv text for the definitions, Proposition 2.1 with Example 2.2 and Remark 2.3, and Section 7. The Benson–Pevtsova statement comes from the abstract and search summaries. The full text is not in the repository, since third-party papers are not committed. The claim that no truncated criterion appears refers only to what was read.

At the first degree, symmetric tuples of any number of forms lift in the matching complex under linear width, because joint kernels are spanned by short elements

23 September 2026 · Working proof and a finite check · Lemma degree \(d=1\), \(p=3\), any number \(r\) of forms. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The previous entry proposed deciding by hand whether symmetric tuples lift at \(r=3\), \(p=3\), \(d=1\) (the symmetric-lift entry's first case). This cycle does so.

Correction to the previous entry. The literature entry called this case "never carried out". That is wrong. The cocycle-reduction entry computed it exactly: symmetric tuples lift at \(d=1\) for \(r\le5\) forms from width \(t=4\) (ex:matching-symmetric-lift-width). It also reduced symmetric lifting to forced-forms exactness, which the forced-forms check found at the one-form row count. The local-lift review then set the line aside, with restart condition "a density mechanism that consumes local lifts of \(O(\operatorname{polylog})\) forms". That condition has not been met, although two later reviews came back to the joint statement for many forms (see below). The pencil splitting entry and the literature entry cited the symmetric-lift entry without these three successors. What this cycle adds is a proof where the record had a finite check and an unproved reduction.

Setting

Let \(k\) be a field of characteristic 3. Use the matching complex of the amplitude theorem, with \(r\) forms.

  • \(K_s\) is the direct sum, over \(s\)-row sets, of arrays on injections into the labels \(\Omega\), with zero ordinary marginal in every row. \(K_0=k\), and \(K_1=\bigoplus_iV_i\), where \(V_i\) is the space of sum-zero functions on \(\Omega\) for row \(i\).
  • Form \(j\) has row functions \(f^{(j)}_i\), and \(D_j=\sum_i\delta_i^{f^{(j)}_i}\). For \(x\in V_i\), put \(F_i(x)=(\langle f^{(j)}_i,x\rangle)_j\in k^r\), and let \(P_i=F_i(V_i)\). Put \(\Theta_u=\sum_ju_jD_j\).
  • A nonzero \(u\in k^r\) is active on row \(i\) if \(u\notin P_i^\perp\), that is, if \(\sum_ju_jf^{(j)}_i\) is not constant. The forms have width \(t\) if every nonzero \(u\) is active on at least \(t\) rows.
  • They are \(L\)-robust if, for every row \(i\), the evaluation matrix \(M_i\) with rows \(1,f^{(1)}_i,\dots,f^{(r)}_i\) keeps its rank after deletion of any \(L\) labels.

With \(\delta=2\) and \(A=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N^r:|\alpha|=2\}\), the polarized lift is \(\Lambda w=(D^\alpha w)_{\alpha\in A}\). This omits the unit factors \(m(\alpha)\), so the symmetry conditions below are stated for \(\zeta_\alpha=z_\alpha/m(\alpha)\). A tuple \((\zeta_\alpha)\) in \(K_1\) is symmetric if \(D_j\zeta_\alpha=D_i\zeta_\beta\) whenever \(\alpha+e_j=\beta+e_i\), and \(D_i\zeta_{2e_i}=0\). The common value is a scalar \(\mu_b\), for \(|b|=3\), with \(\mu_{3e_i}=0\).

Lemma (first-degree lift). Suppose the forms have width at least \(r+3\) and are \((r+1)(r+2)\)-robust. Then every symmetric tuple in \(K_1\) is \(\Lambda w\) for some \(w\in K_3\).

Proof

Tensors. Let \(x\in V_a\), \(c\in V_s\), \(c'\in V_t\) lie on three distinct rows, with pairwise disjoint label supports. Their tensor \(x\otimes c\otimes c'\) is supported on injections, and each ordinary marginal is a multiple of a factor's sum, hence zero, so the tensor lies in \(K_3\). The weighted marginal on a row multiplies by that factor's evaluation, which gives \[ \Theta_u^2(x\otimes c\otimes c')=2\bigl[(u\cdot p_a)(u\cdot p_s)\,c'+(u\cdot p_a)(u\cdot p_t)\,c+(u\cdot p_s)(u\cdot p_t)\,x\bigr], \] with \(p_a=F_a(x)\), \(p_s=F_s(c)\), \(p_t=F_t(c')\). Likewise \(D^bw=b!\,[u^b]\,(u\cdot p_a)(u\cdot p_s)(u\cdot p_t)\) for \(|b|=3\). Here \(\Theta_u^2=\sum_\alpha m(\alpha)u^\alpha D^\alpha\), and for \(D^b\), with \(|b|=3\), each assignment of the three operators to the three rows counts \(b!\) times.

Choosing factors. By robustness, if \(T\) is a set of at most \((r+1)(r+2)\) labels, the matrix \(M_i\) restricted to \(\Omega\setminus T\) has the same column space. That space contains \((0,p)\) for every \(p\in P_i\). So for every \(p\in P_i\) there is \(c\in V_i\) with \(F_i(c)=p\), supported off \(T\), on at most \(\operatorname{rank}M_i\le r+1\) labels.

Spanning. Suppose \(\beta\) is a symmetric bilinear form on \(k^r\) that vanishes on \(P_s\times P_t\) for all distinct \(s,t\) outside a row set \(S\) with \(|S|\le r+1\). Fix \(s\notin S\). A \(u\) orthogonal to every \(P_t\), \(t\notin S\cup\{s\}\), is active on at most \(r+2\) rows, so \(u=0\) by width. Hence those \(P_t\) span \(k^r\), and \(\beta(p,\cdot)=0\) for \(p\in P_s\). The \(P_s\), \(s\notin S\), also span \(k^r\), so \(\beta=0\). The products \((u\cdot p)(u\cdot q)\) therefore span all quadratic forms in \(u\), since a linear functional on quadratic forms that vanishes on them defines such a \(\beta\). In the same way, width at least 3 shows that the products \((u\cdot p)(u\cdot q)(u\cdot q')\), with \(p,q,q'\) from three distinct rows, span all cubic forms.

Moments. Every sum of the tensors above lies in \(K_3\). Their mixed moments \(D^bw=b![u^b]\cdots\), with \(b!\in\{1,2\}\) a unit, therefore take every value in \(k^{\{b\text{ mixed}\}}\): the cubic forms are spanned, using labels at most \(2(r+1)\) at a time. Given a symmetric tuple \(\zeta\) with moments \(\mu\), take such a \(w_1\) with \(D^bw_1=\mu_b\). Then \(\zeta-\Lambda w_1\) is symmetric with all moments zero, so each entry lies in the joint kernel \[ Z=\{x\in K_1:\ D_jx=0\ \text{for all }j\}=\Bigl\{x:\ \textstyle\sum_iF_i(x_i)=0\Bigr\}. \]

Short generation of \(Z\). Call \(x\in Z\) short if it is supported on at most \(r+1\) rows and at most \((r+1)^2\) labels. \(Z\) is spanned by short elements.

  • The kernel of \(x\mapsto(F_i(x_i))_i\) is \(\bigoplus_i(V_i\cap\ker F_i)\). Each summand is the kernel of \(M_i\), which is spanned by circuit vectors. A circuit vector lies on one row and has at most \(\operatorname{rank}M_i+1\le r+2\) labels.
  • The image of \(Z\) is the set of \((p_i)\in\bigoplus_iP_i\) with \(\sum_ip_i=0\). Choose a basis of each \(P_i\). The linear relations among all these basis vectors of \(k^r\) are spanned by circuits, which have at most \(r+1\) terms and so involve at most \(r+1\) rows. Lift each circuit by choosing, on each of its rows, some \(x_i\in V_i\) with the required evaluation and at most \(r+1\) labels.

Kernel part. Let \(x=\sum_{i\in S}x_i\in Z\) be short, with \(p_i=F_i(x_i)\) and \(\sum_ip_i=0\). Take rows \(s\ne t\) outside \(S\), with \(c\in V_s\) and \(c'\in V_t\) chosen as above, off the labels of \(x\) and off each other. That uses at most \((r+1)^2+(r+1)\) labels. Then \(w=\sum_{i\in S}x_i\otimes c\otimes c'\in K_3\). In the sum of the displayed formula over \(i\), the terms in \(c\) and \(c'\) carry the factor \(u\cdot\sum_ip_i=0\), so \[ \Theta_u^2w=2\,(u\cdot p_s)(u\cdot p_t)\,x . \] So \(\Lambda w=(\lambda_\alpha x)_\alpha\), where \(\lambda_\alpha\) is \(2[u^\alpha](u\cdot p_s)(u\cdot p_t)/m(\alpha)\). By the spanning step, these quadratic forms span all quadratic forms, so every tuple \((\lambda_\alpha x)_\alpha\), with arbitrary scalars \(\lambda_\alpha\), is a lift. With short generation, every tuple of elements of \(Z\) is a lift, including \(\zeta-\Lambda w_1\). \(\square\)

The method is the one of the recorded binary lifts, the multirow predicate-trade lift and the relative coded parity lift: lift a joint-kernel element by tensoring with fresh row vectors chosen off its labels. Those results are in characteristic two and go through the projective lemma. Here the odd-prime obstacle, polarization with \(\delta=2\), is met by the spanning of quadratic forms. Each piece gets its own inserted vectors \(c,c'\), chosen off that piece's labels. That is what avoids the obstacle recorded in the local-lift review: one inserted vector cannot avoid the labels of every tensor of a large target. Only the single-row kernel pieces need no cancellation between rows. For a piece over several rows, the cancellation is exact because the same \(c,c'\) serve every row of that piece. Nothing in the proof requires a row with \(P_i=k^r\). So a lack of joint row rank, forms that are dependent modulo constants on every row, is no obstruction; the check below confirms this.

Finite check

The script first_degree_lift.py computes, over \(\mathbb F_3\) at \(r=3\), the dimension of the symmetric tuples as a nullity, and the rank of \(\Lambda\). It checks that the image satisfies the symmetry equations.

  • On small boards, \(K_3\) is the exact nullspace of the marginal map on each row triple. This was run for \(N=6\) and \(9\) labels, \(R=3,\dots,7\) rows, two seeds each, with generic forms and with forms dependent on every row (\(f^{(3)}_i=a_if^{(1)}_i+b_if^{(2)}_i\), so \(\dim P_i\le2\)). Lifting holds in every case of width at least 4 and fails in every case of width at most 3. Examples: generic, 3 rows, 9 labels, 116 of 133; dependent, width 3, 5 rows, 9 labels, 228 of 229. Lifting holds in every dependent case of width 4 or 5.
  • On a board meeting the hypotheses, labels \(\mathbb F_3^4\) with random full-rank linear row maps to \(\mathbb F_3^3\), 6 and 7 rows, width 6 and 7 and 53-robust, sampled difference tensors reach the full symmetric dimension: 2869 of 2869 and 3349 of 3349. That proves the lemma's conclusion on these two boards.

In 15.9 seconds, the output is research/results/odd_prime_first_degree_lift_20260923/first_degree_lift.json. The measured threshold, width 4, matches the recorded one and lies below the lemma's \(r+3\). The lemma's width is sufficient, not sharp.

What this changes

At the first degree, the multi-operator lift is proved for any number of forms, with width linear in \(r\), output degree \(d+\delta\), and no exactness hypothesis. Linear growth is what the local-lift review found sufficient. The local-lift review set this line aside for lack of a density mechanism. The later column-tensor and clause-transfer reviews came back to the joint statement for many forms as the batched mechanism the route item needs, reached from the algebra side. They asked for an input specific to the board, because the implication from pointwise exactness fails in the toy models once \(r\ge3\). Short generation of joint kernels is such an input: it uses the board's tensor structure, which the toy models lack.

A conjectured extension to every degree \(d\) has two parts, both open.

  • Short generation: the joint kernels \(Z_s=\bigcap_j\ker D_j\cap K_s\), for \(1\le s\le d\), are spanned by elements on \(O(r)\) rows and labels.
  • Moment descent: the moments \(\mu_b\in K_{d-1}\), for \(|b|=3\), are realized as \(D^bw\) together with their own symmetry conditions, and so on down to \(K_0\).

A sketch suggests that the descent runs through the same tensor argument, with \(D^b\) applied directly instead of polarization, since \(b!\) is a unit when every \(b_i\le2\). It is not checked here. Given both parts, a short piece of \(Z_s\) would lift by tensoring with fresh vectors on \(d-s+2\) new rows.

The step from symmetric lifts to joint extension, the density mechanism, and the quadratic ceiling of the wide-conditioning conjecture all remain as recorded.

Assessment and next step

The cycle proved its case, and more: every \(r\) at the first degree. Two of the last three cycles took their question from an entry without reading its successors. The route check now requires a search for later links to a cited entry (CLAUDE.md).

The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer is short generation at level two, the first open part of the extension. Test first, at \(r=3\) with random forms, \(R=8\) rows and \(N=7\) labels:

  • \(K_2\) has \(28\cdot29=812\) dimensions, and \(Z_2\) has codimension at most \(8\cdot6\cdot3=144\) in it;
  • compare \(Z_2\) with the span of its elements supported on \(m\) rows, for \(m=4,5,6\): 70, 56 and 28 row sets, of at most 174, 290 and 435 dimensions.

With \(R=8>m\), shortness is a real restriction, and the test can fail. Then prove the observed bound, following the circuit argument of level one: row-local kernels, plus relations among the images. Then take up the moment descent. The step ends with short generation at level two proved, or with a joint-kernel element that no short elements span.

Verification gate. Re-read, from the notebook:

  • the amplitude theorem's statement and its definitions of \(K_s\) and \(\delta_i\);
  • the symmetric-lift entry's setting, lemma and next step;
  • the cocycle-reduction entry, the forced-forms check and the local-lift review;
  • the conclusions of the column-tensor and clause-transfer reviews.

Claim searches for symmetric lifting, polarized and moment lifts, and joint-kernel lifting found:

  • the cocycle reduction and the finite width check;
  • the free-module lemma;
  • the ternary pair theorem;
  • the binary multirow and relative coded lifts.

The exact \(\mathbb F_3\) check above tests the conclusion on boards meeting the hypotheses, and controls below width 4 fail. A fresh-context reviewer, given the draft, these dependencies and the script, found that the record does not imply the lemma for \(r\ge3\). It found no gap in the tensor formulas, the spanning, the short generation, the label budget or the reduction, and no unused hypothesis; width \(r+3\) is used only in the kernel part. It confirmed every number against the JSON. It required changes, all adopted:

  • the degree-\(d\) extension stated as a conjecture with two open parts;
  • \(\dim P_i\le2\) for the dependent family;
  • the label count of the 228-of-229 example;
  • "linear" for the row maps;
  • the binary analogues cited.

These changes only weaken or clarify the claims, so no further pass was made.

Symmetric lifting at every degree reduces to short generation of joint kernels, which holds at level two; the second-degree lift follows

23 September 2026 · Working proofs and finite checks · Matching complex, \(p=3\), any number \(r\) of forms. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The batched mechanism the item names is the joint lift for many forms. The first-degree lift proved it at lemma degree one, and it split the extension to every degree into two open parts: short generation of the joint kernels \(Z_s=\bigcap_j\ker D_j\cap K_s\), and a moment descent. This cycle tests short generation at level two, then tries to prove it and the descent. It ends with proofs, or with a joint-kernel element that no short elements span.

Finite check: level-two kernels are spanned on four or five rows

The script short_generation.py computes \(Z_2\) exactly over \(\mathbb F_3\). For each \(m\) it also computes the span of the subspaces \(Z_2(U)\), the elements supported on pairs inside an \(m\)-row set \(U\). Forms are random; "dependent" means the third form is a combination of the first two on every row.

Every row with three forms has two seeds, and the rows with two and four forms have one. Four rows suffice in every case but one dependent seed, which needs five, and \(m=6\) (and 7, where computed) adds nothing. The number of rows needed does not grow with \(r\) from 2 to 4, or with the board. So short generation holds at these sizes, with far fewer rows than the bound proved below.

Setting

Use the setting of the first-degree lift: a field \(k\) of characteristic 3, the matching complex \(K_s\), and \(r\) forms with operators \(D_j\) and evaluations \(F_i:V_i\to P_i\subseteq k^r\). Width, robustness and the evaluation matrices \(M_i\) are as defined there. Let \(R_1=\{(p_i)\in\bigoplus_iP_i:\sum_ip_i=0\}\), the relations among the rows' evaluations. A symmetric tuple \((\zeta_\alpha)_{|\alpha|=2}\) in \(K_d\) defines an \(R\)-linear map \(\varphi\) from \(\mathfrak m^2\) to \(K\) with \(\varphi(D^\alpha)=\zeta_\alpha\), by the construction of the symmetric-lift entry, which uses only the symmetry conditions. Put \(\tau_b=\varphi(D^b)\in K_{d+2-|b|}\) for \(|b|\ge2\); \(\tau_b=0\) when some \(b_j\ge3\). Say \(Z_s\) is \((\rho,\lambda)\)-short if it is spanned by elements each supported on at most \(\rho\) rows and \(\lambda\) labels.

The reduction

Lemma (short-generation reduction). Fix \(d\ge1\). Suppose that for each \(1\le s\le d\), \(Z_s\) is \((\rho_s,\lambda_s)\)-short. Suppose the width is at least \(\max_{0\le s\le d}(\rho_s+d+2-s)\), with \(\rho_0=0\). Suppose the forms are robust through \(\max_{0\le s\le d}\bigl(\lambda_s+(d+1-s)(r+1)\bigr)\) deleted labels, with \(\lambda_0=0\). Then every symmetric tuple in \(K_d\) is \((D^\alpha w)_{|\alpha|=2}\) for some \(w\in K_{d+2}\).

Proof. Put \(q_s=d+2-s\).

  • Tensors of short pieces. Let \(x\in Z_s\) be short on a row set \(S\), and let \(c_1,\dots,c_q\in V_{t_1},\dots,V_{t_q}\) lie on distinct rows outside \(S\), with label supports disjoint from each other and from \(x\). Then \(w=x\otimes c_1\otimes\dots\otimes c_q\in K_{s+q}\), and each \(D_j\) splits as \(D_j^{x}+D_j^{c}\), commuting parts acting on different tensor factors. Since every \(D_j^{x}\) kills \(x\) (for \(s=0\), \(x=1\)), \(D^bw=x\otimes D^b(c_1\otimes\dots\otimes c_q)\). This vanishes for \(|b|>q\), and for \(|b|=q\) equals \(b!\,[u^b]\prod_k(u\cdot p_k)\,x\), with \(p_k=F_{t_k}(c_k)\): each operator must hit a different \(c\)-row, and \(\Pi_jb_j!\) orders give the same term. When every \(b_j\le2\), \(b!\) is a power of 2, a unit.
  • Spanning. Suppose a symmetric \(q\)-linear form on \(k^r\) vanishes on \(P_{t_1}\times\dots\times P_{t_q}\) for all distinct rows outside \(S\). Fix all arguments but the last. The last ranges over rows outside \(S\) and the \(q-1\) fixed rows. Their \(P_t\) span \(k^r\), since a \(u\) orthogonal to all of them is active on at most \(|S|+q-1<\) width rows. So the form vanishes, by induction on the fixed arguments. A linear functional on forms of degree \(q\) that vanishes on the products \(\prod_k(u\cdot p_k)\) defines such a symmetric \(q\)-linear form, so it vanishes on all products of linear forms, hence on all monomials. Hence the products span all forms of degree \(q\). The vectors \(c_k\) exist, off the labels already used, by robustness, as in the first-degree lift. So every tuple \((\lambda_bx)_{|b|=q}\) with \(\lambda_b=0\) whenever some \(b_j\ge3\) is \((D^bw)_b\) for some \(w\) with \(D^{b'}w=0\) for \(|b'|>q\).
  • Descending induction. We build \(w^{(q)}\in K_{d+2}\), for \(q=d+2\) down to 2, with \(D^bw^{(q)}=\tau_b\) for all \(|b|\ge q\). Given \(w^{(q+1)}\), with \(w^{(d+3)}=0\), put \(\eta_b=\tau_b-D^bw^{(q+1)}\) for \(|b|=q\). Then \(D_j\eta_b=\tau_{b+e_j}-D^{b+e_j}w^{(q+1)}=0\) for every \(j\). So each \(\eta_b\) lies in \(Z_s\), \(s=d+2-q\) (for \(s=0\) this is no condition), and \(\eta_b=0\) when some \(b_j\ge3\). Fix a spanning set \(\{x_\ell\}\) of short elements of \(Z_s\), write \(\eta_b=\sum_\ell\lambda_{b,\ell}x_\ell\) with \(\lambda_{b,\ell}=0\) whenever some \(b_j\ge3\), and apply the previous point to each tuple \((\lambda_{b,\ell}x_\ell)_b\). The result is \(v\) with \(D^bv=\eta_b\) for \(|b|=q\) and \(D^{b'}v=0\) for \(|b'|>q\). Put \(w^{(q)}=w^{(q+1)}+v\). At \(q=2\), \(D^\alpha w^{(2)}=\zeta_\alpha\). \(\square\)

At \(d=1\), with \(\rho_1=r+1\) and \(\lambda_1=(r+1)^2\), this is the first-degree lift. It gives the conclusion of the cocycle reduction with short generation in place of its unproved forced-forms exactness. The output degree is \(d+2\) at every \(d\): no window is needed.

Short generation at level two

Lemma (level-two short generation). Put \(K=(r^3+r^2+2)/2\). If the forms are robust through \(2r+3\) deleted labels, then \(Z_2\) is \((\rho_2,\lambda_2)\)-short, with \(\rho_2=r^3+r^2+r+2\) and \(\lambda_2=8K(r+1)^3\).

Proof. For \(x\in K_2\) with pair components \(x_{ii'}\), let \(g_i(x_{ii'})\in V_i\otimes P_{i'}\) be the contraction of row \(i'\) by all \(r\) forms at once. The component of \((D_jx)_j\) on row \(i\) is \(\sum_{i'}g_i(x_{ii'})\), so \(x\in Z_2\) exactly when \[ \textstyle\sum_{i'\ne i}g_i(x_{ii'})=0\ \text{in } V_i\otimes k^r\quad\text{for every row } i . \] This condition depends only on the data \((g_i(x_{ii'}),g_{i'}(x_{ii'}))\) of each pair. Let \(Y\) be the elements whose every pair component has zero data. Each component of an element of \(Y\) is an injection array annihilated by both rows' evaluation matrices. By the recorded coded-trade spanning theorem, with robustness \(2r+3\), such arrays are spanned by tensors on one pair of rows with at most \(r+2\) labels per row. So \(Y\) is \((2,2r+4)\)-short, and \(Z_2\) is spanned by \(Y\) together with short realizations of generators of the data space.

Choose a set \(B_i\) of \(\operatorname{rank}M_i\le r+1\) labels on which the columns of \(M_i\) are independent and span its column space. Every \(p\in P_i\) then has a unique \(\sigma_i(p)\in V_i\) supported on \(B_i\) with \(F_i(\sigma_i(p))=p\), and \(\sigma_i\) is linear. Write \(V_i=\ker_i\oplus\sigma_i(P_i)\), \(\ker_i=V_i\cap\ker F_i\). The data of a pair split into two parts:

  • parts in \(\ker_i\otimes P_{i'}\);
  • a tensor \(e_{ii'}=(F_i\otimes1)g_i(x_{ii'})\in P_i\otimes P_{i'}\), which by compatibility is also \((1\otimes F_{i'})g_{i'}(x_{ii'})\).

The row conditions split the same way, and the data space is \(D^0\oplus T\):

  • \(D^0=\bigoplus_i\ker_i\otimes R_1^{(\ne i)}\), where \(R_1^{(\ne i)}\) consists of the relations not using row \(i\);
  • \(T\) is the set of symmetric edge tensors \((e_{ii'})\) with \(\sum_{i'}e_{ii'}=0\) in \(P_i\otimes k^r\) for every \(i\).
  • The part \(D^0\). It is spanned by \(a\otimes\rho\), with \(a\) a circuit vector of \(\ker_i\) (at most \(r+2\) labels) and \(\rho\) a circuit of \(R_1\) avoiding row \(i\) (at most \(r+1\) rows). Realize it by \(\sum_{i'}a\otimes c_{i'}\), with \(F_{i'}(c_{i'})=\rho_{i'}\) and \(c_{i'}\) off the support of \(a\). Its data are \(a\otimes\rho_{i'}\) on row \(i\), and \(F_i(a)\otimes c_{i'}=0\) on row \(i'\). It has \(r+2\) rows and at most \((r+2)+(r+1)^2\) labels.
  • The part \(T\) is \(\{t\in R_1\otimes R_1:\ t\text{ symmetric},\ t_{ii}=0\text{ for all } i\}\). The row conditions say \((1\otimes\Sigma)t=0\), where \(\Sigma\) is the sum map, so \(t\in P\otimes R_1\) with \(P=\bigoplus_iP_i\). Symmetry gives \(t\in R_1\otimes P\), hence \(t\in R_1\otimes R_1\). The converse is immediate.
  • Generators of \(T\). Choose a basis of \(\sum_iP_i\) made of basis vectors of the \(P_i\) on a set \(B_0\) of at most \(r\) rows. The fundamental circuits \(\rho_v\), one for each other basis vector \(v\) of each \(P_i\), form a basis of \(R_1\), each supported on \(B_0\cup\{\text{row}(v)\}\). Write \(t=\sum c_{vv'}\rho_v\otimes\rho_{v'}\) with \(c\) symmetric. At a row \(i\notin B_0\), the diagonal block is \(\sum c_{vv'}\,v\otimes v'\) over the basis vectors \(v,v'\) of \(P_i\), so \(c_{vv'}=0\) there. At each of the at most \(r\) rows of \(B_0\), the diagonal block gives at most \(\dim\operatorname{Sym}^2P_i\le r(r+1)/2\) linear equations. So \(T\) is the kernel of a linear map \(E\) of rank at most \(K-1\) on the coordinates \(c_{vv'}\) with \(\text{row}(v)\ne\text{row}(v')\) or both in \(B_0\). A kernel is spanned by vectors with at most \(\operatorname{rank}E+1\le K\) nonzero coordinates. Each coordinate \(\rho_v\odot\rho_{v'}\) is supported on \(B_0\) and two further rows. So \(T\) is spanned by elements on at most \(r+2K=\rho_2\) rows.
  • Realizing \(T\). Split the blocks \(t_{ii'}\), \(i<i'\), of such a generator into rank-one pieces \(p\otimes q\in P_i\otimes P_{i'}\). There are at most \(2K(r+1)^2\) of them. Realize each piece as follows. Let \(x=\sigma_i(p)\otimes c\) with \(F_{i'}(c)=q\) and \(c\) off the support of \(\sigma_i(p)\). Let \(\kappa=c-\sigma_{i'}(q)\in\ker_{i'}\), and let \(x'=-y\otimes\kappa\) with \(F_i(y)=p\) and \(y\) off the support of \(\kappa\). Then \(x+x'\) has data \(\sigma_i(p)\otimes q\) on row \(i\) and \(\sigma_{i'}(q)\otimes p\) on row \(i'\), the data of the piece. It uses at most \(4(r+1)\) labels. Summing gives the generator's data, and the sum lies in \(Z_2\). It has at most \(\rho_2\) rows and \(8K(r+1)^3=\lambda_2\) labels.

Every element of \(Z_2\) minus the realization of its data lies in \(Y\). \(\square\)

The recorded two-row product-code criterion is the obstruction to realizing prescribed two-row data with fixed supports. The realization above avoids it by choosing supports off one another, as robustness allows.

Lemma (second-degree lift). Suppose the forms have width at least \(r^3+r^2+r+4\) and are robust through \(\lambda_2+r+1\) deleted labels. Then every symmetric tuple in \(K_2\) is \((D^\alpha w)_{|\alpha|=2}\) for some \(w\in K_4\).

Proof. Apply the reduction with \(d=2\). The first-degree lift's short generation gives \((\rho_1,\lambda_1)=(r+1,(r+1)^2)\), and the level-two lemma gives \((\rho_2,\lambda_2)\). The reduction's width is then \(\max(4,\,r+4,\,\rho_2+2)=r^3+r^2+r+4\). Its robustness is \(\max(3(r+1),\,(r+1)^2+2(r+1),\,\lambda_2+r+1)=\lambda_2+r+1\), which also covers the \(2r+3\) of the level-two lemma. \(\square\)

Finite check of the second-degree lift

second_degree_lift.py computes the rank of \(\Lambda:K_4\to K_2^A\), with \(K_4\) exact, and the dimension of the symmetric tuples in \(K_2\), at \(r=3\) with 7 labels. It checks that the image satisfies the symmetry equations.

Widths are computed by widths.py (widths.json) for the same seeds. Lifting holds exactly from width 6. Together with the threshold of width 4 at \(d=1\), this fits width \(2d+2\) at \(r=3\), one seed per case: the amplitude theorem's count for one form in the position \(\ker D^{p-1}=\operatorname{im}D\) at \(K_{d+1}\). These boards do not meet the lemma's hypotheses, so this is evidence about the true threshold, not a check of the lemma. The proved width is polynomial in \(r\) because the circuit bound for \(T\) is crude; the level-two check needed at most five rows.

What this changes

The symmetric many-form lift is proved at degrees one and two for any number of forms, at output degree \(d+2\), with no exactness hypothesis. For every degree, only short generation of \(Z_s\) at \(s\ge3\) remains; the moment descent is proved.

At level three the level-two argument does not carry over as it stands. The analogue of \(T\) is the space of symmetric tensors in \(R_1^{\otimes3}\) with zero blocks wherever two slots lie on one row. Its diagonal conditions carry a free third slot, so their number is not bounded by \(r\), and the circuit bound fails. Mixed parts also appear, kernel vectors on some slots and \(T\)-type tensors on the others.

The lift remains a local ingredient. It covers polylogarithmically many forms at a time within the quadratic ceiling. The step from symmetric lifts to joint extension and the density mechanism are open, as recorded in the local-lift review.

Assessment and next step

This line now moves its general implication: two degrees are proved, and every degree has a clean sufficient condition that the data support. Four research cycles have passed since the last review.

The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer is short generation at level three. First test it: at \(r=3\), 8 rows and 7 labels, \(K_3\) has \(56\cdot104=5824\) dimensions, and \(Z_3\) should be compared with spans on \(m=4,\dots,7\) rows. Then look for a proof that replaces the circuit bound with an induction on the level. One candidate is the fundamental-circuit coordinates, with the zero-diagonal conditions imposed one slot pair at a time. The step ends with short generation at level three proved or refuted. The cycle after it should be a route review: whether a lift at every degree is what the batched mechanism needs, and what joint extension and density still require.

Before drafting, a narrowly briefed reviewer checked whether the record implies the reduction or the level-two statement. It found that neither is implied. It asked for citations of the coded-trade spanning theorem, the two-row product-code criterion, the first-degree lift and the cocycle reduction.

Checks: the exact spans of \(Z_2\), and the exact rank of the degree-two lift, whose image is checked against the symmetry equations.

A fresh-context reviewer found no mathematical error in the three lemmas. It checked the coded-trade theorem itself, over any field, with deletion allowance at most \(2r+3\) and supports at most \(r+2\) per row. It confirmed every table entry against the outputs. It required changes, all adopted:

Short generation at every level: stated for all parameters, and proved by peeling rows where every row has full evaluation space and labels are ignored

23 September 2026 · Working proof in a label-free model, and a conjecture · Joint kernels of \(r\) forms at every level. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The short-generation reduction proves the symmetric many-form lift at every degree once each joint kernel \(Z_s\) is spanned by elements on few rows. The cycle opened with a test at level three, and then kept testing further cases. The user asked when a general statement would come. This entry states it, and proves its core in a model without labels.

General statement. Conjecture conj:short-generation: in the matching complex over characteristic 3, with \(r\) forms and width and robustness large enough in terms of \(s\) and \(r\), \(Z_s=\bigcap_j\ker D_j\cap K_s\) is spanned by elements supported on at most \(\rho_s\) rows, where \(\rho_s\) depends only on \(s\) and \(r\). The conjectured bound is \(\rho_s\le s(r+1)\), and \(\rho_s\le2s\) when every row's evaluation space is all of \(k^r\). With the reduction, this would give the symmetric lift at every degree \(d\), with width \(\max_s(\rho_s+d+2-s)\) and output degree \(d+2\).

The data, read against the statement

At \(r=3\) with generic forms (every \(P_i=k^3\)), \(Z_2\) needs 4 rows at 8 and 10 rows (previous entry). \(Z_3\) needs 6 rows at 8 rows (two seeds) and at 10 rows (one seed, 7 labels): the spans on \(m=4,5,6\) rows are 131 or 497, 3338 and 3534 of 3534 at 8 rows, and 747, 8222 and 8747 of 8747 at 10 rows. That is \(2s\) at both levels, with no growth in the number of rows. Forms dependent on every row (\(\dim P_i\le2\)) needed 5 rows at level two in one seed, within \(s(r+1)\). The level-three runs with dependent forms and with four forms were stopped by the jobs' time limits of 25 and 28 minutes and gave no data. Files: short_generation3.py and its logs, in research/results/odd_prime_short_generation_20260923/.

The label-free model

Forget labels and ordinary marginals. Give each row \(i\) of a finite row set a subspace \(P_i\subseteq k^r\), over any field \(k\). Let \(\Lambda_t\) be the square-free tensors of degree \(t\): \[ \Lambda_t=\bigoplus_{|S|=t}\ \bigotimes_{i\in S}P_i , \] and for \(u\in(k^r)^*\) let \(\partial_u:\Lambda_t\to\Lambda_{t-1}\) be the contraction \(\partial_u(\otimes_{i\in S}p_i)=\sum_{i\in S}u(p_i)\,\otimes_{S\setminus i}p\). Put \(T_t=\bigcap_u\ker\partial_u\). This is the part of the joint kernel that the level-two proof isolated: there \(T_2\) appeared as the symmetric zero-diagonal tensors in \(R_1\otimes R_1\), and \(T_1=R_1\). With one form and \(P_i=k\), \(T_t\) is the kernel of the down map from \(t\)-sets to \((t-1)\)-sets of rows.

Lemma (peeling locality). If every \(P_i\) equals one space \(P\), then \(T_t\) is spanned by elements supported on at most \(2t\) rows, for every \(t\) and every number of rows.

Proof. Induction on \(t\), and for fixed \(t\) on the number \(n\) of rows. For \(t=0\), \(T_0=k\), and for \(n\le2t\) there is nothing to prove. Let \(n>2t\), fix a row \(n\) and a basis \(b_1,\dots,b_m\) of \(P\), and write \(x\in T_t\) as \(x=x'+\sum_ky_k\otimes b_k^{(n)}\). Here \(x'\) is supported on sets avoiding \(n\), and \(y_k\in\Lambda_{t-1}\) on the other rows. The part of \(\partial_ux\) on sets containing \(n\) is \(\sum_k\partial_uy_k\otimes b_k^{(n)}\). It vanishes, so every \(y_k\in T_{t-1}\) of the other rows. By induction on \(t\), each \(y_k\) is a sum of elements \(y\in T_{t-1}\) on at most \(2t-2\) rows. For such a \(y\) and \(b\in P\), choose a row \(a\ne n\) outside the rows of \(y\); it exists because \(n-1>2t-2\). Put \[ \gamma=y\otimes b^{(n)}-y\otimes b^{(a)} . \] Then \(\partial_u\gamma=\partial_uy\otimes(b^{(n)}-b^{(a)})+u(b)\,(y-y)=0\), so \(\gamma\in T_t\), supported on at most \(2t\) rows, with part \(y\otimes b^{(n)}\) at row \(n\). Subtracting these \(\gamma\) from \(x\) leaves an element of \(T_t\) on the rows other than \(n\), and induction on \(n\) finishes. \(\square\)

The same step works for arbitrary \(P_i\) whenever \(b\in P_n\) is a sum of vectors \(b_l\in P_{a_l}\) from rows outside the rows of \(y\) and \(n\). Replace the second term by \(\sum_ly\otimes b_l^{(a_l)}\). Then \(r\) spare rows suffice, and each piece has at most \(\rho_{t-1}+r+1\) rows. The spare rows must remain available as rows are peeled. A reserve that still spans each \(P_n\) after the deletion of any \(\rho_{t-1}+1\) rows can need about \(r(\rho_{t-1}+1)\) rows, for example lines each repeated \(\rho_{t-1}+1\) times. So this route gives only \(\rho_t\lesssim r(\rho_{t-1}+2)\), exponential in \(t\), and the conjectured linear bound for arbitrary \(P_i\) is open.

A consistency check in the scalar model. For \(t\le4\) with \(n\) from \(2t\) to \(2t+3\), and for \(t=5\) with \(n=10,11,12\), two things hold over \(\mathbb F_3\) (scalar_generators.py). The kernel's dimension equals Wilson's count for inclusion matrices modulo 3, \(\sum_{0\le i\le t,\ 3\mid t-i}\bigl[\binom ni-\binom n{i-1}\bigr]\), valid for \(n\ge2t-1\). And the kernel is spanned by products of \(i\) disjoint differences with a constant on the \((t-i)\)-subsets of a block of \(t-i+2\) rows. The term \(i=t\) is the span of the polytabloids. The extra elements occur exactly for the \(i\) with \(t-i\) a positive multiple of 3: one extra dimension at \(t=3\), and \(n-1\) at \(t=4\). The lemma does not need them, and its bound \(2t\) holds over every field. In the data, \(2t\) rows are needed at every tested \(n\) for \(t=2\), and at \(n\le2t+1\) for \(t=3,4\). Beyond that, 5 and 6 rows suffice. For one form, the lemma is close to the Graver–Jurkat theorem that null designs are generated over \(\mathbb Z\) by pods. That result is cited as a pointer only and not used; it does not carry over to \(\mathbb F_3\), where the kernel is larger than the reduction of the integral one.

What this changes

Short generation has one proof pattern at every level, peeling one row at a time with a spare row. In the label-free model with a common evaluation space it gives \(2t\), the bound the matching-complex data show for generic forms at levels two and three. Two steps separate it from the conjecture:

  • Labels. In \(K_s\), the row-\(n\) part of \(x\) is \(\sum_\omega y_\omega\otimes e_\omega\), where \(y_\omega\in Z_{s-1}\) avoids label \(\omega\) and \(\sum_\omega y_\omega=0\). It has to be rewritten as a sum of short \(y\otimes v\), with \(v\) a sum-zero vector on row \(n\) off the labels of \(y\). The level-two proof did this with the coded-trade spanning theorem and realizations off supports; the general level needs the same bookkeeping.
  • Unequal evaluation spaces. A linear bound needs spare rows that stay available while rows are peeled.

Assessment and next step

The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer is the peeling proof in the matching complex itself, for forms whose evaluation space is all of \(k^r\) on every row, at every level \(s\). It handles labels by choosing, for each short piece, a partner label outside its support, with robustness polynomial in \(s\) and \(r\). A proof gives short generation with \(\rho_s=2s\). With the reduction, it then gives the symmetric many-form lift at every degree for such forms, with width \(2d+2\) at degree \(d\) (\(\max_s(2s+d+2-s)\), attained at \(s=d\)), the threshold the finite checks show at \(d=1,2\). The step ends with that theorem, or with the point where labels break the peeling. The route review then follows. It asks what the goal's forms look like on their rows, and what joint extension and density still need.
