Short generation holds at every level when every row sees all forms, with 2s rows; the symmetric many-form lift follows at every degree

23 September 2026 · Working proof · Matching complex, forms independent modulo constants on every row; the lift at every degree. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The peeling-locality entry proved short generation without labels. It left the labels of the matching complex as the step between that and the conjecture. This cycle proves the labelled statement for full evaluation spaces, at every level. The label control is taken from the recorded coded-trade spanning theorem.

General statement. Conjecture conj:short-generation, proved here as thm:short-generation-full-spaces for forms with \(P_i=k^r\) on every row: for every \(s\), taking \(d=s\), \(Z_s\) is spanned by elements on at most \(2s\) rows and \(s(r+2)+2s(r+1)(2s(r+2)+r+2)\) labels, which is \(O(s^2r^2)\). With the short-generation reduction this gives cor:symmetric-lift-every-degree: symmetric tuples in \(K_d\) lift to \(K_{d+2}\) for every \(d\), on \(2d+2\) rows with label robustness \(O(d^2r^2)\). For unequal evaluation spaces the conjecture's bound \(s(r+1)\) remains open.

Setting

Let \(k\) be a field; the theorem below holds over any field, and characteristic 3 enters only through the reduction in the corollary. A board has rows \(\mathcal R\) and, for each row \(i\), a set \(\Omega_i\) of allowed labels. \(K_s\) consists of arrays on injections of \(s\)-row sets that send each row \(i\) into \(\Omega_i\), with zero ordinary marginal in every row. The forms and operators \(D_j\) are as in the first-degree lift. \(M_i\) is row \(i\)'s evaluation matrix, with rows \(1,f^{(1)}_i,\dots,f^{(r)}_i\). Full means \(\operatorname{rank}M_i=r+1\) on every row, that is \(P_i=k^r\). A basis of row \(i\) is a set of \(r+1\) labels on which \(M_i\) is invertible. The board is \(L\)-robust if every \(M_i\) keeps rank \(r+1\) after the deletion of any \(L\) labels.

For a row set \(F\), \(Z_s^F\) consists of the arrays in \(K_s\) supported on sets containing \(F\) with two properties. Each row of \(F\) is forced: it is annihilated by \(M_i\), so all its weighted marginals vanish. And \(\sum_{i\notin F}\delta_i^{f^{(j)}}\) vanishes for every \(j\). \(Z_s=Z_s^\varnothing\). Two facts follow because operators on different rows commute and \(\delta_i^2=0\).

  • Slices. For \(x\in Z_s^F\), the slice \(x_{(i,b)}\), fixing label \(b\) at row \(i\), is an array on the other rows. It avoids \(b\) and lies in \(Z_{s-1}^{F\setminus i}\).
  • Codeword pieces. If \(M_ic=0\) for \(c\) on a row \(i\) outside the rows of \(\eta\in Z_{s-1}^{F\setminus i}\), with labels disjoint from those of \(\eta\), then \(c\otimes\eta\in Z_s^F\).

Reserves. Fix \(d\ge1\) and nested row sets \(A_1\subset A_2\subset\dots\subset A_d\), with \(|A_s|=2s-1\). Call the rows of \(A_d\) reserve rows. For each reserve row \(a\), fix a label set \(\Lambda_a\): the union of \(m\) pairwise disjoint bases of row \(a\). The sets \(\Lambda_a\) are pairwise disjoint for different reserve rows.

  • An array is tame at \(a\) if its labels at row \(a\) lie in \(\Lambda_a\), and tame if it is tame at every reserve row.
  • Its outer labels are its labels at non-reserve rows, together with its labels at any reserve row \(a\) that lie outside \(\Lambda_a\).

The support \(\operatorname{supp}x\) of an array is the set of rows it uses. The point of these definitions: if \(y\) has no content at a reserve row \(a\), then every label of \(y\) inside \(\Lambda_a\) is an outer label of \(y\). Put \(\mu_s=s(r+2)\) and \(\lambda_s=\mu_s+2s(r+1)m\). A level-\(s\) piece is an element of \(Z_s^F\) on at most \(2s\) rows, with at most \(\mu_s\) outer labels and at most \(\lambda_s\) labels in all.

The theorem

Theorem (short generation for full spaces). Let the forms be full (this is implied by the robustness below, which keeps rank \(r+1\)), and let the board have at least \(2d-1\) rows. Take \(m=2d(r+2)+r+2\), and let the board be robust through \[ L_d=(2d-1)(r+1)m+\lambda_d+(r+1)+d(r+2). \] Then for \(0\le s\le d\) and every \(F\), every \(x\in Z_s^F\) is a sum of level-\(s\) pieces. So \(Z_s\) is spanned by elements on at most \(2s\) rows and \(\lambda_s=O(d^2r^2)\) labels, for \(s\le d\). The disjoint sets \(\Lambda_a\) exist, since \(L_d\ge(2d-1)(r+1)m\).

The proof proves two statements together, by induction on \(s\), on boards obtained from the given one by deleting at most \((d-s)(r+2)\) labels:

  • (T) every tame \(x\in Z_s^F\) is a sum of tame level-\(s\) pieces supported inside \(\operatorname{supp}x\cup A_s\);
  • (T*) every \(x\in Z_s^F\) is a sum of level-\(s\) pieces, and every piece is tame at each reserve row where \(x\) is tame.

At \(s=0\), \(Z_0=k\) is spanned by the empty array. The label choices below are possible because of three counts.

  • At a non-reserve row, the labels to avoid number at most \(\lambda_{s-1}+(r+1)\) labels of pieces and cleared labels, plus \(d(r+2)\) deleted labels, plus \(|\bigcup_a\Lambda_a|\) when a basis must avoid the reserved sets. \(L_d\) covers these.
  • At a reserve row \(a\), a piece \(y\) with no content at \(a\) meets \(\Lambda_a\) only in its outer labels, at most \(\mu_{s-1}\). The cleared labels add \(r+1\) and the deletions \(d(r+2)\). Since \(m>\mu_d+(r+1)+d(r+2)\), one of the \(m\) disjoint bases in \(\Lambda_a\) avoids all of them.
  • So a vector \(c\) on a row with prescribed \(M c\), or a codeword with a prescribed coefficient at one label, can be taken off any such set. At a reserve row it can be taken inside \(\Lambda_a\), apart from the prescribed label.

Proof of (T), forced case \(F\ne\varnothing\). This is the argument of the recorded coded-trade spanning theorem. Pick \(i\in F\), and choose a basis \(B\) of row \(i\): inside \(\Lambda_i\) if \(i\) is a reserve row, and off \(\bigcup_a\Lambda_a\) otherwise. A tame \(x\) carries labels of \(B\) only at row \(i\) and at non-reserve rows, since the \(\Lambda_a\) are disjoint.

  • Remove the labels of \(B\) one at a time from every row that carries them, row \(i\) included, as in the coded-trade proof. For the next label \(b\), with \(H\subseteq B\) already removed from every row, and a row \(i'\) carrying \(b\), the slice \(x_{(i',b)}\) is tame and lies in \(Z_{s-1}^{F\setminus i'}\), on the board without \(H\cup\{b\}\). By (T) at level \(s-1\) it is a sum of tame pieces \(\eta\). For each \(\eta\), a codeword \(c\) on row \(i'\) with \(c(b)=1\) and its other labels off \(H\cup\{b\}\cup L(\eta)\), inside \(\Lambda_{i'}\) if \(i'\) is a reserve row, gives the tame piece \(c\otimes\eta\). Subtracting these removes \(b\) at row \(i'\) and adds no label of \(H\cup\{b\}\).
  • Then, for each label \(j\notin B\) at row \(i\), subtract \((e_j-\operatorname{rep}_B(j))\otimes\eta\) for the tame pieces \(\eta\) of the slice at \((i,j)\). The slice avoids \(j\) and \(B\) and is decomposed on the board without \(B\cup\{j\}\), so its pieces avoid them too. This is where the allowance of \(r+2\) deleted labels per level is used. The codeword lies inside \(\Lambda_i\) when \(i\) is a reserve row, because \(j\in\Lambda_i\) by tameness.
  • What remains has row-\(i\) labels in \(B\) and is annihilated by \(M_i\) there. Its other rows avoid \(B\), and \(M_i\) is invertible on \(B\), so it is zero.

Each piece has at most \(2s-1\) rows, and at most \(\mu_{s-1}+r+2\) outer labels; the codeword contributes outer labels only at a non-reserve row. Each lies inside \(\operatorname{supp}x\cup A_{s-1}\).

Proof of (T), unforced case \(F=\varnothing\). Process the rows \(n\in\operatorname{supp}x\setminus A_s\) one at a time.

  • The data \(z_j=\delta_n^{f^{(j)}}x\) are tame elements of \(Z_{s-1}\), supported off \(n\). By (T) they are sums of tame pieces \(w\) inside \(\operatorname{supp}x\setminus\{n\}\cup A_{s-1}\), on at most \(2s-2\) rows.
  • For each \(w\) and \(j\), take \(v\) on row \(n\) with \(M_nv=(0,e_j)\), off the labels of \(w\), and inside \(\Lambda_n\) if \(n\) is a reserve row. Take a spare \(a\in A_s\) outside the rows of \(w\); it exists since \(|A_s|=2s-1>2s-2\). Take \(c\) on row \(a\) with \(M_ac=(0,e_j)\), inside \(\Lambda_a\) and off the labels of \(w\).
  • Then \(\gamma=w\otimes v-w\otimes c\) lies in \(Z_s\), because \(D_l\gamma=w\,(F_n(v)-F_a(c))_l=0\). It is tame, on at most \(2s\) rows, with at most \(\mu_{s-1}+r+1\) outer labels, inside \(\operatorname{supp}x\cup A_s\), and its row-\(n\) data are \(w\) at index \(j\).
  • After subtracting all \(\gamma\), the row-\(n\) data vanish. The part on sets containing \(n\) lies in \(Z_s^{\{n\}}\) and is tame, so the forced case decomposes it. The part avoiding \(n\) lies in \(Z_s\), is tame, and is supported inside \(\operatorname{supp}x\setminus\{n\}\cup A_s\).

When no row outside \(A_s\) is left, the remainder is tame and supported on \(A_s\). It is itself a piece: \(2s-1\) rows, no outer labels, and at most \((2s-1)(r+1)m\) labels. No row is ever deleted, so the induction is used only on the given board, with labels deleted.

Proof of (T*). Make \(x\) tame first. Take the reserve rows \(a\) at which \(x\) is not tame, one at a time. For each label \(b\notin\Lambda_a\) at row \(a\), the slice \(x_{(a,b)}\) lies in \(Z_{s-1}^{F\setminus a}\), on the board without \(b\). By (T*) at level \(s-1\) it is a sum of pieces \(\eta\), tame wherever the slice is. For each \(\eta\), take a codeword \(c\) on row \(a\) with \(c(b)=1\) and its other labels inside \(\Lambda_a\setminus L(\eta)\). The piece \(c\otimes\eta\) has at most \(\mu_{s-1}+1\) outer labels. Subtracting these makes row \(a\) tame and keeps every row that was already tame tame. When all reserve rows are tame, apply (T). \(\square\)

The row-forcing step is the odd-prime, many-form form of the induction in the recorded wide-row predicate exactness theorem, which forces one active row at a time into a weighted-marginal code with coded trades, in characteristic two and for one predicate. The reserves with disjoint reserved labels are new here.

Corollary (symmetric lift at every degree). Let \(k\) have characteristic 3 and the forms be full, which the robustness below implies. Let the board have at least \(2d+2\) rows and be robust through \(L_d+(d+1)(r+1)=O(d^2r^2)\). Then every symmetric tuple \((\zeta_\alpha)_{|\alpha|=2}\) in \(K_d\) is \((D^\alpha w)_{|\alpha|=2}\) for some \(w\in K_{d+2}\).

Proof. Apply the short-generation reduction with \(\rho_s=2s\) and \(\lambda_s\) from the theorem. The reserves need only \(2d-1\) rows. With full spaces, every direction is active on every row, so the width is the number of rows. The reduction needs \(\max_s(2s+d+2-s)=2d+2\) of them, and robustness \(\max_s(\lambda_s+(d+1-s)(r+1))\le L_d+(d+1)(r+1)\). \(\square\)

What this changes, and what it does not

For forms that are independent modulo constants on every row, the symmetric many-form lift is now proved at every degree. It has output degree \(d+2\), any number of forms, row count \(2d+2\), the threshold the finite checks show at \(d=1,2\), and label robustness polynomial in \(d\) and \(r\), \(O(d^2r^2)\). No exactness hypothesis is used. This is the local ingredient the cocycle reduction asked for, and its forced-forms hypothesis is no longer needed.

A first version of the proof had a gap, found by the reviewer. It made row \(n\) forced with pieces from level \(s-1\) that could use row \(n\) or rows already cleared, and repairing that by deleting rows made the required row count grow with the level. The reserves with disjoint reserved labels remove the need to delete rows, and they make the label bounds polynomial.

What it does not give:

  • Fullness excludes rows where some combination of the forms is constant. For unequal evaluation spaces the conjecture's bound \(s(r+1)\) remains open.
  • The step from symmetric lifts to joint extension, and the density mechanism, remain as the local-lift review recorded.

Assessment and next step

This is the sixth research entry since the last route review, so the next cycle on odd-prime-clause-transfer is a route review; the turn guidance says so too.

The review should weigh the proved local lift against what the goal needs, and against the other open parts:

  • the label cost \(O(d^2r^2)\) against the boards' \(N\);
  • fullness against the goal's forms;
  • the step from symmetric lifts to joint extension;
  • the density mechanism.

It should then choose the highest-risk one to attack.

Verification gate. Re-read, from the notebook: the short-generation entry (the reduction and its hypotheses), the peeling-locality entry, and the recorded coded-trade spanning theorem with its proof. The claim search found no recorded result that implies the theorem. It found the recorded wide-row predicate exactness theorem as the precedent for forcing rows, now cited.

A first fresh-context review found a fatal gap in the first version. The unforced step used level-\(s-1\) pieces that could lie on row \(n\) or on cleared rows. Repairing that by deleting rows broke the row-count requirement, so the first version proved only \(s\le2\). It also required:

  • a precise induction statement;
  • the forced case on the right board;
  • the removal of an unused remark;
  • a citation of the row-forcing precedent.

The proof was rebuilt with nested reserves, disjoint reserved labels and the tame invariant, which also made the label bounds polynomial. Because the rebuilt proof changed the claim, a second fresh-context pass reviewed it, trying to break the support invariant, tameness, the outer-label bounds, the counts, the forced final step and the corollary. It found no gap. It required:

  • the \(2d-1\) row hypothesis;
  • explicit wording for removing \(B\) at row \(i\) as well, and for decomposing the slices at \((i,j)\) on the board without \(B\cup\{j\}\);
  • the theorem stated over any field;
  • fullness noted as implied by robustness;
  • the \(d=s\) specialization in the General statement;
  • a definition of support.

All were adopted. No finite check was run: the finite thresholds at \(d=1,2\), recorded in the earlier entries, match the corollary's \(2d+2\).

Route review: the many-form lift is proved; the next obligation is completing r selectors' endpoint data to symmetric tuples

23 September 2026 · Route review · The local lift holds at every degree for full robust forms; its next consumer is r-selector completion. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

The line's general claim. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. Since the component review, the thread has worked on the joint lift for many forms, the batched mechanism named by the clause-transfer review. Its local form is now proved.

  • The short-generation reduction reduces the symmetric lift to spanning of joint kernels by short elements.
  • The short-generation theorem proves that spanning for forms independent modulo constants on every row. So symmetric tuples in \(K_d\) lift to \(K_{d+2}\) on \(2d+2\) rows, with label robustness \(O(d^2r^2)\).

The line's claim is that this local lift, fed by the source, gives hardness under many wide constraints.

What the goal needs. The core statement, read by the density entry as Conjecture SR for robust wide constraints. PHP must stay hard at polylogarithmic degree under polynomially many such constraints. Along this line that splits into three obligations:

  1. the source must supply symmetric tuples to lift;
  2. the lift must hold for the goal's forms;
  3. batches of polylogarithmically many constraints must glue across polynomially many.

Falsification attempt

Do the recorded refutations contradict the new theorem, or the line's claim that local lifts feed hardness? Each falls outside the theorem's hypotheses, in an informative way.

  • Occupancy predicates (symmetric-lift entry), refuted from 8 predicates. The column forms have row functions that are indicators, so they are full. But one deleted label makes a column form constant on a row, so robustness fails. The robustness hypothesis is what excludes them, as the density entry's Boolean-image control already showed.
  • The random affine law: about \((N+1-2D)(N-1)\) equations refute at degree \(D\). That is \(r\) of order \(N^2\), while the theorem's robustness \(O(d^2r^2)\) needs far more labels than \(N\). Below \(r\approx\sqrt N\) the law predicts hardness, consistent with the lift.
  • The three-selector control: the forms \(a,b,a+b\) are dependent, hence not full, and it derives a consequence, not a refutation.
  • The closed-tuple failure: the theorem lifts symmetric tuples only.

So nothing recorded refutes the line. But the occupancy case shows that full forms with local lifts can still be refuted. The hypotheses that matter are robustness and the source's supply of symmetric tuples.

Assessment of this line

The local part is now strong: a theorem at every degree, for any number of forms, with the row threshold the data show, and with polynomial label cost.

The obligations above differ in risk.

  1. Source compatibility, highest risk. For two ternary selectors the recorded ternary pair theorem completes the source's endpoint data at every degree. Those data are the self relations \(D_iz_i=0\) and the cross relations \(D_1^2z_2=D_2^2z_1\). For \(r\) selectors the source's endpoint relations are pairwise, while the lift needs a symmetric tuple with mixed entries \(z_{e_i+e_j}\) and triple consistency \(D_kz_{e_i+e_j}=D_iz_{e_j+e_k}\). For \(r=2\) the two notions agree. For \(r\ge3\) the symmetric-lift entry showed that closedness is strictly weaker than symmetry, so pairwise endpoint data may fail to complete. If they fail for the source, the many-predicate route fails whatever the lift can do.
  2. The goal's forms. Fullness requires every form to be active on every row, jointly independent. Collectively wide forms from compiled blocks need not be. For unequal evaluation spaces, the peeling spares must cover each row's space, and the reserve argument then gives only a bound exponential in the level. The conjectured \(s(r+1)\) is open.
  3. Gluing. Beyond polylogarithmic batches, the line is still bounded by the quadratic ceiling of common conditioning. It needs the Conjecture SR-type genericity that no line has reached. This is the deepest item, and it has resisted several lines. It is not the next test, because the first item decides whether batches exist at all.

Next step: r-selector completion

The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer states and tests r-selector completion at \(p=3\). Take \(r\) ternary selectors on full, robust, independent forms. For endpoint data \((z_i)\) in \(K_d\) satisfying the source's self and pairwise cross relations, the question is whether mixed entries \(z_{e_i+e_j}\) exist making \((z_\alpha)_{|\alpha|=2}\) a symmetric tuple. The new theorem then lifts it.

  • First decide it where it is exact: at \(d=1\), where \(K_0=k\), the conditions are linear in scalar moments. On the free module, where the symmetric lift holds, pairwise data may still carry a triple-consistency obstruction.
  • If completion fails, find which further source relation, if any, restores it, from the source identities of the source-interface entry.
  • If it holds, the one-predicate theorem's conditioned filtration extends to \(r\) predicates for full robust forms. That would be the core statement for polylogarithmically many constraints, and the batch that gluing needs.

The step ends with the completion lemma proved, or with the obstruction and the source relation it requires.

Process. The turn-start guidance announced this review before the cycle began, and the finish-time check would have enforced it.

Verification gate. Re-read: the core-statement review, the density entry, and the short-generation theorem and reduction. Also re-read the source-interface entry's endpoint relations and its statement that many-form completion is open, together with the claim records of the one-predicate theorem, the two-selector compatibility lemma and the ternary pair theorem. Each falsification case was checked against the theorem's exact hypotheses. The occupancy forms' non-robustness is the density entry's recorded control. This review proves nothing new and registers no claim.

Endpoint data of any number of ternary selectors complete at every degree; functional PHP keeps stable moments under many wide selectors

23 September 2026 · Working proofs and a finite check · Ternary selectors on forms independent modulo constants on every row. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The route review ranked source compatibility highest. Do the source's endpoint data for \(r\) ternary selectors, the self relations \(D_iz_i=0\) and pairwise cross relations \(D_i^2z_j=D_j^2z_i\), yield one common correction? The review expected that they might have to complete to a symmetric tuple, with triple-consistency conditions that pairwise data need not satisfy.

General statement. thm:many-selector-completion: for \(r\) forms independent modulo constants on every row, on at least \(2d+2\) rows with label robustness \(O(d^2r^2)\) (\(d\ge1\); \(d=0\) needs only 2 rows), every endpoint family \((z_i)\) in \(K_d\) satisfying the self and cross relations equals \((D_i^2w)\) for one \(w\in K_{d+2}\), for every \(d\) and \(r\). cor:many-ternary-selectors-filtration: functional PHP with the \(r\) nonzero-value selectors \(1-L_i^2\) then has stable moments and no PC refutation of degree \(B\).

The source asks only for the pure moments

The recorded endpoint lemma sets \(z_i(f)=\mu(f)-(E\mu)(L_i^2f)\), \(\deg f\le d=s-2\), for an old functional \(\mu\) through \(s-1\) annihilating the legal multiples of every \(q_i=1-L_i^2\), and an old extension \(E\mu\). Its proof is pairwise, so for \(r\) selectors it gives \(D_iz_i=0\) and \(D_i^2z_j=D_j^2z_i\) for all \(i,j\). A correction \(w\in K_{d+2}\) of \(E\mu\) repairs every predicate at once exactly when \(D_i^2w=z_i\) for all \(i\). The mixed moments \(D_iD_jw\) are not prescribed.

So the lift needed is not the symmetric lift, and no triple consistency arises. The review's concern was about the wrong target.

Lifting on an upward-closed set of moments

Use the setting of the short-generation reduction at \(p=3\): the matching complex \(K\), \(r\) forms with operators \(D_j\), and joint kernels \(Z_s\). Let \(E\) be a set of exponent vectors with \(|b|\ge2\) that is upward closed: \(b\in E\) implies \(b+e_j\in E\). A target family on \(E\) is a choice \(\tau_b\in K_{d+2-|b|}\) for \(b\in E\) with two properties:

  • \(D_j\tau_b=\tau_{b+e_j}\);
  • \(\tau_b=0\) whenever some \(b_j\ge3\).

Lemma (upward-closed lift). Under the hypotheses of the short-generation reduction at degree \(d\), every target family on \(E\) is \((D^bw)_{b\in E}\) for some \(w\in K_{d+2}\).

Proof. Repeat the reduction's descending induction, keeping only the moments in \(E\). Build \(w^{(q)}\), for \(q=d+2\) down to \(2\), with \(D^bw^{(q)}=\tau_b\) for \(b\in E\), \(|b|\ge q\). The residuals \(\eta_b=\tau_b-D^bw^{(q+1)}\), for \(b\in E\) with \(|b|=q\), satisfy \(D_j\eta_b=\tau_{b+e_j}-D^{b+e_j}w^{(q+1)}=0\), because \(b+e_j\in E\). So they lie in \(Z_{d+2-q}\), and \(\eta_b=0\) when some \(b_j\ge3\). The tensor pieces of the reduction give any prescribed tuple of such residuals as \((D^bv)\) on all \(|b|=q\) with every \(b_j\le2\), and hence on the part of it in \(E\). They also have \(D^{b'}v=0\) for \(|b'|>q\), so no higher target is disturbed. Moments outside \(E\) are never constrained. \(\square\)

With \(E\) all of \(\{|b|\ge2\}\) this is the reduction itself. The pure case is \(E=\{b:\ b_i\ge2\text{ for some }i\}\), the exponents of the ideal \((D_1^2,\dots,D_r^2)\).

Theorem (many-selector completion). Let \(d\ge1\), and let the forms be independent modulo constants on every row, on a board with at least \(2d+2\) rows that is robust through \(L_d+(d+1)(r+1)\) labels. Here \(L_d=(2d-1)(r+1)m+\lambda_d+(r+1)+d(r+2)\), with \(m=2d(r+2)+r+2\) and \(\lambda_s=s(r+2)+2s(r+1)m\), from the short-generation theorem. So \(L_d=O(d^2r^2)\), and it is nondecreasing in \(d\). Let \(z_1,\dots,z_r\in K_d\) satisfy \(D_iz_i=0\) and \(D_i^2z_j=D_j^2z_i\). Then there is \(w\in K_{d+2}\) with \(D_i^2w=z_i\) for every \(i\).

Proof. For \(b\) in the pure \(E\), put \(\tau_b=D^{b-2e_i}z_i\) for any \(i\) with \(b_i\ge2\).

  • Well defined. If \(b_i,b_j\ge2\), the two choices differ by \(D^{b-2e_i-2e_j}(D_j^2z_i-D_i^2z_j)=0\).
  • Vanishing. If some \(b_j\ge3\), choose \(i=j\). Then \(b-2e_j\) has \(j\)-exponent at least one, and \(D_jz_j=0\) gives \(\tau_b=0\).
  • Compatible. \(D_j\tau_b=\tau_{b+e_j}\) is immediate.

The short-generation theorem, with robustness \(L_d\), gives \(Z_s\) spanned by elements on \(\rho_s=2s\) rows and \(\lambda_s\) labels for \(s\le d\). The reduction's hypotheses then read as follows.

  • Width: \(\max_s(\rho_s+d+2-s)=\max_s(s+d+2)=2d+2\). With full forms the width is the number of rows.
  • Robustness: \(\max_s(\lambda_s+(d+1-s)(r+1))\le\lambda_d+(d+1)(r+1)\le L_d+(d+1)(r+1)\), since \(\lambda_s\) is nondecreasing in \(s\) and \(\lambda_d\le L_d\).

The upward-closed lift then gives \(w\), and at \(|b|=2\) it reads \(D_i^2w=z_i\). \(\square\)

The case \(d=0\). Here \(K_0=k\) and only the reduction's top step is used: tensors of two fresh vectors on two rows, whose products span the quadratic forms. That needs 2 rows and robustness \(r+1\). So \(z_i=D_i^2w\) for some \(w\in K_2\) under these weaker conditions.

Corollary (many ternary selectors). Let \(L_1,\dots,L_r\) be old affine forms over \(\mathbb F_3\) on the functional matching base \(\Gamma\), with the degree-two equations \(q_i=1-L_i^2\). Let their row-linear parts be independent modulo constants on every row. Fix \(B\ge2\), and let the board have at least \(\max(2B-2,2)\) rows and be robust through \(L_{\max(B-2,1)}+(B-1)(r+1)\). Since \(L_d\) is nondecreasing, this covers every \(d\le B-2\). It also implies at least \(2B\) labels, so the recorded old matching extension room holds. Then every NS functional for \(\Gamma+q_1+\dots+q_r\) through degree \(k\le B\) extends through \(B\). The filtration is stable and PC equals NS through \(B\), a normalized design exists, and there is no PC refutation of degree \(B\). The nonrefutation also holds for weak balanced PHP with these predicates, since adding functionality only strengthens the base, as in the recorded two-selector corollary.

Proof. This is the recorded two-selector corollary's argument with \(r\) selectors.

  • Below degree two the predicates are inactive.
  • At each extension from \(s-1\) to \(s\le B\), form the \(r\) defects with \(d=s-2\). They satisfy the relations above, and the theorem gives one correction fixing all of them and every lower moment.
  • Degree-zero normalization is kept. Duality gives filtration stability, and degree-bounded multiplication gives PC equal to NS.

The row and robustness bounds are the theorem's at \(d\le B-2\), and at \(d=0\) its separate case, whose robustness \(r+1\) is at most \(L_1\). Every nonzero combination of full forms is active on every row, so the recorded width conditions hold. \(\square\)

Finite check

pure_lift.py computes the rank of \(w\mapsto(D_i^2w)_i\) from \(K_4\) and the dimension of endpoint data in \(K_2\) at \(r=3\), with 7 labels, exactly over \(\mathbb F_3\). It checks that every lift satisfies the relations.

The boards do not meet the robustness hypothesis, so the check tests the conclusion, not the lemma. Output: research/results/odd_prime_selector_completion_20260923/pure_lift.json.

What this changes

The source-compatibility risk the route review ranked highest does not arise for selectors: their endpoint data ask only for the pure moments, and those always complete. So for any number \(r\) of nonzero-value ternary selectors on full forms, functional PHP has no refutation of degree \(B\). The conditions are \(2B-2\) rows and label robustness polynomial in \(B\) and \(r\). This is the core statement for single-form constraints, far beyond the recorded two selectors. Each selector forbids density \(1/3\), so the total density \(r/3\) is well above one. This agrees with the density entry's finding that density does not govern hardness.

The regime it reaches is set by fullness and robustness. Fullness needs \(r+1\le N\). Robustness \(O(B^2r^2)\le N\) allows \(r\) up to about \(\sqrt N/B\) constraints. The recorded refutations lie outside that regime:

  • the occupancy predicates are not robust;
  • the random selector thresholds, 16 at \(n=6\) and 36 at \(n=8\), exceed \(N-1\);
  • the recorded three-selector degree fall (obs:three-wide-ternary-selectors-degree-fall) uses \(a,b,a+b\). Every pair of them extends but the triple falls at degree three: pairwise relations do not suffice when the forms are dependent. Independence on every row excludes it, and it shows that hypothesis is needed.

Three steps remain open between this and the goal:

  • constraints on several forms, as in the logarithmic-prefix images \(g_iQ\), whose endpoint data are not yet derived;
  • forms that are not full;
  • gluing with the raw coefficient equations across blocks, which the source-interface entry left open.

Assessment and next step

The line produced a theorem at the level of constraint systems, not only local lifts. The next obligation along it is multi-form constraints. The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer derives the source's endpoint data for one product constraint \(\prod_{j\le k}(1-(L_j-a_j)^2)\) over \(\mathbb F_3\), the forbid-value form of the prefix rewrite, and finds which upward-closed target set it prescribes. If that set is upward closed with consistent targets, the lemma applies at once and the prefix images follow for full robust forms. The step ends with that set and its lift, or with the relation the source fails to supply.

The search found nothing recorded that implies completion for more than two selectors. The exact check tests the conclusion at \(d=2\).

Coherent product constraints complete at every degree; incoherent pairs derive lower-degree consequences

23 September 2026 · Working proofs · Product constraints with linear or point-indicator factors, forms independent modulo constants on every row. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The selector completion proved that functional PHP stays hard under many single-form selectors. The goal's constraints involve several forms: the prefix images \(g_iQ\) and their forbid-value rewrites. What endpoint data does such a constraint give, and when do many of them complete together?

General statement. thm:coherent-product-constraints: a system of product constraints over \(\mathbb F_3\) on forms that are jointly independent modulo constants on every row completes at every degree, for any number of constraints, if every pair of constraints is coherent. Each factor is linear or a point indicator in a single form. Coherent means: on each shared form, the factors are equal, or one is \(\chi_a\) and the other \(L-a'\) with \(a'\ne a\). The board needs enough rows and label robustness \(O(B^2r^2)\), with \(r\) the number of forms. cor:coherent-product-constraints-filtration: the conditioned filtration is stable and there is no PC refutation of degree \(B\). obs:incoherent-pair-fall: an incoherent pair derives, from multiples at its common top degree, a lower-degree polynomial vanishing wherever both constraints vanish.

Product constraints and their endpoint data

Work over \(\mathbb F_3\) on the functional matching base \(\Gamma\), with old affine forms \(L_1,\dots,L_r\) and row-linear parts \(\ell_j\). Let \(\chi_a(L)=1-(L-a)^2\), the indicator of \(L=a\). A product constraint is an equation \[ C=\prod_{j\in S_C}h_{C,j}(L_j)=0,\qquad h_{C,j}\in\{\,L_j-a,\ \chi_a(L_j)\,\}. \] Its top part is \(c_C\,\ell^{b_C}\), with \(b_{C,j}=\deg h_{C,j}\in\{1,2\}\) and \(c_C=\pm1\). Examples:

  • selectors, \(\chi_0(L)=1-L^2\);
  • affine equations \(L-a\);
  • forbid-value constraints \(\prod_j\chi_{v_j}(L_j)\);
  • the prefix images in the form \(\chi_0(L_i)\prod_{j\in S}L_j\). This vanishes exactly where \(g_iQ\) does, and each derives the other: multiply by \(\prod_SL_j\), respectively reduce \(L_j^3=L_j\).

At an extension from \(s-1\) to \(s\), let \(\mu\) be an old functional through \(s-1\) annihilating the legal multiples of every constraint, and \(E\mu\) an old extension through \(s\). For \(\deg f\le d_C=s-|b_C|\) put \(z_C(f)=(E\mu)(Cf)\). It vanishes when \(\deg f<d_C\), since \(\mu\) annihilates the legal multiple \(Cf\). As in the recorded endpoint lemma, \(z_C\in K_{d_C}\). A correction \(w\in K_s\) changes \((E\mu)(Cf)\) by \(c_C(D^{b_C}w)(f)\). So all constraints are repaired by one \(w\) exactly when \[ D^{b_C}w=\hat z_C:=-z_C/c_C\quad\text{for every }C. \]

Self relations. \(D_j^{3-b_{C,j}}\hat z_C=0\) for \(j\in S_C\).

Proof. Both cases use two facts. \(E\mu\) annihilates base multiples through \(s\), and \(L^3-L\) lies in the base at degree 3.

  • For \(h=\chi_a\), \(\chi_a(L)\,L-a\,\chi_a(L)=(L-a)\chi_a(L)=L-L^3\). So \(z_C(\ell_jf)=a\,(E\mu)(Cf)+(E\mu)(\text{base multiple})\). Here \(\deg(Cf)\le s-1\), so the first term is \(a\,\mu(Cf)=0\).
  • For \(h=L-a\) with \(a\ne0\), \((L-a)L^2=(L^3-L)+(L-a)(-aL)\), using \(a^2=1\). So \(z_C(\ell_j^2f)\) is a base term plus a multiple of \((E\mu)(C\,L_jf)\), of degree \(s-1\). For \(a=0\), \(L\cdot L^2=(L^3-L)+L\), so the remainder is a multiple of \((E\mu)(Cf)\), of degree at most \(s-2\). In both cases \(\mu\) annihilates the remainder as a legal multiple of \(C\).

The replacement of \(\ell_j^m\) by \(L_j^m\) changes the argument only by a lower-degree legal multiple of \(C\). \(\square\)

Coherence and cross relations. Call two constraints coherent if, on every shared form \(j\), either \(h_{C,j}=h_{C',j}\), or one factor is \(\chi_a\) and the other \(L-a'\) with \(a'\ne a\). Then, with \(b=\max(b_C,b_{C'})\) coordinatewise, \[ D^{b-b_C}\hat z_C=D^{b-b_{C'}}\hat z_{C'} . \]

Proof. Build polynomials \(X\) and \(Y\), products of single-form factors with tops \(\pm\ell^{b-b_C}\) and \(\pm\ell^{b-b_{C'}}\), with \(CX=C'Y\) exactly.

  • On forms of \(C'\) only, \(X\) takes \(C'\)'s factor, and symmetrically for \(Y\).
  • On a shared form with equal factors, both take \(1\).
  • If \(C\) has \(\chi_a\) and \(C'\) has \(L-a'\) with \(a'\ne a\), then \(\chi_a(L)\) vanishes at \(a'\), so \(\chi_a=(L-a')y\) with \(y\) linear. So \(Y\) takes \(y\) and \(X\) takes \(1\).

Then \(D^{b-b_C}\hat z_C(f)=-(E\mu)(CXf)/c_{CX}\): replacing \(\ell^{b-b_C}\) by \(X/c_X\) changes the argument by a lower-degree legal multiple of \(C\). Likewise \(D^{b-b_{C'}}\hat z_{C'}(f)=-(E\mu)(C'Yf)/c_{C'Y}\). The two polynomials are equal, and so are their top coefficients. \(\square\)

Observation (incoherent pairs). For every incoherent pair, suitable multiples of the two constraints of degree \(|b|\), with \(b\) their common top, differ by a nonzero polynomial of lower degree. That polynomial lies in their degree-\(|b|\) span and vanishes wherever both constraints vanish. Let \(H_0\) be the product of the remaining factors.

  • Two indicators \(\chi_a,\chi_{a'}\) on one form, \(a\ne a'\): \(\chi_a-\chi_{a'}=(a-a')(2L-a-a')\) gives \(H_0\,(2L_j-a-a')\), one degree lower. Where both constraints vanish and \(H_0\ne0\), \(L_j\) avoids \(a\) and \(a'\), so \(2L_j-a-a'=0\).
  • Two linear factors \(L-a\), \(L-a'\), \(a\ne a'\): their difference is the constant \(a'-a\), giving \(H_0\), one degree lower.
  • \(\chi_a\) against \(L-a\): \(\chi_a+(L-a)^2=1\) exactly, giving \(H_0\), two degrees lower.

Whether such a polynomial is a genuine degree fall, outside the lower-degree closure, is not shown here in general. In the case of \(\chi_a\) against \(L-a'\), multiples of the lower-degree constraint may already give it below \(|b|\). The prefix-adaptation entry recorded falls of this kind between the rewrites \(G_a\). So coherence is the condition the proof uses. The incoherent cases produce the kind of local interaction that the component line merges.

The graded upward-closed lift

Lemma (graded upward-closed lift). Work in the matching complex over characteristic 3 with \(r\) forms. Fix an extension degree \(s\) and an upward-closed set \(E\) of exponent vectors with minimal order \(h=\min_{b\in E}|b|\ge1\). A target family is a choice of \(\tau_b\in K_{s-|b|}\), \(b\in E\), with \(D_j\tau_b=\tau_{b+e_j}\), and \(\tau_b=0\) whenever some \(b_j\ge3\). Put \(t_0=s-h\). Suppose:

  • for \(1\le t\le t_0\), \(Z_t\) is spanned by elements on at most \(2t\) rows and \(\lambda_t\) labels;
  • every nonzero combination of the forms is active on at least \(2s-h\) rows;
  • the board is robust through \(\max_{0\le t\le t_0}\bigl(\lambda_t+(s-t-1)(r+1)\bigr)\), with \(\lambda_0=0\).

Then some \(w\in K_s\) has \(D^bw=\tau_b\) for all \(b\in E\).

Proof. Build \(w^{(q)}\in K_s\), for \(q=s\) down to \(h\), with \(D^bw^{(q)}=\tau_b\) for \(b\in E\), \(|b|\ge q\); start from \(w^{(s+1)}=0\).

  • Residuals. For \(b\in E\) with \(|b|=q\), put \(\eta_b=\tau_b-D^bw^{(q+1)}\). Since \(E\) is upward closed, \(D_j\eta_b=\tau_{b+e_j}-D^{b+e_j}w^{(q+1)}=0\). So \(\eta_b\in Z_{s-q}\), where \(Z_0=K_0=k\), and \(\eta_b=0\) if some \(b_j\ge3\). Write each \(\eta_b\) in a fixed spanning set of short elements \(x\) of \(Z_{s-q}\): \(\eta_b=\sum_x\lambda_{b,x}x\), with \(\lambda_{b,x}=0\) when some \(b_j\ge3\).
  • Pieces. For a short \(x\) on a row set \(S\), with \(|S|\le2(s-q)\), take \(q\) rows outside \(S\) and vectors \(c_1,\dots,c_q\) on them with prescribed evaluations \(p_k\). Choose them off the labels of \(x\) and of each other, which robustness allows. The tensor \(x\otimes c_1\otimes\dots\otimes c_q\) lies in \(K_s\). Each \(D_j\) splits into a part on \(x\), which kills \(x\), and a part on the \(c\)'s. So \(D^b\) of the tensor vanishes for \(|b|>q\), and equals \(b!\,[u^b]\prod_k(u\cdot p_k)\,x\) for \(|b|=q\).
  • Spanning. The products \(\prod_k(u\cdot p_k)\), over distinct rows outside \(S\), span all forms of degree \(q\). Every nonzero \(u\) is active on more than \(|S|+q-1\) rows, so the evaluation spaces outside any \(|S|+q-1\) rows span \(k^r\), and the multilinear argument of the reduction applies. For \(q=1\) this is one fresh row: the evaluations \(p\) of vectors on rows outside \(S\) span \(k^r\), since the forms are active outside \(S\), so \((u\cdot p)\) spans the linear forms. Because \(b!\) is a unit when every \(b_j\le2\), the coefficient tuples \((b![u^b]F)_{|b|=q}\) range over all tuples. So some combination \(v\) of pieces has \(D^bv=\eta_b\) for \(b\in E\), \(|b|=q\), and \(D^{b'}v=0\) for \(|b'|>q\). Put \(w^{(q)}=w^{(q+1)}+v\).

At \(q=h\), \(w=w^{(h)}\) satisfies every target. The avoidances number at most \(\lambda_{s-q}+(q-1)(r+1)\). \(\square\)

With \(E\subseteq\{|b|\ge2\}\) and \(s=d+2\) this is the recorded upward-closed lift.

The theorem

Theorem (coherent product constraints). Let \(r\) forms be independent modulo constants on every row, and let \(\mathcal C\) be a pairwise coherent set of product constraints on them, of any size. Let \(h=\min_C|b_C|\ge1\), fix \(s\ge h\), and put \(t_0=s-h\). Suppose the board has at least \(2s-h\) rows. Suppose it is robust through \(L_{t_0}+s(r+1)\), with \(L_{t_0}\) from the short-generation theorem for \(t_0\ge1\), and \(s(r+1)\) alone when \(t_0=0\). Then the endpoint data \((\hat z_C)\) above equal \((D^{b_C}w)\) for one \(w\in K_s\).

Proof. Let \(E=\bigcup_C(b_C+\mathbb N^r)\), which is upward closed. For \(b\in E\), put \(\tau_b=D^{b-b_C}\hat z_C\) for any \(C\) with \(b\ge b_C\).

  • Well defined. Two choices \(C,C'\) agree by applying \(D^{b-\max(b_C,b_{C'})}\) to the cross relation.
  • Vanishing. If some \(b_j\ge3\), choose any admissible \(C\). The exponent of \(j\) in \(b-b_C\) is at least \(3-b_{C,j}\) when \(j\in S_C\), and at least 3 otherwise. So the self relation, or \(D_j^3=0\), gives \(\tau_b=0\).
  • Compatible. \(D_j\tau_b=\tau_{b+e_j}\) is immediate.

Apply the graded upward-closed lift. The short-generation theorem gives \(\rho_t=2t\) and \(\lambda_t\) for \(t\le t_0\). It needs \(2t_0-1\) rows, at most the \(2s-h=2t_0+h\) assumed, and robustness \(L_{t_0}\). With full forms the width is the number of rows. The lemma's robustness is at most \(\lambda_{t_0}+s(r+1)\le L_{t_0}+s(r+1)\). At \(h=1\) the row count is \(2t_0+1\), one fewer than the selector theorem's \(2d+2\).

\(\square\)

Corollary (coherent product constraints: stable moments). Under the theorem's hypotheses for every \(s\le B\), every NS functional for \(\Gamma+\mathcal C\) through degree \(k\le B\) extends through \(B\). The filtration is stable, PC equals NS through \(B\), a normalized design exists, and there is no PC refutation of degree \(B\). The nonrefutation holds also for weak balanced PHP with these constraints, as in the recorded two-selector corollary. Since \(L_t\) is nondecreasing, the hypotheses at \(s=B\) cover every \(s\le B\): \(2B-h\) rows and robustness \(L_{\max(B-h,1)}+B(r+1)=O(B^2r^2)\). This robustness gives at least \(B(r+1)\ge2B\) labels, so the recorded old matching extension room holds and \(E\mu\) exists.

Proof. Iterate the theorem over the extensions from \(s-1\) to \(s\le B\). Below degree \(h\) no constraint is active. Each step corrects all constraints at once and fixes every lower moment. Duality and degree-bounded multiplication give stability and PC equal to NS, as in the recorded two-selector corollary. \(\square\)

Consequences

  • Affine equations. A system of affine equations \(L_j=a_j\) on forms independent modulo constants on every row is coherent: each equation sits on its own form. So functional PHP has no degree-\(B\) refutation under it, given \(2B-1\) rows and robustness \(O(B^2r^2)\). Functional PHP has more axioms than ordinary unary PHP, so the ordinary base has no such refutation either. This is a bounded-\(r\), \(p=3\) analogue of the recorded wide-conditioning conjecture (conj:wide-affine-conditioning), not a proof of it. The conjecture asks for per-combination width and robustness depending only on \(p\) and \(D\), at every odd \(p\). Here robustness is a label count that grows with \(r\), and fullness is a different hypothesis from width. For comparison, the recorded random-conditioning law, an empirical count (clause-transfer review), places refutations of random systems near \((N+1-2D)(N-1)\) equations.
  • Forbid-value constraints. These are coherent when any two agree on the values of their shared forms.
  • Prefix images, as \(C_{b,i}=\chi_0(L_{b,i})\prod_{j\in S_b}L_{b,j}\), with every prefix factor \(L_j-0\) as the prefix construction gives. Images of one block are coherent: they share identical prefix factors, and their image forms are distinct and outside \(S_b\). Images of different blocks are coherent unless an image form of one lies in the prefix set of the other, which is \(\chi_0\) against \(L-0\). With other prefix values, two prefix factors on a shared form could also be incoherent. Since \(g_iQ=C_{b,i}\prod_{j\in S_b}L_j\), each original image is a multiple of \(C_{b,i}\) at the same degree. So a degree-\(B\) refutation with the \(g_iQ\) gives one with the \(C_{b,i}\): only nonrefutation transfers, not the stable filtration. The wide-clause statement asks for nonrefutation over the weak base, which has fewer axioms than the functional base, so it transfers too. So the conclusion holds for families in which no image form is another block's prefix form, at every polylogarithmic degree, provided all forms are jointly full and robust.

What this changes

The constraint type is no longer the obstacle. Every coherent system of product constraints completes. Incoherent pairs derive lower-degree consequences, the local interactions the component line identified. Two limits remain.

  • Quantity. Joint fullness and robustness \(O(B^2r^2)\le N\) bound the total number of forms by about \(\sqrt N/B\). The goal's inventories have polynomially many blocks, far more forms than labels, so all forms cannot be jointly full.
  • Incoherence. This comes from overlapping blocks, where an image form is another block's prefix form. It needs the merging of the component line.

The first limit is where the gluing problem now sits. The lift uses all forms as one family of commuting operators, so it cannot exceed the forms' joint rank. What is needed is a version where each constraint uses only its own forms, with the joint condition replaced by one that polynomially many forms can satisfy.

Assessment and next step

The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer is to glue local sections. The global correction problem \(D^{b_C}w=\hat z_C\) is linear in \(w\). It is unsolvable exactly when a syzygy \(\sum_C\ell^{b_C}g_C=0\) of the tops, in the top algebra, pairs nonzero with the defects. The theorem solves every subsystem whose forms are jointly full and robust. So the defects vanish on every syzygy supported inside such a subsystem, and the local solutions glue whenever the top syzygies through degree \(B\) are spanned by local ones.

  • Prove that gluing lemma.
  • State the remaining conjecture, local generation of the top syzygies, a Fröberg-type statement in the board's top algebra.
  • Test it against the random affine law, where long linear dependencies among about \(N^2\) forms are exactly non-local syzygies.

The step ends with the lemma, and with the conjecture stated and tested.

Verification gate. Re-read, from the notebook: the recorded endpoint relations, the two-selector theorem and corollary, the selector-completion entry with the upward-closed lift, the short-generation theorem's parameters, the prefix-adaptation entry, and conj:wide-affine-conditioning. The claim search found no recorded result that implies the theorem; the nearest are the two-selector lift and the selector completion, which it generalizes. No finite check was run: the selector check already tests the lift at its threshold.

A fresh-context reviewer confirmed the endpoint data, the self and cross relations, and the observation's computations. It required changes, all adopted:

  • the affine consequence restated as a bounded-\(r\), \(p=3\) analogue of the wide-conditioning conjecture, with the transfer to the ordinary base and the empirical status of the law;
  • the observation and title weakened: incoherent pairs derive lower-degree consequences, and a genuine fall is not shown in general;
  • the self-relation wording at \(a=0\);
  • the graded upward-closed lift stated and proved as its own lemma, including the one-vector step and the short-generation row requirement;
  • the extension-room check and the bound at \(B=h\);
  • the prefix transfer stated as nonrefutation only, with the prefix-value assumption.

These changes weaken claims or make an existing argument explicit, so no further pass was made.

Local corrections glue exactly along the top syzygies: hardness for any number of constraints reduces to local generation of syzygies

23 September 2026 · Working proofs and a conjecture · Product constraints on the functional base over \(\mathbb F_3\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The product-constraints theorem corrects any coherent system whose forms are jointly full and robust. Joint fullness caps the total at about \(\sqrt N/B\) forms, while the goal has polynomially many blocks. Can local corrections, each on a small full subsystem, be glued into one?

General statement. lem:syzygy-gluing: at each extension step, one correction exists exactly when the defects vanish on every syzygy of the constraints' tops in the top algebra. thm:glued-product-constraints: for any number of product constraints, if the top syzygies through degree \(B\) are spanned by syzygies supported in coherent subsystems with jointly full robust forms, then functional PHP has no refutation of degree \(B\), nor does weak balanced PHP. The board needs about \(2B\) rows and label robustness \(O(B^2r_{\max}^2)\), with \(r_{\max}\) the largest number of forms in one subsystem. conj:local-top-syzygies: for the goal's constraint families, the top syzygies through the needed degree are spanned by such local ones.

The obstruction to gluing is a syzygy pairing

Work on the functional matching base over \(\mathbb F_3\). \(G=\bigoplus_tG_t\) is its top algebra, and \(K_t=G_t^*\) is the matching complex, as recorded in the two-selector theorem's matching hypotheses (\(K_r=(A_0/(z))_r^*\)). The pairing is perfect in every degree, and \(\langle w,\ell_jg\rangle=\langle D_jw,g\rangle\) for \(w\in K_t\), \(g\in G_{t-1\,}\). At an extension from \(s-1\) to \(s\), each product constraint \(C\) has top \(c_C\ell^{b_C}\) and defect \(\hat z_C\in K_{s-|b_C|}\), as in the product-constraints entry. One correction \(w\in K_s\) repairs every constraint exactly when \(D^{b_C}w=\hat z_C\) for all \(C\). Call \((g_C)\in\bigoplus_CG_{s-|b_C|}\) a top syzygy of degree \(s\) if \(\sum_C\ell^{b_C}g_C=0\) in \(G_s\), and say it is supported in a set \(U\) of constraints if \(g_C=0\) for \(C\notin U\).

Lemma (syzygy gluing).

  1. A correction \(w\in K_s\) with \(D^{b_C}w=\hat z_C\) for all \(C\) exists if and only if \(\sum_C\langle\hat z_C,g_C\rangle=0\) for every top syzygy \((g_C)\) of degree \(s\).
  2. Let \(\mathcal U\) be a family of sets of constraints. Suppose each \(U\in\mathcal U\) has a local correction \(w_U\in K_s\) with \(D^{b_C}w_U=\hat z_C\) for \(C\in U\). Suppose the top syzygies of degree \(s\) are spanned by syzygies each supported in some \(U\in\mathcal U\). Then a global correction exists.

Proof.

  1. The map \(\Phi:w\mapsto(D^{b_C}w)_C\) goes from \(K_s\) to \(\bigoplus_CK_{s-|b_C|}\). Under the perfect pairings, its dual is \((g_C)\mapsto\sum_C\ell^{b_C}g_C\), whose kernel is the space of top syzygies. In finite dimension the image of \(\Phi\) is the annihilator of the dual's kernel.
  2. For a syzygy supported in \(U\), \(\sum_C\langle\hat z_C,g_C\rangle=\sum_{C\in U}\langle D^{b_C}w_U,g_C\rangle=\langle w_U,\sum_C\ell^{b_C}g_C\rangle=0\). The pairing is linear, so it vanishes on the span, and part 1 applies.

\(\square\)

In sheaf language, the local corrections are sections over the members of \(\mathcal U\), and the Čech obstruction to gluing is the defect pairing on syzygies that are not locally generated. Part 1 is the functional-side dual of the recorded filtered obstruction quotient (prop:graded-cone-PC-obstruction), in which top syzygies modulo liftable ones equal \(\ker z\). Here the syzygies are paired with the defects of one extension step instead. The recorded filtered tree gluing (lem:filtered-affine-tree-gluing) glues compatible filtered Boolean-algebra functionals over \(\mathbb F_2\) under a running-intersection tree condition. The present lemma needs no tree structure: its condition is on the syzygies, and it works one moment degree at a time.

The glued theorem

Theorem (glued product constraints). Let \(\mathcal C\) be any finite set of product constraints over \(\mathbb F_3\) on the functional base. The factors are linear or point indicators, as in the product-constraints entry. Let \(\mathcal U\) be a family of subsystems. Each \(U\in\mathcal U\) is pairwise coherent, with forms jointly independent modulo constants on every row, and \(r_U\) of them. Let \(h=\min_C|b_C|\) and fix \(B\ge h\). Suppose the board has at least \(2B-h\) rows and is robust through \(\max_{U}\bigl(L_{\max(B-h,1)}(r_U)+B(r_U+1)\bigr)\), where \(L_t(r)\) is the short-generation theorem's robustness for \(r\) forms. Suppose also that for every \(s\le B\), the top syzygies of degree \(s\) of all of \(\mathcal C\) are spanned by syzygies supported in members of \(\mathcal U\). Then:

  • every NS functional for \(\Gamma+\mathcal C\) through degree \(k\le B\) extends through \(B\);
  • the filtration is stable, PC equals NS through \(B\), and a normalized design exists;
  • there is no PC refutation of degree \(B\), also for weak balanced PHP with these constraints, as in the recorded two-selector corollary.

Proof. Iterate over the extensions from \(s-1\) to \(s\le B\), as in the recorded two-selector corollary. At each step the defects \(\hat z_C\) come from one old functional \(\mu\), which annihilates the legal multiples of every constraint, and one old extension \(E\mu\). The recorded matching extension room gives \(E\mu\), since the robustness gives at least \(2B\) labels. For \(U\in\mathcal U\), the defects of its constraints are exactly the product-constraints theorem's endpoint data for the subsystem \(U\). That theorem, with \(r_U\) forms, gives a local correction \(w_U\). Its row and robustness hypotheses at each \(s\le B\) are covered: each \(U\) has minimal order \(h_U\ge h\), and \(L_t(r)\) is nondecreasing in \(t\) and \(r\). The lemma glues the local corrections. \(\square\)

The only global hypothesis is the syzygy condition. The board's size requirements depend on the largest subsystem, not on the number of constraints.

How this sits in the record

The recorded component hypothesis gave a conditional exclusion theorem from three inputs. The glued theorem changes each of them.

  • (a), \(z\)-injectivity of the weak base, is replaced by the recorded extension property of the functional base. That is where the \(2B\)-label hypothesis enters. Nonrefutation then transfers to weak balanced PHP.
  • Local freeness of each component becomes the fullness and robustness hypothesis, under which local solvability is proved.
  • (b), generation of top syzygies by liftable ones, becomes generation by syzygies supported in solvable members. Koszul syzygies of coherent, jointly full pairs are of this kind when the pair is a member. So are Frobenius and other single-constraint syzygies when the constraint lies in a member. For an incoherent pair the Koszul syzygy is where the fall of the product-constraints entry lives, and the defect pairing on it need not vanish.

The main remaining hypothesis is the Fröberg-type genericity of the tops that the thread has circled since the core-statement review. It is now isolated as a statement about syzygies alone.

The conjecture, and the test against the affine law

Conjecture (local top syzygies). Take an inventory whose prefix-image constraints \(\chi_0(L_{b,i})\prod_{j\in S_b}L_{b,j}\) are pairwise coherent, that is, no image form lies in another block's prefix set. Suppose each single constraint and each pair of them has jointly full, robust forms. Then through degree \(B=(4p-1)(p-1)k\), their top syzygies in \(G\) are spanned by syzygies supported on single constraints and on pairs. Merging incoherent overlaps is left open. It would need a replacement for each merged component that consists of product constraints, is equivalent within degree \(B\), and is pairwise coherent, and none is given here.

The affine analogue, set against the recorded random-conditioning law, which is empirical. For \(M\) affine equations the tops are linear forms \(\ell_j\). Two kinds of syzygy are local when their members are solvable: pair syzygies \(\ell_{j'}e_j-\ell_je_{j'}\), and single-constraint syzygies \(g\,e_j\) with \(\ell_jg=0\) in \(G\), such as \(\ell_j^2e_j\). A linear dependence \(\sum_j\alpha_j\ell_j=0\) in \(G_1\) is a syzygy of degree 1. It is non-local when its circuit is not in the span of dependences inside members, and since the tops of a full member are independent, every such dependence is non-local. That holds even for a consistent system, whose defect pairing on it vanishes. So local generation is strictly stronger than hardness. In a fixed degree \(D\), the pairing map from \(\bigoplus_jG_{D-1}\) to \(G_D\) must have a large kernel once \(M\dim G_{D-1}\) exceeds \(\dim G_D\), and the kernel beyond the Koszul-type count is where non-local syzygies must appear. The density entry found that count, Conjecture SR's semi-regular count, to match the recorded thresholds (64.2 against 64, 14.4 against 14, 8.1 against 7). Those counts were computed on the recorded driver's base; the functional base's \(G\) is smaller, and its crossing may come earlier. So the affine analogue of the conjecture, read as holding below the crossing, is consistent with the recorded refutations, provided the single and pair members are locally solvable. It has not been computed that the local syzygies span everything below the crossing.

Assessment and next step

The goal now reduces, along this line, to one algebraic statement: local generation of the top syzygies in the board's top algebra through polylogarithmic degree. The rest is proved or recorded:

  • the local corrections, for full robust forms;
  • the gluing, which is exact linear algebra;
  • the base's extension, on the functional base.

The remaining limits are the fullness of each subsystem's forms, and the merging of incoherent overlaps into coherent components.

The next step on odd-prime-clause-transfer tests the conjecture where it can fail. For random affine equations at \(n=6,7\), degree 3, and \(n=10\), degree 2, compute the first \(M\) at which the top syzygies of degree \(D\) in \(G\) are not spanned by single and pair syzygies. Compare it with the recorded least refuted \(M\): 7, 14 and 64. A refutation over the weak base is also one over the functional base. Suppose the single and pair subsystems are locally solvable, which the local theorem guarantees only on boards larger than these, and should be checked directly at these sizes. Suppose also that the base extension \(E\mu\) exists at these sizes. Then a refutation forces a failed extension step at some degree \(s\le D\), and the lemma makes it a gluing failure there. The test is nonvacuous because a failure far below the refuted \(M\) would show that local generation is much stronger than hardness needs. Agreement at the thresholds would support the conjecture's range.

So check that \(E\mu\) exists at \(n=6,7,10\), and measure non-local syzygies at every degree \(s\le D\), not only at \(D\). Before coding, count the dimensions of \(G_t\) for the functional board at these sizes. The density entry's base-quotient dimensions at \(n=7\), namely 49, 973 and 9661, are for the recorded driver's base and indicate only the scale. Compare the pairing map's size with the compiled \(\mathbb F_3\) elimination. The step ends with the measured first failure against the thresholds.

Local generation of top syzygies is a Tor group: for linear tops it is the recorded truncated freeness

23 September 2026 · Working proof and a finite check · Top algebra of the functional board; affine tops at \(n=6\), degree 3. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The gluing entry reduced hardness for any number of product constraints to conj:local-top-syzygies: through degree \(B\), the top syzygies in the functional board's top algebra \(G\) are spanned by syzygies supported on single constraints and pairs. It proposed a test on the affine analogue. The test measures the first number \(M\) of random affine equations at which local generation fails, and compares it with the recorded least refuted \(M\) (7, 14 and 64). The cycle ends with that measurement, or with a reason why it cannot bear on the conjecture.

General statement. prop:syzygies-as-tor: for tops that are monomials in linear forms, the top syzygies modulo those generated on single constraints and pairs by the Taylor syzygies of the tops' monomial ideal \(J\) form \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(A/J,G)\), where \(A=\mathbb F_p[x_1,\dots,x_M]/(x_j^p)\) acts through the forms. For linear tops, Koszul-and-Frobenius generation through degree \(s\) holds exactly when \(G\) is free over \(A\) through \(s\), which is the recorded truncated-freeness question. The finite check is ex:affine-syzygy-locality-small-board.

Syzygies as a Tor group

Let \(k=\mathbb F_p\) and let \(G=\bigoplus_{t\ge0}G_t\) be the functional board's top algebra, a commutative graded algebra with \(G_0=k\) and \(K_t=G_t^*\), as in the gluing entry. Every \(\ell\in G_1\) has \(\ell^p=0\): each cell squares to zero in \(G\), so \(\ell^p\) is \(p!\) times a sum of products of distinct cells. This is the dual of the recorded \(D^p=0\). Take \(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_M\in G_1\) and \(A=k[x_1,\dots,x_M]/(x_1^p,\dots,x_M^p)\), graded by \(\deg x_j=1\). Then \(G\) is a graded \(A\)-module through \(x_j\mapsto\ell_j\); \(A\) is the recorded \(u(\mathfrak g)\). A constraint \(C\) has top \(\ell^{b_C}=\prod_j\ell_j^{b_{C,j}}\) with \(0\le b_{C,j}\le p-1\), up to a nonzero scalar. Let \(J\subseteq A\) be the ideal generated by the \(x^{b_C}\). A top syzygy of degree \(s\) is \((g_C)\in\bigoplus_CG_{s-|b_C|}\) with \(\sum_C\ell^{b_C}g_C=0\), as in the gluing lemma.

The Taylor syzygies are the \(G\)-multiples of the following elements of \(\bigoplus_CAe_C\):

  • for a pair \(C\ne C'\), with \(m=\max(b_C,b_{C'})\) componentwise, \(x^{m-b_C}e_C-x^{m-b_{C'}}e_{C'}\);
  • for one constraint \(C\) and one index \(j\), \(x_j^{p-b_{C,j}}e_C\).

Each is supported on one constraint or one pair. For linear tops, \(b_C=e_{j}\), they are the Koszul syzygies \(x_{j'}e_j-x_je_{j'}\) and the Frobenius syzygies \(x_j^{p-1}e_j\).

Proposition (syzygies as Tor).

  1. In each degree \(s\), the top syzygies modulo the span of the Taylor syzygies are isomorphic to \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(A/J,G)_s\). So if this group vanishes for all \(s\le B\), every top syzygy through degree \(B\) is a sum of syzygies supported on single constraints and pairs.
  2. For linear tops, \(J=\mathfrak m=(x_1,\dots,x_M)\). Let \(W_t=[q^t]\,\mathrm{HS}_G(q)/(1+q+\dots+q^{p-1})^M\). The top syzygies through degree \(s\) are generated by Koszul and Frobenius syzygies exactly when \(\dim(G/\mathfrak mG)_t=W_t\) for every \(t\le s\), that is, when \(G\) is free over \(A\) through \(s\) in the graded-Nakayama sense of the truncated Dade entry. In particular \(W_t\ge0\) for \(t\le s\) is necessary.

Proof.

  1. Let \(S=k[x_1,\dots,x_M]\) and \(J'=(x^{b_C})_C+(x_j^p)_j\), a monomial ideal of \(S\). Its syzygy module is generated by the pairwise Taylor syzygies of its generators (Taylor's resolution). A relation \(\sum_Ca_Cx^{b_C}=0\) in \(A\) lifts to a relation of \(J'\) in \(S\), and projecting away the coefficients on the \(x_j^p\) gives back \((a_C)\). A pair of two constraints gives the first kind of Taylor syzygy. A pair of \(x^{b_C}\) and \(x_j^p\) gives the second kind. A pair of two powers \(x_j^p,x_{j'}^p\) projects to zero. So the kernel \(Z\) of \(F=\bigoplus_CAe_C\to J\), \(e_C\mapsto x^{b_C}\), is generated by the Taylor syzygies. Hence \(J\otimes_AG=\operatorname{coker}(Z\otimes_AG\to F\otimes_AG)\), which is \(\bigoplus_CGe_C\) modulo the Taylor syzygies. The sequence \(0\to J\to A\to A/J\to0\) and \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(A,G)=0\) give \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(A/J,G)=\ker(J\otimes_AG\to G)\). The map sends \(\sum_Cg_Ce_C\) to \(\sum_C\ell^{b_C}g_C\), so its kernel is the top syzygies modulo the Taylor syzygies. All maps are graded, with \(e_C\) in degree \(|b_C|\).
  2. Part 1 with \(J=\mathfrak m\) identifies the syzygies modulo Koszul and Frobenius ones with \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(k,G)\). Put \(V=G/\mathfrak mG\), choose a graded section \(V\to G\), and let \(\pi:A\otimes_kV\to G\) be the induced map. It is onto by graded Nakayama, since \(\mathfrak m\) is nilpotent. Let \(\Omega=\ker\pi\). The long exact sequence, with \(\pi\otimes k\) an isomorphism \(V\to V\), gives \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(k,G)\cong\Omega/\mathfrak m\Omega\). The lowest nonzero degree of \(\Omega\) survives in \(\Omega/\mathfrak m\Omega\), because \(\mathfrak m\Omega\) starts one degree higher. So \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(k,G)_t=0\) for all \(t\le s\) exactly when \(\Omega_t=0\) for all \(t\le s\). That holds exactly when \(\dim G_t=\dim(A\otimes V)_t\) for \(t\le s\), that is, when \(\mathrm{HS}_G\equiv\mathrm{HS}_V\cdot(1+\dots+q^{p-1})^M\) modulo \(q^{s+1}\). Dividing by the unit power series gives the condition on \(\dim V_t\). Since \(\dim V_t\ge0\), \(W_t\ge0\) is necessary.

\(\square\)

Relation to the record.

  • For \(J=\mathfrak m^{p-1}\), part 1 is implied by the recorded symmetric lifting lemma (lem:symmetric-lift-free-modules), in dual form. That lemma identifies symmetric tuples modulo lifts with \(\operatorname{Ext}^1_A(A/\mathfrak m^{p-1},K)\). Its conditions are only the adjacent pairs, \(a+e_i=a'+e_{i'}\), and one Frobenius condition for each \(i\), on \(z_{(p-1)e_i}\). They form a generating subset of the Taylor syzygies of \(\mathfrak m^{p-1}\), so the recorded lemma is the sharper statement there. The duality \(\operatorname{Ext}^1_A(A/J,K)\cong\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(A/J,G)^*\) holds for any algebra, by adjunction and exactness of the \(k\)-dual, since \(K=G^*\). For an arbitrary monomial ideal \(J\), part 1 generalizes the lemma's Ext clause.
  • Part 2's count is the one the truncated Dade entry recorded for column tensors. The new step is \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(k,G)\cong\Omega/\mathfrak m\Omega\), which identifies Koszul-and-Frobenius generation with that freeness.
  • The recorded finite check ex:selector-degree-four-semiregular concerns square tops \(\ell_j^2\) in the weak base's top algebra at \(n=7\), \(p=3\), with one seed. It found \(\operatorname{rank}\Phi_4=\min(\gamma_4,M(\gamma_2-\gamma_1)-\binom M2)\) for \(M=2,5,20,39,40,41\). Below the fill point this is the Taylor count, so it is evidence for \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(A/(x_j^2)_j,\cdot)_4=0\) over that algebra for \(M\le40\). At \(M=41\) the fill point is passed (\(41\cdot876-820>\gamma_4=34950\)), and \(\operatorname{Tor}_1\ne0\) there. Freeness over all of \(A\) fails much earlier on that algebra. With \((\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\gamma_3)=(48,924,8688)\), \(W_3\) is negative from \(M=14\), and \(W_2\) from \(M=27\).

Scope.

  • The gluing lemma calls a syzygy local whenever it is supported in a solvable member. That includes single syzygies \(ge_C\) with any \(g\) in the annihilator of the top, and every pair-supported syzygy. So in general Taylor generation implies the gluing lemma's local generation, but not conversely. The two agree when no single constraint and no pair has syzygies beyond its Taylor ones. For linear tops under the conjecture's hypotheses this holds, within the degrees the recorded results cover. For a wide single form, the dual of the amplitude theorem's \(\ker D=\operatorname{im}D^{p-1}\) gives \(\operatorname{Ann}(\ell)=\ell^{p-1}G\). For a jointly full robust pair, the recorded two-form lift applies. So for linear tops the conjecture's local generation is equivalent to \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(k,G)=0\). For product tops, agreement on a single constraint needs \(\operatorname{Ann}(\ell^{b})=\sum_j\ell_j^{p-b_j}G\), which the single-form result does not give.
  • Part 2 takes one constraint for each form, with top \(\ell_j\). A linear dependence among the \(\ell_j\) in \(G_1\) is then a non-Taylor syzygy of degree 1, and freeness correctly fails. In part 1, where constraints are indexed separately, two constraints with the same top give \(e_C-e_{C'}\). That is a Taylor syzygy and pair-supported, so it is local.
  • The truncated Dade entry studied column tensors, which have no row relations, and left open the version for the board's own algebra. So the affine analogue is the same kind of question for \(G\), not a recorded one. That entry's counterexample (ex:truncated-dade-special-position) shows that freeness can fail even where \(W_t>0\).
  • For linear tops, \(W_1=g_1-M\) and \(W_2=g_2-Mg_1+\binom M2\), with \(g_t=\dim G_t\), for \(p\ge3\). On the functional board \(g_1=(n+1)(n-1)\) and \(g_2=\binom{n+1}2(n^2-3n+1)\). So \(W_2<0\) for \(M\) within about \(\sqrt2\,n^{3/2}\) of \(n^2\), and \(W_1<0\) beyond \(n^2-1\). Any family of at least about \(n^2-\sqrt2\,n^{3/2}\) linear tops has non-Taylor syzygies by degree 2.

The computation

The board is \(n=6\): 7 rows and 6 labels, with \((g_1,g_2,g_3)=(35,399,1645)\). A first script, syzygy_locality.py, drew uniform forms and compared \(\operatorname{rank}\Phi\) with the count \(L_{\mathrm{kos}}\) of targets consistent with single and Koszul syzygies. It was stopped after its \(n=6\) runs, for two reasons. Its forms were not full in pairs on every row, which is outside the conjecture's hypotheses. And it tested Koszul generation, not the conjecture's pair generation. The partial log is kept as koszul_locality_partial.txt. There seed 1 already fails at \(M=3\), in degree 3, with a pair that is not full on one row.

The second script, syzygy_locality2.py, draws forms by rejection so that every pair is independent modulo constants on every row. For \(M=2,\dots,7\), seeds 1 and 2, and degrees \(s\le3\), it computes four quantities:

  • \(\operatorname{rank}\Phi\), where \(\Phi\) maps \(K_s\) to \(K_{s-1}^M\) by \(w\mapsto(D_jw)_j\);
  • \(L_2\), the dimension of the targets whose restriction to every pair has a correction, which is dual to all pair-supported syzygies;
  • \(L_3\), the same for triples, computed when \(L_2\) fails;
  • \(L_{\mathrm{kos}}\), and the number of pairs whose own targets are not all corrected.

Syzygies of degree \(s\) are generated on pairs exactly when \(\operatorname{rank}\Phi=L_2\). All computations are exact over \(\mathbb F_3\). semiregular_check.py compares \(\dim(G/\mathfrak mG)_t=g_t-\operatorname{rank}\Phi_t\) with \(W_t\).

What the table shows:

  • In degrees 1 and 2, every case is local and \(\dim(G/\mathfrak mG)_t=W_t\).
  • In degree 3, all twelve cases agree with part 2: Koszul-and-Frobenius generation holds exactly when the series matches. In every case \(L_2=L_{\mathrm{kos}}\), and no pair is incomplete. So on this board, pair generation and Koszul generation coincide.
  • Local generation fails first at \(M=5\), where \(W_3\) first turns negative, in both seeds. Since \(\Omega_t=0\) for \(t<3\), the deficiency is \(\dim\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(k,G)_3=\dim\Omega_3=\dim(G/\mathfrak mG)_3-W_3\). In seed 1 the forms fill \(G_3\), so it is \(0+5\). Seed 2 is in special position: its forms leave 22 dimensions unfilled, and the deficiency is \(22+5=27\). At \(M=6,7\) it is \(238\) and \(441\) in both seeds. Triples barely help.

Against the thresholds. The recorded least refuted \(M\) at \(n=6\), \(D=3\) is 7. It was computed on the weak base with the recorded driver, and a weak-base refutation is also a functional-base refutation. So the functional base's own threshold is at most 7, and it was not computed. Local generation fails at 5, where \(W_3\) crosses zero. Either the functional base is refuted at 5 or 6, or between 5 and the functional threshold the defects vanish on non-local syzygies. The runs at \(n=7\) and \(n=10\) were not made. By part 2, what they measure is the Hilbert series of \(G/\mathfrak mG\), the quantity the proposition identifies. And no reachable board meets the conjecture's robustness: at \(d=3\) the short-generation theorem's \(L_3(2)\) is about 950 labels.

Command: python3 syzygy_locality2.py locality_n6.json 7 6 3 8 1 2, then python3 semiregular_check.py locality_n6.json semiregular_n6.json, in research/results/odd_prime_syzygy_locality_20260923. The two seeds took about 6 minutes each.

What this means for the route

The gluing lemma reduced hardness for many constraints to local generation of the top syzygies. The proposition identifies local generation, in its Taylor form, with \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(A/J,G)=0\) through \(B\). For linear tops that is truncated freeness of \(G\) over the forms' algebra, the question the column-tensor and truncated Dade entries left open for the board's own algebra. So, for linear tops, the gluing route leads back to the open core recorded there. It does not go around it. Freeness fails once the semi-regular series turns negative, and with about \(n^2\) or more linear tops that happens by degree 2. The finite check agrees with this at \(n=6\).

For product tops the target is weaker than freeness: only \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(A/J,G)\) has to vanish, for the monomial ideal \(J\) of the tops. On the weak base's top algebra at \(n=7\), with one seed, the recorded square-top data show that relative vanishing in degree 4 for up to 40 forms. Freeness over all of \(A\) fails there from 14 forms on. That relative vanishing, for the goal's prefix-image tops on \(G\), is now the Taylor-form content of conj:local-top-syzygies, and it is the next object.

Assessment of the line. The gluing line did not escape the recorded genericity core. For linear tops it is that core, and it fails at the semi-regular crossing. Its one remaining advantage is for tops of higher degree, where the needed vanishing is relative to \(J\). The only evidence for relative vanishing beyond freeness is the square-top check, on a different algebra, with one seed and at most 40 forms. Whether it survives polynomially many prefix-image tops is open, and no recorded mechanism proves it.

Next step. On odd-prime-clause-transfer: at \(p=3\), find a sufficient condition for \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(A/J,G)=0\) through degree \(s\) for square tops, \(J=(x_1^2,\dots,x_M^2)\). A general statement would explain the recorded count \(\min(\gamma_4,M(\gamma_2-\gamma_1)-\binom M2)\) below the fill point. A candidate tool is the subring \(k[y_j]/(y_j^2)\), \(y_j\mapsto x_j^2\), which is well defined because \(x^4=0\) at \(p=3\). But \(A\) is not free over it: each variable contributes \(k[y]/(y^2)\oplus k\). So a Hilbert-series criterion like part 2's cannot be assumed, and the extra summand has to be handled. First check what the recorded rank formula says about \(\operatorname{Tor}_1\) and the annihilators \(\operatorname{Ann}(\ell_j^2)\). The step ends with a proof of a sufficient condition, or with an obstruction to one.
