Route review: at p = 3, selectors on a pencil refute pairwise local syzygies; gluing needs a site of spans

23 September 2026 · Route review with a refutation · Pencil identity at every odd prime; refutation at \(p=3\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. This is the fifth research cycle since the lift route review. The previous entry reduced the gluing line's conjecture (conj:local-top-syzygies) to the vanishing of \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(A/J,G)\). Before looking for a sufficient condition for that vanishing, this review tries to falsify the conjecture on the smallest configurations its hypotheses allow. It then assesses the line.

General statement. obs:pencil-selector-syzygy: for every odd \(p\), the selector tops of the \(p+1\) forms of a pencil satisfy a scalar linear relation of degree \(p-1\). When the pencil's forms have pairwise independent \((p-1)\)th powers in \(G\), that relation is not generated by syzygies supported on single constraints and pairs. At \(p=3\) the recorded symmetric lift supplies that independence under the conjecture's own hypotheses. So the conjecture is false as stated.

The line's claim and what the goal needs

The line claims a batched mechanism for the window. Take local corrections on small subsystems, from the product-constraints theorem, and glue them along top syzygies with the gluing lemma. This proves hardness for any number of coherent product constraints, provided the top syzygies through degree \(B\) are generated on members that have corrections. The goal needs this for every inventory compiled from a small refutation. Such inventories are arbitrary, not random, at \(B\) polylogarithmic.

Falsification: the pencil syzygy

Work on the functional board's top algebra \(G\) over \(\mathbb F_p\), as in the gluing entry. A selector constraint on a form \(L\) is \(1-(L-a)^{p-1}\), with top \(-L^{p-1}\). Take two forms \(\ell,\ell'\) and the \(p+1\) forms of their pencil, one for each point of \(\mathbf P^1(\mathbb F_p)\): \(v_c=\ell+c\ell'\) for \(c\in\mathbb F_p\), and \(v_\infty=\ell'\).

Observation (pencil syzygy).

  1. \(\sum_{c\in\mathbb F_p}v_c^{\,p-1}+v_\infty^{\,p-1}=0\) in any commutative \(\mathbb F_p\)-algebra, and so in \(G_{p-1}\). Hence \((g_C)=(1,\dots,1)\) is a top syzygy of degree \(p-1\) of the \(p+1\) selectors, with any constants \(a_C\).
  2. Suppose the \(p+1\) powers \(v^{p-1}\) are pairwise linearly independent in \(G_{p-1}\). Then this syzygy is not a sum of syzygies supported on single constraints and pairs.
  3. At \(p=3\), the powers are pairwise independent whenever \(\ell,\ell'\) are independent modulo constants on every row, on a board with at least 4 rows that is robust through \(L_1+6\) labels. Here \(L_1\) is the short-generation theorem's robustness for two forms. So the four selectors are a counterexample to conj:local-top-syzygies within its hypotheses:
    • each selector is the prefix image \(\chi_0(v-a_v)\) with an empty prefix set, so pairwise coherence (no image form in another block's prefix set) holds vacuously;
    • all six pairs of the four forms span the same pencil, so each single constraint and each pair has forms independent modulo constants on every row, the gluing entry's joint fullness;
    • its robustness is the glued theorem's threshold \(\max_U(L_{\max(B-h,1)}(r_U)+B(r_U+1))\) with \(r_U\le2\), which is at least \(L_1+6\). Boards robust through it exist for every \(B\), by taking enough labels.

Proof.

  1. Expand: \(\sum_c(\ell+c\ell')^{p-1}=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\binom{p-1}k\ell^{p-1-k}\ell'^k\sum_cc^k\). The power sum \(\sum_{c\in\mathbb F_p}c^k\) is \(p=0\) for \(k=0\), and \(0\) for \(0<k<p-1\). For \(k=p-1\) it is \(-1\). So the sum is \(-\ell'^{p-1}\), and adding \(v_\infty^{p-1}=\ell'^{p-1}\) gives \(0\). Rescaling a representative by \(\lambda\in\mathbb F_p^\times\) multiplies its power by \(\lambda^{p-1}=1\).
  2. The tops have degree \(p-1\), so a syzygy of degree \(p-1\) has scalar coefficients. A syzygy supported on one constraint or on a pair is then \(\alpha v^{p-1}=0\) or \(\alpha v^{p-1}+\beta w^{p-1}=0\). Pairwise independence forces \(\alpha=\beta=0\). So every syzygy of this degree supported on at most two constraints is zero, and the pencil syzygy, which is nonzero, is not in their span.
  3. Suppose \(\alpha\ell^2+\beta\ell'^2=0\) in \(G_2\), with \(\ell,\ell'\) any two of the four forms. Multiply by \(g\in G_1\) and pair with \(w\in K_3\): \(\langle\alpha D_\ell^2w+\beta D_{\ell'}^2w,g\rangle=0\) for all \(g\), so \(\alpha D_\ell^2w+\beta D_{\ell'}^2w=0\) for all \(w\in K_3\). Here we use the perfect pairing \(K_t=G_t^*\) and the adjunction \(\langle w,\ell g\rangle=\langle D_\ell w,g\rangle\), both recorded in the gluing entry. Take \(0\ne\zeta\in K_1\) with \(D_\ell\zeta=D_{\ell'}\zeta=0\). It exists because \((D_\ell,D_{\ell'})\) maps \(K_1\) to \(K_0^2\), and \(\dim K_0=1\), while \(\dim K_1=R(N-1)>2\) for a board with \(R\ge4\) rows and \(N\ge2\) labels. The vector \(\zeta\) satisfies the symmetric-tuple conditions for \((\zeta,0,0)\) in \(K_1\). The recorded symmetric lift at every degree (cor:symmetric-lift-every-degree, \(d=1\), \(r=2\)) gives \(w\in K_3\) with \(D_\ell^2w=m\zeta\) for a unit \(m\), and \(D_{\ell'}^2w=0\). Hence \(\alpha=0\), and by symmetry \(\beta=0\). All six pairs of the four forms span the same pencil, so each pair satisfies the same hypotheses.

\(\square\)

Relation to the record. At \(p=3\) the relation is the recorded three-selector identity, \(q_1+q_2+q_3=(a-b)^2\), read as a syzygy among four tops. Multiplying it by \(a-b\) gives that entry's degree-three fall, \((a-b)(a^2+b^2+(a+b)^2)=0\), a syzygy of the three selectors alone. Whether that three-term syzygy is non-local is not shown here. Its four-selector completion is what refutes the conjecture. The gluing entry's conjecture should have been tested against this recorded control, which the remaining route lists; its verification gate searched the index but did not do so. The component hypothesis grouped constraints along bounded circuits. The special-position cores entry recorded evidence against bounded cores: in the rank-one model at \(v\le7\), dependencies supported on 8 to 19 points, excluding core size at most 6 in the samples only, at total selector density far above one. Over \(\mathbb F_p\), the pencil relation is the simplest case of the power-sum identity \(\sum_{v\in\mathbb F_p^w}f(v)=0\) for \(\deg f<w(p-1)\).

What survives:

  • the gluing lemma and the glued theorem, which are conditional on the syzygy hypothesis;
  • the syzygies-as-Tor proposition;
  • the local theory.

What fails is the choice of members. Singles and pairs do not generate the syzygies even in the conjecture's own hypotheses. The members must contain every pencil, and more generally every set of constraints whose forms span a small space in special position.

Assessment of the line

The local theory is strong and general: short generation, product constraints and exact gluing are proved at every degree. The global obligation is now visible in its exact form. It is an analogue of the recorded component hypothesis on the functional base. That hypothesis was stated for forbid-value constraints on the weak unary base, and prefix images need the adaptation it notes. Syzygies must be generated on members closed under small-span dependencies, and each member needs its own local correction. Three pieces of evidence bear on it.

  • Linear tops fail at the semi-regular crossing.
  • Pairwise locality fails on a pencil at constant size.
  • Recorded special-position cores are large in small samples at high density.

Two obstacles are recorded, and no mechanism for either:

  • merging a member whose constraints become incoherent point indicators when rewritten on a basis of its span;
  • controlling adversarial cores.

The line has turned the batched mechanism into a precise algebraic statement about a site of subsystems. It has not made that statement easier than the recorded core. The pencil case, however, is small, fully explicit and decidable by hand. The gluing formalism also says exactly what a member must provide.

Next step: pencils as open sets

The sheaf picture changes its site: members are spans of forms, not pairs. The first test is whether a pencil is a legitimate member. On odd-prime-clause-transfer, at \(p=3\), take the four selectors of a pencil, with forbidden values \(a_v\). Their constraints cut out a solution set \(P\subseteq\mathbb F_3^2\) of \((\ell,\ell')\). Decide, as a general statement for jointly full robust \(\ell,\ell'\):

  1. when \(P\ne\emptyset\), does the subsystem have a local correction at every degree, so that the defect pairing on every syzygy supported in the pencil vanishes?
  2. when \(P=\emptyset\), which happens exactly when the four forbidden lines are concurrent, does a refutation exist at degree at most 4?

The candidate method is to rewrite the pencil subsystem on the basis \((\ell,\ell')\) as conditions on the point set \(P\). The difficulty is the incoherent point-indicator pairs this produces. Read the recorded pair-component lifting check first. There, an overlapping pair has no fall through degree 6 exactly when its forbidden lines meet. The step ends with a proof that satisfiable pencils are members, or with the obstruction that stops them.

Verification gate.

  • Re-read from the notebook: the three-selector identity, the symmetric lift at every degree (cor:symmetric-lift-every-degree), the gluing entry's conjecture and its hypotheses, and the syzygies-as-Tor entry.
  • Claim searches: pencil, selector power-sum and concurrent-line relations. They found the three-selector fall, the special-position cores and the local configuration catalogue, all cited.
  • Checks: a brute-force count over all 81 choices of forbidden values confirmed that the four forbidden lines cover \(\mathbb F_3^2\) exactly when they are concurrent.
  • Fresh-context review: the reviewer confirmed the power-sum identity, the scalar-coefficient argument and the symmetric-tuple check. It required the following changes, all adopted:
    • the selectors' admissibility checked against the conjecture's definitions, including its robustness threshold;
    • the duality used in part 3 cited, and the dimension count for \(\zeta\) completed;
    • all six pairs covered;
    • the refutation limited to \(p=3\);
    • the three-selector relation to the record stated precisely;
    • the special-position evidence stated with its sample limits;
    • the component hypothesis called an analogue.

The changes restrict or qualify the claims, so no further pass was made.

Coherent product systems cut out exactly grid up-sets: every pencil is covered, most solution sets on a three-dimensional span are not

23 September 2026 · Working proofs and an exhaustive check · Solution sets of coherent product systems on a span of forms, \(p=3\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The pencil review showed that gluing members must contain pencils. It asked whether a satisfiable pencil subsystem has a local correction, and whether an unsatisfiable one is refuted at low degree. The underlying question is general. Which constraint sets on a span of forms can the product-constraints theorem handle after rewriting? The cycle ends with a characterization, or with an obstruction.

General statement. prop:coherent-sets-are-up-sets: on a span of dimension \(w\), the solution sets of pairwise coherent product systems on jointly independent forms are exactly the up-sets of a coordinatewise total order on \(\mathbb F_3^w\), for some basis. For \(w=2\) this is every subset. For \(w=3\) it is at most \(49{,}533{,}120\) of the \(2^{27}-1\) nonempty subsets. cor:pencil-subsystems: a constraint set on a pencil is refuted at degree 6 or less for selectors when its solution set is empty. When the solution set is a proper nonempty subset, the set has no refutation wherever the coherent two-form system that rewrites it has none.

Coherent systems and up-sets

Work over \(\mathbb F_3\) on the functional base. Let \(W\) be a span of affine forms of dimension \(w\), with a basis \(u_1,\dots,u_w\) independent modulo constants on every row. An invertible linear change of basis, with constant shifts, preserves this property, so every basis of \(W\) has it. A product constraint on forms of \(W\), in the sense of the product-constraints theorem, is \(C=\prod_jh_j(L_j)\) with each factor \(1\), \(L_j-a\) or \(\chi_a(L_j)=1-(L_j-a)^2\). That theorem needs the forms used to be jointly independent modulo constants on every row. Within \(W\) these are at most \(w\) forms, which extend to a basis, so we may take the forms to be \(u_1,\dots,u_w\). Coherence of a pair means that on each shared form the factors are equal, or one is \(\chi_a\) and the other \(L-a'\) with \(a'\ne a\). Identify a point of \(\mathbb F_3^w\) with the values of \((u_1,\dots,u_w)\).

Proposition (coherent sets are up-sets). Order the three values of each coordinate by a total order, and give \(\mathbb F_3^w\) the product order. For every pairwise coherent family \(\mathcal F\) of product constraints on the basis \(u\), there are orders for which the common zero set \(Z(\mathcal F)\) is an up-set. Conversely, for every basis, every choice of orders and every nonempty up-set \(U\), some pairwise coherent family on that basis has \(Z(\mathcal F)=U\).

Proof. Coherence fixes, on each form \(u_j\), at most one indicator value \(a_j\) and at most one linear value \(a'_j\), with \(a'_j\ne a_j\) when both occur: two different indicators or two different linear factors on one form are incoherent. Choose unused values freely, keeping \(a'_j\ne a_j\), and rank the values of coordinate \(j\) as \(a_j\) at level 0, the remaining value at level 1, and \(a'_j\) at level 2.

  • \(\chi_{a_j}(u_j)\) vanishes exactly at level at least 1.
  • \(u_j-a'_j\) vanishes exactly at level 2.

So a constraint vanishes at \(x\) exactly when some coordinate \(j\) in its support has level at least \(t_j\), with \(t_j=1\) for an indicator and \(t_j=2\) for a linear factor. That set is the complement of the principal down-set of the point \(y\) with \(y_j=t_j-1\) on the support and \(y_j=2\) elsewhere. So it is an up-set, and so is the intersection \(Z(\mathcal F)\).

Conversely, let \(U\) be a nonempty up-set with complement \(D\), a down-set. Then \(D\) is the union of the principal down-sets of its maximal elements \(y\), and none of them is the top point, since \(U\ne\varnothing\). For each such \(y\), the complement of its down-set is \(\{x:\exists j,\ \mathrm{level}(x_j)>y_j\}\). That is the zero set of \(\prod_{j:\,y_j<2}h_j\), with \(h_j=\chi_{a_j}(u_j)\) if \(y_j=0\) and \(h_j=u_j-a'_j\) if \(y_j=1\). All these constraints use the single indicator value \(a_j\) and the single linear value \(a'_j\ne a_j\) on each form, so they are pairwise coherent, and their common zero set is \(U\). If \(D\) is empty the family is empty. \(\square\)

Two dimensions: every set. An exhaustive check, coherent_pencil_sets.py, tries the 6 bases of \(\mathbb F_3^2\) among the pencil's 4 directions, all values \(a_j\) and \(a'_j\), and all subfamilies. It finds every one of the 510 proper nonempty subsets of \(\mathbb F_3^2\) as such a zero set, and it records one witness for each. For example, \(\{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)\}\) is cut out by \(uv\), \(\chi_2(u)\) and \(\chi_2(v)\). So, for \(w=2\), every nonempty \(P\subseteq\mathbb F_3^2\) is the solution set of a pairwise coherent family on some basis of the pencil.

Three dimensions: most sets are not. Count the pairs (up-set, order) that could describe a subset of \(\mathbb F_3^3\):

  • unordered bases, up to scaling each form, number \(13\cdot12\cdot9/6=234\);
  • orders number \((3!)^3=216\) for each basis;
  • up-sets of the grid \(\{0,1,2\}^3\) number 980, the plane partitions in a \(3\times3\times3\) box.

So at most \(234\cdot216\cdot980=49{,}533{,}120\) nonempty subsets of \(\mathbb F_3^3\) are solution sets of coherent systems. There are \(2^{27}-1=134{,}217{,}727\) nonempty subsets, so at least 84 million are not.

Pencils

Corollary (pencil subsystems). Let \(\ell,\ell'\) be affine forms. Let \(\mathcal U\) be a finite set of constraints, each a polynomial of degree at most \(e\) in forms of the pencil \(\langle\ell,\ell'\rangle\), with common zero set \(P\subseteq\mathbb F_3^2\).

  1. If \(P=\varnothing\), the functional base plus \(\mathcal U\) has a PC refutation of degree at most \(4+e\), which is 6 for selectors. This part needs no hypothesis on \(\ell,\ell'\).
  2. Suppose the row-linear parts of \(\ell,\ell'\) are independent modulo constants on every row, and \(P\) is a proper nonempty subset. Let \(\mathcal F_P\) be a coherent family on a basis \((u,v)\) of the pencil with \(Z(\mathcal F_P)=P\), which exists by the check. Let \(h=\min_{C\in\mathcal F_P}|b_C|\ge1\), where \(b_C\) is the exponent vector of the top of \(C\), as in the product-constraints entry. Suppose \(B\ge\max(8,e)\), and the board has at least \(2B-h\) rows and is robust through \(L_{\max(B-h,1)}+3B\), with \(L_t\) the short-generation robustness for two forms. Then the functional base plus \(\mathcal U\) has no PC refutation of degree \(B\).

Proof. All constraints are polynomials in \(u,v\). Work on the functional base, which contains Booleanity.

  1. This is the recorded bounded-span equivalence (lem:bounded-span-equivalence) with \(d=2\), \(p=3\): it derives \(1\) at degree at most \((p-1)d+e=4+e\).
  2. Each constraint of \(\mathcal U\) vanishes on \(P=Z(\mathcal F_P)\) and, reduced modulo \(u^3-u\) and \(v^3-v\), has degree at most 4 in \((u,v)\). The members of \(\mathcal F_P\) have degree at most 4. So bounded-span equivalence, applied to \(\mathcal F_P\), derives the reduced form of every constraint of \(\mathcal U\) at PC degree at most \(4+4=8\). Adding back multiples of \(u^3-u\) and \(v^3-v\), which are derivable at degree 3, gives the constraint itself at degree at most \(\max(8,e)\). Take a PC refutation of the base plus \(\mathcal U\) of degree \(D\). First derive each constraint of \(\mathcal U\) from \(\mathcal F_P\), then run the refutation. This is a PC refutation of the base plus \(\mathcal F_P\) of degree at most \(\max(D,8,e)\). The coherent product-constraints corollary, with \(r=2\) forms and the stated rows and robustness, excludes a refutation of the base plus \(\mathcal F_P\) of degree at most \(B\). Since \(B\ge\max(8,e)\), a refutation with \(D\le B\) would give one of degree at most \(B\), so \(D>B\). \(\square\)

When \(P=\mathbb F_3^2\), every constraint of \(\mathcal U\) vanishes identically as a function. It then follows from Booleanity at degree \(\max(e,3)\), and the question reduces to the base alone. With \(B\ge4+e\), bounded-span equivalence also derives each member of \(\mathcal F_P\) from \(\mathcal U\). A transfer of the corollary's stable moments would need that two-way equivalence at degree \(B\), but no such transfer is claimed here.

On the pencil review's two questions:

  • An unsatisfiable pencil is refuted at degree 6. The review asked for degree at most 4, which remains open.
  • A satisfiable isolated pencil has no refutation of degree \(B\). That is nonrefutation, not the local correction the review asked for. A correction would need the corollary's stable moments to transfer through the two-way equivalence.

What this does and does not give the gluing line

  • Isolated members. Any member whose forms lie in a pencil can be rewritten into the product-constraints theorem's setting.
  • Several members. This does not follow. Each pencil gets its own basis and its own family \(\mathcal F_P\). Two rewritten members that share a form, or a member and another constraint on a shared form, need not be coherent. Their forms need not be jointly independent on every row. The rewrite also changes the tops, so the syzygy hypothesis of the glued theorem has to be checked again for the new generators. The corollary is a statement about one pencil, not about members inside an inventory.
  • Spans of dimension three and more. The proposition shows that rewriting into coherent product systems on forms of the span fails for most solution sets, counted uniformly over subsets of \(\mathbb F_3^3\). The count includes the empty up-set, so it is slightly loose. A member whose solution set is not an up-set, for any basis and orders, needs a local theory beyond product constraints: a lift for constraints whose zero set is an arbitrary pattern set, or a proof that such members are refuted, or harmless, at low degree.

Assessment. The sheaf picture now has isolated pencils as local pieces that are not refuted, one at a time. Two things are missing: compatibility between overlapping rewritten members, and a local theory for three-dimensional spans whose solution sets are not up-sets. The second is a sharp, finite question at its smallest case.

Next step. On odd-prime-clause-transfer, at \(p=3\): take the smallest solution sets \(P\subseteq\mathbb F_3^3\) that are not up-sets for any basis and orders, found by exhaustive search over the 234 bases and 216 orders. For one such \(P\), with three jointly full forms on a robust board, decide by proof whether conditioning on \(P\) has local corrections at every degree, or is refuted at degree at most \((p-1)\cdot3+4=10\) by bounded-span equivalence together with some further mechanism. The search is small: \(2^{27}\) subsets against about \(5\times10^7\) describable ones, done as a count over up-sets, not an enumeration of subsets. The step ends with a lift for non-up-set members, or with an obstruction that makes them refutable or harmless.

Verification gate.

  • Re-read from the notebook: the product-constraints theorem's coherence definition and corollary, and the bounded-span equivalence lemma with its proof.
  • Prior-record check: before drafting, a reviewer was asked whether the record already implies the statements. It found that the degree part is the recorded bounded-span equivalence, now cited, with degree 6 in place of this cycle's first estimate of 8. It found that the classification is not recorded. It required the scope limits on several members, now stated.
  • Exhaustive check: all 510 proper nonempty subsets, with witnesses stored.
  • Fresh-context review: the reviewer confirmed the proposition in both directions, the level encoding, the three-dimensional count and the check script. It required the following changes, all adopted:
    • the full set \(P=\mathbb F_3^2\) excluded from part 2 and treated separately;
    • the unused bound \(4+e\) dropped, with its use for two-way equivalence noted;
    • part 1 stated without the independence hypothesis;
    • the answers to the pencil review stated honestly, as degree 6 against the requested 4, and nonrefutation rather than correction;
    • the degree bookkeeping and \(b_C\) made explicit;
    • the title and the scope of the three-dimensional count made precise.

A satisfiable member is never refuted on its own: pinning to one allowed point suffices, and the gluing obstruction lies in compatibility

23 September 2026 · Working proof · Constraint sets on a span of jointly full forms over \(\mathbb F_3\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The pencil-members entry rewrote an isolated pencil into a coherent two-form system to show it is not refuted. It proposed treating three-dimensional solution sets that no coherent system cuts out. Before doing so, this cycle asks whether nonrefutation of an isolated member needs any rewriting at all. It ends with a general statement, or with a member that is refuted although satisfiable.

General statement. lem:member-pinning: for any constraint set on a span of \(w\) jointly full forms over \(\mathbb F_3\), with a nonempty solution set, the functional base plus the set has no PC refutation of degree \(B\) on the boards where an affine system on \(w\) forms has none. It composes the recorded single-constraint dichotomy, extended from point indicators to any constraint vanishing at the pinned point, with the product-constraints corollary. So an isolated member is never the obstruction, whatever its solution set.

The pinning lemma

Lemma (member pinning). Let \(u_1,\dots,u_w\) be affine forms over \(\mathbb F_3\) whose row-linear parts are independent modulo constants on every row. Let \(\mathcal U\) be a set of constraints, each an axiom line \(c(u)\) given as a polynomial in the forms \(u\), with common zero set \(P\subseteq\mathbb F_3^w\) nonempty. Fix \(q\in P\). Suppose the board has at least \(2B-1\) rows and is robust through \(L_{\max(B-1,1)}+B(w+1)\), with \(L_t\) the short-generation robustness for \(w\) forms. Then the functional base plus \(\mathcal U\) has no PC refutation of degree \(B\).

Proof.

  1. The affine system \(u_j=q_j\), \(j\le w\), puts each equation on its own form, so it is pairwise coherent. By the coherent product-constraints corollary, with \(r=w\), \(h=1\) and the stated rows and robustness, the functional base plus this system has no PC refutation of degree \(B\).
  2. Each constraint is \(c(u)\) for a polynomial \(c\in\mathbb F_3[y_1,\dots,y_w]\) with \(c(q)=0\). Division in \(\mathbb F_3[y]\) by the \(y_j-q_j\) gives \(c=\sum_j(y_j-q_j)h_j\) with \(\deg h_j<\deg c\). Substituting \(y=u\) gives an exact identity in the Boolean variables. The linear parts of the \(u_j\) are linearly independent, which follows from the row-wise hypothesis. So the degree of \(c(u)\) in the Boolean variables equals its degree in \(y\), and no monomial of top degree cancels. So \(c\) is derivable from the affine system by multiplications, at degree \(\deg c\). This is the substitution in part 1 of the recorded single-constraint dichotomy (lem:single-constraint-conditioning-equivalence), which treats point indicators \(\chi_w\), \(w\ne q\). The same proof applies to any \(c\) vanishing at \(q\).
  3. In a PC refutation of the base plus \(\mathcal U\) of degree \(D\), replace each axiom line \(c\) by its derivation, of degree \(\deg c\le D\). This gives a refutation of the base plus the affine system of degree \(D\). By step 1, \(D>B\). \(\square\)

Relation to the record.

  • The lemma is a composition of recorded results. The pinning step is the single-constraint dichotomy's part 1, and the rest is the product-constraints corollary for affine systems. For a pencil, \(w=2\), pinning removes part 2 of cor:pencil-subsystems' condition \(B\ge\max(8,e)\) and its need for the up-set classification. The cost is that pinning always runs at \(h=1\), so it needs \(2B-1\) rows and robustness \(L_{\max(B-1,1)}+3B\). Part 2 allows \(h\ge2\), with fewer rows. So pinning subsumes part 2 only when the rewritten family has \(h=1\). That part stays correct. The classification of coherent sets (prop:coherent-sets-are-up-sets) is not needed for nonrefutation of an isolated member. It matters only where rewritten members must be coherent with each other.
  • Pinning every constraint of an inventory to one global point is a deciding design. The recorded ceiling (obs:deciding-designs-capped) says that affine conditioning on forms spanning all linear parts modulo rows fixes every cell and is refuted at degree at most 2. So pinning is capped below about \(N^2\) independent forms. The lemma is the member-sized case of that recorded mechanism, not a way past its ceiling.

What gluing is about

Each member, taken alone, has functionals that satisfy it: pin it to any allowed point. The recorded gluing lemma asks for more. Its corrections must repair the defects \(\hat z_C\), which come from one global functional \(\mu\) and its extension. They are not arbitrary functionals satisfying the member, and \(\mu\) is fixed before the member is looked at. The lemma does not settle whether a member's defects can be repaired. It is necessary that \(\mu\) be compatible with the member's consequences at lower degree. The pencil's degree fall \(\sum_vC_v=\lambda\), an affine polynomial, shows this. Whether this compatibility is also sufficient is not shown. So the remaining obstruction concerns two compatibilities:

  • between members, where they share forms;
  • between each member and the global functional.

In the sheaf language used since the gluing entry, satisfying functionals exist on every member, and the question is whether compatible ones come from one global section. The problem has the structure of a global-section problem for a presheaf of local functionals, the form in which Abramsky and Brandenburger cast contextuality. Here the functionals are PC pseudo-expectations, not probability distributions, and the board's top algebra supplies the gluing maps. That is a statement of the problem's shape, not a result.

Pinning gives global sections as long as one point satisfies all members, with the union of the pinned forms small enough for the affine theory. Once the inventory's forms span all linear parts modulo rows, it cannot: the recorded ceiling refutes any global pinning at degree 2. The recorded selector thresholds (ex:selector-semiregular-thresholds), a finite check at small \(n\), show hardness beyond that regime. At \(n=6\), 76 selectors on uniform affine forms are not refuted at degree 3, although their forms span \(G_1\), of dimension 35. So the global sections that exist there are mixed, not pinned, and no recorded mechanism constructs them.

Assessment and next step

The member-level questions are now closed for nonrefutation, at every span dimension. What remains is the mixed-section problem: construct compatible corrections when no point assignment covers the inventory. The only recorded route to it is the syzygy condition, \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(A/J,G)=0\) through \(B\), for the tops of the whole inventory. For square tops the recorded evidence covers up to 40 forms at \(n=7\), with one seed, on the weak base's algebra.

Next step. On odd-prime-clause-transfer, at \(p=3\): explain the recorded square-top count \(\operatorname{rank}\Phi_4=\min(\gamma_4,M(\gamma_2-\gamma_1)-\binom M2)\) on the weak base's algebra at \(n=7\). The target is an expected rank modulo Koszul syzygies, not a bound set by the domain and codomain. So there are two open conditions: rank at least the target, carried by a nonzero minor, and independence of the Koszul syzygies in the kernel. Both hold for generic forms over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\) once one specialization satisfies them. The F_3 case needs a separate argument, since the minors' degrees exceed 3. The candidate is permutation forms, \(\ell_j=\sum_ix_{i,\pi_j(i)}\) for permutations \(\pi_j\), defined for every \(M\). Their squares are sums of matching monomials, so \(\Phi_4\) becomes a combinatorial incidence map. First compute its rank at \(n=7\) for \(M=2,5,20,39,40\), as recorded, with \(\gamma_4=34950\) columns and at most \(40\cdot924\) rows. If it matches, look for a combinatorial proof for all \(n\). If it does not, the specialization is too special. This covers generic, not adversarial, inventories.

Verification gate.

  • Re-read from the notebook: the product-constraints corollary (rows, robustness, \(h\)), the bounded-span equivalence lemma, the pencil-members corollary, and the deciding-designs ceiling.
  • Claim searches: point conditioning, deciding designs and pinning. They found the single-constraint dichotomy, which is the pinning mechanism, now cited with its proof re-read, and the deciding-designs ceiling, cited as the global version. The first draft proved the pinning step through bounded-span equivalence at degree \(\max(2w+1,e)\). The dichotomy's substitution removes that condition.
  • Fresh-context review: the reviewer confirmed the division identity and the PC replacement, and that the affine system meets the corollary's hypotheses. It required the following changes, all adopted:
    • the subsumption of the pencil corollary limited;
    • unused hypotheses dropped;
    • the degree of \(c(u)\) justified by independence of the linear parts;
    • the unproved sufficiency of compatibility weakened to necessity, and the title reworded;
    • the selector comparison restated as spanning \(G_1\), and labelled as a finite check;
    • "far past pinning" at \(n=7\) dropped;
    • the next step's two open conditions separated, the F_3 remark corrected, and the disjoint-support specialization, which exists only for at most \(n+1\) forms, replaced by permutation forms.

The changes weaken or restrict claims. The new specialization is a proposal, not a claim. So no further pass was made.

At n = 7, generic square tops have only Frobenius and Koszul syzygies in degree 4, proved by one orbit specialization

23 September 2026 · Working proof by exact specialization, and a conjecture · Square tops in degree 4 on the weak unary top algebra, \(n=7\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The member-pinning entry moved the gluing obstruction to compatibility. The only recorded route to compatible sections is \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(A/J,\cdot)=0\) for the inventory's tops. For square tops the degree-four spread entry measured \(\operatorname{rank}\Phi_4=\min(\gamma_4,M(\gamma_2-\gamma_1)-\binom M2)\) at \(n=7\) with one random seed. Can that count be proved, for generic forms, from one specialization? The cycle ends with a proof or a failed specialization.

General statement. conj:square-top-degree-four-semiregular: for every \(n\ge7\) and generic linear forms, the degree-4 syzygies of square tops on the weak unary top algebra are exactly the Frobenius and Koszul ones, below the degree-4 fill point. prop:generic-square-tops-degree-four proves it at \(n=7\) for every \(M\le40\).

Setting

\(A\) is the weak unary PHP top algebra at \(n\) holes over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\), as in the degree-four spread entry. At \(n=7\) its dimensions are \((\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\gamma_4)=(48,924,34950)\). For linear forms \(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_M\in A_1\), let \(\Phi_4:\bigoplus_jA_2e_j\to A_4\), \((a_j)\mapsto\sum_ja_j\ell_j^2\). Its kernel contains two kinds of generators:

  • Frobenius: \(\ell_jm\,e_j\) for \(m\) in a basis of \(A_1\), since \(\ell_j^3=0\);
  • Koszul: \(\ell_k^2e_j-\ell_j^2e_k\) for \(k<j\).

There are \(g_M=M\gamma_1+\binom M2\) of them. Put \(T_M=M\gamma_2-g_M\), which is the recorded count below the fill point: \(T_M\le\gamma_4\) exactly for \(M\le40\) at \(n=7\). The syzygies-as-Tor proposition was stated for the functional board's \(G\). Its Taylor-resolution argument applies to any graded module over \(R=\overline{\mathbb F}_3[x_1,\dots,x_M]/(x_j^3)\), here \(A\). For \(J=(x_j^2)\), the image of the Taylor syzygies in degree 4 is exactly the span of the listed generators. So "kernel equals their span" is \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(R/J,A)_4=0\).

The proposition

Proposition (generic square tops in degree four). At \(n=7\), for every \(M\le40\), there is a nonempty Zariski-open set of \(M\)-tuples of forms on which the Frobenius and Koszul generators are linearly independent and span \(\ker\Phi_4\), and \(\operatorname{rank}\Phi_4=T_M\). At \(M=41\), \(\Phi_4\) is onto \(A_4\) on a nonempty open set.

Proof. Two conditions are open in the forms, since each is the nonvanishing of some minor of a matrix whose entries are polynomials in the forms' coefficients:

  • (a) \(\operatorname{rank}\Phi_4\ge\min(T_M,\gamma_4)\);
  • (b) the \(g_M\) generators have rank \(g_M\).

Both hold at the orbit specialization below, which is an \(\mathbb F_3\)-point, so each defines a nonempty open subset of the irreducible affine space of \(M\)-tuples, and so does their intersection. At a point of the intersection, with \(M\le40\):

  • the kernel contains the generators' span, of dimension \(g_M\);
  • it has dimension \(M\gamma_2-\operatorname{rank}\Phi_4\le M\gamma_2-T_M=g_M\).

So the kernel equals the span, and \(\operatorname{rank}\Phi_4=T_M\). At \(M=41\), (a) says \(\operatorname{rank}\Phi_4=\gamma_4\). \(\square\)

The specialization. Take one uniform form \(\ell\) over \(\mathbb F_3\), seed 0. Take its images under the \(8\cdot7=56\) cyclic shifts \((i,a)\mapsto(i+r,a+h)\) of pigeons and holes, in a seeded random order, and use the first \(M\) of them. function_phi4.py --family orbit computed \(\operatorname{rank}\Phi_4\) for every prefix \(M=1,\dots,41\): it equals \(\min(T_M,\gamma_4)\) in all 41 cases. taylor_independence.py computed the generators' rank for every prefix: it equals \(g_M\) in all 41 cases. So (a) and (b) hold at every \(M\le41\). At \(M=41\) the kernel has dimension \(41\cdot924-34950=2934\), which exceeds \(g_{41}=2788\) by 146, so there \(\operatorname{Tor}_1\ne0\) for every tuple, since \(\operatorname{rank}\Phi_4\le\gamma_4\) always. The result file's field coef is ignored by the orbit family.

A failed specialization. Function forms, \(\ell_j=\sum_ic_{j,i}x_{i,\sigma_j(i)}\), with one cell per pigeon, uniform \(\sigma_j\) and random nonzero \(c_{j,i}\), fall short of \(T_M\):

  • by 2 at \(M=2\), 196 at \(M=5\) and 606 at \(M=20\), at \(n=7\);
  • by 35 at \(M=2\) at \(n=6\), against 12 for uniform forms.

A likely explanation is that concentrating each pigeon on one cell makes pigeons that pick the same hole collide, so their products vanish. The failure of this family proves nothing about necessity. At \(n=6\) the sampled uniform forms also fall short, by \(6\) per form, matching the recorded annihilator excess \(\dim\operatorname{Ann}_{A_2}(\ell^2)=\gamma_1+6\) for sampled forms there. A sample only bounds the generic kernel from above, so generic failure at \(n=6\) is not proved.

Computation. The ranks come from one incremental elimination over \(\mathbb F_3\), which gives every prefix rank. It is gf3_prefix.c: bit-sliced rows, as in the recorded gf3.c, with a fully reduced basis and OpenMP over a block's rows. It was checked against the recorded elimination on 20 random block matrices. It took 222 s for all 41 prefixes, where re-eliminating each \(M\) separately took 396 s for six of them. The generator check took 1 s. Results and scripts are in research/results/odd_prime_permutation_forms_20260923.

What this gives and what it does not

  • It is a proof, not a sample. For generic square tops at \(n=7\), the degree-4 syzygies are exactly the Taylor ones below the fill point, \(M\le40\). The degree-four spread entry's one-seed count is confirmed as the generic behaviour.
  • It is one degree at one board size, on the weak base's algebra, not on the functional board's \(G\).
  • It is generic, not adversarial. The goal's inventories come from an arbitrary small refutation, and the pencil review showed that special position creates non-Taylor syzygies at constant size. A generic statement cannot exclude them.

Conjecture (square tops in degree four). For every \(n\ge7\), generic forms, and \(M\) below the degree-4 fill point, \(\operatorname{rank}\Phi_4=T_M\), and \(\ker\Phi_4\) is spanned by the Frobenius and Koszul generators. The proof above reduces each \((n,M)\) to one specialization. A proof for all \(n\) would need specializations whose rank is computable in general. The orbit family is equivariant under the shift group when \(M\) is the whole group, of order \(n(n+1)\), prime to 3 when \(3\nmid n(n+1)\). But the fill point lies below the whole group, so partial orbits, which carry no equivariance, are what matter.

Assessment and next step

Since the pencil review, the gluing line has produced three results:

  • isolated members are harmless;
  • coherent rewriting is limited to grid up-sets;
  • generic square tops are Taylor-local in degree 4 at \(n=7\).

All three are local or generic. The goal needs compatibility for adversarial inventories, which have special-position configurations. No mechanism for that is in view. That is a line producing special cases without moving its general implication, so the next cycle is a route review.

Next step. On odd-prime-clause-transfer: a route review of the gluing line. State its general claim, and what the goal needs for adversarial inventories. Attempt a falsification: an adversarial square-top family in special position below the fill point that loses Taylor locality in degree 4 while PHP stays unrefuted, so that hardness there must come from defect vanishing. Then weigh the gluing line against the recorded alternatives and propose the next research on the highest-risk item.

Verification gate.

  • Re-read: the degree-four spread entry's claim and its script phi4.py, whose a4lib machinery function_phi4.py reuses, and the syzygies-as-Tor proposition.
  • Claim searches: semi-regular, square tops and specialization. They found the recorded degree-four count and the semi-regularity conjecture relative to the base (conj:semi-regular-relative-to-base), both cited.
  • Checks: the prefix-rank kernel was self-tested against the recorded elimination.
  • Fresh-context review: the reviewer confirmed the proof, the numbers, the scripts, the prefix ordering and the C kernel. It required the following changes, all adopted:
    • "through the fill point" corrected to "below";
    • the \(n=6\) and function-form statements weakened to what samples show;
    • the Tor reading justified for \(A\);
    • a letter-coded name replaced by the claim ID.

The changes weaken claims, so no further pass was made.

Route review: the gluing line localizes everything except compatibility, and adversarial inventories defeat syzygy locality at constant size

23 September 2026 · Route review · The gluing line on odd-prime-clause-transfer. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The generic square-tops entry judged the gluing line to be producing local or generic results while the goal needs adversarial ones. It asked for this review.

General statement. The line's claim is thm:glued-product-constraints: hardness for any number of product constraints follows from local corrections and generation of the top syzygies on members that have them. Its recorded falsifications are obs:pencil-selector-syzygy and lem:member-pinning. Together they show that syzygy locality fails for satisfiable, unrefuted inventories at constant size.

The line's claim and what the goal needs

The line shows the following:

  • Local hardness. Coherent product systems on jointly full robust forms complete at every degree.
  • Exact gluing. A global correction exists exactly when the defects vanish on every top syzygy. Modulo the tops' Taylor syzygies, those syzygies form \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(A/J,G)\).
  • Members. Any satisfiable member is harmless on its own.

The goal needs this for the inventory compiled from an arbitrary polynomial-size refutation, at polylogarithmic \(B\), and in the window. Such an inventory has polynomially many forms, far more than \(N^2\), and they are in whatever position the refutation chooses.

Falsification

The pencil already gives the falsification. Four selectors on a pencil at \(p=3\), with forbidden lines not concurrent, form a satisfiable member. By member pinning it is not refuted on robust boards. Yet by the pencil syzygy it has a non-Taylor syzygy in degree 2. So Taylor locality is not necessary for hardness, and an adversary can break it with four constraints. By contrast, generic square tops at \(n=7\) are Taylor-local in degree 4 below the fill point. So locality is a property of general position, which the goal's inventories need not have.

The pencil also shows what replaces locality. Its four constraints sum to an affine polynomial \(\lambda\), a degree fall from 2 to 1. The defect pairing on the pencil syzygy vanishes only if the global functional already respects \(\lambda\). An adversarial inventory can chain such falls. A derived affine consequence of one member lies in new pencils with other members' forms, and so on. This cascade is how PC refutes, and controlling it is the lower bound itself. The gluing formalism locates the cascade exactly, in the defect pairing on non-Taylor syzygies, but it does not control it.

Assessment of the gluing line

The line has turned the batched mechanism into a precise local-to-global statement. Every local ingredient is proved at every degree, and the global obstruction is identified as a Tor group. Generic evidence supports vanishing of that obstruction below the semi-regular crossing. For the goal, the line faces three limits:

  • Its only sufficient condition for compatibility, Tor vanishing, fails for adversarial inventories at constant size.
  • The replacement condition, defect vanishing, is equivalent to hardness of the cascade of local falls, and no mechanism is recorded for it.
  • The component version needs closure under falls. The recorded special-position cores are large in small samples at high density.

So the line is weak as a route to the goal in its current form. It is strong as a framework: whatever mechanism controls the cascade will enter as defect vanishing on span-supported syzygies.

Next step: test whether falls are local

One named general hypothesis would let the line proceed.

Local-fall hypothesis. Below the semi-regular crossing, every degree fall of a selector inventory at degree \(D\) is generated by the bounded-span consequences of its span-closed members. These are the consequences that bounded-span equivalence derives inside each member.

If it holds, the members' local closures are the whole cascade below the crossing. Gluing then applies to the closed inventory, with local corrections from member pinning and the product-constraints theorem. If it fails, some fall is global, and the line needs a new idea there.

On odd-prime-clause-transfer: test the hypothesis with the recorded fast closure driver and its degree split, at \(n=6\), \(D=3\). Use inventories of random selectors with planted satisfiable pencils. Each pencil's four constraints sum to its affine fall \(\lambda\), whose multiples enter the closure below the top degree. The prediction is additivity. The degree split, low part and top part, equals the recorded no-fall split for the random selectors (\(280+M\) low, \(4291+34M\) top), plus, for each pencil, the change in split that the base plus that pencil alone produces, computed on its own.

  • The prediction is exact and falsifiable below the crossing \(M=76\).
  • The smallest nonvacuous case is one pencil among random selectors.
  • A cascade shows up as a low part larger than the additive prediction, before the crossing.

Count first: each closure at \(n=6\), \(D=3\) took about a minute, and this needs a handful of \(M\) values. Before running, check that the driver's elimination is a compiled kernel and computes every prefix in one incremental pass, as the new compiled-kernel rule requires. The step ends with the measured split against the prediction.

Verification gate. A review. It re-read the pencil review, member pinning, the syzygies-as-Tor proposition, the generic square-tops proposition, and the recorded selector thresholds with their degree split. It adds no mathematical claim, so no reviewer pass was made beyond those of the cited entries.

A satisfiable pencil is an affine equation plus a selector at degree 3, and planted pencils show almost no global fall before refutation

23 September 2026 · Working proof, conjecture and finite check · Selector inventories with planted pencils, \(p=3\), \(n=6\), \(D=3\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The gluing-line review found that adversarial inventories break syzygy locality with four constraints, a pencil. It asked whether the degree falls such configurations create stay local, or cascade before the semi-regular crossing. The cycle ends with the measured degree split of planted-pencil inventories against an additive prediction.

General statement. lem:pencil-reduction: at \(p=3\), the four selectors of a satisfiable pencil and the pair consisting of one affine equation and one selector on a transversal form derive each other at PC degree 3, for any affine forms. conj:local-falls: below the semi-regular crossing of the inventory with each span-closed member replaced by its local reduction, a selector inventory's low-degree closure never exceeds the base's and those members' own, and refutation comes within a few constraints of that crossing. The finite check is ex:planted-pencil-thresholds.

The pencil reduction

Lemma (pencil reduction). Over \(\mathbb F_3\), work in \(\mathbb F_3[y_1,y_2]\) and put \(L_1=y_1\), \(L_2=y_2\). Take \(L_3=L_1+L_2+c_3\) and \(L_4=L_1-L_2+c_4\) with \((c_3,c_4)\ne(0,0)\), and the selectors \(C_v=1-L_v^2\). Put \(\lambda=\sum_vC_v\). Then:

  1. \(\lambda=1-c_3^2-c_4^2+(c_3+c_4)y_1+(c_3-c_4)y_2\) is a nonconstant affine polynomial.
  2. The common zero set \(P\subseteq\mathbb F_3^2\) of the four selector polynomials has exactly two points, both on \(\lambda=0\). At least one \(\tau\in\{y_1,y_2\}\) is not parallel to \(\lambda\), and any such \(\tau\) takes different values at the two points. Let \(t\) be the third value.
  3. The two systems \(\{C_1,\dots,C_4\}\) and \(\{\lambda,\chi_t(\tau)\}\), with \(\chi_t(\tau)=1-(\tau-t)^2\), derive each other at PC degree at most 3. So, over any base, they have the same PC closure at every degree \(D\ge3\). All identities are polynomial identities in \(y\), so they hold after substituting any affine forms \(L_1,L_2\) in any variables. No independence of \(L_1,L_2\) is needed; if they are dependent, \(\lambda\) may become constant after substitution, and the reduced system says so.

Proof.

  1. Expanding, \(\sum_vL_v^2=3L_1^2+3L_2^2+2(c_3+c_4)L_1+2(c_3-c_4)L_2+c_3^2+c_4^2\). Since \(3=0\) and \(4=1\), this gives the formula for \(\lambda\). The linear part vanishes only if \(c_3+c_4=c_3-c_4=0\), which forces \(c_3=c_4=0\).
  2. This is the recorded classification of pencil solution sets: all 72 satisfiable choices of four forbidden values give two points (pencil members). Each \(C_v\) vanishes on \(P\), so \(\lambda\) does too. Since \(\lambda\) is nonconstant, at least one of \(y_1,y_2\) is not parallel to it. Any \(\tau\) not parallel to \(\lambda\) restricts to a bijection from the line \(\lambda=0\), which contains \(P\), onto \(\mathbb F_3\). So it separates the two points.
  3. Use \((\lambda,\tau)\) as affine coordinates on the pencil. Each \(C_w\) is a polynomial \(F_w(\lambda,\tau)\) of degree at most 2. Exactly, \(F_w(\lambda,\tau)-F_w(0,\tau)=\lambda h_w\) with \(\deg h_w\le1\). The polynomial \(F_w(0,\tau)\) has degree at most 2 and vanishes at the two \(\tau\)-values \(t\pm1\) of \(P\). So it equals \(\kappa_w(\tau-t-1)(\tau-t+1)=-\kappa_w\chi_t(\tau)\). Hence \(C_w=h_w\lambda-\kappa_w\chi_t(\tau)\) as polynomials, and each \(C_w\) is derived from \(\{\lambda,\chi_t(\tau)\}\) at degree 2. Conversely, \(\lambda=\sum_vC_v\) needs no multiplication. If every \(\kappa_w\) were zero, each \(C_w\) would be a multiple of \(\lambda\), and \(P\) would be the whole line \(\lambda=0\), of three points. So some \(\kappa_w\ne0\), and \(\chi_t(\tau)=\kappa_w^{-1}(h_w\sum_vC_v-C_w)\) is derived at degree 3. All identities are in \(\mathbb F_3[y_1,y_2]\). \(\square\)

So at \(D\ge3\) a satisfiable pencil is a coherent product system on the two forms \(\lambda,\tau\): one affine equation and one selector. This lowers the degree of the recorded bounded-span equivalence from 6 to 3 for pencils. The exact check pencil_equivalence.py compared the two degree-3 closures at \(n=6\) for 3 seeds and all 8 offsets \((c_3,c_4)\), and found them equal in all 24 cases.

Planted pencils among random selectors

local_falls.py computes the degree-3 closure of weak unary \(\mathrm{PHP}^7_6\) plus \(k\) planted satisfiable pencils, then the first \(M\) selectors of the recorded random sequence. It reports the closure's low part (degree below 3) and top part (degree 3) at every \(M\). The prediction is additive: the recorded no-fall split for the random selectors, \(280+M\) low and \(4291+34M\) top, plus each pencil's own change, measured alone as \(+37\) low and \(+494\) top.

The elimination is a new compiled kernel, gf3_basis.c. It keeps a persistent fully reduced basis over \(\mathbb F_3\), and each product row is inserted once, so one closure per inventory gives every checkpoint. A closure took 1 to 2 s, against about a minute for the recorded driver, and it reproduced the recorded split for the base and for 20 random selectors.

Results, for 3 pencil seeds and \(k=0,\dots,7\), sampled at \(M=0,5,10,15\) and then in steps of 1 from 20 to 76:

  • Almost no global fall. The low part never exceeds the additive prediction without overlaps before refutation. It equals the prediction for \(k\le1\). For \(k\ge2\) it falls short, by 0 to 13, because the pencils' own contributions overlap. One event goes beyond the overlaps. At seed 2, \(k=2\), \(M=48\), the low part rises by 2 instead of 1, from 400 to 402, and the top part by 60 instead of 32. That is a fall of one dimension beyond the members' own, two steps before refutation at \(M=50\).
  • Refutation at the capacity crossing. For \(k\le4\), until the event above, the top part grows by \(34-k\) per random selector. One interpretation, not verified, is that each pencil's affine form \(\lambda\) meets each selector in one Koszul overlap. The least refuted \(M\) equals the first \(M\) at which the extrapolated top part exceeds the 6860 degree-3 columns. This is exact in 14 of the 15 cases with \(k\le4\), where \(M\) is sampled in steps of 1. The values are \(76,63,51,39,27\), with seed 3 at \(k=4\) giving 28, as its own extrapolation predicts. The exception is seed 2 at \(k=2\), refuted at 50 against 51, after the event above. For \(k=5,6\), refutation lies in the sampled interval that contains the prediction.
  • Pencils behave as affine equations. Seven pencils alone are refuted at degree 3. This matches the recorded least refuted number of random affine equations at \(n=6\), \(D=3\), which is 7. By the lemma, seven pencils are seven affine equations plus seven selectors.

Conjecture (local falls). Take a selector inventory on the weak unary base at \(p=3\) and degree \(D\). Replace each span-closed member by its local reduction, as the pencil lemma does for pencils. Then, below the semi-regular crossing of the reduced inventory, the closure's degree-\(<D\) part never exceeds the sum of the base's and the members' own, and refutation occurs within a bounded number of constraints of the crossing. The exact form, with equality less overlaps, fails in one run by one dimension two steps before refutation. The evidence is the check above: one board size, one degree and planted pencils, where members are known in advance. Adversarial inventories may hide members of larger span, whose reductions are not coherent (the up-set limit).

What this means for the route

At these sizes the falls an adversary can plant with pencils stay local. Each pencil acts as an affine equation plus one selector, and refutation comes when the reduced inventory's count fills the top degree, give or take a step, with one fall of a single dimension just before it. That is the picture the gluing line needs: close each member locally, then glue below the crossing. The next obligation is the one the review named: members of larger span, and members hidden in the inventory rather than planted. The first is a three-dimensional span whose solution set is not a grid up-set for any basis of the span, since it has no coherent reduction.

Next step. On odd-prime-clause-transfer, at \(p=3\): find the reduction of a three-dimensional member whose allowed set is not a grid up-set. Take selectors on the 13 directions of a three-dimensional span with an allowed set that is not a grid up-set for any basis of the span. Decide whether their degree-\(D\) closure, for some small \(D\), equals that of a coherent system on derived forms, as for pencils. If it does not, find what extra it derives. The planted-member closure test gives the evidence: an exact comparison of closures at \(n=6\), \(D=3\) and 4, with the kernel above. A proof, or a counterexample to coherent reduction, ends the step.

Verification gate.

  • Re-read: the gluing-line review, the pencil-members classification, bounded-span equivalence, and the recorded selector thresholds with their degree split.
  • Checks: the closure kernel reproduced the recorded split. The pencil reduction was checked in all 24 cases.
  • Fresh-context review: the reviewer confirmed the lemma's identities, the degrees and the closure kernel's correctness argument, a downward induction on insertion order. It required the following changes, all adopted:
    • the lemma stated in \(\mathbb F_3[y]\), with \(P\) as a zero set and the transversality argument completed;
    • the case counts corrected to the actual sampling grid;
    • the one fall beyond the members' own reported, at seed 2, \(k=2\), \(M=48\), and the conjecture weakened accordingly;
    • the Koszul-overlap reading of the slope labelled an interpretation;
    • the route paragraph and the up-set quantifier corrected.

The changes weaken or correct claims, so no further pass was made.

A member with no coherent reduction also falls only locally: four selectors on a three-dimensional span, planted among random selectors

23 September 2026 · Finite check · Selector members on three-dimensional spans, \(p=3\), \(n=6\), \(D=3\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The local-falls entry reduced pencils to coherent systems and found their falls local. It asked about members whose allowed set is not a grid up-set for any basis of their span, which have no coherent reduction. Do their falls also stay local, or does the missing reduction show up as a global fall? The cycle ends with the smallest such member measured against the additive prediction.

General statement. conj:local-falls: below the semi-regular crossing, a selector inventory's low-degree closure never exceeds the base's and its members' own, with refutation near the crossing. This cycle tests it on members outside the coherent class, with the finite checks ex:describable-sets-f3-cubed and ex:plane-member-falls.

The smallest member without a coherent reduction

describable.c, a C enumeration, lists every subset of \(\mathbb F_3^3\) that is a grid up-set for some basis and coordinatewise orders. It uses 234 bases, 216 orders and 980 grid up-sets. 13,905,349 of the 134,217,727 nonempty subsets are describable. The earlier bound of 49,533,120 was only the product of the numbers of bases, orders and up-sets, which counts many sets repeatedly. The enumeration then scans every selector arrangement with at most one forbidden plane per direction, \(4^{13}\) of them, and records which have a nonempty allowed set that is not describable. It ran in 3 s.

  • With at most 3 planes, every allowed set is describable.
  • With exactly 4 planes, 18,954 arrangements have non-describable allowed sets, of sizes 5 and 6.
  • With 5 or more planes, every nonempty allowed set is describable.

An example of size 5: forbid \(A=0\), \(A+C=0\), \(B=1\) and \(B+C=0\) for coordinates \(A,B,C\). The four forms span three dimensions, and they are two pairs linked through \(C\).

Planted among random selectors

plane_falls.py repeats the local-falls design with this member. It uses random affine forms \(A,B,C\) for each copy, \(k=0,1,2,3,4,6,8\) copies, and then the recorded random selector sequence at \(n=6\), \(D=3\). The closures use the incremental kernel gf3_basis.c. There were 2 member seeds, with \(M\) sampled at \(0,5,10,15,20\) and then in steps of 1 up to 76: the option --Ms 0,5,10,15,20,21,...,76.

  • Own contribution. Alone, a member adds \(+5\) to the low part and \(+167\) to the top part. Four random selectors would add \(+4\) and \(+136\). So the member has one extra low dimension, a local fall, and 31 extra top dimensions.
  • No global fall. For every \(k\) and \(M\) before refutation, the low part equals the additive prediction exactly, with excess 0. So is the top part: the random selectors add 34 each, with no overlap with the members.
  • Refutation at the capacity crossing. The least refuted \(M\) is 76, 71, 66, 61, 56, 47 and 37 for \(k=0,1,2,3,4,6,8\). That is exactly the first \(M\) with \(4291+167k+34M>6860\), in all 14 cases.

The two seeds gave identical counts, as the structural counts suggest.

What this means

At \(n=6\), \(D=3\), this one member, the size-5 arrangement, behaves like a coherent one. Its falls are its own, it adds to the count additively, and refutation comes when the count fills the top degree. The hypothesis this supports is that the coherent reduction is a proof device, not what the local-fall law needs. The size-6 arrangement and the other four-plane arrangements were not planted, and both seeds gave identical counts. With the pencil runs, this is evidence for the local-fall conjecture from two member types at one board size and one degree, with planted rather than hidden members. The one recorded deviation stays that of the local-falls entry, a single dimension at one pencil run.

Next step. On odd-prime-clause-transfer: prove additivity for members on independent spans. Take members \(S_1,S_2\), polynomial constraints in forms of spans \(W_1,W_2\), with \(W_1\cap W_2=0\). Suppose \(W_1\oplus W_2\) has a basis independent modulo constants on every row on a board robust as in the product-constraints theorem. Claim: the degree-\(<D\) part of the PC closure of the base plus \(S_1\cup S_2\) is the subspace sum of the degree-\(<D\) parts for the base plus \(S_1\) and the base plus \(S_2\). Their intersection is the base's own degree-\(<D\) part, so the increments over the base add, as the runs measured. The planned proof has three steps, none of them proved yet:

  1. the short-generation theorem makes \(G\) free, through \(D\), over the truncated algebra of \(W_1\oplus W_2\), by the syzygies-as-Tor proposition's part 2;
  2. over a free module, the syzygies of \(J_1+J_2\), with \(J_i\) in disjoint variables, come from those of \(J_1\), of \(J_2\), and Koszul pairs, by Künneth;
  3. the gluing lemma then adds no fall beyond the members'.

The step ends with that lemma, or with the gap between top-algebra freeness and the closure's low part.

Verification gate.

  • Re-read: the local-falls entry, the coherent-sets proposition and its count, and the recorded selector split.
  • Checks: the planted-member closures reproduce the recorded base and random splits.
  • Fresh-context review: the reviewer confirmed the enumeration logic, the example, and every number against the result files. It required the following changes, all adopted:

    • the conclusions restricted to this member at these sizes;
    • an unchecked causal clause dropped;
    • the product bound described for what it is;
    • the next step's claim made precise, with its steps marked as unproved.

A stable union has additive closures: coherent members on a jointly full union add degree by degree

23 September 2026 · Working proofs · PC closures of unions of constraint systems; coherent members, \(p=3\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The plane-members entry measured exact additivity of planted members' closures below the crossing. It asked for a proof in the first general case, members on independent spans. The cycle ends with a lemma, or with the gap between top-algebra freeness and the closure's low part.

General statement. lem:closure-additivity: for any base and constraint systems \(F_1,F_2\), suppose the union has PC closure equal to its NS span at every degree through \(D\), and every NS functional of the union through a degree \(k\le D\) extends through \(D\). Then the union has no fall, and its closures, including their parts of each lower degree, are the sums of the members' closures. cor:coherent-member-additivity: this holds for any two coherent product systems whose union is coherent on jointly full robust forms. That includes members on independent spans whose sum is jointly full and robust for the combined number of forms.

Definitions

Work in the free polynomial ring \(\mathbb F[x]\), with Booleanity and the other field axioms inside the base \(\Gamma\), as in the recorded functional base. Write \(P_{\le d}\) for polynomials of degree at most \(d\), so that \(\deg(mf)=\deg m+\deg f\).

  • For a set \(F\) of polynomials, \(\mathrm{NS}_d(F)\) is the span of all products \(mf\) with \(f\in\Gamma\cup F\), \(m\) a monomial, and \(\deg(mf)\le d\).
  • \(\mathrm{PC}_d(F)\) is the smallest subspace of \(P_{\le d}\) that contains \(\Gamma\cup F\) in degree at most \(d\) and is closed under multiplication by a variable whenever the result has degree at most \(d\).

Always \(\mathrm{NS}_d(F)\subseteq\mathrm{PC}_d(F)\), both are monotone in \(F\), and \(\mathrm{NS}_d(F_1\cup F_2)=\mathrm{NS}_d(F_1)+\mathrm{NS}_d(F_2)\), since every generator of the left side is a generator of one summand.

Extension implies stability. Suppose every NS functional through \(k\) extends through \(D\). That is, every linear functional on \(P_{\le k}\) vanishing on \(\mathrm{NS}_k\) is the restriction of one on \(P_{\le D}\) vanishing on \(\mathrm{NS}_D\). Then \(\mathrm{NS}_D\cap P_{\le k}=\mathrm{NS}_k\).

The inclusion \(\supseteq\) is clear. If \(g\in\mathrm{NS}_D\cap P_{\le k}\) were not in \(\mathrm{NS}_k\), some functional on \(P_{\le k}\) would vanish on \(\mathrm{NS}_k\) but not at \(g\). Its extension would vanish on \(\mathrm{NS}_D\ni g\), a contradiction.

The additivity lemma

Lemma (closure additivity). Let \(F=F_1\cup F_2\) and suppose, for every \(d\le D\):

  • (i) \(\mathrm{PC}_d(F)=\mathrm{NS}_d(F)\);
  • (ii) every NS functional for \(\Gamma+F\) through \(d\) extends through \(D\).

Then, for every \(d\le D\):

  1. \(\mathrm{PC}_d(F)=\mathrm{PC}_d(F_1)+\mathrm{PC}_d(F_2)\);
  2. \(\mathrm{PC}_D(F)\cap P_{\le d}=\mathrm{PC}_d(F_1)+\mathrm{PC}_d(F_2)=\bigl(\mathrm{PC}_D(F_1)\cap P_{\le d}\bigr)+\bigl(\mathrm{PC}_D(F_2)\cap P_{\le d}\bigr)\).

In particular, the union has no fall at all: its filtration is stable, \(\mathrm{PC}_D(F)\cap P_{\le d}=\mathrm{PC}_d(F)\). Every fall of a member must then already lie in \(\mathrm{PC}_d(F_1)+\mathrm{PC}_d(F_2)\). A member with a fall not absorbed there violates the hypotheses. The content of the lemma is in (i) and (ii): a stable union has additive closures. Part 1 uses only (i) at \(d\). Part 2 uses (i) at \(d\) and at \(D\), and (ii) at \(d\).

Proof.

  1. \(\mathrm{PC}_d(F)=\mathrm{NS}_d(F)=\mathrm{NS}_d(F_1)+\mathrm{NS}_d(F_2)\subseteq\mathrm{PC}_d(F_1)+\mathrm{PC}_d(F_2)\subseteq\mathrm{PC}_d(F)\), by (i), additivity of NS spans, and monotonicity.
  2. By (i) and the extension-implies-stability argument, \(\mathrm{PC}_D(F)\cap P_{\le d}=\mathrm{NS}_D(F)\cap P_{\le d}=\mathrm{NS}_d(F)=\mathrm{PC}_d(F)\). By part 1 this is \(\mathrm{PC}_d(F_1)+\mathrm{PC}_d(F_2)\). This sum lies in \(\bigl(\mathrm{PC}_D(F_1)\cap P_{\le d}\bigr)+\bigl(\mathrm{PC}_D(F_2)\cap P_{\le d}\bigr)\), since \(\mathrm{PC}_d(F_i)\subseteq\mathrm{PC}_D(F_i)\) and has degree at most \(d\). That in turn lies in \(\mathrm{PC}_D(F)\cap P_{\le d}\), by monotonicity. So all three are equal. \(\square\)

Hypotheses (i) and (ii) are on the union only. The recorded no-fall criterion (lem:no-fall-criterion) is related. There, stability of the filtration makes the normal-form PC closure equal to the NS-type span.

It gives a sum of subspaces, not additivity of dimensions over the base. The increments over \(\mathrm{PC}(\emptyset)\) add exactly when \(\mathrm{PC}_d(F_1)\cap\mathrm{PC}_d(F_2)=\mathrm{PC}_d(\emptyset)\). The runs measured that equality, and the lemma does not give it.

Coherent members

Corollary (coherent member additivity). Over \(\mathbb F_3\) on the functional base, let \(\mathcal C_1,\mathcal C_2\) be product constraint systems whose union is pairwise coherent, on forms jointly independent modulo constants on every row. Suppose the board meets the coherent product-constraints corollary's rows and robustness for the union's \(r\) forms and some \(B\). Then parts 1 and 2 of the lemma hold for \(F_i=\mathcal C_i\), for every \(d\le D=B\).

This covers members on independent spans \(W_1\cap W_2=0\), provided the \(r_1+r_2\) forms together are jointly independent modulo constants on every row and the board meets the rows and robustness for \(r_1+r_2\) forms. The two members then share no form, so coherence across them holds vacuously, and the union is coherent as soon as each member is. Every constraint is nontrivial, with \(h=\min|b_C|\ge1\), as the theorem requires.

Proof. The corollary gives, for the union, that \(\mathrm{PC}_B=\mathrm{NS}_B\), and that every NS functional through \(k\le B\) extends through \(B\), which is (ii). For \(d\le B\), (i) follows: \(\mathrm{PC}_d\subseteq\mathrm{PC}_B\cap P_{\le d}=\mathrm{NS}_B\cap P_{\le d}=\mathrm{NS}_d\subseteq\mathrm{PC}_d\), using the extension-implies-stability argument. \(\square\)

What this settles and what it does not

  • For coherent members, the local-fall law holds at every degree through \(B\), on a jointly full robust union. Their falls are their own, which for coherent systems means none, since the corollary says each has no fall.
  • For members with their own falls, such as the plane member measured last cycle with one extra low dimension, the lemma needs (i) and (ii) for the union, and no recorded theorem gives them. The natural route is to close each member, replacing \(F_i\) by generators of \(\mathrm{PC}_D(F_i)\), and then show (i) and (ii) for the union of the closed members. That is the local-fall conjecture restated through the lemma, not a proof of it.
  • Joint fullness of the union caps the total number of forms at about \(\sqrt N/B\), as the product-constraints entry recorded. The goal's inventories exceed that. Beyond it, (i) and (ii) for the union are the batched mechanism itself.

Next step. On odd-prime-clause-transfer: find a sufficient condition for (i) and (ii) for the union of closed members when the union is not jointly full. (i) and (ii) are needed only after closing the members. The data support the local-fall target, not (i) and (ii) directly. Below the capacity crossing, planted members and random selectors showed exact additivity of the increments, far beyond joint fullness: 76 selectors against \(\dim G_1=35\). The candidate mechanism is the one the gluing entry made exact: an NS functional for the union extends exactly when the defects vanish on its top syzygies. By the syzygies-as-Tor proposition, those syzygies are Taylor-generated when \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(A/J,G)\) vanishes. So the step is to prove, or refute by construction, \(\operatorname{Tor}_1\) vanishing for square tops in general position below the fill point at \(n=7\). The generic-square-tops proposition already gives degree 4. The next case is degree 5, at \(n=7\), with the prefix-rank kernel.

Verification gate.

  • Re-read: the coherent product-constraints corollary's statement (PC equals NS; NS functionals extend) and the plane-members data.
  • Claim search: additivity, union of closures, and NS span. It found the recorded stable-filtration statements, cited as the corollary's.
  • Fresh-context review: the reviewer confirmed the lemma's inclusions and the duality argument. It required the following changes, all adopted:
    • the free polynomial ring fixed as the setting, so that NS lies inside PC;
    • the lemma framed as "a stable union has additive closures", with the hypotheses used by each part stated;
    • PC equal to NS at every lower degree derived from the corollary's wording;
    • the independent-spans case restated with joint fullness for the combined forms;
    • an unsupported clause on pencils dropped;
    • the evidence claim in the next step corrected.

The changes weaken or restrict claims, so no further pass was made.

The local-fall law holds at a second board size: n = 7, with an all-C closure

23 September 2026 · Finite check · Planted pencils and plane members at \(n=7\), \(D=3\), \(p=3\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The additivity entry proposed extending the generic square-top result to degree 5 at \(n=7\). The count this entry did first shows that step is nearly vacuous. The square-top series for the weak base at \(n=7\) is \((1,48,924,8688,34950,21792,28)\), and its degree-5 coefficient is already negative at \(M=3\), so degree 5 tests only \(M\le2\). It was replaced by a test that can fail at the second reachable board size: does the local-fall law of the local-falls and plane-members entries hold at \(n=7\), \(D=3\)?

General statement. conj:local-falls: below the semi-regular crossing, a selector inventory's low-degree closure never exceeds the base's and its members' own, and refutation comes within a few constraints of that crossing. The finite check is ex:local-falls-n7.

Results

The board has 19,321 columns, 17,920 of them of degree 3. The recorded random selector sequence is refuted at \(M=185\), as recorded, and each selector adds 47 to the top part. The design matches the earlier entries: \(k=1,2,4,8\) planted pencils or plane members, 2 seeds each, with \(M\) sampled at \(0,20,\dots,120\) and then in steps of 1 from 140 to 186.

  • No global fall. For pencils, the low part never exceeds the additive prediction. The excess is \(0,-1,-6,-28\) for \(k=1,2,4,8\), the negative values being overlaps between pencils. For plane members the excess is exactly 0 throughout.
  • Plane members: refutation at the additive capacity crossing. The least refuted \(M\) is 180, 175, 166 and 146 for \(k=1,2,4,8\). That is exactly the first \(M\) at which the random series' top part plus the members' own exceeds 17,920, in all 8 cases.
  • Pencils: refutation at the crossing of their own slope. The top part grows by \(47-k\) per selector, as at \(n=6\), where it was read as one overlap of each pencil's affine form with each selector. The least refuted \(M\) is 168, 152, 120 and 60. Extrapolating each series' own top part to 17,920 gives 168, 152, 119 and 59: exact for \(k=1,2\), and one step early for \(k=4,8\), in both seeds.

Both seeds gave identical counts. With the \(n=6\) entries, the law now holds at two board sizes for both member types, with one recorded deviation of one dimension.

The computation, redone without waste

The first \(n=7\) runs used the earlier driver. It ran the elimination in C, but it formed products in Python. It also restarted the base closure and the random series for every series. On the user's objection, it was replaced before the analysis by gf3_closure.c. That kernel runs the whole closure loop in C, including table-driven products with GF(3) accumulation, and it was checked against the earlier machinery at \(n=5\). It is orchestrated by local_falls3.py, which computes the base closure and the random series once and copies them for every member type, seed and \(k\). All four series took 260 s, against about 560 s for the earlier four runs, and gave identical counts. The Python setup of the monomial space, 16 s, is the remaining overhead.

Next step. On odd-prime-clause-transfer: prove the one-overlap law for a pencil and a selector. Take a satisfiable pencil on forms \(\ell,\ell'\) and one selector on a third form \(L\), with \(\ell,\ell',L\) jointly full and robust. Show that the degree-3 top part of their joint closure is the sum of the separate top parts minus exactly one, the Koszul overlap of the pencil's affine form with \(L^2\). The route:

  1. the pencil reduction makes the system coherent on \(\lambda,\tau,L\);
  2. the coherent product-constraints corollary makes PC equal NS;
  3. the top of the NS span in degree 3 is then computed by Taylor syzygies over a free module, which follows from the short-generation theorem for three forms.

This would explain the measured slope \(47-k\) locally. The step ends with that lemma, or with the term that breaks it.

  • Re-read: the local-falls and plane-members entries and their prediction rules.
