Route review: the local-fall line is supported and proved in the jointly full case; its core is an interpolation theorem for the matching complex

23 September 2026 · Route review · The local-fall and gluing line on odd-prime-clause-transfer. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The n = 7 entry proposed a one-overlap lemma for a pencil and a selector. That lemma would be proved on a jointly full triple of forms. It would explain one measured slope, but it would not move the line's general implication. By the route-check rule that makes this cycle a review.

General statement. The line's claim is conj:local-falls, which is proved for coherent members on a jointly full union as cor:coherent-member-additivity. Its missing general implication is stability of the union beyond joint fullness. For random tops that is the semi-regularity conjecture relative to the base (conj:semi-regular-relative-to-base).

What the line has established

  • Local. Members are harmless alone (member pinning). Pencils reduce to an affine equation plus a selector at degree 3. Closures of a stable union add.
  • Measured. At \(n=6\) and \(n=7\), \(D=3\), planted members of two kinds, with and without a coherent reduction, fall only locally. Refutation comes at the top-degree capacity crossing of the reduced count, with one deviation of one dimension.
  • Missing. The union's stability, meaning PC equal to NS with extendable functionals, once the forms exceed joint fullness, about \(\sqrt N/B\) of them. Every measured inventory is far beyond that. Nothing proves stability there, even for random tops.

Falsification attempt

The sharpest recorded prediction is the capacity law. For \(M\) random selectors, refutation at degree 3 comes exactly at \(\lceil\gamma_3/(\gamma_1-1)\rceil\), which is 76, 185 and 370 at \(n=6,7,8\). Planted members shift it additively. If the union had a global fall of lower order, refutation would come earlier than the count. It never has, at two board sizes and several member types. So the law has survived the tests that could break it at reachable sizes. What it lacks is a mechanism.

The core, read as interpolation

In degree 3 the capacity law is a maximal-rank statement. For \(M\) generic linear forms, the conditions \(D_{\ell_j}^2w=0\) on the matching complex \(K_3\) have the expected codimension \(\min(\gamma_3,M(\gamma_1-1))\). The \(-1\) comes from the Frobenius syzygy of each square. Dually, the degree-3 part of the ideal of squares \(\ell_j^2\) in the top algebra has the expected dimension. In a polynomial ring the same statement is classical. By apolarity (Emsalem–Iarrobino), \((\ell^2)^\perp\) in degree 3 consists of the cubics singular at the point \([\ell]\). So the statement is the Alexander–Hirschowitz theorem for double points on cubics: generic double points impose independent conditions, with a known list of exceptions. Its proof is a degeneration, the Horace method. One specializes some points onto a hyperplane and runs a residual exact sequence, by induction on dimension and degree. The matching complex has a natural analogue of a hyperplane section: restriction to the board with one row or one hole removed. The recorded peeling-locality and short-generation arguments already induct over rows this way.

Assessment of the line. The local theory is complete. The empirical law is sharp and has survived falsification at two sizes. The missing piece is now named in classical terms: an interpolation theorem, double-point independence for generic forms on the matching complex, first in degree 3. Two cautions:

  • Such a theorem covers random tops, not adversarial ones. The local-fall law for planted members would still need the gluing of members, the additivity lemma, with this theorem supplying the union's stability.
  • Degree 3 is the first rung. The goal needs polylogarithmic degree.

So the line is promising as a structural reduction and uncertain as a route to the goal.

Next step. On odd-prime-clause-transfer: read the Horace method, in the Alexander–Hirschowitz proof as simplified by Brambilla and Ottaviani, to find the degeneration step. Then attempt a Horace-type induction for the matching complex in degree 3. Specialize some of the forms to vanish on one row. Use the exact sequence relating \(K_3\) of the board to \(K_3\) and \(K_2\) of the board without that row, through the recorded peeling decomposition. Show that the double-point conditions stay independent up to the capacity \(\min(\gamma_3,M(\gamma_1-1))\) for all \(n\) above a threshold. The recorded thresholds at \(n=6,7,8\) are the base cases and checks. The step ends with the induction step proved, or with the term that fails.

Verification gate. A review. It re-read the local-falls, plane-members, additivity and n = 7 entries, the semi-regularity conjecture and its literature note, and the recorded selector thresholds. The apolarity correspondence is standard: forms vanishing to order \(d-a+1\) at \([\ell]\) are the perpendicular of \(\ell^a\) in degree \(d\). The Alexander–Hirschowitz statement is cited from the literature, not relied on for any claim.

A row-by-row Horace identity for double-point conditions on the matching complex

23 September 2026 · Working proof · Double-point conditions \(D_\ell^2w=0\) on the functional matching complex in degree 3. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The local-fall line review read the degree-3 capacity law as an interpolation statement. For \(M\) generic forms, the double-point conditions \(D_{\ell}^2w=0\) on \(K_3\) have the expected codimension \(\min(\gamma_3,M(\gamma_1-1))\). It proposed a Horace-type induction over the board's rows. This cycle read the method and derived the matching complex's version of its central sequence. It ends with an exact identity, and with the arithmetic that decides where plain induction suffices.

General statement. lem:row-horace-identity: for any board, row \(i\) and forms \(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_M\), the double-point solution space \(Z\subseteq K_3\) satisfies \(\dim Z=\dim\ker T+\dim Z_{\mathrm{res}}-\operatorname{rank}(Z_{\mathrm{res}}\to\operatorname{coker}T)\). Here \(T\) is the trace problem on the board without row \(i\), \(Z_{\mathrm{res}}\) a residual problem, and the cokernel is taken in \(\bigoplus_\ell\ker D'_\ell|_{K'_1}\). It is the matching-complex analogue of the Castelnuovo sequence in the Horace method, with the trace's excess passed to the residual through an explicit coupling map.

The method read

Brambilla and Ottaviani, On the Alexander–Hirschowitz theorem (arXiv:math/0701409), read in its arXiv text, Sections 4 and 5. Section 4 gives the Horace lemma. For double points \(X\) and a hyperplane \(H\) containing \(u\) of them, the Castelnuovo sequence \(0\to I_{\tilde X}(d-1)\to I_X(d)\to I_{X\cap H,H}(d)\) gives \(\dim I_X(d)\le\dim I_{\tilde X}(d-1)+\dim I_{X\cap H}(d)\). Independence follows when the trace and the residual are independent and their expected dimensions have the same sign. Section 5 proves the cubic case with codimension-three subspaces instead of hyperplanes, to avoid arithmetic mismatches. The mismatched cases elsewhere need the differential Horace method. The paper is not in the repository.

The row split

Let a board have \(R\) rows and \(N\) labels, and let \(K_t\) be the arrays on injective labelings of \(t\)-sets of rows with zero ordinary marginals. Fix a row \(i\). Each zero-marginal condition concerns one row set, so \(K_t=K'_t\oplus K^{\ni i}_t\), where:

  • \(K'_t\) consists of the arrays on sets avoiding \(i\), which is the complex of the board without row \(i\);
  • \(K^{\ni i}_t\) consists of the arrays on sets containing \(i\).

For a form \(\ell\), write \(D_\ell=D'_\ell+\partial_\ell\), where \(\partial_\ell\) removes row \(i\) and \(D'_\ell\) removes the other rows. Since \(D_\ell\) maps \(K_t\) to \(K_{t-1}\) and the decomposition is by row sets:

  • \(D'_\ell\) preserves both summands, and on \(K'\) it is the operator of the smaller board;
  • \(\partial_\ell\) maps \(K^{\ni i}_t\) to \(K'_{t-1}\) and kills \(K'_t\);
  • \(\partial_\ell^2=0\).

Define:

  • \(T:K'_3\to\bigoplus_\ell K'_1\), by \(w_0\mapsto(D'^2_\ell w_0)_\ell\), the trace problem;
  • \(Z_{\mathrm{res}}=\{w_1\in K^{\ni i}_3:D'^2_\ell w_1=0\ \forall\ell\}\), the residual problem;
  • \(C:Z_{\mathrm{res}}\to\bigoplus_\ell K'_1\), by \(w_1\mapsto\bigl((\partial_\ell D'_\ell+D'_\ell\partial_\ell)w_1\bigr)_\ell\), the coupling.

Put \(Z=\{w\in K_3:D_\ell^2w=0\ \forall\ell\}\).

Lemma (row Horace identity). \(Z=\{w_0+w_1:\ w_1\in Z_{\mathrm{res}},\ Tw_0=-Cw_1\}\). Hence

\[ \dim Z=\dim\ker T+\dim Z_{\mathrm{res}}-\dim\bigl((C(Z_{\mathrm{res}})+\operatorname{im}T)/\operatorname{im}T\bigr). \]

Proof. For \(w=w_0+w_1\), expand \(D_\ell^2=(D'_\ell+\partial_\ell)^2\):

  • \(D_\ell^2w_0=D'^2_\ell w_0\in K'_1\), since \(\partial_\ell\) kills \(K'\);
  • \(D_\ell^2w_1=D'^2_\ell w_1+(\partial_\ell D'_\ell+D'_\ell\partial_\ell)w_1\), with the first term in \(K^{\ni i}_1\) and the second in \(K'_1\), since \(\partial_\ell^2=0\).

So \(D_\ell^2w=0\) for all \(\ell\) exactly when \(D'^2_\ell w_1=0\) for all \(\ell\) and \(Tw_0=-Cw_1\). The solutions are the \(w_1\in C^{-1}(\operatorname{im}T)\), each with a coset of \(\ker T\). \(\square\)

The lemma holds over any field, for any forms: it uses neither characteristic 3, nor \(D^3=0\), nor genericity.

Where the coupling lands. Over \(\mathbb F_3\), where \(D_\ell^3=0\), \(C(Z_{\mathrm{res}})\subseteq\bigoplus_\ell\ker D'_\ell|_{K'_1}\). For \(w_1\in Z_{\mathrm{res}}\), \(D_\ell^3w_1=D'^3_\ell w_1+D'_\ell Cw_1+\partial_\ell D'^2_\ell w_1\), because \(\partial_\ell Cw_1=0\) with \(Cw_1\in K'\). The left side is 0, and \(D'^2_\ell w_1=0\) kills the first and last terms, so \(D'_\ell Cw_1=0\).

Where the conditions go. Each form imposes at most \(\gamma_1-1\) conditions on \(K_3\), since \(D_\ell^2w\) lies in \(\ker D_\ell\) on \(K_1\). For a general \(w\) the trace component is not in \(\ker D'_\ell\). The relation \(D_\ell^3w=0\) couples the trace part and the residual part. Once the residual conditions hold, the count splits as \(\gamma'_1-1\) on the trace and \(N-1\) on the residual, since \(\gamma_1=R(N-1)\) and \(\gamma'_1=(R-1)(N-1)\). On the residual:

  • \(K^{\ni i}_3\) is the space of tuples \((W_a)_{a\le N}\) with \(W_a\in K_2\) of the board without row \(i\) and without label \(a\), and \(\sum_aW_a=0\);
  • each condition \(D'^2_\ell W_a=0\) is a scalar;
  • the sum over \(a\) vanishes automatically, which leaves \(N-1\) conditions per form.

The trace space and the residual space have dimensions \(\gamma'_3\) and \(\gamma_3-\gamma'_3\), with \(\gamma_t=\binom Rt\delta_t(N)\) and \(\delta_t(N)=\sum_j(-1)^j\binom tj(N)_{t-j}\).

Corollary (expected dimension from the pieces). Work over \(\mathbb F_3\), and suppose no \(\ell\) is constant modulo constants on every row of the smaller board. Then \(\dim\ker D'_\ell|_{K'_1}=\gamma'_1-1\) and \(\dim\ker D_\ell|_{K_1}=\gamma_1-1\). Suppose \(T\) has maximal rank into \(\bigoplus_\ell\ker D'_\ell|_{K'_1}\), and \(Z_{\mathrm{res}}\) has its expected dimension \(\max(\dim K^{\ni i}_3-M(N-1),0)\).

  • If \(M(\gamma'_1-1)\le\gamma'_3\), then \(Z\) has its expected dimension.
  • If \(M(\gamma'_1-1)>\gamma'_3\), then \(Z\) has its expected dimension exactly when the coupling \(Z_{\mathrm{res}}\to\operatorname{coker}T\) has maximal rank.

The first case is the Horace lemma's case (i). The second is where differential Horace is needed, made here into an explicit rank condition.

Proof. In the first case \(T\) is onto its target, which contains \(C(Z_{\mathrm{res}})\), so the correction term vanishes. The residual is not overdetermined here, because its capacity exceeds the trace's (next section). So \(\dim Z_{\mathrm{res}}=\dim K^{\ni i}_3-M(N-1)\), and the dimensions add to \(\gamma_3-M(\gamma_1-1)\). In the second case \(T\) is injective, and the identity gives \(\dim Z=\dim Z_{\mathrm{res}}-\operatorname{rank}\). Here \(\operatorname{rank}\le\min(M(\gamma'_1-1)-\gamma'_3,\dim Z_{\mathrm{res}})\), with equality exactly for maximal rank, which is what the expected dimension requires. \(\square\)

Arithmetic: why row-by-row induction with this split is not enough

Each block of three rows contributes the same dimension, so \(\gamma'_3=\frac{R-3}R\gamma_3\) and \(\gamma_3-\gamma'_3=\frac3R\gamma_3\). With \(\gamma_1=R(N-1)\) and \(\gamma'_1=(R-1)(N-1)\), two comparisons follow:

  • the trace's capacity \(\gamma'_3/(\gamma'_1-1)\) is below the total \(\gamma_3/(\gamma_1-1)\), which reduces to \(3<2R(N-1)\);
  • the residual's capacity \((\gamma_3-\gamma'_3)/(N-1)\) is above the total, which reduces to \(3R(N-1)-3>R(N-1)\).

Both hold on every nontrivial board. For the functional board with \(R=n+1\), \(N=n\), the numbers use \(\gamma_t=\binom Rt\delta_t(N)\), with \(\delta_t(N)=\sum_j(-1)^j\binom tj(N)_{t-j}\), the count of zero-marginal arrays on one \(t\)-set. That formula assumes independent marginal conditions. It fails for small \(N\) (\(\delta_3(4)=-1\)). At \(n=6\) it gives \(\gamma_3=1645\), which matches the computed \(\dim K_3\). In the table it is used only for \(n\ge6\).

So with this one-row split the crossing always falls in the corollary's second case. Every form enters both the trace and the residual, so there is no parameter like the number of points Horace puts on the hyperplane to rebalance the two. Consider an induction on the rows at a fixed \(M\) that uses only the first case. At a total capacity \(M\) it needs the smaller board nondefective at the same \(M\), which exceeds that board's own capacity. That is its second case, which the first case never proves. Splits along several rows or along labels, and the codimension-three subspaces of Brambilla and Ottaviani's cubic proof, were not examined. Everything therefore rests on two statements:

  • (B) the residual problem is nondefective. It asks for one scalar condition \(D'^2_\ell W_a=0\) per form and label \(a\), with \(\ell\) restricted to the board without row \(i\) and label \(a\), on the space of tuples \((W_a)\) constrained by \(\sum_aW_a=0\);
  • (C) in the window between the trace's capacity and the total, the coupling has maximal rank.

Scope. This is the functional matching complex, the home of the recorded local theory. The recorded selector thresholds were measured on the weak base, whose marginal conditions do not split by row sets. So the capacity law has not yet been checked on the functional board.

Next step. On odd-prime-clause-transfer: measure the three pieces on the functional board at \(n=6,7,8\). Use random forms and a compiled GF(3) elimination:

  • the rank of the full double-point map on \(K_3\), which checks the functional capacity law, of sizes \(\gamma_3=1645,5824,16044\);
  • the rank of \(T\);
  • the dimension of \(Z_{\mathrm{res}}\), which checks (B);
  • the rank of the coupling into \(\operatorname{coker}T\), which checks (C).

Do this for every \(M\) around the capacity, in one incremental pass. The smallest nonvacuous size is \(n=6\), where the window \(M=33,\dots,49\) lies between the trace capacity and the total. At \(n=8\) the full map is a dense system of about \(16044\) columns and \(259\cdot62\approx16000\) rows over \(\mathbb F_3\), about 64 MB bit-sliced. Packed incremental elimination is cubic, about \(4\times10^{12}/64\) word operations, a few minutes with OpenMP. The step ends with (B) and (C) confirmed or refuted at the reachable sizes, and, if confirmed, a proof attempt for (B).

Verification gate.

  • Re-read: the matching complex's definition and the operators \(D_\ell\), and the local-fall line review.
  • Checks: the capacities were computed from the closed formula for \(\gamma_t\). At \(n=6\) it gives \(\gamma_3=1645\), which matches the \(\dim K_3\) recorded in the syzygy-locality entry.
  • Fresh-context review: the reviewer confirmed the split, the lemma, the residual description and the table, and verified \(\gamma_3=16044\) at \(n=8\). It required the following changes, all adopted:
    • where the coupling lands proved on its own, and the cokernel's target fixed;
    • the condition split qualified;
    • positivity of the residual justified in case 1;
    • the hypotheses the lemma does not use, and those the corollary does, stated;
    • the capacity comparison proved in general;
    • the formula's range stated, and the no-rebalancing claim limited to this split;
    • (B) worded correctly, and the next step's count made concrete.

The changes weaken, qualify or supply proofs, so no further pass was made.

Double-point conditions have maximal rank on the functional matching complex at n = 6, 7, 8, and both Horace inputs hold there up to the capacity

23 September 2026 · Working proof by exact specialization · Degree 3, functional board, generic forms over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\), \(n=6,7,8\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The row Horace identity reduced double-point independence on \(K_3\) to two inputs, (B) nondefectiveness of the residual and (C) maximal rank of the coupling. It also noted that the capacity law had been measured only on the weak base. Do the capacity law, (B) and (C) hold on the functional board at the reachable sizes? The smallest nonvacuous case is \(n=6\), with window \(M=33,\dots,49\).

General statement. prop:double-points-generic-small-boards: at \(n=6,7,8\), on the functional matching complex over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\), generic forms give the following for every \(M\):

  • the double-point map \(w\mapsto(D_\ell^2w)_\ell\) on \(K_3\) has rank \(\min(\gamma_3,M(\gamma_1-1))\);
  • so does the trace map of the row Horace identity;
  • the residual map and the coupling have their expected ranks for every \(M\le M_{\max}\), which exceeds the total capacity. That covers the whole range the Horace reduction needs.

The computation

horace_pieces.py builds the maps sparse: the operators \(D_\ell\) from index structures, and a block basis of \(K_3\) with one local zero-marginal basis per row triple. It computes three rank series in one incremental pass each, with the compiled prefix-rank kernel gf3_prefix.c: the full map, the trace \(T\) on the board without the last row, and the residual on the arrays containing it, with \(D'_\ell\) as \(D_\ell\) with that row's coefficients zeroed. By the identity, the coupling's rank is \(r_{\mathrm{full}}-r_T-r_{\mathrm{res}}\), so no nullspace is needed. The forms are uniform over \(\mathbb F_3\), with every form checked to be nonconstant on every row, seed 1, for \(M=1,\dots,\lfloor1.15\,\mathrm{capacity}\rfloor+2\).

"None" means that for every \(M\) in the range, all four ranks equal their expected values:

  • full: \(\min(\gamma_3,M(\gamma_1-1))\);
  • trace: \(\min(\gamma'_3,M(\gamma'_1-1))\);
  • residual: \(\min(\dim K^{\ni i}_3,M(N-1))\);
  • coupling: \(\min(M(\gamma'_1-1)-r_T,\dim Z_{\mathrm{res}})\).

The three boards took 25 s in all. Control: function forms, with one nonzero cell per row, deviate at \(n=6\) in all four series, first at \(M=16\), \(1\), \(17\) and \(16\), so the checks can fail.

From one specialization to generic forms

Proposition (double points on small boards). At \(n=6,7,8\), with \(M_{\max}=57,144,299\):

  1. For every \(M\ge1\), there is a nonempty Zariski-open set of \(M\)-tuples of forms over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\) on which the double-point map on \(K_3\) and the trace map \(T\) have maximal rank.
  2. For every \(M\le M_{\max}\), the residual map also has maximal rank on such a set. The coupling into \(\operatorname{coker}T\), with the cokernel taken in the per-form targets \(\ker D'_\ell|_{K'_1}\) of total dimension \(M(\gamma'_1-1)\), then has rank \(\min(M(\gamma'_1-1)-r_T,\dim Z_{\mathrm{res}})\).

Proof. Each rank condition "rank at least \(r\)" is the nonvanishing of an \(r\)-minor of a matrix whose entries are polynomials in the forms' coefficients. So it is open, and nonempty once it holds at one point. For \(M\le M_{\max}\) all three hold at the computed \(\mathbb F_3\)-point, so they hold on a common nonempty open set of the irreducible affine space of tuples. For \(M>M_{\max}\), the full and trace maps have already reached their column counts at \(M_{\max}\), which exceeds their capacities. Adding forms cannot lower a rank, so their maximal rank persists for the prefix tuple and its extensions, which form a nonempty open set. The residual map has not reached its column count at \(M_{\max}\): its capacity is 141, 364 and 764, and at \(M_{\max}\) its rank is 285 of 705, 864 of 2184 and 2093 of 5348. So part 2 is limited to \(M\le M_{\max}\). There, the coupling's rank is \(r_{\mathrm{full}}-r_T-r_{\mathrm{res}}\) by the identity, which equals the expected value at the computed point. \(\square\)

The range the reduction needs. The row Horace corollary uses (B) and (C) for \(M\) up to the total capacity. Above it, \(Z=0\) at \(M=\lceil\mathrm{capacity}\rceil\) persists, since ranks cannot drop. So part 2 covers the whole range at these sizes. The residual's own injective regime, up to its larger capacity, is untested at all three sizes.

So on the functional board, at these sizes, the degree-3 capacity law is a theorem for generic forms, as is the row Horace reduction's claim that (B) and (C) hold.

What this gives and what it does not

  • The capacity law, first measured on the weak base, now holds with proof, for generic forms, on the functional board at \(n=6,7,8\). This is the interpolation statement of the local-fall line review at those sizes.
  • For all \(n\), the row identity reduces the statement to (B) and (C) at every smaller board, for \(M\) up to the total capacity. The data show both holding in that range, with no exception, at three sizes. They are still conjectures for general \(n\).
  • The forms are generic. Adversarial inventories, and degrees above 3, are outside this.

Next step. On odd-prime-clause-transfer: prove (B), residual nondefectiveness, for all \(n\) and every \(M\) up to the total capacity. The residual is a coupled simple-point problem. For each label \(a\), the scalar conditions \(D'^2_\ell W_a=0\) say that \(W_a\) is orthogonal to the squares \(\ell^2\) restricted to the board without row \(i\) and label \(a\). These are Veronese-type conditions, and squares span degree 2. The tuples are coupled only by \(\sum_aW_a=0\). Attempt a proof by generic independence of squares in each slice, plus a count of how the single coupling relation interacts with the slices. Then consider (C) with the same slice structure. The step ends with (B) proved, or with the obstruction.

Verification gate.

  • Re-read: the row Horace identity and its corollary.
  • Checks: the \(\gamma_3\) values match the closed formula and the earlier computed 1645. The control family deviates. All numbers were read from the result files by the script. The residual was checked only up to \(M_{\max}\), below its own capacity.
  • Proof: the specialization argument is the one reviewed for the generic square-tops proposition. The upward persistence uses only that ranks cannot drop when rows are added.
  • Fresh-context review: the reviewer confirmed the script, the block-triangular rank relation and the data. It found that the persistence step wrongly included the residual, whose capacity lies far above \(M_{\max}\). Part 2 is now limited to \(M\le M_{\max}\), and the range the reduction needs is stated. The changes weaken the claim, so no further pass was made.

The Horace residual is nondefective for generic forms, by comparing label slices; the zero-marginal spaces are chessboard-complex cycles

23 September 2026 · Working proof, lemma and finite check · Horace residual on any board; chessboard complexes, \(t\le5\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The small-boards entry proved double-point independence at \(n=6,7,8\) and asked for input (B) of the row Horace identity for all \(n\): the residual problem is nondefective for \(M\) up to the total capacity. The cycle ends with a proof or an obstruction.

General statement. prop:residual-nondefective: for any board with \(R\) rows and \(N\ge2\) labels, any row \(i\), and generic forms over an infinite field of characteristic other than 2, the residual map has rank \(M(N-1)\) whenever \(M\le\dim K_2\) of the board with \(R-1\) rows and \(N-2\) labels. For the PHP boards that covers every \(M\) up to the total capacity: for \(n=6,\dots,10\) by exact dimensions, and for all \(n\ge6\) given the dimension formula. lem:zero-marginal-chessboard-cycles: the zero-marginal space on one \(t\)-set of rows with \(N\) labels is the top cycle space of the \(t\times N\) chessboard complex, so the dimension formula is its Euler characteristic and holds when the lower reduced homology vanishes. ex:chessboard-formula-range: over \(\mathbb F_3\), for \(t\le4\), \(N\le8\), the formula holds exactly when \(N\ge2t-1\), and no 3-torsion is visible on five boards with \(t\le5\).

Setting

Let \(B'\) be the board without row \(i\), with \(N\) labels, and \(V=K_2(B')\). For a label \(a\), let \(V_a\subseteq V\) be the arrays vanishing on labelings that use \(a\); these are exactly the zero-marginal arrays of the slice without label \(a\). For \(a\ne b\), let \(V_{a,b}=V_a\cap V_b\). As recorded in the row Horace entry, \(K^{\ni i}_3\cong X=\{(W_a)_a\in\bigoplus_aV_a:\sum_aW_a=0\}\), with \(W_a\) the part where row \(i\) carries label \(a\). A form \(\ell\), restricted to \(B'\), gives the functional \(q_\ell\) on 2-row arrays, \(q_\ell(\{x,y\},\tau)=2\ell(x,\tau x)\ell(y,\tau y)\), so that \(D'^2_\ell W(\emptyset)=\langle W,q_\ell\rangle\). The residual conditions are \(\langle W_a,q_\ell\rangle=0\) for every form \(\ell\) and label \(a\).

The proposition

Proposition (residual nondefectiveness). Work over an infinite field \(\mathbb F\) of characteristic other than 2, such as \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\), with \(N\ge2\). Let \(m=\dim V_{a,b}\), the same for all \(a\ne b\), and \(M\le m\). For \(M\)-tuples of forms on the full board in a nonempty Zariski-open set, the residual conditions have rank exactly \(M(N-1)\) on \(X\). So \(\dim Z_{\mathrm{res}}=\dim K^{\ni i}_3-M(N-1)\).

Proof.

  1. Squares span each slice. The polarization \(q_{\ell+\ell'}-q_\ell-q_{\ell'}\) of two cell indicators, \(\ell\) at \((x,c)\) and \(\ell'\) at \((y,d)\) with \(x\ne y\) and \(c\ne d\) both different from \(a,b\), is \(2\) times the coordinate functional of the array cell \((\{x,y\},(c,d))\). Since \(2\ne0\) in \(\mathbb F\), the squares span all coordinate functionals of the slice, and so all of \(V_{a,b}^*\).
  2. Generic independence. The map \(\ell\mapsto q_\ell|_{V_{a,b}}\) is polynomial on the affine space of forms, and its image spans \(V_{a,b}^*\). So for \(M\le m\), the \(M\)-tuples with independent images form a nonempty open set. It is open by a minor. It is nonempty by induction, because the forms whose square lies in a proper subspace form a proper closed set. Intersect over the finitely many pairs \(a\ne b\). The forms live on the full board, and restriction to \(B'\) is a linear surjection, so the preimage of a nonempty open set is nonempty and open. The images are then also independent on each \(V_a\supseteq V_{a,b}\), and on \(V\).
  3. Dualizing. \(X=\ker(\Sigma:\bigoplus V_a\to V)\), so \(X^*=\bigl(\bigoplus V_a^*\bigr)/\operatorname{im}\Sigma^*\), where \(\Sigma^*g=(g|_{V_a})_a\). The condition for \((\ell,a)\) is the class of \(q_\ell|_{V_a}\) in slot \(a\). With \(S_a=\operatorname{span}\{q_\ell|_{V_a}\}\), of dimension \(M\) by step 2, the rank of all conditions is \(NM-\dim\bigl(\bigoplus_aS_a\cap\operatorname{im}\Sigma^*\bigr)\).
  4. Comparing slices. Let \(U=\{g\in V^*:g|_{V_a}\in S_a\ \forall a\}\). For \(g\in U\), write \(g|_{V_a}=\sum_\ell c^a_\ell q_\ell|_{V_a}\). For \(a\ne b\), restricting to \(V_{a,b}\) gives \(\sum_\ell(c^a_\ell-c^b_\ell)q_\ell|_{V_{a,b}}=0\), so \(c^a=c^b\) by step 2. With the common coefficients \(c\), \(g-\sum_\ell c_\ell q_\ell\) vanishes on every \(V_a\). So \(U=\operatorname{span}\{q_\ell\}\oplus\ker\Sigma^*\), where the sum is direct because a combination of squares vanishing on \(V_a\) is zero by step 2. Hence \(\dim\bigl(\bigoplus S_a\cap\operatorname{im}\Sigma^*\bigr)=\dim U-\dim\ker\Sigma^*=M\), and the rank is \(NM-M=M(N-1)\). \(\square\)

The proof uses characteristic other than 2 (step 1) and an infinite field (step 2), not characteristic 3. Over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\) it does not by itself give forms defined over \(\mathbb F_3\); for that, one \(\mathbb F_3\)-point of the open set must be exhibited, as in the small-boards entry.

The range

For the PHP board, \(R=n+1\) and \(N=n\), so \(m=\binom n2\delta_2(n-2)\). The row Horace reduction needs (B) for \(M\) up to the total capacity \(\gamma_3/(\gamma_1-1)\).

  • \(n=6,\dots,10\). Computed exactly: the zero-marginal dimensions per row pair with \(n-2\) labels are 5, 11, 19, 29 and 41. Those per row triple with \(n\) labels are 47, 104, 191, 314 and 479, matching the formula \(\delta_t(N)=\sum_j(-1)^j\binom tj(N)_{t-j}\). Then \(m=75,231,532,1044,1845\) against capacities 48.4, 123.9, 258.8, 477.0 and 806.5.
  • General \(n\). With the formula, \(m\ge\gamma_3/(\gamma_1-1)\) becomes \(3(n^2-7n+11)(n^2-2)\ge(n+1)(n^3-6n^2+8n-1)\). Expanding, it is equivalent to \(2n^4-16n^3+25n^2+35n-65\ge0\). The strict inequality holds for all \(n\ge6\): the values are 181 at \(n=6\) and 719 at \(n=7\), and for \(n\ge8\), \(2n^3(n-8)\ge0\) and \(25n^2+35n-65>0\). At \(n=5\) the value is \(-15\).

The general case uses the formula twice: as a lower bound for \(m\), through \(\delta_2(n-2)\), and as an upper bound for \(\gamma_3\), through \(\delta_3(n)\). The formula is verified for \(n\le10\) (residual_range.py). The next section reduces it to a connectivity property of chessboard complexes.

A lead: the zero-marginal spaces are chessboard-complex cycles

The user pointed to the chessboard complex, whose integral homology has 3-torsion by Shareshian and Wachs (arXiv:math/0409054), as a possible source of our exactness properties over \(\mathbb F_3\). The augmented obstruction-complex review recorded the same torsion lead. The following identification connects it to the dimension formula used above.

Lemma (chessboard cycles). Over any field, the space of arrays on injective labelings of a fixed \(t\)-set of rows with \(N\) labels and zero ordinary marginals equals the top cycle space \(Z_{t-1}\) of the \(t\times N\) chessboard complex \(M_{t,N}\). Its faces are the rook placements, the injective partial labelings. Hence its dimension is \(\delta_t(N)+\sum_{j<t-1}(-1)^{t-j}\dim\tilde H_j(M_{t,N})\), and it equals \(\delta_t(N)\) whenever the reduced homology below degree \(t-1\) vanishes over that field.

Proof. The \((t-1)\)-faces are the full placements, one rook in each row, since a placement has at most one rook per row. The boundary of a full placement \(\sigma\) is \(\sum_x\pm(\sigma\setminus x)\), over its rows \(x\). Faces \(\sigma\setminus x\) for different \(x\) have different row sets. For a fixed \(x\) and a fixed partial placement \(\rho\) of the other rows, the sign depends only on the position of \(x\). So the coefficient of \(\rho\) in \(\partial w\) is \(\pm\sum_cw(\rho\cup\{(x,c)\})\), the marginal of \(w\) in row \(x\) at \(\rho\). So \(\partial w=0\) exactly when every marginal vanishes. There are no \(t\)-faces, so \(Z_{t-1}=\tilde H_{t-1}\). The dimension statement is the Euler–Poincaré formula, with \(\delta_t(N)=\sum_j(-1)^j\binom tj(N)_{t-j}\) the alternating count of faces, the empty face included. \(\square\)

Consequence, conditional on an imported theorem not re-read here. Björner, Lovász, Vrećica and Živaljević showed that \(M_{m,n}\) is \((\nu-2)\)-connected, with \(\nu=\min(m,n,\lfloor(m+n+1)/3\rfloor)\), as the bound is usually quoted. If so, the formula \(\delta_t(N)\) holds for \(N\ge2t-1\). That covers \(\delta_2(n-2)\) for \(n\ge5\) and \(\delta_3(n)\) for \(n\ge5\), and so would make the range above unconditional for all \(n\ge6\) once the theorem is imported with its exact statement.

Checks.

  • chessboard_formula.py computed the exact dimension over \(\mathbb F_3\) for \(t=2,3,4\) and \(N\le8\), 16 boards. It equals \(\delta_t(N)\) exactly when \(N\ge2t-1\), in all 16 cases. That includes the recorded failure \(\delta_3(4)=-1\) against dimension 1, and a surplus of 5 at \(t=4\), \(N=6\), where \(\nu=3<t\).
  • chessboard_torsion.py compared the dimensions over \(\mathbb F_3\), \(\mathbb Q\) and \(\mathbb F_{10007}\) on the five boards \((t,N)=(3,4),(4,5),(4,6),(5,6),(5,7)\). They agree on all five, so no 3-torsion in \(\tilde H_{t-2}\) is visible there, which is the only torsion the top cycle space can see, by universal coefficients. The board \((5,8)\) timed out after 110 s in a Python-level elimination, which should have been the compiled kernel, and was dropped.

So the identification is proved, and the formula's range is the chessboard connectivity range, given the imported theorem. The torsion lead is untested so far: every comparison found the dimensions independent of the field. Among the spaces considered here, and if the connectivity theorem holds, torsion can affect only top cycle spaces with \(N<2t-1\), far from the degrees \(t\ll N\) that the route uses. It could also enter through other maps, such as the operators \(D_\ell\) or the cokernels of the double-point conditions, which were not examined.

What this gives

With (B) proved in the needed range, for \(n=6,\dots,10\) unconditionally and for larger \(n\) given the dimension formula (see the lead above), the row Horace corollary reduces double-point independence on \(K_3\) for all \(n\) to two inputs:

  • maximal rank of the trace, which is the same statement on the board with one row fewer and \(N\) labels, and so is an induction over boards with \(R\le N+1\);
  • (C), maximal rank of the coupling in the window between the trace's capacity and the total.

The induction's boards change shape, with fewer rows than labels plus one. So its base cases are small boards of every shape, not only the PHP ones, and the capacity comparisons of the row Horace entry have to be rechecked for those shapes.

Next step. On odd-prime-clause-transfer: attack (C). In the window, \(T\) is injective, and the coupling \(C=(\partial D'+D'\partial)\) maps \(Z_{\mathrm{res}}\) into \(\operatorname{coker}T\). Find a structure for \(\operatorname{coker}T\), such as a slice decomposition like the one used here, that makes the rank computable. In parallel, measure (C) and the trace's maximal rank on boards of all shapes \(R\le N+1\) at small sizes, to fix the induction's base cases. The sizes are small; the largest has \(\gamma_3\) about 16,000. The step ends with (C) proved, or with its failure pinned down.

  • Checks: the dimensions for \(n=6,\dots,10\) were computed from the recorded marginal-basis routine. The measured residual ranks at \(n=6,7,8\) equal \(M(N-1)\), consistent with the proposition.
  • Record check: claim searches for residual, slice, squares, polarization, double points and Horace found only this thread's Horace records. Searching the notebook for the chessboard complex found the torsion lead in the augmented obstruction-complex review, now linked.
  • Fresh-context review of the proposition and range: no mathematical error. It required the following changes, all adopted:
    • \(N\ge2\) in place of \(N\ge3\);
    • characteristic other than 2 and an infinite field named as the only field hypotheses;
    • a proof of the polynomial bound;
    • the dependence on the formula stated in "What this gives";
    • genericity under restriction to \(B'\) justified.
  • Second review, of the chessboard lemma, a new claim: it confirmed the identification, the Euler–Poincaré signs, the range \(N\ge2t-1\), the universal-coefficient claim, and the connectivity bound as usually stated, though not against the source. It required three scope changes to the interpretation, all adopted. They weaken claims, so no further pass was made.

The coupling condition, transposed: syzygies of the trace squares times the removed row, and specializations that keep it

23 September 2026 · Working proof, conjecture and finite check · The row Horace coupling, \(n=6,7,8\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The residual entry proved input (B) of the row Horace identity for all boards, and asked for (C), the coupling. It proposed to transpose (C) and to look for a specialization of the removed row's coefficients under which (C) becomes provable. The cycle ends with the transpose, and with the specializations that do and do not keep (C).

General statement. lem:coupling-dual: for any board, row \(i\) and forms, the rank of the double-point multiplication \(\mu\) equals the trace rank plus the dimension of the residual image plus the image of the trace syzygies under multiplication by \(2\ell_i\ell'\). If the residual map is injective, the kernel of \(\mu\) is the set of trace syzygies whose image lies in the residual image. conj:aligned-double-points: for every \(n\ge6\), forms whose row-\(i\) part is one cell \(x_{i,a}\) and whose other rows avoid label \(a\), with \(a\) balanced over the forms, have double points of maximal rank. The finite check is ex:coupling-specializations.

The transpose

Work in the top algebra \(G\) of a board with \(R\) rows and \(N\) labels over a field \(\mathbb F\), with \(K_t=G_t^*\). \(G\) is the polynomial ring in the cells modulo products of two cells in one row or one label, squares, and the row sums \(\sum_cx_{r,c}\) for every row \(r\). \(D_\ell\) is the transpose of multiplication by \(\ell\). So \(Z=\{w:D_\ell^2w=0\ \forall\ell\}\) is the annihilator of the image of

\[\mu:\bigoplus_\ell G_1\to G_3,\qquad(u_\ell)\mapsto\sum_\ell\ell^2u_\ell.\]

Fix a row \(i\). Every relation involves monomials on one row set, so \(G_t=G'_t\oplus G^{\ni i}_t\), with \(G'\) the top algebra of the board without row \(i\). Write \(\ell=\ell'+\ell_i\) and \(u=u'+v\) the same way; \(G^{\ni i}_1\) has dimension \(N-1\). Define:

  • the trace \(\mu':\bigoplus_\ell G'_1\to G'_3\), \((u'_\ell)\mapsto\sum_\ell\ell'^2u'_\ell\);
  • the residual \(\rho:\bigoplus_\ell G^{\ni i}_1\to G^{\ni i}_3\), \((v_\ell)\mapsto\sum_\ell\ell'^2v_\ell\);
  • the coupling transpose \(\beta:\ker\mu'\to G^{\ni i}_3\), \(u'\mapsto2\sum_\ell\ell_i\ell'u'_\ell\).

Lemma (coupling dual).

  1. \(\operatorname{rank}\mu=\operatorname{rank}\mu'+\dim\bigl(\operatorname{im}\rho+\beta(\ker\mu')\bigr)\).
  2. If \(\rho\) is injective, \((u',v)\mapsto u'\) maps \(\ker\mu\) isomorphically onto \(A=\{u'\in\ker\mu':\beta(u')\in\operatorname{im}\rho\}\).
  3. In characteristic 3, suppose \(\rho\) is injective and every \(\ell'\ne0\) in \(G'_1\). Then \(A\) contains the Frobenius syzygies \(\ell'e_\ell\), a space of dimension \(M\). Also \(\operatorname{rank}\mu=M(\gamma_1-1)\) exactly when \(A\) is spanned by them.

Proof. Two cells in one row multiply to zero, so \(\ell_i^2=0\), and \(\ell^2=\ell'^2+2\ell_i\ell'\). Then

\[\ell^2(u'+v)=\ell'^2u'+\bigl(2\ell_i\ell'u'+\ell'^2v\bigr),\]

where the first term lies in \(G'_3\), the second in \(G^{\ni i}_3\), and the term \(2\ell_i\ell'v\) vanishes. So \(\mu\) is block triangular.

  1. Projecting \(\operatorname{im}\mu\) to \(G'_3\) gives \(\operatorname{im}\mu'\). The fibre over 0 is \(\{\sum_\ell 2\ell_i\ell'u'_\ell+\rho(v):u'\in\ker\mu'\}=\beta(\ker\mu')+\operatorname{im}\rho\).
  2. \((u',v)\in\ker\mu\) exactly when \(u'\in\ker\mu'\) and \(\rho(v)=-\beta(u')\). When \(\rho\) is injective, \(v\) is determined by \(u'\) and exists exactly when \(\beta(u')\in\operatorname{im}\rho\).
  3. \(\ell^3=0\) in characteristic 3, so \(\ker\mu\ni\ell e_\ell\), whose image under part 2 is \(\ell'e_\ell\). These are independent because they lie in different summands and \(\ell'\ne0\). So \(\dim\ker\mu\ge M\). Equality means \(\operatorname{rank}\mu=M\gamma_1-M\), which by part 2 means \(A\) is their span. \(\square\)

This is the transpose of the row Horace identity: \(\mu'\) and \(\rho\) are the transposes of \(T\) and of the residual map. Since \((\operatorname{coker}T)^*=\ker\mu'\), \(\beta\) modulo \(\operatorname{im}\rho\) is the transpose of the coupling \(Z_{\mathrm{res}}\to\operatorname{coker}T\). The proof above is independent of it and makes the coupling explicit. By (B), \(\rho\) is injective for generic forms when \(M\le m\), which covers the total capacity for \(n=6,\dots,10\), and for all \(n\ge6\) given the dimension formula (residual entry). So (C) below the capacity says this: a syzygy of the squares on the smaller board that becomes, after multiplication by \(2\ell_i\ell'\), a combination of residual conditions is a Frobenius syzygy. The row-\(i\) coefficients enter only through \(\beta\), linearly and independently of \(\ker\mu'\).

In label slots. As in the residual entry, \(G^{\ni i}_3\cong\bigl(\bigoplus_aV_a^*\bigr)/\operatorname{im}\Sigma^*\), where \(x_{i,a}g\) corresponds to \(g|_{V_a}\) in slot \(a\). With \(\ell_i=\sum_ac_{\ell,a}x_{i,a}\), \(\beta(u')\) has slot-\(a\) entry \(2\sum_\ell c_{\ell,a}\ell'u'_\ell|_{V_a}\).

The one-slot bound. Suppose every form has \(\ell_i=c_\ell x_{i,a_0}\), with one label for all forms, \(N\ge2\), and the squares restricted to some \(V_{a_0,b}\) independent, which holds for generic \(\ell'\) when \(M\le m\) (residual entry; \(m=75,231,532\) exceeds every \(M\) tested). Then \(\beta(\ker\mu')\) lies in slot \(a_0\), which has dimension at most \(m_1=\dim V_{a_0}\). That slot meets \(\operatorname{im}\rho\) in at least the image of \(S_{a_0}\), of dimension \(M\): an element of \(S_{a_0}\) in slot \(a_0\) alone that lies in \(\operatorname{im}\Sigma^*\) comes from some \(g\in V^*\) with \(g|_{V_{a_0}}=\sum_\ell c_\ell q_\ell|_{V_{a_0}}\) and \(g|_{V_b}=0\). Restricting to \(V_{a_0,b}\subseteq V_b\) gives \(\sum_\ell c_\ell q_\ell|_{V_{a_0,b}}=0\), so \(c=0\) by independence there. So

\[\dim\bigl(\operatorname{im}\rho+\beta(\ker\mu')\bigr)\le\operatorname{rank}\rho+m_1-M.\]

(C) then fails as soon as \(M(\gamma'_1-1)-\operatorname{rank}\mu'>m_1-M\) in the window, while \(\dim Z_{\mathrm{res}}\) is larger. In the window the trace is surjective for generic forms, \(\operatorname{rank}\mu'=\gamma'_3\), so the onset is the least \(M\) with \(M\gamma'_1>\gamma'_3+m_1\). On the PHP board \(m_1=\binom n2\delta_2(n-1)\). Below, this predicts the first failure exactly.

Specializations

coupling_dual.py computes the trace and residual ranks once for uniform random \(\ell'\) over \(\mathbb F_3\), seed 1. It then computes the full rank for three choices of \(\ell_i\), with every prefix \(M\le\lfloor1.15\cdot\text{capacity}\rfloor+2\) in one pass of the compiled prefix-rank kernel. The coupling rank is the full rank minus the other two, compared with \(\min(M(\gamma'_1-1)-\operatorname{rank}T,\dim Z_{\mathrm{res}})\).

\(\ell_i\)\(n=6\) (57 values of \(M\))\(n=7\) (144)\(n=8\) (299)
uniformno deviationno deviationno deviation
one cell, labels balancedno deviationno deviationno deviation
one cell, same labeldeviates for all \(M\ge37\)all \(M\ge97\)all \(M\ge206\)

The trace ranks had no deviation, so the trace is surjective in the window for this seed. The one-slot bound then predicts the first failure from \(30M>940+165\), \(42M>3640+399\) and \(56M>10696+812\), that is at 37, 97 and 206, as observed. From the onset on, the observed coupling rank equals \(m_1-M\) exactly, at every \(M\) and all three sizes, so the bound is attained. Its hypothesis, independence of the squares on some \(V_{a_0,b}\), was assumed for the seed's forms, not checked separately.

aligned.py goes further. Form \(k\) has \(\ell_i=x_{i,a}\) with \(a=k\bmod N\), and its other rows avoid label \(a\), uniform elsewhere. So each label class lives on the slice without its label. At \(n=6\) and 7, the full, trace, residual and coupling ranks equal their expected values for every \(M\le\lfloor1.15\cdot\text{capacity}\rfloor+2\), 57 and 144 values. \(n=8\) was not run.

Cross forms, the analogue of points off the hyperplane. A form supported on row \(i\) and one label column restricts to a column form on the smaller board, whose square is zero. So it adds nothing to the trace, like a point off the Horace hyperplane. But it imposes too few conditions. With \(\ell'^2=0\) and \(\ell_iv=0\), \(\ell^2u=2\ell_i\ell'u'\), so a cross form imposes at most \(\gamma'_1-1=(R-1)(N-1)-1\) conditions, since \(u'=\ell'\) is in the kernel. That is fewer than \(\gamma_1-1\) when \(N\ge2\). Every configuration containing a cross form therefore falls short below the capacity. cross_count.py found the five sampled cross forms imposing 24 conditions each at \(n=6\), against \(\gamma_1-1=34\). At \(n=7\), four imposed 35 against 47 and one imposed 28. The Alexander–Hirschowitz balancing does not transfer this way.

What this means

By openness, one specialization with maximal rank proves the generic statement. So a proof of the double-point theorem for all \(n\) may assume aligned forms. In the aligned configuration, slot \(a\) of \(\beta\) sees only the forms of label class \(a\), and these live on the slice \(V_a\). Setting \(x_{i,a}=1\) turns such a form into the affine form \(1+\ell'\) on that slice. That suggests an induction over slices for inhomogeneous double points, which is not yet formulated.

Conjecture (aligned double points). Over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\), for every \(n\ge6\) and every \(M\), take forms \(\ell_k=x_{i,a_k}+\ell'_k\) with \(a_k=k\bmod N\), and \(\ell'_k\) generic on the other rows subject to avoiding label \(a_k\). Then \(\operatorname{rank}\mu=\min(M(\gamma_1-1),\gamma_3)\), the maximum allowed by the Frobenius kernel. By openness this implies the generic double-point theorem. Evidence: \(n=6,7\), one seed, \(M\le\lfloor1.15\cdot\text{capacity}\rfloor+2\).

Next step. On odd-prime-clause-transfer: formulate the aligned problem slice by slice and look for an induction. Under \(x_{i,a}=1\), class \(a\) becomes affine forms \(1+\ell'\) on the board with \(R-1\) rows and \(N-1\) labels. Write the aligned coupling condition as a statement about these affine double points on the \(N\) slices, glued along the doubly deleted slices \(V_{a,b}\) as in the residual proof. Then test whether that statement follows from the homogeneous statement on the smaller boards, which is the induction hypothesis. Count first: at \(n=6\) the window has \(M=33,\dots,48\) and 5 to 8 forms per class. The step ends with an inductive proof, or with the first place where the affine terms break it, located by a computation on the aligned configuration.

An edge Castelnuovo sequence from the chessboard complex, and why no Horace split balances

23 September 2026 · Working proofs and finite check · Matching complexes of bipartite boards; row and edge splits. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The coupling-dual entry proposed to prove the coupling condition (C) for aligned forms by an induction over slices. Each label class of forms becomes affine forms on a board with one row and one label fewer. The cycle asks what such an induction would rest on and where it breaks.

General statement. lem:edge-castelnuovo-sequence: for any bipartite board \(\Gamma\) and edge \(e\), multiplication by \(x_e\) and deletion of \(e\) give an exact sequence \(0\to G_{t-1}(\Gamma/e)\to G_t(\Gamma)\to G_t(\Gamma\setminus e)\to0\) whenever the deleted board's matching complexes on \(t\)-sets of rows containing the edge's row have no reduced homology in degree \(t-2\). prop:no-horace-balancing: for the row split, and for every edge split of the PHP board with \(n=6,\dots,10\), the trace is overdetermined at the total capacity; for all \(n\ge4\) this holds given the dimension formula and the homology hypothesis. A form whose trace part squares to zero imposes fewer conditions than the maximum \(\gamma_1-1\). So the Horace method's case without coupling does not apply to these splits, and every proof by them must control a coupling. The finite check is ex:edge-sequence-exactness.

Boards and the edge sequence

A board \(\Gamma\) is a bipartite graph between rows and labels. Its top algebra \(G(\Gamma)\) is the polynomial ring in the edge variables \(x_{r,c}\) modulo:

  • products of two edges sharing a row or a label;
  • squares;
  • the row sums \(\sum_{c\in N(r)}x_{r,c}\).

\(K_t(\Gamma)=G_t(\Gamma)^*\) is the space of arrays on \(t\)-matchings with zero row marginals. The complete board with \(R\) rows and \(N\) labels is the functional board. For an edge \(e=(i,a)\):

  • \(\Gamma\setminus e\) deletes the edge;
  • \(\Gamma/e\) deletes row \(i\) and label \(a\).

Lemma (edge Castelnuovo sequence). Over any field:

  1. \(G(\Gamma)/(x_e)=G(\Gamma\setminus e)\). Multiplication by \(x_e\) induces a surjection \(G_{t-1}(\Gamma/e)\to x_eG_{t-1}(\Gamma)\), so the sequence \(G_{t-1}(\Gamma/e)\to G_t(\Gamma)\to G_t(\Gamma\setminus e)\to0\) is exact.
  2. For a set \(S\) of \(t\) rows, let \(M_S(\Gamma)\) be the matching complex of \(\Gamma\) restricted to \(S\). Suppose \(\tilde H_{t-2}(M_S(\Gamma\setminus e))=0\) for every \(t\)-set \(S\ni i\). Then the first map is injective, and \(\dim G_t(\Gamma)=\dim G_t(\Gamma\setminus e)+\dim G_{t-1}(\Gamma/e)\).

Proof.

  1. Killing \(x_e\) turns the row-\(i\) sum into the sum over the remaining neighbours, and leaves every other relation a relation of \(\Gamma\setminus e\). So \(G(\Gamma)/(x_e)=G(\Gamma\setminus e)\). The map \(g\mapsto x_eg\) kills every monomial using row \(i\) or label \(a\), since those collide with \(e\). For a row \(r\ne i\), \(x_e\sum_{c\in N(r)\setminus a}x_{r,c}=x_e\cdot(\text{row sum})-x_ex_{r,a}=0\) in \(G(\Gamma)\). So the map factors through \(G(\Gamma/e)\) and is onto \(x_eG_{t-1}(\Gamma)\), the kernel of the quotient map.
  2. Dually, it suffices that \(K_t(\Gamma)\to K_{t-1}(\Gamma/e)\), taking the coefficients on matchings through \(e\), is onto. Its kernel is \(K_t(\Gamma\setminus e)\), and the image lies in \(K_{t-1}(\Gamma/e)\), since a row marginal at a face through \(e\) sums over labels other than \(a\). Work one row set \(S\ni i\) at a time. As in the chessboard-cycles lemma, zero marginals mean zero boundary in \(M_S\). A cycle \(z\) of the link \(M_{S\setminus i}(\Gamma/e)\) is a \((t-2)\)-cycle of \(M_S(\Gamma\setminus e)\). By the hypothesis \(z=\pm\partial y\) with \(y\) a chain of \(M_S(\Gamma\setminus e)\), with the sign chosen so that \(w=e*z+y\) has \(\partial w=0\), because \(\partial(e*z)=\pm z\). Then \(w\) is a preimage. \(\square\)

This is the deletion–link sequence of the matching complex, read in top degree. It is the analogue of the Castelnuovo sequence \(0\to I_{\tilde X}(d-1)\to I_X(d)\to I_{X\cap H,H}(d)\) of the Horace method, with the degree drop in the residual. edge_sequence.py computed \(\dim K_t\) over \(\mathbb F_3\) and \(\mathbb Q\) for \(t=2,3\) on the complete boards \((R,N)=(4,3),(5,4),(6,5),(7,6),(5,5),(4,5)\) minus one edge. The sequence was exact in all 24 cases, including \(\dim K_3=1645=1480+165\) at \((7,6)\). For \(t=3\) on the PHP board the hypothesis concerns the \(3\times n\) chessboard minus one cell. edge_homology.py found \(\tilde H_1=0\) over \(\mathbb F_3\) and \(\mathbb Q\) for \(n=5,\dots,10\), and \(\tilde H_1\) of dimension 2 at \(n=4\), where the sequence was nevertheless exact: the hypothesis is sufficient, not necessary.

No Horace split balances

Proposition (no Horace balancing). Take the PHP board, \(R=n+1\), \(N=n\), with \(n\ge6\), and forms in characteristic 3.

  1. Edge split. If the edge sequence is exact in degree 3, which holds for \(n=5,\dots,10\) (below), the trace problem on \(\Gamma\setminus e\) has capacity below the total capacity if and only if \(c=\dim G_2(\Gamma/e)\) exceeds the total capacity \(\gamma_3/(\gamma_1-1)\).
  2. For \(n=6,\dots,10\), \(c=165,399,812,1476,2475\) exceeds the total capacity \(48.4,123.9,258.8,477.0,806.5\), by factors 3.41 to 3.07. So at the total capacity the trace is overdetermined. For all \(n\), with the dimension formula, \(c=\binom n2(n^2-5n+5)\), and \(c(\gamma_1-1)-\gamma_3\) is \(\frac{n(n-1)}6\bigl(2n^4-10n^3+7n^2+23n-29\bigr)\). That is positive for \(n\ge4\): the value is 47 at \(n=4\), and for \(n\ge5\), \(2n^3(n-5)\ge0\) and \(7n^2+23n-29>0\). At \(n=3\) it is \(-5\). The formula itself is conditional on the imported connectivity theorem, as in the residual entry.
  3. The row split was recorded in the row Horace entry: its trace capacity is below the total on every nontrivial board.
  4. Trace-free forms. Call a form trace-free if its trace part has square zero: for the row split, \(\ell'^2=0\) in \(G'\); for the edge split, \(\ell=cx_e+\lambda\) with \(\lambda\) a combination of edges other than \(e\) and \(\lambda^2=0\) in \(G(\Gamma)\). The decomposition is not unique, because \(x_e\) equals minus the other row-\(i\) edges; the condition asks for one such \(\lambda\). This is stronger than contributing nothing to the trace. A trace-free form imposes fewer conditions than the maximum \(\gamma_1-1\), which generic forms attain at \(n=6,7,8\) (small boards). Part 4 holds in any characteristic.
    • for the row split, with \(\ell'^2=0\), at most \(\gamma'_1-1=(R-1)(N-1)-1\), for \(N\ge2\);
    • for the edge split, at most \(\gamma_1(\Gamma/e)-1\).

Proof.

  1. Exactness gives \(\gamma_3(\Gamma\setminus e)=\gamma_3-c\), and \(\gamma_1(\Gamma\setminus e)=\gamma_1-1\), so a generic form imposes \(\gamma_1-2\) conditions on the trace. Then \((\gamma_3-c)/(\gamma_1-2)<\gamma_3/(\gamma_1-1)\) is equivalent to \(\gamma_3<c(\gamma_1-1)\).
  2. The numbers are the computed dimensions of the residual entry, with \(c=\binom n2\delta_2(n-1)\).
  3. Recorded.
  4. For the row split, \(\ell^2=2\ell_i\ell'\) and \(\ell_iv=0\), so \(\ell^2u=2\ell_i\ell'u'\), which vanishes at \(u'=\ell'\). For the edge split, \(x_e^2=0\) and \(\lambda^2=0\) give \(\ell^2=2cx_e\lambda\). Its products \(\ell^2u=2cx_e\lambda u\) depend on \(u\) only modulo the edges meeting \(e\), by the lemma's part 1. So they form the image of \(G_1(\Gamma/e)\), which contains \(u=\lambda\) modulo those edges, where the product vanishes. \(\square\)

In the Alexander–Hirschowitz method, balancing comes from points off the hyperplane, which give nothing to the trace and a full double point to the residual. Here the trace-free forms lose at least \(N-1\) conditions each, so they cannot be used below the capacity. With the trace overdetermined, every argument by these splits is in the differential case, where the coupling must be controlled.

Where a slice induction breaks (heuristic)

At the total capacity, an aligned configuration has about \(\lceil\text{capacity}/N\rceil\) forms per class: 9, 18, 33, 53 and 81 for \(n=6,\dots,10\). The row-split trace capacities are 32.4, 88.8, 194.5, 371.5 and 645.8 (edge_homology.py), about 0.67 to 0.80 of the total, and larger than the class size at each of these \(n\). If the forms of one class are generic enough for the trace to have maximal rank on them, which was not checked separately, a single class has only Frobenius syzygies. The window syzygies in the transposed coupling are then all cross-class. Slot \(a\) sees them only through their class-\(a\) components. So, conditionally on that assumption, a slice-by-slice induction has no slice-level statement to use. The inductive hypothesis on smaller boards would have to control how the global syzygies of the trace split over classes, and none of the recorded statements does that.

Assessment

The Horace line has proved (B) for all \(n\), made (C) explicit, and supplied the edge sequence, exact under its homology hypothesis. Two cycles on (C) have not proved it. This cycle shows that neither the row split nor any edge split avoids a coupling, and, heuristically, that an induction over slices meets it at the gluing. The general implication, double-point independence for all \(n\), has not moved since (B). So the next cycle is a route review.

Next step. On odd-prime-clause-transfer: a route review of the double-point line. Weigh the prospects for (C) against the alternatives:

  • a differential Horace degeneration over several rows at once, using the edge sequence;
  • explicit specializations whose rank is computable for all \(n\), such as equivariant ones;
  • a secant-variety reading, in which \(\ell^2G_1\) is the image of the differential of the divided cube \(\ell\mapsto e_3(\ell)\), a map whose differential kills the radial direction in characteristic 3;
  • a return to the adversarial question, which the generic theorem does not answer.

Then propose the next research on the highest-risk item.

Verification gate.

  • Re-read: the row Horace entry, the residual entry (the chessboard-cycles lemma and the dimensions) and the coupling-dual entry.
  • Claim searches: deletion, contraction, edge, exact sequence, link and homology; and trace-free, deficient, balancing and hyperplane. They found only this thread's Horace records and the recorded amplitude exactness theorems, which concern the operators \(D\) and not this sequence.
  • Fresh-context review: the reviewer confirmed both parts of the lemma, the equivalence in the proposition and every quoted number. It required the following changes, all adopted:
    • the homology hypothesis checked, for \(n=4,\dots,10\);
    • the all-\(n\) comparison proved from the polynomials, with its conditionality stated;
    • trace-free defined as square zero;
    • \(\gamma_1-1\) called the maximum;
    • the slice paragraph labelled heuristic, with its capacities named;
    • the assessment narrowed to the row and edge splits.

The added claims are the homology check, read from its result file, and the polynomial comparison, a one-line proof. So no further pass was made.

Route review: the double-point line is a generic theory three rungs below the goal; the adversarial rung comes first

23 September 2026 · Route review · The double-point line on odd-prime-clause-transfer. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The edge-sequence entry found that no row or edge split avoids the coupling condition (C). The line's general implication has not moved since the residual theorem, which makes this cycle a route review. It was designed after re-reading three recorded statements:

  • the local-fall line review;
  • the reduction the goal rests on (thm:logarithmic-prefix-wide-clause-reduction);
  • the random-calibration review, which ties the window to the main record's parked wide-clause line (ctx:HW-parked-relative-rank-count).

General statement. The line's claim is conj:aligned-double-points, and through it the generic double-point theorem: for generic forms, the double-point conditions on \(K_3\) have maximal rank. That is the degree-3, width-1 case of the semi-regularity conjecture relative to the base (conj:semi-regular-relative-to-base). The line has proved the residual input for all \(n\) (prop:residual-nondefective) and the tools recorded since. Its open input is the coupling (C).

What the goal needs

By the logarithmic-prefix reduction, it suffices to show the following. Weak unary PHP plus the clauses \(g_{b,i}\prod_{j\in S_b}L_{b,j}^{p-1}\) of any \(M=n^K\) families of affine forms has no PC refutation of degree \((4p-1)(p-1)k\). Here:

  • the width is \(k=\lceil(K+1)\log n/\log(p/(p-1))\rceil\), logarithmic in \(n\);
  • the prefix sets \(S_b\) are chosen suitably, and the recorded padding refutations show that the choice must see which inputs can vanish;
  • the parameters satisfy \(M(1-1/p)^k<1\).

So the goal differs from the line's statement in three ways: adversarial families instead of generic forms, width \(k\approx2.5(K+1)\log n\) at \(p=3\) instead of width 1, and degree \(22k\) instead of 3.

Falsification attempts

Can a generic theorem be transferred to adversarial families? The lower-bound prover controls three things:

  • the choice of \(S_b\) inside each family;
  • restrictions and substitutions of the board;
  • the degree.

A linear dependency among forms, such as a pencil \(L_3=L_1+L_2+c\), survives every substitution, because substitution is linear. An adversary whose families have exactly \(k\) forms leaves no choice of \(S_b\), and it can place all of them in a low-dimensional subspace. So no step the prover controls moves an adversarial inventory into general position, and a generic maximal-rank theorem does not transfer. The recorded pencil review showed the consequence at width 1: four constraints in special position create a fall and a non-Taylor syzygy. Any adversarial statement must therefore be relative to the linear dependencies of the forms, as the local-fall conjecture is. This attempt succeeds against the line as a route: even complete success, the generic theorem at every degree and width, leaves the adversarial gap exactly where the random-calibration review recorded it, "the clauses a proof produces are not random".

Can adversaries compress width cheaply? Take two width-\(k\) clauses \((L_1=1)\vee R\) and \((L_1=2)\vee R\), where \(R\) is a disjunction of \(k-1\) affine equations. If \(R\) fails, both \(L_1=1\) and \(L_1=2\) must hold, which is impossible. So together they imply \(R\), of width \(k-1\), at every odd \(p\). A binary tree of such pairs removes one unit of width per factor 2 in clauses. Reaching width \(w\) costs \(2^{k-w}\) clauses, while the reduction's parameter condition allows \(M<(p/(p-1))^k\le(3/2)^k\). So this attack reaches width 0 only past the budget, and it stops above width \(k\bigl(1-\log(3/2)/\log2\bigr)\approx0.42k\) at \(p=3\), still logarithmic. This does not bound other compressions. It shows only that the obvious one is priced out by the reduction's own condition.

Assessment of the double-point line

The line is strong as a structural theory of the generic case:

  • an exact Horace identity, and the transpose of its coupling;
  • the residual theorem for every board;
  • the edge Castelnuovo sequence, drawn from chessboard topology;
  • a sharp conjectured specialization, the aligned forms.

It is weak as a route to the goal. Its open input (C) is the differential Horace step, with no balancing available. Its full success would settle the generic case at degree 3 and width 1, the first rung on each of three axes. It would not touch the adversarial gap, which the first falsification attempt shows no generic statement can close. The random calibration itself sits at the compiler degree \(4p-1=11\), behind the parked relative-rank obstruction, so the degree-3 theorem does not settle that either. The line is paused at (C), with the aligned conjecture as its restart point: the step that would advance it is a proof of (C) for aligned forms.

The highest-risk item and the next step

The adversarial rung is the highest risk. The one recorded adversarial candidate is the local-fall conjecture: after each span-closed member is replaced by its local reduction, the closure has no global fall below the reduced crossing. Its evidence covers planted members of span at most 3, at \(n=6,7\), and \(D=3\). The adversary's strongest move, by the first attempt, is to confine many forms to one subspace of moderate dimension \(d\). Such a subspace is a single member of span \(d\), whose local reduction is expensive when \(d\) grows. That is where a global fall, if any, should appear first.

Next step. On odd-prime-clause-transfer: test the local-fall conjecture against confined families.

  • Families. Planted selector families whose forms all lie in a random subspace \(W\subseteq G_1\) of dimension \(d=4,\dots,8\), with \(M_W\) forms from \(W\), up to all its directions, plus the recorded random selector sequence, at \(n=6\), \(D=3\).
  • Prediction. The conjecture predicts additivity: the base's split, plus the member's own change computed alone, plus the random selectors' recorded increments. Refutation should come at the reduced crossing.
  • Count first. The member's own closure at \(d\le8\) fits the recorded compiled kernel, at 1 to 2 s per closure at \(n=6\). The prediction is nonvacuous from \(d=4\), since plane members (\(d=3\)) were additive and the pencil review's special syzygies live in any span \(\ge2\).
  • What ends the step. A global fall beyond the member's own refutes the conjecture in its adversarial regime, and the line's restart must then be relative to a new invariant. Additivity up to \(d=8\) extends the evidence to the regime an adversary would use. The next question would then be a proof for confined members, through the recorded bounded-span equivalence.

Verification gate. A review. It re-read three records: the logarithmic-prefix reduction's statement and assessment, the random-calibration review's account of the parked obstruction, and the local-fall line review. Claim searches covered width compression, adversarial families, shared prefix sets and clause width reduction. They found the reduction, the padding refutations and the local-fall conjecture, all cited. The width-compression example is a two-line semantic check. The review registers no claim, and no reviewer pass was made beyond those of the cited entries.

Confined families fall only locally: selectors packed into one subspace of dimension up to 8

23 September 2026 · Finite check · Confined selector families at \(n=6\), \(D=3\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The double-point review named adversarial families as the highest-risk rung. An adversary's strongest recorded move is to confine many forms to one subspace, whose local reduction grows with its dimension. Does a confined family create a global fall, a closure beyond its own and the base's, before the reduced crossing?

General statement. conj:local-falls: after each span-closed member is replaced by its local reduction, the closure below the reduced crossing never exceeds the base's and the members' own, and refutation comes within a bounded number of constraints of the crossing. The finite check ex:confined-family-falls tests it on members of span up to 8.

Design and count

confined.py draws \(d\) random affine forms \(A_1,\dots,A_d\) on weak unary \(\mathrm{PHP}^7_6\), spanning \(W\), and a planted point \(z\in\mathbb F_3^d\).

  • It picks \(m\) distinct directions \(c\) of \(\mathbb F_3^d\), up to sign, and plants the selectors \(1-(L_c-f_c)^2\) with \(L_c=\sum_tc_tA_t\). Each forbids a value \(f_c\ne c\cdot z\), so \(z\) meets every selector and the family is satisfiable on its span.
  • The recorded random selector sequence follows.

The closure kernel is the recorded compiled one, with one incremental pass per family and every \(M=0,\dots,90\).

The additive prediction is:

  • the base's split, 280 low and 4291 top;
  • plus the family's own change, computed alone;
  • plus \(+1\) low and \(+34\) top per random selector.

There are 6860 degree-3 columns. The configurations are \(d\in\{4,5,6,8\}\) and \(m\in\{d,2d,4d\}\), 12 families, run in 28 s (invocation and timings in confined_s1.log). The test is nonvacuous from \(d=4\): plane members (\(d=3\)) were additive, and the prediction fails if the low part ever exceeds it.

Results

The top slope is the per-selector growth of the top part at the last two unrefuted checkpoints. The additive prediction is the first \(M\) at which the predicted top part exceeds 6860. The extrapolated crossing is the first \(M\) at which the observed top part, continued at the observed slope, exceeds 6860. It is fitted to the run, so agreement with it is close to automatic and shows only that refutation comes when the top degree fills.

  • No global fall. In the 11 families not refuted alone, the low part equals the additive prediction at every \(M\) before refutation.
  • Only the low part is additive. The top part falls short of the prediction in 6 of the 11 families, by up to 124, because the slope drops from 34 to between 28 and 33 per selector. The drop follows the family's own low part rather than \(m\): it occurs exactly when the own low part is at least 38. That is an overlap between the family and each random selector, not a fall. Its mechanism was not identified. So the driver's full additive statement fails for the top part, and the conjecture's low-part claim is what survives.
  • Refutation near the crossing. Against the additive prediction, refutation comes later in 6 families, by up to 4 (\(d=4\), \(m=16\): 32 against 28), because of the overlaps, and one step earlier in one (\(d=6\), \(m=12\): 57 against 58). It matches in the other 4. In every family it comes within 4 constraints of the additive count, with no low excess.
  • A family that refutes alone. At \(d=8\), \(m=32\), the family refutes PHP at degree 3 by itself, with 32 selectors where 76 random ones are needed. This does not contradict member pinning, whose hypotheses need the forms independent modulo constants on every row. Here \(d=8\) exceeds the row dimension \(N-1=5\) modulo constants.

An explanation, not checked in the run: each selector forbids a third of \(\mathbb F_3^d\), so about \(d\log3/\log(3/2)\approx2.7d\) selectors pin the span near one point. By bounded-span equivalence the member then derives about \(d\) affine equations, and the recorded least number of random affine equations refuting at \(n=6\), \(D=3\) is 7. The \(4d\) families at \(d=4,5,6\) are also past \(2.7d\): their expected numbers of allowed points besides \(z\), \(3^d(2/3)^m\), are about 0.12, 0.07 and 0.04, so they are likely pinned too. They pin fewer than 7 coordinates, and they do not refute alone, which fits the explanation. So a confined member's own contribution can itself be a refutation. The local-fall conjecture counts that as local, and it is.

What this means

At width 1 the adversary's confined move produces no global fall at spans up to 8, one board size and one degree. It does let a member refute on its own once it pins its span, at about 2.7 selectors per affine equation.

At the goal's parameters, pinning is priced out by counting. The reduction's clauses say that some \(L_j=0\), and a clause of width \(k\) with independent forms fails on a fraction \((1-1/p)^k\) of its span. At the reduction's \(k=\lceil(K+1)\log n/\log(p/(p-1))\rceil\) and \(M=n^K\), \(M(1-1/p)^k\le1/n\). So, if every clause has exactly \(k\) forms with linearly independent linear parts, all \(M\) clauses together leave at least a fraction \(1-1/n\) of their joint span allowed, by the union bound, and no family can pin it. The fractions are over the abstract \(\mathbb F_p^d\), not over the points realizable on the board. Two cases are not covered. Clauses with dependent forms can fail more often, although not always: \(L\) and \(L+1\) are both nonzero on only a third of the points. And the reduction takes \(|S_b|=\min(k,h_b)\), so a family with \(h_b<k\) forms gives a narrower clause, which fails on a larger fraction. Whether the reduction's choices avoid both is not checked here. The same budget priced out the review's width compression.

The local-fall conjecture thus survives the confined move where it can be tested, and the move's one effect is priced out at the goal's parameters. What remains open for adversaries is the gluing of many members at the goal's width and degree, which no computation at width 1 reaches.

Next step. On odd-prime-clause-transfer: take the adversarial test to width 2, the first width where the reduction's clauses are products. Clauses \(L_1^2L_2^2\) in unary encoding have degree 4, so the smallest PC degree that tests them is \(D=5\).

  • Count first. The recorded closure space at \(n=6\), \(D=5\) has 144,495 columns, 100,842 of them in degree 5, and a dense basis of about 5 GB, beyond the budget. At \(n=5\), \(D=5\) it has 16,807 columns, 7,776 in degree 5, and a dense basis of 0.07 GB. So the test runs at \(n=5\). The additive prediction needs the random width-2 split first: the per-clause low and top increments, measured as for selectors.
  • Then. Plant confined width-2 families, pairs of forms from one subspace \(W\), and compare with the prediction, including whether pinning needs about \(d\log3/\log(9/5)\approx1.9d\) clauses, since a width-2 clause excludes \(4/9\) of its span.
  • Scope. The goal's regime, \(M<(3/2)^k\) at logarithmic \(k\), lies far below every crossing and is out of reach at testable sizes. The width-2 test probes the capacity regime as a proxy, where members and random clauses interact the most.
  • What ends the step. A global fall at width 2 would locate the adversarial obstruction at the goal's first product width. Additivity would extend the local-fall picture one rung toward the goal's width.

Verification gate.

  • Re-read: the local-falls and plane-members entries (design, prediction, recorded split) and bounded-span equivalence.
  • Claim searches: span pinning, allowed set and the random-point count. They found bounded-span equivalence and the deciding-designs cap, cited or consistent.
  • Checks: the base split reproduces the recorded 280 and 4291. The prediction's column count was corrected, before the full run, from all 7638 columns to the 6860 top columns.
  • Claim scope: the entry registers a finite check only. The counting remark is the first-moment reading of the reduction's parameter condition, stated without a new claim. A first draft confused selectors, which exclude \(1/p\) of a span, with the reduction's clauses, which exclude \((1-1/p)^k\); this was corrected before review.
  • Fresh-context review: the reviewer confirmed every own split, the zero low excess, the slopes, the refutation points, the base split, the satisfiability of the families and the counting bounds. It required the following changes, all adopted:
    • the degree-5 column count corrected, which moves the next step to \(n=5\);
    • the additive prediction's refutation points reported, with the fitted crossing described as such;
    • the top part's non-additivity stated;
    • the pinning explanation checked against the other \(4d\) families;
    • the counting remark's caveats completed;
    • the overlap described by the own low part;
    • the run log saved.

The changes weaken or correct claims, so no further pass was made.
