Members within the budget are quiet in low degree, and width 2 is beyond computation

23 September 2026 · Working proof and finite check · Span consequences of clause families within the reduction's budget. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The confined-families entry proposed to test the local-fall conjecture at width 2, at \(n=5\), \(D=5\). The cycle asks whether that test can decide anything, and, if not, what can be proved about adversarial members at the goal's width.

General statement. lem:quiet-members: if \(m\) clauses of width \(k\), each with linearly independent linear parts, allow a set \(P\subseteq\mathbb F_p^d\) of their span, then every nonzero reduced polynomial vanishing on \(P\) has degree at least \((p-1)\log_p\bigl(1/(m(1-1/p)^k)\bigr)\). At the logarithmic-prefix reduction's parameters this is at least \((p-1)\log_pn\). So a member within the budget has no local consequence of degree below that. The finite check is ex:quiet-members-check.

Width 2 is out of computational reach

A width-2 clause \(L_1^2L_2^2\) has degree 4, so a test needs a degree \(D\ge5\) at which the base is not refuted by itself. horizon.py recorded the closure space of the recorded kernel and the base's own closure, for weak unary \(\mathrm{PHP}^{n+1}_n\):

\(n\)\(D\)columnsdense basisbase alone
637,6380.01 GBnot refuted, rank 4,571
549,0310.02 GBrefuted (full rank)
6443,6530.48 GBrefuted (full rank), in 97 s
65144,4955.22 GBnot computed; refuted, since refuted at \(D=4\)
75850,809181 GBnot computed

So the base refutes at degree 4 at both \(n=5\) and \(n=6\), and the first board that might survive degree 5 costs about 181 GB dense, far beyond the 10 GB budget. The step proposed by the confined-families entry is vacuous at every size in reach. The count should have been checked against the base's refutation degree before proposing it.

The lemma

Lemma (quiet members). Let \(p\) be prime and \(y=(y_1,\dots,y_d)\) coordinates on \(\mathbb F_p^d\). Let \(P\) be the common zero set of \(m\) clauses \(C_b(y)=\prod_{j\in S_b}L_{b,j}(y)^{p-1}\), each with \(|S_b|=k\) affine forms whose linear parts are linearly independent, so \(k\le d\). If a nonzero polynomial \(g\), of degree at most \(p-1\) in each variable and of total degree \(r\), vanishes on \(P\), then

\[p^{-r/(p-1)}\le m(1-1/p)^k,\qquad\text{that is}\qquad r\ge(p-1)\log_p\frac1{m(1-1/p)^k}.\]

Proof.

  1. A clause fails where all its \(k\) forms are nonzero. Independent linear parts make the \(k\) values uniform and independent on \(\mathbb F_p^d\), so the clause fails on exactly a fraction \((1-1/p)^k\). By the union bound, \(P\) has fraction at least \(1-m(1-1/p)^k\).
  2. \(g\) vanishes on \(P\), so its nonzero set has fraction at most \(m(1-1/p)^k\).
  3. \(g\) is a nonzero codeword of the generalized Reed–Muller code of order \(r\), whose minimum weight (Kasami, Lin and Peterson) is at least \(p^{d-r/(p-1)}\). So its nonzero set has fraction at least \(p^{-r/(p-1)}\). \(\square\)

Corollary (quiet members at the reduction's parameters). Take \(k=\lceil(K+1)\log n/\log(p/(p-1))\rceil\) and at most \(M=n^K\) clauses, so that \(m(1-1/p)^k\le n^K\cdot n^{-(K+1)}=1/n\). Then every nonzero function on a member's span that vanishes on its allowed set has \(y\)-degree at least \((p-1)\log_pn\). Here a member is any subfamily of the clauses whose forms lie in the span, each clause with independent linear parts. These functions are what bounded-span equivalence derives from the member, its local reduction.

What it gives, and what it does not

  • With the local-fall conjecture. Below the reduced crossing, every fall of a budget inventory would then be generated by polynomials of \(y\)-degree at least \((p-1)\log_pn\) in some member's span. An adversary cannot use members to create constant-degree falls. The width-1 phenomena that did so, pencils and pinned spans, are exactly members outside the budget.
  • Not the goal's degree, even at best. The goal needs hardness at PC degree \((4p-1)(p-1)k\). That exceeds \((p-1)\log_pn\) by the factor \((4p-1)(K+1)\ln p/\ln(p/(p-1))\), about \(29.8(K+1)\) at \(p=3\). There is also a ceiling. Each clause's product \(\prod_jL_{b,j}\), of degree \(k\), vanishes on \(P\), so the least degree is never above \(k\), and order \(k\) is the best any improvement can give. Even then it would fall short of the goal's degree by a factor of about \(4p^2\). What an order-\(k\) bound would buy is structural: members' local falls would stay within a constant factor of the clause width, so any fall to much lower degree would have to be global. At the budget, the current bound is about \(0.37k/(K+1)\) at \(p=3\) against the ceiling \(k\). For a single clause it is \(0.37k\).
  • Hypotheses. The lemma counts over the abstract \(\mathbb F_p^d\), and it needs each clause's forms to be independent. The reduction takes \(|S_b|=\min(k,h_b)\), and clauses of dependent or fewer forms fail more often, as the confined-families entry noted. It also bounds \(y\)-degree. The \(x\)-degree of a consequence can be lower after Boolean reduction.

Check. quiet_members.py computed exactly, over \(\mathbb F_3\), the least degree of a nonzero reduced polynomial vanishing on \(P\). It used random families with \(d=3,4,5\), \(k=1,2,3\) and \(m\in\{1,2,3,4,6,8,12\}\), three trials each, 189 families. No family violated the bound, and 76 came within one degree of it. Of these 76, only 27 have a positive bound: 135 of the 189 families have \(m(2/3)^k\ge1\), where the bound is 0.

Next step

The user directed, after this cycle, to finish the gluing line at the parameters where it is attainable, and only then to generalize. That supersedes the double-point review's pause of the line.

Next step. On odd-prime-clause-transfer: state and prove the glued theorem at the attainable parameters. Combine the recorded pieces into one statement with one probability space and one board:

  • member pinning;
  • the gluing lemma and syzygies as Tor;
  • the proved Tor vanishing for generic square tops, in degree 4 at \(n=7\) for \(M\le40\);
  • the double-point theorem for generic forms on the functional board, in degree 3 at \(n=6,7,8\).

The target is a statement of the form: weak unary or functional PHP plus \(M\) generic selectors has no PC refutation of degree \(D\), for every \(M\) below the proved range, at those \(n\). First re-read each piece's exact hypotheses, the board, the base and the degree convention. The step ends with the glued theorem proved at those parameters, or with the named hypothesis that fails to compose. Generalizing to all \(n\), through the coupling condition (C), comes after. Also open, from this cycle: whether the quiet-members exponent reaches order \(k\) for product-structured families.

Verification gate.

  • Re-read: the reduction's statement and parameters, bounded-span equivalence, and the confined-families entry's counting remark and caveats.
  • Claim searches: Reed–Muller minimum distance, allowed set, zero-set density, multiplicity Schwartz–Zippel and the refutation degree of weak unary PHP. They found the binary multiplicity cover audit and the endpoint theorems, none of which states this lemma.
  • Record check before drafting: a fresh-context subagent, given only the statement, found no recorded result implying it. It confirmed the weakening of the Kasami–Lin–Peterson weight, the union bound and the corollary's arithmetic, and asked for the two scope points now stated: the degree is the reduced \(y\)-degree, and independence needs \(k\le d\).
  • Fresh-context review: the reviewer confirmed the lemma, the direction of the Reed–Muller weakening, the union bound and the check's counts, and found no unused hypothesis. It required the following changes, all adopted:
    • the degree gap corrected to about \(29.8(K+1)\), and the 0.37 given its \(1/(K+1)\);
    • the ceiling at degree \(k\) stated, with what full success would and would not buy;
    • "nonzero" added to the corollary;
    • the width-2 sizes taken from a saved result file;
    • the trivial cases of the check counted.

The changes weaken or correct claims, and the one addition, the ceiling, is a one-line observation. So no further pass was made.

The glue holds in degree 3: independent double points make PHP with selectors unrefutable, and the bound is sharp

23 September 2026 · Working proof and finite check · Functional PHP with selectors, degree 3, any board with at least five labels. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The user directed finishing the gluing line at the parameters where it is attainable, before generalizing (quiet-members entry). The recorded glued theorem needs label robustness of order \(B^2r^2\), about 70 labels at \(B=3\). The proved generic interpolation, double-point independence, holds only at \(n\le8\). Do the two meet anywhere?

General statement. thm:glued-double-points: on the functional board with \(R\ge3\) rows and \(N\ge5\) labels, functional PHP plus any selectors over \(\mathbb F_3\) \(1-(L_j-v_j)^2\) has no PC refutation of degree 3 whenever two conditions hold: the squares \(\ell_j^2\) of the linear parts are independent in \(G_2\), and the double points \(\sum_j\ell_j^2G_1\) have their full dimension \(M(\gamma_1-1)\) in \(G_3\). No robustness is needed. The finite check ex:functional-capacity-sharp shows that, for random forms at \(n=6,7\), refutation comes exactly at the first \(M\) past the capacity.

The theorem

Work over \(\mathbb F_3\) on the functional matching base with \(R\) rows and \(N\) labels, its top algebra \(G\), and \(K_t=G_t^*\), as in the gluing entry. A selector \(C_j=\chi_{v_j}(L_j)=1-(L_j-v_j)^2\) forbids the value \(v_j\) of the affine form \(L_j\). Its top is \(-\ell_j^2\), with \(\ell_j\in G_1\) the linear part, so \(b_{C_j}=2\). The forms and forbidden values are over \(\mathbb F_3\), since the self relation below uses \(L^3-L\) in the base. The ranks in (a) and (b) are the same over \(\mathbb F_3\) and over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\).

Theorem (glued double points). Suppose \(N\ge5\) and \(R\ge3\), and that the linear parts satisfy:

  • (a) \(\ell_1^2,\dots,\ell_M^2\) are linearly independent in \(G_2\);
  • (b) \(\dim\sum_j\ell_j^2G_1=M(\gamma_1-1)\) in \(G_3\), that is, the double-point conditions \(D_{\ell_j}^2w=0\) on \(K_3\) are independent.

Then every NS functional for functional PHP plus \(C_1,\dots,C_M\) through degree \(k\le3\) extends through degree 3. The filtration is stable, PC equals NS through 3, and there is no PC refutation of degree 3. The same holds for weak balanced PHP with these selectors.

Proof. Iterate the extensions from \(s-1\) to \(s\le3\), as in the recorded glued theorem's proof.

  1. Base extensions. At each step, the old functional \(\mu\) annihilates the legal multiples of every constraint. An old extension \(E\mu\) through \(s\) exists by the recorded matching extension theorem, which needs \(m\ge B=3\) rows and \(N\ge2B-1=5\) labels. Nothing else in the proof uses the board's size.
  2. \(s\le1\). No selector is active below its degree \(h=2\), so \(E\mu\) itself extends.
  3. \(s=2\) and \(s=3\). By the syzygy-gluing lemma (part 1), a correction \(w\in K_s\) with \(D_{\ell_j}^2w=\hat z_{C_j}\) for all \(j\) exists if and only if \(\sum_j\langle\hat z_{C_j},g_j\rangle=0\) for every top syzygy \((g_j)\), \(g_j\in G_{s-2}\), \(\sum_j\ell_j^2g_j=0\).
    • At \(s=2\) the \(g_j\) are scalars, and (a) leaves only \(g=0\).
    • At \(s=3\) the syzygies are the kernel of \(\mu_3:\bigoplus_jG_1\to G_3\), \((g_j)\mapsto\sum_j\ell_j^2g_j\). It contains the Frobenius syzygies \(\ell_je_j\), since \(\ell^3=0\). They are \(M\) independent vectors, because each \(\ell_j\ne0\) by (a). By (b), \(\dim\ker\mu_3=M\gamma_1-M(\gamma_1-1)=M\), so the kernel is exactly their span.
    • On \(\ell_je_j\) the pairing is \(\langle\hat z_{C_j},\ell_j\rangle=(D_{\ell_j}\hat z_{C_j})(1)\). That vanishes by the recorded self relation \(D_j^{3-b_{C,j}}\hat z_C=0\) of the product-constraints entry. The self relation uses only that \(E\mu\) annihilates base multiples through \(s\), and that \(L^3-L\) lies in the base at degree 3. It needs no robustness.
  4. Conclusion. Each correction fixes every lower moment. Duality and degree-bounded multiplication give stability and PC equal to NS, and the nonrefutation transfers to weak balanced PHP, as in the recorded corollaries. \(\square\)

In the sheaf language of the gluing entry, each selector's local section exists by its self relation. The Čech obstruction is the defect pairing on syzygies that are not Frobenius, and hypothesis (b) says there are none. The theorem glues the sheaf in degree 3 at every board where (b) holds. The robustness in the recorded glued theorem was needed only to produce local sections at every degree for large subsystems. Here the subsystems are single selectors, and their sections come free.

Corollary (explicit witnesses). At \(n=6\), with the two recorded random sequences, and at \(n=7\), with the one below, the \(\mathbb F_3\) forms satisfy (a) and (b) for every prefix \(M\le48\), respectively \(M\le123\), which are \(\lfloor\gamma_3/(\gamma_1-1)\rfloor\). So functional PHP plus those selectors, with any forbidden values, has no PC refutation of degree 3. At \(n=8\), the small-boards proposition's \(\mathbb F_3\) specialization satisfies (b) for every prefix up to capacity, but (a) was not checked there, so the conclusion at \(n=8\) is conditional on (a) for those forms. The generic statement over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\) does not by itself give \(\mathbb F_3\) forms, since a nonempty Zariski-open set need not contain an \(\mathbb F_3\)-point.

For all \(n\) and \(\mathbb F_3\) forms meeting (a), the theorem reduces degree-3 hardness to double-point independence at those forms, and so to the coupling condition (C) of the row Horace reduction.

Sharpness

glued_check.py takes one uniform random selector sequence over \(\mathbb F_3\), with forms nonconstant on every row. For every prefix it computes three things:

  • (a) and (b) at those forms, from prefix ranks in the compiled kernel;
  • whether the degree-3 PC closure of functional PHP plus the prefix contains 1, from the incremental compiled closure;
  • the functional base, which is the weak base plus the row collisions.
\(n\)seedcapacity \(\gamma_3/(\gamma_1-1)\)(a) and (b) hold up to \(M\)first refuted \(M\)

The theorem predicts no refutation while (a) and (b) hold. It passed, and refutation came at the very next constraint in all three runs. At that constraint, (b) fails only by the dimension count \(M(\gamma_1-1)>\gamma_3\). So random \(\mathbb F_3\) forms are refuted at the first \(M\) past capacity: the degree-3 capacity law holds exactly on the functional board at \(n=6,7\) for these sequences. The theorem is sufficient, and observed tight for random forms. Whether (b) is also necessary, for forms in special position, is not shown. The recorded weak-base thresholds are later (76 and 185) because the weak base lacks the row collisions.

What is glued, and what is next

The gluing line is finished in degree 3: hardness for any number of selectors follows from double-point independence, and for random forms at \(n=6,7\) the two thresholds coincide. Double-point independence is proved at \(n=6,7,8\) and reduced to (C) for all \(n\). Generalizing means:

  • (C) for all \(n\), with the aligned conjecture as the restart point, which would give degree 3, for forms meeting (a), on every board with five or more labels;
  • higher degree, where the syzygies of degree \(s\ge4\) include Koszul pairs \(\ell_k^2e_j-\ell_j^2e_k\), whose pairing with the defects is the recorded cross relation. The generic square-tops entry proved the degree-4 analogue of (b) at \(n=7\) on the weak base's algebra.

Next step. On odd-prime-clause-transfer: glue degree 4. State the degree-4 analogue of the theorem. Hypothesis (b4): the kernel of \((g_j)\mapsto\sum_j\ell_j^2g_j\) on \(\bigoplus_jG_2\) is spanned by the Frobenius syzygies \(\ell_jG_1e_j\), which pair to zero by the self relation, and the Koszul pairs \(\ell_k^2e_j-\ell_j^2e_k\). Prove that the defects vanish on the Koszul pairs, from the recorded cross relation, for selectors on distinct forms.

  • Count first. At \(B=4\) the extension theorem needs \(N\ge7\), so the smallest valid board is \(n=7\). Both the weak and the functional base refute themselves at \(D=4\) for \(n=5,6\) (functional_base.py), consistent with that. At \(n=7\), \(D=4\) the closure space has 162,681 columns, about 6.6 GB dense, within the budget but heavy. So first check whether the functional base survives degree 4 there.
  • Then. Verify (b4) on the functional algebra at \(n=7\) for one \(\mathbb F_3\) sequence, and test sharpness.
  • What ends the step. The degree-4 theorem proved, with an explicit witness at \(n=7\). Or the named obstruction: the base refuting at \(n=7\), \(D=4\), or a syzygy beyond Frobenius and Koszul.

Verification gate.

  • Re-read: the syzygy-gluing lemma and the glued theorem's proof, the product-constraints entry's endpoint data and self relations, the main notebook's matching extension theorem (\(m\ge B\) rows, \(N\ge2B-1\) labels) and the small-boards proposition.
  • Claim searches: glued, extension room and robustness. They found the glued theorem, whose robustness this result avoids at degree 3, and the binary matching-extension audit.
  • Fresh-context review: the reviewer confirmed the four proof steps, including that (b) makes the degree-3 kernel exactly the Frobenius span, and that the self relation gives the vanishing pairing without robustness. It also confirmed the script's hypotheses and the table. It required the following changes, all adopted:
    • the forms and values over \(\mathbb F_3\), and the corollary restricted to explicit \(\mathbb F_3\) witnesses;
    • the extension requirement corrected to \(N\ge5\), \(R\ge3\);
    • the sharpness claims narrowed to sufficiency, observed tight;
    • the next step moved to \(n=7\), where degree 4 is within the hypotheses;
    • the degree-4 Frobenius syzygies stated.

The changes weaken or restrict claims, so no further pass was made.

Taylor generation glues at every degree without robustness; degree 4 is glued at n = 7

23 September 2026 · Working proof and finite check · Functional PHP with selectors, any degree \(B\), boards with at least \(2B-1\) labels. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The glued double-points entry glued degree 3 and asked for degree 4, where the top syzygies of the squares include Koszul pairs. The user directed finishing the gluing line before generalizing. Does the degree-3 argument extend to every degree, and does degree 4 glue at its smallest valid board?

General statement. thm:taylor-glue: on the functional board with \(R\ge B\) rows and \(N\ge2B-1\) labels (on the PHP board \(R=N+1\), so the row condition follows), functional PHP plus any selectors over \(\mathbb F_3\) has no PC refutation of degree \(B\) whenever the top syzygies of the squares \(\ell_j^2\) in every degree \(s\le B\) are spanned by the Taylor syzygies, that is, whenever \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(A/J,G)_s=0\) for \(s\le B\) in the notation of syzygies as Tor. No robustness is needed. The finite check ex:degree-four-glue-n7 verifies the degree-4 hypothesis for an explicit \(\mathbb F_3\) sequence at \(n=7\), \(M\le20\), and records where refutation comes.

The theorem

The setting is the glued double-points entry's: selectors \(C_j=1-(L_j-v_j)^2\) over \(\mathbb F_3\), with tops \(-\ell_j^2\), on the functional matching base, top algebra \(G\), \(K_t=G_t^*\). The Taylor syzygies of the squares in degree \(s\) are spanned by:

  • the Frobenius syzygies \(g\,\ell_je_j\), \(g\in G_{s-3}\), since \(\ell_j^3=0\);
  • the Koszul syzygies \(g\,(\ell_k^2e_j-\ell_j^2e_k)\), \(g\in G_{s-4}\).

By the recorded syzygies-as-Tor proposition, the top syzygies modulo these are \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(A/J,G)_s\), with \(A=\mathbb F_3[x_1,\dots,x_M]/(x_j^3)\) acting by \(x_j\mapsto\ell_j\) and \(J=(x_j^2)\).

Theorem (Taylor glue). Let \(B\ge2\), and suppose the board has \(R\ge B\) rows and \(N\ge2B-1\) labels. If for every \(s\le B\) the degree-\(s\) top syzygies of the squares are spanned by the Taylor syzygies, then every NS functional for functional PHP plus \(C_1,\dots,C_M\) through degree \(k\le B\) extends through \(B\). The filtration is stable, PC equals NS through \(B\), and there is no PC refutation of degree \(B\).

Proof. Iterate the extensions from \(s-1\) to \(s\le B\) as in the glued double-points theorem. The base extension \(E\mu\) exists by the matching extension theorem, which needs \(R\ge B\) rows and \(N\ge2B-1\) labels. By the syzygy-gluing lemma, part 1, a correction exists if and only if the defects pair to zero with every top syzygy. By hypothesis it suffices to check the Taylor generators.

  • Frobenius. \(\langle\hat z_{C_j},g\ell_j\rangle=(D_gD_{\ell_j}\hat z_{C_j})(1)=0\), by the self relation \(D_{\ell_j}\hat z_{C_j}=0\).
  • Koszul. \(\langle\hat z_{C_j},g\ell_k^2\rangle-\langle\hat z_{C_k},g\ell_j^2\rangle=\bigl(D_g(D_{\ell_k}^2\hat z_{C_j}-D_{\ell_j}^2\hat z_{C_k})\bigr)(1)=0\), by the cross relation \(D^{b-b_C}\hat z_C=D^{b-b_{C'}}\hat z_{C'}\). Two selectors on different indexed forms share no form, so they are coherent, and \(b=b_C+b_{C'}\).

Both relations were proved from two facts only: \(E\mu\) annihilates base multiples through \(s\), and \(\mu\) annihilates legal multiples of lower degree (\(C\cdot C'=C'\cdot C\) for the cross relation, \(L^3-L\) in the base for the self relation). Neither uses robustness or independence of the forms. The rest is as in the glued double-points theorem. \(\square\)

The glued double-points theorem is the case \(B=3\): at \(s=2\) there are no Taylor syzygies, so the hypothesis is independence of the squares, and at \(s=3\) only the Frobenius ones \(\ell_je_j\). The recorded glued theorem needed robustness of order \(B^2r^2\) to produce local corrections for general subsystems. For selectors, the self and cross relations make every Taylor syzygy harmless directly, so Tor vanishing alone decides the gluing.

Degree 4 at n = 7

At \(B=4\) the matching extension theorem needs \(N\ge7\), so \(n=7\) is the smallest board. Two new pieces of code:

  • fspace.py is the functional quotient space for the recorded all-C closure: monomials with distinct pigeons and distinct holes, collisions zero. Its self-test reproduces the recorded functional computation at \(n=6\), \(D=3\): codimension 2,080 and the first refutation at 49.
  • base_n7.py found functional \(\mathrm{PHP}^8_7\) not refuted by its own degree-4 closure, with 71,793 columns, in 6 s. \(\mathrm{PHP}^7_6\) is refuted at degree 4.

deg4_check.py takes one uniform \(\mathbb F_3\) sequence, forms nonconstant on every row, seed 1. For every prefix it computes:

  • (a), squares independent in \(G_2\);
  • (b), degree-3 syzygies only Frobenius: rank \(M(\gamma_1-1)\) on \(K_3\);
  • (b4), the dimension \(M\gamma_2-\operatorname{rank}\mu_4\) of the degree-4 syzygies compared with the rank of the Frobenius and Koszul generators. Equality means the generators span the kernel, because they lie in it: \(\ell_j^3=0\) in \(G\), which has characteristic 3 and squarefree rows, and the Koszul pairs cancel;
  • whether the degree-4 closure contains 1.

Here \(\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_4=48,812,5824,15750\). The ranks use the compiled prefix-rank kernel and the closure the all-C kernel. The board and generator construction is vectorized. It reproduced the ranks of an earlier run built with Python loops at all 20 prefixes. That run timed out at \(M=21\), and its log is saved as deg4_n7_s1_loopbuilt_timedout.log.

Result. (a), (b) and (b4) hold at every prefix \(M\le20\). At \(M=20\) the degree-4 syzygies have dimension 1150, equal to the rank of the Frobenius and Koszul generators, and \(\operatorname{rank}\mu_4=15090<\gamma_4\). The degree-4 closure contains 1 first at \(M=21\). There \(\operatorname{rank}\mu_4\) reaches \(\gamma_4=15750\), so (b4) fails only by the dimension count: the syzygies (1302) exceed the generators (1218). So the theorem's prediction passed with an explicit \(\mathbb F_3\) witness at degree 4. As at degree 3, the random sequence is refuted at the first selector past the degree-4 capacity.

Cost. The prefix closures took 0.7 to 31 s each through \(M=20\). The refuting step took 313 s of the 645 s of closure time recorded in the result file, and the run took 667 s by its log (deg4_n7_s1.log), because the closure kernel runs to saturation after 1 has entered. Since the prefix ranks already settle \(M\le20\) through the theorem, one batch closure of the first 20 selectors, then single steps with an early stop at 1, would have answered the same question. That waste was identified after launch. The early stop belongs in the kernel, and CLAUDE.md now requires designing each run from its question.

What is glued, and what remains

The gluing line is finished at every degree in this form: for selectors, hardness through degree \(B\) follows from Tor vanishing through \(B\) on boards with at least \(B\) rows and \(2B-1\) labels. Tor vanishing is verified for explicit seeded \(\mathbb F_3\) sequences only: in degree 3 for \(M\le48\) at \(n=6\) and \(M\le123\) at \(n=7\), and in degree 4 for \(M\le20\) at \(n=7\). It is not verified for all forms at those \(n\). In both degrees those sequences are refuted at the next selector. Generalizing now means proving Tor vanishing, for generic or suitable forms, at all \(n\) and degrees. That is the semi-regularity statement, whose degree-3 case the double-point line reduced to the coupling condition (C). The adversarial and wide-clause axes of the double-point review remain beyond it.

Next step. On odd-prime-clause-transfer, by the user's plan to generalize once glued: prove degree-3 Tor vanishing for all \(n\). That is the coupling condition (C) of the row Horace reduction, with the aligned double-points conjecture as its restart point. Start from the transposed coupling: for aligned forms, a trace syzygy whose product with \(2\ell_i\ell'\) lies in the residual span must be Frobenius. First add the early stop to gf3_closure.c: end the closure when the constant enters, check it against the recorded refutation points (49, 124, 21), and use it in every later sharpness test. The step ends with (C) proved for aligned forms, or with the exact place where the aligned coupling fails, located by the transposed-coupling computation at \(n=6,7\).

Verification gate.

  • Re-read: the syzygy-gluing lemma, the syzygies-as-Tor proposition, the product-constraints entry's self and cross relations with their proofs, the matching extension theorem's requirement and the glued double-points entry.
  • Claim searches: Taylor, gluing and robustness. They found the glued theorem and the syzygies-as-Tor remark that Taylor generation implies local generation. That remark still needs local corrections, and so robustness, which this theorem avoids for selectors.
  • Fresh-context review: the reviewer confirmed the Frobenius and Koszul pairings, including the commutation of \(D_g\), the coherence of selectors on different forms, the \(B=3\) reduction, the Tor identification, the check's code and every number. It required the following changes, all adopted:
    • the timings taken from saved files, and the earlier run's log saved;
    • one row symbol, and the weak-balanced clause dropped, since the check covers only the functional base;
    • the reason that equal dimensions give spanning stated;
    • the verified range stated per seed and per size.

The changes weaken or correct claims, so no further pass was made.

Route review: what the glued sheaf covers, what each parameter needs, and the tools that might carry it

23 September 2026 · Route review · The glued line on odd-prime-clause-transfer, before generalization. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The Taylor-glue entry finished the gluing line for selectors. The user asked for a table of the glued sheaf's parameters against the goal, with a direction for each, and for the leads from modern algebraic geometry, commutative algebra and category theory to be recorded. This review sets the direction for generalization.

General statement. The line's claim is thm:taylor-glue: for selectors on the functional board with at least \(B\) rows and \(2B-1\) labels, Tor vanishing through degree \(B\) (\(\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(A/J,G)_s=0\), \(s\le B\)) gives no PC refutation of degree \(B\). The gluing theorem holds at every \(n\) and \(B\). The small values in the table are where its hypothesis has been verified, for explicit seeded \(\mathbb F_3\) sequences. So generalizing mostly means proving the hypothesis, not re-proving the gluing.

The parameters against the goal

The goal's requirements come from the logarithmic-prefix reduction (thm:logarithmic-prefix-wide-clause-reduction).

The gluing lemma and the Tor framework are stated for all \(p\); the self and cross relations need rechecking for exponent \(p-1\).

So three parameters need genuinely new mathematics, in order of risk: adversarial forms, logarithmic width, and logarithmic degree through Tor vanishing. Two need proofs of the double-point kind: \(n\to\infty\), which is (C), and general \(p\). The rest need nothing.

Leads from algebraic geometry, commutative algebra and category theory

These are proposals, not results. None has been checked against our algebra beyond the stated evidence.

  1. Artinian reduction and Hochster's formula (width; most striking).
    • Idea: \(G\) looks like an Artinian reduction of the face ring of the chessboard complex: squarefree monomials in the edge variables, quotiented by the row sums as linear forms. If that identification holds, Hochster's formula expresses the Tor of such rings through the homology of induced subcomplexes. Tor vanishing for wide monomial tops would then become homology vanishing on chessboard-type subcomplexes. The chessboard connectivity theorem and Shareshian–Wachs torsion would then enter as tools.
    • Related tools: the modern Lefschetz theorems for Artinian reductions of face rings, Adiprasito's generic Lefschetz theorems and the anisotropy method of Papadakis and Petrotou with its extension to odd characteristic.
    • Caveats: those theorems are for spheres and manifolds, and chessboard complexes are neither. In characteristic 3, \(\ell^3=0\) breaks strong Lefschetz in its usual form; the Frobenius syzygies are exactly that failure, so any Lefschetz input needs a characteristic-\(p\) version.
    • Status: the identification of \(G\) is unverified. It is cheap to test.
  2. Gröbner and torus degenerations with semicontinuity (degree). The Tor hypothesis is of Fröberg type: squares of generic forms have the expected Hilbert function below capacity. Fröberg's conjecture is open in general even for polynomial rings, but its known cases are proved by degenerating to monomial or torus-fixed configurations, where Taylor resolutions compute Tor, and lifting by semicontinuity. Our regime is favourable: many variables, \(M\) far below capacity, low degree and only the injective side. This is the systematic form of the specialization plus openness already used at degrees 3 and 4.
  3. Representation stability (\(n\to\infty\)). \(n\mapsto K_t(n)\) is a functor on a category of injections, adding rows and labels. That is the FI-module setting of Church, Ellenberg and Farb, where Noetherianity turns vanishing up to the generation degree into vanishing for all \(n\). The dimension formula \(\delta_t\) is a polynomial in \(N\), the typical signature. The catch is that a fixed tuple of forms breaks the symmetry. It needs equivariant configurations, such as the orbit specializations used in degree 4, with \(M\) growing with \(n\).
  4. Čech and Leray vanishing on the member cover (adversarial). The gluing obstruction is a first Čech group on the cover of the inventory by its members, identified with Tor. A Leray-type theorem would make it vanish when the cover is good, with its own higher obstructions vanishing on overlaps. That is a candidate proof strategy for the local-fall law; the pencil is precisely a bad overlap.
  5. Stratifications, and a warning. Flattening stratification and constructibility say the space of form tuples splits into finitely many strata with constant Tor. But the adversary picks the stratum. Mnëv universality says configuration strata can be arbitrarily complicated, so a stratum-by-stratum classification is hopeless. Any adversarial theorem must use local data only, the members, as the local-fall conjecture does.
  6. Category theory.
    • Where it helps: functoriality on injection categories, lead 3, and the identification of the gluing obstruction with Čech cohomology and Tor, lead 4.
    • Where it does not: the Yoneda lemma, since our objects are explicit finite-dimensional spaces with explicit maps. Adjunctions between the functional and weak bases would be tidy but unproductive.

Assessment and direction

The glued line is complete in form: for selectors, hardness through degree \(B\) is exactly Tor vanishing through \(B\) on small-resource boards, and it is observed sharp at degrees 3 and 4. What remains is the generalization of its hypothesis along three hard axes, adversarial, width and degree, and two routine ones, \(n\) and \(p\).

The cheapest decisive test is lead 1. If \(G\) is an Artinian reduction of the chessboard complex's face ring, Hochster's formula and the Lefschetz literature become available, and topology connects to the width axis. If it is not, the mismatch identifies the right algebra. Lead 2 is the systematic continuation of what already worked for degree. Lead 3 is for \(n\to\infty\) once an equivariant family is in hand. The coupling condition (C) stays the concrete open step for \(n\to\infty\) in degree 3.

Next step. On odd-prime-clause-transfer: test lead 1.

  • Test. Compare the Hilbert function of \(G\) for the functional board, \(\dim G_t=\binom Rt\delta_t(N)\) where the formula holds, with the \(h\)-vector of the chessboard complex \(M_{R,N}\) and with the Hilbert function of its face ring modulo squares and the row sums, at small \((R,N)\).
  • Count first. The face numbers are closed forms, and the exact quotients are small linear algebra at \(R\le8\), \(N\le7\).
  • Then. If an identification holds, state Hochster's formula for the relevant Tor, and test it on the recorded degree-3 and degree-4 witnesses. If none holds, record the mismatch and the algebra \(G\) actually is.
  • What ends the step. An identification with its consequences for wide tops, or a precise negative.

Verification gate. A review. It re-read the Taylor-glue and glued double-points entries, the double-point review, the quiet-members and confined-families entries, and the logarithmic-prefix reduction's statement. It registers no claim. The literature named in the leads (Hochster's formula, the Lefschetz and anisotropy theorems, Fröberg's conjecture, FI-modules, Mnëv universality) is cited from memory as context, not relied on for any claim. Each must be read in its source before use.

What standard theory says about the glued sheaf, and a sharper next step

23 September 2026 · Route review · Observations on Taylor glue; next step refined to a Gröbner degeneration of \(G\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. After the generalization review, the user asked:

  • what modern algebraic geometry says about the glued sheaf;
  • whether witnesses are easier than proofs;
  • whether Fröberg's conjecture deserves a branch;
  • whether any of this changes the next step.

This short cycle records the answers.

General statement. The line's claim is unchanged, thm:taylor-glue: for selectors, Tor vanishing through degree \(B\) gives no PC refutation of degree \(B\). This entry records consequences of standard theory for it and refines the next step. It proves nothing new.

Observations

  1. Gluing is open and generic. Tor vanishing through \(B\) is maximal rank of finitely many multiplication maps. So, for fixed \((n,B,M)\), the tuples of forms where the sheaf glues form a Zariski-open set, dense over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\) once one witness exists. The witnesses at degrees 3 and 4 give such dense sets. Failure lies on a closed determinantal locus, which is where adversarial inventories live. By Mnëv universality that locus can be as complicated as arbitrary varieties, so it cannot be classified. Witnesses over \(\mathbb F_3\) hold over every extension field, but a dense open set over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\) need not contain \(\mathbb F_3\)-points.
  2. A modular representation. In characteristic 3, \(A=\mathbb F_3[x_1,\dots,x_M]/(x_j^3)\) is the group algebra of \((\mathbb Z/3)^M\), with \(x_j=g_j-1\). So \(G\) is a representation of an elementary abelian 3-group, each generator acting as \(1+\ell_j\). Tor vanishing is a truncated, relative projectivity, the subject of Dade's lemma, rank and support varieties, and Jordan types. The shortcut through Dade's lemma, reducing to single generic elements, is refuted in the truncated setting by the recorded truncated Dade counterexample: freeness over every single element plus positivity does not imply truncated freeness without a genericity hypothesis. Only self-injectivity of the group algebra has been used successfully, in the symmetric lifting lemma.
  3. Sharpness as a Hilbert series. Tor vanishing through \(B\) means \(G/(\ell_j^2)\) has its expected Hilbert function through \(B\), as the syzygies-as-Tor proposition states for linear tops. The observed refutations at 49, 124 and 21 are where that expected count first fails in the top degree. So "hardness ends exactly at capacity" is a semi-regularity statement of Fröberg type for \(G\).
  4. Apolarity. \(K_t=G_t^*\), with \(D_\ell\) the transpose of multiplication by \(\ell\), is Macaulay inverse-system duality. That is why degree 3 read as the matching-complex analogue of Alexander–Hirschowitz double points.
  5. Witnesses and families. One witness settles one \((n,B,M)\) generically, but the goal needs every \(n\), \(B\) of order \(\log n\) and \(M\) up to \(n^K\). The checks outgrow any computer quickly, and witnesses are evidence on the generic side, not about adversaries. What scales is a witness family: forms defined for every \(n\) by a rule, with ranks provable uniformly. Alexander–Hirschowitz and the known cases of Fröberg's conjecture are proved that way, and the aligned forms are the candidate here.
  6. Fröberg's conjecture. It concerns generic forms in a polynomial ring, is open in general, and is proved only in special cases, as recalled from the literature (to be read in the sources before use). Our need is weaker and different: our algebra is \(G\), on the injective side, in low degree, far below capacity, with squares of linear forms, the powers-of-forms variant closer to Alexander–Hirschowitz. A branch on Fröberg itself would be a long detour off the critical path. The known-case literature is the reading list for the degeneration lead. A side notebook on the semi-regularity of \(G\) is warranted if that work grows into its own program (recorded in the remaining route).
  7. Hochster's formula concerns a different Tor. It computes the Tor of a face ring over its polynomial ring with respect to the coordinate variables. Ours is Tor over \(A\) acting through generic forms. Using it requires a flat degeneration to a monomial situation first.
  8. Degenerating the forms is obstructed in \(G\). Squares of small-support forms impose too few conditions.
    • A single-cell form has square 0.
    • A two-cell form \(\ell=x_{r,c}+x_{s,d}\), \(r\ne s\), \(c\ne d\), has the monomial square \(2x_{r,c}x_{s,d}\). Then \(\ell^2G_1\) is spanned by \(x_{r,c}x_{s,d}x_e\), with \(e\) in the other \(R-2\) rows and the other \(N-2\) labels. In each such row, the row sum times \(x_{r,c}x_{s,d}\) is one relation among those \(N-2\) cells. So a two-cell form imposes at most \((R-2)(N-3)\) conditions: 15 at \(n=6\), against \(\gamma_1-1=34\).
    • This is the phenomenon behind the recorded failures of function forms and cross forms.
    Monomial specializations of the forms therefore cannot certify maximal rank.
  9. Degenerating the algebra is the viable version. Take a Gröbner degeneration of the relations defining \(G\): squares, row and label collisions, row sums. Keep the forms generic, since multiplication by them is defined on the degenerate algebra. The expected mechanism: in a flat family of \(A\)-modules, Tor dimensions are upper semicontinuous, so vanishing on the degenerate fiber would imply vanishing for \(G\). That needs checking in this setting, including that \(\ell_j^3=0\) holds in every fiber for \(A\) to act. If the initial ideal is squarefree, the degenerate algebra is of Stanley–Reisner type for some complex \(\Delta'\), and Tor becomes combinatorial, where Hochster-type formulas and the chessboard topology apply.

Route update

The recorded next step asked whether \(G\) is an Artinian reduction of the chessboard complex's face ring. Observations 7 to 9 make it precise.

Next step. On odd-prime-clause-transfer: compute a Gröbner basis of the ideal defining \(G\) for the functional board at small \((R,N)\), from \((3,2)\) up to \((7,6)\) if feasible.

  • First question: is the initial ideal squarefree, and if so, which complex \(\Delta'\) does it define? Compare its face numbers with \(\dim G_t\).
  • Then: check whether the degeneration is a flat family of \(A\)-modules for generic forms. At \(n=6\), degree 3, test whether Tor vanishing holds on the degenerate fiber for the recorded witnesses. That is the direction semicontinuity needs.
  • Count first: the polynomial ring has \(RN\) variables, 42 at \(n=6\), and the ideal is generated in degrees 1 and 2, so small Gröbner computations suffice. Use a compiled Gröbner implementation if one is available locally. Otherwise the linear-algebra version, degree by degree up to 4, through the recorded compiled elimination kernels.
  • What ends the step: a squarefree degeneration with Tor vanishing on it, which opens the Hochster route, or the precise way the degeneration fails.

After that, a witness family for (C) through the aligned forms remains the concrete route to \(n\to\infty\) in degree 3.

Verification gate. A review. It re-read the truncated-Dade record and the syzygies-as-Tor proposition, and the two-cell bound is proved in observation 8. Observations 1 to 7 rest on standard facts:

  • semicontinuity of rank, and base change for field extensions;
  • the isomorphism \(\mathbb F_3[x]/(x^3)\cong\mathbb F_3[\mathbb Z/3]\);
  • Hochster's formula, Fröberg's conjecture, Dade's lemma and Mnëv universality, recalled as context.

Semicontinuity of Tor in flat families, in observation 9, is to be checked in this setting during the next step. The literature is to be read in the sources before any is used in a proof. No claim is registered.

A Gröbner degeneration makes degree 3 combinatorial: pattern-avoiding matchings carry the double points

23 September 2026 · Working proof, conjecture and finite check · Lex degeneration of the functional top algebra, degree 3, \(n=5\) to 8. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The observations entry proposed to degenerate the algebra \(G\), not the forms. What is the initial ideal of \(G\)'s relations, and does degree-3 Tor vanishing hold on the degenerate algebra? If it does, semicontinuity carries it back to \(G\).

General statement. lem:degeneration-transfer: for any term order, if the double-point map on the degenerate algebra \(\operatorname{in}(G)\) attains \(\min(\gamma_3,M(\gamma_1-1))\) at some forms, the double-point map on \(G\) attains it for generic forms over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\). conj:initial-complex-patterns: in the lex order, for every \(n\ge5\), the initial complex through degree 3 is the complex of matchings of the \(R\times(N-1)\) board avoiding five fixed label patterns. ex:degenerate-double-points: the degenerate algebra attains the maximal double-point rank at \(n=6,7,8\).

Correction: the chessboard connectivity theorem is already in the record

The residual entry called the connectivity theorem of Björner, Lovász, Vrećica and Živaljević "imported, not re-read" and asked for it to be imported with its exact statement. The record already contains it, and its searches did not surface it:

  • the homological bound over \(\mathbb F_2\) for every rectangular board, as augmented cycle filling for cell counts \(k<\min(a,b,\lfloor(a+b+1)/3\rfloor)\), formalized in Lean (formalization/third-party-claims/ChessboardHomology.lean, by a star-cover argument);
  • its informal expansion, proof:chessboard-homology-expansion;
  • its binary uses, thm:chessboard-quadratic-design-extension and thm:functional-PHP-stable-filtration.

What this thread needs is the bound over \(\mathbb F_3\): the dimension formula, the range of (B) and the edge sequence's hypothesis. As published, the theorem is a homotopy statement: the chessboard complex is \((\nu-2)\)-connected. That gives integral homology vanishing in the same range, and so vanishing over \(\mathbb F_3\). So the \(\mathbb F_3\) range is available as an imported statement, pending a re-read of the source. What the record lacks is a verified \(\mathbb F_3\) proof. The formalized star-cover argument is over \(\mathbb F_2\), and vanishing over \(\mathbb F_2\) alone would not imply vanishing over \(\mathbb F_3\). Porting it with oriented faces is needed only for a verified proof. The residual and edge-sequence entries' dependence is restated accordingly.

The degeneration

\(G\) is the polynomial ring in the cells \(x_{r,c}\) modulo squares, row and label collisions, and the row sums. Eliminate \(x_{r,N-1}=-\sum_{c<N-1}x_{r,c}\), and write \(y_{r,c}\), \(c<N-1\), for the remaining cells.

  • The squares and collisions of the \(y\) are monomials. Modulo them the basis is the matchings of the \(R\times(N-1)\) board.
  • Collisions with the eliminated label become one quadric per pair of rows, \(q_{rs}=\sum_{c\ne c'}y_{r,c}y_{s,c'}\), \(r<s\). Indeed \(x_{r,N-1}^2\) and \(x_{r,N-1}y_{r,c}\) expand into squares and row collisions of the \(y\). The label collision \(x_{r,N-1}x_{s,N-1}=\sum_{c,c'}y_{r,c}y_{s,c'}\) becomes \(q_{rs}\) modulo the label collisions \(y_{r,c}y_{s,c}\).

So \(G=\mathbb F_3[y]/\bigl((y^2)+(\text{collisions})+(q_{rs})\bigr)\). Every non-squarefree monomial is a leading term, so for any term order the standard monomials are squarefree matchings closed under taking subsets: a simplicial complex \(\Delta'\). The degenerate algebra \(\operatorname{in}(G)\) has the faces of \(\Delta'\) as basis, and multiplies faces to their union when that is a face, and to 0 otherwise.

degeneration.py computes, in lex order with the variables \(y_{r,c}\) decreasing in \(r(N-1)+c\), the leading monomials of \(\operatorname{span}\{q_{rs}m\}\) in each degree \(t\). They are the pivots of an echelon form over the matchings, sorted in decreasing order, from the compiled \(\mathbb F_3\) elimination. The standard monomials number exactly \(\dim G_t=\binom Rt\delta_t(N)\): 165 and 280 at \(n=5\), 399 and 1645 at \(n=6\), in degrees 2 and 3.

The initial complex through degree 3

patterns.py compares the minimal generators of the initial ideal with an explicit list at \(n=5,6,7,8\), and they agree exactly:

  • size 2: \(\{(r,0),(s,1)\}\) for every \(r<s\);
  • size 3: for every row triple \(r<s<u\), the four label patterns \((0,2,3)\), \((1,0,2)\), \((1,2,0)\), \((1,2,3)\) on rows \(r,s,u\).

The counts are 15, 21, 28, 36 generators of size 2 and 80, 140, 224, 336 of size 3, that is \(\binom R2\) and \(4\binom R3\).

Conjecture (initial-complex patterns). For every \(n\ge5\), in this lex order, the faces of \(\Delta'\) of size at most 3 are the matchings of size at most 3 of the \(R\times(N-1)\) board that avoid these five patterns. Consequently the degree-\(\le3\) part of \(\operatorname{in}(G)\) is a fixed combinatorial algebra, uniform in \(n\). The patterns involve only labels 0 to 3 and the relative order of rows. The size-2 part is immediate: \(q_{rs}\) has leading term \(y_{r,0}y_{s,1}\), and each row pair gives one relation. A proof in degree 3 would reduce the S-pairs of the \(q_{rs}\) to computations on three rows and the first four labels.

Transfer to \(G\)

Lemma (degeneration transfer). Fix a term order and linear forms \(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_M\) in the \(y\). Write \(\gamma_t=\dim G_t=\dim\operatorname{in}(G)_t\), so \(\gamma_1=R(N-1)\). In characteristic 3, \(\ell^3=\sum_ia_i^3y_i^3=0\) on both algebras, since the cross coefficients 3 and 6 vanish and \(y_i^2=0\). So each \(\ell_j\) lies in the kernel of its own block, and the double-point rank is at most \(\min(\gamma_3,M(\gamma_1-1))\) on both. If the double-point map \((u_j)\mapsto\sum_j\ell_j^2u_j\), from \(\bigoplus\operatorname{in}(G)_1\) to \(\operatorname{in}(G)_3\), attains that bound, then the same map on \(G\) attains it for forms in a nonempty Zariski-open set over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\).

Proof. Choose an integral weight \(w\) with \(\operatorname{in}_w(I)=\operatorname{in}(I)\) in degrees \(\le3\). The weight homogenization \(I_\tau\) of \(I\) gives the standard Gröbner family over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3[\tau]\): it is flat, its fiber at \(\tau=0\) is \(\operatorname{in}(G)\), and for \(\tau\ne0\) the substitution \(y_i\mapsto\tau^{w_i}y_i\) identifies the fiber with \(G\). By flatness the standard monomials are a basis of every fiber in each degree. In that basis the double-point map with the fixed forms \(\ell_j\) is a matrix whose entries are polynomials in \(\tau\). Its rank at \(\tau=0\) is at most its rank at all but finitely many \(\tau\), and it is bounded above by the same maximum on every fiber. At such \(\tau\ne0\), the map is the double-point map of \(G\) at the rescaled forms \(\ell_j(\tau^{w}y)\), so the bound is attained at some point, and attaining it is an open condition. \(\square\)

Maximal rank on \(G\) at \(M\le\gamma_3/(\gamma_1-1)\) is hypothesis (b) of the glued double-points theorem, for forms over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\). The transfer gives genericity, not an \(\mathbb F_3\) witness. Our direct \(\mathbb F_3\) witnesses on \(G\) stand as before.

Double points on the degenerate algebra

degeneration.py --dp computes the double-point map on \(\operatorname{in}(G)\) through the face products, for one random \(\mathbb F_3\) sequence of forms in \(y\), rejection-sampled so that every row has a nonzero coefficient. It checks every prefix \(M\) against \(\min(\gamma_3,M(\gamma_1-1))\):

\(n\)\(\gamma_1\)\(\gamma_3\)prefixes \(M\)deviations
6351,6451 to 57none
7485,8241 to 144none
86316,0441 to 299none

The degenerate algebra therefore has maximal double-point rank at every \(M\) in these ranges. With the lemma, degree-3 Tor vanishing on \(G\) for generic forms at \(n=6,7,8\) follows again, now through a combinatorial algebra.

What this changes

If the pattern conjecture holds, degree-3 Tor vanishing for all \(n\) would follow from a rank statement on an explicit monomial algebra: matchings avoiding five fixed label patterns, uniform in \(n\). The transfer goes one way only, so this is a sufficient condition. We expect the Horace machinery to simplify there, with monomial pieces after a row split and combinatorial trace, residual and coupling maps. That is unchecked. Also, the lex order breaks the symmetry between rows, so the pieces left after a row split need not be pattern algebras of the same kind.

Next step. On odd-prime-clause-transfer: first, prove the pattern conjecture by reducing the S-pairs of the \(q_{rs}\) to three rows and four labels. Then attack double points on the pattern algebra with the row Horace split, where every map is combinatorial. The residual and trace pieces should reduce to smaller pattern algebras. The coupling is the part to watch. Count first: the pattern algebra's pieces at \(n=6\) are the same sizes as before (\(\gamma_3=1645\)), so each Horace piece can be checked directly on it.

    • the maximal-rank bound on both algebras, which is where characteristic 3 enters, and \(\gamma_t\) defined;
    • the sampling described exactly;
    • "reduces" weakened to "would follow from", and the Horace expectations hedged;
    • the correction completed: the published theorem is homotopical, so the \(\mathbb F_3\) range is available as an import pending a re-read, and only a verified proof needs the port.

The changes weaken or correct claims, and the one addition, the upper bound, is a one-line computation. So no further pass was made.

The pattern theorem: the degenerate algebra is pattern-avoiding matchings for every n, and the degree-3 dimension formula needs no import

23 September 2026 · Working proof and finite check · Lex initial complex of the functional top algebra, degrees 2 and 3, every board with \(N\ge5\) labels. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The degeneration entry found the lex initial complex through degree 3 to be the matchings avoiding five label patterns, exactly at \(n=5,\dots,8\), and conjectured it for all \(n\). This cycle proves it.

General statement. thm:initial-complex-patterns: on the functional board with \(R\) rows and \(N\ge5\) labels (the PHP board has \(R=n+1\), \(N=n\), so \(n\ge5\)), in the lex order of the degeneration entry, the standard monomials of degree at most 3 of the functional top algebra \(G\) are exactly the matchings of the \(R\times(N-1)\) board avoiding the five patterns. cor:three-row-dimension-formula: over \(\mathbb F_3\), the zero-marginal arrays on 3 rows with \(N\ge5\) labels have dimension \(\delta_3(N)=N^3-6N^2+8N-1\), and the \(3\times N\) chessboard complex has \(\tilde H_1(\,\cdot\,;\mathbb F_3)=0\) (false for \(N=3,4\)), with no appeal to the connectivity theorem.

Setting

As in the degeneration entry: a board with \(R\) rows and \(N\) labels (for PHP, \(R=n+1\), \(N=n\)), \(L=N-1\), variables \(y_{r,c}\) (\(c<L\)), and \(G=\mathbb F_3[y]/\bigl((y^2)+(\text{collisions})+(q_{rs})\bigr)\) with \(q_{rs}=\sum_{c\ne c'}y_{r,c}y_{s,c'}\). The lex order has the variables decreasing in \(r(N-1)+c\). Let \(Q\) be the image of the ideal generated by the \(q_{rs}\) in the span of matchings.

  • \(Q_t\) splits over \(t\)-sets of rows, since \(q_{rs}m\) lives on the rows of \(m\) and \(\{r,s\}\).
  • On a row triple \(a<b<c\) a matching is an injective label tuple \((f_a,f_b,f_c)\). A monomial is larger in lex exactly when its tuple is lexicographically smaller: the row-\(a\) variable decides first, and a smaller label means a larger variable.
  • So the leading term of an element is its smallest tuple.

The theorem

Theorem (initial-complex patterns). Let \(N\ge5\), so \(L\ge4\).

  1. In degree 2, on rows \(r<s\), the leading terms of \(Q_2\) are exactly \(y_{r,0}y_{s,1}\).
  2. In degree 3, on rows \(a<b<c\), the leading terms of \(Q_3\) are exactly:
    • the tuples with a 0 on a row above a 1, of which there are \(3(L-2)\);
    • the four tuples \((0,2,3)\), \((1,0,2)\), \((1,2,0)\) and \((1,2,3)\).

So the standard monomials of degree at most 3, the faces of \(\Delta'\) of size at most 3, are the matchings avoiding these patterns.

Proof.

Degree 2. On rows \(r<s\), \(Q_2=\langle q_{rs}\rangle\). The smallest tuple of \(q_{rs}\) is \((0,1)\).

Degree 3: leading terms from explicit elements. On rows \(a<b<c\):

  • A tuple with 0 on row \(i\), 1 on a lower row \(j\), and label \(d\) on the third row \(k\) is the smallest tuple of \(q_{ij}y_{k,d}\). The support of \(q_{ij}y_{k,d}\) is all injective tuples with \(d\) on row \(k\).
  • \(q_{ac}y_{b,0}\) is the sum of all tuples with 0 on row \(b\), so its smallest tuple is \((1,0,2)\).
  • \(q_{ab}y_{c,0}\) likewise has smallest tuple \((1,2,0)\).
  • For a label \(x\), \[e_{\ne x}=\sum_{d\ne x}q_{ab}y_{c,d}-q_{bc}y_{a,x}-q_{ac}y_{b,x}\] is the sum of all tuples avoiding \(x\). The first sum covers every tuple with \(f_c\ne x\), and the two subtracted terms are exactly the tuples in it with \(f_a=x\), respectively \(f_b=x\). So \(e_{\ne0}\) has smallest tuple \((1,2,3)\), and \(e_{\ne1}\) has \((0,2,3)\).
  • The four patterns contain no 0 above a 1, so these are \(3(L-2)+4\) distinct leading terms. Hence \(\dim Q_3^{(abc)}\ge3(L-2)+4\).

Degree 3: an upper bound on the leading terms. On the triple, \(G_3^{(abc)}\) is the quotient of the \(L(L-1)(L-2)\) tuples by \(Q_3^{(abc)}\). It is dual to the zero-marginal arrays on 3 rows with \(N\) labels. By the chessboard-cycles lemma, those form the top cycle space \(Z_2\) of the chessboard complex \(M_{3,N}\). Neither this lemma (residual entry) nor the duality \(K_t=G_t^*\) (gluing entry) uses the connectivity theorem; both are direct identifications. That complex is connected for \(N\ge3\): two cells in different rows and labels are adjacent, and any two cells are joined through a third. So \(\tilde H_0=0\) and \(\tilde H_{-1}=0\). The Euler–Poincaré relation then gives \[\dim Z_2=\dim\tilde H_2=\tilde\chi+\dim\tilde H_1\ge\tilde\chi=\delta_3(N),\] the alternating face count with the empty face. So \(\dim Q_3^{(abc)}\le L(L-1)(L-2)-\delta_3(N)\).

The bounds meet. With \(N=L+1\), \[L(L-1)(L-2)-3(L-2)-4=N^3-6N^2+8N-1=\delta_3(N).\] So \(\dim Q_3^{(abc)}=3(L-2)+4\), and the leading terms found are all of them. \(\square\)

Corollary (three-row dimension formula). For \(N\ge5\), over \(\mathbb F_3\), the zero-marginal arrays on 3 rows with \(N\) labels have dimension exactly \(\delta_3(N)\), and \(\tilde H_1(M_{3,N};\mathbb F_3)=0\).

Proof. Equality holds throughout the chain above, so \(\dim\tilde H_1=0\). \(\square\)

The two-row formula \(\delta_2(N')=N'^2-3N'+1\), for \(N'\ge3\), is the cycle space of a connected graph, also unconditional. The residual entry's all-\(n\) range used exactly \(\delta_2(n-2)\) and \(\delta_3(n)\). In the residual entry's range section, \(m=\binom n2\delta_2(n-2)\) is the two-row formula with \(N'=n-2\ge4\), and \(\gamma_3=\binom{n+1}3\delta_3(n)\) is the three-row formula with \(N=n\ge6\). So the residual theorem's range, \(m\ge\gamma_3/(\gamma_1-1)\) for all \(n\ge6\), now holds without the connectivity theorem. Only that dependency is removed. The edge sequence's degree-3 hypothesis, about the \(3\times n\) board minus one cell, and the formula for more than three rows still rest on the connectivity theorem or on computation.

Check

verify_patterns.py checks exactly, for \(L=4,\dots,9\) on one row triple:

  • the identities for \(e_{\ne0}\) and \(e_{\ne1}\), and the supports of the two \(q\cdot y\) products;
  • their smallest tuples;
  • that every tuple with a 0 above a 1 is the smallest tuple of some \(q\cdot y\) product;
  • the count identity.

All hold, consistent with the generator lists found at \(n=5,\dots,8\).

What this gives, and next

The transfer lemma uses the degenerate algebra only in degrees at most 3: the double-point map runs from \(\operatorname{in}(G)_1\) to \(\operatorname{in}(G)_3\). So faces of size at most 3 determine it, and the theorem describes exactly those. Degree-3 Tor vanishing for generic forms on \(G\), at every \(n\ge5\), would therefore follow from maximal double-point rank on one explicit algebra: the matchings of size at most 3 of an \(R\times(N-1)\) board avoiding five fixed patterns, with faces multiplying to their union. The theorem says nothing about faces of size 4 or more, which a degree-4 version would need.

Next step. On odd-prime-clause-transfer: prove maximal double-point rank on the pattern algebra for all \(n\).

  • Setting. Rows enter the patterns only through their order, so induction on the last row is natural. In lex order the last row's variables are the smallest, so removing the last row leaves a pattern algebra of the same kind with one row fewer. Check that first.
  • Split. Split the degree-3 faces by whether they use the last row. The pieces are:
    • a trace on the smaller pattern algebra;
    • a residual of degree-2 faces on the other rows, restricted by the patterns;
    • a coupling, now combinatorial.
  • Count first. At \(n=6\), \(\gamma_1=35\) and \(\gamma_3=1645\) (degeneration entry). Compute each piece's rank for random forms before attempting proofs.
  • What ends the step. An inductive proof, or the piece that fails.

Verification gate.

  • Re-read: the degeneration entry's construction, and the chessboard-cycles lemma for the identification of \(G_3\) per triple with \(Z_2\).
  • Checks: verify_patterns.py, and the recorded pattern computations at \(n=5,\dots,8\).
  • Claim searches: initial ideal, Gröbner, pattern-avoiding matchings and leading terms; and three rows, zero marginals, dimension formula, Euler characteristic and chessboard. They found the degeneration records, the chessboard records and lem:matching-marginal-cycle. That lemma identifies compatible matching moments with augmented chessboard cycles, the moment-side counterpart of the chessboard-cycles identification used here. None states the pattern theorem or the unconditional three-row formula.
  • Fresh-context review: the reviewer confirmed the lex order, the explicit elements and their supports, the distinctness of the leading terms, the connectivity argument, the Euler-characteristic signs, the count identity and the two-row formula, and found no mathematical error. It required changes, all adopted: definitions of \(n\), \(R\) and \(N\); the independence of the lemmas used from the connectivity theorem; the exact residual dependency removed and the ones that remain; the degrees the transfer lemma needs; an anchor for the sizes; and the field for \(\tilde H_1\). They restrict or clarify claims, so no further pass was made.

Row induction on the pattern algebra: the residual comes free, three rows are defective, and the coupling remains

23 September 2026 · Working proofs and finite checks · Double points on the pattern algebra, row split and a tropical bound. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The pattern theorem reduced degree-3 Tor vanishing for generic forms, at every \(n\), to maximal double-point rank on an explicit monomial algebra \(P\), by the transfer lemma. Its next step proposed a proof by induction on the last row: split the degree-3 faces into trace, residual and coupling pieces, compute each piece's rank first, and end with an inductive proof or the piece that fails. The cycle ends with the piece that fails. The coupling is the same obstacle as on \(G\), and the monomial structure of \(P\) is not used by the row split. A tropical lower bound that does use it is tested as the next mechanism.

General statement. lem:pattern-row-reduction: on the pattern algebra \(P(R,L)\) in characteristic 3 with \(R\ge4\) and \(L\ge5\), the last-row split is exact. The residual splits into label slices without a quotient, and it is injective for generic forms at every \(M\le\lceil\gamma_3/(\gamma_1-1)\rceil\). So maximal rank at \((R,L)\) is equivalent to a trace-plus-coupling rank condition, which reduces to the coupling alone when the trace has maximal rank on \(P(R-1,L)\). At the capacity the trace is overdetermined, so the coupling cannot be avoided. Separately, the three-row defect: on three rows every form imposes at most \(\gamma_1-2\) conditions, so the induction cannot start below four rows. lem:tropical-leading-bound: for forms whose coefficients carry tie-free integer powers of \(t\), the double-point rank of generic forms is at least the number of distinct pairs (winning form, heaviest cell) over the 3-faces, and that number is at most \(M(\gamma_1-2)\), so tie-free weights never certify maximal rank at or below the capacity. The finite checks are ex:pattern-general-boards and ex:tropical-tie-free-count.

Setting

For \(R\) rows and \(L\ge4\) labels, \(P=P(R,L)\) has as basis the matchings of at most 3 cells of the \(R\times L\) board, with rows \(0,\dots,R-1\) and labels \(0,\dots,L-1\), that avoid two kinds of pattern:

  • a 0 on a row above a 1;
  • on rows \(a<b<c\), the label tuples \((0,2,3)\), \((1,0,2)\), \((1,2,0)\) and \((1,2,3)\).

Two disjoint faces multiply to their union when that is a face, and every other product is 0; in particular \(x^2=0\) for a cell \(x\); degrees above 3 are not used. By the pattern theorem, \(P(R,L)\) is the lex initial algebra of the functional top algebra of the board with \(R\) rows and \(N=L+1\ge5\) labels, through degree 3. The PHP board has \(R=n+1\) and \(L=n-1\).

Whether a matching avoids the patterns depends only on the relative order of its rows. So a row triple carries \(T(L)=L(L-1)(L-2)-3(L-2)-4=\delta_3(L+1)\) faces:

  • \(\gamma_1=RL\);
  • \(\gamma_3=\binom R3T(L)\);
  • the capacity is \(\operatorname{cap}(R,L)=\gamma_3/(\gamma_1-1)\): 48.4 at \(n=6\), 123.9 at \(n=7\).

For forms \(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_M\in P_1\), the double-point map is

\[\mu:\bigoplus_{j}P_1\to P_3,\qquad(u_j)\mapsto\sum_j\ell_j^2u_j.\]

In characteristic 3, \(\ell^3=6\sum_{x<y<z}c_xc_yc_z\,xyz=0\), so \(\ell_je_j\in\ker\mu\) (the Frobenius syzygies), and \(\operatorname{rank}\mu\le\min(\gamma_3,M(\gamma_1-1))\), called maximal rank. Genericity is over an infinite field of characteristic 3, such as \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\).

The row reduction

Let \(P'\) be the span of the faces avoiding the last row \(R-1\), and \(P^{\rm last}\) the span of those using it. Write \(\ell_j=\ell'_j+\lambda_j\), with \(\lambda_j\) supported on the last row, and \(u_j=u'_j+v_j\) likewise. As in the coupling-dual entry, define:

  • the trace \(\mu':(u'_j)\mapsto\sum_j\ell'^2_ju'_j\);
  • the residual \(\rho:(v_j)\mapsto\sum_j\ell'^2_jv_j\);
  • \(\beta:\ker\mu'\to P^{\rm last}_3\), \(u'\mapsto2\sum_j\lambda_j\ell'_ju'_j\).

For a label \(c\), let \(V_c\subseteq P'_2\) be spanned by the 2-faces \(f\) of \(P'\) such that \(f\cup\{(R-1,c)\}\) is a face, and let \(\pi_c\) be the coordinate projection onto \(V_c\). Write \(d_c=\dim V_c\).

Lemma (pattern row reduction). Let \(R\ge4\), \(L\ge5\), in characteristic 3. Parts 1 to 3 hold in any characteristic, and parts 1 and 2 for every \(R\ge2\), \(L\ge4\). The bounds \(R\ge4\), \(L\ge5\) enter only the constants of parts 3 and 5; characteristic 3 enters parts 4 and 5, through the Frobenius syzygies and the definition of maximal rank.

  1. Exact split. \(P'=P(R-1,L)\), \(P_t=P'_t\oplus P^{\rm last}_t\), and \(\operatorname{rank}\mu=\operatorname{rank}\mu'+\dim(\operatorname{im}\rho+\beta(\ker\mu'))\).
  2. Slices. \(P^{\rm last}_3=\bigoplus_cy_{R-1,c}V_c\), and \(\rho=\bigoplus_c\rho_c\) with \(\rho_c:\mathbb F^M\to V_c\), \((v_{jc})_j\mapsto\sum_jv_{jc}\pi_c(\ell'^2_j)\). Here \(v_j=\sum_cv_{jc}y_{R-1,c}\). With \(C=\binom{R-1}2\):
    • \(d_0=C((L-1)(L-2)-1)\), and \(d_c\) has the same value for \(c\ge4\);
    • \(d_1=C(L-2)(L-3)\);
    • \(d_2=C((L-1)(L-2)-2)\);
    • \(d_3=C((L-1)(L-2)-3)\).
    The minimum is \(d_1\).
  3. Residual. For generic \(\ell'_j\), \(\rho\) is injective if and only if \(M\le d_1\). Moreover \(\lceil\operatorname{cap}(R,L)\rceil\le d_1\).
  4. Reduction. For generic forms and \(M\le d_1\), \(\operatorname{rank}\mu=\operatorname{rank}\mu'+ML+\dim\kappa\), with \(\kappa=(\operatorname{im}\rho+\beta(\ker\mu'))/\operatorname{im}\rho\). So \(\mu\) has maximal rank exactly when \(\operatorname{rank}\mu'+\dim\kappa=\min(\gamma_3,M(\gamma_1-1))-ML\). When \(\mu'\) has maximal rank on \(P(R-1,L)\), this is a condition on \(\kappa\) alone. Maximal rank at every \(M\) follows from maximal rank at \(M=\lfloor\operatorname{cap}\rfloor\) and \(M=\lceil\operatorname{cap}\rceil\).
  5. The trace is overdetermined. \(\operatorname{cap}(R,L)-\operatorname{cap}(R-1,L)>5\). So at \(M=\lfloor\operatorname{cap}(R,L)\rfloor\), maximal rank requires \(\dim\kappa\) equal to \(M(\gamma'_1-1)-\operatorname{rank}\mu'\), which is positive when the trace has maximal rank.

Three-row defect. In characteristic 3, on \(P(3,L)\) with \(L\ge4\), every form \(\ell\) satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}(u\mapsto\ell^2u)\le\gamma_1-2\). So \(\operatorname{rank}\mu\le M(\gamma_1-2)\), below maximal rank whenever \(M(\gamma_1-2)<\gamma_3\), in particular at \(M=1\), since \(\gamma_1-2=3L-2<T(L)\) for \(L\ge4\). The rank bound itself needs no bound on \(L\). On \(R\ge4\) rows the row rescalings used below give only the Frobenius syzygy.

Proof.

  1. A face of \(P\) avoiding the last row avoids the patterns exactly as a face of \(P(R-1,L)\), since the patterns see only relative row order. A product of faces uses the last row exactly when a factor does. So the split is a direct sum compatible with multiplication by \(P'\). Two cells in one row multiply to 0, so \(\lambda_j^2=0\), \(\ell_j^2=\ell'^2_j+2\lambda_j\ell'_j\), and \(2\lambda_j\ell'_jv_j=0\). This is all the proof of the coupling-dual lemma uses. Its parts 1 and 2 therefore hold verbatim on \(P\).
  2. A 3-face using the last row is \(f\cup\{(R-1,c)\}\) with \(f\) a 2-face of \(P'\) in \(V_c\). The basis vectors \(y_{R-1,c}f\) for distinct pairs \((c,f)\) are distinct faces, which gives the direct sum. For a 2-face \(g\) of \(P'\), \(y_{R-1,c}\,g\) is the face \(g\cup\{(R-1,c)\}\) when \(g\in V_c\), and 0 otherwise. So \(\ell'^2_jy_{R-1,c}=y_{R-1,c}\,\pi_c(\ell'^2_j)\), which gives the formula for \(\rho\). For the counts, take a pair of rows \(a<b<R-1\) and labels \((x,y)\) distinct from \(c\). A 0 above a 1 excludes \((x,y)=(0,1)\), and also any 0 when \(c=1\). The four triple patterns end in \(c=3,2,0,3\) and exclude \((0,2)\) and \((1,2)\) when \(c=3\), \((1,0)\) when \(c=2\), and \((1,2)\) when \(c=0\). Counting the ordered pairs from the \(L-1\) labels other than \(c\) gives the four values. The smallest is \(d_1\): \((L-2)(L-3)<(L-1)(L-2)-3\) for \(L\ge4\). The values sum to \(C\,T(L)=\gamma_3-\gamma'_3\).
  3. For a 2-face \(\{x,y\}\) of \(P'\), \((x+y)^2=2xy\), since \(x^2=y^2=0\). So the squares of forms in \(P'_1\) span \(P'_2\), and their projections span each \(V_c\). If \(M\le d_c\), some \(M\) squares have independent projections to \(V_c\). The corresponding \(M\times M\) minor is a polynomial in the coefficients of \(\ell'_1,\dots,\ell'_M\), nonzero at one point, hence on a nonempty Zariski-open set. Intersecting over the finitely many \(c\) gives injectivity of every \(\rho_c\) when \(M\le d_1\). If \(M>d_1\), then \(\rho_1\) cannot be injective. For the bound, \(T(L)\le L(L-1)(L-2)\) gives \[\frac{\operatorname{cap}(R,L)}{d_1}\le\frac{\binom R3L(L-1)(L-2)}{(RL-1)\binom{R-1}2(L-2)(L-3)}=\frac{RL}{RL-1}\cdot\frac{L-1}{3(L-3)}\le\frac{20}{19}\cdot\frac23<0.71.\] The last step holds because both factors decrease in \(R\) and \(L\). Since \(d_1\ge3\cdot3\cdot2=18\), \(\lceil\operatorname{cap}\rceil\le0.71d_1+1\le d_1\).
  4. By parts 1 and 3, \(\dim(\operatorname{im}\rho+\beta(\ker\mu'))=ML+\dim\kappa\). The two opens of generic forms (for \(\rho\) and for \(\mu'\)) intersect. For monotonicity: \(\dim\ker\mu\ge M\), with equality exactly at rank \(M(\gamma_1-1)\). If the kernel is spanned by the Frobenius syzygies at \(M_0\) forms, then for the first \(M<M_0\) of them the kernel is its intersection with the first \(M\) summands, again Frobenius. Surjectivity at \(M_0\) persists for more forms.
  5. Write \(\binom R3=C\cdot R/3\) and \(\binom{R-1}3=C(R-3)/3\). Then \[\operatorname{cap}(R,L)-\operatorname{cap}(R-1,L)=\frac{C\,T(L)}{3}\Bigl(\frac R{RL-1}-\frac{R-3}{(R-1)L-1}\Bigr)=\frac{C\,T(L)\,(2RL-3)}{3(RL-1)((R-1)L-1)},\] because \(R((R-1)L-1)-(R-3)(RL-1)=2RL-3\). With \((2RL-3)/(RL-1)\ge2-1/19\) and \(C/((R-1)L-1)\ge(R-2)/(2L)\), the difference is at least \(1.9\,(R-2)T(L)/(6L)\ge1.9\cdot2\cdot9.4/6>5\). Here \(T(L)/L\) increases from \(47/5=9.4\) at \(L=5\). So \(\lfloor\operatorname{cap}(R,L)\rfloor>\operatorname{cap}(R-1,L)\). Then \(M(\gamma'_1-1)>\gamma'_3\), so a maximal-rank trace is surjective with a kernel beyond the Frobenius syzygies. The claim follows from part 4 with \(\min(\gamma_3,M(\gamma_1-1))=M(\gamma_1-1)=M(\gamma'_1-1)+ML\). \(\square\)

Proof of the three-row defect. Let \(a_r\) be the row-\(r\) part of \(\ell\), so \(a_r^2=0\) and \(\ell^2=2\sum_{r<s}a_ra_s\). For scalars \(\lambda_r\), \[\ell^2\sum_r\lambda_ra_r=2\sum_{r<s<t}(\lambda_r+\lambda_s+\lambda_t)\,a_ra_sa_t.\] On three rows this is \(2(\lambda_0+\lambda_1+\lambda_2)a_0a_1a_2\), which vanishes on the 2-dimensional space \(\sum\lambda_r=0\). The \(a_r\) are independent, since they are nonzero with disjoint supports. On \(R\ge4\) rows the products for different row triples lie in different summands. Where they are nonzero, the kernel condition is \(\lambda_r+\lambda_s+\lambda_t=0\) for every triple. Two triples differing in one row force all \(\lambda_r\) to be equal, and \(3\lambda=0\) holds, which is the Frobenius syzygy. This rules out only this defect on four or more rows. If instead some \(a_r=0\) on three rows, say \(a_0=0\), then \(\ell^2=2a_1a_2\) and \(\ell^2u=2a_1a_2u_0\) depends only on the row-0 part \(u_0\), so the rank is at most \(L\le\gamma_1-2=3L-2\). \(\square\)

Relation to the record. Parts 1 and 4 adapt the coupling-dual lemma from \(G\) to \(P\). Part 5 is the pattern-algebra case of the overdetermined row-split trace recorded in the row Horace entry and used in no Horace balancing. On \(G\) the residual's slots are taken modulo the image of the row sums, and the residual theorem needed the dimension formula for its range. On \(P\), parts 2 and 3 are free, which is the only simplification. The coupling \(\kappa\) is the object that conj:aligned-double-points addresses on \(G\), and the edge-sequence entry's heuristic, that window syzygies are cross-class, applies unchanged.

Computations

pieces_P.py computes the full, trace and residual ranks on \(P(R,L)\) with the compiled prefix-rank kernel, for uniform random \(\mathbb F_3\) forms, every \(M\) up to a bound in one pass. The coupling is the difference.

  • PHP boards. At \(n=6\) and \(7\), every \(M\le57\) and \(M\le144\) was tested, for two families of last-row parts: uniform, and one cell \(y_{R-1,\,j\bmod L}\). Unlike the aligned family, the other rows here are uniform. All four pieces equal their expected values for both families.
  • General boards (grid.sh, grid2.sh, seeds.sh), every \(M\le\lceil\operatorname{cap}\rceil+1\), uniform family. The summary is from summarize.py.

\(L=4\), \(R=4,\dots,9\)Deviations in every seed tried, at varying \(M\). Outside \(L\ge5\); not separated from \(\mathbb F_3\) sampling

slice_counts.py checks \(T(L)\), \(\gamma_3\), the four slice dimensions and \(\lceil\operatorname{cap}\rceil\le d_1=\min_cd_c\) by enumeration on the 49 boards \(R=4,\dots,10\), \(L=5,\dots,11\). All agree, with \(\lceil\operatorname{cap}\rceil/d_1\le0.556\).

What the row induction needs

By the lemma, a row induction at fixed \(L=n-1\) from \(R=4\) to \(R=n+1\) needs two inputs:

  • maximal rank on \(P(4,L)\) for every \(L\ge5\), itself an infinite family, which holds at \(L=5,\dots,9\) in the checks;
  • the coupling condition on \(\kappa\) at every \((R,L)\) with \(5\le R\le L+2\), at \(M=\lfloor\operatorname{cap}\rfloor\) and \(\lceil\operatorname{cap}\rceil\).

The second is the open obligation (C) of the row Horace entry, now on \(P\). The degeneration made the residual free, but not the coupling. Nothing in the row split uses that \(P\) is monomial.

A tropical lower bound that uses the monomial structure

Lemma (tropical leading bound). Give the forms coefficients \(c_{j,x}t^{w_j(x)}\), with generic \(c\) and integer weights \(w_j\). For a 3-face \(F\), let \(m(F)=\min_{j,\,u\in F}\bigl(w_j(F)-w_j(u)\bigr)\), where \(w_j(F)=\sum_{x\in F}w_j(x)\). Let \(A_0\) be the matrix of \(\mu\) with row \(F\) replaced by the coefficients of its terms of order \(m(F)\). Then generic forms over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\) give \(\operatorname{rank}\mu\ge\operatorname{rank}A_0\). If the weights are tie-free, that is each minimum is attained at a single pair \((j(F),z(F))\), then \(z(F)\) is the \(w_{j(F)}\)-heaviest cell of \(F\). In that case \(\operatorname{rank}A_0\) is the number of distinct pairs \((j(F),z(F))\), and this number is at most \(M(\gamma_1-2)\).

Proof. The entry of \(\mu\) at row \(F\) and column \((j,u)\), \(u\in F\), is \(2c_{j,x}c_{j,y}t^{w_j(F)-w_j(u)}\), where \(\{x,y\}=F\setminus u\). Multiply row \(F\) by \(t^{-m(F)}\). The matrix becomes \(A_0+tB(t)\), with polynomial entries, and its rank over \(\mathbb F(t,c)\) is unchanged. A minor nonzero in \(A_0\) is a polynomial in \(t\) and \(c\) that is nonzero at \(t=0\), so it is nonzero at some point with \(t\ne0\) in \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\). That point is a choice of forms of rank at least \(\operatorname{rank}A_0\). The forms of rank at least \(r\) form a Zariski-open set, so once it is nonempty it contains generic forms. When the weights are tie-free, each row of \(A_0\) has one nonzero entry, at \((j(F),z(F))\). Rows sharing a column are proportional, and rows at distinct columns are independent. For the upper bound, the two \(w_j\)-lightest cells are never the \(w_j\)-heaviest cell of a 3-face, which has three distinct cells. So form \(j\) meets at most \(\gamma_1-2\) columns, and the count is at most \(M(\gamma_1-2)\). \(\square\)

This is the simplest case of Draisma's tropical approach to secant dimensions (J. Pure Appl. Algebra, 2008; not re-read). In the general method, ties give blocks with several entries per row, whose ranks are computed locally.

tropical_count.py evaluates the tie-free bound with 20 draws each of uniform random real weights (tie-free almost surely, and replaceable by integers without changing the minima) and of noisy bilinear functions of row and label. The fraction reported is the best draw's count over the maximal rank \(\min(\gamma_3,M(\gamma_1-1))\).
