Conjecturally, a column span is free when its worst direction is: a graded Dade-type criterion fits 96 of 97 cases, and the defects are not overfull Gale flats

24 September 2026 · Lemma, refutations, conjecture and finite check · Column model, spans of dimension 2 to 4, degrees 3 to 5, \(n\le20\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The relative-line review put the column component first. It asked for the special position behind the column model's degree-4 and degree-5 defects, and a criterion for them. The cycle ends with a criterion, or with defects that no simple special position explains.

General statement. conj:worst-direction-freeness: for fixed span dimension \(d\) and degree \(t\), and \(n\ge n_0(d,t)\), a column span is free in the column model through degree \(t\) exactly when every nonzero direction has column count \(c\ge2t-1\), that is \(c_{\min}\ge2t-1\), the single-form threshold. lem:gale-group-algebra: in characteristic 3 the Gale-dual quotient is \(T_r/(m_1^2,\dots,m_n^2)\) with \(T_r=\mathbb F_3[(\mathbb Z/3)^r]\), so the column component's model is again squares of linear forms on a group algebra. The finite check ex:worst-direction-tests supports the conjecture in 96 of 97 configurations. Its one exception, near capacity, refutes the version without the size condition, and the check also refutes the overfull-flat explanation of the defects.

The group-algebra form

Lemma (Gale quotient as a group-algebra quotient). In the setting of prop:column-model-gale, \(\operatorname{Sym}(V)/(m_1^2,\dots,m_n^2)=T_V/(m_1^2,\dots,m_n^2)\), where \(T_V=\operatorname{Sym}(V)/(v^3:v\in V)\cong\mathbb F_3[(\mathbb Z/3)^r]\), \(r=\dim V\).

Proof. The \(m_j\) span \(V\), since the \(e_j\) span \(\mathbb F_3^n\). For \(v=\sum_jc_jm_j\), characteristic 3 gives \(v^3=\sum_jc_j^3m_j^3\), and \(m_j^3=m_j\cdot m_j^2\) lies in the ideal. So every cube of a linear form lies in \((m_j^2)\), and the quotient factors through \(T_V\). \(\square\)

So the column component's model is an instance of the thread's own question: squares of linear forms on a free group algebra, here in the Gale-dual position. tr_squares.py computes \(\mathrm{HF}(T_r/(m_j^2))\) directly. It equals the column model's in all six degree-4 configurations at \(n=15,16,17\), an independent check of the proposition. For \(n\) uniform random vectors in \(\mathbb F_3^r\), five draws per configuration, the result reaches the free prediction in 20 of 30 draws, against 3 of the 6 model configurations. Random \(\mathbb F_3\) vectors are themselves often in special position, so these data do not separate special position from a counting effect. A first draft read only two draws per configuration and claimed all were free; the full count above replaces that claim.

Not flats

gale_flats.py computes, for the model configurations of the Gale entry, the largest number of Gale points in flats of rank 1, 2 and 3. In every configuration, defective or free, the Gale points are in general position there: at most 1, 2 and 3 points respectively. So the defects do not come from overfull Gale flats of rank at most 3, the only flats tested. That candidate is refuted; special position of other kinds is not.

The worst direction

In the primal hole configurations, the defects did not track repeated values or lines. They tracked the minimum column count \(c_{\min}\) over the span's nonzero directions. For a single column form with count \(c\), the occupancy theorem and the \(\mathbb Z/3\) heuristic of the Gale entry give freeness exactly through degree \(\lceil c/2\rceil\), that is through degree \(t\) iff \(c\ge2t-1\). In the positive-prediction cases of the Gale entry, every degree-4 defect had \(c_{\min}\le6\), every degree-4 free span \(c_{\min}\ge7\), and every degree-5 span tested \(c_{\min}\le8\) and a defect.

worst_direction.py tests this deliberately. It draws random hole functions with a prescribed \(c_{\min}\) and compares freeness in the model with the criterion \(c_{\min}\ge2t-1\).

\(d\)\(t\)\(n\)\(c_{\min}\)CasesAgree
2310, 12, 143–62424
2413, 15, 175–82424
3415, 16, 175–82424
3518, 207–1088

4416, 186–866

All predictions were positive. The exception is \(n=12\), \(d=4\), \(t=3\), \(c_{\min}=6\): Hilbert function \((1,7,16,8)\) against the free \((1,7,16,5)\). The prediction there is small (5), close to capacity. The same \(d\) and \(t\) at \(n=14\) agree in all six cases. So the criterion without a size condition is false, and the conjecture requires \(n\ge n_0(d,t)\).

A heuristic for why the worst direction might decide. Dade's lemma detects ungraded, full freeness over \((\mathbb Z/3)^d\) on cyclic shifted subgroups over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\), and the conjecture is a graded, truncated analogue of it. Non-rational directions have column counts no smaller than the rational ones. For \(u\in\overline{\mathbb F}_3^{\,d}\), let \(W_u=u^\perp\cap\mathbb F_3^d\), a proper rational subspace. Two holes take the same value under \(u\) exactly when \(\varphi(j)-\varphi(j')\in W_u\). A rational \(u'\ne0\) with \(W_u\subseteq u'^\perp\) has classes that are unions of classes of \(u\), so \(c(u)\ge c(u')\ge c_{\min}\). But \(\ell_u\) can take more than three values in \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\), and the single-form threshold is recorded only for \(\mathbb F_3\) values. So "no worse" also needs freeness to depend only on the partition of the holes, monotonically under refinement. That step is open. The recorded truncated Dade counterexample shows that such a lemma fails for general column tensors. The data suggest the truncated analogue holds for column spans away from capacity; this is a heuristic, not an argument. The rank-variety theory of elementary abelian groups (Carlson, Friedlander–Pevtsova) is the tool for a proof, recalled here as context.

What it would give

Everything in this paragraph is conditional on the conjecture and on the model being exact for \(A\), which is checked in degree 3 in three cases. Condition (c) at PC degree \(D\) concerns the syzygies of the squares \(\ell_i^2\) in degrees at most \(D\). By the truncation step of the Künneth lemma, \(\operatorname{Tor}_1\) through degree \(D\) depends only on degrees at most \(D\). Freeness of the column component over the algebra of its forms through degree \(D\) therefore makes that \(\operatorname{Tor}_1\) the algebra's own: Frobenius \(y_ie_i\) and Koszul \(y_j^2e_i-y_i^2e_j\). So the threshold is \(c\ge2D-1\) at degree \(t=D\). Q-robustness bounds every value class by \(n-Q-1\) holes, so \(c\ge Q+1\), and \(c\ge2D-1\) is \(Q\ge2D-2\), the threshold of conj:column-component-splitting. Such a component would be free through degree \(D\). Its top syzygies would be Koszul and Frobenius, which lift by the recorded Frobenius lemma. That is condition (c) of the relative gluing theorem for the column component. The only remaining column obstruction would be narrow directions, with \(c<2t-1\), which involve few holes, the local structure the local-fall conjecture reduces away. At the goal's degree, \(t\) of order \(\log n\), the threshold \(c\ge2t-1\) is logarithmic in \(n\).

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the Gale proposition, the occupancy theorem's threshold, the recorded truncated Dade counterexample, and the relative gluing theorem's condition (c). A fresh-context reviewer checked the lemma and its proof, the table counts, the exception, the \(n=14\) agreement and the flat counts against the result files. It required changes, all adopted:

  • withdraw the random-vector claim, which rested on a partial reading of the output, and give the full count of 20 of 30;
  • mark the criterion as conjectural in the title;
  • correct the non-rational-direction argument and state its open step;
  • make the degree bookkeeping and the \(Q\)/\(c\) correspondence explicit and label the chain conditional;
  • limit the flat refutation to rank at most 3;
  • mark the Dade link as heuristic.

The changes restrict or withdraw claims, so no second pass was made.

Remaining gap

A proof of the worst-direction criterion with an explicit \(n_0(d,t)\), perhaps via rank varieties, since \(T_r\) is a group algebra. Model exactness for \(A\). And the exceptional configuration at \(n=12\): what distinguishes it.

Every pencil class obeys the worst-direction criterion except the affine plane, and a tensor-decomposition proof fails on degree-0 blocks

24 September 2026 · Finite check and a failed proof route · Pencils in the column model, degrees 3 to 5, \(n\le14\), exhaustive up to symmetry. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The worst-direction entry proposed proving conj:worst-direction-freeness for pencils first. Before a proof, the pencil case turns out to be finite at each size and can be decided exhaustively. The cycle does that and tries one proof route.

General statement. The statement under test is conj:worst-direction-freeness for \(d=2\): for \(n\ge n_0(2,t)\), a pencil of column forms is free in the column model through degree \(t\) iff its four rational directions all have column count \(c\ge2t-1\). The finite check ex:pencil-worst-direction confirms it on every pencil class at degree 3 for \(n=10,11,12\), at degree 4 for \(n=9,\dots,14\), and at degree 5 for \(n=12,13,14\). The only exceptions at the sizes tested are two configurations at degree 3. One is the affine plane \(\mathrm{AG}(2,3)\), every point once, at \(n=9\). The other is the plane minus a point, the recorded occupancy pair, at \(n=8\). So \(n_0(2,3)=10\) at the sizes tested.

Reduction to a finite check

A pencil's column model depends only on the multiset of value points \((\varphi_1(j),\varphi_2(j))\in\mathbb F_3^2\), up to the affine group \(\mathrm{AGL}(2,3)\) of 432 elements:

  • hole permutations do not change \(R\) or the quotient;
  • a change of basis of the pencil does not change the span;
  • adding a constant to a hole function changes a form by a multiple of \(\sum_jt_j=0\).

pencil_exhaustive.py enumerates the compositions of \(n\) into 9 multiplicities, reduces them modulo \(\mathrm{AGL}(2,3)\), and discards the classes whose span is not 2-dimensional modulo constants. For each remaining class it computes \(c_{\min}\) over the four rational directions and the model Hilbert function through degree \(t\), by exact GF(3) ranks, and compares freeness with the criterion.

Results

399493yesthe plane: \(c_{\min}=6\), \(\mathrm{HF}\) (1, 6, 12, 7) against (1, 6, 12, 5)
310, 11, 12156, 252, 403allyesnone

The two exceptions are the most uniform configurations, every point of the plane used once, rather than concentrated ones. At \(n=9\) the prediction is positive and the plane still fails, so the size condition of the conjecture is needed even for pencils. From \(n=10\) on no exception occurs at the degrees tested.

A proof route that fails

A natural attempt drops the relation \(\sum_jt_j=0\) by treating the constant as a third direction. It writes \(\mathbb F_3[t]/(t_j^2)=\bigotimes_p B_p\) over value points \(p\), with \(B_p\) the \(m_p\)-th tensor power of the Jordan block \(J_2\), inflated along the affine character \((1,p)\). The algebra \(\mathbb F_3[y]/(y^3)\) with primitive \(y\) is a Hopf algebra, so projective tensor anything is projective. Each \(B_p\) is free over \(\mathbb Z/3\) up to one small block in its middle degree. Expanding, every term with free factors along a spanning set of characters is free. The non-free terms need all points off some line to contribute their small blocks, which first happens near degree \(c/2\) for that line's direction: the criterion.

The argument fails for two reasons. A point of multiplicity 1 contributes \(B_p=J_2\), a non-free block starting in degree 0. And freeness through degree \(t\) is a statement about relations in low degree, not about direct summands: the whole module has dimension \(2^n\), never divisible by 27, so it is never free. The two exceptions are exactly configurations made of multiplicity-1 points. A proof must control truncated freeness directly. The rank-variety or vector-bundle view of the pencil, Grothendieck splitting of its kernel sheaf on \(\mathbf P^1\), is the remaining candidate.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the worst-direction conjecture and its data, and the recorded pencil splitting identity. The symmetry reduction preserves the model's Hilbert function, by the three reasons listed. The enumeration is exhaustive over compositions, and every number above is read from the result files. The exceptions coincide with the recorded occupancy pair and the model's recorded full-plane configuration. The entry has no proof, only a failed route, and was not sent to a reviewer.

Remaining gap

A proof for pencils, and \(n_0(d,t)\) in general. Model exactness for \(A\), which carries every column statement to the board: the next step tests it on all pencil classes at \(n=8,9\).

The column model is a direct summand of the weak PHP algebra, so every column defect lifts to the board

24 September 2026 · Working proof · The weak unary top algebra over its column subalgebra, every \(n\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. Every column statement since the Gale entry was made in the column model, with its exactness for the board algebra \(A\) only computed. The user asked for general formulas instead of further cases. The cycle asks what the relation between \(A\) and the model is, for every \(n\).

General statement. prop:column-model-summand holds for every \(n\) and every column span. As a module over the column subalgebra, the weak unary top algebra \(A\) over \(\mathbb F_3\) decomposes as \(A=R\oplus A_{\ge1}\) by a grading, the U-degree. \(R=\mathbb F_3[C_1,\dots,C_n]/(C_j^2,\sum_jC_j)\) is exactly the column model, the U-degree-0 part. Consequently, for any column span:

  • \(\mathrm{HF}(A/(\ell_\varphi)A)=\mathrm{HF}(R/(\ell_\varphi)R)+\mathrm{HF}(A_{\ge1}/(\ell_\varphi)A_{\ge1})\);
  • the board's excess over the free prediction is the model's excess plus that of \(A_{\ge1}\);
  • if the model is not free through degree \(t\), neither is \(A\).

Setting

\(A=\mathbb F_3[x_{ij}:i\in[n+1],\,j\in[n]]/(x_{ij}^2,\ x_{ij}x_{i'j}\ (i\ne i'),\ r_i)\) with row sums \(r_i=\sum_jx_{ij}\), as in the component-hypothesis entry. Its column sums are \(C_j=\sum_ix_{ij}\), and a column-type form is \(\ell_\varphi=\sum_j\varphi(j)C_j\). \(K=\mathbb F_3[C_1,\dots,C_n]/(C_j^2)\) is the free column algebra, and the model \(R\) is \(K/(\sum_jC_j)\).

The decomposition

Proposition (column model as a summand). Let \(B=\mathbb F_3[x]/(x_{ij}^2,\ x_{ij}x_{i'j})\), so \(A=B/(r_0,\dots,r_n)\). For each hole \(j\) let \(U_j=\operatorname{span}\{x_{ij}:i\ge1\}\). Then:

  1. \(B=\bigotimes_jB_j\) with \(B_j=\mathbb F_3\oplus\mathbb F_3C_j\oplus U_j\), all products inside \(B_j\) zero. Hence \(B=\bigoplus_{S\subseteq[n]}K_{[n]\setminus S}\otimes U_S\), with \(K_T=\mathbb F_3[C_j:j\in T]/(C_j^2)\) and \(U_S=\bigotimes_{j\in S}U_j\). Call \(|S|\) the U-degree. The summand of U-degree \(k\) is a \(K\)-submodule, with \(C_j\) acting as zero on the factor \(U_j\).
  2. \(r_i\) has U-degree 1 for \(i\ge1\), and \(r_0\equiv s:=\sum_jC_j\) modulo \((r_1,\dots,r_n)\), with \(s\) of U-degree 0. So the ideal \((r_0,\dots,r_n)=(s,r_1,\dots,r_n)\) is homogeneous for the U-degree, and \(A=\bigoplus_{k\ge0}A^{(k)}\) as \(K\)-modules.
  3. \(A^{(0)}=K/(s)=R\).

Proof.

  1. The relations of \(B\) involve one hole at a time, so \(B\) is the tensor product of the algebras \(B_j=\mathbb F_3[x_{0j},\dots,x_{nj}]/(\text{all products})=\mathbb F_3\oplus V_j\), with \(V_j\) the span of the \(x_{ij}\). Since \(x_{0j}=C_j-\sum_{i\ge1}x_{ij}\), \(V_j=\mathbb F_3C_j\oplus U_j\). Expanding the tensor product over the choice, for each \(j\), of \(\mathbb F_3\oplus\mathbb F_3C_j\) or \(U_j\) gives the sum over \(S\). The column sums act factorwise and kill \(U_j\), since products in \(V_j\) vanish. So each summand is a \(K\)-submodule on which \(C_j\) for \(j\in S\) acts as 0, and it is isomorphic to \(K_{[n]\setminus S}\otimes U_S\).
  2. For \(i\ge1\), \(r_i=\sum_jx_{ij}\) with \(x_{ij}\in U_j\), which is U-degree 1. And \(r_0=\sum_jx_{0j}=\sum_jC_j-\sum_{i\ge1}r_i\). Multiplication by an element of fixed U-degree shifts the U-degree by that amount: products of summands for \(S\), \(S'\) vanish unless \(S\cap S'=\emptyset\), where they land in \(S\cup S'\), or unless a \(C_j\) meets \(U_j\), where they are 0. So the ideal generated by U-homogeneous elements is U-homogeneous, and the quotient inherits the grading as \(K\)-modules.
  3. The ideal \(\sum_{i\ge1}r_iB\) lies in U-degree at least 1. So the U-degree-0 part of \(A\) is \(B^{(0)}/(sB)^{(0)}=K/sK\). \(\square\)

Corollary. Let \(\ell_{\varphi_1},\dots,\ell_{\varphi_d}\) be column forms, and let \(S_d=\mathbb F_3[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_i^3)\), the group algebra of \((\mathbb Z/3)^d\), act on both \(A\) and \(R\) by \(x_b\mapsto\ell_{\varphi_b}\). It is one algebra for both, and it is self-injective. The column subalgebra of \(A\) is exactly \(R\), since \(K\cap I=I^{(0)}=sK\). The forms lie in \(K\), in U-degree 0, so they preserve the decomposition: \(A/(\ell)A=R/(\ell)R\oplus A_{\ge1}/(\ell)A_{\ge1}\). Take the free prediction of a module \(M\) to be the untruncated coefficients \([q^s]\,\mathrm{HS}_M/(1+q+q^2)^d\), which are linear in \(\mathrm{HS}_M\). Since \(\mathrm{HS}_A=\mathrm{HS}_R+\mathrm{HS}_{A_{\ge1}}\), the board's excess is the model's excess plus \(A_{\ge1}\)'s. Freeness over \(S_d\) through degree \(t\) is the vanishing of \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^{S_d}(\mathbb F_3,-)\) in degrees at most \(t\), and \(\operatorname{Tor}_1\) of a direct sum is the direct sum. So if \(R\) is not free through \(t\), neither is \(A\). \(\square\)

What it explains, and what is left

  • Every model defect is a board defect, for every \(n\). This includes the single-form threshold, so the non-free direction of the worst-direction criterion transfers from the model to the board with no computation. In the 54 pencil classes at \(n=8\) and the 25 robust ones at \(n=9\) compared in this cycle's validation runs (board_pencils.py, compare_n9.py), the board's excess was never below the model's. By additivity, that means \(A_{\ge1}\)'s excess was nonnegative in these data. The decomposition alone forces only the lowest nonzero coefficient of a non-free summand's excess to be positive.
  • Model exactness through degree \(t\) is the freeness of \(A_{\ge1}\) through \(t\). Zero excess through \(t\) means that the surjection \(G\otimes S_d\to M\), from lifts \(G\) of generators, is an isomorphism through \(t\). At \(n=9\) the board equals the model in all 25 robust pencil classes (\(c_{\min}\ge4\)), so \(A_{\ge1}\) contributes nothing there. At \(n=8\) it contributes large excesses exactly for narrow pencils (\(c_{\min}\le3\), board excess 27 to 600 in degree 3 against the model's 3 to 8).
  • A route to the free direction. \(A^{(k)}\) is \(\bigoplus_{|S|=k}K_{[n]\setminus S}\otimes U_S\) modulo \(s\) and the images of the \(r_i\) from U-degree \(k-1\). Its pieces are column models on the holes outside \(S\), shifted by \(k\). A robust span loses at most \(k\) of its column count on \([n]\setminus S\) while the degree drops by \(k\): \(c-k\ge2(t-k)-1\) whenever \(c\ge2t-1\). Here \(c\) is the column count of a direction of the span restricted to the holes outside \(S\). Removing a hole lowers each class size of that direction by at most one, so \(c\) drops by at most \(k\). Under the worst-direction conjecture, every piece would then be free in the needed range. Suppose the row-sum relations admit an exact resolution in the U-direction, by pieces of the same form; that resolution is still to be found, and is not the Koszul complex of the \(r_i\), which are not expected to form a regular sequence. Then freeness of \(A^{(k)}\) would follow, because \(S_d\) is self-injective and a module with a finite resolution by free \(S_d\)-modules is free. The truncated form of that step needs care. This is a route, not a result.

With this, the column chain has three links. The proposition carries every model defect to the board. The worst-direction criterion in the model is conjectured, with exhaustive pencil evidence. Model exactness for robust spans is the freeness of \(A_{\ge1}\), for which the route above is the next step.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the weak base's definition in the component-hypothesis entry, the column model and the Gale proposition. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed four points: the tensor structure of \(B\), the splitting \(V_j=\mathbb F_3C_j\oplus U_j\) in any characteristic, the U-grading as an algebra grading, and \(A^{(0)}=K/sK\). It required changes, all adopted:

  • the untruncated, linear free prediction;
  • one self-injective algebra \(S_d\) acting on both \(R\) and \(A\), with the column subalgebra of \(A\) identified with \(R\);
  • nonnegativity of \(A_{\ge1}\)'s excess attributed to the data, not to the decomposition;
  • "through degree \(t\)";
  • the route's caveats: the resolution is not the Koszul complex, \(c\) is defined on sub-hole-sets, and the conjecture is assumed.

The changes restrict or make precise, so no second pass was made.

Remaining gap

Exactness of the U-direction row-sum complex, and the truncated free-resolution step, which together would give model exactness for robust spans. A proof of the worst-direction criterion in the model.

The base condition of relative gluing is the matching-moment theorem on the functional base; on the weak base it splits by row content, and functionality kills the symmetric column sums

24 September 2026 · Working proofs · Condition (a) of relative gluing on the functional and weak unary bases, every \(n\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The relative-line review reduced the goal to three hypotheses of the relative gluing theorem and called the first one, (a), "weak unary PHP alone has no fall below \(D\)", untouched and open at logarithmic degree, on the weak base. The user pointed to our bit PHP paper for inspiration. Its Step 3 rests on a theorem that every low-degree functional of the functional PHP axioms extends, proved from chessboard homology. The cycle asks what exactly (a) needs, on which base, and what a change of base costs the column component.

General statement. lem:functional-relative-gluing: over every field, on the functional unary base with \(N\ge\max(1,2D-1)\) columns and any number of rows, hypothesis (a) of the relative gluing theorem holds, so constraints satisfying (b), (c) and (d) with respect to the functional top algebra \(G\) have no PC refutation of degree \(D\), and neither do they together with the weak base \(\Gamma_{\rm w}\). So (a) is proved on the functional base, as the gluing entry had already used for its own theorem; the review stated it for the weak base, where it remains open. prop:weak-content-splitting: on the weak base, the extension step from degree \(k\) to \(k+1\) splits over row contents \(c\), \(|c|=k+1\); the contents with at most one cell per row form exactly the functional step, and, when \(N\ge\max(1,2k+1)\), (a) for the weak base holds in degree \(k\) exactly when, for every annihilator \(\mu\) of the degree-\(k\) weak NS space, every content with a repeated row has a solution of \(\sum_{j\notin\mathrm{cols}(T)}\nu(T+(i,j))=(2-c_i)\mu(T)\). prop:functional-column-symmetric-relations: \(e_k(C_1,\dots,C_N)=0\) in \(G\) for every \(k\ge1\), while \(e_p\ne0\) in the column model whenever \(N=qp+p-1\) with \(p\nmid q\). So for those \(N\) the column model, a direct summand of the weak algebra, does not embed in \(G\): its image is a proper quotient.

Two versions of the matching-moment theorem

The record holds the theorem in two forms, and a cycle using it must pick the one that covers its field and board.

  • thm:all-field-matching-filtration, informal, working proof: over every field, with \(m\ge B\) rows and \(N\ge2B-1\) columns. It fills oriented chains, with the chain coefficient \((-1)^jz_T\) on a matching missing the \(j\)-th row of the row set.
  • audit:matching-extension-arbitrary-row-count, established and Lean-verified (formalization/claims/MatchingFiltration.lean), and Theorem 3.2 of the paper: over \(\mathbb F_2\) only, for every \(m\), with \(N\ge\max(1,2B-1)\). Its filling is unoriented, since the cycle condition reads \(z_U+z_U=0\).

The formalized version drops the row hypothesis by one remark: if a row set would need \(s>m\) rows, there is no such set and nothing to fill. The oriented argument fills each row set separately in the same way, so the remark applies to it verbatim. Over every field, then, the theorem holds with \(N\ge\max(1,2B-1)\) and any \(m\). Only the \(\mathbb F_2\) case is Lean-verified. \(\mathbb F_3\), the thread's field, needs the oriented informal version. On the PHP board \(m=N+1\ge B\), so the row hypothesis never mattered there. The registry had no edge between the two versions. This entry adds one.

The functional gluing lemma

Setting. \(\mathbb F\) is any field. The functional base \(\Gamma_{\rm f}\) on \(m\) rows and \(N\) columns has generators \(x_{ij}^2-x_{ij}\), \(x_{ij}x_{ij'}\) (\(j\ne j'\)), \(x_{ij}x_{i'j}\) (\(i\ne i'\)) and \(\rho_i-1\), \(\rho_i=\sum_jx_{ij}\). The weak base \(\Gamma_{\rm w}\) omits the row exclusions \(x_{ij}x_{ij'}\). For a generator set \(\Gamma\), \(I_k(\Gamma)\) is the span of the products \(ug\), \(g\in\Gamma\), \(u\) a monomial, \(\deg u+\deg g\le k\). \(B_\Gamma\) is the polynomial ring in the variables and \(z\) modulo the homogenizations \(g^{\rm h}\) of the generators, as in the relative gluing theorem. \(G\) is \(B_{\Gamma_{\rm f}}/zB_{\Gamma_{\rm f}}\), the functional top algebra with relations \(x_{ij}^2\), both exclusions, and \(r_i=\sum_jx_{ij}\).

Step 0 (injectivity is stability). For every generator set and every \(k\), \(z:(B_\Gamma)_k\to(B_\Gamma)_{k+1}\) is injective if and only if \(I_{k+1}(\Gamma)\cap\mathcal P_{\le k}=I_k(\Gamma)\), where \(\mathcal P_{\le k}\) is the space of polynomials of degree at most \(k\).

Proof. Setting \(z=1\) is a linear bijection from the degree-\(k\) forms in the variables and \(z\) onto \(\mathcal P_{\le k}\). Since \(\deg g^{\rm h}=\deg g\), the degree-\(k\) part of the ideal is spanned by the products \(u\,g^{\rm h}z^{e}\) with \(\deg u+e=k-\deg g\), and setting \(z=1\) maps them onto the products \(ug\) with \(\deg u\le k-\deg g\), which span \(I_k(\Gamma)\). For a form \(v\) of degree \(k\), \(zv\) lies in the ideal exactly when \(v|_{z=1}\in I_{k+1}(\Gamma)\), and \(v\) lies in it exactly when \(v|_{z=1}\in I_k(\Gamma)\). \(\square\)

Lemma (functional gluing). Let \(N\ge\max(1,2D-1)\) and \(m\) arbitrary. Let the constraints \(g_b\), \(b\in U\), grouped into members, satisfy hypotheses (b) and (c) of the relative gluing theorem through \(D\) for the base \(\Gamma_{\rm f}\), with tops in \(G\), and let no constraint be a nonzero constant. Then:

  1. \(z\) is injective on \(B_{\Gamma_{\rm f}}/J_U\) below \(D\);
  2. \(\Gamma_{\rm f}\) together with the constraints has no PC refutation of degree \(D\);
  3. \(\Gamma_{\rm w}\) together with the constraints has none either.

Proof. By the all-field theorem with the row remark, applied with \(B=D\), \(I_D(\Gamma_{\rm f})\cap\mathcal P_{\le k}=I_k(\Gamma_{\rm f})\) for every \(k\le D\). For \(k<D\), \(I_{k+1}\subseteq I_D\) gives \(I_{k+1}\cap\mathcal P_{\le k}=I_k\). By Step 0, \(z\) is injective on \(B_{\Gamma_{\rm f}}\) below \(D\), which is hypothesis (a). No functional generator is a constant, so (d) holds. The relative gluing theorem then gives items 1 and 2. Its steps 1 to 4 are linear algebra over the field, and its step 5 uses the socle criterion, which is stated and proved for any field and supplied system. For item 3, \(\Gamma_{\rm w}\subseteq\Gamma_{\rm f}\), so a degree-\(D\) PC refutation from \(\Gamma_{\rm w}\) and the constraints is one from \(\Gamma_{\rm f}\) and the constraints. \(\square\)

Either base may carry the goal's reduction: the complete-board transfer compiles refutations of ordinary unary PHP over the functional linear-row base, as the base remark of the complex line records.

So on the functional base, (a) is a theorem in the linear range \(D\le(N+1)/2\), far beyond the goal's logarithmic degree. It is the paper's Step 3 input with orientations. The gluing entry made this replacement for the glued product-constraints theorem. The relative-line review restated (a) for the weak base and missed that option.

The weak base splits by row content

Whether the line should change base depends on what (a) costs on the weak base. A column-injective set \(T\) is a set of cells with distinct columns; rows may repeat. Its content is the vector \(c(T)\) with \(c_i(T)\) the number of its cells in row \(i\).

Proposition (content splitting). Over every field, for \(\Gamma_{\rm w}\) on \(m\) rows and \(N\) columns and every \(k\ge0\):

  1. The functionals on \(\mathcal P_{\le k}\) annihilating \(I_k(\Gamma_{\rm w})\) are exactly the functions \(\mu\) on column-injective sets of size at most \(k\) satisfying, for \(|T|\le k-1\) and every row \(i\), \[\sum_{j\notin\mathrm{cols}(T)}\mu\bigl(T\cup\{(i,j)\}\bigr)=\bigl(1-c_i(T)\bigr)\mu(T).\tag{W}\] The value on a monomial is \(\mu\) of its support if that support is column-injective, and \(0\) otherwise.
  2. \(z\) is injective on \(B_{\Gamma_{\rm w}}\) in degree \(k\) if and only if, for every such \(\mu\) and every content \(c\) with \(|c|=k+1\), there is a function \(\nu\) on the column-injective sets of content \(c\) with \[\sum_{j\notin\mathrm{cols}(T)}\nu\bigl(T\cup\{(i,j)\}\bigr)=(2-c_i)\,\mu(T)\qquad(i\in\operatorname{supp}c,\ c(T)=c-e_i).\tag{W\(_c\)}\]
  3. For a content with every \(c_i\le1\), (W\(_c\)) is the functional step (OP-marginals) for \(\mu\) restricted to matchings, and it is solvable when \(N\ge\max(1,2k+1)\). (The recorded chessboard-cycle identification treats this case.) So (a) for \(\Gamma_{\rm w}\) through \(D\) is equivalent, when \(N\ge2D-1\), to the solvability of (W\(_c\)) for every content with a repeated row and \(|c|\le D\).

Proof.

  1. Booleanity multiples \(u(x^2-x)\) within degree \(k\) identify every monomial with its squarefree support. Column exclusions kill supports that repeat a column. So an annihilator is a function \(\mu\) on column-injective sets of size at most \(k\), subject only to the row-equation multiples. By Booleanity within degree \(k\), it suffices to take the multipliers \(u=x_T\), \(T\) column-injective, \(|T|\le k-1\). In \(x_T(\rho_i-1)\), the term \(x_Tx_{ij}\) contributes \(\mu(T)\) if \((i,j)\in T\), which happens for \(c_i(T)\) columns. It contributes \(0\) if column \(j\) holds a cell of another row, and \(\mu(T\cup\{(i,j)\})\) if \(j\notin\mathrm{cols}(T)\). This is (W).
  2. By Step 0 and finite-dimensional duality, \(z\) is injective in degree \(k\) if and only if every annihilator of \(I_k\) is the restriction of an annihilator of \(I_{k+1}\). By item 1, the extension must assign values to the column-injective \((k+1)\)-sets so that (W) holds for \(|T|=k\). The equation for \((T,i)\) involves only sets of content \(c(T)+e_i\), and \(c_i(T)=c_i-1\) there, which gives the coefficient \(2-c_i\). Each unknown and each equation belongs to exactly one content, so the system is the direct sum of the systems (W\(_c\)).
  3. For \(c\) the indicator of a row set \(S\), the sets of content \(c\) are the matchings on \(S\), and the equations are those of unused rows, with coefficient \(1\): these are the OP-marginals. \(\mu\) restricted to matchings satisfies (W) for matchings \(T\) and unused rows \(i\), which are the OP-marginals below \(k\). So it annihilates \(I_k(\Gamma_{\rm f})\), and the all-field theorem with \(B=k+1\) extends it. For a matching \(T\) and a used row \(i\), the equation belongs to the content \(c(T)+e_i\), which repeats row \(i\). \(\square\)

Two kinds of repeated content are settled by the argument below.

  • If \(c_i=2\) in \(\mathbb F\) for every \(i\in\operatorname{supp}c\), the right side of (W\(_c\)) vanishes, and \(\nu=0\) solves it. This covers \(c=2e_a\).
  • \(c=2e_a+e_b\), the smallest content on two rows, is solvable when the characteristic is not 2 and \(N\ge5\). A vector orthogonal to the image assigns \(w_A\) to the row-\(b\) equation of a pair \(A\) in row \(a\), and \(h(x,j)\) to the row-\(a\) equation of the set \(\{(a,x),(b,j)\}\). Orthogonality means \(w_A+h(a_1,j)+h(a_2,j)=0\) for \(A=\{a_1,a_2\}\) and every \(j\notin A\). For \(j\ne j'\), put \(d_x=h(x,j)-h(x,j')\). Any two distinct \(x,y\notin\{j,j'\}\) give \(d_x=-d_y\). Three such columns, available when \(N\ge5\), give \(2d_y=0\), so \(h(x,j)=h(x)\) and \(w_A=-h(a_1)-h(a_2)\). The right side pairs with this vector to \(-\sum_xh(x)\sum_{y\ne x}\mu(\{(a,x),(a,y)\})\), where (W) for \(T=\{(a,x)\}\), \(i=a\), makes the inner sum \((1-1)\mu=0\).

The other content of size 3, \(c=3e_a\), has right side \(-\mu\) in every characteristic and is not settled; its solvability depends on the rank of the inclusion matrix of pairs in triples in characteristic \(p\). The general repeated content is open. It is a filling problem on the complex of column-injective sets with at most \(c_i\) cells in row \(i\), a multiple chessboard complex in the sense of Jojić, Vrećica and Živaljević (not yet read). Its unknowns are symmetric, not alternating, in the cells of a repeated row. Heuristically, in characteristic \(p\) this is the difference between symmetric and divided powers, and the chessboard homology need not apply directly; this is not proved.

Functionality kills the symmetric column sums

Changing to the functional base changes the column component's ring. \(C_j=\sum_ix_{ij}\), \(R=\mathbb F[t_1,\dots,t_N]/(t_j^2,\sum_jt_j)\) is the column model, and \(e_k\) is the \(k\)-th elementary symmetric polynomial.

Proposition (functional column relations). Over every field:

  1. \(e_k(C_1,\dots,C_N)=\sum_{|I|=k}\prod_{i\in I}r_i=0\) in \(G\) for every \(k\ge1\).
  2. \(e_k\ne0\) in \(R_k\) if and only if some function \(f\) on \(k\)-subsets of \([N]\) with \(\sum_{j\notin S'}f(S'\cup\{j\})=0\) for every \((k-1)\)-set \(S'\) has \(\sum_Sf(S)\ne0\). Over \(\mathbb F_p\), this holds for \(k=p\) and \(N=qp+p-1\) with \(p\nmid q\).
  3. For those \(N\), \(R\to G\), \(t_j\mapsto C_j\), is not injective. In the weak algebra \(A\) over \(\mathbb F_3\), where \(R\) is a direct summand (prop:column-model-summand), \(e_3(C)\ne0\) at \(N=5,8,14,\dots\), including the thread's recorded board \(n=8\).

Proof.

  1. Expanding \(\prod_{j\in S}C_j\), row exclusions leave the terms that put distinct rows on the columns of \(S\). Summing over \(S\), \(e_k(C)\) is the sum of \(x_T\) over all \(k\)-matchings \(T\). Expanding \(\prod_{i\in I}r_i\), column exclusions leave the terms with distinct columns on the rows of \(I\). Summing over \(I\) gives the same sum. Each \(r_i\) is \(0\) in \(G\).
  2. \(R_k\) is the span of the \(k\)-sets modulo the span of \(\bigl(\sum_jt_j\bigr)t_{S'}=\sum_{j\notin S'}t_{S'\cup\{j\}}\). Its dual is the space of such \(f\), and \(f\) pairs with \(e_k\) to \(\sum_Sf(S)\). For \(k=p\) and \(N=qp+p-1\), the constant \(f=1\) has marginals \(N-p+1=qp\equiv0\). Its total is \(\binom Np\equiv\binom q1\binom{p-1}0=q\pmod p\) by Lucas' theorem.
  3. Item 3 follows from items 1 and 2. In \(A\), \(e_3(C)\) is the image of \(e_3\in R\), which is nonzero by item 2, under the split inclusion. \(\square\)

Dehomogenized, item 1 is the top form of a counting identity of the functional base: \(\sum_T x_T\), over the \(k\)-matchings, equals \(\binom mk\) modulo the base at degree \(k\), because \(\prod_{i\in I}\rho_i=1\). In the column variables it says that the number of occupied \(k\)-sets of holes is \(\binom mk\). This is pigeon counting, and it lives in the column ring only when rows are functional. On the weak base a row may hold \(1+p\) cells, and the identity has no column form.

What this means

On the functional base, hypothesis (a) is not an open PHP problem: it is our own theorem, with the degree range \(D\le(N+1)/2\), and the goal's reduction then needs only (b), (c) and (d) for the constraints, stated on \(G\). The price is the column component. The summand and the worst-direction work were done on the weak algebra \(A\), where the column model is a direct summand. On \(G\) the model does not embed for \(N=qp+p-1\), \(p\nmid q\): every \(e_k(C)\) vanishes there, and \(e_p\), nonzero in \(R\) for those \(N\), is killed, carrying pigeon counting into the column ring. So there are two consistent routes:

  • Functional base. (a) is proved. The column component must be redone on \(G\), starting from the image of \(R\) in \(G\), whose kernel contains every \(e_{jp}\) (the other \(e_k\) are already \(0\) in \(R\), since \(ke_k=e_1e_{k-1}\)).
  • Weak base. The column machinery stands. (a) reduces to the repeated-content systems (W\(_c\)), a PHP-only filling problem of the same kind as the paper's, with one of the two contents of size 3 solved above, in characteristic other than 2 and for \(N\ge5\).

The weak route keeps more recorded work, and its remaining piece of (a) is a single well-posed statement. The next step takes it.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read from their sources: the relative gluing theorem and its proof; the all-field matching filtration and the paper's matching-moment lemma, theorem and corollary, with the Lean audit's scope line (\(\mathbb F_2\), any \(m\)); the socle criterion's field scope; the column-model summand statement; and the complete-board transfer. The claim search for the content splitting found only the chessboard-cycle identification of the 0/1 case. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed Step 0, the row remark over every field, the derivation of (W) and its content decomposition, the \(2e_a+e_b\) argument, and the column computations. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the Step 0 degree argument through \(\deg g^{\rm h}=\deg g\);
  • the socle criterion's any-field scope, stated with a link;
  • (d) assumed for the constraints only;
  • "ordinary PHP" replaced by the weak base, and the review's assessment corrected only on the functional base;
  • the \(N\) hypothesis and the quantifier over \(\mu\) in the content statement;
  • \(3e_a\) recorded as the other, unsettled content of size 3;
  • the symmetric-power remark marked heuristic;
  • non-embedding limited to \(N=qp+p-1\).

The changes only weaken or correct claims, so no further pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • (W\(_c\)) for every content with a repeated row, over \(\mathbb F_3\), at \(N\ge2|c|-1\) or any linear bound.
  • The image of \(R\) in \(G\): is its kernel exactly \((e_p,e_{2p},\dots)\)?
  • (b) and (c) for the column component on either base.

One-row contents of the weak base extend at every degree, and at the tested column counts the weak base falls exactly when the functional base does

24 September 2026 · Working proofs, conjecture and finite check · Hypothesis (a) of relative gluing on the weak unary base. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The base-condition entry reduced hypothesis (a) of relative gluing on the weak base to the repeated-content systems (W\(_c\)). It solved \(c=2e_a+e_b\) and left \(3e_a\) and every larger content open. The weak base keeps the column summand, so (a) there decides whether the relative line can stay on it. The cycle asks whether (a) holds on the weak base in the functional range \(N\ge2D-1\), and proves as much of it as the record's tools allow.

General statement. thm:weak-single-row-contents: over every prime field and for every \(k\), when \(N\ge2k+1\) every content confined to one row, \(c=(k+1)e_a\), has a solution of (W\(_c\)) for every annihilator \(\mu\). The proof combines Wilson's rank formula for inclusion matrices with the weak chain \(\partial\mu_j=(2-j)\mu_{j-1}\). lem:weak-row-reduction: the weak base on \(m\) rows is \(z\)-injective in degree \(k\) whenever the weak base on some \(r\) rows with \(k+1\le r\le m\) and the same \(N\) is. conj:weak-base-stability: over \(\mathbb F_p\), the weak base on \(m\ge D\) rows is \(z\)-injective below \(D\) when \(N\ge2D-1\), as the functional base is; the PHP board has \(m=N+1\ge D\). ex:weak-base-stability-small verifies it over \(\mathbb F_3\) at \(D=4\), \(N=7\), and \(D=5\), \(N=9\), for every \(m\ge D\), and shows that at \(N=6\), \(D=4\) both bases fall.

Setting

As in the base-condition entry: \(\Gamma_{\rm w}\) is the weak base on \(m\) rows and \(N\) columns over \(\mathbb F_p\); an annihilator through degree \(k\) is a function \(\mu\) on column-injective sets of size at most \(k\) satisfying (W); the extension to \(k+1\) splits into the content systems (W\(_c\)), \(|c|=k+1\), with coefficient \(2-c_i\) on row \(i\). For \(t\le u\), \(W_{t,u}\) is the inclusion matrix of \(t\)-subsets against \(u\)-subsets of \([N]\), acting on functions on \(u\)-sets by \((W_{t,u}f)(Z)=\sum_{Y\supseteq Z}f(Y)\). It satisfies \(W_{t,j}W_{j,u}=\binom{u-t}{j-t}W_{t,u}\).

One-row contents

Imported (Wilson's rank formula). R. M. Wilson, A diagonal form for the incidence matrices of \(t\)-subsets vs. \(k\)-subsets, European J. Combin. 11 (1990) 609–615: for \(t\le\min(u,N-u)\), the rank of \(W_{t,u}\) over \(\mathbb F_p\) is \(\sum_i m_i\) over the \(i\le t\) with \(p\nmid\binom{u-i}{t-i}\), where \(m_i=\binom Ni-\binom N{i-1}\). The paper was not read for this entry; the statement is the standard one.

Theorem (one-row contents). Let \(p\) be prime, \(k\ge1\), \(N\ge2k+1\), \(m\ge1\), and let \(\mu\) annihilate \(I_k(\Gamma_{\rm w})\). For every row \(a\), the system (W\(_c\)) with \(c=(k+1)e_a\), \[\sum_{j\notin Y}\nu(Y\cup\{j\})=(1-k)\,\mu_k(Y)\qquad(Y\subseteq[N],\ |Y|=k),\] has a solution \(\nu\) on the \((k+1)\)-subsets of \([N]\). Here \(\mu_t(Y)\) is \(\mu\) of the set of cells \(\{a\}\times Y\).

Proof.

  1. The chain. For \(1\le j\le k\), (W) for \(T=\{a\}\times Y\), \(|Y|=j-1\), and row \(a\) reads \(W_{j-1,j}\mu_j=(2-j)\mu_{j-1}\).
  2. If \(k\equiv1\pmod p\), the right side is \(0\) and \(\nu=0\) solves the system.
  3. The cokernel. The system is \(W_{k,k+1}\nu=(1-k)\mu_k\). It is solvable if and only if \((1-k)\mu_k\) is orthogonal to \(\ker W_{k,k+1}^{\mathsf T}\). Let \(I_{\rm bad}=\{0\le i\le k:i\equiv k+1\pmod p\}\). It is empty exactly when \(k<p-1\); then Wilson's formula with \(t=k\), \(u=k+1\) (valid since \(N\ge2k+1\)) gives full rank and there is nothing to prove. Otherwise its largest element is \(i_*=k+1-p\), so \(k-i_*=p-1\).
    • For \(i\in I_{\rm bad}\), \(W_{k,k+1}^{\mathsf T}W_{i,k}^{\mathsf T}=(W_{i,k}W_{k,k+1})^{\mathsf T}=(k+1-i)W_{i,k+1}^{\mathsf T}=0\), so \(\operatorname{Im}W_{i_*,k}^{\mathsf T}\subseteq\ker W_{k,k+1}^{\mathsf T}\).
    • Wilson's formula with \(t=k\), \(u=k+1\) gives \(\dim\ker W_{k,k+1}^{\mathsf T}=\binom Nk-\operatorname{rank}=\sum_{i\in I_{\rm bad}}m_i\), since \(\binom{k+1-i}{k-i}=k+1-i\).
    • With \(t=i_*\), \(u=k\) (valid since \(i_*<k\le N-k\)), \(\binom{k-i}{i_*-i}\) for \(i\le i_*\) is \(\binom{b+p-1}{b}\) with \(b=i_*-i\). By Lucas' theorem it is \(1\) when \(p\mid b\), from the digits \(\binom{p-1}{0}\binom{b/p}{b/p}\). When \(p\nmid b\) its last digits give \(\binom{r-1}{r}=0\), \(r\) the last digit of \(b\). So \(\operatorname{rank}W_{i_*,k}=\sum_{i\in I_{\rm bad}}m_i\).
    Hence \(\ker W_{k,k+1}^{\mathsf T}=\operatorname{Im}W_{i_*,k}^{\mathsf T}\), and the system is solvable exactly when \((1-k)\,W_{i_*,k}\mu_k=0\).
  4. The chain kills it. For \(i_*<j\le k\), \(W_{i_*,j-1}W_{j-1,j}=(j-i_*)W_{i_*,j}\) with \(1\le j-i_*\le p-1\), so by item 1 \[W_{i_*,k}\mu_k=\prod_{j=i_*+1}^{k}\frac{2-j}{j-i_*}\;\mu_{i_*}.\] The \(p-1\) consecutive values \(j=i_*+1,\dots,k\) meet every residue except \(i_*\equiv k+1\). So some \(j\equiv2\pmod p\) occurs unless \(k\equiv1\), which item 2 handled, and the product is \(0\). \(\square\)

The theorem settles the content \(3e_a\) left open by the base-condition entry: over \(\mathbb F_3\), \(k=2\), \(i_*=0\), and \(W_{0,2}\mu_2=\tfrac{(2-1)(2-2)}{1\cdot2}\mu_0=0\). It uses only row \(a\), so it holds on any board. The obstruction space \(\operatorname{Im}W_{i_*,k}^{\mathsf T}\) is annihilated by the weak chain relations, not by a filling as in the matching-moment theorem.

Row reduction

Lemma (row reduction). Over any field, let \(k+1\le r\le m\). If the weak base on \(r\) rows and \(N\) columns is \(z\)-injective in degree \(k\), so is the weak base on \(m\) rows and \(N\) columns.

Proof. By the content splitting (prop:weak-content-splitting, item 2), it suffices to solve (W\(_c\)) for every annihilator \(\mu\) through \(k\) on \(m\) rows and every content \(c\), \(|c|=k+1\). The support of \(c\) has at most \(k+1\le r\) rows. Choose \(r\) rows \(R'\supseteq\operatorname{supp}c\). The restriction of \(\mu\) to the column-injective sets within \(R'\) satisfies (W) for every \(T\) within \(R'\) and every row \(i\in R'\), since those equations are among \(\mu\)'s. So it annihilates \(I_k\) of the weak base on \(R'\), and by hypothesis, the content splitting and the isomorphism of all \(r\)-row boards, it extends there. The extension solves (W\(_c\)), whose equations and right side involve only rows of \(R'\). \(\square\)

So (a) for the weak base through \(D\) follows from the \(D\)-row board for every \(m\ge D\). The lemma goes one way only: a fall on \(D\) rows is not shown to give a fall on more rows, since extending an annihilator by zero violates (W) for an added row. Boards with fewer than \(D\) rows are not reached.

Exact test

Tested statement. conj:weak-base-stability at the smallest open degrees. For \(p\) odd the contents of size at most 3 are settled: one-row contents by the theorem, \(2e_a+e_b\) by the base-condition entry (characteristic not 2, \(N\ge5\)), and the thin ones by the matching-moment theorem. In size 4, \(4e_a\) is covered by the theorem (\(N\ge7\)), \(2e_a+2e_b\) has right side \(0\), and the thin content is covered by matching moments. The first open contents are \(2e_a+e_b+e_c\) and \(3e_a+e_b\), which enter at \(D=4\), \(N\ge7\). By row reduction the 4-row board gives every \(k<4\) on every \(m\ge4\), and the 5-row board every \(k<5\) on every \(m\ge5\). The quantity is \(\dim\ker(z:B_k\to B_{k+1})=\mathrm{HF}_B(k)+\mathrm{HF}_A(k+1)-\mathrm{HF}_B(k+1)\), from Hilbert functions through \(D\) of the homogenized base \(B\) and of \(A=B/zB\). The conjecture predicts \(0\) for every \(k<D\), and a positive value at \(N\ge2D-1\) refutes it.

base_injectivity.py writes a Macaulay2 script for each case. It reads the Hilbert functions from the leading terms of Gröbner bases truncated at \(D\), which is exact there since all generators are homogeneous. Results, all over \(\mathbb F_3\) (d4.json, d5.json):

baserows × \(N\)\(D\)\(\dim\ker z\) in degrees \(0,\dots,D-1\)role
weak6 × 540, 0, 0, 451control: full PHP board, \(N<2D-1\)
functional4 × 740, 0, 0, 0control: covered by the theorem
weak4 × 740, 0, 0, 0test
weak4 × 640, 0, 0, 69boundary
functional4 × 640, 0, 0, 5boundary
weak5 × 950, 0, 0, 0, 0test

The control falls, so the test can detect a fall. The weak base is injective in every degree below \(D\) on the 4 × 7 board at \(D=4\) and on the 5 × 9 board at \(D=5\), so, by row reduction, on every board with \(m\ge D\) rows at these \((D,N)\). The 5 × 9 case ran in Singular after Macaulay2 stopped with a garbage-collector heap error (a tool failure); Singular reproduced the three Macaulay2 cases exactly (validate_singular.json) and took 521 s. At \(N=6\) both bases fall at degree 4, so the range \(N\ge2D-1\) is sharp for both there.

What this means

On the weak base, hypothesis (a) is now proved for every content confined to one row, and verified at \((D,N)=(4,7)\) and \((5,9)\) over \(\mathbb F_3\) for every \(m\ge D\). The remaining contents mix fat and thin rows. Heuristically, for one fat row with thin rows, the thin equations are a chessboard problem for each fixed fat set, and the fat equations then leave a one-row (Wilson) problem with values in top chessboard designs on the complementary columns; this is not proved, and it suggests where a proof could combine the two methods. The evidence supports keeping the relative line on the weak base, with (a) a conjecture there in the same range as the functional theorem.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the content splitting and the base-condition entry's two settled contents; the matching-moment theorem's range. The claim search for Wilson-type arguments over the weak base found nothing recorded. The computation was checked against a control that must fall (the refuted 6 × 5 board), against the functional theorem at 4 × 7, and across two engines. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed the one-row theorem (chain, identities, both Wilson counts, Lucas cases, residue argument, the empty and \(k\equiv1\) cases) and the row-reduction lemma. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • \(2e_a+2e_b\) removed from the open contents, since its right side is 0;
  • "for \(p\) odd" on the settled size-3 contents;
  • row reduction stated as one-way, with the conjecture and the check restricted to \(m\ge D\);
  • the check's scope given as the exact \((D,N)\) pairs, and the title limited to the tested column counts;
  • the fat-plus-thin sketch labelled heuristic;
  • \(I_{\rm bad}\) and \(i_*=k+1-p\) made explicit.

The changes only weaken or correct claims, so no further pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • Boards with fewer than \(D\) rows, and characteristic 2, where \(2e_a+e_b\) is open.
  • Wilson's rank formula is imported without reading the paper.

The weak base has no falls below D when N ≥ (p−1)D²: a free seed in a block of columns makes the column tensor power free in low degree

24 September 2026 · Working proof · Hypothesis (a) of relative gluing on the weak unary base, every \(p\), \(D\le\sqrt{N/(p-1)}\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The repeated-contents entry proved hypothesis (a) on the weak base only for one-row contents, and verified it through \(D=5\). The user asked for (a) settled in general. The goal needs it at degree \(D=O(\log N)\), so any range \(N\ge\mathrm{poly}(D)\) suffices. The cycle asks for a proof in such a range.

General statement. thm:weak-base-stability-quadratic: over any field of characteristic \(p\), the homogenized weak unary base on \(m\ge D\) rows and \(N\ge(p-1)D^2\) columns is \(z\)-injective below \(D\). So hypothesis (a) of the relative gluing theorem holds on the weak base at the goal's logarithmic degree. The proof rests on lem:free-seed-tensor: if a graded module \(W\) over the Hopf algebra \(T=\mathbb F[R_1,\dots,R_u]/(R_i^p)\), with primitive \(R_i\), lives in degrees \(\ge0\) and satisfies \(W_0=\mathbb F\cdot w\) and \(\operatorname{Ann}_T(w)=0\), then \(W^{\otimes n}\otimes M\) is, for every graded \(T\)-module \(M\) living in degrees \(\ge0\), a free module plus a module concentrated in degrees \(\ge n\). The row sums then have only Frobenius syzygies through degree \(D\), and these lift.

Setting

\(\mathbb F\) has characteristic \(p\). The weak base on \(m\) rows and \(N\) columns has generators \(x_{ij}^2-x_{ij}\), \(x_{ij}x_{i'j}\) (\(i\ne i'\)) and \(\rho_i-1\), \(\rho_i=\sum_jx_{ij}\). Put \(\tilde A_z=\mathbb F[x,z]/(x_{ij}^2-x_{ij}z,\ x_{ij}x_{i'j})\), \(f_i=r_i-z\) with \(r_i=\sum_jx_{ij}\), and \(B=\tilde A_z/(f_1,\dots,f_m)\), the homogenized weak base. Put \(\tilde A=\tilde A_z/z\tilde A_z=\mathbb F[x]/(x_{ij}^2,\ x_{ij}x_{i'j})\) and \(A=\tilde A/(r_1,\dots,r_m)\), the weak top algebra.

Step 1: falls come from non-Frobenius syzygies

Lemma. \(\ker(z:B_k\to B_{k+1})\) is the image of the connecting map \(\delta:H_1(r_1,\dots,r_m;\tilde A)_{k+1}\to B_k\), and \(\delta\) vanishes on the classes of the cycles \(r_i^{p-1}a\,e_i\), \(a\in\tilde A_{k+1-p}\). (With \(e_i\) in degree 1, a cycle of degree \(k+1\) has coefficients in \(\tilde A_k\).)

Proof.

  1. \(\tilde A_z\) is free over \(\mathbb F[z]\) with basis the monomials \(x_T\), \(T\) column-injective. The relations \(x_{ij}^2-x_{ij}z\) and \(x_{ij}x_{i'j}\) form a Gröbner basis for any degree order with every \(x_{ij}>z\), in which \(x_{ij}^2\) leads: pairs with coprime leading terms and pairs of monomials reduce to \(0\), and the remaining ones, \(x_{i'j}(x_{ij}^2-x_{ij}z)-x_{ij}(x_{ij}x_{i'j})=-x_{ij}x_{i'j}z\), reduce to \(0\). So \(z\) is a nonzerodivisor on \(\tilde A_z\).
  2. The Koszul complexes \(K=K(f;\tilde A_z)\) have free terms, so \(0\to K(-1)\xrightarrow{z}K\to K(r;\tilde A)\to0\) is exact. Its long exact sequence contains \(H_1(r;\tilde A)_{k+1}\xrightarrow{\delta}H_0(K)_k\xrightarrow{z}H_0(K)_{k+1}\), and \(H_0(K)=B\). Hence \(\ker z=\operatorname{im}\delta\).
  3. \(\delta\) of a cycle \((a_i)\), \(a_i\in\tilde A_k\), is computed thus: take any homogeneous lifts \(\tilde a_i\in(\tilde A_z)_k\); then \(\sum_i\tilde a_if_i=zu\) for a unique \(u\) of degree \(k\), and \(\delta[(a_i)]\) is the class of \(u\) in \(B_k\). As a connecting map, \(\delta\) does not depend on the lifts or on the representative of the class, so item 4 may use a particular lift.
  4. In \(\tilde A_z\), which has characteristic \(p\), \(r_i^p=\sum_jx_{ij}^p=\sum_jx_{ij}z^{p-1}=r_iz^{p-1}\), since \(x^p=xz^{p-1}\) follows from \(x^2=xz\). So \(\tilde ar_i^{p-1}f_i=\tilde a(r_iz^{p-1}-zr_i^{p-1})=-z\,\tilde ar_i\,(r_i^{p-2}-z^{p-2})\). Since \(r_i^{p-2}-z^{p-2}=f_ih\) for a polynomial \(h\), \(u=-\tilde ar_ihf_i\) lies in \((f)\), and \(\delta\) of the class is \(0\). For \(p=2\), \(u=0\) directly. \(\square\)

Step 2: the free seed

\(T=\mathbb F[R_1,\dots,R_u]/(R_1^p,\dots,R_u^p)\) is a graded Hopf algebra with \(R_i\) primitive and antipode \(R_i\mapsto-R_i\): \((R_i\otimes1+1\otimes R_i)^p=R_i^p\otimes1+1\otimes R_i^p\) in characteristic \(p\), so \((R^p)\) is a Hopf ideal. It is cocommutative, and as a finite-dimensional graded complete intersection it is a graded Frobenius algebra, hence injective as a graded module over itself. \(T\) acts on tensor products diagonally.

Lemma (free seed). Let \(W\) be a graded \(T\)-module in degrees \(\ge0\) with \(W_0=\mathbb F w\) and \(\operatorname{Ann}_T(w)=0\), and let \(M\) be a graded \(T\)-module in degrees \(\ge0\). Then for every \(n\ge1\), \(W^{\otimes n}\otimes M\cong F\oplus Q\) as graded \(T\)-modules, with \(F\) graded free and \(Q\) concentrated in degrees \(\ge n\).

Proof. \(T\to W\), \(t\mapsto tw\), is injective and graded, so its image \(T\cdot w\cong T\) is a graded direct summand by injectivity: \(W=Tw\oplus Q_1\). Since \(W\) lives in degrees \(\ge0\) and \(W_0=\mathbb Fw\), \(Q_1\) lives in degrees \(\ge1\). Expanding \((Tw\oplus Q_1)^{\otimes n}\otimes M\), every term with a factor \(Tw\) is, after moving it to the front (the swap is \(T\)-linear by cocommutativity), \(T\otimes X\cong T\otimes X^{\rm triv}\) by the tensor identity \(t\otimes x\mapsto\sum t_{(1)}\otimes \sigma(t_{(2)})x\), \(\sigma\) the antipode, which is graded free. The remaining term \(Q_1^{\otimes n}\otimes M\) lives in degrees \(\ge n\). \(\square\)

Step 3: the column tensor power

On \(u\) rows, \(\tilde A=V_1\otimes\cdots\otimes V_N\) as algebras, with \(V_j=\mathbb F\oplus\operatorname{span}(x_{1j},\dots,x_{uj})\) and all products in \(V_j^+\) zero. Multiplication by \(r_i=\sum_jx_{ij}\) is the diagonal action of the primitive \(R_i\), with \(R_i\) acting on \(V_j\) as multiplication by \(x_{ij}\). Since \(r_i^p=0\) in \(\tilde A\), this makes \(\tilde A\) a graded \(T\)-module, and \(H_1(r;\tilde A)=\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathcal S}_1(\mathbb F,\tilde A)\) for \(\mathcal S=\mathbb F[R_1,\dots,R_u]\) acting through \(T\).

Let \(b=u(p-1)\) and \(W=V_1\otimes\cdots\otimes V_b\), the algebra \(\tilde A\) on \(b\) columns, with \(w=1\). Then \(\operatorname{Ann}_T(1)=0\). Indeed, for \(0\le a_i\le p-1\), \[\prod_ir_i^{a_i}=\prod_ia_i!\sum_{(P_i)}\prod_ix_{i,P_i},\] the sum over pairwise disjoint column sets with \(|P_i|=a_i\), because \(x^2=0\) removes repeated columns within a row and column exclusions remove shared columns across rows. Since \(\sum_ia_i\le b\), some such family exists. \(\prod a_i!\ne0\) in characteristic \(p\), and different exponent vectors have different row contents, so the images of the basis \(R^a\) of \(T\) are linearly independent.

Write \(N=bn+e\), \(0\le e<b\). Then \(\tilde A\cong W^{\otimes n}\otimes(V_1\otimes\cdots\otimes V_e)\), and by the free-seed lemma \(\tilde A\cong(T\otimes C)\oplus Q\) with \(C\) a graded vector space and \(Q\) in degrees \(\ge n\).

Consequence. For \(d\le n\), \(H_1(r;\tilde A)_d\) is spanned by the classes of cycles \(r_i^{p-1}a\,e_i\). \(\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathcal S}_1(\mathbb F,Q)_d\) is a subquotient of \(Q_{d-1}\otimes\operatorname{span}(e_i)=0\). \(\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathcal S}_1(\mathbb F,T\otimes C)=\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathcal S}_1(\mathbb F,T)\otimes C\), and for the complete intersection \(T=\mathcal S/(R_i^p)\) it is spanned by the cycles \(R_i^{p-1}e_i\). Under the \(T\)-linear embedding of \(T\otimes C\) into \(\tilde A\) these become \(r_i^{p-1}a\,e_i\).

The theorem

Theorem (weak base stability, quadratic range). Over any field of characteristic \(p\), let \(D\ge1\), \(m\ge D\) and \(N\ge(p-1)D^2\). The homogenized weak unary base on \(m\) rows and \(N\) columns is \(z\)-injective below \(D\).

Proof. Fix \(k<D\) and take \(u=D\) rows. On the \(u\)-row board, \(N\ge(p-1)D\cdot D=b\,D\), so \(n\ge D\ge k+1\). By Step 3, \(H_1(r;\tilde A)_{k+1}\) is spanned by Frobenius classes, and by Step 1 \(\delta\) kills them, so \(z\) is injective on \(B_k\) of the \(u\)-row board. This is the notion of the row-reduction lemma: there, \(z\)-injectivity in degree \(k\) is \(\ker(z:B_k\to B_{k+1})=0\), which prop:weak-content-splitting translates into extension of annihilators. Since \(k+1\le u\le m\), the row-reduction lemma (lem:weak-row-reduction) gives \(z\)-injectivity in degree \(k\) on \(m\) rows. \(\square\)

For fixed \(p\), at the goal's degree \(D=c\log N\) the hypothesis \(N\ge(p-1)c^2\log^2N\) holds for large \(N\). So hypothesis (a) of the relative gluing theorem holds on the weak base in the range the goal uses; on the functional base it holds for \(D\le(N+1)/2\) by lem:functional-relative-gluing (base condition). On the weak base the column-model summand remains available.

Relation to the record and the data

  • The theorem gives the quadratic range. The recorded conjecture conj:weak-base-stability asks for \(N\ge2D-1\), the functional theorem's range, and remains open there.
  • The recorded Hilbert functions are consistent with the stronger form of Step 3, freeness of \(\tilde A\) over \(T\) through \(D\) at \(N=2D-1\); equality with the prediction is necessary for that freeness, not sufficient. On the 4 × 7 board at \(D=4\) and the 5 × 9 board at \(D=5\), \(\mathrm{HF}_A\) equals \([q^t]\,(1+uq)^N\bigl((1-q)/(1-q^p)\bigr)^u\), the prediction of freeness on \(u\) rows (1, 24, 230, 1064, 2001 and 1, 40, 685, 6445, 35005, 99649). On the boards that fall it does not: at 4 × 6 the value in degree 4 is 256 against 145. These are the existing result files d4.json and d5.json, reread; no new computation was run.
  • The method is the recorded one of the column-tensor review (lem:column-tensor-exactness), which treats one form over \(\mathbb F_3[x]/(x^3)\) through the decomposition \(V_2\otimes V_2=V_3\oplus V_1[1]\). The free-seed lemma is its version for several forms at once. For one form over \(\mathbb F_3\) with nonzero column parts in \(c\) columns, a seed sits on 2 such columns, \(n=\lfloor c/2\rfloor\), and the lemma recovers the positive half of that result, freeness below \(\lfloor c/2\rfloor\); it does not give the failure at \(\lfloor c/2\rfloor\). The lemma does not contradict the recorded counterexample to a truncated Dade lemma (ex:truncated-dade-special-position), which is a rank-one column tensor on 14 columns with six forms acting diagonally. A seed for six forms over \(\mathbb F_3\) needs a block whose top degree reaches that of \(T\), 12, so at least 12 columns; with 14 columns \(n\le1\), and the lemma says nothing above degree 1.
  • The argument does not transfer to the functional base: row exclusions break the tensor product over columns.
  • Remark, not a result: column-type forms act on the column algebra \(K=\bigotimes_j\mathbb F[C_j]/(C_j^2)\) diagonally as primitive elements, so the lemma would give freeness of \(K\) in low degree if enough disjoint column blocks each carried a free seed. No seed is exhibited here, and the column model is \(K/(\sum_jC_j)\), so a further step would be needed.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the row-reduction lemma and the content splitting; the recorded single-form column-tensor result and the truncated-Dade counterexample. A claim search for the tensor-identity device found only the single-form precedent. A fresh-context reviewer checked Steps 1 to 3 and the theorem: the Gröbner basis, the exact sequence and the connecting map's degrees, the Frobenius lift including \(p=2\), the Hopf ideal, graded self-injectivity, the tensor identity, the seed injectivity and the \(H_1\) conclusion. It recomputed the freeness predictions 1, 24, 230, 1064, 2001 and 145. It found no unused hypothesis. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the hypothesis that \(W\) lives in degrees \(\ge0\);
  • the Gröbner order and S-pairs stated exactly;
  • explicit degrees, and independence of \(\delta\) from the lift;
  • separate symbols for the row count, the column sets, the ring and the antipode;
  • the link between the two notions of \(z\)-injectivity;
  • "for fixed \(p\)", and the functional base cited by claim;
  • the exact relation to the single-form result and the corrected reason for the Dade counterexample;
  • the column-form remark marked as unproved;
  • the Hilbert-function remark stated as a necessary condition only.

The changes add one hypothesis that the application already met and otherwise clarify or weaken, so no further pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • The linear range \(N\ge2D-1\) (conj:weak-base-stability). It is not needed for the goal.
  • (b) and (c) of relative gluing for the column component. The free-seed device is the candidate tool for the column algebra.

Route review: the base condition is settled at logarithmic degree, and the relative line now rests on the column component alone

24 September 2026 · Route review · The relative gluing line after the base-condition cycles. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

General statement. The line's claim is thm:relative-gluing with its base hypothesis discharged. On the weak unary base with \(N\ge(p-1)D^2\) (thm:weak-base-stability-quadratic), or on the functional base with \(N\ge2D-1\) (lem:functional-relative-gluing), constraints whose tops split by members as in hypothesis (b), and whose members have no falls of their own as in (c), have no PC refutation of degree \(D\).

What the goal needs

By the logarithmic-prefix reduction, the goal needs no PC refutation of degree \(D=(4p-1)(p-1)k\), \(k\approx2.5(K+1)\log n\), for the product clauses of any \(n^K\) adversarial families. That is \(D=O(\log n)\) for fixed \(p\) and \(K\), so \(N\ge(p-1)D^2\) holds for large \(n\), and hypothesis (a) is now a theorem there. What remains is (b) and (c) for those families at logarithmic width:

  • (b): the tops split by members. Tested only at width 1, degree at most 3, \(n\le10\). The column constraints do not split among themselves and form one member.
  • (c) for the column component: its own closure has no fall. This is the occupancy window.
  • (c) for narrow members: the local-fall conjecture, tested at width 1 only.

Falsification attempt: the new results against recorded obstructions

If either new result contradicted a recorded obstruction, the base would not be settled. Four confrontations, all with recorded data and statements:

  1. Recorded falls of the weak base. The weak base falls at degree 3 on the refuted 5- and 6-column boards and on the 4 × 6 board at \(D=4\) (repeated contents). All three have \(N<(p-1)D^2=32\). No conflict.
  2. The truncated Dade counterexample (ex:truncated-dade-special-position): six forms on 14 columns. A free seed there needs 12 columns, so the lemma asserts nothing beyond degree 1. No conflict.
  3. The occupancy non-freeness theorem (thm:occupancy-non-freeness): a column form with \(c=n-\#\varphi^{-1}(a)\) is not free through degree \(\lceil c/2\rceil+1\). On the column algebra \(K=\bigotimes_j\mathbb F_3[C_j]/(C_j^2)\), the free-seed lemma gives freeness below \(\lfloor c'/2\rfloor\), where \(c'\) counts the columns with \(\varphi(j)\ne0\). In the model, \(\sum_jC_j=0\) lets \(\varphi\) shift by a constant, so the best \(c'\) is \(c\). The seed bound lies below the recorded failure. No conflict.
  4. The functional column relations (prop:functional-column-symmetric-relations): on the functional base, the column model does not embed. The weak theorem leaves the line on the weak base, where the model is a direct summand. No conflict.

The attempt fails. The confrontations are consistency checks, not tests of (b) or (c).

Assessment of the relative line

The line now has a proved skeleton. Relative gluing, with its base hypothesis proved in the goal's range on the base that keeps the column summand, reduces the goal to local statements about members. Three cycles turned the base condition from "untouched" into a theorem. The free-seed lemma is the first tool in the record that gives freeness of a column tensor power under several forms at once in a provable range.

The obligations that carry the difficulty are untouched: (b) at logarithmic width and (c) for the column component. The column component's closure is where PHP counting enters. On the functional base the counting relations \(e_{jp}(C)\) are visible in the column ring, and on the weak base they are not. So (c) on the weak base asks whether the column constraints of an adversary can reconstruct counting from the column model alone. All evidence for (b) and (c) is at width 1, degree at most 3 on the board (5 in the model) and \(n\le10\).

The highest-risk item and the next step

(c) for the column component is the highest risk. Next step: apply the free-seed lemma to column spans, as the proposed next step states.

  1. State when a block of columns carries a free seed for a span's truncated algebra on \(K\), in terms of the span's column structure.
  2. Pass from \(K\) to the model \(R=K/(\sum_jC_j)\), and by the summand to the weak algebra's column part.
  3. Compare the result with the worst-direction conjecture: it should give a provable, weaker range for the conjecture's free direction.

This would replace the conjectured worst-direction criterion with a theorem in a polynomial range, which is enough for logarithmic degree.

Column seeds: a column span is free in the model through degree t when an affine basis of its values has multiplicity (p−1)(t+1)

24 September 2026 · Working proof · The free direction of the worst-direction conjecture, in a provable range. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The route review left hypothesis (c) for the column component as the highest risk. The recorded chain to (c) for robust column components uses conj:worst-direction-freeness for the column model and model exactness for the board. The cycle applies the free-seed lemma (lem:free-seed-tensor) to column spans, to prove a free direction for the model in a range polynomial in the degree.

General statement. thm:column-seed-freeness: over a field of characteristic \(p\), let \(\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_d\) be hole functions on \([n]\). Call a set \(B\) of holes a seed when, for every \(e\le(d+1)(p-1)\), the products \(\prod_{j\in S}L_j\), \(S\subseteq B\), \(|S|=e\), of the forms \(L_j(y)=y_0+\sum_b\varphi_b(j)y_b\) span the degree-\(e\) part of \(\mathbb F[y_0,\dots,y_d]/(y_0^p,\dots,y_d^p)\). If the holes contain \(t+1\) pairwise disjoint seeds, then the column model \(R=\mathbb F[C_1,\dots,C_n]/(C_j^2,\sum_jC_j)\) is free over \(\mathbb F[\ell_1,\dots,\ell_d]/(\ell_b^p)\), \(\ell_b=\sum_j\varphi_b(j)C_j\), through degree \(t\), with no lower bound on \(n\). One seed already forces \(1,\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_d\) to be linearly independent, since otherwise the \(L_j\) span a proper subspace of the linear forms, so \(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_d\) span a \(d\)-dimensional space of forms. In particular this holds when some affine basis of \(\mathbb F^d\) has all its points taken as values \((\varphi_1(j),\dots,\varphi_d(j))\) by at least \((p-1)(t+1)\) holes each.

The algebra

\(K=\bigotimes_{j=1}^nV_j\) with \(V_j=\mathbb F\oplus\mathbb FC_j\), \(C_j^2=0\), is the free column algebra, and \(R=K/(s)\) with \(s=\sum_jC_j\). Put \(\ell_0=s\) and \(T=\mathbb F[L_0,\dots,L_d]/(L_b^p)\) with \(L_b\) primitive, acting on \(K\) by \(L_b\mapsto\ell_b\). Multiplication by \(\ell_b=\sum_j\varphi_b(j)C_j\), with \(\varphi_0\equiv1\), is the diagonal action in which \(L_b\) acts on \(V_j\) as multiplication by \(\varphi_b(j)C_j\). Since \(\ell_b^p=\sum_j\varphi_b(j)^pC_j^p=0\), \(K\) is a graded \(T\)-module.

Seeds

Lemma (seed criterion). For a set \(B\) of holes, \(\operatorname{Ann}_T(1)=0\) in \(K_B=\bigotimes_{j\in B}V_j\) if and only if \(B\) is a seed.

Proof. For \(0\le a_b\le p-1\), expanding the product and using \(C_j^2=0\) gives \[\prod_bL_b^{a_b}\cdot1=\prod_ba_b!\sum_{S\subseteq B,\ |S|=|a|}\Bigl([y^a]\prod_{j\in S}L_j(y)\Bigr)C_S.\] The \(|a|\) factors go to distinct holes. A hole receiving a factor \(L_b\) contributes \(\varphi_b(j)\), and the sum over assignments with the given multiplicities is the coefficient of \(y^a\), up to the orderings \(\prod a_b!\), which are units. Images of different degrees \(|a|\) are independent. Within degree \(e\), the images of the \(y^a\) with all \(a_b\le p-1\) are independent exactly when the matrix \(\bigl([y^a]\prod_{j\in S}L_j\bigr)_{a,S}\) has full row rank. That is, when the \(\prod_{j\in S}L_j\), reduced modulo \((y_b^p)\), span the degree-\(e\) part of the truncated ring. The basis of the truncated ring is the \(y^a\) with \(a_b\le p-1\). \(\square\)

Lemma (multiplicity seeds). If \(B\) contains \(p-1\) holes with value \(P_i\) for each point \(P_i\) of an affine basis \(P_0,\dots,P_d\) of \(\mathbb F^d\), then \(B\) is a seed.

Proof. The forms \(M_i=y_0+\langle P_i,y'\rangle\), \(y'=(y_1,\dots,y_d)\), are a basis of the linear forms, since the \((1,P_i)\) are linearly independent. In characteristic \(p\) the ideal \((y_0^p,\dots,y_d^p)\) is the ideal generated by the \(p\)-th powers of all linear forms, because \((\sum c_by_b)^p=\sum c_b^py_b^p\). So it equals \((M_0^p,\dots,M_d^p)\), and the truncated ring has the basis \(\prod_iM_i^{k_i}\), \(k_i\le p-1\). Each such monomial is \(\prod_{j\in S}L_j\) for \(S\) made of \(k_i\) of the \(p-1\) holes of value \(P_i\). \(\square\)

The theorem

Theorem (column seeds). Let \(\mathbb F\) have characteristic \(p\), and let \([n]\) contain \(t+1\) pairwise disjoint seeds for \(\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_d\). Then \(\mathrm{HF}(R/(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_d)R)_k=[q^k]\,\mathrm{HS}_R\,\bigl((1-q)/(1-q^p)\bigr)^d\) for \(k\le t\), and \(R\) is a free \(\mathbb F[\ell]/(\ell^p)\)-module plus a part in degrees \(\ge t+1\). For \(p=3\) this is freeness through \(t\) in the sense of conj:worst-direction-freeness, whose divisor \((1+q+q^2)^d\) is \(((1-q^3)/(1-q))^d\); for other \(p\) it is the same notion with \((1-q^p)/(1-q)\).

Proof.

  1. Group the holes as \(B_0,\dots,B_t\) (the seeds) and the rest. \(K=K_{B_0}\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{B_t}\otimes K_{\rm rest}\) as algebras, and multiplication by \(\ell_b\) is the diagonal action of the primitive \(L_b\) on this tensor product, by the Leibniz rule. By the seed criterion, \(T\to K_{B_i}\), \(t\mapsto t\cdot1\), is injective. By graded self-injectivity of \(T\), \(K_{B_i}=T\cdot1\oplus Q_{1,i}\), with \(Q_{1,i}\) in degrees \(\ge1\) because \((K_{B_i})_0=\mathbb F\cdot1\). Expand \(\bigl(\bigotimes_i(T\cdot1\oplus Q_{1,i})\bigr)\otimes K_{\rm rest}\). Every term with a factor \(T\cdot1\) is graded free, by cocommutativity (to move that factor to the front) and the tensor identity. The remaining term \(\bigotimes_iQ_{1,i}\otimes K_{\rm rest}\) lies in degrees \(\ge t+1\). Hence \(K\cong(T\otimes C)\oplus Q\) by a graded \(T\)-linear isomorphism, where \(T\) acts on \(T\otimes C\) through the left factor, \(C\) is a graded vector space and \(Q\) lies in degrees \(\ge t+1\). This is the free-seed lemma's argument with unequal factors.
  2. \(R/(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_d)R=K/(\ell_0,\dots,\ell_d)K=\mathbb F\otimes_TK\). Its Hilbert function is \(\mathrm{HS}_C\) plus a part in degrees \(\ge t+1\).
  3. Reducing the \(T\)-linear isomorphism modulo \(\ell_0\) gives \(R=K/\ell_0K\cong(T/L_0T\otimes C)\oplus Q/\ell_0Q\) as \(T'\)-modules, with \(T/L_0T=\mathbb F[L_1,\dots,L_d]/(L^p)=:T'\). So \(\mathrm{HS}_R=\mathrm{HS}_{T'}\mathrm{HS}_C\) plus a part in degrees \(\ge t+1\), and \([q^k]\mathrm{HS}_R/\mathrm{HS}_{T'}=[q^k]\mathrm{HS}_C\) for \(k\le t\). Here \(\mathrm{HS}_{T'}=((1-q^p)/(1-q))^d\) has constant term 1.
  4. Items 2 and 3 give the equality for \(k\le t\). As a \(T'\)-module, \(R\) is \(T'\otimes C\) plus a part in degrees \(\ge t+1\), which is freeness through \(t\). \(\square\)

Corollary (multiplicity form). If some affine basis of \(\mathbb F^d\) has each of its points as the value of at least \((p-1)(t+1)\) holes, the column model is free through degree \(t\).

Comparison with the conjecture. The multiplicity hypothesis forces every nonzero direction \(\lambda\) to have column count \(c(\lambda)\ge(p-1)(t+1)\), the number of holes outside the most frequent level set of \(\lambda\circ\varphi\). A nonconstant affine function is not constant on an affine basis, so at least one basis point, with its \((p-1)(t+1)\) holes, lies outside that level set. For \(p=3\) this gives \(c\ge2t+2>2t-1\). The corollary therefore lies strictly inside the conjectured free range, consistently with the conjecture. It also misses spans the conjecture covers. For \(d=1\), \(p=3\), value multiplicities \((n-2t,t,t)\) give \(c=2t\ge2t-1\), but no value other than the first is taken \(2(t+1)\) times. The gap lies in how the holes are distributed among values, not only in their number.

What this means

  • The worst-direction conjecture now has a proved sufficient condition for freeness, strictly inside its conjectured range: multiplicity \((p-1)(t+1)\) on an affine basis of the values. The "if" direction at the conjectured threshold \(c\ge2t-1\), and the converse, remain open.
  • For \(p=3\), where the summand is stated, model freeness is the \(U\)-degree-0 half of freeness of the weak board; the summand has not been checked for other \(p\). Model exactness, freeness of \(A_{\ge1}\), is still needed for the board.
  • The multiplicity form needs \((p-1)(d+1)(t+1)\) holes at least, and needs repeated values. A span of dimension \(d\approx\log_pn\) can take mostly distinct values, and then only the general seed criterion can apply: products of distinct forms \(L_j\) spanning the truncated ring. It resembles the Gale entry's reformulation through squares of the Gale transform, but the relation between the two is not worked out.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the free-seed lemma and its proof, the statement of conj:worst-direction-freeness, and the summand proposition's scope. A fresh-context reviewer checked the diagonal action and \(\ell_b^p=0\), including \(b=0\); the seed-criterion formula, its \(a_b!\) factor and its converse; the equality \((y_b^p)=(M_i^p)\) and the monomial basis; and the Hilbert-series bookkeeping. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the independence hypothesis dropped, as it is implied by one seed;
  • the general-\(p\) definition of freeness through \(t\) stated;
  • the unequal-factor splitting written out;
  • the \(T\)-linearity of the splitting made explicit;
  • the comparison with the conjectured threshold made precise, with a consistency check and an example the corollary misses;
  • the transfer to the board limited to \(p=3\).

The changes clarify or weaken, so no further pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • Freeness of \(A_{\ge1}\) for spans with seeds (model exactness).
  • Seeds for spans with mostly distinct values (the general criterion).
  • Hypothesis (b) at logarithmic width.
