Board seeds: the weak PHP algebra is free over a column span through degree t on polynomial multiplicities, by reduction to t+1 rows

24 September 2026 · Working proofs · Board freeness over column forms, and condition (c) for seeded selector members. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The column-seeds entry proved freeness in the column model. The recorded chain from freeness to hypothesis (c) for column members of selectors needs freeness of the board algebra \(A\) itself (worst-direction entry, the paragraph on condition (c)). Model exactness, freeness of \(A_{\ge1}\), was the missing link. The cycle asks for board freeness directly.

General statement. lem:board-content-reduction: over any field, the weak unary top algebra \(A\) on \(m\) rows and \(n\) holes splits, as a module over the column-type forms, into summands \(A^{(c)}\) indexed by the row contents \(c\) of rows \(1,\dots,m-1\). The summand \(A^{(c)}\) depends only on the rows in the support of \(c\) and lives in degrees \(\ge|c|\). So \(A\) is free through degree \(t\) exactly when the weak algebra on \(\min(m,t+1)\) rows is. thm:board-seed-freeness: in characteristic \(p\), let hole functions \(\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_d\) have an affine basis \(P_0,\dots,P_d\) of \(\mathbb F^d\) among their values, with \(P_0\) taken by at least \((p-1)(t+1)^2\) holes and each \(P_b\), \(b\ge1\), by at least \((p-1)(t+1)\) holes. Then \(A\), on any number of rows, is free through degree \(t\) over \(\mathbb F[W_1,\dots,W_d]/(W_b^p)\) acting by \(W_b\mapsto\ell_b\). cor:seeded-selector-members: at \(p=3\), a member of selectors \(1-(L_b-v_b)^2\) with column-type linear parts satisfying the condition at \(t=D\) satisfies hypothesis (c) of relative gluing through \(D\).

Content reduction

As in the summand entry, write \(C_j=\sum_ix_{ij}\) and eliminate row 0 by \(x_{0j}=C_j-u_j\), \(u_j=\sum_{i\ge1}x_{ij}\). Then \(A=B/(s,r_1,\dots,r_{m-1})\) with \(B=\bigotimes_j(\mathbb F\oplus\mathbb FC_j\oplus U_j)\), \(U_j=\operatorname{span}(x_{ij}:i\ge1)\), \(C_j^2=C_jU_j=U_j^2=0\), \(s=\sum_jC_j\) and \(r_i=\sum_jx_{ij}\). The summand entry derives this presentation over \(\mathbb F_3\). It holds over any field: \(C_j\) and the \(x_{ij}\) lie in the square-zero part \(V_j^+\) of column \(j\), which uses every \(x_{ij}^2\) and every \(x_{ij}x_{i'j}\), so \(C_j^2=C_jU_j=U_j^2=0\).

Lemma (content reduction). Over any field, \(B\) is graded by the row content \(c\in\mathbb N^{\{1,\dots,m-1\}}\) of its \(x\)-part. The relations \(s\) (content 0) and \(r_i\) (content \(e_i\)) are homogeneous, and every column-type form \(\ell_\varphi=\sum_j\varphi(j)C_j\) has content 0. Hence \(A=\bigoplus_cA^{(c)}\) as graded modules over any graded connected algebra acting through content-0 elements, such as \(\mathbb F[W_1,\dots,W_d]/(W_b^p)\) acting by \(W_b\mapsto\ell_b\), with \(A^{(c)}=B^{(c)}/\bigl(sB^{(c)}+\sum_{i\in\operatorname{supp}c}r_iB^{(c-e_i)}\bigr)\). This depends only on the rows in \(\operatorname{supp}c\) and on the holes, and lives in degrees \(\ge|c|\). Consequently, \(A\) on \(m\) rows is a free module plus a part in degrees \(\ge t+1\) over such an algebra exactly when the weak algebra on \(u=\min(m,t+1)\) rows is.

Proof. The grading and the homogeneity are immediate. For a content \(c\) with \(|c|\le t\), \(|\operatorname{supp}c|\le\min(m-1,t)=u-1\), so the support can be renamed into rows \(1,\dots,u-1\). The renaming gives an isomorphism \(B_m^{(c)}\cong B_u^{(c)}\) that fixes every \(C_j\) and commutes with multiplication by the \(C_j\), because the rules \(C_j^2=C_jU_j=0\) are the same on both sides. It carries the relations to the relations, so \(A_m^{(c)}\cong A_u^{(c)}\) with the same action of the forms. Conversely, every summand of \(A_u\) is a summand of \(A_m\). By the Krull–Schmidt theorem for finite-dimensional graded modules, a direct summand of a module of the form (free) \(\oplus\) (degrees \(\ge t+1\)) has the same form, and summands with \(|c|\ge t+1\) lie in degrees \(\ge t+1\). Both directions follow. \(\square\)

This is the column-form analogue of the row reduction for the weak base (lem:weak-row-reduction). Unlike it, it is an equivalence.

Seeds on few rows

On \(u\) rows, \(\tilde A_u=\mathbb F[x_{ij}]/(x_{ij}^2,x_{ij}x_{i'j})=\bigotimes_jV_j\), with \(V_j=\mathbb F\oplus\operatorname{span}(x_{0j},\dots,x_{u-1,j})\) square-zero, and \(A_u=\tilde A_u/(r_0,\dots,r_{u-1})\). Let \(T=\mathbb F[Y_0,\dots,Y_{u-1},W_1,\dots,W_d]/(Y_i^p,W_b^p)\) with primitive generators act by \(Y_i\mapsto r_i\) and \(W_b\mapsto\ell_b=\sum_j\varphi_b(j)C_j\). On \(V_j\), \(Y_i\) sends \(1\) to \(x_{ij}\) and \(W_b\) sends \(1\) to \(\varphi_b(j)\sum_ix_{ij}\). Multiplication in \(\tilde A_u\) is the diagonal action, and all \(p\)-th powers vanish.

Seed criterion. To a cell \((i,j)\) attach the form \(M_{ij}=y_i+\langle\varphi(j),w\rangle\) in \(\mathbb F[y_0,\dots,y_{u-1},w_1,\dots,w_d]\). For a set \(B\) of holes, \(\operatorname{Ann}_T(1)=0\) in \(\bigotimes_{j\in B}V_j\) if and only if, in every degree, the products \(\prod_{(i,j)\in X}M_{ij}\) over column-injective cell sets \(X\subseteq[u]\times B\) span the truncated ring \(\mathbb F[y,w]/(y^p,w^p)\). The proof is that of the column-seed criterion. A factor \(Y_i\) placed on hole \(j\) gives \(x_{ij}\), and a factor \(W_b\) gives \(\varphi_b(j)x_{ij}\) for some row \(i\). So \(\prod Y^aW^c\cdot1=\prod a!\,c!\sum_X\bigl([y^aw^c]\prod_{(i,j)\in X}M_{ij}\bigr)x_X\), and the factorials are units since the exponents are at most \(p-1\).

Lemma (board seed blocks). A hole set \(B\) is a seed in this sense if, for an affine basis \(P_0,\dots,P_d\), it contains \(u(p-1)\) holes of value \(P_0\) and \(p-1\) holes of value \(P_b\) for each \(b\ge1\).

Proof. Assign to row \(i\) its own \(p-1\) holes of value \(P_0\), and to row 0 also the holes of value \(P_b\). The forms \(y_i+\langle P_0,w\rangle\), \(0\le i<u\), and \(y_0+\langle P_b,w\rangle\), \(1\le b\le d\), are a basis of the linear forms. The differences \(\langle P_b-P_0,w\rangle\) span the \(w\)-forms, since \(P_0,\dots,P_d\) is an affine basis, and then each \(y_i\) is in the span. In characteristic \(p\) the truncation ideal is generated by the \(p\)-th powers of any basis of linear forms. So the products of at most \(p-1\) copies of each basis form are a basis of the truncated ring. Each is \(\prod_{(i,j)\in X}M_{ij}\) for \(X\) made of assigned cells on distinct holes. \(\square\)

The theorem

Theorem (board seeds). Let \(\mathbb F\) have characteristic \(p\), \(t\ge0\), and let \(\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_d\) have an affine basis of values \(P_0,\dots,P_d\) with multiplicities at least \((p-1)(t+1)^2\) at \(P_0\) and \((p-1)(t+1)\) at each \(P_b\). Then the weak unary top algebra \(A\) on any number \(m\ge1\) of rows is a free module over \(T'=\mathbb F[W_1,\dots,W_d]/(W_b^p)\), acting by \(W_b\mapsto\ell_b\), plus a part in degrees \(\ge t+1\). In particular, \(\mathrm{HF}(A/(\ell)A)_k=[q^k]\,\mathrm{HS}_A\bigl((1-q)/(1-q^p)\bigr)^d\) for \(k\le t\).

Proof.

  1. By content reduction it suffices to treat \(u=\min(m,t+1)\le t+1\) rows.
  2. The multiplicities give \(t+1\) disjoint seed blocks, since \(u(p-1)(t+1)\le(p-1)(t+1)^2\).
  3. By the free-seed argument with unequal factors, as in the column-seeds entry (graded self-injectivity of \(T\), cocommutativity, the tensor identity), \(\tilde A_u\cong(T\otimes C)\oplus Q\) by a graded \(T\)-linear isomorphism, with \(Q\) in degrees \(\ge t+1\).
  4. Reducing modulo \(Y_0,\dots,Y_{u-1}\), which act as \(r_0,\dots,r_{u-1}\), gives \(A_u\cong(T/(Y)\otimes C)\oplus Q/(Y)Q\) as modules over \(T/(Y)=T'\), acting by the \(\ell_b\). The first summand is free and the second lies in degrees \(\ge t+1\).
  5. The Hilbert-function identity follows as in the column-seeds theorem. \(\square\)

Corollary (seeded selector members). Let \(p=3\), and let a member \(U_i\) of the relative gluing theorem consist of selectors \(g_b=1-(L_b-v_b)^2\), \(b=1,\dots,d\), on the weak unary base, where \(L_b\) has column-type linear part \(\ell_b=\sum_j\varphi_b(j)C_j\) and \(v_b\in\mathbb F_3\). If \(\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_d\) satisfy the multiplicity condition with \(t=D\), the member satisfies hypothesis (c) of thm:relative-gluing through \(D\).

Hypothesis (c) reads: every top syzygy of degree at most \(D\) supported on a single member is liftable in \(U\). A top syzygy is \((\sigma_b)\) with \(\sum_b\sigma_bP_b=0\) in \(A_{\rm top}=B/zB\), here the weak top algebra \(A\), with tops \(P_b=-\ell_b^2\). Liftable means that homogeneous lifts satisfy \(\sum_b\tilde\sigma_bg_b^{\rm h}=z\rho\) with \(\rho\in J_U\).

Proof.

  1. The syzygies live in the free part. By the theorem, \(A\cong(T'\otimes C)\oplus Q'\) as graded \(T'\)-modules, with \(T'=\mathbb F_3[W_1,\dots,W_d]/(W_b^3)\) and \(Q'\) in degrees \(\ge D+1\). A member syzygy of degree \(s\le D\) has \(\sigma_b\in A_{s-2}\), and the equation \(\sum_bW_b^2\sigma_b=0\) holds separately in each summand. The \(Q'\)-components of the \(\sigma_b\) have degree \(s-2<D+1\), so they vanish. Hence \((\sigma_b)\) lies in \((T'\otimes C)^d\) and is a syzygy of \((W_b^2)\) on the free module \(T'\otimes C\), that is, a sum \(\sum_kz_k\otimes c_k\) of syzygies \(z_k\) of \((W_b^2)\) in \(T'\).
  2. Syzygies of the squares in \(T'\). \(T'=\bigotimes_b\mathbb F_3[W_b]/(W_b^3)\), and the Koszul complex of \((W_1^2,\dots,W_d^2)\) on \(T'\) is the tensor product of the complexes \(\mathbb F_3[W]/(W^3)\xrightarrow{W^2}\mathbb F_3[W]/(W^3)\). Each has \(H_1=\ker W^2=(W)\), generated by the class of \(We\). By the Künneth formula over a field, \(H_1\) of the product is \(\bigoplus_bH_1^{(b)}\otimes\bigotimes_{c\ne b}H_0^{(c)}\), which is spanned by classes of \(W_be_b\) times elements of \(T'\). So every syzygy of \((W_b^2)\) in \(T'\) is a \(T'\)-combination of the Frobenius syzygies \(W_be_b\) and the Koszul syzygies \(W_c^2e_b-W_b^2e_c\).
  3. Back in \(A\). The isomorphism is \(T'\)-linear. So the image of \(\bigl(\sum_k\alpha_kW_be_b+\cdots\bigr)\otimes c\) is an \(A\)-combination of \(\ell_be_b\) and of \(\ell_c^2e_b-\ell_b^2e_c\): the image of \((W_bt)\otimes c\) is \(\ell_b\) times the image of \(t\otimes c\). Hence every member syzygy of degree at most \(D\) is an \(A\)-combination of Frobenius syzygies \(\ell_be_b\) and member Koszul syzygies.
  4. Lifting. Koszul syzygies lift exactly: \(g_c^{\rm h}g_b^{\rm h}-g_b^{\rm h}g_c^{\rm h}=0\). The Frobenius syzygies lift with zero correction by the recorded Frobenius lift lemma (component-hypothesis entry). Its hypotheses are the weak unary base over \(\mathbb F_3\) and constraints \(\prod_k(1-(\ell_k-a_k)^2)\), here with \(w=1\). It gives \((L_b-v_b)g_b\) in the base ideal at degree 3, so \(\ell_bg_b^{\rm h}=z\,v_bg_b^{\rm h}\) modulo the homogenized base, with \(v_bg_b^{\rm h}\in J_U\). Liftable syzygies are closed under \(A\)-combinations (step 3 of the relative gluing proof). \(\square\)

Relation to the record. The worst-direction entry sketched this chain conditionally on conj:worst-direction-freeness and on model exactness, which together would give freeness of \(A\). Here freeness of \(A\) is proved under the multiplicity condition, which replaces both. The chain's threshold \(c\ge2D-1\) and its \(Q\)-robustness step are not used.

What this means

  • Model exactness is no longer needed for spans with seeds: the board is treated directly, by reducing to \(t+1\) rows and using seeds for the row sums and the column forms together.
  • At the goal's degree \(D=O(\log n)\), the condition asks for an affine basis of values with multiplicities of order \(\log^2n\) at one point and \(\log n\) at the others, about \((d+1)(p-1)(D+1)+(p-1)(D+1)^2\) holes in all. So spans of dimension up to about \(\log n\) are covered when their values concentrate on an affine basis. Not covered: spans whose values have no affine basis with these multiplicities, for example nearly injective \(\varphi\); and narrow members, which the local-fall conjecture treats.
  • Hypothesis (b), splitting between members, is untouched.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the summand presentation; the column-seeds theorem and the free-seed argument; the relative gluing theorem's hypothesis (c) and proof steps; the recorded Frobenius lift lemma and its hypotheses; and the worst-direction entry's conditional chain. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed the presentation over any field, the content grading and homogeneity, the diagonal action, the seed-criterion formula, the basis of \(u+d\) forms and its realization on distinct holes, the block count, the splitting, the reduction modulo \(Y\), and the Hilbert-function identity. It found no unused hypothesis. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the presentation justified through \(V_j^2=0\);
  • content reduction stated as an equivalence, with its renaming isomorphism made explicit;
  • the truncated algebra named as an abstract algebra acting through the forms;
  • the corollary proved in full, with (c) quoted, the free-part splitting, the Künneth computation of the syzygies of the squares, and the Frobenius lift lemma checked against selectors;
  • the relation to the recorded chain restated;
  • the corollary registered as its own claim;
  • the coverage remark corrected;
  • notation made uniform.

The written-out corollary adds no hypothesis beyond the reviewed theorem and the recorded lemma; no further pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • Seeds for spans with mostly distinct values: products of distinct cell forms spanning the truncated ring without repeated values.
  • Members that are not selectors (product clauses of width above 1): their own syzygies in the truncated algebra.
  • Hypothesis (b) at logarithmic width.

Span transfer: on a free column span, a member's syzygies lift when they lift in the finite function ring of the span, so Gröbner-augmented seeded members satisfy condition (c)

24 September 2026 · Working proof · Hypothesis (c) of relative gluing for Gröbner-augmented members on seeded column spans. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The board-seeds entry proved hypothesis (c) for selector members on seeded column spans. The goal's members are product clauses of logarithmic width (lem:prefix-image-rewrite) and their unions. The cycle asks what (c) needs for a member of arbitrary polynomial constraints in the forms of one span.

General statement. lem:span-transfer: in characteristic \(p\), let a member consist of the constraints \(g_k=h_k(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_d)\) on the weak unary base, where the \(\ell_b\) are linear forms with coefficients in \(\mathbb F_p\) and the \(h_k\) are reduced polynomials over \(\mathbb F_p\) (every exponent below \(p\)). Suppose \(A\cong(T'\otimes C)\oplus Q'\) by a graded isomorphism, linear over \(T'=\mathbb F_p[W]/(W^p)\) acting by \(W_b\mapsto\ell_b\), with \(Q'\) in degrees \(\ge D+1\). Suppose also that the member has no fall below \(D\) in its span ring \(\mathbb F_p[y,z]/(y_b^p-y_bz^{p-1},h_k^{\rm h})\). Then the member satisfies hypothesis (c) of thm:relative-gluing through \(D\). thm:seeded-member-condition: for column-type forms whose values are seeded at \(t=D\) (thm:board-seed-freeness), and a member with nonempty allowed set in \(\mathbb F_p^d\), adding \(h(\ell)\) for \(h\) in a reduced degree-order Gröbner basis of \((h_k)+(y_b^p-y_b)\) gives a member that satisfies (c) through \(D\) and (d). A lower bound for the augmented system is one for the original.

Setting

The weak base has generators \(x_{ij}^2-x_{ij}\), \(x_{ij}x_{i'j}\) and \(\rho_i-1\). \(B\) is the quotient by their homogenizations, \(A=B/zB\), and \(J_U\) is the ideal of all homogenized constraints, as in the relative gluing theorem. A constraint \(g_k\) is the expanded polynomial \(h_k(\ell)\) in the \(x_{ij}\), homogenized at its own degree in \(x\). The span ring is \(S=\mathbb F_p[y_1,\dots,y_d,z]/(y_b^p-y_bz^{p-1})\), with top algebra \(S/zS=T'\). \(\phi:\mathbb F_p[y,z]\to\mathbb F_p[x,z]\) is the graded ring map \(y_b\mapsto\ell_b\), \(z\mapsto z\). "No fall below \(D\) in the span ring" means that \(z\) is injective from degree \(k\) to \(k+1\), \(k<D\), on \(S/(h_k^{\rm h})\).

The transfer lemma

Lemma (span transfer). Under the hypotheses of the general statement, every top syzygy of the member of degree at most \(D\) is liftable, with correction in \(J_{U_i}\subseteq J_U\). The lemma uses no property of the forms beyond \(\mathbb F_p\) coefficients and the freeness hypothesis; for column-type forms, the board-seed theorem supplies that hypothesis.

Proof.

  1. \(\phi\) respects the bases. In characteristic \(p\), with coefficients in \(\mathbb F_p\), \(\ell_b^p=\sum c_{ij}^px_{ij}^p=\sum c_{ij}x_{ij}^p\). And \(x^p-xz^{p-1}=(x^2-xz)\sum_{j=0}^{p-2}x^jz^{p-2-j}\). So \(\phi(y_b^p-y_bz^{p-1})\) lies in the ideal of the homogenized Booleanity generators.
  2. Tops. The decomposition gives an injective \(T'\)-linear map \(T'\to A\), \(t\mapsto t\cdot1\), in all degrees, because \(A_0=\mathbb F_p\) lies in \(T'\otimes C\). For reduced \(h_k\), the top form \(\operatorname{in}(h_k)\) is a nonzero element of \(T'\), so \(\operatorname{in}(h_k)(\ell)\ne0\) in \(A\). Then \(\operatorname{in}(h_k)(\ell)\ne0\) in \(\mathbb F_p[x]\) as well, so \(\deg_xg_k=\deg h_k\). Hence \(g_k^{\rm h}=\phi(h_k^{\rm h})\), and the top of \(g_k\) is \(P_k=\operatorname{in}(h_k)(\ell)\).
  3. Syzygies are span syzygies. Let \((\sigma_k)\) be a member syzygy of degree \(s\le D\), so \(\sigma_k\in A_{s-\deg h_k}\) with \(s-\deg h_k<D+1\). The \(Q'\)-components of the \(\sigma_k\) vanish, so \(\sigma_k=\sum_j\tau_{kj}\cdot\hat c_j\), with \(\tau_{kj}\in T'\), a basis \(c_j\) of \(C\) and \(\hat c_j\) the image of \(1\otimes c_j\). The syzygy equation reads \(\sum_j\bigl(\sum_k\tau_{kj}\operatorname{in}(h_k)\bigr)\otimes c_j=0\) in \(T'\otimes C\). So for each \(j\), \(\zeta_j=(\tau_{kj})_k\) is a syzygy of the \(\operatorname{in}(h_k)\) in \(T'\), a top syzygy of the span system, and \((\sigma_k)=\sum_j\hat c_j\cdot\zeta_j(\ell)\).
  4. Lift in the span ring. Take homogeneous lifts \(\tilde\tau_{kj}\in\mathbb F_p[y,z]\). Then \(\sum_k\tilde\tau_{kj}h_k^{\rm h}\) vanishes modulo \(z\) in \(S\), so it equals \(z\rho_j\) in \(S\), with \(\deg\rho_j=\deg\zeta_j-1\le D-1\). Since \(z\rho_j\in(h^{\rm h})S\), injectivity of \(z\) on \(S/(h^{\rm h})\) from degree \(\deg\zeta_j-1\) to \(\deg\zeta_j\le D\) gives \(\rho_j\in(h^{\rm h})S\). This is step 1 of the relative gluing proof, applied in \(S\). Write \(\rho_j=\sum_kr_{kj}h_k^{\rm h}+\beta_j\) in \(\mathbb F_p[y,z]\), with \(\beta_j\) in the ideal of the \(y_b^p-y_bz^{p-1}\).
  5. Transfer. \(\phi\) is graded and reduces modulo \(z\) to \(y\mapsto\ell\), so \(\phi(\tilde\tau_{kj})\) is a homogeneous lift of \(\tau_{kj}(\ell)\). Applying \(\phi\) and item 1, \(\sum_k\phi(\tilde\tau_{kj})g_k^{\rm h}=z\sum_k\phi(r_{kj})g_k^{\rm h}\) in \(B\). So each \(\zeta_j(\ell)\) is liftable, with correction in \(J_{U_i}\). Liftable syzygies are closed under \(A\)-combinations (step 3 of the relative gluing proof), so \((\sigma_k)\) is liftable. \(\square\)

Seeded members

Theorem (seeded members). In characteristic \(p\), let a member consist of constraints \(g_k=h_k(\ell)\), with \(h_k\) reduced over \(\mathbb F_p\), in column-type forms \(\ell_b=\sum_j\varphi_b(j)C_j\), \(\varphi_b\) with values in \(\mathbb F_p\). Let the values have an affine basis with multiplicities \((p-1)(D+1)^2\) at one point and \((p-1)(D+1)\) at the others, and let the allowed set \(Z=\{y\in\mathbb F_p^d:h_k(y)=0\ \forall k\}\) be nonempty. Let \(G\) be the reduced Gröbner basis, for a degree order, of \(I=(h_k)+(y_b^p-y_b)\), without the elements \(y_b^p-y_b\). Then the member \(\{g_k\}\cup\{h(\ell):h\in G\}\) satisfies hypotheses (c) and (d) of thm:relative-gluing through \(D\).

Proof.

  • \(G\) is reduced. \(y_b^p\) is in the leading-term ideal of \(I\). The only element of the reduced basis with leading monomial \(y_b^p\) is \(y_b^p-y_b\), which is removed. Every other element has no monomial divisible by a leading monomial of the basis, so all its exponents are below \(p\).
  • No fall in the span ring. \(G\cup\{h_k\}\cup\{y_b^p-y_b\}\) lies in \(I\) and contains a Gröbner basis of \(I\), so it is one, for a degree order. Every element of \(I\) of degree at most \(k\) is then a combination \(\sum q_gg\) with \(\deg q_g+\deg g\le k\). So the homogenizations generate the homogenization of \(I\), which is \(z\)-saturated, and \(z\) is injective on the span system in every degree.
  • Freeness. The board-seed theorem gives the decomposition of \(A\) required by the lemma. The lemma gives (c).
  • (d). Since \((y_b^p-y_b)\subseteq I\), \(\mathbb F_p[y]/I\) is the ring of functions on \(Z\), so \(Z\ne\emptyset\) means \(1\notin I\), and no \(h\in G\) is a nonzero constant. Each \(h\) is reduced, and each nonconstant \(h\) has \(\operatorname{in}(h)(\ell)\ne0\) by item 2 of the lemma. So \(h(\ell)\) is a nonconstant polynomial in \(x\). \(\square\)

Reduction is free at degree \(D\). For a constraint \(h(\ell)\) with \(h\) not reduced, \(\deg h\le D\), and \(\mathbb F_p\) coefficients, let \(h^{\rm red}\) be the reduction modulo \((y_b^p-y_b)\). The standard representation \(h-h^{\rm red}=\sum_br_b(y_b^p-y_b)\) has \(\deg r_b+p\le\deg h\). By item 1, \(\ell_b^p-\ell_b\) has a Nullstellensatz certificate of degree \(p\) from Booleanity. So \(h(\ell)=h^{\rm red}(\ell)+N\) with \(N\) in the base's Nullstellensatz span of degree \(\le\deg h\le D\). Each constraint is then derivable from the other within degree \(D\), and the two systems have the same fixed-degree-\(D\) PC closure. The goal's product clauses of degree at most \(D\) may therefore be taken reduced.

Augmentation is harmless. The original constraints are a subset of the augmented system, so any PC refutation of the original system is a refutation of the augmented one. No refutation for the augmented system therefore implies none for the original. The relative gluing theorem is applied to the augmented system, and its hypothesis (b) must be checked for the augmented tops. The two sufficient conditions of lem:tensor-splitting-locality behave as follows. The module condition on \(A\) over the members' form algebras does not involve the constraints. The second condition, that every top is a polynomial in its member's forms, holds for each \(\operatorname{in}(h)(\ell)\), \(h\in G\).

What this means

  • For column members, hypothesis (c) now holds for any \(\mathbb F_p\)-polynomial constraints in the forms of one seeded span with nonempty allowed set, after Gröbner augmentation. The member's own falls are removed by the augmentation.
  • The width of the constraints enters only through the span dimension \(d\): a clause of width \(w\) on independent forms has \(d\ge w\). The seed condition needs \((p-1)(D+1)^2+d(p-1)(D+1)=(p-1)(D+1)(D+1+d)\) holes on an affine basis of values.
  • Open for (c): column spans without a heavy affine basis of values, and non-column members. Hypothesis (b) is open throughout, and must be checked for augmented tops.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the relative gluing theorem's hypotheses and proof steps 1 and 3; the board-seed theorem's decomposition; the tensor-splitting lemma's conditions; the logarithmic-prefix rewrite. A fresh-context reviewer checked the base transfer, the tops, the free-part argument, the lift in the span ring, the transfer, and the Gröbner facts, and found the argument sound. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • \(\mathbb F_p\) coefficients and Booleanity among the base generators;
  • freeness as the global decomposition;
  • the degree step in item 2;
  • the \(T'\)-linearity step written out;
  • the correction placed in \(J_{U_i}\);
  • reducedness of \(G\);
  • (d) at the level of \(x\);
  • the reason for harmlessness, and (b) for augmented tops;
  • the hole count;
  • width entering through \(d\);
  • unused hypotheses removed from the lemma.

The changes make statements precise and weaken two claims, so no further pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • Column spans whose values have no heavy affine basis.
  • Non-column (narrow) members.
  • Hypothesis (b) at logarithmic width, now the main open condition of the line.

Occupancy transfer: every column member's content-0 syzygies lift after augmentation, whatever its span; content 1 is a gluing of column models on sub-boards

24 September 2026 · Working proofs and finite check · Hypothesis (c) for column members of any span, content 0; content 1. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The span-transfer entry proved hypothesis (c) for column members on seeded spans. The recorded column non-splitting makes all column constraints one member. Its span dimension \(d\) is the adversary's choice, and for \(d\) above about \(n/((p-1)(D+1))\) no seed exists. The cycle asks what can be proved for column members of any span dimension.

General statement. lem:occupancy-transfer: over \(\mathbb F_p\), for a column member, meaning constraints \(h_k(C_1,\dots,C_n)\) with \(C_j=\sum_ix_{ij}\), whose system in the occupancy ring \(O=\mathbb F_p[C,z]/(C_j^2-C_jz,\ \sum_jC_j-mz)\) (\(m\) the number of rows) has no fall below \(D\), the content-0 component of every member top syzygy of degree at most \(D\) is liftable. After augmentation by a degree-order Gröbner basis in the occupancy ring, this holds for every column member with nonempty allowed set, with no condition on the span. lem:occupancy-stability: the occupancy system alone, a single weak row with right-hand side \(m\), has no fall below \(D\) when \(n\ge2D-1\), and its top algebra is the column model \(R\). prop:content-one-restriction: the content-\(e_i\) summand of the weak algebra is \(\operatorname{coker}\bigl(\rho:R_{[n]}\to\bigoplus_jR_{[n]\setminus j}\bigr)\), \(\rho(f)=(f|_{C_j=0})_j\), shifted by one degree. ex:restriction-injectivity-small: over \(\mathbb F_3\), \(\rho\) is injective in degree \(t\) in all 24 tested cases with \(2t<n\), \(n\le11\), \(t\le4\), and fails in five of the nine tested cases with \(2t\ge n\).

Occupancy stability

Lemma (occupancy stability). Over \(\mathbb F_p\), for every \(m\) and \(n\ge2D-1\), \(O\) is \(z\)-injective below \(D\). Its top algebra \(O/zO\) is \(R=\mathbb F_p[C]/(C_j^2,\sum_jC_j)\).

Proof. \(z\)-injectivity from degree \(k\) to \(k+1\) means that every annihilator of the degree-\(k\) Nullstellensatz space extends to degree \(k+1\) (the base-condition entry's Step 0 and duality). The system is a single weak row with right-hand side \(m\) in place of 1, so the only content systems are \(c=(k+1)e_a\). For \(k=0\) the system is \(\sum_j\nu(\{j\})=m\mu_0\), solvable since \(n\ge1\). For \(k\ge1\), the proof of thm:weak-single-row-contents (repeated contents) goes through with the chain \(W_{j-1,j}\mu_j=(m-j+1)\mu_{j-1}\) and the system \(W_{k,k+1}\nu=(m-k)\mu_k\). The kernel identification is unchanged. \(W_{i_*,k}\mu_k\) carries the factor \(\prod_{j=i_*+1}^k(m-j+1)\) over \(p-1\) consecutive \(j\), which vanishes unless \(m+1\equiv i_*\equiv k+1\), that is \(k\equiv m\). In that case the right side \((m-k)\mu_k\) is zero. \(\square\)

The lemma is standalone. It shows that the column model is the top algebra of a system with no falls in the range the goal uses. The transfer lemma below does not need it.

Content decomposition of member syzygies

As in the board-seeds entry, with row 0 eliminated, \(A=\bigoplus_cA^{(c)}\) over the column algebra \(K=\mathbb F_p[C]/(C_j^2)\). Here \(A^{(c)}=E^{(c)}/(sE^{(c)}+\sum_ir_iE^{(c-e_i)})\) with \(E=\bigotimes_j(\mathbb F\oplus\mathbb FC_j\oplus U_j)\) and \(s=\sum_jC_j\). \(A^{(0)}=E^{(0)}/sE^{(0)}=K/(s)=R\), because every \(r_i\), \(i\ge1\), raises content. This holds over any field. A column member's tops \(P_k\) (the top-degree form of \(h_k\), evaluated at \(C\), possibly zero) have content 0. So a member syzygy \((\sigma_k)\) splits into content components \((\sigma_k^{(c)})\), each a syzygy in \(A^{(c)}\). Liftable syzygies are closed under sums, so \((\sigma_k)\) is liftable when every component is.

Occupancy transfer

Lemma (occupancy transfer). Over \(\mathbb F_p\), let a member consist of \(g_k=h_k(C)\) for polynomials \(h_k\in\mathbb F_p[C]\), and suppose \(z\) is injective below \(D\) on \(O/(h_k^{\rm h})\). Then the content-0 component of every member top syzygy of degree at most \(D\) is liftable, with correction in the member's ideal.

Proof.

  1. The map. \(\phi:C_j\mapsto\sum_ix_{ij}\), \(z\mapsto z\), is an injective graded map, since the \(C_j\) go to linearly independent linear forms. So \(g_k^{\rm h}=\phi(h_k^{\rm h})\) for every \(h_k\). \(\phi\) sends \(C_j^2-C_jz\) to \(\sum_i(x_{ij}^2-x_{ij}z)+2\sum_{i<i'}x_{ij}x_{i'j}\), and \(\sum_jC_j-mz\), \(m\) the number of rows, to \(\sum_i(r_i-z)\). Both lie in the homogenized weak base ideal.
  2. Lift. The content-0 component \((\sigma^{(0)}_k)\) is a syzygy of the \(P_k\) in \(R=O/zO\), a top syzygy of the system \(O/(h^{\rm h})\). Step 1 of the relative gluing proof, in \(O\) with the injectivity hypothesis, gives homogeneous lifts \(\tilde\sigma_k\) with \(\sum_k\tilde\sigma_kh_k^{\rm h}=z\sum_kq_kh_k^{\rm h}\) modulo the occupancy relations.
  3. Transfer. Applying \(\phi\) and item 1 gives \(\sum_k\phi(\tilde\sigma_k)g_k^{\rm h}=z\sum_k\phi(q_k)g_k^{\rm h}\) in the homogenized weak base ring. \(\phi(\tilde\sigma_k)\) lifts \(\sigma^{(0)}_k\), because \(R\to A\) is \(C\mapsto C\). \(\square\)

Augmentation. For a member with nonempty allowed set in \(\{C\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_jC_j\equiv m\}\), add \(h(C)\) for every element \(h\) of a reduced degree-order Gröbner basis of \((C_j^2-C_j,\ \sum_jC_j-m,\ h_k)\). The generators then contain a Gröbner basis of the member's ideal in the occupancy ring, so \(O/(h^{\rm h})\) is \(z\)-saturated and has no fall in any degree. Generators of degree above \(D\) do not affect degrees at most \(D\). The allowed set is nonempty, so no added generator is a nonzero constant. Adding constraints only makes refutations easier, since the original system is a subset of the augmented one. No span dimension, seed or multiplicity condition enters. The augmented member has more tops, so hypothesis (b) must hold for them.

Content one

Proposition (content-one restriction). Over any field, for each row \(i\ge1\), \(A^{(e_i)}_d\cong\operatorname{coker}(\rho)_{d-1}\) as \(K\)-modules, where \(\rho:R_{[n]}\to\bigoplus_{j=1}^nR_{[n]\setminus j}\), \(f\mapsto(f|_{C_j=0})_j\). Here \(R_{[n]\setminus j}=K_{[n]\setminus j}/(\sum_{j'\ne j}C_{j'})\) is the column model on the other holes, with \(C_j\) acting as 0 on the \(j\)-th summand. The shift is by the degree of \(x_{ij}\).

Proof. \(E^{(e_i)}=\bigoplus_jK_{[n]\setminus j}\,x_{ij}\), since \(C_jx_{ij}=0\). The relations in content \(e_i\) are \(sE^{(e_i)}\), where \(s\) acts on the \(j\)-th summand as \(s_j=\sum_{j'\ne j}C_{j'}\), and \(r_iE^{(0)}=\{\sum_jf\,x_{ij}:f\in K\}\). The first quotient is \(\bigoplus_jR_{[n]\setminus j}\), shifted. The image of \(f\in K\) is \((f|_{C_j=0})_j\), which depends only on \(f\) modulo \(s\), since \(s|_{C_j=0}=s_j\). \(\square\)

Finite check: injectivity of \(\rho\). Dually, \(\rho\) is injective in degree \(t\) of \(R\) exactly when the zero-marginal functions on \(t\)-subsets of \([n]\) are spanned by the zero-extensions of zero-marginal functions on \(t\)-subsets of \([n]\setminus j\), \(j=1,\dots,n\), since \(\rho^*\) is extension by zero. In characteristic 0 this holds for \(2t<n\): polytabloids span the zero-marginal space for \(t\le n/2\) and are supported on \(2t\) holes. In characteristic \(p\) the zero-marginal space can be larger, by Wilson's formula only when \(t\ge p\). rho_injectivity.py computes both dimensions exactly over \(\mathbb F_3\) for \(3\le n\le11\), \(1\le t\le\min(4,n-1)\) (rho_p3.json). In all 24 cases with \(2t<n\), \(\rho\) is injective. Of the nine cases with \(2t\ge n\), it fails in five: \((n,t)=(4,2),(5,3),(6,3),(6,4),(8,4)\). The test can decide: it detects failures, and the goal needs only degrees \(t\le D-1\) with \(n\ge2D+1\), inside \(2t<n\).

What this means

  • For column members of any span dimension, the content-0 part of hypothesis (c) is proved, after augmentation, whose tops (b) must then accommodate. What remains of (c) lives in the components with content \(c\ne0\), \(|c|\le D\). The gluing description is proved for \(c=e_i\).
  • Proposed route, not proved. Split \(0\to\ker\rho\to R\to\bigoplus_jR_{[n]\setminus j}\to A^{(e_i)}\to0\) into two short exact sequences. If \(\ker\rho=0\) in the relevant degrees, as the check suggests for \(2t<n\), relate content-one syzygies to those of the restricted members in the column models on \(n-1\) holes. Three things would then be needed: a transfer of their lifts into the weak base through \(x_{ij}\cdot\phi\), for occupancy right-hand side \(m-1\); augmentation of the restricted members, since restricting a Gröbner basis does not give one; and the connecting maps. Higher contents would need the analogous gluings, not yet described.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the one-row theorem and its proof, the board-seeds content reduction, and the relative gluing theorem's steps 1 and 3. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed the content-0 lift and the content-one proposition, and the residue argument of occupancy stability. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • unused hypotheses dropped from the transfer lemma: normal forms, stability, nonzero tops;
  • augmentation by the full Gröbner basis, consistent with the lemma;
  • the normal-form reduction removed;
  • (b) for the augmented tops noted;
  • the stability proof completed: the duality, the single content, and \(k=0\);
  • notation separated, with \(m\) stated as the number of rows;
  • the degree shift stated;
  • the long-exact-sequence paragraph relabeled as a proposed route, with its three missing pieces;
  • the General statement limited to what is proved;
  • the characteristic-\(p\) remark qualified.

The injectivity check was added after the review. It is exact and registered separately. The changes weaken or correct claims, so no further pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • A proof that \(\rho\) is injective for \(2t<n\) over \(\mathbb F_p\), and the proposed route for content one.
  • Contents \(|c|\ge2\).
  • Hypothesis (b), including for augmented tops.

The restriction map of column models is injective below n/2 in every characteristic, so content one is resolved by column models on n and n−1 holes

24 September 2026 · Working proof · Injectivity of the restriction map \(\rho\) for \(2t<n\), any field of characteristic \(p\) or 0; cycle odd-prime-restriction-injectivity. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The occupancy-transfer entry proved hypothesis (c) for column members in content 0. It showed that content one is \(\operatorname{coker}\bigl(\rho:R_{[n]}\to\bigoplus_jR_{[n]\setminus j}\bigr)\), and found \(\rho\) injective in all 24 tested cases with \(2t<n\) over \(\mathbb F_3\) (ex:restriction-injectivity-small). The cycle asks for a proof.

General statement. thm:restriction-injectivity: over any field of characteristic \(p\) or 0, for \(n\ge2t+1\), every zero-marginal function on the \(t\)-subsets of \([n]\) is a sum of zero-marginal functions each vanishing on the sets that contain some hole \(j\) and zero-marginal on \([n]\setminus j\). Equivalently, \(\rho\) is injective in degree \(t\). So for every row \(i\ge1\), \(0\to R_{[n]}\to\bigoplus_jR_{[n]\setminus j}\to A^{(e_i)}\to0\) is exact with the first two terms in degree \(t\) and \(A^{(e_i)}\) in degree \(t+1\), for \(t\le(n-1)/2\). lem:placed-pigeon-identity: multiplying by \(x_{ij}\) carries the occupancy relations of the other holes, with right-hand side \(m-1\), into the homogenized weak base ideal. So a lifting identity for the specialized member \(h^{\rm h}|_{C_j=z}\) in the occupancy ring of the other holes gives an identity for \(x_{ij}\) times a lift on the \(j\)-th summand, one piece of the proposed content-one route.

Notation

For a finite set \(X\) and \(t\ge0\), \(Z_t(X)\) is the space of functions \(f\) on \(t\)-subsets of \(X\) with zero marginals: \(\sum_{k\in X\setminus S'}f(S'\cup\{k\})=0\) for every \((t-1)\)-subset \(S'\). \(Z_0(X)=\mathbb F\). For \(j\in X\), \(\iota_j\) extends a function on \(t\)-subsets of \(X\setminus j\) by zero, and \(\iota_jZ_t(X\setminus j)\subseteq Z_t(X)\). Indeed, at \(S'\not\ni j\) the extra term \(f(S'\cup\{j\})\) is 0, and at \(S'\ni j\) every term is 0. The link at \(j\) is \(f^{+j}(S')=f(S'\cup\{j\})\), for \((t-1)\)-subsets \(S'\) of \(X\setminus j\). \(R_X\) is the column model on \(X\), with \((R_X)_t^*=Z_t(X)\), and \(\rho^*\) is extension by zero (occupancy-transfer entry).

Two lemmas

Lemma 1 (links are zero-marginal). For \(f\in Z_t(X)\), \(f^{+j}\in Z_{t-1}(X\setminus j)\). If moreover \(f^{+j}=0\), then \(f\in\iota_jZ_t(X\setminus j)\).

Proof. The marginal of \(f^{+j}\) at a \((t-2)\)-subset \(T\) of \(X\setminus j\) is \(\sum_{k\notin T\cup\{j\}}f(T\cup\{j,k\})\), the marginal of \(f\) at \(T\cup\{j\}\), which is 0. If \(f^{+j}=0\), then \(f\) vanishes on sets containing \(j\). The marginals of its restriction to \(X\setminus j\) are those of \(f\) at sets avoiding \(j\), minus the term \(f(S'\cup\{j\})=0\), so they vanish. \(\square\)

Lemma 2 (link surjectivity). Over a field of characteristic \(p\) or 0, if \(|X|\ge2t\) and \(t\ge1\), then \(Z_t(X)\to Z_{t-1}(X\setminus j)\), \(f\mapsto f^{+j}\), is surjective.

Proof. Given \(h\in Z_{t-1}(X\setminus j)\), set \(f(S'\cup\{j\})=h(S')\), and look for the values \(f_0\) of \(f\) on \(t\)-subsets of \(Y=X\setminus j\).

  • The marginals of \(f\) at sets containing \(j\) are marginals of \(h\), which vanish.
  • At a \((t-1)\)-subset \(S''\subseteq Y\), the marginal is \((W_{t-1,t}f_0)(S'')+h(S'')\), with \(W_{t-1,t}\) the inclusion matrix on \(Y\).

So we need \(-h\in\operatorname{Im}W_{t-1,t}\) on \(Y\), \(|Y|\ge2t-1=2(t-1)+1\). For \(t=1\), \(h\) is a constant and \(\operatorname{Im}W_{0,1}=\mathbb F\) because \(Y\ne\emptyset\). Let \(t\ge2\). By the kernel identification in the proof of thm:weak-single-row-contents (repeated contents), applied with \(k=t-1\) on \(Y\), \(\ker W_{t-1,t}^{\mathsf T}=\operatorname{Im}W_{i_*,t-1}^{\mathsf T}\). The lemma uses only the cokernel paragraph of that proof, which needs only \(|Y|\ge2k+1\). Here \(i_*\) is the largest \(i\le t-1\) with \(i\equiv t\pmod p\), and the kernel is 0 if there is none. The identification is proved over \(\mathbb F_p\). Both sides are given by integer matrices, so the dimensions and the equality persist over any field of characteristic \(p\). In characteristic 0 the kernel is 0: for a prime \(p>t\), Wilson's formula gives full rank over \(\mathbb F_p\), since every \(\binom{t-i}{t-1-i}=t-i\) lies in \(1,\dots,t\), and the rank of an integer matrix over \(\mathbb Q\) is at least its rank over \(\mathbb F_p\). So it suffices that \(W_{i_*,t-1}h=0\). Since \(i_*\le t-p\le t-2\), \(W_{i_*,t-2}W_{t-2,t-1}=(t-1-i_*)W_{i_*,t-1}\), and \(t-1-i_*\equiv-1\pmod p\) is a unit. Hence \(W_{i_*,t-1}h=(t-1-i_*)^{-1}W_{i_*,t-2}(W_{t-2,t-1}h)=0\), because \(W_{t-2,t-1}h\) is the marginal of \(h\). \(\square\)

The theorem

Theorem (restriction injectivity). Over a field of characteristic \(p\) or 0, for \(t\ge0\) and \(|X|\ge2t+1\), \(Z_t(X)=\sum_{j\in X}\iota_jZ_t(X\setminus j)\).

Proof. By induction on \(t\). For \(t=0\), \(\iota_jZ_0(X\setminus j)=Z_0(X)\). Let \(t\ge1\), \(f\in Z_t(X)\), and fix \(j\in X\).

  1. By Lemma 1, \(h=f^{+j}\in Z_{t-1}(X\setminus j)\). Since \(|X\setminus j|\ge2t\ge2(t-1)+1\), the induction hypothesis gives \(h=\sum_{k\ne j}\iota_kh_k\) with \(h_k\in Z_{t-1}(X\setminus\{j,k\})\).
  2. For each \(k\ne j\), Lemma 2 on \(X'=X\setminus k\), \(|X'|\ge2t\), with the point \(j\), gives \(\varphi_k\in Z_t(X\setminus k)\) with \(\varphi_k^{+j}=h_k\). Then \(\iota_k\varphi_k\in Z_t(X)\), and \((\iota_k\varphi_k)^{+j}=\iota_kh_k\): on sets containing \(k\) both sides are 0.
  3. \(\varphi=\sum_{k\ne j}\iota_k\varphi_k\) lies in the span and satisfies \(\varphi^{+j}=h=f^{+j}\). By Lemma 1, \(f-\varphi\in\iota_jZ_t(X\setminus j)\). So \(f=\varphi+(f-\varphi)\) lies in the span. \(\square\)

Corollary. For \(n\ge2t+1\), \(\rho\) is injective in degree \(t\), since \(\rho^*\) is extension by zero and the theorem is its surjectivity. For every row \(i\ge1\), \(0\to R_{[n]}\to\bigoplus_jR_{[n]\setminus j}\to A^{(e_i)}\to0\) is exact with the first two terms in degree \(t\) and \(A^{(e_i)}\) in degree \(t+1\) (the shift by \(\deg x_{ij}\)), for \(t\le(n-1)/2\). The goal needs only \(t\le D-1\) with \(n\ge2D+1\) (occupancy-transfer entry), which lies inside this range.

The theorem proves ex:restriction-injectivity-small's pattern for \(2t<n\) at every \(n\) and \(p\). The recorded failures all have \(2t\ge n\), outside the theorem.

The placed-pigeon identity

Lemma (placed pigeon). With \(m\) rows, any row \(i\), hole \(j\), and \(C_{j'}\) standing for \(\sum_{i'}x_{i'j'}\): \(x_{ij}(C_j-z)\), \(x_{ij}\bigl(\sum_{j'\ne j}C_{j'}-(m-1)z\bigr)\) and \(x_{ij}(C_{j'}^2-C_{j'}z)\) lie in the homogenized weak base ideal. So \(x_{ij}\,H(C,z)\equiv x_{ij}\,H(C,z)|_{C_j=z}\) modulo that ideal for every polynomial \(H\).

Proof. \(x_{ij}C_j=x_{ij}^2+\sum_{i'\ne i}x_{ij}x_{i'j}\equiv x_{ij}z\), by Booleanity and column exclusions. So \(x_{ij}(C_j-z)\) lies in the ideal, and \(x_{ij}\bigl(\sum_{j'\ne j}C_{j'}-(m-1)z\bigr)=x_{ij}\bigl(\sum_{j'}C_{j'}-mz\bigr)-x_{ij}(C_j-z)\). The first term is \(x_{ij}\sum_{i'}(r_{i'}-z)\). The relations \(C_{j'}^2-C_{j'}z\) are in the ideal by the occupancy transfer lemma. Substituting \(C_j\to z\) in \(h\) changes \(x_{ij}h\) by multiples of \(x_{ij}(C_j-z)\). \(\square\)

Apply this to \(H=h_k^{\rm h}\), the homogenized member, and its specialization \(h_k^{\rm h}|_{C_j=z}\), a polynomial in the other holes' \(C\) and \(z\). Take an identity \(\sum_k\tilde\sigma_k\,h_k^{\rm h}|_{C_j=z}=z\sum_kq_k\,h_k^{\rm h}|_{C_j=z}\) in the occupancy ring of the holes \([n]\setminus j\) with right-hand side \(m-1\). Multiplied by \(x_{ij}\), it becomes \(\sum_kx_{ij}\tilde\sigma_k\,g_k^{\rm h}\equiv z\sum_kx_{ij}q_k\,g_k^{\rm h}\) modulo the homogenized weak base. That is an identity for \(x_{ij}\) times a lift on the \(j\)-th summand. Using the specialization of the homogenized member, rather than the homogenization of the restricted member, avoids a power of \(z\) whenever \(h_k|_{C_j=1}\) has lower degree than \(h_k\). A content-\(e_i\) syzygy is a sum over \(j\) whose summands need not be syzygies separately, so what the route still needs is:

  • augmentation of the restricted members, since restricting a Gröbner basis does not give one;
  • the long exact sequence of the resolution above for the member's syzygies: syzygies on \(\bigoplus_jR_{[n]\setminus j}\), plus the kernel of \(R/(P)\to\bigoplus_jR_{[n]\setminus j}/(P|_j)\), whose lifts must be compared.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the one-row theorem's kernel identification and its hypotheses, and the occupancy-transfer entry's content-one proposition and transfer lemma. A fresh-context reviewer checked Lemma 1, the extension by zero, the marginal computation of Lemma 2, \(i_*\le t-2\) and the unit, the product formula, the induction sizes, the link of \(\iota_k\varphi_k\), the final step, the duality with \(\rho\), and the placed-pigeon memberships, and found no error. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • characteristic 0 and general fields of characteristic \(p\) justified;
  • \(t=1\) handled directly;
  • the degree shift of \(A^{(e_i)}\) stated;
  • the degree claim replaced by the recorded need;
  • the title corrected;
  • two unused hypotheses dropped from the placed-pigeon lemma;
  • the transfer restated for the specialized homogenized member, and narrowed to one summand.

The changes add justifications and narrow claims, so no further pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • The content-one syzygy argument: the two items above.
  • Contents \(|c|\ge2\): the analogous resolutions over several removed holes.
  • Hypothesis (b).

Placed-pigeon falls: a column member without occupancy falls can fall on the board, and after its placed-pigeon closure it falls exactly like the weak base on the merged board

24 September 2026 · Refutation by finite check, and conjecture · Hypothesis (c) for column members beyond content 0; cycle odd-prime-content-one. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The occupancy-transfer entry proved hypothesis (c) for column members in content 0, and the restriction-injectivity entry resolved content one by column models on \(n\) and \(n-1\) holes. The proposed route for content one needed the specialized members, with one pigeon placed, to have no falls. The cycle first tests whether a column member whose occupancy system has no fall can fall on the board at all.

General statement. ex:placed-pigeon-falls refutes the extension of occupancy transfer to all contents. The member \(\{C_1C_2\}\), holes 1 and 2 not both occupied, has no fall in the occupancy ring, yet with the weak base it falls on the board. The falls come from placed pigeons: \(x_{i1}C_2\equiv x_{i1}C_1C_2\) is derivable at degree 3 but not at its own degree 2. After the member is closed under its placed-pigeon consequences, derivable one degree higher by lem:placed-pigeon-identity, the remaining falls coincide in every tested case with those of the weak base on the board with holes 1 and 2 merged. conj:effective-board: for a column member, the weak base plus the member's placed-pigeon closure has, below \(D\), the falls of the weak base on the member's effective board. Hypothesis (c) for column members is then hypothesis (a) on a smaller board.

The test

Tested statement. Hypothesis (c) of thm:relative-gluing for the member \(\{C_1C_2\}\), \(C_j=\sum_ix_{ij}\): the homogenized weak base plus \((C_1C_2)^{\rm h}\) is \(z\)-injective below \(D\). Its occupancy system \(\{C_j^2-C_j,\ \sum C_j-m,\ C_1C_2\}\) has no fall, so the occupancy-transfer argument covers its content-0 syzygies. The quantity is \(\dim\ker(z:B_k\to B_{k+1})\), from exact Hilbert functions truncated at \(D\) in Singular (member_fall.py, fall.json). Controls: the base alone, and the weak base on \(N-1\) columns (merged_compare.json, the recorded base_injectivity.py).

rows × \(N\)\(D\)basebase + \(C_1C_2\)base + closureweak base, rows × \((N-1)\)
3 × 530, 0, 00, 0, 50, 0, 80, 0, 8
3 × 740, 0, 0, 00, 0, 4, 520, 0, 0, 210, 0, 0, 21
4 × 740, 0, 0, 00, 0, 6, 1060, 0, 0, 690, 0, 0, 69

The entries are \(\dim\ker z\) in degrees \(0,\dots,D-1\). The closure adds, for all rows \(i,i'\), the placed-pigeon consequences \(x_{i1}C_2\) and \(x_{i2}C_1\) (a pigeon in one hole empties the other), and \(x_{i1}x_{i'2}\) (no pigeons in both).

What the numbers show

  • The member falls. On the 3 × 7 board the fall in degree 2 has dimension 4. That is the span of \(x_{i1}C_2\) and \(x_{i2}C_1\), \(i=0,1,2\), modulo their two sums over \(i\), which equal \(C_1C_2\) and so lie in the member ideal at degree 2. Each \(x_{i1}C_2\) is derivable at degree 3: \(x_{i1}\cdot C_1C_2\equiv x_{i1}C_2\) by the placed-pigeon identity (\(x_{i1}C_1\equiv x_{i1}\)). So occupancy no-fall does not imply board no-fall, and hypothesis (c) fails for this member as it stands.
  • The closure removes the placed-pigeon falls, and what remains is the merged board. The closure's elements are derivable from the member at one degree more, so the closed system has the same PC closure at every degree \(D\ge3\). Its falls equal, in all three cases, those of the weak base on \(N-1\) columns. Semantically, \(C_1C_2=0\) with its closure makes holes 1 and 2 one hole: \(y_i=x_{i1}+x_{i2}\) satisfies \(y_i^2\equiv y_i\) and \(y_iy_{i'}\equiv0\) modulo the closure, and the row sums become those of the merged board. At \(N=7\), \(D=4\), the merged board has \(N-1=6<2D-1\) columns, below the stability range of conj:weak-base-stability, and its falls appear.

The conjecture

Conjecture (effective board). For a column member with allowed set \(Z\) in the occupancy cube, let its placed-pigeon closure be the member together with all \(x_Xf\) for column-injective cell sets \(X\) of size at most \(D\) and polynomials \(f\) in the other holes' \(C\) vanishing on the points of \(Z\) with the holes of \(X\) occupied, of degree at most \(D-|X|\). Below \(D\), the weak base plus the closure falls exactly as the weak base on the member's effective board does: the board on which \(Z\) becomes a structure of merged or removed holes. In particular, for members that merge holes, the closure is stable below \(D\) when the merged board has at least \((p-1)D^2\) columns (thm:weak-base-stability-quadratic).

Evidence: the three exact matches above, for the simplest merging member. What is checked directly: the closure is derivable one degree higher (lem:placed-pigeon-identity). The merged base maps into the closed system through \(y_i=x_{i1}+x_{i2}\): \(y_i^2-y_i\equiv2x_{i1}x_{i2}\), \(y_iy_{i'}\equiv x_{i1}x_{i'2}+x_{i2}x_{i'1}\) modulo column exclusions, and both lie in the closure, while the row sums map to row sums. Open: a definition of the effective board for general \(Z\), and the isomorphism of fall spaces.

What this means

  • Hypothesis (c) must be applied to members after placed-pigeon closure. The closure carries pigeon cells, so hypothesis (b) must allow tops of positive content, and the tensor-splitting framework, stated for tops in the members' form algebras, must be extended.
  • If the conjecture holds, (c) for column members is hypothesis (a) on a smaller board, and a column member is harmless exactly when it leaves an effective board in the stability range. For the goal, the column constraints come from wide clauses in the budget (lem:quiet-members), each forbidding a fraction about \(p^{-k}\) of the occupancy patterns. How far such constraints can shrink the effective board is the question that decides the column component.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the relative gluing theorem's hypothesis (c), the occupancy-transfer lemma's scope (content 0), and the placed-pigeon identity. The Singular driver reproduced the base-alone controls. They show no fall, matching the recorded weak-base data (these sizes lie below the proved quadratic range). The merged-board values come from the recorded, cross-engine-validated base_injectivity.py. The fall dimension 4 at 3 × 7 is explained after the run by 6 placed-pigeon products minus 2 sums; the value 5 at 3 × 5 is not explained. The entry registers one finite check and one conjecture, and no proof, so no reviewer pass was run.

Remaining gap

  • A proof of the effective-board conjecture, first for merging members.
  • The extension of hypothesis (b) to members with tops of positive content.
  • The size of the effective board left by budget column members.

Route review: column members act as board restrictions; the exact effective-board law fails below the stability range, and its stability form is the target

24 September 2026 · Route review with a refutation · The relative gluing line after the column-member cycles; cycle odd-prime-effective-board-review. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

General statement. The line's claim is thm:relative-gluing with (a) proved at logarithmic degree (thm:weak-base-stability-quadratic). For column members, (c) holds after Gröbner augmentation on seeded spans (thm:seeded-member-condition) and in content 0 for any span (lem:occupancy-transfer). Beyond content 0 it holds only after placed-pigeon closure (ex:placed-pigeon-falls). The review's new claim is conj:effective-board-stability: for a column member whose closed system is a weak base on an effective board, the closed system is stable below \(D\) when that board is in the stability range. ex:merge-three-effective-board refutes the exact form of conj:effective-board below that range.

What the goal needs

At degree \(D=O(\log n)\), for the product clauses of any \(n^K\) adversarial families:

  • (a): proved.
  • (c) for the column component, which cannot split: after placed-pigeon closure, no falls below \(D\). If column members act as board restrictions, this asks that the adversary's column constraints leave an effective board in the stability range, of order \(D^2\) columns.
  • (c) for non-column members: open.
  • (b) for closed members, whose tops carry pigeon cells: open, and the tensor-splitting framework needs extending.

Falsification attempt: a three-hole merge

If the exact effective-board law held, merging holes 1, 2, 3 (\(C_aC_b=0\), \(a\ne b\)) with its placed-pigeon closure (\(x_{ia}C_b\), \(x_{ia}x_{i'b}\)) would fall exactly like the weak base on \(N-2\) columns. merge3.py computes the closed system's falls exactly in Singular (merge3.json), and base_injectivity.py the comparison (merge3_compare.json). Values are \(\dim\ker z\) in degrees 0 to 3, \(D=4\), over \(\mathbb F_3\):

rows × \(N\)closed merge of 3weak base, rows × \((N-2)\)
4 × 80, 0, 0, 690, 0, 0, 69
3 × 90, 0, 0, 00, 0, 0, 0
3 × 70, 0, 0, 1080, 0, 0, 48

The exact law fails at 3 × 7, where the merged board has 5 columns, below \(2D-1=7\). There the closed system falls more than the merged base. It holds at 4 × 8, and at 3 × 9, where the merged board has 7 columns and neither falls. The attempt refutes the exact form. It leaves the stability form, which matters for the goal: no falls when the effective board is in range.

Why the stability form should be provable for merging members

For a merge of a hole set \(H\), the closed system is exactly a weak base with one fat column. The generators \(x_{ia}x_{i'b}\), \(a\ne b\in H\), together with the column exclusions inside each hole of \(H\), make the span of all \(x_{ia}\), \(a\in H\), a square-zero column. The member's constraints \(C_aC_b\) and \(x_{ia}C_b\) are combinations of these. The proof of thm:weak-base-stability-quadratic uses:

  • a column tensor product with square-zero columns and a \(z\)-free lift;
  • row sums acting diagonally;
  • Frobenius lifts;
  • seeds made of ordinary columns;
  • row reduction.

A fat column is one more tensor factor, the module \(M\) of the free-seed lemma. So the closed system should be stable below \(D\) whenever the ordinary columns number at least \((p-1)D^2\). This is the next step, to be written as a proof.

Assessment of the line

In twelve cycles the line went from four conjectural hypotheses to a proved base condition (a), a proved member condition (c) in two regimes, seeded spans and content 0, and a precise picture of what remains. Column members behave as restrictions of the board. Their harm is measured by how much board they leave, which is the PHP counting question in its natural form.

The evidence for this picture is exact, but at sizes \(n\le9\) and \(D\le4\). Its exact form has now failed once, below the stability range. Two parts are untested at the goal's scale:

  • whether budget column constraints, wide and few, can shrink the effective board below order \(D^2\);
  • whether (b) survives the closure.

Both are where the thread's oldest difficulty, the occupancy window, now sits.

The highest-risk item and the next step

The column component remains the highest risk. Next:

  1. Prove conj:effective-board-stability for merging members, by the fat-column extension of the weak-base stability proof.
  2. Then ask what effective boards budget column constraints can produce: members that forbid a \(p^{-k}\) fraction of occupancy patterns on spans of dimension about \(\log n\).

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the placed-pigeon-falls entry and its conjecture, the weak-base stability proof's ingredients, and the free-seed lemma. The comparison values come from the recorded, cross-engine-validated driver. The refutation is exact; the stability form is recorded as a conjecture. No reviewer pass was run, since the review adds no proof.

Fat columns: a weak board with merged holes has no falls below D when (p−1)D² holes stay unmerged, so merging members satisfy condition (c) after closure

24 September 2026 · Working proof · Effective-board stability for merging column members, every \(p\); cycle odd-prime-fat-columns. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The effective-board review found that a merging column member, closed under its placed-pigeon consequences, is exactly a weak base with a fat column. It proposed proving conj:effective-board-stability for such members by extending the weak-base stability proof. The cycle carries this out.

General statement. thm:fat-board-stability: over a field of characteristic \(p\), take a weak board whose columns are ordinary or fat. A fat column is a set of cells \((i,a)\), \(a\) in a hole set \(H\), with every product of two distinct of its cells a generator. If the board has \(m\ge D\) rows and at least \((p-1)D^2\) ordinary columns, its homogenized base is \(z\)-injective below \(D\). cor:merging-members: for disjoint hole sets \(H_1,\dots,H_q\), the weak base plus the merging constraints \(C_aC_b\) (\(a\ne b\) in the same \(H_s\)) and their placed-pigeon closure generates the same homogenized ideal as such a fat board. So if at least \((p-1)D^2\) holes lie outside \(\bigcup_sH_s\), the closed system has no fall below \(D\) and no PC refutation of degree \(D\). The closed member satisfies hypothesis (c) of thm:relative-gluing through \(D\). Hypothesis (b) must then accommodate its tops, which are not polynomials in the column sums. The unclosed system has no refutation of degree \(D\) either.

The fat board

Rows \(0,\dots,m-1\). Columns are ordinary holes \(j\), with cells \((i,j)\), or fat columns \(F\) with cells \((i,a)\), \(a\in H_F\). The generators are Booleanity \(x_c^2-x_c\) for every cell, the products \(x_cx_{c'}\) of distinct cells in the same column, ordinary or fat, and the row equations \(\sum_{c\in\text{row }i}x_c-1\). An ordinary column is the case \(|H|=1\), with the usual column exclusions.

The proof

Theorem (fat-board stability). Under the hypotheses of the general statement, \(z\) is injective on the homogenized fat base below \(D\).

Proof. The proof of thm:weak-base-stability-quadratic (weak-base stability) goes through, with these changes.

  1. Step 1 (falls come from non-Frobenius syzygies). \(\tilde A_z=\mathbb F[x,z]/(x_c^2-x_cz,\ x_cx_{c'})\), for all pairs of distinct cells in a common column. Use a degree order with every \(x_c>z\), so \(x_c^2\) leads. Then \(\tilde A_z\) is free over \(\mathbb F[z]\) on the monomials \(x_T\), \(T\) meeting each column in at most one cell. The only S-pairs without coprime leading terms, other than pairs of monomials, are \(x_{c'}(x_c^2-x_cz)-x_c(x_cx_{c'})=-x_cx_{c'}z\), and symmetrically in \(c'\); they reduce to 0. The Koszul exact sequence, the connecting map and the Frobenius lift are unchanged: \(r_i^p=\sum_cx_c^p=r_iz^{p-1}\) in characteristic \(p\).
  2. Step 2 (free seed). Unchanged.
  3. Step 3 (column tensor power). On \(u\) rows, \(\tilde A=\bigotimes_{\text{columns}}V\). An ordinary column has \(V=\mathbb F\oplus\operatorname{span}(x_{ij}:i<u)\). A fat column has \(V_F=\mathbb F\oplus\operatorname{span}(x_{ia}:i<u,\ a\in H_F)\). Both are square-zero. \(R_i\) acts on \(V_F\) as multiplication by \(y_i=\sum_{a\in H_F}x_{ia}\), which sends \(1\) to \(y_i\) and every \(x_{ia}\) to 0. The \(y_i\) commute, and \(y_i^p=0\), so \(V_F\) is a \(T\)-module. Multiplication by \(r_i\) is the diagonal primitive action, as before. The seeds are taken among the ordinary columns: \(b=u(p-1)\) of them carry a free copy of \(T\), by the same computation. The fat columns, the ordinary columns of the leftover \(e\), and the other ordinary columns outside the seed blocks form the factor \(M\) of the free-seed lemma, which may be any graded module in degrees \(\ge0\). With at least \((p-1)D\cdot D\) ordinary columns and \(u=D\), there are \(n\ge D\) seed blocks.
  4. Row reduction. The content splitting and the row-reduction lemma (lem:weak-row-reduction) go through. Annihilators are functions \(\mu\) on cell sets meeting each column at most once. For \(|T|\le k-1\) and each row \(i\), the equation is \(\sum_c\mu(T\cup\{c\})=(1-c_i(T))\mu(T)\). The sum runs over the cells \(c\) of row \(i\) whose column, ordinary or fat, meets no cell of \(T\), and \(c_i(T)\) counts the cells of \(T\) in row \(i\), fat cells included. Every equation involves one row content. Restricting an \(m\)-row annihilator to the sets within \(r\) rows gives an \(r\)-row fat-board annihilator, since each row-\(i\) equation involves only the rows of \(T\cup\{i\}\). The rest of the restriction argument is unchanged.

So \(z\) is injective below \(D\) on the \(D\)-row fat board, and by row reduction on \(m\ge D\) rows. \(\square\)

Merging members

Corollary (merging members). Over a field of characteristic \(p\), let \(H_1,\dots,H_q\) be disjoint hole sets, and let the member \(U\) consist of the constraints \(C_aC_b\) for \(a\ne b\) in a common \(H_s\), with \(C_j=\sum_ix_{ij}\). Let the closure \(\bar U\) be \(U\) together with \(x_{ia}C_b\) and \(x_{ia}x_{i'b}\), for all rows \(i,i'\), \(i=i'\) included, and \(a\ne b\) in a common \(H_s\). The \(x_{ia}C_b\) and the \(C_aC_b\) are sums of the \(x_{ia}x_{i'b}\). If at least \((p-1)D^2\) holes lie outside \(\bigcup_sH_s\) and \(m\ge D\), then:

  1. the weak base plus \(\bar U\) generates, in every degree, the same homogenized ideal as the fat base with fat columns \(H_1,\dots,H_q\). So it has no fall below \(D\), and no PC refutation of degree \(D\): by the socle criterion, as in step 5 of the relative gluing proof, \(z\)-injectivity below \(D\) with no constant generator excludes one;
  2. the weak base plus \(U\) alone has no PC refutation of degree \(D\), since its generators are a subset;
  3. \(\bar U\), as a member of the relative gluing theorem, satisfies hypothesis (c): every top syzygy of degree at most \(D\) supported on it is liftable. This follows from the sufficient condition stated in (c), \(z\) injective on the base plus the member below \(D\), which is item 1. The relative gluing theorem allows any polynomial constraints as members, so \(\bar U\) is admissible. Its tops are not polynomials in the column sums, which matters for (b), not for (c).

Proof. For item 1, the generators of the weak base plus \(\bar U\) are Booleanity, the column exclusions inside each hole, the products \(x_{ia}x_{i'b}\) across holes of one \(H_s\), and the row equations. Together these are all products of distinct cells in each fat column. \(C_aC_b=\sum_{i,i'}x_{ia}x_{i'b}\) and \(x_{ia}C_b=\sum_{i'}x_{ia}x_{i'b}\) lie in the ideal they generate at the same degree. The theorem applies with the unmerged holes as ordinary columns. Items 2 and 3 follow as stated. \(\square\)

Relation to the data. At \(p=3\) the corollary needs at least 18 unmerged holes for \(D=3\) and 32 for \(D=4\). The tested boards of ex:placed-pigeon-falls and ex:merge-three-effective-board have 5 to 9 columns, so the data lie below the proved range, neither testing the corollary nor following from it. Those checks compared the closed system, the fat base, with the ordinary weak base on \(N-|H|+1\) columns. The fat base's falls can exceed that board's (3 × 7: 108 against 48), so the exact effective-board law is not claimed.

The closure is also cheap to derive. \(x_{ia}\cdot C_aC_b\equiv x_{ia}C_b\) at degree 3 by the placed-pigeon identity, and \(x_{i'b}\cdot x_{ia}C_b\equiv z\,x_{ia}x_{i'b}\). So the closure is PC-derivable from the member at degree 3. For lower bounds only the subset direction of item 2 is needed.

What this means

  • conj:effective-board-stability, stated with at least \((p-1)D^2\) ordinary columns, is proved for merging members in that range.
  • Remark: a member forcing \(C_j=0\) gives \(x_{ij}C_j\equiv x_{ij}z\), so each \(x_{ij}\) is derivable at degree 2, and the system is the weak base on \(N-1\) columns. Removals therefore reduce the ordinary column count by one.
  • Other column members, such as couplings \(C_1=C_2\) or cardinality patterns on several holes, are not known to close to fat boards. Their effective boards are not yet defined.
  • For the goal, the question becomes which effective boards the budget column constraints can produce, and whether they always leave order \(D^2\) ordinary columns.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the weak-base stability proof in full, the row-reduction lemma and content splitting, the relative gluing theorem's hypothesis (c) and step 5, and the two finite checks. A fresh-context reviewer found the theorem's proof correct (Steps 1 to 3 and row reduction), item 1 of the corollary correct with the ideal-equality wording, and no unused hypothesis. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the data placed below the proved range;
  • the comparison board named correctly;
  • (c) quoted and matched in degree, with admissibility and the consequence for (b);
  • \(\bar U\) defined explicitly, with \(i=i'\);
  • ideal equality in place of identity;
  • the term order and the symmetric S-pairs;
  • the fat module's \(T\)-structure;
  • the row equation and the restriction step written out;
  • the socle criterion cited for nonrefutation;
  • the removal remark derived and the coupling remark weakened;
  • the derivation degree stated.

The changes make statements precise or weaken them, so no further pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • Column members whose closure is not a fat board.
  • The effective boards of budget column constraints.
  • Hypothesis (b) for closed members; non-column members.

Conditioning on occupancy: the weak base with every column sum fixed has no falls below D when N ≥ (p−1)D²

24 September 2026 · Working proof · The weak onto system, every \(p\); cycle odd-prime-budget-columns. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The fat-columns entry proved hypothesis (c) for merging column members after closure. For general column members the entry proposed classifying budget constraints. That test cannot decide at computable sizes: a wide clause has degree \((p-1)k\) and is invisible below \(D\) there. The cycle takes another route. A column member constrains the occupancy vector, so condition on it: fix every column sum. The question is whether the weak base conditioned on a full occupancy pattern, a weak onto system, keeps the base's stability. If it does, it is the fiber statement for a general column member.

General statement. thm:onto-stability: over a field of characteristic \(p\), let the weak onto system on \(m\) rows and \(N\) columns be the weak unary base together with the column equations \(C_j-1\), \(C_j=\sum_ix_{ij}\), for every column. If \(m\equiv N\pmod p\) and \(N\ge(p-1)D^2\), its homogenization is \(z\)-injective below \(D\). If \(m\not\equiv N\), it is refuted at degree 1. Conditioning the weak base on an occupancy pattern with support \(S\) gives, after deleting the variables of empty columns, which are derived at degree 2, the onto system on the columns of \(S\). So this reduced conditioned system is stable below \(D\) when \(|S|\ge(p-1)D^2\) and \(|S|\equiv m\). The unreduced conditioned system has falls at degree 1, one for each deleted variable.

Setting

\(\tilde A_z=\mathbb F[x,z]/(x_{ij}^2-x_{ij}z,\ x_{ij}x_{i'j})\) and \(\tilde A=\tilde A_z/z\tilde A_z=\bigotimes_jV_j\), \(V_j=\mathbb F\oplus\operatorname{span}(x_{ij}:i<m)\) square-zero, as in the weak-base stability entry, with rows indexed \(0,\dots,m-1\) here (the entry uses \(1,\dots,m\)). The onto system is \(B=\tilde A_z/(r_i-z,\ C_j-z)\). Since \(\sum_ir_i=\sum_jC_j\) in \(\tilde A_z\), \((r_0-z)=\sum_j(C_j-z)-\sum_{i\ge1}(r_i-z)+(N-m)z\). If \(N\not\equiv m\), this puts \(z\) in the homogenized ideal at degree 1, so the dehomogenized system derives 1 at degree 1. If \(N\equiv m\), \(r_0-z\) is redundant, and \(B=\tilde A_z/(f)\) for the sequence \(f=(r_1-z,\dots,r_{m-1}-z,\ C_1-z,\dots,C_N-z)\) with tops \((r_1,\dots,r_{m-1},C_1,\dots,C_N)\).

The proof

Theorem (onto stability). Under the hypotheses of the general statement with \(m\equiv N\pmod p\), \(z\) is injective on \(B\) below \(D\).

Proof. By Step 1 of the weak-base stability proof, which uses only that \(\tilde A_z\) is \(z\)-free and that the generators are homogeneous of degree 1, \(\ker(z:B_k\to B_{k+1})\) is the image of the connecting map \(\delta\) on \(H_1(r_1,\dots,r_{m-1},C_1,\dots,C_N;\tilde A)_{k+1}\). Call a Koszul 1-cycle \(((a_i)_{i\ge1},(b_j)_j)\), with \(\sum_ia_ir_i+\sum_jb_jC_j=0\) in \(\tilde A\), liftable when \(\delta\) kills its class. Liftable cycles form a subspace. It contains the following:

  • Koszul boundaries, among the \(r\), among the \(C\), and mixed. Their lifts are exact.
  • Frobenius cycles \(r_i^{p-1}c\,e_i\). \(\tilde a\,r_i^{p-1}(r_i-z)\in z\,(r_i-z)\) as in the weak-base proof, since \(r_i^p=r_iz^{p-1}\) in \(\tilde A_z\).
  • Placed cycles \(x_{ij}y\,e'_j\), for any \(y\). These are cycles since \(x_{ij}C_j=0\) in \(\tilde A\). In \(\tilde A_z\), \(x_{ij}C_j=x_{ij}^2+\sum_{i'\ne i}x_{ij}x_{i'j}=x_{ij}z\), so \(\tilde y\,x_{ij}(C_j-z)=0\) and \(u=0\).

We show every cycle of degree \(k+1\le D\) is a sum of these.

  1. Modulo the column sums. The \(C_j\) act column by column, so \(\bar A=\tilde A/(C_1,\dots,C_N)\tilde A=\bigotimes_jW_j\), with \(W_j=V_j/\mathbb FC_j\). A basis of \(W_j^+\) is given by the images \(\bar x_{ij}\), \(i\ge1\), since \(\bar x_{0j}=-\sum_{i\ge1}\bar x_{ij}\). So \(W_j\) is the column module of the weak board on rows \(1,\dots,m-1\), and \(\bar r_i\), \(i\ge1\), acts on \(\bar A\) as that board's row sums act. In other words, \(\bar A\) is the column tensor power \(\tilde A_{m-1}\) of the weak board on \(m-1\) rows, with its row sums.
  2. Row-sum syzygies modulo the column sums are Frobenius. \(\bar A\) is graded by the row content of rows \(1,\dots,m-1\), and each \(\bar r_i\) has content \(e_i\). The content-\(c\) parts of \(K_1\) and \(K_2\) of \(K(\bar r;\bar A)\) coincide with the content-\(c\) parts of \(K(\bar r_{\operatorname{supp}c};\bar A_{\operatorname{supp}c})\), the complex of the weak column tensor power on the \(u=|\operatorname{supp}c|\) rows of \(\operatorname{supp}c\). So the content components of a cycle of degree \(k+1\le D\) are cycles there, with \(u\le\min(k+1,m-1)\). On \(u\) rows, Step 3 of the weak-base stability proof (free seeds) with blocks of \(b=(p-1)u\le(p-1)D\) columns gives \(n\ge D\) blocks from \(N\ge(p-1)D^2\), so \(H_1\) in degrees \(\le D\) is spanned by Frobenius classes. Frobenius cycles and boundaries have content-homogeneous components of the same kinds, so each content component is Frobenius plus a boundary. Hence \(\bar a_i=\bar r_i^{\,p-1}\bar c_i+\sum_{i'}\bar r_{i'}\bar t_{ii'}\) with \(\bar t\) antisymmetric.
  3. Lift and subtract. Lift to \(\tilde A\), with \(c_i\), \(t\) and \(w_{ij}\) homogeneous of the right degrees and \(t\) antisymmetric (lift \(\bar t_{ii'}\) for \(i<i'\) and set \(t_{i'i}=-t_{ii'}\)): \(a_i=r_i^{p-1}c_i+\sum_{i'}r_{i'}t_{ii'}+\sum_jC_jw_{ij}\). Subtract the Frobenius cycles \(r_i^{p-1}c_ie_i\), the \(r\)-Koszul boundaries of \(t\), and the mixed boundaries \(C_jw_{ij}e_i-r_iw_{ij}e'_j\). The remainder is a cycle \((0,(b'_j))\), a syzygy of the column sums alone.
  4. Column-sum syzygies are placed. The Koszul complex of \((C_j)\) on \(\bigotimes_jV_j\) is the tensor product of the complexes \(V_j\xrightarrow{C_j}V_j\). Each has \(H_1=\ker C_j=V_j^+=\operatorname{span}(x_{ij})\), since \(C_j\cdot1=C_j\ne0\) and \(C_jV_j^+=0\). By the Künneth formula over a field, \(H_1\) of the product is spanned by classes \(x_{ij}y\,e'_j\). So \((0,b')\) is a sum of placed cycles and \(C\)-Koszul boundaries. \(\square\)

Conditioning

For an occupancy pattern \(c\in\{0,1\}^N\) with support \(S\), the conditioned system is the weak base with \(C_j-c_j\) for all \(j\). For \(j\notin S\), \(x_{ij}\cdot C_j\equiv x_{ij}\) at degree 2, by Booleanity and column exclusions, so \(x_{ij}\) is derived at degree 2. In the homogenized system \(x_{ij}z\) lies in the ideal while \(x_{ij}\) does not at degree 1: the functional with \(z\mapsto0\) and values \(+1,-1,-1,+1\) at \((i,j),(i,j'),(i',j),(i',j')\) kills every degree-1 generator. So the unreduced conditioned system falls at degree 1. Deleting the variables \(x_{ij}\), \(j\notin S\), which is the restriction setting them to 0, gives the onto system on the columns of \(S\) with \(m\) rows. A PC refutation of degree \(D\) of the conditioned system restricts to one of the reduced system, whose generators the restriction maps to generators or to 0. By the theorem the reduced system is stable below \(D\), hence has no refutation of degree \(D\) (by the socle criterion), when \(|S|\ge(p-1)D^2\) and \(|S|\equiv m\pmod p\). On the PHP board, \(m=N+1\) and \(|S|\le N\).

What this means

  • The fibers of a column member are stable in reduced form: for each allowed occupancy pattern with support large enough and of the right residue, the weak base conditioned on it, with the empty columns' variables deleted, has no falls below \(D\). Its only extra falls before deletion are those variables, derived at degree 2. Patterns with the wrong residue are excluded by the base at degree 1, which is the occupancy ring's relation \(\sum_jC_j=m\).
  • Proposed route for general column members, not proved. A member with allowed set \(Z\) should be stable when every pattern of \(Z\) has a large support. Its annihilators would be glued from occupancy-ring annihilators on \(Z\), stable after augmentation by lem:occupancy-transfer, and onto-system annihilators on each fiber, stable by this theorem. The gluing across fibers is the missing piece. It is a relative-gluing statement with the occupancy ring as the base and the fibers as the members.
  • Patterns of support below \((p-1)D^2\) are not covered, since they lie outside the hypothesis \(N\ge(p-1)D^2\). On the PHP board every pattern, large or small, is excluded only by counting, since \(|S|\le N<m\). The theorem shows that for large supports this counting needs degree at least \(D\). Whether small supports need separate treatment is open.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the weak-base stability proof in full (Step 1, the free-seed lemma, Step 3 and row reduction) and the placed-pigeon identity. Searches: onto system, column sums fixed, occupancy conditioning, fiber. Found no earlier result that implies the theorem. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed the setting (\(\sum r_i=\sum C_j\), the elimination of \(r_0-z\), the applicability of Step 1), the three liftable families, \(W_j=V_j/\mathbb FC_j\) and the Künneth step. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the conditioning claim restricted to the reduced presentation, with the degree-1 falls of the unreduced one shown;
  • the unused hypothesis \(m-1\ge D\) dropped, by applying Step 3 on the \(|\operatorname{supp}c|\) rows of each content;
  • the content-component step and antisymmetric homogeneous lifts written out;
  • the row indexing and the degree-1 refutation stated precisely;
  • the small-support bullet corrected.

The changes weaken the conditioning claim or drop a hypothesis without adding a claim, so no further pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • The gluing of fibers and occupancy ring for a general column member.
  • Patterns of small support.
  • Hypothesis (b) for closed members; non-column members.
