Fiber gluing: a column member has no falls when its specializations have none and the board modulo its tops is row-free; augmentation does not make dense selectors' specializations fall-free

24 September 2026 · Working proofs, finite checks and a conjecture · Hypothesis (c) for general column members; cycle odd-prime-fiber-gluing. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The onto-stability entry proved that the weak base with every column sum fixed has no falls, and proposed gluing such fibers for a general column member. The missing implication is hypothesis (c) of thm:relative-gluing for the column member the budget produces: the weak base plus the member has no falls below \(D\). The cycle generalizes the onto proof to any column member, which splits (c) into two conditions, and tests both on dense members, selectors and clauses on column forms that touch every hole.

General statement. thm:fiber-gluing: over a field of characteristic \(p\), the weak base plus a column member is \(z\)-injective below \(D\) if (i) for every hole set \(S\), \(|S|<D\), the member's occupancy system specialized at \(C_S=1\) has no fall below \(D-|S|\), and (ii) the row-sum syzygies of the board modulo the tops of the occupancy system are Frobenius cycles plus boundaries through degree \(D\), which holds when that module is free over the row-sum algebra in low degrees. lem:sparse-row-freeness proves (ii) for members supported on holes \(H\) with \(N-|H|\ge(p-1)(D+1)D\). cor:base-by-fibers: the weak base itself satisfies both, for every row count. conj:row-freeness: (ii) holds for every column member when \(N\ge(p-1)(D+1)D\), with no restriction on the support. Its support, ex:dense-row-freeness, covers only augmented members, content \(ke_1\) and smaller \(N\). ex:hereditary-falls shows that (i) can fail for dense selectors and clauses even after Gröbner augmentation.

Setting

Rows \(0,\dots,m-1\), holes \(1,\dots,N\), \(\tilde A_z\) and \(\tilde A=\bigotimes_jV_j\) as in the onto-stability entry. A column member is given by homogenized generators \(f_k^{\rm h}\in\mathbb F[C,z]\), \(C_j=\sum_ix_{ij}\), none constant. Since \(\sum_ir_i=s:=\sum_jC_j\) in \(\tilde A_z\), \(r_0-z=(s-mz)-\sum_{i\ge1}(r_i-z)\). So the weak base plus the member is \(B=\tilde A_z/(r_1-z,\dots,r_{m-1}-z,\ g'^{\rm h})\), where \(g'^{\rm h}\) runs over \(s-mz\) and the \(f_k^{\rm h}\): the member's occupancy system \(J\), in the occupancy ring \(O_z=\mathbb F[C,z]/(C_j^2-C_jz)\), which maps to \(\tilde A_z\) by \(C_j\mapsto\sum_ix_{ij}\), since \(C_j^2-C_jz\mapsto0\) there (lem:occupancy-transfer). The map is injective for \(m\ge1\): the images of the \(C_Tz^a\), \(T\) a hole set, are nonzero with disjoint supports in the \(\mathbb F[z]\)-basis \(x_{T'}\) of \(\tilde A_z\), since \(x_{T'}\) determines its hole set. Write \(g'\) for the tops, elements of \(O'=\mathbb F[C]/(C_j^2)\subset\tilde A\).

In \(\tilde A\) put \(U_j=\operatorname{span}(x_{ij}:i\ge1)\). Then \(V_j=\operatorname{span}(1,C_j)\oplus U_j\), \(C_jU_j=0\), and as \(O'\)-modules \[\tilde A=\bigoplus_{S\subseteq[N]}O'_{S^c}\otimes U^{\otimes S},\qquad U^{\otimes S}=\operatorname{span}\Bigl(y=\prod_{j\in S}x_{i_jj}:\ i_j\ge1\Bigr),\] with \(C_j\), \(j\in S\), acting as 0 on the \(S\)-summand. Grading \(C_j\) by content 0 and \(x_{ij}\) by \(e_i\) makes \(\tilde A\) graded by the content of rows \(1,\dots,m-1\); the \(g'\) have content 0.

For a hole set \(S\), the specialized system \(J_S\) lives in \(O_z^{S^c}=\mathbb F[C_{S^c},z]/(C_j^2-C_jz)\), generated by \(g'^{\rm h}|_{C_S=z}\): the member with the holes of \(S\) occupied, and the row \(\sum_{j\notin S}C_j-(m-|S|)z\).

The theorem

Theorem (fiber gluing). Over a field of characteristic \(p\), with \(m\ge1\), suppose:

  1. for every \(S\subseteq[N]\) with \(|S|\le D-1\), \(\emptyset\) included, \(z\) is injective on \(O_z^{S^c}/J_S\) in degrees \(<D-|S|\);
  2. every Koszul 1-cycle of \((r_1,\dots,r_{m-1})\) on \(\bar A=\tilde A/(g')\tilde A\) of degree at most \(D\) is a sum of Frobenius cycles \(r_i^{p-1}c\,e_i\) and boundaries.

Then \(z\) is injective on \(B\) below \(D\).

Proof. Step 1 of the weak-base stability proof uses only that \(\tilde A_z\) is \(z\)-free and that the generators are homogeneous and nonconstant. So \(\ker(z:B_k\to B_{k+1})\) is the image of the connecting map \(\delta\) on \(H_1(r_1,\dots,r_{m-1},g';\tilde A)_{k+1}\). Frobenius cycles and Koszul boundaries have \(\delta=0\) there. Fix a cycle \(((a_i),(b_\ell))\), \(\sum_ia_ir_i+\sum_\ell b_\ell g'_\ell=0\), of degree \(k+1\le D\).

  1. Row-sum part. Modulo \((g')\), \((\bar a_i)\) is a cycle on \(\bar A\). By (ii), \(\bar a_i=\bar r_i^{\,p-1}\bar c_i+\sum_{i'}\bar r_{i'}\bar t_{ii'}\), \(\bar t\) antisymmetric. Lift to \(\tilde A\) homogeneously, with \(t_{i'i}=-t_{ii'}\): \(a_i=r_i^{p-1}c_i+\sum_{i'}r_{i'}t_{ii'}+\sum_\ell g'_\ell w_{i\ell}\). Subtract the Frobenius cycles, the \(r\)-boundaries of \(t\) and the mixed boundaries \(g'_\ell w_{i\ell}e_i-r_iw_{i\ell}e'_\ell\). The remainder is a cycle \((0,(b'_\ell))\): \(\sum_\ell b'_\ell g'_\ell=0\) in \(\tilde A\).
  2. Placed decomposition. The \(g'_\ell\) act on each \(S\)-summand. Expanding \(b'_\ell=\sum_{S,y}\beta_{\ell,y}\,y\) over a basis \(y\) of each \(U^{\otimes S}\), with \(\beta_{\ell,y}\in O'_{S^c}\), each \((\beta_{\ell,y}y)_\ell\) is a cycle, and \(\sum_\ell\beta_{\ell,y}\,g'_\ell|_{C_S=0}=0\) in \(O'_{S^c}\). The \(S\)-summand has degree at least \(|S|\), so \(|S|\le k\).
  3. Lift through the fiber. Lift \(\beta_{\ell,y}\) to \(\tilde\beta_\ell\in O_z^{S^c}\), homogeneous. In \(\tilde A_z\), \(x_{ij}C_j=x_{ij}z\), so \(y\,g'^{\rm h}_\ell=y\,g'^{\rm h}_\ell|_{C_S=z}\). Hence \(\sum_\ell\tilde\beta_\ell\,y\,g'^{\rm h}_\ell=y\,P\), with \(P=\sum_\ell\tilde\beta_\ell g'^{\rm h}_\ell|_{C_S=z}\in(J_S)\). \(P\) reduces to 0 modulo \(z\), so \(P=zv\) with \(v\in O_z^{S^c}\) of degree \(k-|S|\), and \(\delta\) of the cycle is the class of \(yv\). Since \(zv\in J_S\) and \(k-|S|<D-|S|\), (i) gives \(v=\sum_\ell\gamma_\ell\,g'^{\rm h}_\ell|_{C_S=z}\) in \(O_z^{S^c}\). Mapping to \(\tilde A_z\), where \(C_j^2-C_jz\) vanishes, \(yv=\sum_\ell\gamma_\ell\,y\,g'^{\rm h}_\ell\), which lies in the ideal of \(B\) in degree \(k\). So \(\delta=0\). \(\square\)

For the onto system, \(J_S\) is the onto system on \(S^c\), which has no fall when \(m\equiv N\pmod p\), and \(\bar A\) is the weak column tensor power on \(m-1\) rows, whose row-sum syzygies are Frobenius by item 2 of thm:onto-stability's proof. So the theorem contains thm:onto-stability; its item 3 replaces that proof's Künneth step. The case \(S=\emptyset\) of item 3 is lem:occupancy-transfer's lift.

Row freeness for sparse members

Lemma (sparse row freeness). Over a field of characteristic \(p\), if the \(f_k\) involve only the holes of \(H\) and \(N-|H|\ge(p-1)(D+1)D\), condition (ii) holds.

Proof. The content-\(c\) parts of \(K_1\) and \(K_2\) of \(K(r;\bar A)\) coincide with those of the same construction on the \(u=|\operatorname{supp}c|\) rows of \(\operatorname{supp}c\), since the \(g'\) have content 0 and \(x_{ij}\) with \(i\notin\operatorname{supp}c\) never occurs. For a cycle of degree \(k+1\le D\), \(u\le D\). On those rows, \(V_j=\operatorname{span}(1,C_j,x_{ij}:i\in\operatorname{supp}c)\) is a square-zero column of \(u+1\) rows, with \(C_j\) in the place of row 0: \(C_j^2=C_jx_{ij}=x_{ij}x_{i'j}=x_{ij}^2=0\) in \(\tilde A\). So \(\tilde A\) is the weak column tensor power on \(u+1\) rows, with row sums \(s,r_i\), a module over \(T_{u+1}=\mathbb F[R_0,\dots,R_u]/(R^p)\), \(R_0\) acting as \(s\). It factors as \(\tilde A_H\otimes\tilde A_{H^c}\), and \(\tilde A/(f^{\rm top})=(\tilde A_H/(f^{\rm top}))\otimes\tilde A_{H^c}\), a \(T_{u+1}\)-module since multiplication by \(f^{\rm top}\) commutes with the row sums. Step 3 of the weak-base stability proof on \(u+1\) rows gives seed blocks of \((p-1)(u+1)\) columns in \(H^c\), at least \(D\) of them. The free-seed lemma, with \(M=(\tilde A_H/(f^{\rm top}))\otimes(\text{leftover columns})\), gives \(\tilde A/(f^{\rm top})\cong F\oplus Q\), \(F\) graded free over \(T_{u+1}\), \(Q\) in degrees \(\ge D\). Quotienting by \(s\), \(\bar A\cong F/R_0F\oplus Q/R_0Q\), with \(F/R_0F\) free over \(T_u\). So \(H_1(r;\bar A)\) in degrees \(\le D\) is spanned by Frobenius classes, as in Step 3's consequence, and its content components are Frobenius cycles plus boundaries. \(\square\)

Corollary (base by fibers). Over \(\mathbb F_p\), for every \(m\ge1\), \(D\ge1\) and \(N\ge(p-1)(D+1)D\), the homogenized weak base is \(z\)-injective below \(D\).

Proof. Take the empty member, \(H=\emptyset\). (ii) is the lemma. \(J_S\) is a single weak row with right-hand side \(m-|S|\) on \(N-|S|\) holes, \(z\)-injective below \(D-|S|\) by lem:occupancy-stability, since \(N-|S|\ge2(D-|S|)-1\). That lemma's proof uses the right-hand side only as an element of \(\mathbb F_p\), so \(m-|S|\le0\) is covered. \(\square\)

thm:weak-base-stability-quadratic assumes \(m\ge D\) and \(N\ge(p-1)D^2\), over any field of characteristic \(p\). The corollary needs \(N\ge(p-1)(D+1)D\), over \(\mathbb F_p\), and no bound on \(m\): \(u\le\min(D,m-1)\), the bulk row replaces row reduction, and for \(m=1\) (ii) is vacuous.

Tests of the two conditions on dense members

Can the tests decide. The lemma covers members on few holes. The goal's members are selectors and clauses on column forms \(\ell=\sum_j\phi_jC_j\) with every \(\phi_j\ne0\), for which neither condition is known. Both tests compute the condition's own quantity exactly, with controls on each side.

Condition (ii), one row. For \(u=1\), (ii) says \(\operatorname{ann}(\rho)=\rho^{p-1}\bar A\) in degrees \(<D\): \((I:\rho)=I+(\rho^{p-1})\), where \(I\) is the ideal of \(\bar A\) in \(\mathbb F[c,y]\). row_freeness.py computes both Hilbert functions in Singular, over \(\mathbb F_3\). The tops \(g'\) are the full top ideal of the occupancy system, computed as the saturated homogenization at \(z=0\), which is the augmented member. Members: the base; onto; merge (\(C_1C_2\)); linear (\(s=m\), \(\ell=v\)); selector (forbid \(\ell=v\)); clause2 (forbid \(\ell_1=v_1,\ell_2=v_2\)). The excess \(\dim(I:\rho)/(I+\rho^{p-1})\) in degrees \(0,\dots,D-1\) is 0 for all six members at \(N=12\), \(D=3\), for two random seeds (the seed draws the coefficients \(\phi\in\{1,2\}^N\) of the forms and the forbidden values), and at \(N=16\), \(D=4\) (rf_N12.json, rf_N16.json). These sizes meet only the one-row seed bound \((p-1)\cdot2\cdot D=4D\), not the lemma's or the conjecture's range \((p-1)(D+1)D\), which is 24 and 40. Below the range the test detects failures: at \(N=3\), \(D=4\) every member has excess 1 in degree 2, and at \(N=4\) the excess is up to 4 (rf_control.json). This is ex:dense-row-freeness. It tests only content \(ke_1\). The clause's own top has degree 4, so its test at \(D=4\) sees only its augmentation below degree 4.

Condition (i). For the augmented member, whose generators are all of \(I(Z)\) up to degree \(D\), \(Z\) the allowed set in the slice \(L=\{c:\sum c\equiv m\}\), the degree-\(e\) part of \(J_S\) is exactly \(\{f|_{C_S=1}:f\in I(Z),\ \deg f\le e\}\) plus row multiples, since every element of \(I(Z)\) up to degree \(D\) is a generator. Modulo the row it is \(R_e\), as functions on \(L_S\), when the polynomials of degree \(\le e+1\) vanishing on \(L_S\) are the row multiples. The script asserts this saturation for every hole count, residue and degree it uses (\(n=10,11\), degrees up to 4). The fall in degree \(e\) is \(\dim(R_{e+1}\cap P_e)-\dim R_e\), with \(P_e\) the functions of degree \(\le e\). hereditary_falls.py computes it by exact elimination over \(\mathbb F_3\) at \(N=12\), \(D=5\), all \(1\le|S|\le2\), \(e<D-|S|\) and \(N-|S|\ge2e+3\): 246 checks per member. \(S=\emptyset\) is settled by the augmentation (hered_s1.json, hered_s2.json).

Merge is the control: its fall at \(S=\{1\}\), \(e=1\), is \(C_2\), the recorded placed-pigeon fall. validate_hereditary.py recomputes \(\dim\ker z\) on \(O_z^{S^c}/J_S\) from the saturated homogenization in Singular, independently of the function-space reduction, and agrees on six cases: merge \(S=\{1\}\) gives 0, 1, 9, 35; the selector at two falling holes gives 1 in degree 3, and at a non-falling hole 0; clause2 at \(S=\{5\}\) gives 2 in degree 3, and at \(S=\{1\}\) 0 (validate.json). What this means

  • For column members, (c) follows from two conditions. (ii) is a freeness statement about the board, proved for sparse members and supported for dense ones in content \(ke_1\). (i) is a statement about the occupancy ring alone.
  • (i) fails for dense members too, not only for merges. A single occupied hole can make an augmented selector's specialization fall. The theorem is only sufficient, and these tests do not show that the board falls. Board sizes in the stability range, \(N\ge(p-1)(D+1)D\) at \(D=5\), are out of reach. The fall element \(v\) of \(J_S\) gives the candidate board fall \(x_{ij}v\), \(j\in S\), as for merges.
  • Proposed repair, not proved. Add the placed-pigeon closure: \(x_Xg\) for column-injective cell sets \(X\) in rows \(\ge1\) and \(g\in I(Z_{S(X)})\), \(\deg\le D-|X|\), where \(S(X)\) is the hole set of \(X\). Item 3 then holds without (i): \(v\) vanishes on \(Z_S\), so \(yv\) is a closure generator. The closure adds tops of positive content, \(x_Xg^{\rm top}\), so items 1 and 2 must be redone for them. \(\bar A\) becomes \(\bigoplus_S\operatorname{gr}(O/I(Z_S))\otimes U^{\otimes S}\), and (ii) must be proved for that module. The closure adds generators, so lower bounds for the closed system imply them for the original.

It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the check count stated for \(1\le|S|\le2\);

Closure gluing: a column member closed under its placed-pigeon consequences has no falls when the graded functions on its assignments are row-free

24 September 2026 · Working proofs, conjecture and finite check · Hypothesis (c) for closed column members; cycle odd-prime-closure-gluing. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The fiber-gluing entry reduced hypothesis (c) for a column member to (i), no falls in its specializations at occupied holes, and (ii), row freeness of the board modulo its tops. It found that (i) fails for some dense selectors even after Gröbner augmentation, and proposed closing the member under its placed-pigeon consequences. The cycle asks whether the closure removes (i), and what then remains.

General statement. lem:closure-saturation: for a nonempty set \(Z\) of occupancy patterns, the polynomials of degree at most \(d\) vanishing on the assignments with occupancy in \(Z\) are exactly the sums of placed products \(x_Yg\), with \(g\) vanishing on the patterns of \(Z\) that occupy the holes of \(Y\), \(|Y|+\deg g\le d\). So the closed member, all such polynomials through degree \(D\), has no falls of its own. thm:closure-gluing: the weak base plus the closed member is \(z\)-injective below \(D\) when the row-sum syzygies of the associated graded algebra of functions on those assignments are Frobenius through degree \(D\). The condition cannot hold for every \(Z\): prop:single-hole-member refutes the closed system of the member allowing one occupied hole at degree 2. conj:closed-row-freeness states the condition for members that forbid value patterns of dense column forms on at most half the slice, when \(N\ge(p-1)(D+1)D\). ex:closed-row-freeness supports it in one-row contents at small sizes. Condition (i) disappears; hypothesis (c) for such members is implied by the single freeness condition.

Setting

Rows \(0,\dots,m-1\), \(m\ge1\), holes \(1,\dots,N\), a field \(\mathbb F\) of characteristic \(p\). \(\mathcal P\) is the set of column-injective assignments: partial maps from holes to rows. \(\tilde A_1=\mathbb F[x]/(x_{ij}^2-x_{ij},\ x_{ij}x_{i'j})\) is the algebra of functions on \(\mathcal P\), since the ideal contains \(x^2-x\) and its zero set is \(\mathcal P\). \(F_d\subseteq\tilde A_1\) is the span of the monomials \(x_T\), \(|T|\le d\), and \(\tilde A_z\), free over \(\mathbb F[z]\) with basis \(x_T\) (Step 1 of the weak-base stability proof), is the Rees algebra of this filtration. For an ideal \(\mathcal J\) generated by homogenizations \(w^{\rm h}\), \(w\in F_{\deg w}\), the degree-\(d\) part of \(\tilde A_z/\mathcal J\) is \(F_d/\mathcal J_{(d)}\), with \(\mathcal J_{(d)}=\operatorname{span}\{tw:t\in F_{d-\deg w}\}\). So \(z\) is injective in degree \(d\) exactly when \(\mathcal J_{(d+1)}\cap F_d=\mathcal J_{(d)}\).

For \(Z\subseteq\{0,1\}^N\), \(\mathcal P_Z\) is the set of assignments whose occupancy pattern lies in \(Z\). The base forces \(\sum_jC_j=m\), so take \(Z\) inside the slice \(\sum_jc_j\equiv m\pmod p\) and nonempty. For a hole set \(S\), \(Z_S=\{c\in Z:c_S=1\}\), as patterns on the other holes. The closed member of \(Z\) through degree \(D\) is \(\mathcal M_D(Z)=I(\mathcal P_Z)\cap F_D\), all polynomials of degree at most \(D\) vanishing on \(\mathcal P_Z\), as generators.

Closure saturation

Lemma (closure saturation). For every \(d\), \[I(\mathcal P_Z)\cap F_d=\bigoplus_Yx_Y\cdot\bigl(I(Z_{S(Y)})\cap F_{d-|Y|}[C_{S(Y)^c}]\bigr),\] the sum over column-injective cell sets \(Y\) in rows \(1,\dots,m-1\), with \(S(Y)\) the holes of \(Y\), \(C_j=\sum_ix_{ij}\), and \(F_e[C_{S^c}]\) the multilinear polynomials of degree \(\le e\) in the \(C_j\), \(j\notin S\). Consequently \(\mathcal M_D(Z)\) is generated by these placed products, \(z\) is injective on \(B'=\tilde A_z/(\mathcal M_D(Z)^{\rm h})\) in degrees \(<D\), and \(B'/zB'\) agrees with \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal P_Z}=\bigoplus_d F_d|_{\mathcal P_Z}/F_{d-1}|_{\mathcal P_Z}\) in degrees \(\le D\).

Proof.

  1. Bulk basis. The products \(C_Rx_Y\), \(R\cap S(Y)=\emptyset\), \(|R|+|Y|\le d\), form a basis of \(F_d\). Expanding \(C_j=x_{0j}+\sum_{i\ge1}x_{ij}\), \(C_Rx_Y\) is \(x_{(R\times0)\cup Y}\) plus monomials with fewer row-0 cells and the same size. This is triangular against the monomial basis.
  2. Vanishing. So every \(f\in F_d\) is uniquely \(\sum_Yx_Y\varphi_Y\) with \(\varphi_Y\in F_{d-|Y|}[C_{S(Y)^c}]\). If each \(\varphi_Y\) vanishes on \(Z_{S(Y)}\), \(f\) vanishes on \(\mathcal P_Z\): at an assignment \(a\), \(x_Y(a)=1\) forces the holes of \(Y\) occupied. Conversely, let \(f\) vanish on \(\mathcal P_Z\), and induct on \(|Y|\). For \(c\in Z_{S(Y)}\), take the assignment with cells \(Y\) in rows \(\ge1\) and row 0 on the other occupied holes of \(c\), which lies in \(\mathcal P_Z\) since row 0 exists. There \(0=f(a)=\sum_{Y'\subseteq Y}\varphi_{Y'}(c)\), and \(c\in Z_{S(Y')}\) for every \(Y'\subseteq Y\). By induction \(\varphi_{Y'}(c)=0\) for \(Y'\subsetneq Y\), so \(\varphi_Y(c)=0\).
  3. Saturation. Each placed product with \(|Y|+\deg g\le d\le D\) lies in \(\mathcal M_D(Z)\) and in \(F_d\). For \(d\le D\), every element of \(I(\mathcal P_Z)\cap F_d\) is itself a generator, and every generator vanishes on \(\mathcal P_Z\), so \(\mathcal M_D(Z)_{(d)}=I(\mathcal P_Z)\cap F_d\). Item 2 is used only for the generation by placed products and for the direct-sum form of \(G\). Then for \(d<D\), \(\mathcal M_D(Z)_{(d+1)}\cap F_d\subseteq I(\mathcal P_Z)\cap F_d=\mathcal M_D(Z)_{(d)}\), so \(z\) is injective in degree \(d\), and also in degree \(D\), since \(I(\mathcal P_Z)\cap F_D=\mathcal M_D(Z)_{(D)}\). In degree \(d\le D\), \(B'/zB'=F_d/(I(\mathcal P_Z)\cap F_d+F_{d-1})\), which is \(\operatorname{gr}_d\mathbb F^{\mathcal P_Z}\). \(\square\)

The placed products are the placed-pigeon closure of conj:effective-board; for a merge they are the fat-column generators of cor:merging-members. The case \(Y=\emptyset\) is the augmented member. Row-0 cells need no separate generators: \(x_{0j}g=C_jg-\sum_{i\ge1}x_{ij}g\), and \(C_jg\) vanishes on \(Z\) when \(g\) vanishes on \(Z_{\{j\}}\). The closure need not be derivable from the member at degree \(D\). For lower bounds it does not have to be: it only adds generators, so a degree-\(D\) lower bound for the closed system implies one for the original.

The theorem

Theorem (closure gluing). Over a field of characteristic \(p\), with \(m\ge1\) and \(Z\) nonempty inside the slice, suppose every Koszul 1-cycle of \((r_1,\dots,r_{m-1})\) on \(G=\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal P_Z}\) of degree at most \(D\) is a sum of Frobenius cycles \(r_i^{p-1}c\,e_i\) and boundaries. Then the homogenized weak base plus \(\mathcal M_D(Z)\) is \(z\)-injective below \(D\), and has no PC refutation of degree \(D\).

Proof. Since \(s-m\in\mathcal M_D(Z)\), \(s=\sum_jC_j\), and \(r_0-z=(s-mz)-\sum_{i\ge1}(r_i-z)\), the system is \(B=B'/(r_1-z,\dots,r_{m-1}-z)\). \(z\) is injective on \(B'\) in degrees \(<D\) by the lemma. So for \(k+1\le D\) the sequence \(0\to K(r-z;B')(-1)\xrightarrow{z}K(r-z;B')\to K(r;B'/zB')\to0\) is exact in the degrees involved, and its long exact sequence gives \(\ker(z:B_k\to B_{k+1})=\delta\bigl(H_1(r;B'/zB')_{k+1}\bigr)\), with \(B'/zB'=G\) through degree \(D\). Boundaries have \(\delta=0\). For a Frobenius cycle, Step 1 of the weak-base stability proof computes \(\delta\) in \(\tilde A_z\), using only \(r_i^p=r_iz^{p-1}\) there, and gets 0. By hypothesis these span. The generators vanish on the nonempty \(\mathcal P_Z\), so none is a nonzero constant, and the socle criterion excludes a refutation of degree \(D\), as in step 5 of the relative gluing proof. \(\square\)

The hypothesis reduces to few rows. \(G=\bigoplus_Yx_Y\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{Z_{S(Y)}}\) by the lemma, graded by the content of rows \(1,\dots,m-1\), and its content-\(c\) part involves only the rows of \(\operatorname{supp}c\), \(|\operatorname{supp}c|\le D\). The summand \(x_Y\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{Z_{S(Y)}}\) sits in degrees shifted by \(|Y|\). In \(G\), products of overlapping \(x_Y\) vanish (column exclusions and \(x^2\mapsto0\)), and so does \(C_jx_Y\) for \(j\in S(Y)\), since \(C_jx_{ij}=x_{ij}\) has lower degree. So the content grading is multiplicative, and the hypothesis is a statement about \(\mathcal P_Z^{(u)}\), assignments to the bulk row and \(u\le D\) rows. For the onto system, with \(N\equiv m\pmod p\) so that \(Z=\{1^N\}\) lies in the slice, each \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{Z_S}\) is \(\mathbb F\) and \(G\) is the weak column tensor power on \(m-1\) rows. The onto system is the base plus the \(C_j-1\), not \(\mathcal M_D(\{1^N\})\), but they agree in degrees \(\le D\): a multilinear \(g\) vanishing at \(1^N\) expands as \(\sum_{R\ne\emptyset}a_R\prod_{j\in R}(C_j-1)\), so \(x_Yg\) lies in the ideal of the \(C_j-1\) at degree \(|Y|+\deg g\). So thm:onto-stability reduces to this theorem. Compared with thm:fiber-gluing, condition (i) is gone. Condition (ii) now concerns \(G\), whose \(S\)-summands are \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{Z_S}\), in place of the restrictions of the unclosed member's top algebra. The closure changes the summands only at specializations that fall.

The condition needs room

Proposition (single-hole member). Let \(m\ge2\), \(m\equiv1\pmod p\), and let \(Z=\{e_1,\dots,e_N\}\), the patterns with one occupied hole. Then the weak base plus \(\mathcal M_2(Z)\) has a PC refutation of degree 2, so the hypothesis of thm:closure-gluing fails for every \(D\ge2\) and every \(N\).

Proof. \(Z\) lies in the slice. \(x_{0j}x_{1j'}\), \(j\ne j'\), vanishes on \(\mathcal P_Z\), which occupies one hole, so it lies in \(\mathcal M_2(Z)\). With the column exclusions for \(j=j'\), \(r_0r_1=\sum_{j,j'}x_{0j}x_{1j'}\) lies in the ideal at degree 2, and \(1=r_0r_1-(r_0-1)r_1-(r_1-1)\). By the theorem the hypothesis must then fail. \(\square\)

The same holds whenever every pattern of \(Z\) has weight below some \(w\le\min(m,D)\): \(r_0r_1\cdots r_{w-1}\) vanishes on \(\mathcal P_Z\), since its monomials put \(w\) pigeons in \(w\) distinct holes, and has degree \(w\), so it lies in \(\mathcal M_D(Z)\) and yields a refutation of degree \(w\). So a sufficient condition must use the size of the patterns in \(Z\). The members the goal produces forbid value patterns of column forms and leave most of the slice, which contains patterns of weight about \(N/2>D\).

The conjecture and its check

Conjecture (closed row freeness). Over a field of characteristic \(p\), let \(Z\) contain at least half of the slice \(\{c\in\{0,1\}^N:\sum_jc_j\equiv m\pmod p\}\), for any \(m\ge1\). If \(N\ge(p-1)(D+1)D\), the hypothesis of thm:closure-gluing holds.

The budget's members are slices minus unions of forbidden-value sets \(\{c:\ell_b(c)=v_b,\ b\le k\}\) of column forms over \(\mathbb F_p\), with values in \(\mathbb F_p\). On the slice such sets are arbitrary: adding a multiple of \(s\) to a form changes its coefficients but not the set it cuts, and \(N\) forms cut out a single pattern. So the conjecture is stated by density alone. For \(m\le N\) the base plus the member may be satisfiable, and the refutation part of the theorem says nothing there; the goal has \(m=N+1\). The conjecture about \(G\) is meaningful for every \(m\).

Onto is outside the conjecture's class, and its check is a control, not evidence. closed_row_freeness.py tests the one-row case: \(G\) for \(u=1\) is the top algebra of the point ideal \((c_j^2-c_j,\ y_j^2-y_j,\ c_jy_j-y_j,\ s-m,\ h)\) of \(\mathcal P_Z^{(1)}\), with \(c_j\) the occupancy and \(y_j\) the board row. Singular computes it as the saturated homogenization at \(z=0\), and compares \((I:\rho)\) with \(I+(\rho^{p-1})\) in degrees \(\le D-1\), with \(I\) this top ideal and \(\rho=\sum_jy_j\), over \(\mathbb F_3\). The sizes \(N=12\), \(D=3\) and \(N=16\), \(D=4\) meet the one-row seed bound \(4D\) but lie below the conjecture's \(N\ge(p-1)(D+1)D\), which is 24 and 40, so a failure there would not refute it. Members as in ex:dense-row-freeness: the base, onto, merge, linear, selector and a two-form clause, on forms with nonzero coefficients on every hole.

Results (crf_N12.json, crf_N16_onto.json, crf_N16_linear.json, crf_control.json). The excess \(\dim(I:\rho)/(I+\rho^{p-1})\) is 0 in degrees 0 to 2 for all six members at \(N=12\), \(D=3\), for two seeds, and 0 in degrees 0 to 3 for onto and linear at \(N=16\), \(D=4\). At \(N=16\) the base, merge and selector runs hit the 30-minute cap without a result: the saturated homogenization of the point ideal in 32 variables is the bottleneck, and the clause was not attempted. The control detects failures below the seed bound: at \(N=4\), \(D=4\) every member has positive excess, up to 7. This is ex:closed-row-freeness. At these sizes the closure changes no summand in the degrees tested: the specialization falls of ex:hereditary-falls appear at board degree 4, which needs \(D\ge5\). So the check does not yet test the closure itself. That needs a compiled kernel on the direct-sum description of \(G\), in place of a Gröbner basis of the point ideal.

What this means

  • For column members, hypothesis (c) after closure is implied by one sufficient condition, the row freeness of graded functions on \(\mathcal P_Z\). The occupancy-ring condition of fiber gluing is gone.
  • If conj:closed-row-freeness holds, every member allowing at least half the slice satisfies (c) after closure once \(N\ge(p-1)(D+1)D\), with no condition on its span. The single-hole member and its weight generalization show that some condition on \(Z\) is necessary.
  • The conjecture is a statement about one finite set of points and its degree filtration. Dehomogenized, \(r_i\) acts on \(\mathbb F^{\mathcal P_Z}\) as the row-\(i\) count modulo \(p\), and the fiber over a pattern \(c\) is the grid of row assignments to the occupied holes, a cube on them when \(u=1\). For large support it is free in low degree, by onto stability. The question is whether the degree filtration glues these fibers freely.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: Step 1 of the weak-base stability proof (the connecting map and the Frobenius lift), the socle criterion as used in the relative gluing proof, the fiber-gluing entry and the onto-stability proof. Claim searches (vanishing ideal of assignments, graded functions on a point set, low-weight members) found no result implying the lemma or the theorem. The nearest record is ex:component-hypothesis-injectivity-counterexample, where Frobenius generation fails for an equation member at \(n=8\), outside the conjecture's class and range. A fresh-context reviewer found the lemma, the theorem and the proposition correct. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • saturation argued directly, since every vanishing polynomial of degree \(\le D\) is a generator;
  • the onto system matched to the closed member in degrees \(\le D\), with \(N\equiv m\);
  • an unproved comparison with fiber gluing weakened;
  • sufficiency wording throughout;
  • the proposition generalized to all low-weight members;
  • the conjecture's class stated by density, since forbidden-value sets of forms over \(\mathbb F_p\) cut arbitrary sets on the slice, and its range of \(m\) stated;
  • the check's sizes placed below the conjecture's range, its ideal and degrees named, onto marked as a control;
  • the fibers described as grids and the content grading justified.

The changes weaken or justify statements; the only added claim, the weight generalization, is a two-line argument checked with the proposition. No further pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • conj:closed-row-freeness, in several-row contents and at the sizes where specializations fall.
  • Hypothesis (b) for closed members, whose tops carry pigeon cells; non-column members.

Route review: the closed column member belongs in the base; three obligations remain, and the generic members' splitting over the closed base is the least tested

24 September 2026 · Route review and conjecture · The relative gluing line after closure gluing; cycle odd-prime-closed-freeness. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

General statement. The line's claim is thm:relative-gluing applied to the budget's members. After thm:closure-gluing, the column component enters closed, and its closed tops carry pigeon cells. So the column component can no longer be a member in the sense of hypothesis (b), whose tops must be polynomials in the member's own forms. The review moves it into the base. The new claim is conj:closed-base-splitting: the generic members' forms split over the top algebra of the weak base plus the closed column member, as conj:column-component-splitting asserted over the weak base alone.

The line after closure

Put \(B^\sharp\) for the homogenized weak base plus the closed column member \(\mathcal M_D(Z)\), \(Z\) the column constraints' allowed set. Apply thm:relative-gluing with \(B^\sharp\) as base and the generic (non-column) members as members. It needs:

  1. \(z\) injective on \(B^\sharp\) below \(D\): by thm:closure-gluing this follows from conj:closed-row-freeness for \(Z\);
  2. top syzygies through \(D\) split into cross-member Koszul syzygies and member-supported ones. By lem:tensor-splitting-locality this holds when the top algebra of \(B^\sharp\) is, through \(D\), free over the generic members' form algebras, or of the tensor form that lemma allows. This is conj:closed-base-splitting;
  3. each generic member alone over \(B^\sharp\) has no fall below \(D\);
  4. no constant generator, which holds since \(\mathcal P_Z\) is nonempty.

Hypothesis (a) of the weak base alone is proved (thm:weak-base-stability-quadratic, cor:base-by-fibers); it is now the case \(Z=\) the whole slice.

What the goal needs

For every fixed odd \(p\) and \(K\), all three items for the product clauses of any \(n^K\) adversarial families, at \(D=O(\log n)\), with column constraints in \(Z\) and all others as generic members. Items (a) to (c) are each open in general.

Falsification attempt

The attempt checks conj:closed-row-freeness, the input to (a), against the obstructions and parameters now recorded.

  • Low weight. prop:single-hole-member and its weight generalization refute the closed system when every pattern of \(Z\) has weight below \(\min(m,D)\). The budget's \(Z\) is the slice minus the patterns on which some clause's forms all take the forbidden values. By lem:quiet-members' union bound, those patterns have density at most \(n^K(1-1/p)^k\le1/n\) in the forms' value space. When the forms' values are close to uniform on the slice, which is the robustness the budget assumes, \(Z\) covers all but about \(1/n\) of the slice. So it contains patterns of every weight near \(N/2\), and the conjecture's density hypothesis holds. The obstruction does not apply.
  • Range. \(N\ge(p-1)(D+1)D\) holds at \(D=O(\log n)\) for large \(n\).
  • Visibility. lem:quiet-members bounds the degree of polynomials vanishing on the allowed set in the forms' coordinates, not in the \(C_j\). Heuristically, a nonzero polynomial in the \(C_j\) of low degree cannot vanish off a set of density about \(1/n\), so \(\mathcal M_D(Z)\) agrees with the slice's own ideal up to degree of order \(\log n\). The closure would then matter only between that degree and \(D\), where the finite checks cannot reach. In ex:closed-row-freeness and ex:hereditary-falls the specialization falls start at board degree 4, which needs \(D\ge5\), and \(N\ge20\) for one row or \(N\ge60\) for the range.
  • Splitting. The closure's placed products \(x_Yg\) are not polynomials in column forms. So conj:column-component-splitting, stated for column-type constraints over the weak base, does not transfer. Its evidence, at \(n=8,9\) through degree 3, concerns unclosed components.

No obstruction refutes the conjectures. The attempt finds that (b) had to change form, and that its new form is untested.

Assessment of the line

Since the effective-board review, five cycles proved general statements:

  • fat-board stability;
  • onto stability;
  • fiber gluing, with a second proof of the base condition;
  • closure saturation;
  • closure gluing.

Hypothesis (c) for the column component went from a conjecture about effective boards to one freeness conjecture, stated for allowed sets covering half the slice, with a proved sparse analog. A necessary condition on the pattern weights is known. The evidence is exact but small, below the conjecture's range, and at degrees where the closure changes nothing. So the column side is reduced but not decided. The generic side has not moved since the splitting checks at \(n\le9\). Moving the column component into the base changes what (b) and (c) mean there, and neither has been tested in the new form. On this evidence the line is coherent and each step is general, but its decisive statements are conjectures whose tests exceed the current tools.

The highest-risk item and the next step

The highest-risk item is (b) in its new form, since the architecture fails if it fails and nothing tests it. conj:closed-base-splitting: over \(\mathbb F_p\), for a column allowed set \(Z\) covering at least half the slice and generic forms \(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_k\) of the kind conj:column-component-splitting allows, the top algebra of \(B^\sharp\) is, through degree \(t\), free over \(\mathbb F[\ell_1,\dots,\ell_k]/(\ell^p)\) plus a part above degree \(t\).

Next step, on route item odd-prime-clause-transfer: test conj:closed-base-splitting at the sizes of the recorded splitting checks, \(n=8,9\) through degree 3. Compare the Hilbert series of the closed base's top algebra modulo random generic forms with the free prediction \(\mathrm{HS}/(1+q+q^2)^k\), for a closed selector and a closed clause, with the unclosed and base-only controls. Then return to conj:closed-row-freeness with a compiled kernel on the direct sum of \(G\).

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the statements of thm:relative-gluing (hypotheses (a) to (d)), lem:tensor-splitting-locality, conj:column-component-splitting and its checks, lem:quiet-members, and the last five entries. The review adds a conjecture and no proof, so no reviewer pass was run.

Closed-base splitting: generic forms split exactly over the weak base plus a closed column member at n = 8, 9 through degree 3

24 September 2026 · Finite check · conj:closed-base-splitting at the recorded splitting sizes; cycle odd-prime-closed-splitting. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The closed-base review moved the closed column member into the base and named hypothesis (b) in its new form, conj:closed-base-splitting, as the least tested obligation. The cycle tests it where the recorded splitting checks ran.

General statement. conj:closed-base-splitting: the top algebra of the weak base plus a closed column member is free over generic forms through the degrees considered. ex:closed-base-splitting finds it exact in all 14 tested cases, including 7 where the closure changes the algebra.

The test

Tested statement. For the weak unary top algebra \(A\) over \(\mathbb F_3\) on \(n\) holes and \(n+1\) rows, and a column allowed set \(Z\), let \(A^\sharp=A/N\), with \(N\) the top ideal of the closed member. By lem:closure-saturation, \(N\) is spanned in degree \(t\) by \(x_Y\tau(C)\), \(Y\) in rows \(1,\dots,n\), \(\tau\) in the degree-\((t-|Y|)\) tops of polynomials vanishing on \(Z_{S(Y)}\). The prediction is \(\mathrm{HS}(A^\sharp/(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_k)A^\sharp)=\mathrm{HS}(A^\sharp)/(1+q+q^2)^k\) through degree 3, for \(k\le4\) uniform random forms \(\ell\in\mathbb F_3^{(n+1)\times n}\), which are row-dependent and generic. By graded Nakayama this is freeness over \(\mathbb F_3[\ell]/(\ell^3)\) through degree 3.

Can it decide. The recorded splitting checks ran at these sizes: ex:column-member-splitting and ex:column-splitting-boundary, at \(n=8,9\) through degree 3. There random forms split off from the weak base and from unclosed column components. A failure would show that closing the member breaks the splitting. The test also records the closure's effect \(\dim A^\sharp_{\rm unclosed}-\dim A^\sharp\) by degree, so cases where the closure changes nothing are identified. Control: the unclosed member, the ideal of \(A\) generated by the augmented member's tops.

closed_split.py uses the a4lib normal forms and the compiled prefix-rank kernel of the recorded checks. Members: selector (forbid \(\ell=v\)), clause2 (forbid \(\ell_1=v_1,\ell_2=v_2\)) and merge (\(C_1C_2\)), on column forms with coefficients in \(\{1,2\}\), two seeds; the base is the whole slice. Independent check: for the merge, the closed member must give the fat board of cor:merging-members. validate_fat.py computes the fat board's top algebra in Singular: 1, 63, 1575, 19284 at \(n=8\) and 1, 80, 2645, 45940 at \(n=9\). These equal closed_split.py's \(\mathrm{HS}(A^\sharp)\) (validate_fat.json).

Global closure: closing all constraints at once gives an alternative sufficient condition for non-refutability; the generic members' own condition is not decidable at the sizes point-ideal Gröbner bases reach

24 September 2026 · Working proof (global closure gluing); cycle odd-prime-generic-over-closed. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. After the closed-base review and the closed-splitting check, the untested obligation is (c): each generic member alone has no fall over the weak base plus the closed column member. The cycle tests it exactly on small boards. The test is not decidable at the sizes the point-ideal Gröbner computation reaches. The cycle then observes that the closure argument does not need members at all.

General statement. thm:global-closure-gluing: over a field of characteristic \(p\), for any nonempty set \(\mathcal Q\) of column-injective assignments whose total occupancy is \(\equiv m\pmod p\), and \(D\ge1\), the weak base plus all polynomials of degree at most \(D\) vanishing on \(\mathcal Q\) has no fall below \(D\) and no PC refutation of degree \(D\), provided the row-sum syzygies on the graded functions \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal Q}\) are Frobenius through degree \(D\). With \(\mathcal Q\) the assignments in the slice satisfying every budget constraint (row equations excluded), this is an alternative sufficient condition, besides (a) to (c) of relative gluing, for the lower bound the Taylor glue uses. The small-board attempt at (c) is recorded below and decides nothing.

The test of (c) and why it cannot decide

generic_fall.py computes \(\dim\ker z\) exactly in Singular over \(\mathbb F_3\), from Hilbert functions truncated at \(D\). It compares four systems:

  • the weak base;
  • the base plus a generic selector \(1-(\ell-v)^2\), \(\ell\) a uniform random form with row-dependent coefficients;
  • the base plus a closed column member, the degree-\(\le D\) part of the saturated homogenization of its point ideal;
  • the base plus both.

On the \(3\times7\) board, \(D=4\) (gf_3x7.json), \(\dim\ker z\) in degrees 0 to 3:

column memberseedbasebase + genericclosedclosed + generic
selector10, 0, 0, 00, 0, 0, 00, 0, 1, 270, 0, 1, 27
selector20, 0, 0, 00, 0, 0, 10, 0, 1, 270, 0, 1, 28
merge10, 0, 0, 00, 0, 0, 00, 0, 0, 210, 0, 0, 27

The closed merge's falls, 0, 0, 0, 21, equal the recorded fat-board value on this board (ex:placed-pigeon-falls, base plus closure), a consistency check of the closure computation. The closed base falls at this size, and so does the base plus a generic member in one seed. Both are below their ranges: thm:weak-base-stability-quadratic needs \(N\ge(p-1)D^2=32\), and conj:closed-row-freeness needs \((p-1)(D+1)D=40\). So (c), which presupposes (a) for the closed base, cannot be isolated here. At \(3\times12\), \(D=3\), the Gröbner basis of the closed point ideal did not finish within the run's 120 s limit. The base and the base plus a generic selector have no fall there, but that board is also below both ranges (18 and 24), so this is not evidence either. Reaching the range needs the direct-sum construction of the closure, as in closure saturation, not a point-ideal Gröbner basis. It decides nothing about (c), and no finite-check claim is registered for it.

Global closure

Setting as in the closure-gluing entry: \(\mathcal P\) the column-injective assignments, \(F_d\) the functions of degree \(\le d\), \(\tilde A_z\) the Rees algebra. For a nonempty \(\mathcal Q\subseteq\mathcal P\) whose assignments all place a number of pigeons \(\equiv m\pmod p\), put \(\mathcal M_D(\mathcal Q)=I(\mathcal Q)\cap F_D\), as generators.

Theorem (global closure gluing). Over a field of characteristic \(p\), with \(m\ge1\) and \(D\ge1\), put \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal Q}=\bigoplus_dF_d|_{\mathcal Q}/F_{d-1}|_{\mathcal Q}\), and suppose every Koszul 1-cycle of \((r_1,\dots,r_{m-1})\) on \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal Q}\) of degree at most \(D\) is a sum of Frobenius cycles \(r_i^{p-1}c\,e_i\) (\(i\ge1\), \(c\in\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal Q}\)) and boundaries. Then the homogenized weak base plus \(\mathcal M_D(\mathcal Q)\) is \(z\)-injective below \(D\) and has no PC refutation of degree \(D\). Consequently, the weak base plus any constraints of degree at most \(D\) vanishing on \(\mathcal Q\) has no PC refutation of degree \(D\). In particular this applies to constraints of degree at most \(D\) when \(\mathcal Q\), the assignments in \(\mathcal P\) with total occupancy \(\equiv m\) on which the constraints vanish, is nonempty and satisfies the hypothesis. The row equations are not among the constraints: if they were, every \(r_i\) would be constant on \(\mathcal Q\), \(e_i\) would be a cycle that is neither Frobenius nor a boundary, and the hypothesis would fail for every \(m\ge2\).

Proof. The closure-gluing proof applies verbatim. Saturation: for \(d\le D\), every element of \(I(\mathcal Q)\cap F_d\) is a generator, so the degree-\(d\) part of the ideal is \(I(\mathcal Q)\cap F_d\) and \(z\) is injective in degrees \(<D\). The top algebra agrees with \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal Q}\) through degree \(D\). Since \(s-m\) vanishes on \(\mathcal Q\) and \(D\ge1\), it is a generator, and \(r_0-z\) lies in the ideal generated by \(\mathcal M_D(\mathcal Q)\) and the \(r_i-z\), \(i\ge1\). The Koszul sequence and Step 1's Frobenius lift give \(z\)-injectivity. The socle criterion excludes a refutation, since no generator is a nonzero constant for nonempty \(\mathcal Q\). For the consequence: each constraint \(g\) reduces, by the Boolean and column-exclusion axioms within degree \(\deg g\), to its multilinear form \(\bar g\in I(\mathcal Q)\cap F_D\). So a PC refutation of the smaller system of degree \(\le D\) is one of the larger system. Only non-refutability passes to the smaller system; \(z\)-injectivity does not, as the placed-pigeon falls show. \(\square\)

The column-member case is thm:closure-gluing, with \(\mathcal Q=\mathcal P_Z\). The direct-sum description of \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal Q}\) used there is special to column members. For general \(\mathcal Q\) the graded module has no such decomposition, and no content reduction is available in general.

The hypothesis is not automatic for large \(\mathcal Q\). Let \(m\ge2\), \(p\ge3\), \(N\ge p+1\), and let \(\mathcal Q\) be the assignments with at most one pigeon in row 1 and total occupancy \(\equiv m\). Then \(r_1^2-r_1\) vanishes on \(\mathcal Q\), so \(r_1^2=0\) in \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal Q}\), and \(r_1e_1\) is a cycle of degree 2. For \(p\ge3\) no Frobenius cycle has degree 2. The only affine relation on \(\mathcal Q\) is \(s=m\): pick \(1\le k\le N-1\) with \(k\equiv m\) and put \(k\) pigeons in row 0. Moving one of them to another row at the same hole (allowed for row 1, which is empty) shows that a relation \(\sum a_{ij}x_{ij}=b\) has \(a_{0j}=a_{ij}\), and moving it to an empty hole shows \(a_{0j}=a_{0j'}\). So every affine relation is a multiple of \(s-m\), and the \(r_i\), \(i\ge1\), are independent in \(\operatorname{gr}_1\). Degree-2 boundaries have coefficients in \(\operatorname{gr}_0=\mathbb F\), so the \(e_1\)-coefficient of a boundary is \(\sum_{j\ge2}a_jr_j\ne r_1\). The hypothesis fails. The weak base already derives \(r_1^2-r_1\) at degree 2. The obstruction comes from the extra generators, such as \(x_{1j}x_{1j'}\), not from \(r_1^2-r_1\). The failure of this sufficient hypothesis does not show a fall or a refutation. It shows that a conjecture for the budget's \(\mathcal Q\) must exclude such sets.

What this means

  • For the lower bound the Taylor glue needs, no PC refutation of degree \(B\) for the weak base plus the budget's constraints of degree at most \(B\), the theorem gives an alternative sufficient condition: row freeness through degree \(B\) of \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal Q}\), with \(\mathcal Q\) the assignments in the slice satisfying all budget constraints (row equations excluded), nonempty. The entry shows no implication in either direction between this condition and (a) to (c). It does not give the unclosed system's \(z\)-injectivity, which the placed-pigeon falls show can fail.
  • The pinned-row example shows that some condition excluding pinned rows is needed in any conjecture of this form.
  • (c) for generic members over the closed base is not decidable at the sizes the point-ideal Gröbner computation reaches; the direct-sum construction of the closure is needed to reach the range.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the closure-gluing entry (setting, lemma, theorem, proof), Step 1 of the weak-base stability proof, the socle criterion, and the Taylor glue's conclusion. Claim search (vanishing ideal of a solution set, graded functions, row freeness) found lem:closure-saturation and the cycle's neighbours, none implying the theorem. The small-board numbers are read from gf_3x7.json and the run logs. A fresh-context reviewer found the transfer of the closure-gluing proof sound. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the consequence restricted to non-refutability, with the reduction of constraints to multilinear forms;
  • \(\mathcal Q\) defined in the slice, nonempty, without row equations, and \(D\ge1\);
  • \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal Q}\) and the Frobenius cycles defined;
  • the content-reduction remark weakened;
  • the pinned-row example proved, with its hypotheses, and its conclusions limited;
  • "replaces" changed to "an alternative sufficient condition", and the relative-gluing and robustness claims removed;
  • "untestable" made precise;
  • the ranges named and the \(3\times12\) case placed below them.

The changes weaken or justify statements; the pinned-row argument adds no claim beyond the draft's. No further pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • A statement of global row freeness for the budget's \(\mathcal Q\), with its robustness hypothesis, and evidence at sizes in range.
  • conj:closed-row-freeness at \(D\ge5\); (c) for generic members over the closed base, tested with the direct-sum closure.

Sparse closure stability: any closed column member on few holes has no falls with the weak base, and the slice is saturated in range

24 September 2026 · Working proofs · Closed row freeness for members on few holes; cycle odd-prime-direct-sum-kernel. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. By thm:closure-gluing, a closed column member has no falls with the weak base when the graded functions \(G=\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal P_Z}\) on its allowed assignments are row-free. conj:closed-row-freeness asserts this for allowed sets covering half the slice. The closure-gluing condition had no proved case beyond onto, and the conjecture's checks run below range (closure gluing). The route's finite-check budget is spent, so the cycle proves the condition for members on few holes. This is the closed analog of lem:sparse-row-freeness.

General statement. thm:sparse-closure-stability: over a field of characteristic \(p\), let \(Z\) be the patterns in the slice whose restriction to a hole set \(H\) lies in a set \(Z_H\), with \(Z\) nonempty. If \(N-|H|\ge(p-1)(D+1)(D+p-1)\), the weak base plus the closed member \(\mathcal M_D(\mathcal P_Z)\) is \(z\)-injective below \(D\) and has no PC refutation of degree \(D\). The key step is lem:slice-strictness: if \(\ker(s|\Gamma_e)=s^{p-1}\Gamma_{e-p+1}\) for \(e\le D+p-2\) in a filtered algebra's graded algebra \(\Gamma\), the level set \(t=s-m=0\) (\(t^p=t\)) is cut out without degree loss through degree \(D\). cor:slice-saturation: the occupancy slice is saturated through degree \(D\) when \(N\ge(p-1)(D+p-1)\), on the cube and on the weak board with any number of rows.

Slice strictness

Lemma (slice strictness). Let \(F\) be a filtered commutative algebra of functions on a finite set, \(F_0=\mathbb F\subseteq F_1\subseteq\cdots\), \(\Gamma=\operatorname{gr}F\). Let \(t\in F_1\) satisfy \(t^p=t\), with top \(s\in\Gamma_1\). Suppose that for \(e\le D+p-2\), \(\ker(s:\Gamma_e\to\Gamma_{e+1})=s^{p-1}\Gamma_{e-p+1}\). Then \(F_d\cap tF=tF_{d-1}\) for \(d\le D\), and the functions on the level set \(\{t=0\}\) satisfy \(\operatorname{gr}_d\mathbb F^{\{t=0\}}=\Gamma_d/s\Gamma_{d-1}\) for \(d\le D\).

Proof. Let \(h\in F_d\cap tF\). Then \(h\) vanishes on \(\{t=0\}\), and \(t^{p-1}=1\) off it, since \(t\) takes values in \(\mathbb F_p\) there. So \(h=t\cdot f\) with \(f=ht^{p-2}\), of degree \(\le d+p-2\). While \(e=\deg f\ge d\): the product \(tf=h\) has degree \(\le d\le e\), so \(s\bar f=0\) in \(\Gamma_{e+1}\), with \(\bar f\) the top of \(f\). Since \(e\le D+p-2\), \(\bar f=s^{p-1}\bar g\) for some \(g\in F_{e-p+1}\) with top \(\bar g\). Put \(f'=f-t^{p-1}g+g\). Then \(tf'=tf-t^pg+tg=tf\). The top of \(t^{p-1}g\) is \(s^{p-1}\bar g=\bar f\), so \(\deg(f-t^{p-1}g)<e\), and \(\deg g<e\). So \(\deg f'<e\). Repeating ends with \(\deg f\le d-1\), so \(h\in tF_{d-1}\). For the level set, \(\mathbb F^{\{t=0\}}=F/tF\) with the image filtration, and \(\operatorname{gr}_d=F_d/(F_d\cap tF+F_{d-1})=F_d/(tF_{d-1}+F_{d-1})=\Gamma_d/s\Gamma_{d-1}\). \(\square\)

The theorem

Theorem (sparse closure stability). Over a field of characteristic \(p\), with \(m\ge1\), a hole set \(H\), and \(Z=\{c\text{ in the slice}:c_H\in Z_H\}\) nonempty, suppose \(N-|H|\ge(p-1)(D+1)(D+p-1)\). Then the homogenized weak base plus \(\mathcal M_D(\mathcal P_Z)\) is \(z\)-injective below \(D\) and has no PC refutation of degree \(D\).

Proof. By thm:closure-gluing it suffices that every Koszul 1-cycle of \((r_1,\dots,r_{m-1})\) on \(G\) of degree at most \(D\) is Frobenius plus a boundary.

  1. Content reduction. By lem:closure-saturation, \(G=\bigoplus_Yx_Y\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{Z_{S(Y)}}\), graded by the content of rows \(1,\dots,m-1\). Its content-\(c\) part, and the content-\(c\) parts of \(K_1,K_2\), coincide with those for the same construction on the rows of \(\operatorname{supp}c\), \(u=|\operatorname{supp}c|\le D\). The summands \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{Z_S}\) do not depend on the rows. By the same lemma, that construction is \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal P^{(u)}_Z}\), where \(\mathcal P^{(u)}_Z\) is the set of assignments of holes to the rows of \(\operatorname{supp}c\) and a bulk row, with occupancy in \(Z\). The lemma's proof (bulk basis, vanishing, saturation) never uses the slice, only that the set is nonempty and that row 0 exists, so it applies to this set. The \(r_i\)-action on the summands depends only on the \(Z_S\), so the identification is one of \(T_u\)-modules. Work with this set.
  2. Dropping the slice. Let \(\mathcal P'\) be the same assignments with \(c_H\in Z_H\) but no slice condition, and \(F=\mathbb F^{\mathcal P'}\) with the degree filtration in the variables \(C_j\), \(x_{ij}\) (\(i\in\operatorname{supp}c\)). \(\mathcal P'=\mathcal P'_H\times\mathcal P_{H^c}\), where \(\mathcal P_{H^c}\) is all assignments of the holes of \(H^c\), and the variables split. So \(\Gamma=\operatorname{gr}F=\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal P'_H}\otimes\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal P_{H^c}}\). The second factor is \(\bigotimes_{j\in H^c}V_j\), \(V_j=\operatorname{span}(1,C_j,x_{ij})\) square-zero, since \(C_j^2=C_j\) and \(C_jx_{ij}=x_{ij}\) as functions. This is the weak column tensor power on \(u+1\) rows, with \(C_j\) in the place of row 0.
  3. Free seeds. \(T_{u+1}=\mathbb F[R_0,\dots,R_u]/(R^p)\) acts on \(\Gamma\) by \(R_0\mapsto s=\sum_jC_j\) and \(R_i\mapsto r_i\), diagonally over the two factors. The \(p\)-th powers vanish in \(\Gamma\): \(s^p=s\) and \(r_i^p=r_i\) as functions, since they take values in \(\mathbb F_p\), so their degree-\(p\) tops are 0. On the first factor, \(R_0\) and \(R_i\) act through \(s_H=\sum_{j\in H}C_j\) and \(r_i^H\), which take values in \(\mathbb F_p\). Their \(p\)-th powers equal themselves as functions and vanish in gr, so \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal P'_H}\) is a graded \(T_{u+1}\)-module in degrees \(\ge0\). The isomorphism \(\Gamma\cong\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal P'_H}\otimes\bigotimes_{j\in H^c}V_j\) is \(T_{u+1}\)-linear with the diagonal action, since \(s=s_H+\sum_{j\in H^c}C_j\) and likewise for \(r_i\). Step 3 of the weak-base stability proof on \(u+1\) rows gives seed blocks of \((p-1)(u+1)\) holes of \(H^c\), at least \(D+p-1\) of them. The free-seed lemma, with \(M=\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal P'_H}\otimes(\text{leftover holes})\), gives \(\Gamma\cong\Phi\oplus Q\), with \(\Phi\) free over \(T_{u+1}\) and \(Q\) in degrees \(\ge D+p-1\).
  4. Restoring the slice. Let \(x\in\Gamma_e\), \(e\le D+p-2\), with \(sx=0\). Then \(Q_e=0\), so \(x\in\Phi_e\). \(\Phi\) is free over \(T_{u+1}\), hence over \(\mathbb F[R_0]/(R_0^p)\), so \(x\in s^{p-1}\Phi_{e-p+1}\). So lem:slice-strictness applies with \(t=s-m\): \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal P^{(u)}_Z}=\Gamma/s\Gamma\cong\Phi/R_0\Phi\oplus Q/R_0Q\) through degree \(D\). Here \(\Phi/R_0\Phi\) is free over \(T_u\), and \(Q/R_0Q\) lives in degrees \(\ge D+p-1\).
  5. Frobenius. \(H_1\) in degrees \(\le D\) uses \(\Gamma/s\Gamma\) only in degrees \(\le D\), and its identification with \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal P^{(u)}_Z}\) is compatible with the \(r_i\), since restriction is an algebra map. As in Step 3's consequence, \(H_1(r;\cdot)\) in degrees \(\le D\) is spanned by Frobenius classes. Their content components are Frobenius cycles plus boundaries, which gives the hypothesis content by content. \(\square\)

Corollary (slice saturation). Over a field of characteristic \(p\), let \(F\) be the functions on the cube \(\{0,1\}^N\), or on the weak board's column-injective assignments with any number of rows, with the degree filtration, and \(s=\sum_jC_j\). If \(N\ge(p-1)(D+p-1)\), then \(I(\{s\equiv m\})\cap F_d=(s-m)F_{d-1}\) for \(d\le D\).

Proof. \(\Gamma=\bigotimes_jV_j\), with \(V_j=\operatorname{span}(1,C_j)\) on the cube and \(\operatorname{span}(1,C_j,x_{ij})\) on the board, square-zero. \(s\) acts diagonally as the primitive \(R\) of \(\mathbb F[R]/(R^p)\), by \(C_j\) on \(V_j\), and \(s^p=0\) in \(\Gamma\). On a block of \(p-1\) holes, \(s^{p-1}\cdot1=(p-1)!\,C_1\cdots C_{p-1}\ne0\), so \(\operatorname{Ann}(1)=0\) and the block is a free seed. With \(N\ge(p-1)(D+p-1)\) there are \(D+p-1\) blocks. The free-seed lemma, with the other factors as \(M\), gives \(\Gamma\cong\Phi\oplus Q\), \(\Phi\) free and \(Q\) in degrees \(\ge D+p-1\). So the kernel condition of lem:slice-strictness holds for \(e\le D+p-2\). \(\square\)

At \(p=3\) the bound is \(N\ge2(D+2)\). The fiber-gluing check (hered_s1.json, hered_s2.json) asserted this saturation on cubes for \((n,d)\) with \(d\le3\) at \(n=10\) and \(d\le4\) at \(n=11\). The corollary covers all of these except \(n=11\), \(d=4\), which needs \(N\ge12\).

Cases. A merge of a hole set \(H\) is a case, with \(Z_H\) the patterns occupying at most one hole of \(H\). The theorem gives the conclusion of cor:merging-members for its closed system in the range \(N-|H|\ge(p-1)(D+1)(D+p-1)\). The theorem allows any constraint on the occupancy of \(H\), including selectors and clauses whose forms vanish off \(H\).

What this means

  • The theorem proves the conclusion of conj:closed-row-freeness, the closure-gluing hypothesis, for every \(Z\) of the form slice \(\cap\{c_H\in Z_H\}\), with no density condition but in the larger range \(N-|H|\ge(p-1)(D+1)(D+p-1)\). It covers the conjecture's own instances only when \(N-|H|\) meets that range. The members the goal produces touch every hole, so the conjecture's dense case stays open.
  • The proof gives a sufficient condition for the dense case. Take an extension \(Z'\not\subseteq\) slice with \(Z'\cap\text{slice}=Z\), for example the members' forbidden-value sets on the whole cube, and \(\mathcal P'=\mathcal P_{Z'}\) on \(u\) rows and the bulk row. The condition is the kernel condition of lem:slice-strictness for \(\Gamma=\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal P'}\), together with freeness of \(\Gamma/s\Gamma\) over \(T_u\) through degree \(D\). Freeness of \(\Gamma\) over \(T_{u+1}\) below degree \(D+p-1\) gives both. For a sparse member the product structure supplied it; a dense member has no unconstrained holes to supply seeds.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: lem:closure-saturation and thm:closure-gluing with their proofs, lem:sparse-row-freeness, and the free-seed lemma and Step 3 of the weak-base stability proof. The claim search (sparse closed member, slice saturation) found no result implying the lemma or the theorem; cor:merging-members is the nearest special case. A fresh-context reviewer found the lemma (construction, descent, degree bookkeeping, gr of the level set) and the theorem's proof (product decomposition, square-zero factor, seed count, free-seed hypotheses, quotient by \(s\), Frobenius conclusion) correct. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the relation to conj:closed-row-freeness stated precisely (its conclusion, in a larger range);
  • "no proved case beyond onto" referred to the closure-gluing condition;
  • the saturation claim restated as cor:slice-saturation, proved with seeds of \(p-1\) holes on the cube and on the board with any number of rows, and compared exactly with the earlier check's sizes;
  • the merge case weakened to the conclusion of cor:merging-members;
  • closure saturation's use without the slice justified;
  • the module structures, the kernel condition and the compatibility with the \(r_i\) written out;
  • the dense-case condition stated as a sufficient condition with its extension \(Z'\);
  • the unused hypothesis \(D\ge1\) dropped.

cor:slice-saturation is new in this form; its proof is the reviewer's suggested argument and uses only the free-seed lemma and lem:slice-strictness, so no further pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • Freeness of \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal P'}\) over the row-sum algebra for dense \(Z\) (conj:closed-row-freeness).
  • (c) for generic members over the closed base; global row freeness for the budget's solution set.

Seeded closure stability: every closed column member whose forms have a seeded span has no falls with the weak base, whatever its allowed values

24 September 2026 · Working proofs · Closed row freeness for seeded dense members; cycle odd-prime-dense-closure. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The sparse-closure entry proved the closure-gluing hypothesis for members on few holes, with seeds from unconstrained holes. The budget's members touch every hole. The cycle asks whether seeds for the members' own forms, as in thm:board-seed-freeness, can replace the unconstrained holes, for any allowed set of form values.

General statement. lem:filtered-freeness-transfer: let \(R\) be the algebra of functions on a finite set of form values, filtered by degree, acting on a filtered algebra \(F\) of functions. If \(\operatorname{gr}F\) agrees below degree \(n_0\) with a free \(\operatorname{gr}R\)-submodule, then for every ideal \(J\subseteq R\), \(\operatorname{gr}(F/JF)=\operatorname{gr}F\otimes_{\operatorname{gr}R}\operatorname{gr}(R/J)\) in degrees \(<n_0\). thm:seeded-closure-stability: over a field of characteristic \(p\), if column forms \(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_d\) have an affine basis of values with multiplicity \((p-1)(D+1)^2\) at \(P_0\) and \((p-1)(D+1)\) at each other point, then for every set \(\Omega\) of allowed values, the weak base plus the closed member of \(Z=\{c\text{ in the slice}:\ell(c)\in\Omega\}\), if nonempty, has no fall below \(D\) and no PC refutation of degree \(D\). cor:seed-transfer-ranges: the same lemma improves cor:slice-saturation to \(N\ge(p-1)(D+1)\) and thm:sparse-closure-stability to \(N-|H|\ge(p-1)(D+1)^2\).

Filtered freeness transfer

Lemma (filtered freeness transfer). Let \(R=\mathbb F^{\mathbb F_p^e}\), filtered by polynomial degree, with \(T_R=\operatorname{gr}R=\mathbb F[w_1,\dots,w_e]/(w^p)\). Let \(F\) be a filtered algebra with \(F_{-1}=0\) and a filtered algebra map \(R\to F\), and put \(\Gamma=\operatorname{gr}F\), a graded \(T_R\)-module. Suppose \(\Phi\subseteq\Gamma\) is a graded \(T_R\)-submodule, free on a homogeneous basis \((\bar b_\alpha)\) of degrees \(a_\alpha\), and \(\Gamma_d=\Phi_d\) for \(d<n_0\). Then for every ideal \(J\subseteq R\) and \(d<n_0\):

  1. \(F_d\cap JF=\sum_\alpha(J\cap R_{d-a_\alpha})\,b_\alpha\), for lifts \(b_\alpha\in F_{a_\alpha}\) of \(\bar b_\alpha\);
  2. \(\operatorname{gr}_d(F/JF)\cong\bigoplus_\alpha\operatorname{gr}_{d-a_\alpha}(R/J)=(\Phi\otimes_{T_R}\operatorname{gr}(R/J))_d\).

Suppose moreover that \(\Phi\) is free over \(T_R\otimes T_{\rm row}\), \(T_{\rm row}=\mathbb F[y_1,\dots,y_u]/(y^p)\), on a basis \((\bar c_\beta)\), with \(T_{\rm row}\) acting through the tops of elements \(y_i\in F_1\) that satisfy \(y_i^p=y_i\) in \(F\). Then in degrees \(<n_0\), \(\operatorname{gr}(F/JF)\) agrees with \(T_{\rm row}\otimes\operatorname{gr}(R/J)\otimes\operatorname{span}(\bar c_\beta)\), with \(y_i\) acting on the first factor. Nothing is claimed about \(y_i\) from degree \(n_0-1\) into degree \(n_0\).

Proof. Define \(\psi:\bigoplus_\alpha R\,e_\alpha\to F\), \(e_\alpha\mapsto b_\alpha\), filtered with \(e_\alpha\) in degree \(a_\alpha\). For \(r\in R\) of exact degree \(k\), the top of \(rb_\alpha\) is \(\bar r\bar b_\alpha\ne0\), since \(\Phi\) is free. So \(\operatorname{gr}\psi\) is the inclusion \(\Phi\hookrightarrow\Gamma\), and \(\psi\) is injective and strict: \(\psi(x)\in F_d\) exactly when \(x\) has filtration degree \(\le d\). For \(d<n_0\), \(\Gamma_d=\Phi_d\), so by induction on \(d\) from \(F_{-1}=0\), \(F_d=\psi\bigl(\bigoplus_\alpha R_{d-a_\alpha}e_\alpha\bigr)\).

\(R\) is a product of copies of \(\mathbb F\), so every \(R\)-module is semisimple; here only the \(R\)-module structure of \(F\) is used. The submodule \(M=\psi(\bigoplus R\,e_\alpha)\) is a direct summand, \(F=M\oplus M'\), and \(JF=JM\oplus JM'\). For \(d<n_0\), \(F_d\subseteq M\), so \(F_d\cap JF=F_d\cap JM=F_d\cap\psi(\bigoplus J\,e_\alpha)\). By strictness this is \(\psi(\bigoplus(J\cap R_{d-a_\alpha})e_\alpha)\), which is (a). Then \(\operatorname{gr}_d(F/JF)=F_d/(F_d\cap JF+F_{d-1})\). By (a) and \(F_{d-1}=\psi(\bigoplus R_{d-1-a_\alpha}e_\alpha)\), this is \(\bigoplus_\alpha R_{d-a_\alpha}/(J\cap R_{d-a_\alpha}+R_{d-1-a_\alpha})\), which is (b).

For the last part, take the \(T_R\)-basis \(\bar y^a\bar c_\beta\) of \(\Phi\), with \(0\le a_i<p\), and lifts \(y^ac_\beta\); these are lifts because the top of a product is the product of the tops. In \(F/JF\), \(y_i\cdot(\rho\,y^ac_\beta)=\rho\,y^{a+e_i}c_\beta\) if \(a_i+1<p\). Otherwise it is \(\rho\,y_i^py^{a-(p-1)e_i}c_\beta\), and \(y_i^p=y_i\) has lower degree, so the product vanishes in gr. So \(y_i\) acts on \(\bigoplus\operatorname{gr}(R/J)\,[\bar y^a\bar c_\beta]\) as on \(T_{\rm row}\otimes\operatorname{gr}(R/J)\otimes\operatorname{span}(\bar c_\beta)\), in degrees \(<n_0\). \(\square\)

The slice case. For \(e=1\), \(R\) the functions of \(s\), and \(J\) the functions vanishing at \(m\): \(J\cap R_k=(s-m)R_{k-1}\) for every \(k\). Polynomials of degree \(\le\min(k,p-1)\) represent \(R_k\), and \((w-m)R_{p-2}\) already has dimension \(p-1=\dim J\). So (a) gives \(F_d\cap JF=(s-m)F_{d-1}\) for \(d<n_0\), the conclusion of lem:slice-strictness. The hypotheses differ: slice strictness assumes a kernel condition through degree \(D+p-2\), the transfer lemma a free submodule below \(D+1\), and neither implies the other.

The theorem

Theorem (seeded closure stability). Over a field \(\mathbb F\) of characteristic \(p\), with \(m\ge1\), let column forms \(\ell_b=\sum_j\varphi_b(j)C_j\), \(\varphi_b:[N]\to\mathbb F_p\), \(b=1,\dots,d\), have an affine basis \(P_0,\dots,P_d\) of \(\mathbb F_p^d\) among the value vectors \((\varphi_1(j),\dots,\varphi_d(j))\). Let \(P_0\) be taken by at least \((p-1)(D+1)^2\) holes and each \(P_b\) by at least \((p-1)(D+1)\). Let \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb F_p^d\), and let \(Z=\{c\text{ in the slice}:\ell(c)\in\Omega\}\) be nonempty. Then the homogenized weak base plus \(\mathcal M_D(\mathcal P_Z)\) is \(z\)-injective below \(D\) and has no PC refutation of degree \(D\).

Proof. By thm:closure-gluing it suffices that the row-sum Koszul cycles on \(G=\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal P_Z}\) of degree at most \(D\) are Frobenius plus boundaries.

  1. Content reduction. As in the sparse-closure proof, step 1, the content-\(c\) part of \(G\) is that of \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal P_Z^{(u)}}\) on the \(u=|\operatorname{supp}c|\le D\) rows of \(\operatorname{supp}c\) and a bulk row. The identification is one of \(T_u\)-modules.
  2. Joint seeds. Let \(F\) be the functions on all assignments to these \(u+1\) rows. Then \(\Gamma=\operatorname{gr}F\) is the column tensor power \(\tilde A_{u+1}\). The proof of thm:board-seed-freeness shows, for the full column tensor power on \(u'\) rows, with \(T=\mathbb F[Y_0,\dots,Y_{u'-1},W_1,\dots,W_d]/(Y_i^p,W_b^p)\) acting by \(Y_i\mapsto r_i\) and \(W_b\mapsto\ell_b\): a hole set with \(u'(p-1)\) holes of value \(P_0\) and \(p-1\) of each \(P_b\) is a seed, and \(t+1\) disjoint seeds give \(\tilde A_{u'}\cong(T\otimes M_0)\oplus Q\), with \(Q\) in degrees \(\ge t+1\). Here \(u'=u+1\le D+1\) and \(t=D\). The \(D+1\) blocks need \((u+1)(p-1)(D+1)\le(p-1)(D+1)^2\) holes at \(P_0\) and \((p-1)(D+1)\) at each \(P_b\). Replace \(Y_0\) by \(S=\sum_iY_i\), which acts as \(s=\sum_jC_j\). Since \((\sum_iY_i)^p=\sum_iY_i^p=0\), \(T=T_u\otimes T_R\) with \(T_u=\mathbb F[Y_1,\dots,Y_u]/(Y^p)\) and \(T_R=\mathbb F[S,W]/(p\text{-th powers})\). A \(T\)-module isomorphism does not depend on the choice of generators.
  3. Transfer. Let \(R\) be the functions on \(\mathbb F_p^{1+d}\), mapping to \(F\) by \((s,\ell_1,\dots,\ell_d)\). These take values in \(\mathbb F_p\), so \(R\to F\) is a filtered algebra map with \(\operatorname{gr}R=T_R\). Let \(J\) be the functions vanishing on \(\{m\}\times\Omega\). Then \(F/JF\) is the functions on \(\mathcal P_Z^{(u)}\). The lemma, with \(n_0=D+1\), \(\Phi=T\otimes M_0\), and \(T_{\rm row}=T_u\) acting through the \(r_i\), \(i\in\operatorname{supp}c\), gives that \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal P_Z^{(u)}}\) is free over \(T_u\) in degrees \(\le D\).
  4. Frobenius. \(H_1\) of the row sums in degrees \(\le D\) uses only degrees \(\le D\). On a free \(T_u\)-module it is spanned by Frobenius classes, whose content components are Frobenius cycles plus boundaries. \(\square\)

Scope. \(\Omega\) is arbitrary, so the theorem covers every member defined by conditions modulo \(p\) on forms in the seeded span: a single clause forbidding one value pattern, several clauses whose forms lie in one seeded span, and selectors or equations on such forms. A clause whose forms' value vectors span only a proper affine subspace must first be rewritten on a basis of that span. Members defined by integer occupancy counts, such as exactly one occupied hole of a set of at least \(p\) holes, are not of this form. The members need not be sparse: every hole may carry nonzero coefficients.

Improved ranges

Corollary (seed-transfer ranges). Over a field of characteristic \(p\):

  • the conclusion of cor:slice-saturation holds for \(N\ge(p-1)(D+1)\);
  • the conclusion of thm:sparse-closure-stability holds for \(N-|H|\ge(p-1)(D+1)^2\).

Proof. In both proofs replace lem:slice-strictness by the transfer lemma with \(R\) the functions of \(s\) and \(J\) the functions vanishing at \(m\), using \(J\cap R_k=(s-m)R_{k-1}\) (the slice case above). It needs the free submodule only below degree \(D+1\). For the slice, seed blocks of \(p-1\) holes, \(D+1\) of them, give \(\Gamma\) free over \(\mathbb F[S]/(S^p)\) up to degrees \(\ge D+1\). For sparse members, blocks of \((p-1)(u+1)\) holes of \(H^c\), \(D+1\) of them, give freeness over \(T_{u+1}\supseteq\mathbb F[S]/(S^p)\). The \(T_u\)-freeness of the quotient follows from the lemma's last part. \(\square\)

What this means

  • The closure-gluing hypothesis now holds for every closed column member, with any allowed values, whose forms have an affine basis of values with multiplicities \((p-1)(D+1)^2\) at \(P_0\) and \((p-1)(D+1)\) at each other point, and whose allowed set \(Z\) is nonempty. This includes dense single clauses and families of clauses sharing such a span.
  • For this approach, what remains for the column component is span dimension. The theorem needs \(d\le(N-(p-1)(D+1)^2)/((p-1)(D+1))\). Above that the seed argument gives nothing, and freeness there is open. The budget's column constraints, from up to \(N^K\) clauses of about \(\log N\) forms each, can span that much. The transfer lemma gives a sufficient condition: freeness of the column tensor power over the full form algebra. Hypothesis (b) for closed members and (c) over the closed base remain open, as the remaining gap lists.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: thm:board-seed-freeness with its proof, including the seed criterion and the lemma on board seed blocks for the full column tensor power, quoted in step 2; lem:closure-saturation, thm:closure-gluing, the sparse-closure proof and lem:slice-strictness. The claim search (seeded closed member, freeness transfer) found no result implying the lemma or the theorem; cor:seeded-selector-members is the nearest, for unclosed augmented selectors at \(p=3\). A fresh-context reviewer found the lemma (injectivity, strictness, surjectivity below \(n_0\), the direct summand, (a), (b), the last part including \(a_i+1=p\)), \(F/JF\) as the functions on \(\mathcal P_Z^{(u)}\), the degree bookkeeping, and both corollary ranges correct. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the relation to slice strictness corrected, with \(J\cap R_k=(s-m)R_{k-1}\) proved;
  • the lemma's hypotheses stated as used, with "free in degrees \(<n_0\)" defined;
  • the board-seeds claim quoted exactly, with the block count;
  • notation clashes removed;
  • the scope limited to conditions modulo \(p\) on forms in the span;
  • the comparison with cor:seeded-selector-members removed;
  • the span-dimension bullet restricted to this approach, with the theorem's bound and open status.

The changes weaken or justify statements and add no claim, so no further pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • Closed column members whose forms span more than seeds allow.
  • (c) for generic members over the closed base; global row freeness for the budget's solution set.

Generic form freeness: random column forms act freely far beyond the seed range, up to a span threshold that shrinks with the degree

24 September 2026 · Finite check and conjecture · Freeness over large column spans; cycle odd-prime-large-span. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. thm:seeded-closure-stability needs the column tensor power free over the row sums and the members' forms, which board seeds give only for span dimension up to about \(N/((p-1)(D+1))\) (seeded closure). Seeds are sufficient, not necessary. The cycle asks how far freeness actually extends for generic forms, and whether it can carry the large spans the budget produces.

General statement. conj:generic-form-freeness: for each \(D\) there is \(c_D>0\) such that for column forms in general position with span dimension \(d\le c_DN-O(1)\), the column tensor power on few rows is free through degree \(D\) over its row sums and the forms. ex:generic-form-freeness supports it at \(p=3\), \(D=3,4\), and shows that freeness fails beyond a threshold, of about \(N/2\) at \(D=3\) and \(N/4\) at \(D=4\). So freeness over the full form algebra cannot carry spans of order \(N\) at the goal's degrees.

The test

Tested statement. Over \(\mathbb F_3\), the column tensor power \(\tilde A\) on \(R=2\) rows and \(N\) holes is free through degree \(D\) over \(T=\mathbb F[Y_0,Y_1,W_1,\dots,W_d]/(p\text{-th powers})\), acting by the row sums and column forms \(\ell_b=\sum_j\varphi_b(j)C_j\). By graded Nakayama this holds exactly when \(\mathrm{HF}(\tilde A/(r,\ell))_k=[q^k]\,(1+2q)^N/(1+q+q^2)^{2+d}\) for \(k\le D\), with the prediction positive there. That is the hypothesis lem:filtered-freeness-transfer needs in the seeded-closure proof on one board row plus the bulk row. form_freeness.py computes the Hilbert function in Singular. Forms: uniform random \(\varphi_b\in\mathbb F_3^N\), one seed. Controls: \(d=0\), the row sums alone, and coordinate forms \(C_1,\dots,C_d\), for which \(C_b^2=0\) forces failure.

Can it decide. Board seeds at \(D=3\) need an affine basis with multiplicity \((p-1)(D+1)^2=32\) at one point, so at these \(N\) they give nothing for any \(d\ge1\). A pass is freeness beyond seeds; a failure with positive prediction is genuine non-freeness.

Excess \(\mathrm{HF}-\text{prediction}\), from degree 2 up (degrees 0 and 1 are 0 throughout; ff_R2_D3.json, ff_R2_D3_large.json, ff_R2_D4.json; the prediction is positive in every case):

\(D\)\(N\)results
312d=0: free; d=2: free; d=4: excess 0, 7; d=6: excess 1, 46; d=8: excess 6, 112; coord d=4: excess 8, 132
316d=0: free; d=2: free; d=4: free; d=6: excess 0, 1; d=8: excess 0, 25; coord d=4: excess 8, 196
320d=4: free; d=6: free; d=8: free; d=10: excess 0, 4; d=12: excess 0, 43
324d=4: free; d=6: free; d=8: free; d=10: free; d=12: excess 0, 1
416d=2: free; d=4: free; d=6: excess 0, 1, 71; d=8: excess 0, 25, 558; d=10: excess 2, 118, 1335
420d=2: free; d=4: free; d=6: excess 0, 0, 6; d=8: excess 0, 0, 50; d=10: excess 0, 4, 548
424d=2: free; d=4: free; d=6: free; d=8: excess 0, 0, 1; d=10: excess 0, 0, 8

Random forms are free up to \(d=2,4,8,10\) at \(N=12,16,20,24\) for \(D=3\), and up to \(d=4,4,6\) at \(N=16,20,24\) for \(D=4\). They fail from \(d=4,6,10,12\) and \(d=6,6,8\) respectively. Coordinate forms fail from degree 2, and the row sums alone are free. This is ex:generic-form-freeness.

What this means

  • Freeness extends far beyond the seed range for generic forms: at \(N=24\), \(D=3\), ten random forms act freely where seeds allow none.
  • It still stops at a span threshold that shrinks with \(D\): about \(N/2\) at \(D=3\) and \(N/4\) at \(D=4\). The data cannot tell whether the decay is like \(1/D\) or exponential in \(D\); \(D=5\) would need \(N\) near 48. Either way the covered span shrinks relative to \(N\) as \(D\) grows, while the budget's column constraints can span up to \(N\) at \(D=O(\log N)\).
  • So the transfer lemma must be applied with a smaller algebra than all the forms: the member needs only \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal P_Z}\) free over the rows, not freeness over its forms. Large spans need an argument that uses the allowed set, for instance through a seeded sub-span that already determines \(Z\) up to low degree.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: thm:seeded-closure-stability and lem:filtered-freeness-transfer, the board-seeds proof's seed criterion, and the graded-Nakayama criterion used in the recorded board-affine checks. The controls behave as predicted: the row sums alone are free, and coordinate forms fail from degree 2 since \(C_b^2=0\). The entry registers a finite check and a conjecture and no proof, so no reviewer pass was run.

Remaining gap

  • The rate of the threshold in \(D\); a proof of generic freeness below it.
  • Closed column members of large span, through the allowed set rather than the full form algebra.
