Route review: closed column members are stable for sparse, seeded and block-structured constraints; the adversarial dense case is the recorded largest gap

24 September 2026 · Route review, finite check and conjecture · The column component after closure; cycle odd-prime-column-review. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

General statement. The line's claim is that the budget's column constraints, closed under their vanishing polynomials, leave the weak base without falls below \(D\) (thm:closure-gluing, conj:closed-row-freeness). The review's falsification attempt finds that span dimension alone is not the obstacle: ex:pair-matching-closed-freeness shows a member of span \(N/2\), beyond both the seed range and the generic threshold, with row-free graded functions. The new claim is conj:block-seed-stability: constrained hole blocks act as seeds, so column members that are products over many disjoint blocks are stable.

The line since the closed-base review

Since the closed-base review, five research cycles ran:

  • closed splitting, a check at \(n=8,9\);
  • global closure, an alternative sufficient condition for non-refutability;
  • sparse closure, members on few holes, and slice saturation;
  • seeded closure, with the filtered freeness transfer lemma: members whose forms have a seeded span, for any allowed values;
  • generic form freeness: freeness over the forms extends beyond seeds but stops at a span threshold that shrinks with \(D\).

What the goal needs

At \(D=O(\log N)\), for the column constraints of any \(N^K\) adversarial clauses: the closure-gluing hypothesis for their allowed set \(Z\), which covers all but about \(1/N\) of the slice. Then (b) and (c) over the closed base, or the global closure condition for all constraints together.

Falsification attempt: is span the obstacle?

If large span alone broke closed stability, the column route would fail for the budget, whose column constraints can span up to \(N\). The attempt takes a member of large span with no seeded structure: pair merges over a perfect matching of the holes, at most one occupied hole in each pair \(\{2t,2t+1\}\). Its forms \(C_{2t}+C_{2t+1}\) span \(N/2\). That is beyond the seed range, and beyond the generic threshold of ex:generic-form-freeness, about 2 at \(N=12\), \(D=3\) and 4 at \(N=16\), \(D=4\). closed_row_freeness.py (member 'pairs') computes the one-row test of conj:closed-row-freeness exactly in Singular. The excess is 0 at \(N=12\), \(D=3\) and at \(N=16\), \(D=4\), and 0 for the base control (crf_pairs.json). This is ex:pair-matching-closed-freeness. Like the earlier closed checks it lies below the conjecture's range and tests content \(ke_1\) only.

The explanation is structural. The closed member is a board of \(N/2\) fat columns. A fat column is a square-zero module with \(1\mapsto\) the row sums of its cells, and in a tensor product of such blocks the products of row sums over distinct blocks are independent, as for ordinary columns. So the constrained blocks supply the seeds themselves. The attempt does not refute the line; it locates the obstacle. Large span is harmless when the constraints factor over many blocks. The open case is entanglement: dense forms that tie all holes together, so that no block of holes is free of the others. That is the adversarial axis the generalization review called the largest gap: special position survives every choice of prefix sets, so no generic theorem transfers.

Assessment of the line

The column component went from effective boards to one freeness condition with three proved classes: sparse, seeded, and, conjecturally, block-structured members. Each proof is general in its class. Their method is the same: seeds from somewhere, then transfer. The budget's worst case, dense entangled forms of span near \(N\), is covered by none of them. The generic-form data show that freeness over the forms themselves stops at a threshold shrinking with \(D\). So a proof for that case cannot come from freeness over the forms, and must use the allowed set, which covers all but \(1/N\) of the slice. (b) and (c) over the closed base, and the global condition, are untested at sizes in range. The line has become a precise statement of what is left: freeness of graded functions on nearly-full allowed sets cut by entangled forms. No recorded mechanism reaches it.

The highest-risk item and the next step

The highest-risk item remains the column component's dense entangled case. Before attacking it, the next cycle should secure what the falsification attempt suggests, since block structure is the natural intermediate class. conj:block-seed-stability: over a field of characteristic \(p\), if the column constraints factor over disjoint hole blocks \(B_1,\dots,B_M\), each block's allowed set having nonconstant occupancy count and some occupied hole, and \(M\ge(p-1)(D+1)^2\), then the closed member has no falls with the weak base below \(D\).

Next step, on route item odd-prime-clause-transfer: prove conj:block-seed-stability by the block-seed argument, with lem:filtered-freeness-transfer for the slice. Then ask whether an entangled member contains, after restriction to a large sub-board, a block-structured or seeded one at the degrees that matter. That is a density question about the allowed set, not about the forms.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the statements and proofs of thm:sparse-closure-stability, thm:seeded-closure-stability, lem:filtered-freeness-transfer, thm:fat-board-stability (whose seeds were ordinary columns), the generic-form data, and the adversarial row of the generalization review. The pair-matching check reuses the recorded closed-freeness driver with one added member. The review adds a finite check and a conjecture and no proof, so no reviewer pass was run.

Block-seed stability: closed column members that factor over many blocks, each allowing two occupancy counts mod p, have no falls with the weak base

24 September 2026 · Working proofs · Closed column members factoring over hole blocks; cycle odd-prime-block-seeds. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The column-component review found pair merges of span \(N/2\) row-free and conjectured that constrained hole blocks act as seeds (conj:block-seed-stability). The cycle proves its version with the count condition read modulo \(p\), a refinement; the integer-count version stays open for blocks whose counts agree modulo \(p\).

General statement. lem:good-block-seeds: call a hole block \(B\) with allowed set \(Z_B\subseteq\{0,1\}^B\) good if \(Z_B\) contains two patterns whose weights differ modulo \(p\). A product of \((p-1)(u+1)\) good blocks is a free seed for the row sums of \(u\) rows and the occupancy count. thm:block-seed-stability: over a field of characteristic \(p\), if the holes are partitioned into blocks, \(Z\) is the set of slice patterns whose restriction to each block \(B_t\) lies in \(Z_t\), \(Z\) is nonempty, and at least \((p-1)(D+1)^2\) blocks are good, then the weak base plus the closed member \(\mathcal M_D(\mathcal P_Z)\) has no fall below \(D\) and no PC refutation of degree \(D\). An unconstrained hole is a good block of size one, so the theorem contains cor:seed-transfer-ranges for sparse members. A merged pair is a good block, so it contains merges of a perfect matching.

Good blocks are seeds

Work, as in the sparse-closure proof, on \(u\) board rows and a bulk row, with the degree filtration in the variables \(C_j\) and \(x_{ij}\). For a block \(B\) let \(\mathcal P'_B\) be the assignments of the holes of \(B\) to these rows with occupancy in \(Z_B\), and \(\Gamma_B=\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal P'_B}\). \(T_{u+1}=\mathbb F[R_0,\dots,R_u]/(R^p)\) acts on \(\Gamma_B\) by \(R_0\mapsto s_B=\sum_{j\in B}C_j\) and \(R_i\mapsto r_i^B=\sum_{j\in B}x_{ij}\). These take values in \(\mathbb F_p\), so their \(p\)-th powers vanish in gr. \(\Gamma_B\) lives in degrees \(\ge0\), with \(\Gamma_{B,0}=\mathbb F\) when \(Z_B\ne\emptyset\).

Lemma (good-block seeds). If \(B\) is good, the images of \(s_B,r_1^B,\dots,r_u^B\) in \(\Gamma_{B,1}\) are linearly independent. If \(B_1,\dots,B_b\) are good, \(b=(p-1)(u+1)\), then in \(W=\Gamma_{B_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\Gamma_{B_b}\), with \(T_{u+1}\) acting diagonally, \(\operatorname{Ann}_{T_{u+1}}(1)=0\).

Proof. Independence: suppose \(\alpha s_B+\sum_i\beta_ir_i^B\) is constant on \(\mathcal P'_B\). \(Z_B\) has a pattern with an occupied hole \(j\), since two weights differ. Moving the pigeon at \(j\) between the bulk row and row \(i\) keeps the occupancy and changes \(r_i^B\) by 1, so \(\beta_i=0\). Then \(\alpha s_B\) is constant on \(Z_B\), where \(s_B\) takes two values modulo \(p\), so \(\alpha=0\).

Seed: \(W\) is multigraded by the degree in each block. Write \(y_0^{(t)}=s_{B_t}\) and \(y_i^{(t)}=r_i^{B_t}\). For an exponent vector \(a\), \(a_i\le p-1\), \(|a|\le b\), the component of \(\prod_iR_i^{a_i}\cdot1\) in multidegree 1 on a set \(K\) of \(|a|\) blocks and 0 elsewhere is \(a!\sum_\sigma\bigotimes_{t\in K}y^{(t)}_{\sigma(t)}\). The sum runs over the maps \(\sigma:K\to\{0,\dots,u\}\) taking each value \(i\) exactly \(a_i\) times, and \(a!=\prod a_i!\) is a unit. By the independence in each block, these tensors for distinct \(a\) with the same \(|a|\) are linearly independent. Elements with different \(|a|\) have different degrees. So a relation \(\sum_a\lambda_a\prod R^a\cdot1=0\) forces every \(\lambda_a=0\). \(\square\)

The theorem

Theorem (block-seed stability). Over a field of characteristic \(p\), with \(m\ge1\), let the holes be partitioned into blocks \(B_1,\dots,B_M\), let \(Z_t\subseteq\{0,1\}^{B_t}\), and let \(Z=\{c\text{ in the slice}:c_{B_t}\in Z_t\ \forall t\}\) be nonempty. If at least \((p-1)(D+1)^2\) of the blocks are good, the homogenized weak base plus \(\mathcal M_D(\mathcal P_Z)\) is \(z\)-injective below \(D\) and has no PC refutation of degree \(D\).

Proof. By thm:closure-gluing it suffices that the row-sum Koszul cycles on \(G=\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal P_Z}\) through degree \(D\) are Frobenius plus boundaries.

  1. Content reduction. As in the sparse-closure proof, step 1, pass to \(\mathcal P_Z^{(u)}\) on the \(u\le D\) rows of a content's support and the bulk row, as \(T_u\)-modules.
  2. Product without the slice. Let \(\mathcal P'=\prod_t\mathcal P'_{B_t}\), the assignments with \(c_{B_t}\in Z_t\) for all \(t\), without the slice. The variables split over the blocks, so \(\Gamma=\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal P'}=\bigotimes_t\Gamma_{B_t}\). This is a \(T_{u+1}\)-linear isomorphism with the diagonal action, since \(s=\sum_ts_{B_t}\) and \(r_i=\sum_tr_i^{B_t}\). Each \(Z_t\) is nonempty because \(Z\) is.
  3. Seeds. Group \((p-1)(u+1)(D+1)\le(p-1)(D+1)^2\) good blocks into \(D+1\) groups of \((p-1)(u+1)\). By the lemma each group \(W_k\) is a free seed: \((W_k)_0=\mathbb F\cdot1\) and \(\operatorname{Ann}(1)=0\). The groups are different seeds, since each block has its own \(Z_t\). The free-seed lemma's proof applies unchanged to \(W_1\otimes\cdots\otimes W_{D+1}\otimes M\): each \(W_k\) splits as \(T_{u+1}\cdot1\oplus Q_k\) with \(Q_k\) in degrees \(\ge1\), and the expansion is the same. With the remaining blocks as \(M\) (a graded \(T_{u+1}\)-module in degrees \(\ge0\)), it gives \(\Gamma=\Phi\oplus Q\) with \(\Phi\) free over \(T_{u+1}\) and \(Q\) in degrees \(\ge D+1\).
  4. Slice. \(T_{u+1}=\mathbb F[S]/(S^p)\otimes T_u\), with \(S=R_0\) acting as \(s\). Apply lem:filtered-freeness-transfer with \(R\) the functions of \(s\), \(J\) those vanishing at \(m\), \(n_0=D+1\), and \(T_{\rm row}=T_u\) acting through the \(r_i\), which satisfy \(r_i^p=r_i\). It gives that \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{\mathcal P_Z^{(u)}}=\operatorname{gr}(\mathbb F^{\mathcal P'}/J\mathbb F^{\mathcal P'})\) is free over \(T_u\) in degrees \(\le D\).
  5. Frobenius. As in the seeded-closure proof, step 4. \(\square\)

Cases. A hole outside every constraint is a block with \(Z_t=\{0,1\}\), good. So a member on a hole set \(H\) with \(N-|H|\ge(p-1)(D+1)^2\) is a case, which is cor:seed-transfer-ranges for sparse members. A merge of a pair has \(Z_t=\{00,10,01\}\), weights 0 and 1, so it is good. For \(N\) even and \(m\ge1\), merges of a perfect matching are stable once \(N/2\ge(p-1)(D+1)^2\); \(Z\ne\emptyset\) holds since occupying up to \(N/2\ge p-1\) pairs hits every residue modulo \(p\). The checks of ex:pair-matching-closed-freeness, at \(N=12\), \(D=3\) and \(N=16\), \(D=4\), lie far below this range (\(N\ge64\) at \(D=3\)), so the theorem does not cover them. A block whose allowed set fixes its count modulo \(p\), such as an onto block \(Z_t=\{1\}\) or a block allowing exactly one occupied hole, is not good. Such blocks are allowed, but they do not count as seeds.

What this means

  • The theorem proves the modulo-\(p\) version of conj:block-seed-stability, a partial resolution: large-span column members that factor over many good blocks are stable. A block with allowed counts \(\{0,p\}\) satisfies the conjecture's integer condition but is not good, since \(s_B\) is constant on it modulo \(p\); that case stays open. Span is not the obstacle, and the seeds may come from the constrained blocks themselves.
  • The remaining column cases are members that neither factor with at least \((p-1)(D+1)^2\) good blocks nor have a seeded span (thm:seeded-closure-stability). These include factored members made mostly of count-fixed blocks, and dense forms tying all holes together. The next question is whether such a member, restricted to a large sub-board, contains a factored or seeded one at the degrees that matter.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the sparse-closure proof, lem:filtered-freeness-transfer with its slice case, the seeded-closure proof, the free-seed lemma, and conj:block-seed-stability. The claim search (block seeds, fat columns, factored members) found thm:fat-board-stability and the sparse and seeded theorems, none implying this one. A fresh-context reviewer found the lemma (independence via the pigeon move, the seed computation) and the theorem (product decomposition, count, transfer hypotheses) correct and every hypothesis used. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the free-seed lemma stated for distinct seeds;
  • the relation to the conjecture recorded as a partial resolution (modulo \(p\));
  • the remaining gap restated to include factored members with few good blocks and to exclude seeded spans;
  • the perfect-matching case given its hypotheses and compared with the check's sizes.

The changes weaken statements or add a one-sentence justification, so no further pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • Column members that neither factor with enough good blocks nor have a seeded span; the integer-count case of conj:block-seed-stability.
  • (c) for generic members over the closed base; global row freeness for the budget's solution set.

Entangled probe: dense selector and clause families are closed row-free at small sizes, and hole deletions and placements cannot supply seeds for dense forms

24 September 2026 · Finite check and observation · Closed column members with entangled dense forms; cycle odd-prime-entangled. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. After the block-seed and seeded-closure theorems, the open column case is members that neither factor over many good blocks nor have a seeded span: families of clauses on dense forms that tie all holes together. The cycle probes whether such members break the closure-gluing hypothesis, and whether a restriction could reduce them to a proved case.

General statement. conj:closed-row-freeness asserts the closure-gluing hypothesis for allowed sets covering half the slice. ex:entangled-closed-freeness finds it, in one-row contents at \(N=12\), \(D=3\), for families of 2 to 4 selectors and of 4 two-form clauses on independent dense random forms, including spans beyond the generic threshold of ex:generic-form-freeness. obs:restriction-no-seeds: for \(p\ge3\), when the forms' value map \(j\mapsto(\varphi_1(j),\dots,\varphi_d(j))\) is injective, no restriction that deletes holes or places pigeons produces value multiplicities, so thm:seeded-closure-stability cannot be reached by these restrictions. Random forms are injective with probability at least \(1-\binom N2p^{-d}\), so with high probability once \(d\ge2\log_pN+\omega(1)\).

The probe

Tested statement. For \(Z\) the slice minus the forbidden sets of a clause family, the associated graded functions on \(\mathcal P_Z^{(1)}\) (one board row and the bulk row) satisfy \((I:\rho)=I+(\rho^{p-1})\) in degrees \(<D\), \(I\) the top ideal of the point ideal. This is the one-row case of the closure-gluing hypothesis, as in ex:closed-row-freeness. closed_row_freeness.py gains members 'selectorsT', \(T\) selectors \(1-(\ell_t-v_t)^2\) on independent dense forms (coefficients in \(\{1,2\}\), span \(T\)), and 'clausesT', \(T\) clauses each forbidding one value pattern of two fresh dense forms (span \(2T\)).

Can it decide. At \(p=3\) a selector has degree 2, so the selector families are visible in the degrees the test compares, \(\le D-1=2\). The two-form clauses have degree 4 and are visible only through lower-degree elements of their vanishing ideal. The generic-form threshold at \(N=12\), \(D=3\) is about \(d=2\), so selector families of span 3 and 4 are beyond it, where freeness over the forms fails. The sizes meet the one-row seed bound \(4D\) and lie below the conjecture's range \((p-1)(D+1)D=24\). The selector families cover about \((2/3)^T\) of the slice, below the conjecture's half; the clause family covers more than half. A failure here would therefore not refute the conjecture, but a pass shows that entangled members do not fail where freeness over their forms already does.

selectors2210, 0, 0

selectors441, 20, 0, 0

This is ex:entangled-closed-freeness.

Restrictions do not supply seeds

Two restrictions keep the system an instance of the weak base plus a column member. Deleting a hole \(j\) sets \(x_{ij}=0\) for all \(i\): the board has \(N-1\) holes, and the member is restricted to \(C_j=0\). Placing pigeon \(i_0\) in hole \(j_0\) sets \(x_{i_0j_0}=1\), \(x_{ij_0}=0\) for \(i\ne i_0\) and \(x_{i_0j}=0\) for \(j\ne j_0\): the board has \(m-1\) rows and \(N-1\) holes, and the member is restricted to \(C_{j_0}=1\). A PC refutation restricts to a PC refutation of the restricted system at no larger degree, so a degree lower bound for a restriction gives one for the original. Reaching a proved case this way would also need the restricted member to meet that theorem's other hypotheses: the allowed set is shifted by \(\varphi_b(j_0)\) under a placement, and the theorems conclude closure stability, which gives the lower bound through the socle criterion.

Observation (restriction gives no seeds). Let \(p\ge3\), and let the value map \(j\mapsto\varphi(j)=(\varphi_1(j),\dots,\varphi_d(j))\) of the member's forms be injective on the holes. Then after any sequence of hole deletions and pigeon placements, the remaining holes have pairwise distinct value vectors, so no value is taken twice. The multiplicity condition of thm:seeded-closure-stability needs at least \((p-1)(D+1)\ge2\) holes at each basis point, so it fails for every such restriction with \(d\ge1\). Uniform random \(\varphi\in(\mathbb F_p^N)^d\) is injective with probability at least \(1-\binom N2p^{-d}\).

Proof. A deletion restricts the value map to the remaining holes. A placement replaces each form by \(\ell_b|_{C_{j_0}=1}\), which keeps the coefficients \(\varphi_b(j)\) of the other holes and shifts the allowed values by \(\varphi_b(j_0)\). Both preserve injectivity on the remaining holes. Two fixed holes share a value vector with probability \(p^{-d}\), and the union bound gives the estimate. \(\square\)

The seeded theorem is applied to the forms through which \(Z\) is defined. A sub-span or projection of the forms need not define \(Z\), so the observation does not address a seeded sub-span that determines \(Z\) up to low degree; that route is open. Other restrictions, such as setting single cells to 0 or identifying holes, are not covered. Remark, not proved: whether a restriction can make a dense member factor over blocks depends on its span, since combinations such as \(\ell_1-\ell_2\) may be block-supported, not on the supports of the individual forms. No claim is made about the block route.

What this means

  • In the one-row test at \(N=12\), \(D=3\), entangled selector and clause families behave like the proved classes: no failure appeared. The probe covers degree-2 structure only, and \(D\ge5\) would be needed to see the clause families' own degree.
  • Hole deletions and pigeon placements cannot reach the seeded theorem for dense random forms. What remains is a proof of closed row freeness for nearly full allowed sets cut by dense forms, through the block route, a seeded sub-span that determines the allowed set at low degree, or the allowed set directly, or a counterexample at larger degree.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: thm:seeded-closure-stability's multiplicity condition, thm:block-seed-stability's block condition, the closed-freeness driver and its earlier controls (ex:closed-row-freeness, including failures below the seed bound), and ex:generic-form-freeness. A fresh-context reviewer checked the observation. It found the seed part correct for the two restrictions with \(p\) odd, and required: the restrictions defined exactly (placements remove a pigeon and a hole); the scope limited to these two restriction types; \(p\ge3\) stated; the projection question addressed; the probability statement given with its \(\omega(1)\) margin; and the block sentence downgraded to an unproved remark. All were adopted. They weaken statements, so no further pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • A proof, or a counterexample, of closed row freeness for entangled dense members, at degrees where their clauses are visible.
  • (c) for generic members over the closed base; global row freeness for the budget's solution set.

Sequential transfer attempt: cutting clauses out one at a time gives no reduction, since only the last step's hypothesis is used

24 September 2026 · Unsuccessful attempt, withdrawn at review · Entangled column members; cycle odd-prime-subspan. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. thm:seeded-closure-stability needs freeness over all of a member's forms at once, which stops at a span threshold (ex:generic-form-freeness). The cycle tried to cut an entangled member's clauses out one at a time, so that each step would involve one clause's few forms and the total span would never enter.

General statement. The all-parameter claim the cycle targeted is conj:closed-row-freeness for entangled members. The attempt does not advance it. Iterating lem:filtered-freeness-transfer does not carry freeness over the next clause's forms through a quotient, since the lemma returns only freeness over the rows. So a clause-by-clause statement uses only its last step's hypothesis, which involves every clause through the quotient. No claim is registered.

Why the reduction is vacuous

Put \(F_0\) for the functions on all assignments to \(u\) rows and the bulk row, and \(F_t=F_{t-1}/J_tF_{t-1}\) for the clauses in some order, with the slice last. The drafted lemma assumed, at each step \(t\), that \(\operatorname{gr}F_{t-1}\) is free below degree \(n_0\) over clause \(t\)'s forms and the rows, and concluded freeness of the final quotient over the rows. The last part of lem:filtered-freeness-transfer returns freeness over the rows only, so step \(t\) never supplies step \(t+1\)'s hypothesis. The conclusion follows from the last step alone, by one application of the transfer lemma to \(F_{T-1}\). With the slice last, that hypothesis is that the graded functions on the unsliced set allowed by all clauses are free below \(D+1\) over \(\mathbb F[S]/(S^p)\otimes T_u\), which involves every clause. A genuinely sequential version would carry freeness over the remaining clauses' forms through each quotient. The transfer lemma's last-part argument extends to any \(\mathbb F_p\)-valued degree-1 elements, but that version needs joint freeness at the first step, which is the threshold the attempt meant to avoid. A fresh-context reviewer identified this, and the lemma is withdrawn before registration.

The small-size data

seq_freeness.py computed, on one board row and the bulk row (\(u=1\)) at \(N=12\), \(D=3\) over \(\mathbb F_3\), whether \(G_{t-1}\) is free through degree \(D\) over \(s\), \(r=\sum_jy_j\) and clause \(t\)'s forms. \(G_{t-1}\) is gr of the functions on the unsliced assignments allowed by clauses \(1,\dots,t-1\). The quantity is excess \(=\mathrm{HF}(G_{t-1}/(s,r,\ell_t))-[q^k]\,\mathrm{HS}(G_{t-1})\bigl((1-q)/(1-q^3)\bigr)^{2+k_t}\) in degrees 0 to 3, with the \(T\)-action induced by the forms and the row sum. By graded Nakayama a positive excess refutes freeness. Zero excess is necessary for freeness but does not verify the transfer lemma's hypothesis in higher degrees. The joint control is freeness of \(G_0\) over all the forms at once (seq_*.json):

What this means

  • There is no clause-by-clause shortcut through the transfer lemma. Any route through it needs freeness of the whole allowed set's graded functions over the rows and \(s\), which is the closure-gluing hypothesis itself, or joint freeness over the forms, which stops at the span threshold.

Route review: the closure route proves every structured column member, fails at entangled ones, and pinned symmetric counts break it at low density

24 September 2026 · Route review with a finite check · The clause-transfer line after the column-component cycles; cycle odd-prime-line-review. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

General statement. The line's claim is that the budget's constraints, closed under their vanishing polynomials, leave the weak base without a refutation of degree \(D=O(\log N)\): by relative gluing over the closed column base (conj:closed-row-freeness, conj:closed-base-splitting, and (c)), or by thm:global-closure-gluing's single condition. The falsification attempt, ex:symmetric-pin-nonfreeness, finds a new obstruction: an allowed set pinning a symmetric occupancy count of degree 3 breaks closed row freeness at a size where the base and a selector pass.

Where the line stands

Proved, with fresh-context review: closure saturation and closure gluing; global closure gluing; closed stability for sparse members, for seeded spans with any allowed values (via the filtered freeness transfer lemma), and for members factoring over many good blocks; slice saturation in a linear range. Measured: freeness over the forms stops at a span threshold that shrinks with \(D\) (ex:generic-form-freeness). Failed: reaching seeds by restriction for dense forms (obs:restriction-no-seeds), and clause-by-clause transfer, withdrawn as vacuous (sequential attempt). Untested in range: (b) and (c) over the closed base, and entangled members.

What the goal needs

For the column constraints of any \(N^K\) adversarial clauses at \(D=O(\log N)\): the closure-gluing hypothesis for an allowed set covering all but about \(1/N\) of the slice, cut by dense forms of span up to \(N\). Then (b) and (c), or the global condition.

Falsification attempt: pinned symmetric counts

The pinned-row example (global closure) showed that pinning a row count breaks the freeness condition. Its column analog pins a symmetric function of the occupancy. The attempt takes \(Z=\{c\text{ in the slice}:e_3(c)\equiv a\pmod3\}\), where \(e_3\) is the third elementary symmetric polynomial. By Lucas' theorem this fixes the weight modulo 9, a relation of degree 3 covering about a third of the slice. closed_row_freeness.py (member 'e3pin') computes the one-row closed test exactly in Singular over \(\mathbb F_3\). At \(N=12\), \(D=4\) the excess is 0, 0, 0, 970 in degrees 0 to 3. The base and a single selector, which covers two thirds of the slice, give 0 throughout at the same size (crf_e3pin.json, crf_e3pin_control.json). At \(N=9\), \(D=4\) the pin gives 0, 1, 0, 0. \(N=12\) is below the one-row seed bound \(4D=16\) at \(D=4\), so the comparison with the controls, not the size, carries the conclusion. This is ex:symmetric-pin-nonfreeness.

The pin lies outside conj:closed-row-freeness's class, which needs half the slice, so it refutes nothing recorded. It shows what the density hypothesis must exclude: low-degree relations on the allowed set that pin symmetric occupancy counts. For the budget's allowed set, which covers all but about \(1/N\) of the slice, a relation vanishing on it has degree at least about \(\log_2N\): a nonzero multilinear polynomial of degree \(r\) is nonzero on at least a \(2^{-r}\) fraction of the cube, and the slice condition changes this only by a constant factor. So such pins can arise only between degree \(\log_2N\) and \(D\). That window is exactly where the clauses are visible and where no test so far reaches.

Assessment of the line

Every structured class of column members is now proved: sparse, seeded, and block-factored. The two attempts at entangled members failed for identifiable reasons. The obstructions found are pinned counts: of a row, of a low-weight occupancy, and of a symmetric occupancy function. All three are excluded by density, and all live at degrees the budget's allowed set cannot reach below \(\log_2N\). The remaining question is sharp: whether entangled dense clause families can create such a pin between \(\log_2N\) and \(D\). Neither the proofs nor the checks reach that window. The line's prospects depend on a mechanism that controls low-degree relations on nearly full allowed sets. The pinning obstructions suggest one: show that the closed algebra of a nearly full allowed set has no pinned symmetric relation below \(D\), and that this suffices for freeness.

The highest-risk item and the next step

The highest-risk item is the entangled column case in the window between \(\log_2N\) and \(D\). Next step, on route item odd-prime-clause-transfer: build a compiled kernel for the closed algebra's direct-sum form \(G=\bigoplus_Yx_Y\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{Z_{S(Y)}}\), for one row, computing \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{Z_S}\) from function spaces on the slice. Use it for a counterexample search: entangled selector and clause families at sizes in range (\(N\ge24\) at \(D=3\)). Include families designed to approximate a symmetric pin with many clauses. Record whether any fails where the base passes.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the pinned-row example and its proof, conj:closed-row-freeness and its class, the closed-freeness controls, and the entries of this line since the column-component review. The pin check uses the recorded driver with one added member and two controls at the same size. The degree bound for relations on nearly full sets is the standard Schwartz–Zippel-type bound on the cube, stated here as a heuristic for the slice. The review adds a finite check and no proof, so no reviewer pass was run.

Direct-sum search: a compiled kernel for the closed algebra finds entangled selector families row-free in range at degree 3, where they do not yet interact

24 September 2026 · Finite check with a validated kernel · Entangled column members in the conjecture's range; cycle odd-prime-direct-sum-search. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The line review asked for a counterexample search for closed row freeness on entangled members at sizes in range, beyond what point-ideal Gröbner bases reach, including members built to approximate a pin.

General statement. conj:closed-row-freeness, in its one-row case. ex:in-range-selector-freeness: at \(N=24\), \(D=3\), inside the conjecture's range \(N\ge(p-1)(D+1)D=24\), the base and families of 1 to 16 selectors on independent dense random forms (three seeds up to 8 forms, two seeds for 12 and 16) all pass. Families of 12 and 16 forms are beyond the generic-form threshold of about 10 at this size. The selectors' contributions to the Hilbert function are exactly additive through degree 3, so at this degree they do not interact and the test cannot see entanglement.

The kernel

direct_sum.cpp computes the one-row test on the direct-sum form of lem:closure-saturation: \(G=\bigoplus_Sy_SQ_S\), \(Q_{S,e}=\mathrm{Mon}_e(S^c)/\mathfrak a_{S,e}\), with \(\rho(\mu y_S)=\sum_{j\notin S\cup\mu}[\mu]_{S\cup j}y_{S\cup j}\). The excess is \(\dim\ker(\rho|G_k)-\dim\rho^{p-1}G_{k-p+1}\) for \(k\le D-1\), the quantity of closed_row_freeness.py. The tops \(\mathfrak a_{S,e}\) come from the kernel of evaluation on a random sample of allowed points. Each kernel vector is verified on every point of the subcube by a subset-sum transform, and failures add points and repeat, so the result is exact. run_direct_sum.py builds the members with the recorded random sequence.

Validation. Against the recorded Singular values the kernel agrees in every case tried (ds_validation.json):

  • the base and four selectors at \(N=12\), \(D=3\): 0, 0, 0;
  • the symmetric pin at \(N=9\), \(D=4\): 0, 1, 0, 0;
  • at \(N=12\), \(D=4\): 0, 0, 0, 970 for the symmetric pin, and 0 for the base and a selector;
  • the below-range controls: 0, 1, 1, 0 for the base at \(N=3\), and 0, 0, 2, 0 for a selector and a clause at \(N=4\).

An \(N=18\) case takes 2 seconds, and an \(N=24\), \(D=3\) case about 2 to 3 minutes on 12 threads.

The in-range search

Can it decide. \(N=24\), \(D=3\) is the smallest size in the conjecture's range at \(D=3\). A selector has degree 2 and is visible in the degrees compared, \(\le2\) for the kernel condition. Symmetric pins of degree 3 are not visible at \(D=3\), and \(D=4\) in range would need \(N\ge40\), out of reach, so the pin-approximating families asked for by the review were not run. The families' allowed sets cover about \((2/3)^T\) of the slice, so for \(T\ge2\) they lie outside the conjecture's half-slice class. A failure would still be informative. A pass is evidence only for what the degrees compared can see.

What this means

  • The kernel makes the one-row closed test exact and fast, with all Singular values reproduced. It reaches the conjecture's range at \(D=3\) and closes the "below range" objection there.
  • At \(D=3\), however, dense selector families do not interact, so no in-range test at this degree can probe entanglement. Interactions need degree at least that of products of the members' constraints, which is \(\ge4\) for selectors at \(p=3\), and \(D=4\) in range needs \(N\ge40\). The entangled case therefore stays undecided by computation, and needs a proof or a structural argument about interactions.

Interaction locality: the closed algebra of an intersection is determined by its pieces in the Mayer–Vietoris sense exactly when vanishing ideals add degree by degree, which fails on small boards, also for pairwise determination

24 September 2026 · Working proof (degreewise gluing) and a finite refutation of unconditional locality; cycle odd-prime-interactions. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The direct-sum search left entangled members at degrees where their constraints interact, out of computational reach in range. Its next step asked for a structural statement: the closed algebra of an intersection of allowed sets is determined through degree \(D\) by the pieces and their small interactions, with freeness under a robustness condition. The missing implication is row freeness of \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{Z}\) for \(Z=\bigcap_iU_i\), the budget's allowed set, from that of simpler sets. The natural tool is the Mayer–Vietoris sequence of function modules. It transfers freeness from \(U\), \(W\), \(U\cup W\) to \(U\cap W\) when it stays exact after grading by degree. The cycle states exactly when it does, bounds the failure, and tests the exactness on small boards before building a transfer on it.

General statement. lem:degreewise-gluing: for subsets \(U,W\) of the Boolean cube over any field, degree-\(d\) functions on \(U\) and \(W\) that agree on \(U\cap W\) glue to a degree-\(d\) function on \(U\cup W\) exactly when \(I_d(U\cap W)=I_d(U)+I_d(W)\). This holds for all \(d\le D\) exactly when the graded Mayer–Vietoris sequence is exact through degree \(D\). Gluing always succeeds after a degree shift \(\delta\), the degree of a polynomial separating \(U\) from \(W\setminus U\), which is \(k(p-1)\) for a \(k\)-form clause. For \(n\) sets, gluing in a chosen order gives the shift \((n-1)\delta\). ex:interaction-locality-failure: over \(\mathbb F_3\), for dense random selectors on the slice with \(N\le11\) and \(d\le4\), both exact pairwise locality and the pairwise determination of triple intersections fail in some cases. Neither holds unconditionally. All the boards are below the ranges of the recorded closed-freeness conjectures, so the check says nothing about them in range.

Setting

\(\mathbb F\) is any field in (a) and (b); in (c) it has characteristic \(p\). \(P\) is the space of multilinear polynomials in \(x_1,\dots,x_N\), identified with functions on \(\{0,1\}^N\) and filtered by degree, \(P_d\) the part of degree \(\le d\). For \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^N\):

  • \(I_d(X)=\{f\in P_d:f|_X=0\}\);
  • \(F_d(X)=P_d|_X\), so \(\mathbb F^X\) is filtered by the \(F_d(X)\);
  • \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^X=\bigoplus_dF_d(X)/F_{d-1}(X)\), the graded functions of the global-closure entry, with the convention \(F_{-1}(X)=0\).

In the application \(X\) lies in the occupancy slice and is cut out by allowed-value conditions on \(\mathbb F_p\)-linear forms. By lem:closure-saturation, the closed member's top algebra through degree \(D\) is \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^X\) there.

The lemma

Lemma (degreewise gluing). Let \(U,W\subseteq\{0,1\}^N\) and \(d\ge0\). Parts (a) and (b) hold over any field.

  1. The following are equivalent:
    1. every pair \(f\in F_d(U)\), \(g\in F_d(W)\) with \(f=g\) on \(U\cap W\) is the pair of restrictions of one \(h\in F_d(U\cup W)\);
    2. \(I_d(U\cap W)=I_d(U)+I_d(W)\);
    3. \(\Delta_d:=\dim F_d(U\cup W)-\dim F_d(U)-\dim F_d(W)+\dim F_d(U\cap W)=0\).
    Always \(\Delta_d\le0\).
  2. (i) holds for every \(d\le D\) if and only if the sequence \(0\to\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{U\cup W}\to\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{U}\oplus\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{W}\to\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{U\cap W}\to0\), with maps induced by the restrictions and the difference of restrictions (restriction preserves the filtration), is exact in every degree \(\le D\). The quantifier over all \(d\le D\) is needed: exactness of the degree-\(d\) part alone does not give (i) at \(d\).
  3. Shift. Let \(\mathbb F\) have characteristic \(p\). Suppose \(\chi\in P\) has degree \(\le\delta\), \(\chi=0\) on \(U\) and \(\chi=1\) on \(W\setminus U\); nothing is required elsewhere. Then \(I_d(U\cap W)\subseteq I_{d+\delta}(U)+I_{d+\delta}(W)\), so every compatible pair as in (i) glues in \(F_{d+\delta}(U\cup W)\). For a clause allowed set \(U=\{c:(\ell_1(c),\dots,\ell_k(c))\ne(v_1,\dots,v_k)\}\), with \(\ell_t\) affine forms with coefficients in \(\mathbb F_p\) and \(v=(v_1,\dots,v_k)\in\mathbb F_p^k\), the multilinear reduction of \(\prod_t\bigl(1-(\ell_t-v_t)^{p-1}\bigr)\) is such a \(\chi\) with \(\delta=k(p-1)\). For \(n\ge2\) sets \(U_1,\dots,U_n\) in a chosen order, with \(\chi_i\) for \(i<n\) of degree \(\le\delta\), \(0\) on \(U_i\) and \(1\) off \(U_i\) on the whole cube, \(I_d(\bigcap_iU_i)\subseteq\sum_{i<n}I_{d+i\delta}(U_i)+I_{d+(n-1)\delta}(U_n)\). No \(\chi_n\) is needed, \(n=2\) is the two-set statement, and the bound depends on the order.

Proof. (a) Choose representatives \(\tilde f,\tilde g\in P_d\). A glue exists if and only if some \(h\in P_d\) has \(h-\tilde f\in I_d(U)\) and \(h-\tilde g\in I_d(W)\), that is, if and only if \(\tilde f-\tilde g\in I_d(U)+I_d(W)\): given \(\tilde f-\tilde g=a+b\), put \(h=\tilde f-a=\tilde g+b\). Compatibility means \(\tilde f-\tilde g\in I_d(U\cap W)\), and every \(e\in I_d(U\cap W)\) arises, with \(\tilde f=e\), \(\tilde g=0\). So (i) is (ii). Next, \(\dim I_d(X)=\dim P_d-\dim F_d(X)\), \(I_d(U)\cap I_d(W)=I_d(U\cup W)\) and \(I_d(U)+I_d(W)\subseteq I_d(U\cap W)\). Hence \(\dim I_d(U\cap W)-\dim(I_d(U)+I_d(W))=-\Delta_d\ge0\), with equality exactly under (ii).

(b) The level-\(d\) sequence \(L_d\colon0\to F_d(U\cup W)\to F_d(U)\oplus F_d(W)\to F_d(U\cap W)\to0\) is a complex. It is injective on the left, since a function on \(U\cup W\) is determined by its restrictions, and surjective on the right, since \(F_d(U\cap W)\) is a restriction of \(P_d\). It is exact in the middle exactly under (i). The inclusions \(L_{d-1}\subseteq L_d\) give a short exact sequence of complexes \(0\to L_{d-1}\to L_d\to\operatorname{gr}_d\to0\), where \(\operatorname{gr}_d\) is the degree-\(d\) part of the graded sequence and \(L_{-1}=0\). By its long exact homology sequence, exactness of \(L_{d-1}\) and \(L_d\) gives exactness of \(\operatorname{gr}_d\), and exactness of \(L_{d-1}\) and \(\operatorname{gr}_d\) gives exactness of \(L_d\). Induction on \(d\) proves (b).

(c) For \(f\in I_d(U\cap W)\) write \(f=f\chi+f(1-\chi)\). \(f\chi\) vanishes on \(U\). \(f(1-\chi)\) vanishes on \(U\cap W\) because \(f\) does, and on \(W\setminus U\) because \(\chi=1\) there. Multilinear reduction does not raise degree, so both terms lie in \(P_{d+\delta}\). For the clause, \((\ell_t-v_t)^{p-1}\) is 1 where \(\ell_t\ne v_t\) and 0 where \(\ell_t=v_t\), since the values lie in \(\mathbb F_p\); the product is the indicator of the forbidden set. For \(n\) sets, \(1=\sum_{i<n}\chi_i\prod_{j<i}(1-\chi_j)+\prod_{j<n}(1-\chi_j)\) by telescoping, as polynomials. Multiply by \(f\). For \(i<n\) the \(i\)-th term vanishes on \(U_i\) and has degree \(\le d+i\delta\). The last term has degree \(\le d+(n-1)\delta\) and vanishes on \(U_n\): on \(\bigcap_jU_j\) because \(f\) does, and elsewhere on \(U_n\) because some \(1-\chi_j\), \(j<n\), vanishes there. \(\square\)

What (b) would give. If the graded sequence is exact through \(D\) and \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{U\cup W}\) is free over the truncated row algebra, then its image is a direct summand, since free modules over that self-injective algebra are injective. So \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{U\cap W}\) is a direct summand of \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^U\oplus\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^W\) and inherits freeness from them. Making this precise through a finite degree needs care with truncation; it is not stated as a result here, because its exactness hypothesis fails in the checks below.

The checks

Can it decide. The unconditional statements "\(\Delta_d=0\) for dense selector pairs" and "\(I_d(U_1\cap U_2\cap U_3)=\sum_{i<j}I_d(U_i\cap U_j)\)" are refuted by one failing case at any size. In range, the conjectures need \(N\ge(p-1)(D+1)D\), 24 at \(D=3\) and 40 at \(D=4\). There the ideals do not interact through \(D=3\) (the direct-sum search), and \(D\ge4\) is out of reach. So these checks can refute only the unconditional forms, not a range-restricted one. Sizes: the slice \(\sum c\equiv m\pmod3\) has 85 points at \(N=8\), 341 at \(N=10\), 683 at \(N=11\); \(P_4\) has 386 monomials at \(N=10\).

The forms have independent uniform coefficients in \(\{1,2\}\), not all equal, over \(\mathbb F_3\); a selector forbids one value \(v\) of its form. mv_locality.py computes \(\Delta_d\) by ranks for two selectors, or two two-form clauses, on the slice and on its pinned sub-slices \(x_j=1\) for \(j\le2\) (degrees \(\le4-|S|\)); 17 checks per case. triple_locality.py computes the ideals as nullspaces for three selectors, and compares \(I_d(U_1\cap U_2\cap U_3)\) with the sum of the pairwise and of the single ideals. validate_locality.py confirms that the rank and nullspace computations of \(\Delta_d\) agree, and that the shift bound of (c) holds, in all 12 pair cases it runs at \(N=8,10\).

Triples, \(d=2,3,4\) (tri_*.json): of 18 triples \(\times\) degrees, the pair defects are nonzero in 16 of 54 pairs. \(I_d\) of the triple intersection exceeds the sum of the pairwise ideals twice: by 1 at \(N=8\), \(d=2\), and by 2 at \(N=11\), \(d=4\) (seed 1). It exceeds the sum of the single ideals by up to 12. This is ex:interaction-locality-failure.

The defect is not monotone in \(d\): at \(N=8\), pair \(\{1,2\}\) has \(\Delta=-1,-4,-1\) at \(d=2,3,4\). That fits the shift of (c): an element of \(I_d(U\cap W)\) outside the sum lies in the sum at degree \(d+2\).

What this means

  • The structural statement asked for, in its Mayer–Vietoris form, is exactly (ii) of the lemma at each degree. It is false without a range hypothesis, even for two dense selectors, and pairwise determination of triples is false too. So interaction-locality cannot be a lemma valid on all boards. Any version must use the range, which is the regime where the direct-sum search shows no interaction through degree 3.
  • The always-available version loses \(\delta=k(p-1)\) degrees per gluing and, done clause by clause, \((n-1)\delta\) in total. For \(n^K\) clauses at \(D=O(\log n)\) that is useless. Whether the loss must grow with the number of sets is open. The recorded sequential transfer attempt failed for the same reason, a clause-by-clause argument whose cost is paid at each step.
  • The main record's filtered affine tree gluing (lem:filtered-affine-tree-gluing) is the analogous statement for functionals on subalgebras. Its three-space example, pairwise-consistent but not gluable, is the same phenomenon at degree one. It is not a statement about vanishing ideals of point sets and does not imply the lemma.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: lem:closure-saturation's identification of the top algebra with \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^X\), the direct-sum search's additivity data, the sequential-transfer withdrawal, and lem:filtered-affine-tree-gluing. Claim searches (the lemma's content words; Mayer–Vietoris; the dual functional form) found only the tree-gluing lemma, which neither implies nor follows from this one. The rank and nullspace computations agree on every validation case, and every quoted count is read from the result files by script. A fresh-context reviewer found no wrong step. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the field hypothesis confined to (c), with \(v\in\mathbb F_p^k\) and \(\mathbb F_p\) coefficients explicit;
  • the convention \(F_{-1}=0\);
  • the induced maps named in (b), and a note that the quantifier over all \(d\le D\) is needed;
  • the sharper \(n\)-set bound, which needs no \(\chi_n\), depends on the order and recovers the two-set case;
  • the two-set hypothesis on \(\chi\) kept to \(U\cup W\).

The changes state hypotheses and sharpen one bound; no further pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • Row freeness of \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^{Z}\) for the budget's allowed set, at degrees where its constraints interact, now without a locality shortcut valid on all boards.
  • Whether degreewise locality holds in range, and whether the gluing loss must grow with the number of sets.

Route review: locality holds where the forms are jointly free and reduces to form space there; the budget has far more forms than any free range, so the entangled window needs a t-wise mechanism

24 September 2026 · Route review and conjecture · The clause-transfer line after the locality cycle; cycle odd-prime-range-locality. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

General statement. The line's claim is still that the budget's constraints, closed under their vanishing polynomials, leave the weak base without a refutation of degree \(D\). Via thm:global-closure-gluing this needs row freeness of \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^Z\) for the budget's allowed set \(Z\), or relative gluing over the closed column base. The review adds conj:t-wise-locality. If every subfamily of at most \(t\) clauses has linearly independent combined forms that are jointly free through \(D\), with \(t\) large enough in terms of \(D\), then the vanishing ideal of \(Z\) is generated degree by degree by the single clauses' ideals. The review planned to open a range-locality cycle. Its first step showed that range locality, where it can be proved, is a restatement of the recorded transfer lemma. So this cycle became a review.

Where the line stands

Since the last line review, two cycles were run. The direct-sum search reached the closed-freeness range at \(D=3\) and found selector families additive there, so it could not see entanglement. The interaction-locality cycle proved lem:degreewise-gluing: Mayer–Vietoris gluing is exact exactly when vanishing ideals add degree by degree. It found that property failing for pairs and triples of dense selectors below range. Neither entered the window the last review named as decisive: degrees between about \(\log_2N\) and \(D\), for entangled members.

What the goal needs

At \(p=3\) the goal's PC degree is \(D=(4p-1)(p-1)k\) with \(k=\lceil(K+1)\log n/\log(p/(p-1))\rceil\) (quiet members), so \(D\approx37.6(K+1)\log_2n\). A forbidden set has density \(\le n^{-(K+1)}\), so a set of \(t\) forbidden sets whose forms are jointly independent meets in density \(\le n^{-t(K+1)}\). On the cube, a nonzero multilinear polynomial of degree \(r\) is nonzero on at least a \(2^{-r}\) fraction of points. So density excludes a function supported on such an intersection only below degree \(t(K+1)\log_2n\), and interactions of up to about 37 clauses remain possible below \(D\). This uses the cube bound as a heuristic for the slice, as the last review did. The budget has up to \(n^K\) clauses with \(k\) forms each, far more forms than the \(N=n\) coordinates.

Falsification attempt: what locality can be proved, and where it stops

Where the forms are jointly free, locality reduces to form space. Let \(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_s\) be \(\mathbb F_p\)-linear forms of the occupancies. Let \(R\) be the functions on \(\mathbb F_p^s\), acting on the slice's functions \(F\) through \(y=\ell(c)\). Suppose \(\operatorname{gr}F\) is free over \(\operatorname{gr}R\) through degree \(d\). For \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb F_p^s\) put \(X_\Omega=\{c:\ell(c)\in\Omega\}\) and \(J=I(\Omega)\subseteq R\). Then \(JF\) is the ideal of functions vanishing on \(X_\Omega\), since \(J\) is generated by the idempotent \(1_{y\notin\Omega}\). The transfer lemma, lem:filtered-freeness-transfer, gives \(\operatorname{gr}(JF)=\operatorname{gr}J\cdot\operatorname{gr}F\) below \(d\), so \(I_d(X_\Omega)=\sum_eI_e(\Omega)(\ell)\,F_{d-e}\): the ideal is generated from form space. Hence \(I_d(X_{\Omega_1}\cap X_{\Omega_2})=I_d(X_{\Omega_1})+I_d(X_{\Omega_2})\) whenever \(I_e(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2)=I_e(\Omega_1)+I_e(\Omega_2)\) in \(R\) for all \(e\le d\). That holds when \(\Omega_1\) and \(\Omega_2\) depend on disjoint blocks of coordinates. In that case they are a product, and a filtration-compatible basis of each factor that is adapted to its ideal gives the degreewise sum. This is only a consequence of the recorded transfer lemma, so no new claim is registered for it.

Independence is needed. Take one form \(\ell\), jointly free, and the selectors \(\ell\ne0\) and \(\ell\ne1\) over \(\mathbb F_3\). Their forbidden sets are disjoint. In form space \(I_1(\{2\})\ni y-2\), while \(I_1(\{1,2\})=I_1(\{0,2\})=0\), since a nonzero polynomial of degree 1 in one variable has one root. By the reduction, the degree-1 locality fails on the cube whenever \(\ell\) is free through degree 1. So disjoint, and hence invisible, forbidden intersections do not suffice. What matters is linear independence of the clauses' forms, as in the recorded three-space example for filtered affine tree gluing.

Where it stops. Joint freeness needs few forms: the measured threshold is about \(N/2\) at \(D=3\) and \(N/4\) at \(D=4\) (conj:generic-form-freeness). The budget's forms number \(n^Kk\gg N\), so no argument that assumes joint freeness of all forms can reach \(Z\). Up to that threshold, the reduction covers the families the record already handles, the seeded and block cases.

Assessment of the line

The cycles since the last review sharpened the gap without narrowing it. Every proved statement about closed members either assumes joint freeness of all forms involved, or structure (sparse, seeded, block) that implies a free sub-span. Every failure found (pins, dependent forms, small-board locality) is a failure of independence or of density. The decisive regime needs a statement that uses independence only locally, for small subfamilies, and turns it into a global statement about \(Z\). No recorded mechanism does that. The \(p\)-complex's common-conditioning form also stopped for want of such a local-to-global step (the wide-conditioning conjecture). On this evidence the line is coherent. It is blocked on one missing local-to-global statement, which has now been stated in a testable form but has no proof strategy yet.

The highest-risk item and the next step

The highest-risk item is that local-to-global step. conj:t-wise-locality: over \(\mathbb F_p\), let clauses \(b=1,\dots,M\) with \(k\) affine forms of the occupancies each cut allowed sets \(U_b\) of the slice. Suppose every subfamily of at most \(t\) clauses has linearly independent combined linear parts that are jointly free through degree \(D\). If \(t\ge t_0(D,k,p)\), then \(I_d(\bigcap_bU_b)=\sum_bI_d(U_b)\) for every \(d\le D\). By the reduction above, the hypothesis gives this for every subfamily of at most \(t\) clauses. The conjecture asserts that once \(t\) is large relative to \(D\), dependencies among more than \(t\) clauses create nothing new below \(D\). For random forms with \(tk\ll N\) the hypothesis is expected to hold, and for adversarial forms it is the robustness condition the budget would need, as pairwise coherence was for product constraints. Degreewise generation by single clauses would reduce the closed base to single-clause closures. It does not by itself give row freeness.

Relation to the record. The conjecture is the vanishing-ideal, many-clause analog of two recorded statements. lem:closure-additivity, with cor:coherent-member-additivity, proves that PC closures add for two members on independent spans under robustness. conj:component-hypothesis asks for syzygy generation after grouping clauses into components along bounded circuits. Its version with local freeness read as injectivity is refuted by an occupancy pair whose forms are not jointly free (ex:component-hypothesis-injectivity-counterexample). conj:t-wise-locality assumes joint freeness of every small subfamily, so that pair lies outside its hypothesis. With no circuits of size at most \(t\), every component there is a single clause.

Next step, on route item odd-prime-clause-transfer: attempt conj:t-wise-locality. First look for a counterexample in form space, where the question is exact and small: \(M\) clauses on forms in \(\mathbb F_3^s\) whose every \(t\)-subfamily is independent while the whole family is dependent. There, compare \(I_e(\bigcap\Omega_b)\) with \(\sum_bI_e(\Omega_b)\) for \(e\) up to \((p-1)s\). Then try a proof that a degree-\(d\) element of \(I(\bigcap\Omega_b)\) decomposes through subfamilies of size bounded in terms of \(d\).

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: lem:filtered-freeness-transfer (the exact statement in the seeded-closure entry), lem:degreewise-gluing, the quiet-members entry's parameters and degree gap, the last line review, conj:generic-form-freeness's thresholds, lem:filtered-affine-tree-gluing, lem:closure-additivity, cor:coherent-member-additivity, conj:component-hypothesis and its counterexample. Claim searches (t-wise independence, subfamily, vanishing ideal generated by single clauses; coherent product constraints) found those and no statement implying the conjecture. The reduction is a direct consequence of the transfer lemma plus the product-set decomposition, and the one-form example is a two-line count. The review adds a conjecture and no new proved claim, so no reviewer pass was run.

Pairing obstruction: s-wise independent selectors fail degreewise locality at degree ⌈s/2⌉, so t-wise locality needs t above 2D

24 September 2026 · Working proof (pairing obstruction) · Lower bound on the independence threshold of t-wise locality; cycle odd-prime-t-wise-locality. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The locality review stated conj:t-wise-locality. If every subfamily of at most \(t\) clauses has independent, jointly free forms and \(t\ge t_0(D,k,p)\), then the allowed set's vanishing ideal is generated degree by degree by the single clauses. The missing implication is this local-to-global step. The cycle searches form space for a counterexample, where the question is exact, and asks how the first failing degree grows with \(t\). If failures persisted at bounded degree for every \(t\), the conjecture would be false. If the failing degree grows, the growth rate bounds \(t_0\), which decides whether the budget can meet the hypothesis.

General statement. prop:pairing-obstruction: over \(\mathbb F_3\), for every \(s\ge2\), a family of \(s+1\) selectors on \(\mathbb F_3^s\) in general position (every \(s\) linear parts independent) fails degreewise locality at degree \(\lceil s/2\rceil\). This holds on the slice as well, whenever the \(s\) forms are jointly free through two degrees more. So the form-space version of conj:t-wise-locality needs \(t_0(D,1,3)\ge2D+1\). On the slice it needs \(t_0(D,1,3)\ge2D-3\) for \(D\ge3\), provided some slice carries \(2D-4\) occupancy forms jointly free in degrees \(\le D\). The obstruction comes from products of pair differences \(\prod(x_{2i-1}-x_{2i})\), which are supported on one weight level. The conjecture is not refuted: the failing degree grows linearly in \(t\), and computations up to \(s=9\) find no failure below \(\lceil s/2\rceil\) for this family.

The search

Can it decide. In form space, \(R\) is the functions on \(\mathbb F_3^s\), filtered by degree, and the defect \(\dim I_e(\bigcap_bU_b)-\dim\sum_bI_e(U_b)\) is exact linear algebra of size \(3^s\). A family with \(s\) independent forms has \(t\le s\). A counterexample to the conjecture needs failures at bounded degree for unbounded \(t\), so the test is the growth of the first failing degree with \(t\). form_locality.py computes the defect and the family's \(t\) for random families. With \(k=1\) (selectors), the first failing degree over all trials was 1 or 2 for \(t\le4\), \(s\le4\) (fl_*.json). Among general-position families (\(t=s\)), only some choices of forbidden values fail. That led to the canonical family.

The canonical family. The forbidden sets are \(B_i=\{y_i=0\}\) for \(1\le i\le s\) and \(B_0=\{y_1+\dots+y_s=c\}\). Any \(s\) of the linear parts span \(\mathbb F_3^s\), so \(t=s\). canonical_family.py scans all \(c\) for \(s\le5\) (canonical.json). The allowed set lies in \(\{1,2\}^s\), a Boolean cube under \(y=1+x\), and there \(\sum y=s+|x|\). Modulo the coordinate selectors' ideal, which is degree-compatible because \(\{1,2\}^s\) is a product, the defect becomes a question on the Boolean cube. It counts functions of degree \(\le e\) supported on a weight class \(|x|\equiv r\pmod3\), beyond the multiples \(1_{W_r}\cdot F_{e-2}\). weight_class.py computes that form for \(s\le9\) and all \(r\) (weight_class_2_9.json). It agrees with the direct computation at \(s\le5\). In every case the defect is 0 below \(e=\lceil s/2\rceil\) and exactly 1 at \(e=\lceil s/2\rceil\) for one class \(r\) (even \(s\)) or two (odd \(s\)), with a second 1 at \(s/2+1\) for even \(s\). Only the failure at \(\lceil s/2\rceil\) is proved below; "0 below" is a finite observation and is not registered.

The proposition

Proposition (pairing obstruction). Over \(\mathbb F_3\), let \(s\ge1\) and \(e=\lceil s/2\rceil\). Put \(w_0=e\) if \(s\) is even, and \(w_0\in\{e-1,e\}\) if \(s\) is odd, and \(c\equiv s+w_0\pmod3\). Consider the \(s+1\) selectors on \(\mathbb F_3^s\) with forbidden sets \(B_i=\{y_i=0\}\), \(1\le i\le s\), and \(B_0=\{y_1+\dots+y_s=c\}\). Every \(s\) of their linear parts are independent, and \(I_e(\bigcap_bU_b)\ne\sum_bI_e(U_b)\). The same holds on the occupancy slice for the selectors on \(\mathbb F_3\)-linear forms \(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_s\), \(\ell_1+\dots+\ell_s\) of the occupancies, whenever the slice's graded functions are free over the truncated algebra \(\mathbb F[\ell_1,\dots,\ell_s]/(\ell^3)\) in every degree \(\le e+2\). Consequently the form-space version of conj:t-wise-locality (with \(F=R\), where freeness holds in every degree) needs \(t_0(D,1,3)\ge2D+1\). The conjecture as stated, on the slice, needs \(t_0(D,1,3)\ge2D-3\) for every \(D\ge3\) for which some slice carries \(2D-4\) occupancy forms jointly free in degrees \(\le D\). The record has no proved instance of such a slice at every \(D\); conj:generic-form-freeness predicts one. For \(s=1\) the two forms coincide, a degenerate family. The construction is specific to \(p=3\) and is not claimed for other primes.

Proof. The degree filtration of \(R\), the functions on \(\mathbb F_3^s\) with exponents \(\le2\), is invariant under invertible affine coordinate changes, since these and their inverses have degree 1.

Step 0 (one selector). For a selector forbidding \(\{u=v\}\), \(u\) a nonzero linear form, use coordinates \((u,w_2,\dots,w_s)\). A function supported on the hyperplane is \((1-(u-v)^2)h(w)\), with \(h\) its restriction. This product is reduced, with top term \(u^2\) times the top of \(h\), so its degree is \(2+\deg h\). Hence \(I_e(U)=\chi\cdot R_{\le e-2}\), with \(\chi=1-(u-v)^2\), and \(I_e(U)=0\) for \(e<2\).

Step 1 (the element). On \(C'=\{1,2\}^s\) put \(y=1+x\), so \(x\in\{0,1\}^s\) and \(y_{2i-1}-y_{2i}=x_{2i-1}-x_{2i}\). For even \(s\) take \(m=e\) and \(\psi=1\). For odd \(s\) take \(m=e-1\), with \(\psi=2-y_s\ (=1-x_s)\) if \(w_0=e-1\) and \(\psi=y_s-1\ (=x_s)\) if \(w_0=e\). Put \(f=\prod_{i\le m}(y_{2i-1}-y_{2i})\cdot\psi\), a polynomial of degree \(e\). On \(C'\), \(f=P\psi\) with \(P=\prod_{i\le m}(x_{2i-1}-x_{2i})\). \(P\) is nonzero only when each pair has exactly one 1, and then \(\psi\ne0\) forces the integer weight \(|x|=w_0\). The allowed set is \(Z=\bigcap_bU_b=\{y\in C':\sum y\ne c\}=\{x:|x|\not\equiv w_0\pmod3\}\), since \(\sum y=s+|x|\). So \(f\) vanishes on \(Z\), and on the class \(|x|\equiv w_0\) it survives only on the integer level \(L=\{|x|=w_0\}\): \(f\in I_e(Z)\).

Step 2 (not in the sum). Suppose \(f=a_0+\sum_{i\ge1}a_i\) with \(a_b\in I_e(U_b)\). Each \(a_i\), \(i\ge1\), vanishes on \(U_i\supseteq C'\). So on \(C'\), \(f=a_0=\chi_0g\) with \(\deg g\le e-2\) (Step 0), \(\chi_0=1-(\sum y-c)^2\). On \(L\), \(\sum y=c\) and \(\chi_0=1\), so \(f=g\) on \(L\). Under \(y=1+x\) with \(x_i^2=x_i\), \(g|_{C'}\) is a multilinear function of \(x\) of degree \(\le e-2\). Define \(\mu(h)=\sum_{x\in L}P(x)h(x)\), built from \(P\) alone. For a monomial \(x_T\) with \(|T|\le e-2\le m-1\), some pair \(\{2i-1,2i\}\) misses \(T\). Swapping its two coordinates maps \(L\) to itself, fixes \(x_T\) and negates \(P\), so \(\mu(x_T)=-\mu(x_T)=0\) in characteristic 3, and \(\mu(g)=0\). But \(\mu(f)=\sum_LP^2\psi\) counts the \(x\in L\) with \(P(x)\ne0\) and \(\psi(x)=1\). There are \(2^m\) of them, and \(2^m\ne0\) in \(\mathbb F_3\). This contradiction proves \(f\notin\sum_bI_e(U_b)\).

Step 3 (independence). Any \(s\) of \(y_1,\dots,y_s,\ y_1+\dots+y_s\) span the linear forms on \(\mathbb F_3^s\).

Step 4 (slice). Let \(F\) be the slice's functions and \(R\) act through \(y=\ell(c)\). Suppose \(\operatorname{gr}F\) is free over \(\operatorname{gr}R=\mathbb F[y]/(y^3)\) in degrees \(\le n\), with \(n=e+2\). \(\operatorname{gr}F\) is spanned by 1 in degree 0, so a homogeneous basis \(\{v_j\}\) has exactly one element of degree 0, a nonzero multiple of 1, which can be rescaled to \(v_0=1\). Lift each \(v_j\) to \(\tilde v_j\in F_{\le\deg v_j}\), with \(\tilde v_0=1\). By induction on the degree, every \(h\in F_{\le d}\), \(d\le n\), is \(\sum_jr_j\tilde v_j\) with \(\deg r_j\le d-\deg v_j\), uniquely. For uniqueness: in a relation \(\sum_jr_j\tilde v_j=0\), let \(k=\max_j(\deg r_j+\deg v_j)\le n\). The symbol of \(r_j(\ell)\tilde v_j\) in \(\operatorname{gr}F_k\) is \(\sigma(r_j)v_j\) for the maximizing \(j\), so a nonzero relation among these symbols would contradict freeness in degree \(k\). Put \(\pi(h)=r_0\). Now take \(h\in F_{\le e}\) vanishing on \(X_{U_b}=\{c:\ell(c)\in U_b\}\). Then \(h=\chi_b(\ell)h\) as functions, where \(\chi_b\) is the indicator of \(B_b\) of degree 2. Writing \(h=\sum r_j\tilde v_j\), both \(\sum r_j\tilde v_j\) and \(\sum(\chi_br_j)\tilde v_j\) are expansions of the same element within degree \(e+2\). By uniqueness \(r_0=\chi_br_0\), so \(\pi(h)\in I_e(U_b)\). Also \(f(\ell)\in F_{\le e}\) vanishes on \(X_Z=\bigcap_bX_{U_b}\), and \(\pi(f(\ell))=f\). If \(f(\ell)=\sum_bh_b\) with \(h_b\in I_e(X_{U_b})\), then \(f=\sum_b\pi(h_b)\in\sum_bI_e(U_b)\), contradicting Step 2.

Consequence. The conjecture's hypothesis must hold for every subfamily of at most \(s\) clauses. Its forms are a subset of \(\{\ell_1,\dots,\ell_s,\sum\ell_i\}\) of at most \(s\) elements, linearly independent by Step 3. Joint freeness of \(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_s\) passes to them. First extend them to a basis of the span. \(\operatorname{gr}R\) is the associated graded ring of the functions on \(\mathbb F_3^s\), which does not depend on the choice of coordinates: \((\sum a_iy_i)^3=\sum a_i^3y_i^3\) in characteristic 3. Constant shifts do not change the symbols. So freeness over the truncated algebra of \(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_s\) is freeness over that of the new basis. Then restrict: \(\mathbb F[y]/(y^3)\) is free over the subalgebra of any subset of coordinates, so \(\operatorname{gr}F\), free over the former in degrees \(\le n\), is free over the latter in those degrees. In form space \(F=R\) is free in every degree. With \(s=2D\) the family has \(t=s\), and locality fails at \(d=D\), so \(t_0(D,1,3)\ge2D+1\) there. On the slice with freeness in degrees \(\le D\), Step 4 applies when \(e+2\le D\). With \(s=2D-4\ge2\), that is \(D\ge3\), \(e=D-2\) and \(t=2D-4\), so \(t_0(D,1,3)\ge2D-3\) whenever such a slice exists. \(\square\)

What this means

  • Locality is not refuted, but its threshold is at least \(2D+1\) clauses of independent forms in form space, and \(2D-3\) on the slice under the stated freeness condition. At the goal's parameters that means independence and joint freeness for subfamilies of about \(2D\approx75(K+1)\log_2n\) clauses at \(p=3\), with about \(2Dk\) forms. That is \(O((K+1)^2\log^2n)\), far below \(N=n\). So random families plausibly meet the hypothesis, and for adversarial families it is the robustness condition the budget would have to impose.
  • The obstruction is the slice's own structure: pair differences are the lowest-degree functions on a weight level that lower degrees cannot reproduce, the same functions that witness degree on the Johnson slice. A proof of the conjecture would have to show that, with \(t>2D\), such level-supported functions cannot arise from dependencies among more than \(t\) clauses below degree \(D\).

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: conj:t-wise-locality and the reduction in the locality review; lem:degreewise-gluing; the direct-sum and interaction-locality data. Claim searches (pairing, differences, weight level, slice; hyperplanes in general position, vanishing ideal of a union) found lem:quiet-members, which bounds degrees from below and says nothing about additivity, and obs:pencil-selector-syzygy, whose forms are dependent. Neither implies the proposition. The weight-class reduction was checked against the direct form-space computation at \(s\le5\), and every quoted defect is read from the result files. A fresh-context reviewer found no error in Steps 0 to 3. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • coordinate invariance of the filtration;
  • the exact support of \(f\), and \(\mu\) built from \(P\) alone;
  • the multilinear degree of \(g\);
  • \(p=3\) marked as essential, and \(s\ge2\) relaxed;
  • the freeness convention and the lifting argument made explicit in Step 4;
  • a proof that the conjecture's hypothesis holds for every subfamily.

It also questioned Step 4's reliance on the transfer lemma. Step 4 was rewritten to avoid that lemma: it uses the uniqueness of the free expansion two degrees higher. That weakens the slice consequence from \(2D+1\) to \(2D-3\), while the form-space bound stays \(2D+1\). The changes weaken the slice statement or make hypotheses explicit. The rewritten Step 4 is a new argument, so it was checked in a second focused pass. That pass found Step 4 correct and required further changes, all adopted: the rescaling of the degree-0 basis vector, the symbol computation in the uniqueness step, the coordinate independence of \(\operatorname{gr}R\), \(D\ge3\), the conjecture's scope for each bound, and the qualified summary bullet. These restrict scope, so no third pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • conj:t-wise-locality itself, with \(t_0\) at least \(2D+1\); the matching upper bound for the canonical family ("no failure below \(\lceil s/2\rceil\)") is only computed to \(s=9\).
  • Even with locality, row freeness of the allowed set's closure does not follow directly.

Covering obstruction: t-wise independent selectors that cover all but one point fail locality at degree 1 for every t, and density alone does not restore it

24 September 2026 · Working proof (covering obstruction) and a finite check · t-wise locality refuted as stated; cycle odd-prime-t-wise-proof. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The pairing obstruction left conj:t-wise-locality with a threshold of at least \(2D+1\), and all data then fitted a sharp form: in form space, selector locality at degree \(e\) whenever \(t\ge2e+1\). The cycle set out to prove that form. Before drafting it tested the form on \(t\)-wise independent families with many hyperplanes, the case the canonical family does not cover. That test ends the attempt: independence alone cannot give locality.

General statement. prop:covering-obstruction: over \(\mathbb F_3\), for every \(t\) there are selector families on \(\mathbb F_3^s\) with every \(t\) linear parts independent whose forbidden hyperplanes cover every point except 0. For every such family, degreewise locality fails at degree 1. So conj:t-wise-locality is false for every threshold in its form-space version. On the slice it is false at every \(D\ge1\), whenever a slice carries \(s\) occupancy forms jointly free in degrees \(\le\max(D,3)\), for the \(s\) the construction needs. ex:dense-dependent-locality-failure shows that density of the allowed set, without independence, does not give locality either: 51 of the 52 multi-clause dense families tested fail. Any corrected statement needs both hypotheses. At the sizes where form space is computable they cannot hold together.

The failure of the sharp form

sharp_locality.py builds \(t\)-wise independent families greedily. At \(s=4\), \(t=3\), three families of 8 to 10 selectors fail at degree 1, with allowed sets of 1, 2 and 4 points (sl_4_3_10_3_2_1.json). The failures come from covering, not from dependencies. A degree-1 function vanishing on the allowed set exists as soon as that set lies in an affine hyperplane. No single selector's ideal has elements of degree below 2.

The proposition

Proposition (covering obstruction). Over \(\mathbb F_3\), let \(t\ge1\). For every \(s\ge s_0(t)\) there are \(M=3s\) selectors on \(\mathbb F_3^s\), with forbidden hyperplanes \(H_b=\{v_b\cdot y=c_b\}\), \(c_b\in\{1,2\}\), such that every \(t\) of the \(v_b\) are linearly independent and \(Z=\bigcap_bU_b=\{0\}\). For every selector family with \(Z=\{0\}\), \(I_1(Z)\) is the \(s\)-dimensional space of linear forms, while \(\sum_bI_1(U_b)=0\). On the occupancy slice the selectors on \(v_b\cdot\ell\) fail at degree 1 with defect at least \(s\), whenever \(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_s\) are jointly free in degrees \(\le3\). Consequently the form-space version of conj:t-wise-locality fails for every \(t_0\) and every \(D\ge1\). The slice version fails for every \(t_0\) and every \(D\ge1\) at which some slice carries \(s\ge s_0(t_0)\) occupancy forms jointly free in degrees \(\le\max(D,3)\). A selector with \(v_b=0\) and \(c_b\ne0\) forbids nothing and has \(I_1(U_b)=0\) trivially. The construction uses \(p=3\) only in the numbers; it is stated for \(p=3\).

Proof. Degree 1. By Step 0 of the pairing obstruction, \(I_e(U_b)=\chi_b\cdot R_{\le e-2}\), which is 0 for \(e=1\). \(I_1(\{0\})\) consists of the affine functions vanishing at 0, the linear forms, of dimension \(s\ge1\). So the defect at degree 1 is \(s\).

Existence. Choose \(v_1,\dots,v_M\in\mathbb F_3^s\) uniformly and independently, and then \(c_b\in\{1,2\}\) uniformly and independently.

  1. Since \(t\le M\), a dependent set of at most \(t\) vectors, a zero vector included, lies in a dependent set of exactly \(t\). So it gives a nonzero coefficient vector supported on some \(t\)-set with \(\sum a_jv_j=0\). There are \(\binom Mt(3^t-1)<(3M)^t\) such coefficient vectors. For each, \(\sum a_jv_j=0\) has probability \(3^{-s}\), because some \(a_j\ne0\) and \(v_j\) is uniform. So \(t\)-wise independence fails with probability less than \((9s)^t3^{-s}\).
  2. \(0\notin H_b\) since \(c_b\ne0\). For \(y\ne0\), given the \(v_b\), \(y\) avoids \(H_b\) with probability 1 if \(v_b\cdot y=0\) and \(1/2\) otherwise. Over uniform \(v_b\), \(v_b\cdot y\) is uniform, so \(y\) avoids \(H_b\) with probability \(\tfrac13+\tfrac23\cdot\tfrac12=\tfrac23\), independently in \(b\). The expected number of nonzero points outside every \(H_b\) is \((3^s-1)(2/3)^{3s}<(8/9)^s\).

For \(s\ge s_0(t)=O(t\log t)\), \((9s)^t3^{-s}+(8/9)^s<1\). This forces \(s>2t\), so \(t\le s\) and \(t\le M\). By Markov's inequality applied to the count in (b), with positive probability both events hold. Then \(Z=\{0\}\) and the linear parts are \(t\)-wise independent.

Slice. Follow Step 4 of the pairing obstruction with \(e=1\), freeness in degrees \(\le3\), and the retraction \(\pi\) onto the coefficient of \(\tilde v_0=1\). \(\pi\) is linear because the expansion is unique. For a nonzero linear form \(f\), uniqueness gives \(\pi(f(\ell))=f\), with \(r_0=f\) and every other \(r_j=0\). And \(f(\ell)\) vanishes on \(X_Z\). If \(f(\ell)=\sum_bh_b\) with \(h_b\in I_1(X_{U_b})\), Step 4 gives \(\pi(h_b)\in I_1(U_b)=0\), so \(f=\pi(f(\ell))=0\), a contradiction. Applied to the \(s\)-dimensional space of linear forms, this gives defect at least \(s\) on the slice.

Hypothesis on the slice. Freeness in degree 1 makes \(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_s\) independent modulo constants on the slice, since the \(y_i\cdot1\) are independent in \(\operatorname{gr}F_1\). So independent \(v_b\) give independent linear parts \(v_b\cdot\ell\). The three steps of the pairing Consequence paragraph apply to any linearly independent set of combinations \(v_b\cdot\ell\): extend to a basis, use that \(\operatorname{gr}R\) is coordinate-free, and restrict to a subset of coordinates. So joint freeness of \(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_s\) in degrees \(\le\max(D,3)\) gives the conjecture's hypothesis through \(D\) for every subfamily of at most \(t\) clauses. The failure is at \(d=1\le D\). \(\square\)

Density alone does not suffice

Both obstructions have sparse allowed sets: \(\{0\}\) here, and density about \((2/3)^{s+1}\) for the pairing family. The budget's allowed set has density \(1-1/n\). So the cycle asked whether density alone gives locality. dense_locality.py draws random clauses of \(k\) forms on \(\mathbb F_3^s\) and keeps families whose allowed set has density at least 1/2. It imposes no independence and records each family's \(t\). It computes the defect at every \(e\le2s\), at \(s=4,5\), \(k=1,2,3\) and 1 to 10 clauses (dl_*.json). Of 57 families, the 5 single-clause ones are local, as they must be. Of the 52 families with at least two clauses, 51 fail, at degrees from 3 upward, all of them with dependent forms. This is ex:dense-dependent-locality-failure. So density does not replace independence.

Can it decide. A corrected conjecture would assume \(t\)-wise independence with \(t\) above \(2D\) together with a dense allowed set. In \(\mathbb F_3^s\) with \(s\le5\), independence of more than two clauses of width \(k\ge2\) is impossible. So no family in computable form space meets both hypotheses at once, and no such check was run.

What this means

  • conj:t-wise-locality as stated is false in form space for every threshold, and on the slice at every \(D\) under a freeness condition in degrees \(\le\max(D,3)\) that conj:generic-form-freeness predicts for moderate \(s\). The failure is a covering failure. It needs an allowed set concentrated in a hyperplane, which the budget's dense allowed set excludes.
  • The two recorded obstructions, pairing and covering, both use sparse allowed sets. The dense families that fail all have dependent forms. A statement true for the budget would need independence and density together. It would be a Helly-type statement for degree-\(D\) moments: a functional representable avoiding every small subfamily's forbidden sets is representable avoiding all of them. That combination is beyond computation in form space, so it would have to be proved.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: conj:t-wise-locality's exact statement, and Steps 0 and 4 and the Consequence paragraph of the pairing obstruction. The claim searches of the pairing cycle (general position, vanishing ideal of a union) cover the objects here. The counts are read from the result files by script. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed the probability bounds, the independence across clauses and the degree-1 defect. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the slice proviso corrected to freeness in degrees \(\le\max(D,3)\), which yields failure at every \(D\ge1\) and replaces a misscoped "\(D\ge3\)";
  • the slice step written out for \(e=1\) instead of cited as verbatim;
  • independence modulo constants from degree-1 freeness;
  • the general form of the Consequence steps;
  • a clean count in (a), \(s>2t\), and Markov's inequality named;
  • the trivial case \(v_b=0\).

The corrections rescope and make explicit; the only strengthening, a defect of at least \(s\) on the slice, follows from the same argument. No further pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • A locality statement using both independence and density, or a different route to row freeness of the dense allowed set's closure.
