Route review: the locality sub-line needs independence between members, not clauses, and dependencies surface at about half their combined degree

24 September 2026 · Route review with a finite check · The locality sub-line after the pairing and covering obstructions; cycle odd-prime-locality-review. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

General statement. The line's claim is still that the budget's constraints, closed under their vanishing polynomials, leave the weak base without a refutation of degree \(D\). Via thm:global-closure-gluing this needs row freeness of the closure of the budget's dense allowed set. The locality sub-line tried to reduce that closure to single clauses. prop:pairing-obstruction and prop:covering-obstruction refuted conj:t-wise-locality as stated: independence alone fails by covering, and density alone fails with dependent forms. The review's falsification attempt, ex:combined-locality-calibration, tests both hypotheses together at the smallest form space that allows them. There, a dependency among \(t+1\) clauses of width \(k\) breaks locality at degree 7 or 8, with \(t=3\), \(k=2\), about half the combined degree \((t+1)(p-1)k=16\) of the dependent clauses.

Where the sub-line stands

Since the locality review:

  • the pairing obstruction proved that general-position selectors fail at degree \(\lceil s/2\rceil\);
  • the covering obstruction proved that \(t\)-wise independent selectors covering all but one point fail at degree 1 for every \(t\);
  • dense families with dependent forms fail at degrees 3 and above (ex:dense-dependent-locality-failure).

Proved and still valid: lem:degreewise-gluing, and the reduction of locality to form space when all forms are jointly free.

What the goal needs

At \(p=3\), \(D=(4p-1)(p-1)k\), so a single clause's indicator already has degree \((p-1)k=D/11\). If locality fails only at about half the combined degree of a dependent set, then a dependency among \(t+1\) clauses stays invisible below \(D\) once \((t+1)(p-1)k/2>D\), that is, \(t+1>2(4p-1)=22\). The budget needs no bound on the number of clauses, only this local independence. That is a much weaker requirement than the \(t>2D\) that the selector obstructions suggest. The reason is that \(D\) counts in units of single-form degree, while the dependencies cost whole clause indicators.

Falsification attempt

Can it decide. Independence of \(t\) clauses of width \(k\) needs \(s\ge tk\), and the forbidden union should stay below half the space. The smallest case with a dependent family is \(s=6\), \(k=2\), \(t=3\), with 4 or 5 clauses. Its function space has dimension \(3^6=729\), which is computable. combined_locality.py draws such families, checks \(t\)-wise independence, and computes the defect at every \(e\le12\). The runs of 4 and 5 clauses reached their 115-second limit; each family's result is saved as it finishes, and only completed families are counted.

Files: cl_*.json. This is ex:combined-locality-calibration. The control is local, as the product argument requires. Every dependent family fails, first at degree 8 for four clauses and at degree 7 for five. That is about half the combined degree \(4\cdot4=16\) of four dependent clauses, and below the conjecture's scope, \(t=3\) against \(D\ge7\). So nothing recorded is refuted. What the check calibrates is where a dependency first appears.

The budget's clauses are not independent

Two clauses sharing a form are already dependent. The logarithmic-prefix reduction's clauses are adversarial, and many clauses can lie in one small span. So clause-level \(t\)-wise independence is the wrong hypothesis. The natural unit is the member of lem:quiet-members: a subfamily whose forms lie in one span. By that lemma, a member's allowed set in its span has no vanishing function below degree \((p-1)\log_p(1/(m(1-1/p)^k))\). A locality statement for the budget would group clauses into members and require independence between the members' spans, not between clauses. It would also require each member's own closure to be handled in its span's form space, where joint freeness is plausible because a member's span is small. This is the shape of conj:component-hypothesis, which groups clauses along bounded circuits. Its version with local freeness as injectivity was refuted by a pair that is not jointly free. With the members' spans jointly free, that counterexample is excluded, as for conj:t-wise-locality.

Assessment of the sub-line

Four cycles on locality produced one general lemma and two obstructions, all proved and reviewed. They identified what a true statement must assume: independence and sparsity together, at the level of members. The calibration, at one size only, suggests the required independence is modest, about \(2(4p-1)\) members. So the sub-line is not dead. But every positive statement so far holds only where all forms are jointly free, which is the regime of the recorded seeded and block results, and no proof technique for the dependent-but-sparse regime is in hand. The decisive statement, member locality with jointly free small spans, has not been formulated precisely. The sub-line is coherent and sharply bounded, with no mechanism yet for its central claim.

The highest-risk item and the next step

The highest-risk item is a locality statement at member level that the budget's adversarial clauses satisfy. Next step, on route item odd-prime-clause-transfer: formulate member locality precisely. Group the budget's clauses into members by spans, require the members' spans to be \(t\)-wise independent with \(t\) of order \(2(4p-1)\) and each span jointly free through \(D\). Then attempt a proof that locality holds below degree \((t+1)\) times half the least member indicator degree. Start from the fully independent case, which the product argument proves, and add one dependency at a time. That case, a single dependency among \(t+1\) spans, is the one ex:combined-locality-calibration measures.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: conj:t-wise-locality, prop:pairing-obstruction, prop:covering-obstruction, ex:dense-dependent-locality-failure, lem:quiet-members, conj:component-hypothesis and its counterexample. The calibration's independence is asserted in code, the control behaves as the product argument requires, and all counts are read from the result files. The review adds a finite check and no proof, so no reviewer pass was run.

Single-dependency threshold: one dependency among t+1 selectors is invisible exactly below degree ⌈t/2⌉

24 September 2026 · Working proof (single-dependency threshold) · The base case of member locality, for selectors over F_3; cycle odd-prime-member-locality. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The locality line review asked for member locality, starting from its base case: one linear dependency among \(t+1\) members, every \(t\) of them independent. The missing implication is the degree below which such a dependency cannot create a function vanishing on the allowed set that the single members' ideals do not already give. The review's calibration, and the pairing obstruction for selectors, measured that degree. This cycle proves it for selectors over \(\mathbb F_3\).

General statement. thm:single-dependency-threshold: over \(\mathbb F_3\), let \(t+1\) selectors have linear parts with exactly one dependency, and every \(t\) of them independent. Then degreewise locality holds in every degree \(e<\lceil t/2\rceil\), for all forbidden values, and it fails at \(e=\lceil t/2\rceil\) for suitable values by prop:pairing-obstruction. So the threshold is exactly \(\lceil t/2\rceil\). The proof reduces the question to the Boolean cube, as in the pairing obstruction. It then uses lem:pair-seed-decomposition: \(\mathbb F_3[x_1,\dots,x_s]/(x_i^2)\) is a free module over \(\mathbb F_3[e_1]/(e_1^3)\) plus one summand of dimension at most 2, in degree \(\lceil s/2\rceil\). This refines lem:free-seed-tensor at \(p=3\).

The decomposition

Put \(\Lambda=\mathbb F_3[y]/(y^3)\), graded with \(y\) in degree 1, and give it the coproduct \(y\mapsto y\otimes1+1\otimes y\). This respects \(y^3=0\) in characteristic 3, since \((y\otimes1+1\otimes y)^3=y^3\otimes1+1\otimes y^3\). Let \(A_s=\mathbb F_3[x_1,\dots,x_s]/(x_i^2)\), graded, with \(y\) acting as \(e_1=x_1+\dots+x_s\). Then \(A_{s+s'}=A_s\otimes A_{s'}\) with \(y\) acting diagonally. Write \(J_a\) for the Jordan block \(\Lambda/(y^a)\), and \([m]\) for a shift putting its lowest degree at \(m\).

Lemma (pair-seed decomposition). As graded \(\Lambda\)-modules, \(A_s\cong P_s\oplus N_s\), with \(P_s\) graded free, \(N_{2m}=J_1[m]\) and \(N_{2m+1}=J_2[m]\). Consequently \(\ker(e_1\colon A_{s,d}\to A_{s,d+1})=e_1^2A_{s,d-2}\) for every \(d\ne\lceil s/2\rceil\), and this fails at \(d=\lceil s/2\rceil\).

Proof. \(A_1=J_2[0]\), with basis \(1,x\). Three small products suffice.

  • \(J_1[a]\otimes J_2=J_2[a]\).
  • \(J_2\otimes J_2\cong\Lambda\oplus J_1[1]\). This is \(A_2\): \(e_1\cdot1=x_1+x_2\) and \(e_1^2\cdot1=2x_1x_2\ne0\), so \(\Lambda\cdot1\) has dimension 3. \(x_1-x_2\) spans a complement in degree 1, killed by \(e_1\) since \((x_1+x_2)(x_1-x_2)=x_1^2-x_2^2=0\).
  • \(\Lambda\otimes J_2\cong\Lambda\oplus\Lambda[1]\). With \(Y=y\otimes1+1\otimes y\) and \(J_2\) spanned by \(1,x\): \(Y(1\otimes1)=y\otimes1+1\otimes x\), \(Y^2(1\otimes1)=y^2\otimes1+2y\otimes x\), \(Y(1\otimes x)=y\otimes x\) and \(Y^2(1\otimes x)=y^2\otimes x\). These six vectors span the 6-dimensional space, so \(1\otimes1\) and \(1\otimes x\) are free generators.

Induction on \(s\), using \(A_{s+1}=A_s\otimes J_2\): \(P_s\otimes J_2\) is free by the third item, applied summand by summand. \(N_{2m}\otimes J_2=J_2[m]=N_{2m+1}\) by the first. \(N_{2m+1}\otimes J_2=(\Lambda\oplus J_1[1])[m]\) is \(\Lambda[m]\oplus N_{2m+2}\) by the second. For the consequence: a free module satisfies \(\ker y=y^2(\cdot)\) in every degree. \(J_1[m]\) violates it only in degree \(m\). \(J_2[m]\), spanned by \(v\) in degree \(m\) and \(yv\) in degree \(m+1\), has \(\ker y\) spanned by \(yv\), while \(y^2(\cdot)=0\), so it violates it only in degree \(m+1\). In both cases that degree is \(\lceil s/2\rceil\). \(\square\)

lem:free-seed-tensor, with \(W=A_2\), gives a free part plus a summand in degrees \(\ge\lfloor s/2\rfloor\). The lemma identifies that summand up to isomorphism. For odd \(s=2m+1\) the summand \(J_2[m]\) still starts in degree \(m\), but \(\ker e_1=e_1^2(\cdot)\) now holds in degree \(\lfloor s/2\rfloor=m\) as well. That is the degree the theorem below needs.

The theorem

Theorem (single-dependency threshold). Over \(\mathbb F_3\), let \(t\ge1\) and let \(L_1,\dots,L_{t+1}\) be affine forms on \(\mathbb F_3^{s'}\) whose linear parts span a space of dimension \(t\), with every \(t\) of them independent. Given rank \(t\), this is equivalent to the unique dependency having every coefficient nonzero. For any values \(\alpha_b\), put \(U_b=\{L_b\ne\alpha_b\}\). Then \(I_e(\bigcap_bU_b)=\sum_bI_e(U_b)\) for every \(e<\lceil t/2\rceil\). For suitable \(\alpha\) this fails at \(e=\lceil t/2\rceil\).

Proof. Every step below is an invertible affine change of coordinates, which preserves the degree filtration, or a product decomposition.

Step 1 (normal form). The dependency is \(\sum_b\lambda_bL_b^{\mathrm{lin}}=0\) with every \(\lambda_b\ne0\), since every \(t\) linear parts are independent. Take \(y_b=\lambda_b(L_b-\alpha_b)\) for \(b\le t\), and extend by coordinates \(z\) to a coordinate system. Then \(U_b=\{y_b\ne0\}\) for \(b\le t\), and \(U_{t+1}=\{y_1+\dots+y_t\ne c\}\), where \(c\) runs over all of \(\mathbb F_3\) as \(\alpha_{t+1}\) varies. No set depends on \(z\).

Step 2 (free coordinates). All sets have the form \(X\times\mathbb F_3^{z}\), and \(R=R_y\otimes R_z\) with the tensor filtration. By the product argument of the locality review, \(I_e(X\times\mathbb F_3^z)=\sum_jI_j(X)\otimes(R_z)_{\le e-j}\), and the same holds for sums of such ideals. Put \(\mathrm{def}_j=\dim I_j(\bigcap_bX_b)-\dim\sum_bI_j(X_b)\) in \(y\)-space. It is \(\ge0\), since the sum lies in the ideal of the intersection. The defect in degree \(e\) is then \(\sum_j\mathrm{def}_j\cdot\dim\operatorname{gr}_{e-j}R_z\). Since \(\dim\operatorname{gr}_0R_z=1\) and all terms are \(\ge0\), it vanishes for all \(e<\tau\) if and only if \(\mathrm{def}_e=0\) for all \(e<\tau\), and it is positive at \(e\) whenever \(\mathrm{def}_e>0\). Hence take \(s'=t\), in both directions.

Step 3 (reduction to the cube). \(C'=\bigcap_{b\le t}U_b=\{1,2\}^t\) is a product. In each coordinate the filtration-compatible basis \(\{1,y_b,1-y_b^2\}\) is adapted to \(I(U_b)\), and \(I_e(U_b)=(1-y_b^2)R_{\le e-2}\). So the product argument gives \(\sum_{b\le t}I_e(U_b)=I_e(C')\). Put \(y=1+x\) on \(C'\), with \(x\in\{0,1\}^t\). Restriction \(\pi\) to \(C'\) maps \(R_{\le e}\) onto the multilinear functions of \(x\) of degree \(\le e\), \(F_{\le e}(C')\). By Step 0 of the pairing obstruction, \(I_e(U_{t+1})=\chi R_{\le e-2}\) with \(\chi=1-(\sum y-c)^2\). On \(C'\), \(\sum y=t+|x|\), so \(\pi(\chi)=\chi_W:=1-(e_1-r)^2\), the indicator of \(W_r=\{|x|\equiv r\}\), with \(r=c-t\). Here \(e_1=\sum x_i\) is read mod 3. Since \(I_e(C')=\ker\pi\cap R_{\le e}\) lies in both sides, locality at \(e\) holds if and only if every \(f\in F_{\le e}(C')\) supported on \(W_r\) lies in \(\chi_WF_{\le e-2}(C')\).

Step 4 (descent). Identify \(\operatorname{gr}F(C')\) with \(A_t\): the multilinear monomials of degree \(d\) give a basis of \(\operatorname{gr}_d\). Let \(f\in F_{\le d}(C')\) be supported on \(W_r\), with \(d\le e<\lceil t/2\rceil\) and degree-\(d\) part \(\sigma_d(f)\in A_{t,d}\). Since \(e_1-r\) vanishes on \(W_r\), \((e_1-r)f=0\). Its degree-\((d+1)\) part is \(e_1\sigma_d(f)\), because reducing \(x_i^2\) to \(x_i\) lowers degree. So \(e_1\sigma_d(f)=0\), and by the lemma, since \(d\ne\lceil t/2\rceil\), \(\sigma_d(f)=e_1^2a\) with \(a\in A_{t,d-2}\); here \(a=0\) if \(d<2\). Lift \(a\) to \(h\in F_{\le d-2}(C')\). The degree-2 part of \(\chi_W\) is \(-e_1^2\), so the degree-\(d\) part of \(\chi_Wh\) is \(-e_1^2a\). Then \(f+\chi_Wh\) is supported on \(W_r\) and has degree \(\le d-1\). By induction on \(d\) it lies in \(\chi_WF_{\le d-3}(C')\), so \(f\in\chi_WF_{\le d-2}(C')\). The base \(d<0\) is \(f=0\). \(\square\)

Consistency. The pairing cycle computed the weight-class defect for \(s\le9\) and every \(r\). It found 0 below \(\lceil s/2\rceil\) and a failure at \(\lceil s/2\rceil\) for some \(r\) (weight_class_2_9.json), as the theorem and the pairing obstruction predict.

The failure half. By Step 1, \(c\) can be chosen as \(t+w_0\), which gives the canonical family of prop:pairing-obstruction, stated there for every \(s\ge1\). That proposition gives a positive defect at \(\lceil t/2\rceil\) in \(y\)-space. For \(t=1\) directly: if \(c\ne0\), the intersection is the single value \(y_1=\) the remaining element of \(\{1,2\}\), so \(y_1\) minus that value lies in \(I_1\), while \(I_1(U_b)=0\). By Step 2 the failure persists in the full space.

What this means

  • For selectors the base case of member locality is settled. One dependency among \(t+1\) selectors is invisible exactly below \(\lceil t/2\rceil\). The mechanism is the only non-free summand of the Boolean algebra over its full sum. The pairing obstruction shows that the pair-difference product represents it; the lemma fixes the summand only up to isomorphism.
  • For clauses of width \(k\), the review's calibration (one dependency among 4 clauses of width 2 first visible at degree 8) suggests the same mechanism with each dependent clause contributing its extra indicator degree. The general case needs the analog of Step 3 with the other forms of each clause, where the product structure is no longer available. That is the next step.
  • The threshold grows linearly in the number of dependent members, as the budget needs. A dependency among \(t+1\) selector members is invisible in every degree \(\le D\) once \(\lceil t/2\rceil>D\). For wide members the calibration suggests far fewer.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: prop:pairing-obstruction (statement, Step 0 and the canonical family), the product argument of the locality review, lem:free-seed-tensor, cor:slice-saturation and the pairing cycle's weight-class data. Claim search (free seed, block of holes, free over the sum) found lem:free-seed-tensor, which the lemma refines at \(p=3\), and no statement of the theorem. The theorem's prediction matches the recorded weight-class data. A fresh-context reviewer found no error in the lemma or the theorem. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the failure half derived for general forms, through the choice of \(c\) and both directions of Step 2, with the case \(t=1\) checked directly;
  • the defect's nonnegativity and \(\dim\operatorname{gr}_0R_z=1\) stated in Step 2;
  • the adapted basis cited in Step 3;
  • the comparison with lem:free-seed-tensor corrected;
  • the claim that the pair-difference product is the non-free summand weakened;
  • the hypothesis stated as nonzero dependency coefficients.

The changes add justification and weaken one remark, so no further pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • The single-dependency threshold for clauses of width \(k\ge2\), and then several dependencies at once, the case of five clauses in the calibration, which failed a degree earlier.
  • Member locality for the budget, and from it row freeness of the closure.

Wide dependency threshold: each extra form of a dependent clause delays the dependency by exactly p−1 degrees

24 September 2026 · Working proof (wide dependency threshold) · Single dependencies among clauses of any widths over F_3; cycle odd-prime-wide-dependency. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The single-dependency threshold settled one dependency among \(t+1\) selectors. The budget's clauses have width \(k\) of order \(\log n\). The missing implication is the degree below which one dependency among \(t+1\) such clauses stays invisible. That number decides how much independence member locality must ask of the budget.

General statement. thm:wide-dependency-threshold: over \(\mathbb F_3\), let clauses \(b=1,\dots,t+1\) of widths \(k_b\) forbid one point each. Suppose their combined linear parts have exactly one dependency and every \(t\) clauses have independent combined linear parts. Then degreewise locality holds in every degree \(e<\lceil t/2\rceil+2\sum_b(k_b-1)\), for all forbidden points, and fails at that degree for suitable points. The proof is lem:peeling, which holds over any \(\mathbb F_p\). Removing a form that is a coordinate occurring in no other clause lowers the locality question by exactly \(p-1\) degrees. This holds in both directions whenever the remaining clauses are local in the relevant degrees, for example point-forbidding clauses with jointly independent forms. At \(p=3\) and the budget's degree \(D=22k\), the threshold \(\tau\) exceeds \(D\) when \(t+1\ge12\) and \(k\ge10\). So such a dependency, with no other clauses present, is invisible in every degree \(\le D\).

The peeling lemma

Setting: \(R\) is the functions on \(\mathbb F_p^s\) with the degree filtration. A clause forbids one point of its forms, and \(I_e\), \(U_c\), locality at degree \(e\) are as in lem:degreewise-gluing. Let \(F\) be a family of clauses, and let \(w\) be a coordinate that occurs in exactly one clause \(b\), whose forbidden set is a product \(\{w=0\}\times B'_b\). Let \(R'\) be the functions of the other coordinates. \(F'\) is \(F\) with \(w\) removed from clause \(b\), so clause \(b\) forbids \(B'_b\), and \(F\setminus b\) is \(F\) without clause \(b\). Both are families on the coordinates other than \(w\), and their locality is taken in \(R'\).

Lemma (peeling). If \(F\) is local at degree \(e\), then \(F'\) is local at degree \(e-(p-1)\). Conversely, if \(F'\) is local at degree \(e-(p-1)\) and \(F\setminus b\) is local in degrees \(e-p+2,\dots,e\), then \(F\) is local at degree \(e\). For \(e<p-1\) the condition on \(F'\) holds trivially.

Proof. Write \(R=R'\otimes R_w\), where \(R'\) is the functions of the other coordinates. In \(R_w\) take the filtration-compatible basis \(1,w,\dots,w^{p-2},\delta\), with \(\delta=1-w^{p-1}\) the indicator of \(w=0\) of degree \(p-1\). Every \(g\in R_{\le e}\) is uniquely \(\sum_{i<p-1}A_iw^i+C\delta\), with \(A_i\in R'_{\le e-i}\) and \(C\in R'_{\le e-p+1}\). At \(w=0\), \(g=A_0+C\). At each of the \(p-1\) nonzero values of \(w\), \(g=\sum_iA_iw^i\). This is a Vandermonde system in the \(A_i\), invertible over the \(p-1\) distinct nonzero values. Over \(w\ne0\), clause \(b\) is inactive and the allowed set of \(F\) is \(Z(F\setminus b)\). Over \(w=0\) it is \(Z(F')\), and \(Z(F')\subseteq Z(F\setminus b)\).

(\(\Leftarrow\)) Let \(f\in I_e(Z(F))\). By the Vandermonde system, every \(A_i\) vanishes on \(Z(F\setminus b)\). Locality of \(F\setminus b\) in degrees \(e-i\), \(i<p-1\), gives \(A_i=\sum_{c\ne b}a_{c,i}\) with \(a_{c,i}\in I_{e-i}(U_c)\). Each \(a_{c,i}w^i\) lies in \(I_e(U_c)\), since \(U_c\) does not involve \(w\). \(A_0+C\) vanishes on \(Z(F')\) and so does \(A_0\), so \(C\in I_{e-p+1}(Z(F'))\). Locality of \(F'\) gives \(C=\sum_{c\ne b}c_c+c'_b\), with \(c_c\in I_{e-p+1}(U_c)\) and \(c'_b\) vanishing on the narrowed clause's allowed set \(U'_b\). Then \(c_c\delta\in I_e(U_c)\). And \(c'_b\delta\in I_e(U_b)\): \(U_b\) is \(U'_b\) together with \(\{w\ne0\}\), where \(c'_b=0\) and \(\delta=0\) respectively. So \(f\in\sum_cI_e(U_c)\).

(\(\Rightarrow\)) This direction uses no hypothesis on \(F\setminus b\). Let \(C\in I_{e-p+1}(Z(F'))\) be outside \(\sum_cI_{e-p+1}(U'_c)\), where \(U'_c=U_c\) for \(c\ne b\). Then \(f=C\delta\in R_{\le e}\) vanishes on \(Z(F)\). Suppose \(f=\sum_ca_c\) with \(a_c\in I_e(U_c)\), and take \(\delta\)-coefficients, a linear map by uniqueness of the expansion. For \(c\ne b\), \(a_c\) vanishes on \(U_c\times\mathbb F_p\). By the Vandermonde system its \(A\)-coefficients vanish on \(U_c\), and then its \(\delta\)-coefficient \(C_c\) does too, from the value at \(w=0\). For \(a_b\), vanishing on \(\{w\ne0\}\) forces its \(A\)-coefficients to be 0, and then its \(C_b\) vanishes on \(U'_b\). So \(C=\sum C_c\in\sum_cI_{e-p+1}(U'_c)\), a contradiction. \(\square\)

The theorem

Theorem (wide dependency threshold). Over \(\mathbb F_3\), let \(t\ge1\) and let clause \(b\), \(1\le b\le t+1\), forbid \(\{\ell_b=\alpha_b\}\) for \(k_b\) affine forms \(\ell_b\). Suppose the \(\sum_bk_b\) linear parts have rank \(\sum_bk_b-1\), and those of every \(t\) clauses are independent. This implies independence within each clause, and, given the rank, it is equivalent to the unique dependency having a nonzero component \(\mu_b\) in every clause. \(p=3\) enters only through the base threshold and through \(p-1=2\) in \(\tau\). Put \(\tau=\lceil t/2\rceil+2\sum_b(k_b-1)\). Then \(I_e(\bigcap_bU_b)=\sum_bI_e(U_b)\) for every \(e<\tau\) and all \(\alpha\), and this fails at \(e=\tau\) for suitable \(\alpha\).

Proof. Normal form. The dependency is \(\sum_b\mu_b=0\), where \(\mu_b\) is a linear combination of clause \(b\)'s linear parts. Every \(\mu_b\ne0\), since every \(t\) clauses are independent. Extend \(\mu_b\) to a basis \(\mu_b,\nu_{b,1},\dots,\nu_{b,k_b-1}\) of clause \(b\)'s span. The only relation among all these forms is \(\sum_b\mu_b=0\). So \(y_b=\mu_b-(\text{const})\) for \(b\le t\), together with all \(w_{b,j}=\nu_{b,j}-(\text{const})\), extended by free coordinates \(z\), is a coordinate system. Clause \(b\)'s forbidden point is an invertible affine image of \(\{\ell_b=\alpha_b\}\). With the constants chosen, clause \(b\le t\) forbids \(\{y_b=0,\ w_b=0\}\), and clause \(t+1\) forbids \(\{y_1+\dots+y_t=c,\ w_{t+1}=0\}\). Here \(c\) runs over \(\mathbb F_3\) as \(\alpha_{t+1}\) varies. The free coordinates \(z\) are kept: the lemma allows arbitrary other coordinates, and the single-dependency threshold covers selector families in any ambient dimension.

Peeling. Remove the coordinates \(w_{b,j}\) one at a time with the lemma, in the ring of the coordinates not yet removed. At each stage the family without the clause being narrowed consists of \(t\) clauses. Their forms are independent: the \(y_c\) for \(c\le t\), \(c\ne b\), and \(\sum y\) if \(b\ne t+1\), together with their remaining \(w\)'s. After a linear change they are disjoint coordinate blocks, each clause forbidding one point of its block. Such a family is local in every degree by the product argument. In each block take the monomials in the shifted coordinates, with the top monomial replaced by the point indicator \(\delta_c\). The transition from monomials is triangular in degree, so the tensor basis is filtration-compatible. The non-\(\delta\) elements restrict to a basis of the functions on the block minus its point. So a function of degree \(\le e\) vanishing on the product of these sets is a sum of basis tensors of degree \(\le e\), each containing some \(\delta_c\) and hence lying in \(I_e(U_c)\). After \(\sum_b(k_b-1)\) steps, locality at degree \(e\) is equivalent to locality at degree \(e-2\sum_b(k_b-1)\) of the selector family, the canonical family of the single-dependency threshold. That family is local below \(\lceil t/2\rceil\) for every \(c\), and fails at \(\lceil t/2\rceil\) for \(c=t+w_0\), in any ambient dimension. So the wide family is local for \(e<\tau\) and fails at \(\tau\). \(\square\)

Consistency. wide_single.py computes the defect in normal form for widths \((2,1,1)\), \((1,1,2)\), \((2,2,1)\), \((2,2,2)\) with \(t=2\), and \((1,1,1,2)\) with \(t=3\) (wide_single.json). It finds 0 below \(\tau\) and a defect of 1 at \(\tau\) when \(c=t+w_0\), and no defect at \(\tau\) for \(t=3\), \(c=0\), where no \(w_0\) matches.

What this means

  • For single dependencies the member-locality threshold is now exact over \(\mathbb F_3\) at every width. The cost of a dependency is \(\lceil t/2\rceil\) from the dependent forms, plus \(p-1\) for every other form of every dependent clause.
  • At the budget's width \(k\), with \(D=(4p-1)(p-1)k=22k\), a family of exactly \(t+1\) clauses of width \(k\) with one dependency, every \(t\) independent and no other clauses present, is local in every degree \(\le D\) once \(\tau>D\). For \(t+1=12\) that holds when \(k\ge10\); for large \(k\) the condition approaches \(t+1>11\). So a single such dependency needs about a dozen clauses to be harmless. Several dependencies, and dependencies inside larger families, are not covered.
  • The calibration families had a two-dimensional space of dependencies among 4 clauses of width 2, and failed at degree 8. The single-dependency prediction for 4 clauses of width 2 is \(2+8=10\). So several dependencies can surface earlier, and the next case is a dependency space of dimension more than one.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: thm:single-dependency-threshold (statement, normal form, Step 2), prop:pairing-obstruction's canonical family, the product argument, and ex:combined-locality-calibration. The consistency runs agree with \(\tau\) in every case. A fresh-context reviewer found no gap in the lemma or the chain of equivalences. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the numeric boundary corrected: the draft's \(k\ge12\) gave equality at \(t+1=12\), now \(\tau>D\) for \(t+1\ge12\), \(k\ge10\);
  • the rings of \(F'\) and \(F\setminus b\) stated;
  • the exact degrees in which \(F\setminus b\) is used, and that one direction needs no hypothesis;
  • the product form of clause \(b\)'s forbidden set;
  • the peeling principle's wording;
  • the free coordinates kept rather than removed;
  • the product argument written out;
  • notation, the implied hypothesis, and the role of \(p=3\);
  • the overreach about dozens of clauses qualified.

The changes correct one numeric claim and weaken or make precise the rest, so no further pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • Dependency spaces of dimension \(\ge2\), and families with many overlapping dependencies, as in the budget.
  • From member locality to row freeness of the closure.

Several dependencies: a rank formula fits every measured threshold, its failure half is proved for all families, and clauses on one span fail at 2k−1

24 September 2026 · Working proof (point extension, failure half), conjecture and finite check · Dependency spaces of dimension at least 2 over F_3; cycle odd-prime-double-dependency. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The wide dependency threshold is exact for one dependency. The calibration showed that two dependencies among 4 clauses surface at degree 8, below the single-dependency value 10. The missing implication is the threshold for a dependency space of dimension \(r\ge2\). The cycle measures it on the configurations computable in form space, looks for a formula and proves what it can.

General statement. conj:rank-threshold: over \(\mathbb F_3\), for \(t+1\) point-forbidding clauses with every \(t\) of them independent and combined linear parts of rank \(\rho<\sum_bk_b\) (at least one dependency), degreewise locality holds below \(\tau=\lceil t/2\rceil+2(\rho-t)\) for every forbidden point, and fails at \(\tau\) for some. It is proved for \(r=1\) (thm:wide-dependency-threshold). It matches every measured case with \(r=2,3\) (ex:double-dependency-thresholds), all of which have \(r=\max_bk_b\), so \(1<r<\max_bk_b\) is untested. Its failure half is proved for every family in scope (prop:rank-threshold-failure). The proof is lem:point-extension, over any finite field. Taking the AND of a family with any family whose forbidden sets share a point, in \(m\) coordinates, delays a failure by at most \((p-1)m\). The forbidden sets of the first family may be arbitrary. Two clauses on the same span fail exactly at degree \(2k-1\), far below \(D=22k\). That sharpens the value \(4k-3\) that the wide threshold gives for two clauses sharing one direction.

The measurements

Can it decide. A dependency space of dimension \(r\) among \(t+1\) clauses, every \(t\) independent, needs \(\rho=\sum_bk_b-r\ge t\max_bk_b\). The computable sizes are \(\rho\le6\), which gives width 2 with \(t\le3\) and width 3 with \(t\le2\). The inequality \(\sum_bk_b-r\ge t\max_bk_b\) forces \(r\le1\) at width 1, so selector families give no data for \(r\ge2\).

  • double_base.py: random families of 3 clauses of width 2 on \(\mathbb F_3^4\), with every 2 independent and rank 4 (\(r=2\)). It takes the minimum over the forbidden values of the two non-normalized forms. The first failure is at degree 5 in all 3 families (db_4_2_3_3_5_2.json). Four selectors on \(\mathbb F_3^2\) can cover the plane, and fail at degree 0 (db_2_1_4_3_1_2.json).
  • With every \(t\) clauses independent, a family of \(t+1\) clauses of width \(r\) and rank \(rt\) is, after affine coordinate changes in each clause, the AND of \(r\) copies of the canonical selector family: clause \(b\) forbids \(y^{(j)}_b=0\) in every copy, and clause \(t+1\) forbids \(\sum_iy^{(j)}_i=c_j\) in every copy. and_family.py computes that normal form. \(t=2,r=2\): first failure at 5 for \(c=(0,0)\), none through 5 for \((1,0),(2,0),(0,1)\). \(t=2,r=3\): 9 for \((0,0,0)\), none through 9 for \((1,0,0),(1,1,1)\). \(t=3,r=2\): 8 for \((1,0)\) (and_*.json). The calibration's 4 clauses of width 2 have \(t=3\), \(\rho=6\), and failed at 8.

This is ex:double-dependency-thresholds. Every case agrees with \(\tau=\lceil t/2\rceil+2(\rho-t)\): \(1+2\cdot2=5\), \(1+2\cdot4=9\), \(2+2\cdot3=8\). For one dependency the formula is the wide threshold, since \(\rho=\sum_bk_b-1\) gives \(\rho-t=\sum_b(k_b-1)\). The calibration's 5 clauses on \(\mathbb F_3^6\) do not have every 4 independent, so they lie outside the formula's hypothesis.

The point-extension lemma

Let \(F\) and \(G\) be families of clauses indexed by the same set, with \(F\) on coordinates \(y\in\mathbb F_p^a\) and \(G\) on \(z\in\mathbb F_p^m\). Their AND \(F\wedge G\) has clause \(b\) forbidding \(B^F_b\times B^G_b\).

Lemma (point extension). Over \(\mathbb F_p\), let the forbidden sets \(B^F_b\) be arbitrary, and suppose all forbidden sets \(B^G_b\) contain a common point \(z^*\). If \(F\) is not local at degree \(e\), then \(F\wedge G\) is not local at degree \(e+(p-1)m\).

Proof. Let \(P\in I_e(Z(F))\) lie outside \(\sum_bI_e(U^F_b)\), and let \(\delta\) be the indicator of \(z^*\), of degree \((p-1)m\). Then \(f=P\otimes\delta\) has degree \(\le e+(p-1)m\). Over \(z\ne z^*\) it is 0. Over \(z^*\) every clause's \(G\)-part is forbidden, so \((y,z^*)\) is allowed exactly when \(y\in Z(F)\), where \(P=0\). So \(f\in I_{e+(p-1)m}(Z(F\wedge G))\).

Define \(C(g)(y)=(-1)^m\sum_{z\in\mathbb F_p^m}g(y,z)\). Since \(\sum_{z\in\mathbb F_p}z^i\) is \(-1\) for \(i=p-1\) and 0 for \(0\le i<p-1\), \(C(g)\) is the coefficient of the top monomial \(\prod_iz_i^{p-1}\) in the reduced form of \(g\), with degree at most \(p-1\) in each variable. So \(C\) maps degree \(\le e+(p-1)m\) to degree \(\le e\). Also \(C(f)=(-1)^mP\sum_z\delta(z)=(-1)^mP\). If \(a_b\) vanishes on \(U_b(F\wedge G)\supseteq U^F_b\times\mathbb F_p^m\), then \(a_b(y,\cdot)=0\) for \(y\in U^F_b\), so \(C(a_b)\in I_e(U^F_b)\). A decomposition \(f=\sum_ba_b\) would therefore give \(P=(-1)^m\sum_bC(a_b)\in\sum_bI_e(U^F_b)\), a contradiction. \(\square\)

Proposition (rank threshold, failure half). Over \(\mathbb F_3\), let \(t+1\) point-forbidding clauses have every \(t\) of them independent and combined linear parts of rank \(\rho<\sum_bk_b\). Then for suitable forbidden points the family is not local at degree \(\tau=\lceil t/2\rceil+2(\rho-t)\). That \(\tau\) is the first such degree is the locality half.

Proof. Let \(K\), of dimension \(r\), be the space of dependencies among the clauses' linear parts. If \(\kappa\in K\) had zero component in clause \(b\), it would be a dependency among the other \(t\) clauses, so \(\kappa=0\). So \(K\) maps injectively into each clause's span. Choose a basis \(\kappa^1,\dots,\kappa^r\) of \(K\). In clause \(b\) the components \(\kappa^j_b\) are independent; extend them by \(k_b-r\) private forms. Relations among all these forms are exactly \(\sum_b\kappa^j_b=0\), \(j=1,\dots,r\). Any relation is a dependency, so it equals \(\sum_j\gamma_j\kappa^j\). Since the \(\kappa^j_b\) and the private forms are a basis of clause \(b\)'s span, comparing components gives coefficient \(\gamma_j\) on each \(\kappa^j_b\) and 0 on every private form. Each relation contains \(\kappa^j_{t+1}\) with coefficient 1. So the \(\kappa^j_b\), \(b\le t\), together with the private forms of all \(t+1\) clauses, are independent, \(rt+\sum_{b=1}^{t+1}(k_b-r)=\sum_bk_b-r=\rho\) of them. Coordinates \(w\) that no clause uses can be ignored: if \(P\) is not local at degree \(e\) on the other coordinates, neither is \(P\otimes1\), since setting \(w\) to a point in a decomposition gives a decomposition of \(P\) with the same degrees. After affine changes within each clause, clause \(b\) forbids a point of its copy coordinates \(y^{(j)}_b\) (for \(b=t+1\), of \(\sum_iy^{(j)}_i\)) and of its private coordinates. The family is the AND of \(r\) canonical copies with the private family, whose forbidden sets are products of points in disjoint blocks and so share a point. Here \(c_j\) is fixed by clause \(t+1\)'s forbidden point, with the sign from \(\kappa^j_{t+1}=-\sum_{b\le t}\kappa^j_b\) absorbed. Varying that point realizes every \(c\in\mathbb F_3^r\), so choose \(c_1=t+w_0\) and \(c_j=0\) for \(j\ge2\), with the private points arbitrary. Copy 1 fails at \(\lceil t/2\rceil\) by prop:pairing-obstruction. Copies \(2,\dots,r\) together with the private family share the point \(0\), in \(m=t(r-1)+\sum_b(k_b-r)=\rho-t\) coordinates. By the lemma the family fails at \(\lceil t/2\rceil+2(\rho-t)\). \(\square\)

The locality half, below \(\tau\), is proved only for \(r=1\). With the proposition, conj:rank-threshold is exactly that half.

Clauses on one span

Take \(t=1\): two clauses on the same \(k\)-dimensional span, so \(\rho=k\) and \(r=k\). They forbid points \(a\ne b\); after a linear change on the span, \(a-b\) is a coordinate vector. The proposition gives failure at \(\lceil1/2\rceil+2(k-1)=2k-1\): \(\delta_a-\delta_b\) vanishes on the allowed set and factors as \(\prod_{i\ge2}\delta_{a_i}(y_i)\) times a nonzero polynomial of degree 1 in \(y_1\), so it has degree \(2k-1\). Locality also holds below \(2k-1\). Coordinates \(w\) outside the span can be removed: write \(f\in I_e(Z\times\mathbb F_3^w)\) as \(\sum_\beta f_\beta(y)w^\beta\); each \(f_\beta\) lies in \(I_{e-|\beta|}(Z)\), so locality in every degree \(\le e\) on the span gives locality at \(e\). On the span, an element of \(I(Z)\) is \(\alpha\delta_a+\beta\delta_b\), with top coefficient \(\pm(\alpha+\beta)\), so its degree is at least \(2k-1\) unless it is 0. So the threshold is exactly \(2k-1\), and conj:rank-threshold holds in this case for every \(r=k\ge2\).

The wide dependency threshold already gave clause-level failure at \(4k-3\) for two clauses sharing one direction. This case sharpens it to \(2k-1\), far below \(D=22k\). A budget adversary can place many clauses on one span, so clauses on a common span must be grouped and closed together, as the locality line review required. Grouping alone does not suffice. Two members whose spans meet, forbidding suitable points, fail below \(D\) by the same count (\(4k-2s-1\le4k-3\) for spans sharing \(s\ge1\) dimensions), so independence between members stays a requirement. A member forbids an arbitrary subset of its span. The point-extension lemma allows that in its first factor, but the other results above are for points.

What this means

  • The measured thresholds for several dependencies fit the rank formula \(\lceil t/2\rceil+2(\rho-t)\), and its failure half is proved for all families in scope. If the locality half holds, a dependent cluster of \(t+1\) point-forbidding clauses of width \(k\), every \(t\) independent, is harmless through \(D\) once \(\lceil t/2\rceil+2(\rho-t)>D\). Since \(\rho\ge tk\), \(t\ge12\) with \(k\ge10\) suffices at \(p=3\).
  • Clauses on a common span break clause-level locality at exactly degree \(2k-1\). Member locality must therefore treat each member's forbidden set as an arbitrary subset of its span, and still require independence between members. The next step is the single-dependency threshold for members with arbitrary forbidden subsets, beginning with one dependency among \(t+1\) members.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: thm:wide-dependency-threshold, thm:single-dependency-threshold, prop:pairing-obstruction (canonical family and the values \(c=t+w_0\)), and ex:combined-locality-calibration. Every measured value is read from the result files. A fresh-context reviewer found the lemma, the AND application and the span example correct. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the failure half stated for all families in scope, with the normal-form argument supplied;
  • the lemma stated for arbitrary forbidden sets in its first factor;
  • the false width-1 sentence replaced by the rank inequality;
  • a false remark that the lemma cannot apply to clauses sharing coordinates removed;
  • the locality half of the span example proved;
  • untested ranks of \(r\) flagged;
  • overclaims corrected: "same span", the earlier \(4k-3\) credited, grouping not shown sufficient, \(k\ge10\).

The strengthening follows from the reviewer's normal-form argument, which I checked: injectivity from every \(t\) being independent, and the count \(rt+\sum_b(k_b-r)=\rho\). The span case's locality half is a two-line degree count. Because the strengthening adds a claim, a second focused pass checked the proposition and the span section. It found them correct and required: the hypothesis \(\rho<\sum_bk_b\) (at least one dependency), also in the conjecture; the one-line reason why the relations are exactly the \(\kappa^j\); the private sum over all clauses; the realization of the values \(c_j\); the unused-coordinate argument stated in the direction used; the inline removal of outside coordinates in the span case; "for suitable points" for meeting members; and "not local at \(\tau\)" instead of "fails at \(\tau\)". All adopted.

Remaining gap

  • The locality half of conj:rank-threshold for \(r\ge2\), except two clauses on one span (\(t=1\), \(\rho=k\)), proved here.
  • Member locality with arbitrary forbidden subsets of the members' spans.

Member inconsistency: suitable dependent members lose the pairing term and fail at 2Σ(k_b−1), below D for small clusters

24 September 2026 · Working proof (member inconsistency) · One dependency among members with arbitrary forbidden subsets, over F_3; cycle odd-prime-member-dependency. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The several-dependencies entry showed that clauses on one span must be grouped into members, and asked for the single-dependency threshold of members, whose forbidden sets are arbitrary subsets of their spans. The missing implication is how small a dependent cluster of members can break locality. That decides whether member locality can hold for the budget, whose clauses are adversarial.

General statement. prop:member-inconsistency: over \(\mathbb F_3\), let \(t+1\) members have independent forms spanning spaces of dimensions \(k_b\), with exactly one dependency among them all and every \(t\) members independent. Then for suitable forbidden sets, each of two points, the family is not local at degree \(2\sum_b(k_b-1)\), with a nonempty allowed set whenever some \(k_b\ge2\). So for such sets the least failing degree is at most \(2\sum_b(k_b-1)\). The pairing term \(\lceil t/2\rceil\) of the point-forbidding threshold is lost. Two members sharing one direction, of span dimension \(k\), fail at \(4k-4\). With \(D=22k\), where \(k\) is the clause width, a cluster fails below \(D\) whenever \(\sum_b(k_b-1)\le11k\); for members of span dimension \(k\) this means \(t+1\le11k/(k-1)\), at least 11 for every \(k\). So member locality does not hold for arbitrary member families and needs a hypothesis on the budget. Whether the budget meets one is open.

The proposition

Proposition (member inconsistency). Over \(\mathbb F_3\), let \(t\ge1\), and let members \(b=1,\dots,t+1\) have linear forms \(\ell_b\) spanning spaces of dimensions \(k_b\). Suppose the combined linear parts have rank \(\sum_bk_b-1\), and every \(t\) members are independent. Then there are forbidden sets \(\Phi_b\), each consisting of two points of member \(b\)'s form values, such that the family is not local at degree \(2\sum_b(k_b-1)\). Its allowed set is nonempty when \(\sum_b(k_b-1)\ge1\).

Proof. Use the normal form of thm:wide-dependency-threshold: coordinates \(y_1,\dots,y_t\) for the dependency's components, private coordinates \(w_b\) (\(k_b-1\) of them) for each member, and free coordinates \(z\). Member \(b\le t\)'s forms are \((y_b,w_b)\) up to an affine change, and member \(t+1\)'s are \((y_1+\dots+y_t,\ w_{t+1})\). Coordinates no member uses are ignored: non-locality of \(P\) on the others gives non-locality of \(P\otimes1\) at the same degree.

Take \(\Phi_b=\{y_b\ne0,\ w_b=0\}\) for \(b\le t\), and \(\Phi_{t+1}=\{\sum y\ne1,\ w_{t+1}=0\}\), each of two points in the member's coordinates. This family is \(F\wedge G\), with \(F\) on \(y\) and \(G\) on \(w\), where:

  • \(F\)'s member \(b\) forbids \(\{y_b\ne0\}\) (\(b\le t\)), and member \(t+1\) forbids \(\{\sum y\ne1\}\);
  • \(G\)'s member \(b\) forbids \(\{w_b=0\}\).

\(Z(F)=\{y=0\}\cap\{\sum y=1\}=\emptyset\), so \(1\in I_0(Z(F))\). Each \(U^F_b\) is nonempty, a hyperplane, so \(I_0(U^F_b)=0\), and \(F\) is not local at degree 0. \(G\)'s forbidden sets all contain \(w=0\), in \(m=\sum_b(k_b-1)\) coordinates. By lem:point-extension, which allows arbitrary forbidden sets in \(F\), the family is not local at degree \(0+2m\). If some \(k_b\ge2\), set \(w_b\ne0\) for every \(b\) with \(k_b\ge2\), which makes those members inactive. If \(k_{t+1}\ge2\), take \(y=0\): every member \(b\le t\) with \(k_b=1\) allows \(y_b=0\). Otherwise some \(b_0\le t\) has \(k_{b_0}\ge2\); take \(y=e_{b_0}\). Then members \(b\le t\), \(b\ne b_0\), allow \(y_b=0\), and member \(t+1\) allows \(\sum y=1\). So the allowed set is nonempty. \(\square\)

Each member forbids two points, as two clauses on the same span would, and one point per member would give the point-forbidding threshold instead. The obstruction is inconsistency: the members' allowed values of the dependent coordinates are incompatible, which makes the \(y\)-level allowed set empty. No pairing structure is needed, so the \(\lceil t/2\rceil\) term is lost.

What this means

  • For point-forbidding clauses a single dependency costs exactly \(\lceil t/2\rceil+2\sum_b(k_b-1)\). For suitable members forbidding two points, the least failing degree is at most \(2\sum_b(k_b-1)\). At \(p=3\), \(D=22k\), a cluster with \(\sum_b(k_b-1)\le11k\) is non-local below \(D\) for such forbidden sets, and two members sharing one direction fail at \(4k-4\).
  • Heuristically, merging dependent members into one larger member removes the dependency but enlarges the span. If an adversary could chain clauses so that merging never stops, the merged member would be the whole allowed set, and the question would again be global row freeness of the closure of \(Z\). No argument here shows that such chaining is possible within the budget.
  • So the locality program reduces the budget's closure to members only under a hypothesis on the budget that excludes small inconsistent dependent clusters. Nothing recorded provides one, and whether the reduction's budget meets one is open. This is the point for a route review of the clause-transfer line.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: lem:point-extension (its first factor may have arbitrary forbidden sets), the normal form of thm:wide-dependency-threshold, and prop:rank-threshold-failure. A fresh-context reviewer found the proof correct, including the two-point count, the product structure, degree-0 non-locality and the free coordinates. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the nonemptiness argument corrected for the last member;
  • "costs at most" and "disappears" stated for suitable forbidden sets and a single degree;
  • the cluster condition stated exactly, as \(\sum_b(k_b-1)\le11k\);
  • clause width and member span dimension distinguished;
  • the chaining argument labeled heuristic;
  • the adversarial claims weakened to "not for arbitrary families; open for the budget";
  • the title made conditional;
  • "minimal in kind" replaced;
  • independence within members added to the hypotheses.

The changes weaken or correct, so no further pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • Whether the budget's clauses, as produced by the logarithmic-prefix reduction, satisfy any robustness that bounds dependent clusters, or whether the closure route must handle giant members directly.

Route review: the budget's clauses form inconsistent dependent clusters freely, so the locality program cannot reduce its closure to members

24 September 2026 · Route review · The locality sub-line against the reduction's actual budget; cycle odd-prime-budget-structure-review. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

General statement. The line's claim is the hypothesis of thm:global-closure-gluing for the budget: row freeness through degree \(D\) of the graded functions on the allowed set \(Z\) of the logarithmic-prefix reduction's constraints. The locality sub-line tried to reduce this to members. prop:member-inconsistency shows that small inconsistent dependent clusters break member locality below \(D\). This review checks the reduction's budget and finds such clusters admissible, so the reduction to members is unavailable for the budget as stated.

What the budget is

thm:logarithmic-prefix-wide-clause-reduction takes any \(M=n^K\) families of affine forms, arising from the lines of a refutation, and chooses prefix sets \(S_b\) with \(|S_b|=\min(k,h_b)\). The constraints are \(g_{b,i}\prod_{j\in S_b}L_{b,j}^{p-1}\). Their allowed sets are \(\{\text{some }L_{b,j}=0,\ j\in S_b\}\), up to the multipliers \(g_{b,i}\). Each clause therefore forbids the product set \(\{L_{b,j}\ne0\ \forall j\in S_b\}\), two values per form at \(p=3\), subject only to \(M(1-1/p)^k<1\). The forms are arbitrary. The recorded choice-rule entries (uniform rule, density rule) showed that any rule for \(S_b\) must be invariant modulo the base, and no such rule is known.

Falsification attempt: inconsistent clusters in the budget

Take three blocks whose chosen forms include \(\ell_1\), \(\ell_2\) and \(\ell_1+\ell_2-c\) with \(c\ne0\), the rest of each block's forms being private. At the level of these three forms each clause allows only the value 0, and the three conditions are inconsistent. This is the configuration of prop:member-inconsistency with \(t=2\), except that here each factor forbids \(\{\ell\ne0\}\) rather than a single point. The proposition's proof applies unchanged: the \(y\)-level family, forbidding \(\{y_1\ne0\}\), \(\{y_2\ne0\}\) and \(\{y_1+y_2\ne c\}\), has an empty allowed set and is non-local at degree 0. The private factors \(\{L\ne0\}^{k-1}\) share a point, for example all ones. So by lem:point-extension the three clauses are non-local at degree \(3\cdot2(k-1)=6(k-1)<D=22k\). The configuration only needs one affine relation among three forms from different lines, for example \(X_{11}\), \(X_{12}\) and \(X_{11}+X_{12}-1\) in a refutation's lines. It is compatible with the density condition. So member locality fails for budgets the reduction must handle, unless a choice of \(S_b\) excludes all such clusters. No recorded choice rule does, and when a block has \(h_b=k\) there is no choice at all.

Merging each cluster into one member removes its non-locality but enlarges the member. Whether merging stays bounded for adversarial families is not shown. It is plausibly not: \(n^Kk\) forms on \(n\) coordinates admit many short affine relations.

What the goal needs and what is proved

The goal needs the global statement, row freeness of \(\operatorname{gr}\mathbb F^Z\) in degrees between about \(\log_2n\) and \(D\), for every admissible budget. Proved statements cover structured \(Z\): sparse, seeded, block, and every \(Z\) whose forms are jointly free. The locality sub-line then gave exact thresholds for point-forbidding clauses in general position, and obstructions (pairing, covering, member inconsistency) that close it for adversarial budgets. Non-locality is not a failure of the goal. It only removes the reduction to members. Whether an inconsistent cluster breaks closed row freeness itself is untested.

Assessment of the line

The closure route stands on thm:global-closure-gluing, and its hypothesis is proved only where the forms are jointly free. The locality program was the plan for reaching adversarial \(Z\) from such pieces, and it is now closed by an obstruction the budget can realize. What remains is the global freeness statement with no reduction and no mechanism. The one computational handle, the direct-sum kernel, reaches the conjecture's range only at \(D=3\), below the degrees where clusters act. On this evidence the line is blocked at its central claim. The next step must either test that claim against the new obstruction or leave the line for another.

The highest-risk item and the next step

The highest-risk item is whether closed row freeness survives inconsistent clusters. If it fails, the closure route is refuted for adversarial budgets, as the symmetric pin refuted low-density classes. If it holds where locality fails, the line continues without locality, and the structure that saves it becomes the target.

Next step, on route item odd-prime-clause-transfer: a controlled test of closed row freeness on an inconsistent three-clause cluster, with the direct-sum kernel. Use clauses of width 2 whose dependent forms satisfy \(\ell_1+\ell_2-\ell_3=c\). Compare \(c\ne0\), the inconsistent case, non-local at degree 6, with \(c=0\), the consistent case, and with the base, at the largest board the kernel reaches with \(D\ge7\). The board will be below the conjecture's range. As with the symmetric pin, only a difference between the inconsistent case and its controls at the same size would carry a conclusion.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: thm:logarithmic-prefix-wide-clause-reduction (statement and constraint form), both choice-rule entries, prop:member-inconsistency and lem:point-extension (arbitrary forbidden sets in the first factor), and thm:global-closure-gluing. The cluster application is the proposition's proof with forbidden sets \(\{\ell\ne0\}\) and a shared all-ones private point. The review registers no claim, so no reviewer pass was run.

Budget clusters: consistent clusters are local in every degree, inconsistent ones fail exactly at their number of private forms

24 September 2026 · Working proof (budget cluster dichotomy) · Simple single-dependency clusters of budget-type clauses over F_3; cycle odd-prime-cluster-freeness. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The budget review found that the reduction's clauses can form inconsistent dependent clusters. It asked for a controlled test of whether such a cluster breaks closed row freeness. The missing implication: which clusters of budget clauses break locality, and at which degree. The budget's clauses forbid all their forms being nonzero, not single points, so the point-forbidding thresholds do not apply directly.

General statement. thm:budget-cluster-dichotomy: over \(\mathbb F_3\), consider \(t+1\) clauses, each forbidding \(\{\text{all its forms}\ne0\}\). Suppose they have one dependency, every \(t\) independent, and each clause's component of the dependency is a nonzero multiple of the linear part of one of its forms. If the dependent forms can vanish together (consistent), the family is local in every degree. If they cannot (inconsistent), it is local exactly below \(\sum_b(k_b-1)\), the number of private forms. The proof combines lem:budget-peeling, where removing a private form costs one degree, and lem:supported-extension, which generalizes lem:point-extension to any common forbidden subset carrying a low-degree function. So for an isolated simple cluster of budget clauses, only an affine inconsistency breaks locality. An inconsistent cluster of \(t+1\) clauses of width \(k\) is not local at some degree \(<D=22k\) exactly when \((t+1)(k-1)<22k\). That holds for every \(t+1\le22\), and for \(t+1\le22+22/(k-1)\) in general, with equality excluded.

The kernel test cannot decide

The review's test used three budget clauses of width 2 on the occupancy slice at \(N=10\), \(D=7\), with the direct-sum kernel (cluster_freeness.py, cf_N10_D7_*.json). Excess in degrees 0 to 6:

  • base: 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 4, 351;
  • consistent (\(c=0\)): 0, 0, 0, 13, 341, 60, 1;
  • inconsistent (\(c=1\)): 0, 0, 0, 5, 154, 49, 1;
  • inconsistent (\(c=2\)): 0, 0, 0, 7, 191, 107, 5.

Every variant fails from degree 3, the consistent one included, and the base fails from degree 5. Three width-2 clauses leave about \((5/9)^3\approx17\%\) of the slice, far outside the density the budget guarantees, and \(N=10\) is far below the one-row range. The density condition \(M(2/3)^k<1\) needs \(k\ge3\) for three clauses, where a cluster acts only at degree \(\ge2\cdot3=6\) on these counts and higher on the point-forbidding ones. That is beyond the kernel at any size in range. So the test decides nothing. It should have been ruled out by the density count before it was run.

Two lemmas

Families, locality and \(I_e\) are as in lem:degreewise-gluing, over \(\mathbb F_p\), for clauses with arbitrary forbidden sets. Locality holds trivially at negative degrees, where \(I_e=0\).

Lemma (supported extension). Let \(F\) on \(y\) and \(G\) on \(z\in\mathbb F_p^m\) be families on the same index set, and let \(F\wedge G\) be their AND, with clause \(b\) forbidding \(B^F_b\times B^G_b\). Suppose a set \(T\) lies in every \(B^G_b\), and \(h\ne0\) is a function of \(z\) of degree \(d\) vanishing off \(T\). If \(F\) is not local at degree \(e\), then \(F\wedge G\) is not local at degree \(e+d\).

Proof. Let \(P\in I_e(Z(F))\) lie outside \(\sum_bI_e(U^F_b)\), and put \(f=P\otimes h\), of degree \(\le e+d\). Off \(T\), \(h=0\). On \(T\) every clause's \(G\)-part is forbidden, so \((y,z)\) is allowed exactly when \(y\in Z(F)\), where \(P=0\). So \(f\in I_{e+d}(Z(F\wedge G))\). Since \(\deg h=d\), there is a linear functional \(\varphi\) on the functions of \(z\) vanishing on degree \(\le d-1\) with \(\varphi(h)\ne0\). Put \(C(g)(y)=\varphi(g(y,\cdot))\). Writing \(g=\sum_\alpha g_\alpha(y)z^\alpha\) in reduced form, only \(|\alpha|\ge d\) contribute, and \(\deg g_\alpha\le\deg g-|\alpha|\). So \(C\) maps degree \(\le e+d\) to degree \(\le e\). \(C(f)=\varphi(h)P\). If \(a_b\) vanishes on \(U_b(F\wedge G)\supseteq U^F_b\times\mathbb F_p^m\), then \(C(a_b)\) vanishes on \(U^F_b\). So \(f=\sum_ba_b\) would give \(P\in\sum_bI_e(U^F_b)\), a contradiction. \(\square\)

lem:point-extension is the case \(T=\{z^*\}\), with \(h\) the indicator, of degree \((p-1)m\).

Lemma (budget peeling). Over \(\mathbb F_3\), let \(w\) be a coordinate occurring only in clause \(b\), whose forbidden set is \(\{w\ne0\}\times B'_b\). Let \(F'\) be \(F\) with clause \(b\) narrowed to \(B'_b\), and \(F\setminus b\) be \(F\) without clause \(b\), both on the other coordinates. If \(F\setminus b\) is local at degree \(e\) and \(F'\) is local at degrees \(e-1\) and \(e-2\), then \(F\) is local at degree \(e\).

Proof. Write \(f\in I_e(Z(F))\) as \(A+Bw+Cw^2\), with \(\deg A\le e\), \(\deg B\le e-1\), \(\deg C\le e-2\). Over \(w=0\) clause \(b\) is inactive, so \(A=f|_{w=0}\) vanishes on \(Z(F\setminus b)\). Over \(w=\pm1\) the allowed set is \(Z(F')\), so \(A\pm B+C\) vanish there. Hence \(B\) vanishes on \(Z(F')\), and so does \(A+C\). Since \(Z(F')\subseteq Z(F\setminus b)\), \(A\) vanishes there too, and so does \(C\). Locality of \(F\setminus b\) at \(e\) gives \(A=\sum_{c\ne b}a_c\), \(a_c\in I_e(U_c)\). Locality of \(F'\) at \(e-1\) gives \(B=\sum_{c\ne b}b_c+b'_b\), with \(b'_b\) vanishing on \(U'_b\). Then \(b_cw\in I_e(U_c)\), and \(b'_bw\in I_e(U_b)\), because \(U_b=\{w=0\}\cup(\mathbb F_3\times U'_b)\). The same holds for \(C\) with \(w^2\), at degree \(e-2\). \(\square\)

The dichotomy

Theorem (budget cluster dichotomy). Over \(\mathbb F_3\), let \(t\ge1\) and let clause \(b\), \(1\le b\le t+1\), have \(k_b\) affine forms and forbid \(\{\text{all of them}\ne0\}\). Suppose the combined linear parts have rank \(\sum_bk_b-1\), every \(t\) clauses are independent, and the dependency's component in each clause is a nonzero multiple of the linear part of one of its forms \(\ell_b\). Given the rank, the independence of every \(t\) clauses is equivalent to the component being nonzero in every clause, since a dependency among \(t\) clauses would be a second one. Put \(m=\sum_b(k_b-1)\).

  • If the forms \(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_{t+1}\) have a common zero (consistent), the family is local in every degree.
  • Otherwise it is local in every degree \(e<m\) and not local at degree \(m\).

Proof. Normal form. Take \(y_b=\ell_b\) for \(b\le t\), the other forms as private coordinates \(w\), and free coordinates for the rest. These affine forms have independent linear parts, by the rank and because the one dependency involves \(\ell_{t+1}\) with a nonzero coefficient. So the change of coordinates is an invertible affine map, which preserves the degree filtration. The dependency gives \(\ell_{t+1}=\sum_b\lambda_by_b+c\) with every \(\lambda_b\ne0\). Rescaling \(y_b\) by \(\lambda_b\) keeps \(\{y_b\ne0\}\), so \(\ell_{t+1}=\sum y+c\). The forms have a common zero exactly when \(c=0\). Each clause forbids \(\{y\text{-form}\ne0\}\times\{w_b\ne0\}\). Free coordinates \(x\) belong to no clause. For locality, expand \(f=\sum_\alpha f_\alpha x^\alpha\) in them: each \(f_\alpha\) vanishes on the allowed set with degree \(\le e-|\alpha|\), so locality in all degrees \(\le e\) without them gives locality at \(e\). For non-locality, apply lem:supported-extension with \(h=1\), \(d=0\).

Base. The family on \(y\) alone forbids \(\{y_b\ne0\}\) and \(\{\sum y+c\ne0\}\). If \(c=0\), its allowed set is \(\{0\}\). \(I_e(\{0\})=\sum_by_bR_{\le e-1}\), since every monomial of positive degree is divisible by some \(y_b\), and \(y_bR_{\le e-1}\subseteq I_e(\{y_b=0\})\). So it is local in every degree. If \(c\ne0\), its allowed set is empty and every \(U_b\) is nonempty, so it is not local at degree 0.

Peeling. Remove the private coordinates one at a time with lem:budget-peeling. At each stage the family without the narrowed clause consists of \(t\) clauses with independent forms, which are disjoint blocks with arbitrary forbidden sets. It is therefore local in every degree by the product argument, with a filtration-compatible basis of each block adapted to its ideal. If \(c=0\), induction from the base gives locality in every degree at every stage. If \(c\ne0\), each removal raises the least failing degree by at least 1, so the family is local below \(m\).

Failure. If \(c\ne0\), apply lem:supported-extension with \(F\) the family on \(y\), not local at degree 0, and \(G\) the private family. Every \(G\)-forbidden set contains \(T=\{\text{all private coordinates}\ne0\}\). \(h=\prod w_i\) has degree \(m\) and vanishes off \(T\). So the family is not local at degree \(m\). \(\square\)

Consistency. budget_type.py computes the defect for 18 families already in normal form, with \(t=1\) to 4 and widths up to 4 (budget_type.json, budget_type_more.json). So it tests the base, peeling and failure steps, not the reduction to normal form. It checks every degree up to \(2s\), the top degree of the form space. Every consistent family is local in all of them, and every inconsistent one first fails at \(m\).

What this means

  • For an isolated simple cluster of budget clauses, the dependency alone does not break locality; only an affine inconsistency among the dependent forms does. A consistent simple cluster in isolation is local at every degree, however small. Locality of the cluster alone says nothing yet about the cluster inside a larger family.
  • An inconsistent simple cluster of \(t+1\) clauses of width \(k\) first fails at \((t+1)(k-1)\), a degree \(<D=22k\) for every \(t+1\le22\). Such clusters are affine relations with nonzero constant among the chosen forms of a few blocks. These are the base-level contradictions that the choice-rule entry requires a choice of \(S_b\) to detect. The locality question and the choice question now meet at one object.
  • Not covered: dependencies whose component in a clause mixes several of its forms, several dependencies, and inconsistency modulo the base rather than as affine functions.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: lem:point-extension, prop:member-inconsistency, thm:wide-dependency-threshold (normal form and product argument), thm:logarithmic-prefix-wide-clause-reduction (the budget's clause form) and the density-choice-rule entry. The kernel values and the 18 form-space families are read from the result files. A fresh-context reviewer found all three proofs sound: \(\varphi\), the three fibers, the memberships, the base cases, both inductions and the failure application. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the false "exactly when \(t+1\le22\)" replaced by the exact bound;
  • "below \(D\)" made strict;
  • the dichotomy scoped to isolated simple clusters, in the statement and the first bullet;
  • the redundant hypothesis marked as implied;
  • the normal form's affine change and its reason stated;
  • free coordinates treated directly;
  • negative degrees stated;
  • the computation's scope stated.

The changes restrict scope or make steps explicit, so no further pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • The dichotomy for mixed components and for several dependencies.
  • Whether a choice of \(S_b\) can avoid small inconsistent clusters, or whether their closures can be absorbed.

Resolvent absorption: inconsistent clusters cannot always be avoided, but adding their resolvent restores locality in every degree

24 September 2026 · Working proof (resolvent absorption) and a finite check · Isolated simple clusters of budget-type clauses over F_3; cycle odd-prime-cluster-avoidance. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The budget-cluster dichotomy located the only threat to locality in an isolated simple cluster: an affine relation with nonzero constant among the dependent forms. Its next step asked whether a choice of prefix sets \(S_b\) can avoid such clusters. If not, the missing implication is a way to neutralize them.

General statement. thm:resolvent-absorption: over \(\mathbb F_3\), let an inconsistent simple cluster of budget clauses be given, as in thm:budget-cluster-dichotomy. Clause \(b\) is \((\ell_b=0)\vee(\text{some private form of }b=0)\), and the \(\ell_b\) have no common zero. Add the resolvent \(R\): some private form of some clause is 0. The enlarged family, which has the same allowed set, is local in every degree. The proof is lem:shared-peeling, budget peeling for a coordinate shared by several clauses. So a cluster that cannot be avoided can be absorbed by a \(t\)-step Res(Lin) derivation. ex:resolvent-absorption-check confirms this on 6 normal-form families. Under the reduction's rule \(|S_b|=\min(k,h_b)\), avoidance is impossible in general. Blocks with at most \(k\) inputs leave no choice, and an adversary can give three of them the forms \(X_{11}\), \(X_{12}\), \(X_{11}+X_{12}-1\), with their other forms independent. For the hole family, whose forms are distinct variables, there are no small clusters for any choice.

Avoidance

  • Hole family. Block \(t\) has inputs \(X_{jt}-1\), one hole's variables. Chosen forms from different blocks are distinct variables, so they have no affine relation. Modulo the base, the pigeon equations \(\sum_tX_{jt}=1\) relate the forms of one pigeon across all \(n\) holes. Every combination of pigeon equations has support on at least \(n\) of the forms, so any relation involves at least \(n\) clauses. By thm:budget-cluster-dichotomy an inconsistent cluster of \(t+1\) clauses of width \(k\) fails at \((t+1)(k-1)\), below \(D=22k\) exactly when \(t+1<22k/(k-1)\), in particular for \(t+1\le22\). So for \(n>22k/(k-1)\) the hole family has no cluster failing below \(D\).
  • In general. thm:logarithmic-prefix-wide-clause-reduction takes \(|S_b|=\min(k,h_b)\), so blocks with \(h_b\le k\) leave no choice. Three such blocks with forms \(X_{11}\), \(X_{12}\), \(X_{11}+X_{12}-1\), and other forms independent of each other and of these, form an inconsistent simple cluster, since \(X_{11}=X_{12}=0\) gives \(-1\). A refutation may contain such lines. So no choice rule under that reduction avoids small inconsistent clusters for every inventory.

Shared peeling

Setting as in lem:budget-peeling, over \(\mathbb F_3\), with arbitrary forbidden sets. Locality holds trivially at negative degrees.

Lemma (shared peeling). Let \(w\) be a coordinate, and let \(Q\) be the set of clauses containing \(w\), each forbidding \(\{w\ne0\}\times B'_c\). Let \(F^0\) be \(F\) without the clauses in \(Q\), and \(F^1\) be \(F\) with each clause in \(Q\) narrowed to \(B'_c\), both on the other coordinates. If \(F^0\) is local at degree \(e\) and \(F^1\) is local at degrees \(e-1\) and \(e-2\), then \(F\) is local at degree \(e\).

Proof. Write \(f\in I_e(Z(F))\) as \(A+Bw+Cw^2\). Over \(w=0\) every clause in \(Q\) is inactive, so \(A\) vanishes on \(Z(F^0)\). Over \(w=\pm1\) the allowed set is \(Z(F^1)\subseteq Z(F^0)\), so \(B\), \(A+C\), \(A\) and \(C\) vanish there, as in lem:budget-peeling. Decompose \(A\) by \(F^0\) at \(e\), \(B\) by \(F^1\) at \(e-1\), and \(C\) by \(F^1\) at \(e-2\). A term \(b'_c\) vanishing on \(U'_c\), for \(c\in Q\), gives \(b'_cw\in I_e(U_c)\), because \(U_c=\{w=0\}\cup(\mathbb F_3\times U'_c)\). The same holds for \(w^2\). The other terms lie in \(I_e(U_c)\) for clauses \(c\) not containing \(w\). \(\square\)

lem:budget-peeling is the case \(|Q|=1\).

Absorption

Theorem (resolvent absorption). Over \(\mathbb F_3\), let \(t+1\) budget clauses satisfy the hypotheses of thm:budget-cluster-dichotomy with the \(\ell_b\) having no common zero. Let \(R\) be the clause whose forms are all the private forms of all \(t+1\) clauses, forbidding all of them nonzero. Then \(R\) is implied by the cluster, and the family of the \(t+1\) clauses together with \(R\) is local in every degree.

Proof. On a point where every private form is nonzero, each clause forces \(\ell_b=0\), which is impossible. So the allowed set of the cluster lies in that of \(R\), and adding \(R\) does not change it. Use the normal form of the dichotomy: coordinates \(y\), private coordinates \(w\) (\(m\) of them), free coordinates. Free coordinates are handled as there. Induct on the number \(m'\) of private coordinates remaining, over the class of such clusters in which clause \(b\) has \(m_b\ge0\) private coordinates. A clause with none is the unit clause \((\ell_b=0)\). At each step apply lem:shared-peeling to a private coordinate \(w\) of some clause \(b\) that still has one. Then \(Q=\{b,R\}\). Locality is invariant under affine coordinate changes.

  • \(F^0\) is the other \(t\) clauses with their remaining private coordinates, with clause \(b\) and \(R\) removed. The only affine relation of a simple cluster involves every \(\ell_b\), as \(\sum y+c\) does in the normal form. Removing any one clause, \(b=t+1\) included, therefore leaves independent forms, which are disjoint blocks after an affine change. So \(F^0\) is local in every degree by the product argument.
  • \(F^1\) is the same cluster with \(w\) removed from clause \(b\) and from \(R\). It is an inconsistent simple cluster with \(m'-1\) private coordinates together with its resolvent, local in every degree by induction.

At \(m'=0\) the resolvent has no forms, so its forbidden set is the whole space. Then \(I(U_R)\) is everything and the family is trivially local. \(\square\)

In Res(Lin) terms, \(R\) is the resolvent of the cluster: from \((\ell_b=0)\vee P_b\), \(b\le t+1\), with \(\{\ell_b=0\}\) inconsistent, derive \(\bigvee_bP_b\). Its width is \(m=\sum_b(k_b-1)\). Its forbidden density \((2/3)^m\) equals the product of the clauses' densities, \((2/3)^{\sum_bk_b}\), times \((3/2)^{t+1}\).

Check. resolvent_absorption.py recomputes inconsistent dichotomy families with \(R\) added (absorption.json). Two were also run without \(R\) in this file, and they fail from degree 2 and 3. With \(R\), all 6 inconsistent families tested, with \(t=1\) to 3 and widths up to 4, are local in every degree up to \(2s\). Without \(R\) all 6 fail by the dichotomy. For 5 of them this was also computed, in this file or in budget_type*.json; the family with widths \((3,3)\) was not run without \(R\). This is ex:resolvent-absorption-check.

What this means

  • Under the reduction's prefix rule the budget cannot avoid inconsistent clusters, but it can absorb them. Adding the resolvents of small inconsistent clusters, which are Res(Lin) consequences of the budget, keeps the allowed set and removes the cluster's non-locality. This is proved for an isolated simple cluster.
  • This suggests a saturated budget: close the family under resolvents of inconsistent clusters of at most about 22 clauses. The closure is finite, since there are finitely many clauses, but its size is not controlled. Resolvent widths need not grow when unit clauses take part. A clause of width above \(D\) has no nonzero function of degree \(\le D\) vanishing on its allowed set, since such a function is divisible by the product of its forms. It does not, however, drop out of the allowed set. The open statement, a conjecture, is that a saturated family is local through \(D\). That includes clusters inside larger families and resolvents that form new clusters, and it is the next step.
  • If the saturation derived a clause with no forms, the budget with the base would have a Res(Lin) refutation of width at most about \(D\). Such a family is trivially local, since the empty clause's ideal is everything. So locality is informative for the hardness goal only when the closure does not derive the empty clause. The saturated-locality question and the hardness question are not independent.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: thm:budget-cluster-dichotomy (normal form, product argument), lem:budget-peeling, thm:logarithmic-prefix-wide-clause-reduction (\(|S_b|=\min(k,h_b)\)) and the choice-rule entries. The check's values are read from the result files. A fresh-context reviewer found the shared peeling lemma and the absorption induction correct, including the shape of \(R\), the fibres, \(F^1\) being the narrowed cluster with its own resolvent, the base case, and \(b=t+1\). It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the induction class allowing clauses without private coordinates;
  • the reason \(F^0\) is independent;
  • "one step" corrected to a \(t\)-step derivation;
  • the density stated as an equality;
  • the avoidance claims scoped to the reduction's rule, with the independence of the other forms;
  • the constant 22 derived and the hole family's \(n\) condition stated;
  • the check's coverage stated;
  • the saturation's finiteness and the empty-clause remark corrected and labeled conjectural.

The changes weaken or correct, so no further pass was made.

Remaining gap

  • Locality of saturated families: clusters inside larger families, mixed components, several dependencies, and interaction between resolvents.

Saturated locality fails: dense pairs of budget clauses with overlapping spans are non-local at low degree and admit no resolvent

24 September 2026 · Finite check (refutation of the saturated-locality conjecture in form space) · Dense budget-type families over F_3; cycle odd-prime-saturated-locality. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The resolvent-absorption entry conjectured that a budget closed under resolvents of small inconsistent clusters is local through \(D\), unless the closure derives the empty clause. That was the last reduction the locality program offered for adversarial budgets. The cycle tests it where it could fail: dense families in which clusters overlap or have more than one dependency.

General statement. The conjecture tested is saturated locality: a family of budget clauses closed under resolution of inconsistent literal sets, and not containing the empty clause, is local in every degree. ex:saturated-locality-failure refutes its form-space version in the dense regime. Over \(\mathbb F_3^4\), two clauses of width 3 whose spans meet in dimension 2 admit no resolvent. They are non-local at degree 4 in 4 of the 5 such pairs tested, with allowed sets of density about 1/2. So consistency and saturation do not give locality once a dependency space has dimension 2 or a component mixes several forms of a clause. thm:budget-cluster-dichotomy and thm:resolvent-absorption are sharp in their scope, single simple dependencies.

The test

Can it decide. A counterexample needs a saturated family, meaning no resolvent applies or all are added, with a dense allowed set and a locality defect. Form space is exact at \(s\le5\). Width-3 clauses forbid \(8/27\) each, so two or three of them keep density near 1/2 or above. These are the smallest sizes where the budget's density regime and non-simple dependencies coexist.

saturated.py draws random clauses of \(k\) affine forms on \(\mathbb F_3^s\), each allowing "some form \(=0\)". It closes them under the rule: from clauses \(C_1,\dots,C_r\), \(r\le3\), and one literal from each whose zero sets are jointly inconsistent, derive the union of the other literals, keeping only minimal clauses. It computes the locality defect in every degree up to \(2s\) before and after closure (sat_*.json).

  • With 2 or 3 clauses of width 2 on \(\mathbb F_3^3\), allowed sets of 2 to 5 points: saturation removes some defects, as absorption predicts, but others remain. These families are in the covering regime.
  • With width 3 on \(\mathbb F_3^4\) and \(\mathbb F_3^5\), allowed density 0.31 to 0.58: of 20 families, 15 are non-local before closure, and the same 15, at the same first degree (3 to 5), after closure. Closure added clauses in 7 families and changed no first failing degree.
  • Two-clause families, where no resolvent can apply unless the literal sets are inconsistent: of 5 pairs whose spans meet in dimension 2, 4 fail first at degree 4. Of 5 pairs meeting in dimension 1, 1 fails, first at degree 5. That pair has a single dependency, so its component in some clause must mix several forms; otherwise the dichotomy would give locality or a first failure at 4.

This is ex:saturated-locality-failure. Inspection of the first failing pair: forms of ranks 3 and 3, all six of rank 4, spans meeting in dimension 2, consistent, with no inconsistent literal set.

What this means

  • Locality at clause level fails for dense, consistent, saturated budget families as soon as two clauses share a two-dimensional part of their spans. An adversarial budget can contain such pairs. So no closure under resolution restores clause-level locality.
  • Grouping overlapping clauses into members removes these pairs but brings back member-level obstructions: prop:member-inconsistency, and the chaining that merging may cause. The locality program has now been tested against every reduction it offered: t-wise, member, cluster and resolvent. Each fails for adversarial budgets, and the positive results cover only single simple dependencies.
  • This is the point for a route review of the clause-transfer line. Three research entries have passed since the budget review, which already found the central claim without a mechanism.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: thm:budget-cluster-dichotomy and thm:resolvent-absorption (scope: single simple dependencies), and the absorption entry's conjecture. Every count is read from the result files by script. The resolution rule and the defect computation reuse the validated form-space routines. The entry registers a finite check and no proof, so no reviewer pass was run.
