Overlap Tor: two members on a free joint span split exactly when their ideals meet only in products and shared generators

24 September 2026 · Working proof (overlap Tor) · Hypothesis (b) for two members with overlapping spans; cycle odd-prime-overlapping-members. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. After the generic span members, (c) and (d) hold for satisfiable members on generic spans. The open hypothesis is (b), splitting of the top syzygies across members. lem:tensor-splitting-locality proves (b) when the members' spans form a direct sum. The inventory's members cannot all have independent spans. The missing implication is (b) for members whose spans intersect, starting with two members.

General statement. prop:overlap-tor: over \(\mathbb F_3\), let two members have tops generating ideals \(I_1\subseteq T(W_1)\) and \(I_2\subseteq T(W_2)\), where \(T(W)=\mathrm{Sym}(W)/(\text{cubes})\). Let \(I_{12}\) be the ideal of the generators common to both. Suppose the top algebra \(A\) is free through \(D\) over \(T(V)\), \(V=W_1+W_2\), meaning its minimal free cover is bijective in degrees \(\le D\). Then (b) holds for the two members through \(D\) if and only if \((I_1T\cap I_2T)/(I_1T\cdot I_2T+I_{12}T)\) vanishes in degrees \(\le D\). With no shared generators this module is \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^S(T(W_1)/I_1,T(W_2)/I_2)\), \(S=T(W_1\cap W_2)\). For selector members on all directions of \(W_1\) and \(W_2\), it has dimension \(k(d_1-k)(d_2-k)\) in degree 3, where \(k=\dim(W_1\cap W_2)\). That is the recorded formula for the shortfall of member additivity (ex:member-configurations-free). Pairwise conditions do not suffice for more than two members. Three single selectors on \(x\), \(y\), \(x+y\) have pairwise independent spans, yet (b) fails in degree 3.

The proposition

Setting. Let \(V=W_1+W_2\) and \(U=W_1\cap W_2\), and choose complements \(W_i=W_i'\oplus U\), so \(V=W_1'\oplus U\oplus W_2'\). Then \(T=T(V)=T(W_1)\otimes_ST(W_2)\) with \(S=T(U)\), and each \(T(W_i)=T(W_i')\otimes S\) is free over \(S\). Member \(i\) has generators \(g\), its tops, in \(T(W_i)\), generating \(I_i\). Hypothesis (b) of thm:relative-gluing asks that every top syzygy of the combined generators be a combination of syzygies supported on one member and of cross-member Koszul syzygies \(g_2e_{g_1}-g_1e_{g_2}\).

Proposition (overlap Tor). Take the union of the two generating sets, each common generator listed once, with \(G_{12}\) the common generators and \(I_{12}\) their ideal. In \(T\), the top syzygies modulo member-supported and cross-member Koszul syzygies form a graded module isomorphic to \(Q=(I_1T\cap I_2T)/(I_1T\cdot I_2T+I_{12}T)\). If \(G_{12}=\emptyset\), \(Q=\operatorname{Tor}_1^T(T/I_1T,T/I_2T)\cong\operatorname{Tor}_1^S(M_1,M_2)\), with \(M_i=T(W_i)/I_i\). If \(A\) is free through \(D\) over \(T\), then (b) holds through \(D\) exactly when \(Q\) vanishes in degrees \(\le D\).

Proof.

  1. The quotient. Count the common generators with member 1. Send a syzygy \((a_g)\) to \(\sum_{g\in G_1}a_gg\). This equals \(-\sum_{g\in G_2\setminus G_{12}}a_gg\), so it lies in \(I_1T\cap I_2T\), and the map onto the intersection is surjective. Its kernel is the syzygies whose two partial sums vanish, which are sums of syzygies supported on \(G_1\) and on \(G_2\setminus G_{12}\). A syzygy supported on member 2 that uses common generators maps into \(I_{12}T\), and every element of \(I_{12}T\) arises this way: \(\sum_{g\in G_{12}}a_gg\) against the same combination read in member 2. A Koszul syzygy \(g_2e_{g_1}-g_1e_{g_2}\) maps to \(\pm g_1g_2\), so the Koszul syzygies map onto \(I_1T\cdot I_2T\). Hence the quotient is \(Q\). With no common generators, \(Q=(I_1T\cap I_2T)/(I_1T\cdot I_2T)=\operatorname{Tor}_1^T(T/I_1T,T/I_2T)\).
  2. Base change (no common generators). \(T/I_1T=M_1\otimes_ST(W_2)\) and \(T/I_2T=T(W_1)\otimes_SM_2\). Take a free \(T(W_1)\)-resolution \(P\to M_1\). Since \(T(W_2)\) is free over \(S\), \(P\otimes_ST(W_2)\) is a free \(T\)-resolution of \(T/I_1T\). Tensoring it over \(T\) with \(T(W_1)\otimes_SM_2\) gives \(P\otimes_SM_2\), and \(P\) is an \(S\)-free resolution of \(M_1\). So \(\operatorname{Tor}^T_1=\operatorname{Tor}^S_1(M_1,M_2)\), degree by degree. The complements may be chosen separately for each member, since \(W_1'\oplus U\oplus W_2'=V\) for any choices.
  3. In \(A\). Let the cover \(T\otimes C\to A\) be bijective in degrees \(\le D\). A top syzygy of degree \(s\le D\) in \(A\) is the image of one in \(T\otimes C\), and it splits along a basis of \(C\) into syzygies in \(T\), as in the span-transfer argument. The splitting preserves member support and Koszul syzygies. So if \(Q\) vanishes through \(D\), (b) holds in \(A\) through \(D\). Conversely, a syzygy in \(T\) not in the member-supported and Koszul span stays outside that span in \(A\): its image is its tensor with \(1\in C_0\), and the projection onto the coordinate of \(1\) recovers it. \(\square\)

Consequences.

  • If \(W_1\cap W_2=0\) and there are no common generators, then \(S=\mathbb F_3\) and \(Q=0\). This is the two-member case of lem:tensor-splitting-locality. The same holds when a member's generators lie in \(T(L)\) for some \(L\) with \(L\cap W_2=0\), which is that lemma applied with span \(L\).
  • Selectors on all directions. Here \(I_i\) is spanned by the squares of forms in \(W_i\), which span \(\mathrm{Sym}^2W_i\) in characteristic 3, and the common generators are the squares of forms in \(U=W_1\cap W_2\). In degree 3 there are no Koszul products. Modulo \(I_{12}T\), the intersection is spanned by the monomials \(xuy\), with \(x\), \(u\), \(y\) running over bases of complements \(W_1'\), \(U\), \(W_2'\). Indeed \(xu\in I_1\) and \(uy\in I_2\), so \(xuy\) lies in both ideals, while every other monomial of degree 3 lies in only one ideal or in \(I_{12}T\). So \(\dim Q_3=k(d_1-k)(d_2-k)\).
  • More than two members. Pairwise vanishing does not give (b). Take three single selectors \(x^2\), \(y^2\), \((x+y)^2\) in \(T(x,y)\). Every pair has independent spans, so every pairwise \(Q\) vanishes. But the degree-3 syzygies form a space of dimension \(6-2=4\), against 3 member-supported (Frobenius) ones, and Koszul syzygies start in degree 4. This is the three-selector configuration, whose extra syzygy derives \(a-b\) at degree 3 when the values conflict.

Consistency with the record

overlap_tor.py computes, exactly over \(\mathbb F_3\) in \(T(V)\) for selector members on all directions, \(\dim(I_1T\cap I_2T)_3\) and the dimension of the part generated by the common selectors. Their difference is \(\dim Q_3\), since \(I_1T\cdot I_2T\) starts in degree 4. In the six configurations \((d_1,d_2,k)=(2,2,1),(3,3,1),(3,4,1),(3,3,2),(4,4,2),(4,5,2)\), it is 1, 4, 6, 2, 8, 12 (overlap_tor.json). Those are the values of \(k(d_1-k)(d_2-k)\), as the monomial argument predicts. That is the formula the record gives for the degree-3 shortfall of member additivity on the functional top algebra, where the record also reports agreement with the freeness prediction over the joint span. The six configurations here were chosen to test the formula and are not claimed to be the record's measured ones.

What this means

  • For two members on a free joint span, (b) is exactly the vanishing of \(Q\): their ideals may meet only in products and common generators. When both members constrain shared directions, \(Q\) can be nonzero, as for selectors. Such members can be merged into one member on \(W_1+W_2\). thm:generic-span-members covers the merged member if it is satisfiable and its span basis has a seeded single-row projection.
  • Pairwise conditions are not enough. A linear dependency among forms of different members produces syzygies outside the member-supported and Koszul span, even when every pair of spans is independent. So (b) for the inventory depends on its dependencies, not only on overlaps. This is the dependency structure the recorded budget-cluster dichotomy classified for locality: consistent clusters are local, inconsistent ones fail.
  • Uniformly random forms have no small dependencies. \(s\) forms in a space of dimension about \(N^2\) are dependent with probability about \(3^{s-N^2}\). Adversarial inventories can have them, since the budget's clauses form dependent clusters freely.

Next: dependency-induced syzygies for wide tops. For members whose tops are products of \(w\) forms, find the least degree at which a linear dependency among \(s\) forms of different members yields a syzygy outside the member-supported and Koszul span. Compare it with \(D\). If it exceeds \(D\) for the inventory's widths, (b) holds in range despite dependencies. If not, compare the extra syzygies with the budget-cluster dichotomy.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: thm:relative-gluing (hypothesis (b) and its union of generating sets), lem:tensor-splitting-locality and lem:kunneth-component-locality, ex:member-configurations-free, and lem:span-transfer's use of the cover. The claim search (members, overlapping spans, intersection, Tor, shared forms) found ex:member-configurations-free, whose shortfall formula this explains. The check computes the entry's quantity and was read from its JSON. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed the Tor identity, the base change to \(S\) and the passage to \(A\). It required these changes, all adopted:

  • common generators: the quotient is \(Q\), with the \(I_{12}T\) term, and it equals Tor only without them;
  • the selector values restated for \(Q\), with the monomial proof;
  • the free-complement consequence identified as lem:tensor-splitting-locality;
  • the converse in \(A\) written out;
  • the relation to the record stated as matching its formula;
  • "What this means" weakened;
  • the proposed next step replaced. It claimed that pairwise vanishing suffices, which the three-selector configuration refutes.

The changes correct or weaken, so no further pass was made.

Circuit syzygies: a dependency among s clauses adds one syzygy in degree s(w−1)+1, which lifts exactly when the cluster is consistent and derives the resolvent otherwise

24 September 2026 · Working proof (circuit syzygies) · Hypothesis (b) for single-clause members whose forms have one linear dependency; cycle odd-prime-dependency-degree. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The overlap Tor entry showed that a linear dependency among forms of different members breaks hypothesis (b) of relative gluing, even when every pair of spans is independent. The missing implication is the degree at which such a dependency acts for wide tops, and whether the syzygies it creates lift. Relative gluing needs lifting, not splitting: its proof uses (b) only to write every top syzygy through \(D\) as a combination of liftable ones, as in the component-hypothesis criterion.

General statement. prop:circuit-syzygies: over \(\mathbb F_3\), take \(s\ge2\) single-clause members \(C_i=(\Lambda_i-a_i)M_i\). Each \(M_i\) is a product of \(w-1\) linear factors \(Y_{i,t}-b_{i,t}\). The linear parts of the \(\Lambda_i\) form one circuit, \(\sum_i\lambda_i=0\), so \(\sum_i\Lambda_i\) is a constant \(c\). The linear parts \(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_{s-1}\) and all \(y_{i,t}\) are linearly independent. Suppose the top algebra is free through \(D\) over the truncated algebra of their span. Then, through \(D\), the top syzygies are spanned by member-supported (Frobenius) syzygies, cross-member Koszul syzygies, and \(A\)-multiples of one circuit syzygy \(\sigma=(\prod_{j\ne i}m_j)_i\) of degree \(s(w-1)+1\). As polynomials, \(\sum_i\prod_{j\ne i}M_j\cdot C_i=(c-\sum_ia_i)\prod_jM_j\). So \(\sigma\) lifts exactly when the cluster is consistent (\(\sum a_i=c\)). The base plus the clauses then has no fall below \(D\) and no PC refutation of degree \(D\) over the weak base in its stability range. When the cluster is inconsistent, \(\sigma\) is liftable if and only if the homogenized resolvent \(R^{\rm h}\), \(R=\prod_jM_j\) of degree \(s(w-1)\), lies in the constraint ideal. Otherwise there is a fall in degree \(s(w-1)\). Adding \(R\) makes \(\sigma\) liftable. This is the syzygy form of the recorded budget-cluster dichotomy and resolvent absorption. Circuits with \(s(w-1)+1>D\) do not act below \(D\).

Setting

Over \(\mathbb F_3\), the base is the weak unary base, \(A\) is its top algebra, and \(B\) is its homogenized algebra. Clause \(i\) is \(C_i=(\Lambda_i-a_i)M_i\) with \(M_i=\prod_{t<w}(Y_{i,t}-b_{i,t})\), all forms affine with \(\mathbb F_3\) coefficients, and linear parts \(\lambda_i\), \(y_{i,t}\). The tops are \(P_i=\lambda_im_i\), \(m_i=\prod_ty_{i,t}\). The circuit is \(\sum_i\lambda_i=0\), after rescaling each \(\Lambda_i\) and \(a_i\) by a nonzero constant, which multiplies \(C_i\) by a unit. Then \(\sum_i\Lambda_i\) is a constant, called \(c\). Any proper subset of the \(\lambda_i\) is linearly independent: a relation among them would be a multiple of the circuit, whose coefficients are all nonzero. Over \(\mathbb F_3\), the cube of every linear form lies in the ideal of the cubes of any basis, so \(T(V)\) does not depend on the basis. Let \(V\) be spanned by \(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_{s-1}\) and the \(y_{i,t}\), all linearly independent, so \(\dim V=s-1+s(w-1)\). Let \(T(V)=\mathrm{Sym}(V)/(\text{cubes})=T(\lambda)\otimes T(y)\). Assume the minimal free cover \(T(V)\otimes C\to A\) is bijective in degrees \(\le D\). By thm:projection-freeness this holds, for instance, when these forms are jointly affinely independent on enough holes.

The syzygies

Lemma. In \(T(V)\), in degrees \(\le D\), every syzygy of \(P_1,\dots,P_s\) is a combination of the Frobenius syzygies \(\ell^2e_i\), for \(\ell\) a factor of \(P_i\), the Koszul syzygies \(P_je_i-P_ie_j\), and \(T(V)\)-multiples of \(\sigma=(\prod_{j\ne i}m_j)_i\). No syzygy of degree below \(s(w-1)+1\) needs \(\sigma\).

Proof. Grade \(T(V)\) by the exponent vector \(\beta\) in the \(y\)-variables. The \(\lambda\)'s have degree 0 in this grading, and \(P_i\) has degree \(\delta_i\), the indicator of member \(i\)'s variables. The supports of the \(\delta_i\) are disjoint. The syzygy module is graded, so take a syzygy of degree \(\beta\). Its component \(a_i\) is \(y^{\beta-\delta_i}\alpha_i\) with \(\alpha_i\in T(\lambda)\), and it is nonzero only if \(\beta\ge\delta_i\).

  • If some entry of \(\beta\) is at least 3, then \(y^\beta=0\) and each term \(a_iP_i\) vanishes separately. A nonzero \(a_i\) then has exponent 2 on a variable of \(\delta_i\), since \(\beta-\delta_i\) has entries at most 2. So \(a_ie_i\) is a multiple of the Frobenius syzygy of that factor.
  • Otherwise every \(y^{\beta-\delta_i}m_i=y^\beta\ne0\), and the equation reads \(y^\beta\sum_{i\in I}\alpha_i\lambda_i=0\), with \(I=\{i:\beta\ge\delta_i\}\). Since \(T(V)=T(\lambda)\otimes T(y)\), this is \(\sum_{i\in I}\alpha_i\lambda_i=0\) in \(T(\lambda)\).
    • If \(I\ne\{1,\dots,s\}\), the \(\lambda_i\), \(i\in I\), are linearly independent, so they are coordinates. In the truncated ring the syzygies of coordinates are generated by \(\lambda_j e_i-\lambda_ie_j\) and \(\lambda_i^2e_i\). The first becomes \(y^{\beta-\delta_i-\delta_j}(P_je_i-P_ie_j)\), since \(\beta\ge\delta_i+\delta_j\) for disjoint supports. The second is Frobenius.
    • If \(I=\{1,\dots,s\}\), substitute \(\lambda_s=-\sum_{i<s}\lambda_i\). Then \((\alpha_i-\alpha_s)_{i<s}\) is a syzygy of coordinates, so \(\alpha=\alpha_s(1,\dots,1)\) plus Koszul and Frobenius terms. The term \(\alpha_s(1,\dots,1)\) gives \(y^{\beta-\sum\delta_j}\alpha_s\sigma\).

\(\sigma\) is needed only when \(\beta\ge\sum_j\delta_j\), that is, in total degree at least \(s(w-1)+1\). \(\square\)

\(\sigma\) is not in the span of the other syzygies. Setting all \(\lambda\) to 0 kills every Koszul syzygy and every Frobenius syzygy of a \(\lambda\)-factor, and it leaves \(\sigma\) unchanged. The remaining Frobenius syzygies have components divisible by the square of a \(y\)-factor of their own member, while \(\sigma_i=\prod_{j\ne i}m_j\) is squarefree in the other members' variables. For \(s=2\) the circuit is a shared form, \(\lambda_2=-\lambda_1\), and \(\sigma=(m_2,m_1)\) is the syzygy that performs the resolution step on that form. Clauses with equal factors on the shared form have dependent \(y\)'s only when their other factors agree too, which is outside the setting.

Lifting

As polynomials, \(\sum_i\bigl(\prod_{j\ne i}M_j\bigr)C_i=\prod_jM_j\cdot\sum_i(\Lambda_i-a_i)=(c-\sum_ia_i)\prod_jM_j\). Homogenizing at degree \(s(w-1)+1\) gives \(\sum_i\tilde\sigma_iC_i^{\rm h}=z\,(c-\sum a_i)\,R^{\rm h}\), with \(R=\prod_jM_j\) of degree \(s(w-1)\).

Proposition (circuit syzygies). In the setting above, with \(D\) at most the base's stability range:

  1. If \(\sum_ia_i=c\) (a consistent cluster), every top syzygy through \(D\) is a combination of liftable ones. The weak base plus \(C_1,\dots,C_s\) has no fall below \(D\) and no PC refutation of degree \(D\).
  2. If \(\sum_ia_i\ne c\), then \(\sigma\) is liftable if and only if \(R^{\rm h}\in J_U\). In any case \(zR^{\rm h}\in J_U\), so either \(R^{\rm h}\in J_U\) or there is a fall in degree \(s(w-1)\). Adding \(R\) as a constraint makes \(\sigma\) liftable. The enlarged family is not analysed here: its locality in the recorded setting is thm:resolvent-absorption. Its new syzygies \(\prod_{j\ne i}m_je_i-\lambda_ie_R\) lift exactly and sum to \(\sigma\).

Proof. For part 1, apply the lemma in \(A\) through the cover, as in the span-transfer argument. Frobenius syzygies \(\ell^2e_i\) of a linear factor \(L-a\) of \(C_i\) lift. With the lift \(((L-a)^{\rm h})^2\) the correction is \(zC_i^{\rm h}\in J_U\), because \((L-a)^3-(L-a)\) lies in the base ideal in degree 3 for affine forms over \(\mathbb F_3\). Koszul syzygies lift exactly, by step 2 of the relative gluing proof. \(\sigma\) lifts with correction 0 by the identity. Liftable syzygies are closed under combinations. Steps 4 and 5 of the relative gluing proof then give no fall below \(D\) from the base's \(z\)-injectivity (thm:weak-base-stability-quadratic), and no refutation, since no generator is a nonzero constant. For part 2, the identity gives \(\rho=(c-\sum a_i)R^{\rm h}\). Two lifts differ by \(z\) times an element of \(J_U\), since they agree modulo \(z\), so \(\rho\) is determined modulo \(J_U\). Hence \(\sigma\) is liftable if and only if \(R^{\rm h}\in J_U\). \(\square\)

What this means

  • This is the syzygy form of the recorded results. thm:budget-cluster-dichotomy found consistent clusters local and inconsistent ones failing at degree \(\sum_b(k_b-1)\). thm:resolvent-absorption added the resolvent. Here the obstruction is the circuit syzygy's lift, at degree \(s(w-1)\), and the repair is the same resolvent. That \(R^{\rm h}\notin J_U\) for inconsistent clusters, so that a fall really occurs, is the dichotomy's result and is not reproved here.
  • Only circuits with \(s(w-1)+1\le D\) matter. For clauses of width \(k\) at \(D=(4p-1)(p-1)k=22k\) (\(p=3\)), that is \(s\le22\) roughly, as in the dichotomy's count. Uniformly random forms rarely have such small circuits: \(s\) forms in a space of dimension about \(N^2\) are dependent with probability about \(3^{s-N^2}\). Adversarial inventories can.
  • The proposition treats one circuit with otherwise independent factors. Interacting circuits and shared factors are not covered. Several circuits can create new ones after resolvents are added. That is the saturation question, whose finite check failed for dense overlapping pairs (saturated locality).

Next: two circuits sharing clauses, the smallest interaction. Compute the syzygies of four clauses whose forms satisfy two independent circuits, by the same grading. Test whether they are generated by the two circuit syzygies, Koszul and Frobenius syzygies. If a new syzygy appears, find its lift, and compare with the saturated-locality failure.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: thm:relative-gluing with its definition of liftable syzygies and steps 2 to 5; thm:budget-cluster-dichotomy and thm:resolvent-absorption (summaries and statements); thm:projection-freeness; lem:span-transfer's use of the cover; thm:weak-base-stability-quadratic. The claim search (dependency, circuit, resolvent, syzygy, cluster) returned the budget-cluster results, which this rederives on the syzygy level. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed the lemma (both cases, the Koszul conversion, the full-circuit substitution, the degree, and the independence of \(\sigma\)), the identity and its homogenization, the passage through the cover, and the arithmetic. Its Python check over \(\mathbb F_3\) for \(s=3\), \(w=2\) found the listed generators short exactly in degrees 4 to 7 without \(\sigma\), and complete with it. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the \(s=2\) remark kept inside the setting;
  • part 2 stated as an if-and-only-if, with the fall alternative and without claiming non-membership;
  • \(c\) defined rather than assumed, with the rescaling explained;
  • basis independence of \(T(V)\) and independence of proper subsets of the circuit;
  • the Frobenius lift's correction stated exactly;
  • the enlarged family attributed to thm:resolvent-absorption.

The changes correct or weaken, so no further pass was made.

Head dependencies: clauses whose only dependent factors are their heads glue exactly when the head system is consistent

24 September 2026 · Working proof (head dependencies) · Single-clause members with arbitrary dependencies among one factor each; cycle odd-prime-two-circuits. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The circuit syzygies entry treated one dependency among the forms of single-clause members. Its next step asked about two circuits sharing clauses, the first case where dependencies interact. The recorded failure of saturated locality (ex:saturated-locality-failure) involved clauses whose spans overlap in several dimensions. The missing implication is (b), or rather generation by liftable syzygies, for many clauses with many dependencies.

General statement. thm:head-dependencies: over \(\mathbb F_3\), take \(n\) single-clause members \(C_i=(\Lambda_i-a_i)M_i\), where each \(M_i\) is a product of \(w_i-1\) linear factors, the private factors. Let the heads' linear parts \(\lambda_i\) be nonzero and satisfy arbitrary linear relations. Let the private factors' linear parts be linearly independent of each other and of the span of the heads. Suppose the top algebra is free through \(D\) over the truncated algebra of the whole span. Then the top syzygies through \(D\) are generated by Frobenius, cross-member Koszul and circuit syzygies. The circuit syzygies are \(\sigma_\gamma=(\gamma_i\prod_{j\in\gamma,j\ne i}m_j)_{i\in\gamma}\), one for each circuit \(\gamma\) of the heads, of degree \(\sum_{j\in\gamma}(w_j-1)+1\). Each \(\sigma_\gamma\) lifts exactly when its circuit is consistent. All circuits are consistent exactly when the head system \(\{\Lambda_i=a_i\}\) is solvable over \(\mathbb F_3\). In that case the weak base plus the clauses has no fall below \(D\) and no PC refutation of degree \(D\), in the base's stability range. When some circuit is inconsistent, its syzygy lifts if and only if its resolvent lies in the constraint ideal. This generalizes prop:circuit-syzygies from one circuit to any dependency structure among the heads. With a consistent head system, head dependencies cause no fall. The recorded failures of saturated locality lie outside this setting.

Setting and the syzygies

As in the circuit-syzygies entry, with \(n\) clauses. \(C_i=(\Lambda_i-a_i)M_i\), \(M_i=\prod_t(Y_{i,t}-b_{i,t})\), tops \(P_i=\lambda_im_i\). The linear parts \(y_{i,t}\) are independent and independent of \(H=\operatorname{span}(\lambda_i)\). \(V=H\oplus\operatorname{span}(y)\), and \(T(V)=T(H)\otimes T(y)\), which does not depend on the basis. All \(\lambda_i\ne0\). The relation space is \(\mathcal R=\{\rho\in\mathbb F_3^n:\sum_i\rho_i\lambda_i=0\}\). Its circuits are its nonzero vectors of minimal support, with their scalar multiples, which are again circuits.

Lemma. In \(T(V)\), every syzygy of \(P_1,\dots,P_n\) is a combination of Frobenius syzygies, Koszul syzygies \(P_je_i-P_ie_j\), and multiples of the circuit syzygies \(\sigma_\gamma\).

Proof. Grade by the \(y\)-exponent \(\beta\), with the members' supports \(\delta_i\) disjoint. A syzygy of degree \(\beta\) has components \(a_i=y^{\beta-\delta_i}\alpha_i\), \(\alpha_i\in T(H)\), for \(i\in I=\{i:\beta\ge\delta_i\}\). If some entry of \(\beta\) is at least 3, each component is a multiple of a Frobenius syzygy of a private factor, as in the circuit-syzygies entry. Otherwise the equation is \(\sum_{i\in I}\alpha_i\lambda_i=0\) in \(T(H)\).

Choose a basis \(B\subseteq I\) of \(\operatorname{span}(\lambda_i:i\in I)\), and write \(\lambda_j=\sum_{b\in B}c_{jb}\lambda_b\) for \(j\in I\setminus B\). Then \(\sum_{b}(\alpha_b+\sum_{j\notin B}c_{jb}\alpha_j)\lambda_b=0\) is a syzygy of coordinates, so it is generated by Koszul syzygies \(\lambda_{b'}e_b-\lambda_be_{b'}\) and Frobenius syzygies \(\lambda_b^2e_b\). This holds in \(T(H)\) even when the \(\lambda_b\) do not span \(H\), since \(T(H)=T(\lambda_B)\otimes T(\text{complement})\) is free over \(T(\lambda_B)\). Hence \(\alpha=\sum_{j\notin B}\alpha_j\rho^{(j)}\) plus such terms, with \(\rho^{(j)}=e_j-\sum_bc_{jb}e_b\in\mathcal R\), supported in \(B\cup\{j\}\subseteq I\). Every relation is a sum of circuits whose supports lie in its own support, a standard fact for the circuits of a linear matroid. So \(\alpha\) is a \(T(H)\)-combination of circuits \(\gamma\) with \(\operatorname{supp}\gamma\subseteq I\), plus Koszul and Frobenius terms. Translate back to \(T(V)\). A Koszul term \(\lambda_{b'}e_b-\lambda_be_{b'}\) becomes \(y^{\beta-\delta_b-\delta_{b'}}(P_{b'}e_b-P_be_{b'})\), since \(\beta\ge\delta_b+\delta_{b'}\). A circuit term becomes \(y^{\beta-\sum_{j\in\gamma}\delta_j}\sigma_\gamma\), since \(\beta\ge\sum_{j\in\gamma}\delta_j\). \(\square\)

Lifting

For a circuit \(\gamma\), \(\sum_{i\in\gamma}\gamma_i\Lambda_i\) is a constant \(c_\gamma\), and as polynomials

\[\sum_{i\in\gamma}\gamma_i\Bigl(\prod_{j\in\gamma,j\ne i}M_j\Bigr)C_i=\Bigl(c_\gamma-\sum_{i\in\gamma}\gamma_ia_i\Bigr)R_\gamma,\qquad R_\gamma=\prod_{j\in\gamma}M_j.\]

Homogenized, the right side is \(z\) times \((c_\gamma-\sum\gamma_ia_i)R_\gamma^{\rm h}\). The circuit is consistent when \(\sum_{i\in\gamma}\gamma_ia_i=c_\gamma\). All circuits are consistent exactly when every relation \(\rho\in\mathcal R\) satisfies \(\sum\rho_ia_i=\sum\rho_i\Lambda_i\) (a constant). By linear algebra, that says the affine system \(\Lambda_i=a_i\) is solvable.

Theorem (head dependencies). In this setting, suppose the minimal free cover \(T(V)\otimes C\to A\) of the weak top algebra is bijective in degrees \(\le D\), and \(D\) is in the weak base's stability range.

  1. If the head system \(\{\Lambda_i=a_i\}\) is solvable, every top syzygy through \(D\) is a combination of liftable syzygies. The weak base plus \(C_1,\dots,C_n\) has no fall below \(D\) and no PC refutation of degree \(D\).
  2. Otherwise, for each inconsistent circuit \(\gamma\) with \(\deg\sigma_\gamma\le D\), \(\sigma_\gamma\) is liftable if and only if \(R_\gamma^{\rm h}\in J_U\), and \(zR_\gamma^{\rm h}\in J_U\) always holds.

Proof. Pass the lemma to \(A\) through the cover, as in lem:span-transfer. Frobenius syzygies of linear factors lift, with correction \(zC_i^{\rm h}\in J_U\). Koszul syzygies lift exactly. Consistent circuit syzygies lift with correction 0. Liftable syzygies are closed under combinations, and steps 4 and 5 of the relative gluing proof give the conclusions of part 1. Part 2 is the circuit-syzygies argument for each circuit. \(\square\)

What this means

  • With a consistent head system, dependencies among heads cause no fall, however many and however entangled. This needs the private factors independent, and the whole span free through \(D\), which holds, for instance, when its basis has a seeded single-row projection. Two circuits sharing clauses are a special case.
  • Inconsistent circuits need their resolvents, as thm:budget-cluster-dichotomy and thm:resolvent-absorption found. A resolvent's private part is the union of its clauses' private parts, so absorbing it takes the family out of this setting.
  • The recorded failures of ex:saturated-locality-failure lie outside this setting. Two clauses whose spans meet in dimension 2 cannot be arranged so, since two heads give a relation space of dimension at most 1. That check also used form-space locality on \(\mathbb F_3^4\) and \(\mathbb F_3^5\), where this freeness hypothesis is not established. This theorem does not explain those failures. It only excludes one class of families.
  • For an inventory, the theorem needs every relation among all factors to involve only the heads, one designated factor per clause, with the private factors independent of everything else.

Next: combine this with thm:generic-span-members. Dependencies inside a small span can be absorbed into one member, since that theorem covers any satisfiable member on a generic span. The combined claim to prove: members on spans \(W_i\), each Gröbner-augmented, glue when every relation across members involves only one designated head form per member, the rest of the spans are independent, and the head system is consistent. This would cover families that combine overlaps inside members with head dependencies across them.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the circuit-syzygies entry (setting, lemma, lifting, proposition); thm:relative-gluing with liftability and steps 4 and 5; thm:budget-cluster-dichotomy and thm:resolvent-absorption; ex:saturated-locality-failure. No computation of mine; the reviewer's check is reported below. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed the reduction to head syzygies, the supports of the relations, the translation back to \(T(V)\), the polynomial identity, the equivalence of circuit consistency with solvability, and both parts of the theorem. Its Python check over \(\mathbb F_3\) used four width-2 clauses with heads \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_1+\lambda_2,\lambda_1-\lambda_2\), which form four circuits of size 3 sharing clauses. In every degree from 4 to 13, the Frobenius, Koszul and circuit syzygies span all syzygies, for example 229 of 229 in degree 6. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the hypothesis \(\lambda_i\ne0\), without which a clause can be a nonzero constant;
  • circuits taken with scalars, and the flatness remark for syzygies of coordinates;
  • the claim about the recorded non-locality restricted to consistent heads;
  • projection freeness named as sufficient only;
  • the relation to ex:saturated-locality-failure stated as "outside this setting", with the reason;
  • the goal-setting condition made precise;
  • the next step made well posed.

The changes add a needed hypothesis and weaken interpretations, so no further pass was made.

Route review: on a free joint span, satisfiable families need no splitting; the open core is gluing beyond the free range

24 September 2026 · Route review with a working corollary (joint-span families) · The (b) and (c) line of relative gluing; cycle odd-prime-members-with-heads. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The head-dependencies entry proposed combining generic span members with head dependencies across members. Before proving it, this cycle checked what the combination would add. It adds nothing beyond one step: the whole family can be treated as one member. That changes the line's picture, so this entry is a route review.

General statement. cor:joint-span-families: over \(\mathbb F_p\), take any family of reduced \(\mathbb F_p\)-polynomial constraints of degree \(\le D\) in linear forms on the weak unary board. Suppose a basis of the family's joint span has a seeded single-row projection at \(t=D\) with \(N\ge(p-1)(D+1)(D+1+d)\), \(d\) the joint dimension, and \(m\ge D\). Suppose also that the family's allowed set in \(\mathbb F_p^d\) is nonempty. Then the weak base plus the family has no PC refutation of degree \(D\). This is thm:generic-span-members applied to the family as a single member, so hypothesis (b) is not used. It contains the consistent cases of prop:circuit-syzygies and thm:head-dependencies, since a solvable head system satisfies every clause, though not their exact-lift and no-fall statements for the unaugmented family. So (b) is needed only when the joint span is not free, beyond about \(N/((p-1)(D+1))\) dimensions under the seed count and in any case beyond \(\dim A_1\).

The corollary

Proof. Let \(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_d\) be a basis of the joint span and write each constraint as \(h_k(\ell)\) with \(h_k\) reduced, which is free at degree \(D\) by the reduction remark of the span-transfer entry. thm:generic-span-members, part 2, applies to the single member \(\{h_k(\ell)\}\): its hypotheses are the seeded projection, the hole and row counts, reducedness, degree \(\le D\) and a nonempty allowed set. For single clauses \(C_i=(\Lambda_i-a_i)M_i\) with a solvable head system, any solution of the heads satisfies every clause, so the allowed set is nonempty. \(\square\)

The circuit and head results remain useful for what the corollary does not give. They show that the family itself, without Gröbner augmentation, has no fall. They name the one syzygy per circuit and its degree. And they describe the inconsistent case through the resolvent.

Review of the line

General claim of the line. The goal's inventory, compiled to product constraints over the weak base, has no PC refutation of degree \(D=O(\log n)\). Relative gluing proves this from (a), no falls of the base, and from the liftability of all top syzygies, which (b) and (c) supply.

What has been proved since the last review (projection review):

  • Every satisfiable member of degree \(\le D\) on a generic span, dependent forms included, satisfies (c) and (d) (generic span members).
  • For two members on a free joint span, (b) is the vanishing of \((I_1\cap I_2)/(I_1I_2+I_{12})\) (overlap Tor).
  • Circuits among heads give one syzygy each, which lifts exactly when consistent (circuits, heads).

With the corollary, all of this is subsumed on free joint spans. Satisfiable families there are not refutable at degree \(D\).

What the goal needs. The inventory has \(N^K\) constraints, for every \(K\), on forms spanning up to \(\dim A_1=(N+1)(N-1)\) dimensions. The free range is at most about \(N/(2(D+1))\) under the seed count, and freeness over a span of dimension \(d\) needs \(d\le\dim A_1\) in any case. So the goal lies beyond the free range. There the syzygies are not controlled by any recorded result.

Falsification attempt. The line's claim could fail beyond the free range in two recorded ways:

  • Random selectors on the weak base are refuted exactly at the Taylor count \(M=\lceil\gamma_3/(\gamma_1-1)\rceil\) (ex:selector-semiregular-thresholds). Those families are not satisfiable in the span sense. Their values are random, so they fall outside the corollary. They show that beyond the free range, satisfiability or some other structure is indispensable.
  • Pencils stay additive past \(\gamma_1\) (ex:member-configurations-free). That is dimension evidence beyond the free range, not syzygy splitting.

Nothing recorded decides whether satisfiable families beyond the free range have falls.

Assessment of this line. The member side is settled for generic spans. The recent cycles restate, at the syzygy level, results already implied on free spans. The line's content is now the original batched question in algebraic form: the liftability of top syzygies of a satisfiable constraint family whose joint span is not free. The route description calls this the batched mechanism the window needs, and nothing recorded provides it. The line has not produced evidence either way on it. Further refinement on free spans would not advance the goal.

Next step, on the highest-risk item (odd-prime-clause-transfer). Test the core directly at the smallest informative size. Over the weak base on 3 rows and 18 holes at \(D=3\), inside the base's stability range, take planted families of generic row-dependent selectors. Each selector's value is set by one fixed matching, so every family is satisfiable, and some families are larger than the Taylor count. That count is about \(18065/50\approx361\), from \(\gamma_1=51\) and \(\gamma_3=18065\) (mf_3x18_D3.json). Measure \(z\)-injectivity below 3, which is falls, not refutation, since satisfiable families are never refuted. If planted families beyond the count have no falls, their syzygies beyond the Taylor span lift. That would be the first evidence for a mechanism beyond freeness. If they fall, the no-fall route cannot glue large families, and the base must absorb them. Run a sizing case first. The controls are random-valued families at the same size, which the record shows refuted, and planted families below the count.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: thm:generic-span-members (hypotheses and part 2), prop:circuit-syzygies, thm:head-dependencies, ex:selector-semiregular-thresholds, ex:member-configurations-free, and the in-range values in mf_3x18_D3.json. The corollary is a direct application of a reviewed theorem, and no new argument is involved beyond satisfiability of solvable heads. So no reviewer pass was run. The subsumption of the consistent circuit and head cases was missed by the reviews of those entries and is recorded here.

Planted families beyond the count pin their point: every selector past the top dimension adds one fall, so no-fall gluing stops there

24 September 2026 · Finite check and a conjecture · Degree-2 falls of planted and random generic selector families over the weak base, 3 rows and 18 holes; cycle odd-prime-planted-families. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The joint-span review found that satisfiable families on a free joint span need no splitting. The goal lies beyond the free range. It asked whether satisfiable (planted) families of generic selectors beyond the Taylor count still have no falls, which would indicate a gluing mechanism beyond freeness. If they fall, the no-fall route cannot glue large families.

General statement. conj:planted-excess-falls: over \(\mathbb F_3\), on the weak unary base in its degree-2 stability range, a planted family of \(M\) generic selectors has \(\dim\ker(z:B_1\to B_2)=\min\bigl(\gamma_1,\max(0,M-\tau_2)\bigr)\). A planted family is one whose values avoid the forms' values at a fixed matching, so it is satisfiable. Here \(\tau_2\) is the dimension of the degree-2 top space the selectors can fill, and \(\gamma_1=\dim A_1\). So planted families have no falls up to the count. Each selector beyond it adds exactly one derived linear consequence, until the family's degree-2 closure is the whole ideal of the planted point. Random-valued families are refuted instead. ex:planted-excess-falls-check confirms this exactly at 3 rows and 18 holes, where \(\tau_2=1218\) and \(\gamma_1=51\).

Decidability and method

At degree 3 the test is out of reach this way. Singular took 28 s for 25 dense selectors and exceeded 90 s for 50, against a count of about 361. At degree 2 the same question is linear algebra. The base is \(z\)-injective below 2 for \(N\ge8\), and the Taylor count at degree 2 is the dimension \(\tau_2\) of the top space. fall_d2.py works on multilinear monomials of degree \(\le2\) with no two cells in one column, 1432 coordinates. Booleanity and column exclusions are degree-2 generators, so reducing modulo them stays inside \(V_2\). \(V_2\) is spanned by the reduced selectors and the products \((r_i-1)m\), \(\deg m\le1\). \(\ker z_1=\dim(V_2\cap P_{\le1})-\dim V_1\), computed as \(\operatorname{rank}V_2-\operatorname{rank}(\text{top part})-3\). It reproduces Singular's values at \(M=200\) and 400: top-algebra dimensions 1018 and 818, \(\ker z=0\) (validate_d2.json). It uses the same random stream as planted_fall.py. Planted values satisfy \(v_t\ne\ell_t(x^*)\), since \(1-(\ell-v)^2=0\) means \(\ell\ne v\), for the matching \(x^*\) with row \(i\) in hole \(i\).

Results

All on 3 rows and 18 holes, seed 1, values read from the JSON files:

  • Planted, \(M=200,400,1000,1218\): \(\ker z_1=0\) (validate_d2.json, below_count.json, at_count.json).
  • Planted, \(M=1219\): 1; \(M=1240\): 22 (at_count.json); \(M=1300,1500,2000\): 51 (planted_beyond.json). \(V_2\) then has rank 1431 of 1432: every polynomial of degree \(\le2\) vanishing at \(x^*\), and 1 is not derived.
  • Random values, \(M=1000\): \(\ker z_1=0\) (below_count.json); \(M=1300,1500,2000\): 1 is derived, a refutation at degree 2 (random_beyond.json).
  • The top part has rank \(1159+\) until it saturates at 1377, the full degree-2 coordinate space. The base's own tops take 159, so \(\tau_2=1377-159=1218\).

What this means

  • Below the count, planted and random families behave alike and have no falls. Beyond it, the difference is satisfiability. Random families are refuted. Planted families pin their point: each extra selector forces one more linear consequence, as a maximal-rank count predicts. This matches ex:planted-overload-thresholds, where pinned forms derived their values and refutation thresholds followed the conditioned base's count.
  • So the no-fall route of relative gluing cannot glue dense satisfiable families. Their closure is a restriction, here the ideal of a point. The recorded way to handle such members is closure into the base. For a pinned family the closure is the ideal of the pinned partial assignment, and the base conditioned on it is again a weak base, on fewer rows and holes.
  • For the goal this points to conditioning. Dense parts of the inventory act as restrictions of PHP, and hardness must survive them. This is the restriction-mixture line, parked at its top-size lemma.

Next: conditioned gluing. Prove that the weak base together with the ideal of a partial matching \(\rho\) on \(r\) rows has no falls below \(D\) whenever the restricted board, \(m-r\) rows and \(N-r\) holes, is in the stability range. The base conditioned on \(\rho\) is then a valid base for relative gluing, and pinned members can be absorbed into it. Then test a family that pins one row and leaves the rest generic, against the prediction from the conditioned count.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the joint-span review's proposed test and counts; ex:selector-semiregular-thresholds and ex:planted-overload-thresholds (the conditioning interpretation); the fall formula of the generic-members checker. The degree-2 kernel was validated against Singular on two recorded-style cases before use, and all numbers are read from the result files. A sign error in the first planted runs (values equal to the forms at \(x^*\), which makes \(x^*\) violate every selector) was found before any result was used, and those runs were discarded. The conjecture was searched under planted, pinning, closure and dense selectors. The nearest records are ex:planted-overload-thresholds and ex:confined-family-falls. No proof is claimed, so no reviewer pass was run.

Conditioned base: closing the pins of a partial matching gives the restricted weak base, so pinned parts can be absorbed

24 September 2026 · Working proof (conditioned base) · Base condition (a) after pinning a partial matching; cycle odd-prime-conditioned-gluing. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The planted-families entry found that dense satisfiable families pin their point, so no-fall gluing stops at the count, and dense parts act as restrictions. Its next step asked for the interface: when does the weak base together with a pinned partial matching satisfy hypothesis (a), no falls below \(D\)?

General statement. prop:conditioned-base: over any field, let \(\rho\) be a partial matching on a set \(R\) of \(r\) rows of the weak unary board. Consider the closed pins: \(x_{ij}-[j=\rho(i)]\) for \(i\in R\) and all \(j\), and \(x_{i'j}\) for \(i'\notin R\) and \(j\in\rho(R)\). The homogenized algebra of the weak base plus the closed pins is isomorphic, as a graded \(\mathbb F[z]\)-algebra, to the homogenized weak base on the \((m-r)\times(N-r)\) board. So, under the field hypotheses of thm:weak-base-stability-quadratic, the conditioned base has no falls below \(D\) when \(N-r\ge(p-1)D^2\) and \(m-r\ge D\). Its top algebra is the restricted board's. With only the open pins \(x_{i\rho(i)}-1\), there are falls (for \(r\ge1\), \(m\ge2\), \(N\ge2\)). And a PC refutation of degree \(D\) of the weak base plus any constraints restricts to one of the restricted base plus the restricted constraints. So a lower bound for the restricted system gives one for the original.

Proof

  1. Elimination. The homogenized closed pins are \(x_{ij}-[j=\rho(i)]z\) and \(x_{i'j}\), linear and homogeneous. Quotienting \(\mathbb F[x,z]\) by them substitutes these values for the fixed variables and leaves the polynomial ring in the free variables (\(i\notin R\), \(j\notin\rho(R)\)) and \(z\).
  2. The base generators. Under the substitution:
    • Booleanity of a fixed variable becomes \(c^2z^2-cz\cdot z=0\) for \(c\in\{0,1\}\).
    • A column exclusion with a fixed variable becomes 0. In a pinned column \(\rho(i)\), every variable other than the pinned cell is fixed to 0, because \(\rho\) is injective: a second pinned row \(i''\) has \(x_{i''\rho(i)}\) fixed to 0, while \(\rho(i)=\rho(i'')\) would map \(x_{i\rho(i)}x_{i''\rho(i)}\) to \(z^2\). In a free column, a variable of a pinned row is fixed to 0.
    • A pinned row's equation becomes \(z-z=0\).
    • A free row's equation becomes the restricted row equation \(\sum_{j\notin\rho(R)}x_{i'j}-z\).
    • Generators among free variables are unchanged.
    So the quotient is the restricted homogenized weak base, as a graded \(\mathbb F[z]\)-algebra, and \(z\)-injectivity transfers degree by degree.
  3. Open pins fall. Let \(r\ge1\), \(m\ge2\), \(N\ge2\), and \(i'\ne i\). With only the open pins added, homogenized, \(z\,x_{i'\rho(i)}=x_{i'\rho(i)}x_{i\rho(i)}-x_{i'\rho(i)}(x_{i\rho(i)}-z)\) lies in the ideal in degree 2. The degree-1 part of the ideal is spanned by the homogenized row equations and open pins, since there are no other linear generators. In a combination \(\sum_ka_k(\rho_k-z)+\sum_{i\in R}b_i(x_{i\rho(i)}-z)\), the coefficient of \(x_{i'j}\) for \(j\ne\rho(i)\) is \(a_{i'}\), which must vanish for \(x_{i'\rho(i)}\) to result. Then \(x_{i'\rho(i)}\) has coefficient 0. So \(x_{i'\rho(i)}\) is not in the ideal in degree 1, and \(z\) is not injective from degree 1 to degree 2.
  4. Restriction. Substituting the closed-pin values into a PC refutation maps each base generator to a restricted base generator or to 0, as in step 2. It maps each constraint to its restriction, and it does not raise degrees. PC rules commute with substitution. So a lower bound for the restricted system gives one for the original. If some constraint restricts to a nonzero constant, the restricted system is trivially refutable, so \(\rho\) must be chosen consistent with the constraints. \(\square\)

What this means

  • Pinned parts of a family can be absorbed: condition on the pinned matching, work on the restricted board, and keep the rest of the family restricted. The theorem then gives (a) while \(N-r\ge(p-1)D^2\) and \(m-r\ge D\). This is the range in which it applies, not a limit on pinning.
  • A conditional remark on the compiled inventory. The weak-base compiler produces selector inputs \(1-L^{p-1}\), whose tops have degree \(p-1=2\) at \(p=3\), with a PC refutation through the fixed degree \(4p-1\). Degree 3 is the first degree where a Taylor count for such tops bites, since the (F) syzygies \(\ell e\) appear there and Koszul syzygies only at degree 4. The count \(M(\gamma_1-1)\le\gamma_3\) caps selectors on distinct forms. On the PHP board, \(\gamma_1=(N+1)(N-1)\), and \(\gamma_3\) is at most the number of multilinear degree-3 monomials in distinct columns, about \(\binom N3(N+1)^3\approx N^6/6\). So the cap is of order \(N^4/6\), and beyond it Taylor generation fails. Whether the no-fall route also stops there is conj:planted-excess-falls, supported only by the degree-2 check and ex:selector-semiregular-thresholds. Whether the compiled inventory has that many distinct selector forms is not established here.
  • Conditioning helps only for dense parts supported on few rows. A dense family of generic forms on all rows constrains the whole board. How the compiled inventory's constraints sit relative to rows is the question the recorded restriction-mixture line reduced to a one-count design problem (the top-size lemma).

Next: connect the two lines. Re-read the restriction-mixture entries and the top-size lemma. Then determine whether the conditioning here, which absorbs pinned rows into the base, together with generic gluing on the restricted board, which uses projection freeness and joint-span families, supplies that one-count design.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: thm:weak-base-stability-quadratic (range and hypotheses), the weak-base compiler statement (inputs \(1-L^{p-1}\), ceiling \(4p-1\)), conj:planted-excess-falls, and ex:selector-semiregular-thresholds. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed the elimination and the restriction. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the column-exclusion case of pinned rows in free columns, with the use of injectivity of \(\rho\);
  • the open-pin identity homogenized, and its non-membership proved from the degree-1 part of the ideal, with \(r\ge1\), \(m\ge2\), \(N\ge2\);
  • the field hypotheses of the stability theorem;
  • the direction of the restriction transfer, and consistency of \(\rho\);
  • the range remark;
  • the density remark made conditional, with the count derived.

The changes correct or weaken, so no further pass was made.

One-count link: the restriction-mixture problem follows from joint freeness for member-type blocks, beyond the reach of the proved freeness methods

24 September 2026 · Working proof (a conditional reduction) · The top-size lemma's one-count problem for member-type blocks on independent random spans; cycle odd-prime-restriction-link. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The conditioned-base entry proposed connecting the gluing results with the restriction-mixture line. Under typicality, that line's top-size lemma reduces mixtures to a one-count problem (top-size lemma): a degree-\(D\) PC design for the old base plus \(n\) independent random blocks, each with \(h\) input forms, for one \(h\) in the window. The missing implication is whether the recent results supply that design.

General statement. prop:one-count-by-freeness: over \(\mathbb F_3\), on the weak unary base in its stability range, suppose three things. Each of \(n\) blocks is a satisfiable member: a set of reduced polynomial constraints of degree \(\le D\) in its \(h\) input forms. The \(nh\) forms are linearly independent. The weak top algebra is free through \(D\) over the truncated algebra of their joint span. Then the base plus the blocks has no PC refutation of degree \(D\). This is lem:span-transfer, the Gröbner augmentation and relative gluing with one member, applied to the whole family, as in cor:joint-span-families but with freeness assumed rather than obtained from seeds. For the one-count problem it leaves two gaps. First, the compiler's blocks are ENS blocks with extension variables and companions, and whether they can be replaced by members in their input forms is not established. Second, the needed freeness is over about \(nh\) generic forms. The proved methods, board seeds and projection freeness, reach only about \(N/(2(D+1))\) forms. The recorded evidence (ex:board-random-defect-pointwise) finds random systems free up to about \(\gamma_1/3\) forms at small size.

The reduction

Proof. The \(n\) members have independent spans, so their allowed sets multiply, and the family is satisfiable because each member is. Write the whole family as one member \(\{h_k(\ell)\}\) on a basis \(\ell\) of the joint span, of dimension \(nh\). A union of reduced constraint sets on independent spans is reduced for the joint member, since each constraint involves only its own member's variables. By hypothesis the minimal free cover of the top algebra over \(T=\mathbb F_3[W_1,\dots,W_{nh}]/(W_i^3)\), \(W_i\mapsto\ell_i\), is bijective in degrees \(\le D\). So lem:span-transfer applies in the form checked in the generic-span-members entry. So does the Gröbner augmentation of thm:seeded-member-condition, whose no-fall and (d) steps use only reducedness and satisfiability, together with the injectivity of the tops through \(D\). Relative gluing with one member and thm:weak-base-stability-quadratic then exclude a refutation of degree \(D\) of the augmented family, and hence of the original. \(\square\)

What the one-count problem would need

  • Sizes. The one-count problem takes \(n\) tuples and \(h\) between \(R(L)=L/(4.4\times10^7)\) and \(Q(L)\approx1.6\times10^4L\Lambda_M\), at the compiler's degree \(D=4p-1=11\). Independence of the \(nh\) forms needs \(nh\le\dim A_1\approx N^2\). That is necessary, not sufficient. Freeness through \(D\) over \(d\) forms forces the low-degree Hilbert function of \(A\) to be at least that of the truncated algebra in \(d\) variables, which the base's relations violate as \(d\) approaches \(\gamma_1\). The limit that freeness can allow is therefore below \(\gamma_1\). The evidence below reaches about \(\gamma_1/3\) at degree 3.
  • Freeness. The seed-based methods need, by thm:row-rank-seeds at \(r=1\), \(N\ge(p-1)(t+1)(t+1+d)\). There are \(t+1\) disjoint seed blocks, each with \((p-1)\) holes for each of \(t+1+d\) basis forms, the row forms included. So \(d\le N/((p-1)(t+1))-t-1\), about \(N/(2(t+1))\) at \(p=3\), or about \(N/24\) at \(t=11\). With \(n\approx N\) tuples and a largest size \(L\) of order \(N\), both assumed here, the one-count problem needs \(d=nh\ge N^2/(4.4\times10^7)\). That exceeds \(N/24\) only for \(N\) above about \(1.8\times10^6\), so the gap is asymptotic. Freeness over that many generic forms is a Fröberg-type semi-regularity statement for the weak top algebra, in the family of conj:semi-regular-relative-to-base. The evidence is 15 of 16 random systems free through degree 3 with up to 22 forms at \(n=8\) (\(\gamma_1=63\)). The one exception is pointwise.
  • ENS blocks. The compiler's blocks introduce extension variables with companions (\(P=1-rL\), \(LP\), \(r^p-r\) in the rank-one bridge). The reduction applies once a block can be replaced, for degree-\(D\) refutations, by polynomial constraints in its input forms. This is unverified.

What this means

  • The gluing line and the restriction line meet at one algebraic statement: freeness of the weak top algebra over many generic forms through a fixed degree. With it, and with member-type blocks, the one-count problem follows for every \(h\) with \(nh\) within the range where freeness holds. That range is below \(\gamma_1\). The evidence suggests about \(\gamma_1/3\) at degree 3.
  • The proved freeness methods cannot reach it asymptotically. Both put a basis of all forms into each seed block, which caps the number of forms near \(N/(2(t+1))\). A different argument is needed for \(\Theta(N^2)\) forms.

Next: freeness over many forms. A single form's non-free summands can be located by the Clebsch–Gordan rule. On the algebra without row sums, \(\bigotimes_j(\mathbb F\oplus V_j)\), multiplication by \(\ell=\sum_j\ell_j\) acts as \(\sum_j1\otimes\cdots\otimes\ell_j\otimes\cdots\otimes1\), homogeneous with cube 0 in characteristic 3. A column with \(\ell_j\ne0\) gives \(J_2\), in degrees 0 and 1, plus \(m-1\) copies of \(J_1\) in degree 1. Then \(J_2\otimes J_2=J_3\oplus J_1\), with \(J_1\) in degree 1. So \(J_2^{\otimes a}\) is free apart from \(J_1\) in degree \(a/2\) for even \(a\), or \(J_2\) in degrees \((a-1)/2\) and \((a+1)/2\) for odd \(a\). Taking \(J_1\) from \(k\) of \(N\) touched columns puts the non-free summand at \(k+\lfloor(N-k)/2\rfloor\ge\lfloor N/2\rfloor\). So the first non-free summand is near degree \(N/2\), the order of the diagonal threshold \(N\ge2t\). Extend this count to \(d\) generic forms through the rank-variety condition of conj:worst-direction-freeness: freeness on every line of the span. Then include the row sums, and compare with the diagonal and random data.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the top-size lemma entry (its one-count reduction, sizes and typicality hypothesis), the weak-base and full-board compiler statements (ENS blocks, inputs \(1-L^{p-1}\), ceiling \(4p-1\)), cor:joint-span-families, lem:span-transfer, thm:row-rank-seeds, conj:semi-regular-relative-to-base, and ex:board-random-defect-pointwise. A fresh-context reviewer found the conditional reduction sound once its hypothesis was made precise, and confirmed the Clebsch–Gordan rule \(J_2\otimes J_2=J_3\oplus J_1\). It required these changes, all adopted:

  • blocks stated as literal members, with replacement of ENS blocks named as unverified;
  • the multi-variable \(T\), and reducedness of the joint member;
  • the seed cap derived from thm:row-rank-seeds, with consistent constants;
  • the asymptotic nature of the gap stated, with its assumptions \(n\approx N\) and \(L\) of order \(N\);
  • "up to about \(N\)" replaced by the range where freeness can hold;
  • the Clebsch–Gordan statements made precise, including the action used and the check over subsets.

The changes correct or weaken, so no further pass was made.

Many forms: every seed proof caps near N/(2t) forms, while the record shows generic freeness up to the positivity bound

24 September 2026 · Working proof (seed cap) and a conjecture · Freeness of the weak top algebra over many generic forms; cycle odd-prime-many-form-freeness. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The one-count link reduced the restriction-mixture problem, for member-type blocks, to freeness of the weak top algebra over about \(nh\) generic forms through a fixed degree. The recorded proofs reach about \(N/(2(t+1))\) forms. The missing implication is freeness over many more forms. This cycle asks whether the seed method can be pushed further, and what the record says the truth is.

General statement. lem:seed-cap: in characteristic \(p\), let \(T=\mathbb F[U]/(u^p)\), \(\dim U=k\), act diagonally on \(\bigotimes_{j\in B}V_j^+\), with each \(V_j^+=\mathbb F\oplus V_j\) square-zero and \(U\) acting through linear maps into the \(V_j\). If \(\operatorname{Ann}_T(1)=0\), then \(|B|\ge(p-1)k\). So any argument that seeds \(t+1\) disjoint blocks free over the \(t+1+d\) row and form directions needs \(N\ge(p-1)(t+1)(t+1+d)\). The seed caps of thm:board-seed-freeness, thm:row-rank-seeds and thm:projection-freeness are intrinsic to the method. conj:maximal-generic-freeness: over \(\mathbb F_3\), the weak unary top algebra \(A\) of the PHP board is free through \(t\) over \(d\) generic forms whenever \([q^k]\,\mathrm{HS}_A/(1+q+q^2)^d\ge0\) for all \(k\le t\). The recorded evidence at \(n=8\), \(t=3\) reaches that positivity bound, \(d=21\) of \(\gamma_1=63\) forms, where the seed methods give nothing.

The seed cap

Proof. \(T\) has a monomial basis \(\prod u_b^{e_b}\), \(e_b\le p-1\), for a basis \(u_b\) of \(U\). Its top element \(\prod u_b^{p-1}\) has degree \((p-1)k\). The module \(\bigotimes_{j\in B}V_j^+\) is graded by the number of tensor factors taken from the \(V_j\), so it has no elements of degree above \(|B|\). \(T\) acts by homogeneous maps of degree 1 per linear form, so \(\tau\cdot1\) has degree \(\deg\tau\). If \((p-1)k>|B|\), the top element of \(T\) sends 1 to 0, so \(\operatorname{Ann}_T(1)\ne0\). In the free-seed argument each of \(t+1\) disjoint blocks must satisfy \(\operatorname{Ann}_T(1)=0\) for \(T\) on the \(u\le r+t\) row directions and the \(d\) form directions, which gives the stated count. \(\square\)

So pushing seeds cannot reach \(\Theta(N^2)\) forms. A proof must either use a free summand generated above degree 0, or avoid seeds altogether.

What the record shows

For \(A\) on the PHP board with \(n=8\) (9 rows), \(\mathrm{HS}_A=(1,63,1656,22929)\) through degree 3. The free prediction \(\mathrm{HS}_A/(1+q+q^2)^d\) in degree 3 is 659 at \(d=20\), 74 at \(d=21\) and \(-468\) at \(d=22\), so the positivity bound through degree 3 is \(d=21\). In degree 2 the prediction stays nonnegative through \(d=36\). ex:board-random-defect-pointwise found 15 of 16 random affine systems, with 4 to 22 forms, at the expected (truncated) Hilbert function through degree 3, and the one exception was pointwise. So at this size generic forms behave maximally, up to the positivity bound. The seed methods need \(N\ge2\cdot4\cdot(4+d)\) at \(t=3\) and give nothing at \(N=8\). A new check at larger sizes by Gröbner bases is not practical: 10 random forms at \(n=8\), \(t=3\) took 96 s in Singular, and 20 did not finish in 120 s (sizing.json). So no new data was taken.

What this means

  • The freeness the one-count problem needs is the maximal behaviour of generic forms, a Fröberg-type property of the weak top algebra. Fröberg's conjecture for generic forms in a polynomial ring is itself open. What might make this case tractable is the algebra's tensor structure over the columns.
  • The seed method is exhausted. A proof over \(\Theta(N^2)\) forms needs a different mechanism.

Next: a mechanism beyond seeds on the algebra without row sums, \(\bigotimes_j(\mathbb F\oplus V_j)\), for \(d\le m\) generic forms. Each column is then \(u(W)/\mathfrak m^2\) plus trivial summands, over \(u(W)=\mathbb F_3[W]/(w^3)\). The question is the lowest degree of a non-free summand of \((u(W)/\mathfrak m^2)^{\otimes N}\). For \(d=1\) it is \(\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), by the Clebsch–Gordan rule. Compute it for small \(d\) and \(N\) with a compiled rank kernel, after a sizing run, and look for a formula of the form \(\lfloor N/(c\,d)\rfloor\) or \(\lfloor N/c\rfloor\). The second would give freeness over many forms through \(t\) whenever \(N\ge ct\).

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the free-seed argument as cited in thm:board-seed-freeness and thm:row-rank-seeds (blocks with \(\operatorname{Ann}_T(1)=0\)), ex:board-random-defect-pointwise, and the recorded \(\mathrm{HS}_A\) at \(n=8\). The positivity values were computed from that series by a short script, and the sizing times are read from sizing.json. The lemma is a degree count, so no reviewer pass was run. The conjecture was searched under semi-regular, Fröberg and generic freeness. The nearest records are conj:semi-regular-relative-to-base (product clauses) and ex:board-random-defect-pointwise.

Generic forms, up to the number of rows, are row sums; conjectured threshold N ≥ 2t−1 for every such number

24 September 2026 · Working proof (generic forms as row sums), a conjecture and a finite check · Column tensor powers over F_3; cycle odd-prime-column-tensor-power. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The many-forms entry found the seed method capped near \(N/(2t)\) forms. It asked for the lowest non-free degree of the column tensor power \((u(W)/\mathfrak m^2)^{\otimes N}\), \(u(W)=\mathbb F_3[W]/(w^3)\), \(d=\dim W\). The missing implication is freeness over many generic forms.

General statement. prop:generic-forms-as-row-sums: over any field of characteristic \(p\), let \(d\le m\) linear forms on the weak board without row sums, \(\tilde A=\bigotimes_j(\mathbb F\oplus V_j)\), have injective column maps \(\pi_j:W\to V_j\). This holds for generic forms over an extension field, but uniformly random forms over \(\mathbb F_3\) with \(d=m\) usually fail it in some column. Let \(u(W)=\mathbb F[W]/(w^p)\). Then, as a graded \(u(W)\)-module, \(\tilde A\) is a direct sum of shifted copies of \((u(W)/\mathfrak m^2)^{\otimes k}\), and \((u(W)/\mathfrak m^2)^{\otimes k}\) is the weak algebra on \(d\) rows and \(k\) holes over its row sums. So freeness over such forms is the freeness of column tensor powers over row sums, which is the kind of freeness the base's stability proof uses, up to the caveat below on the notion of freeness. conj:column-tensor-power-freeness: over \(\mathbb F_3\), the weak algebra without row sums on \(d\ge1\) rows and \(N\) holes is free through \(t\) over its row sums, in the sense of the minimal free cover, if and only if \(N\ge2t-1\), for every \(d\). ex:column-tensor-power-thresholds confirms the threshold exactly in all 25 cases checked to completion (\(2\le N\le8\), \(1\le d\le4\)). If true, \(\tilde A\) is free over any \(d\le m\) forms with injective column maps through \(t\) exactly when \(N\ge2t-1\). That goes far beyond the seed cap. It matches the threshold of the recorded conj:weak-base-stability, though whether cover-freeness suffices for that conjecture's proof route is not checked.

Generic forms as row sums

Proof. In a tensor product of commutative algebras, multiplication by \(\ell=\sum_j\ell_j\) satisfies the Leibniz rule, so it is the diagonal action of a primitive element. The forms commute and \(\ell^p=\sum_j\ell_j^p=0\), so this is an action of \(u(W)\). \(W\) acts on \(\mathbb F\oplus V_j\) by \(w\cdot1=\pi_j(w)\) and \(w\cdot V_j=0\), since \(V_j^2=0\). Choose a complement \(V_j=\pi_j(W)\oplus V_j'\). Then \(\mathbb F\oplus V_j=(\mathbb F\oplus\pi_j(W))\oplus V_j'\) as \(u(W)\)-modules, with \(V_j'\) trivial in degree 1. When \(\pi_j\) is injective, \(\mathbb F\oplus\pi_j(W)\cong u(W)/\mathfrak m^2\) by \(1\mapsto1\), \(\pi_j(w)\mapsto w\). The diagonal action on the tensor product distributes over direct sums, so \(\tilde A\cong\bigoplus_{S\subseteq[N]}(u(W)/\mathfrak m^2)^{\otimes([N]\setminus S)}\otimes\bigotimes_{j\in S}V_j'\). The factor \(\bigotimes_{j\in S}V_j'\) is trivial, in degree \(|S|\). On \(d\) rows with forms the row sums \(R_i\mapsto r_i=\sum_jx_{ij}\), each \(\pi_j\) sends \(R_i\) to \(x_{ij}\), an isomorphism onto \(V_j\). So the \(d\)-row algebra on \(k\) holes is \((u(W)/\mathfrak m^2)^{\otimes k}\) over its row sums. \(\square\)

A tensor factor that is trivial and sits in degree \(s\) shifts freeness degrees by \(s\). So \(\tilde A\) is free through \(t\) over the \(d\) forms exactly when \((u/\mathfrak m^2)^{\otimes(N-s)}\) is free through \(t-s\) for every \(s\) with nonzero multiplicity. Under the conjecture that requires \(N-s\ge2(t-s)-1\). The summand \(s=0\) always occurs with multiplicity 1, so it binds: \(N\ge2t-1\).

The check

tensor_power.py builds \(M=(u(W)/\mathfrak m^2)^{\otimes N}\) with basis (column subset, labels) and the action of \(w_b\) inserting label \(b\) in a new column. It computes \(\mathrm{HF}(M/\mathfrak mM)\) by exact ranks over \(\mathbb F_3\) and compares with \([q^k](1+dq)^N/(1+q+q^2)^d\). It stops at the first inequality. The lemma's failure test is \(\mathrm{HF}>\mathrm{pred}\), and every recorded failure has \(\mathrm{HF}>\mathrm{pred}\). By the openness lemma of thm:projection-freeness, equality through \(t\) is equivalent to the minimal free cover being bijective through \(t\). Matrices are capped at 6000 columns. Results (tensor_power.json):

  • In all 25 cases that reached their first failure (\(2\le N\le8\), \(1\le d\le4\)), \(M\) is free through exactly \(\lceil N/2\rceil\) and not through \(\lceil N/2\rceil+1\), whatever \(d\).
  • Three cases stopped at the cap while still free: \((N,d)=(7,4)\) through 3, \((8,3)\) through 4, \((8,4)\) through 3. They are consistent with the pattern.
  • For \(d=1\) the values agree with the Clebsch–Gordan count, which was not computed separately by the script. The reviewer recomputed \((N,d)=(4,2),(5,2),(6,1),(8,1),(4,3),(6,2)\) with separate code over full tuples, and all matched.

This extends the record's evidence. The weak-base-stability entry found \(\mathrm{HF}_A\), which is \(M/\mathfrak mM\), equal to the freeness prediction on the \(4\times7\) and \(5\times9\) boards at \(N=2D-1\), and unequal on boards that fall. That entry calls equality "necessary for that freeness, not sufficient". For freeness in the sense of the minimal free cover, the openness lemma makes it sufficient too. Whether that weaker notion suffices for Step 3 of the stability proof, whose free-seed decomposition is into free plus high-degree parts, is not checked here.

What this means

  • Two open ends of the line meet. The base's stability proof uses freeness of column tensor powers over row sums, in the free-plus-high-degree sense. Freeness over forms with injective column maps is cover-freeness of the same modules for \(d\le m\). The data put the cover-freeness threshold at \(N\ge2t-1\) independently of \(d\), against the seed cap \(d\le N/(2(t+1))\).
  • Not covered: more forms than rows, \(d>m\), where the column maps have kernels; and the weak algebra with its row sums together with further forms, which is again more than \(m\) directions. The one-count problem needs \(d\) up to about \(N^2\), so both matter.

Next: prove conj:column-tensor-power-freeness. The iterative criterion reduces freeness over \(u(w_1,\dots,w_d)\) to \(w_1\) acting freely and freeness of the quotient over the rest. The Clebsch–Gordan rule handles \(w_1\). The quotient is the question. Then treat non-injective column maps, the case \(d>m\), with the same kernel.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the weak-base stability entry (Steps 1 to 3, the free-seed lemma, the \(\mathrm{HF}_A\) evidence and its remark), the openness lemma of thm:projection-freeness, lem:seed-cap, and conj:weak-base-stability. The check was validated for \(d=1\) against the Clebsch–Gordan count, and the reviewer recomputed six cases independently. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed the decomposition, the identification with the row-sum algebra, the shift argument, and the case counts. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the title and statement hedged: the threshold is a conjecture, and the proposition covers \(d\le m\) forms with injective column maps;
  • the identification with the stability ingredient qualified by the cover-freeness caveat;
  • characteristic \(p\) with \(u(W)=\mathbb F[W]/(w^p)\), and the reason the action is defined;
  • injectivity stated as the hypothesis, with random \(\mathbb F_3\) forms flagged;
  • the conjecture's letter changed to \(d\);
  • the Clebsch–Gordan comparison and the script's stopping test described accurately.

The changes weaken or clarify, so no further pass was made.

Line necessity: column tensor powers are free through at most ⌈N/2⌉ for every number of forms, so the conjecture's remaining half is a graded Dade lemma

24 September 2026 · Working proof (line necessity) · Half of conj:column-tensor-power-freeness; cycle odd-prime-tensor-power-proof. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The column-tensor-power entry found \(M_N=(u(W)/\mathfrak m^2)^{\otimes N}\) free through exactly \(\lceil N/2\rceil\) over \(u(W)=\mathbb F_3[W]/(w^3)\) in every checked case, whatever \(d=\dim W\). It conjectured this for all \(d\) (conj:column-tensor-power-freeness). This cycle attempts the proof.

General statement. prop:line-necessity: over \(\mathbb F_3\), for every \(d\ge1\) and \(N\ge1\), \(M_N\) is not free through \(\lceil N/2\rceil+1\) over \(u(W)\), in the sense of the minimal free cover. Its restriction to every line \(u(\langle x\rangle)\), \(0\ne x\in W\otimes\overline{\mathbb F}_3\), is free through exactly \(\lceil N/2\rceil\). The proof has two parts. Freeness through \(t\) passes to restrictions to lines. And on a line, \(M_N\) decomposes by the graded Clebsch–Gordan rule \(J_2\otimes J_2=J_3\oplus J_1(-1)\). So the "only if" half of the conjecture holds for every \(d\), and the conjecture is equivalent to the "if" half: freeness on every line through \(t\) implies freeness through \(t\), for this module. By prop:generic-forms-as-row-sums the same holds for the weak algebra without row sums over any \(d\le m\) forms with injective column maps, including the \(d\)-row algebra over its row sums. Freeness through \(t\) there needs \(N\ge2t-1\).

Restriction to lines

Lemma. If a graded \(u(W)\)-module \(M\), finite-dimensional in each degree and in degrees \(\ge0\), is free through \(t\), then so is its restriction to \(u(\langle x\rangle)\) for every \(0\ne x\in W\). The same holds for \(x\in W\otimes\overline{\mathbb F}_3\) after base change, since the minimal free cover base-changes and freeness through \(t\) is unchanged by field extension. Necessity below needs only one \(x\in W\).

Proof. Let \(0\to K\to F\to M\to0\) be the minimal free cover over \(u(W)\), with \(K\) in degrees \(\ge t+1\). \(u(W)\) is free over \(u(\langle x\rangle)\), because \(x^3=0\) and \(x\) extends to a basis of \(W\), so \(F\) is free over \(u(\langle x\rangle)\), and \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^{u(x)}(\mathbb F,F)=0\). The long exact sequence gives \(0\to\operatorname{Tor}_1^{u(x)}(\mathbb F,M)\to K/xK\), so \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^{u(x)}(\mathbb F,M)\) vanishes in degrees \(\le t\). For graded modules over \(u(x)\), that is freeness through \(t\). If \(K'\) is the kernel of the minimal cover over \(u(x)\), then \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^{u(x)}(\mathbb F,M)=K'/xK'\), and \(K'\) is bounded below. So by graded Nakayama its lowest degree is the lowest degree of \(\operatorname{Tor}_1\). \(\square\)

On a line

Let \(0\ne x\in W\). On \(u(W)/\mathfrak m^2=\mathbb F\oplus W\), \(x\) sends \(1\mapsto x\) and kills \(W\). So the restriction is \(J_2\oplus J_1(-1)^{d-1}\), with \(J_2=\langle1,x\rangle\) in degrees 0 and 1. The action on \(M_N\) is diagonal, with \(x\) primitive, so \(M_N|_x=\bigoplus_{S\subseteq[N]}J_2^{\otimes(N-|S|)}\otimes J_1(-|S|)^{(d-1)^{|S|}}\).

Clebsch–Gordan, graded. \(J_2\otimes J_2=J_3\oplus J_1(-1)\) (reviewed in the one-count entry). By induction, \(J_2^{\otimes a}\) is free plus one non-free summand: \(J_1(-a/2)\) for even \(a\ge2\), and \(J_2(-(a-1)/2)\) for odd \(a\). For the step, tensoring with \(J_2\) keeps free summands free and gives \(J_1(-a/2)\otimes J_2=J_2(-a/2)\) and \(J_2(-(a-1)/2)\otimes J_2=J_3(\cdot)\oplus J_1(-(a+1)/2)\). \(J_2^{\otimes0}=J_1\).

Where freeness first fails. The minimal free cover of \(J_1(-a)\) has kernel starting in degree \(a+1\), and that of \(J_2(-a)\) in degree \(a+2\). So a summand \(J_1(-a)\) makes freeness fail first at \(t=a+1\), and \(J_2(-a)\) at \(t=a+2\).

The summand indexed by \(S\), \(|S|=s\), is \(J_2^{\otimes(N-s)}\) shifted by \(s\). Its non-free part fails freeness first at \(\lceil(N+s)/2\rceil+1\). If \(N-s\) is even, the part is \(J_1(-(N+s)/2)\), failing at \((N+s)/2+1\). If \(N-s\) is odd, it is \(J_2(-(N+s-1)/2)\), failing at \((N+s-1)/2+2\). This is smallest at \(s=0\), with value \(\lceil N/2\rceil+1\). For odd \(N\), \(s=1\) ties with it through \(J_1(-(N+1)/2)\).

So \(M_N|_x\) is free through exactly \(\lceil N/2\rceil\). \(\square\)

By the lemma, \(M_N\) is not free through \(\lceil N/2\rceil+1\) over \(u(W)\). The same holds for the weak algebra without row sums over \(d\le m\) forms with injective column maps. By prop:generic-forms-as-row-sums, \(M_N\) is a \(u(W)\)-direct summand of it (the summand \(s=0\)), and a direct summand that is not free through a degree blocks freeness of the whole through that degree. This is consistent with all rows of ex:column-tensor-power-thresholds. The failure at \(\lceil N/2\rceil+1\) is observed wherever the check reached it; the rows \((7,4)\), \((8,4)\) and \((8,3)\) stopped before.

What remains

  • The conjecture now says that for \(M_N\), freeness through \(t\) on every line implies freeness through \(t\). That is a graded, truncated Dade lemma for one family of modules. Dade's lemma itself, for finite-dimensional modules over elementary abelian \(p\)-groups, is the ungraded, untruncated statement. The recorded truncated version for column spans, conj:worst-direction-freeness, has a counterexample near capacity, so the truncated form needs the structure of \(M_N\).
  • A possible route, stated as a question: \(M_N\) is the \(N\)-th tensor power of one module, \(u(W)/\mathfrak m^2\), whose restriction to every line over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\) has Jordan type \([2][1]^{d-1}\). Tensor products respect restriction to lines here because the coproduct is primitive; for the group-algebra coproduct of Dade's setting they do not, so any comparison must use the \(u(W)\) Hopf structure. Is truncated freeness detected on lines for tensor powers of a module of constant Jordan type?

Next: the route review is due. After it, test the graded Dade statement for \(M_N\) against the constant-Jordan-type literature: modules of constant Jordan type and their tensor products, in the sense of Carlson, Friedlander and Pevtsova.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the column-tensor-power entry and its JSON; the graded Clebsch–Gordan rule (reviewed in the one-count entry); the openness lemma of thm:projection-freeness; prop:generic-forms-as-row-sums; conj:worst-direction-freeness (its counterexample near capacity). A fresh-context reviewer confirmed the restriction lemma, the decomposition on a line and the Clebsch–Gordan induction. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the bound for \(|S|\ge1\), wrong as written for even \(N\) with \(s=1\), replaced by the uniform failure degree \(\lceil(N+s)/2\rceil+1\);
  • the base change and the Nakayama step in the lemma, with the freeness of \(u(W)\) over \(u(x)\);
  • the JSON consistency stated per row;
  • the direct-summand statement used from prop:generic-forms-as-row-sums;
  • the primitive coproduct named, and the constant-Jordan-type route stated as a question.

The changes correct the reasoning without changing the conclusion, or weaken, so no further pass was made.
