Route review: the line now rests on one module family, the column tensor powers, whose freeness would give (a) and generic freeness

24 September 2026 · Route review · The (b) and (c) line after the joint-span review; cycle odd-prime-tensor-review. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. Six research entries have followed the joint-span review. This review states the line's claim and what the goal needs from it, tries to falsify the current conjecture, assesses the line, and names the next step.

General statement. The line's general claim is unchanged. The goal's inventory, compiled to constraints over the weak base, has no PC refutation at the compiler's degree. Relative gluing reduces this to the base's stability (a) and to liftable top syzygies. The last six entries turned the remaining obligations into statements about one module family. The column tensor powers \(M_N=(u(W)/\mathfrak m^2)^{\otimes N}\) carry the base's stability, through the row sums. They carry freeness over up to \(m\) forms with injective column maps (prop:generic-forms-as-row-sums). And through the one-count link they carry the restriction-mixture problem for member-type blocks (prop:one-count-by-freeness). conj:column-tensor-power-freeness puts their threshold at \(N\ge2t-1\) for every \(d\). Its "only if" half is proved (prop:line-necessity). Its "if" half is a graded Dade lemma for \(M_N\).

What happened since the last review

  • Beyond the Taylor count, planted families pin their point and random ones are refuted (planted families). So dense parts must be treated as restrictions. Closing the pins of a partial matching gives the restricted weak base (conditioned base).
  • For member-type blocks, the restriction line's one-count problem follows from freeness over the joint span (one-count link).
  • Every seed proof caps near \(N/(2t)\) forms, while the record shows freeness up to the positivity bound (many forms).
  • Forms with injective column maps act like row sums, and the threshold data give \(N\ge2t-1\) independently of \(d\) (column tensor power). Its "only if" half is proved (line necessity).

What the goal needs

Three things remain on this route. The line now bears on the first two.

  1. Freeness over the forms of the inventory. For up to \(m\) forms with injective column maps, the conjecture gives it. The inventory needs about \(nh\), up to order \(N^2\), with column maps that have kernels. Freeness also has to hold together with the row sums, which are \(m\) further directions.
  2. Blocks as members. The compiler's ENS blocks must be replaced by polynomial constraints in their input forms, which is unverified.
  3. Adversarial, non-generic forms, and dense parts of the inventory that are spread over many rows. For those, neither conditioning nor generic freeness applies.

Falsification attempt

The conjecture is most at risk with many more forms than holes. tensor_power.py was rerun with \((N,d)=(3,6),(3,10),(4,6),(4,10),(5,6),(6,5)\) (large_d.json). For \(N=3,4\), with up to ten forms, freeness holds through exactly \(\lceil N/2\rceil=2\) and fails at 3. For \((5,6)\) and \((6,5)\), freeness holds through 3, the limit of the size cap and equal to \(\lceil N/2\rceil\). No case contradicts the conjecture. The leading coefficient in \(d\) of the free prediction at \(t=\lceil N/2\rceil\) is also positive in the cases computed by hand (\((N,t)=(5,3),(6,3),(7,4)\)). So the positivity bound does not cut in for large \(d\). The recorded failure of the truncated Dade form for column spans (conj:worst-direction-freeness) concerns a different module, the column model with a row-sum relation. It does not refute this one.

Assessment of this line

The line has narrowed from many hypotheses to one algebraic family, and its two main open ends now coincide. If conj:column-tensor-power-freeness holds, then conj:weak-base-stability's range becomes linear, subject to whether cover-freeness suffices for the stability proof's Step 3. Freeness over up to \(m\) generic forms would follow at the same threshold. That would be substantial. It still falls short of the goal in three ways:

  • it does not reach \(d>m\) forms;
  • it does not cover the row sums together with further forms;
  • it leaves the ENS blocks and adversarial forms open.

The conjecture is a clean statement with a proved half and uniform evidence. Its missing half is a question of a known kind, detection of freeness on lines, for which general theory exists in the ungraded setting. Proving it would be real progress. It would not by itself close the route.

Next step

On odd-prime-clause-transfer: attack the "if" half of conj:column-tensor-power-freeness. Two routes:

  • Read the constant-Jordan-type theory, with care for the primitive coproduct. Carlson, Friedlander and Pevtsova treat modules whose restrictions to all lines have the same Jordan type. Check whether their generic-kernel or tensor-product results give truncated freeness for tensor powers of \(u(W)/\mathfrak m^2\).
  • Prove the \(d=2\) case directly. Use the iterative criterion: \(w_1\) by Clebsch–Gordan, then \(M_N/w_1M_N\) as a \(u(w_2)\)-module, whose Jordan type can be computed.

In parallel, extend the conjecture to column maps with kernels (\(d>m\)), since the inventory needs that case.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read the six entries since the joint-span review and their registered claims, and conj:worst-direction-freeness. The falsification values are read from large_d.json. Stability from tensor powers: cover-freeness of the D-row column tensor power through D is what the stability proof uses, so the tensor-power conjecture implies linear stability at p = 3

24 September 2026 · Working proof (stability from tensor powers) · The link between conj:column-tensor-power-freeness and conj:weak-base-stability; cycle odd-prime-dade-tensor. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The tensor-power review left a caveat. The base's stability proof decomposes the column tensor power into free plus high-degree parts. The tensor-power conjecture concerns only freeness in the sense of the minimal free cover. Does the conjecture give the base's stability?

General statement. prop:stability-from-tensor-power: over \(\mathbb F_p\), let \(\tilde A\) be the weak algebra without row sums on \(D\) rows and \(N\) columns, and \(T=\mathbb F_p[R_1,\dots,R_D]/(R_i^p)\) acting through its row sums. Then \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^T(\mathbb F,\tilde A)\) is the Koszul homology \(H_1(r;\tilde A)\) modulo the Frobenius classes \(r_i^{p-1}a\,e_i\). So \(\tilde A\) is free through \(t\) over \(T\), in the sense of the minimal free cover, exactly when \(H_1(r;\tilde A)\) is spanned by Frobenius classes in degrees \(\le t\). That is the only consequence of Step 3 that the stability proof uses. Hence, if \(\tilde A\) is cover-free through \(D\), the weak base on any \(m\ge D\) rows and \(N\) columns has no falls below \(D\). In particular conj:column-tensor-power-freeness, over \(\mathbb F_3\) with \(d=D\) and \(t=D\), implies the \(p=3\) case of conj:weak-base-stability, \(N\ge2D-1\). The review's caveat is resolved. The record calls Hilbert-function equality "necessary, not sufficient" for freeness in the direct-sum sense, which remains unrefuted. But the stability proof never needs that stronger sense. Equality through \(D\) is cover-freeness through \(D\), by the openness lemma of thm:projection-freeness, and that suffices.

Proof

  1. Tor over the truncated algebra. \(T=\bigotimes_i\mathbb F_p[R_i]/(R_i^p)\). The minimal resolution of \(\mathbb F\) over each factor is periodic: \(A\xleftarrow{R}A(-1)\xleftarrow{R^{p-1}}A(-p)\leftarrow\cdots\). Their tensor product is a free resolution of \(\mathbb F\) over \(T\) whose first two terms are \(P_1=\bigoplus_iT(-1)e_i\) and \(P_2=\bigoplus_iT(-p)f_i\oplus\bigoplus_{i<j}T(-2)e_{ij}\). Here \(f_i\mapsto R_i^{p-1}e_i\) and \(e_{ij}\mapsto R_je_i-R_ie_j\). Tensoring with \(M=\tilde A\) gives \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^T(\mathbb F,M)=\ker\bigl(\bigoplus_iM(-1)\to M\bigr)/\bigl(\text{Frobenius}+\text{Koszul images}\bigr)\).
  2. Koszul homology. The Koszul complex of \(r_1,\dots,r_D\) on \(M\) over \(\mathcal S=\mathbb F_p[R]\) gives \(H_1(r;M)=\ker\bigl(\bigoplus_iM(-1)\to M\bigr)/(\text{Koszul images})\). The kernels agree, so \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^T(\mathbb F,M)=H_1(r;M)/\langle r_i^{p-1}a\,e_i\rangle\), degree by degree, with \(e_i\) in degree 1.
  3. Cover-freeness. By graded Nakayama, the kernel of the minimal free cover over \(T\) starts in the lowest degree of \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^T(\mathbb F,M)\). So cover-freeness through \(t\) is the vanishing of \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^T\) in degrees \(\le t\), that is, \(H_1\) spanned by Frobenius classes there. It is also Hilbert-function equality, by the openness lemma of thm:projection-freeness. The cover \(T\otimes M/\mathfrak mM\to M\) is onto, and the Hilbert function of its source through \(t\) depends only on \(M/\mathfrak mM\) through \(t\). So \(\mathrm{HF}_{M/\mathfrak mM}=[q^k]\,\mathrm{HS}_M/\mathrm{HS}_T\) for all \(k\le t\) holds exactly when the kernel vanishes through \(t\).
  4. Stability. The proof of thm:weak-base-stability-quadratic uses Step 3 only through its stated consequence: \(H_1(r;\tilde A)_{k+1}\) is spanned by Frobenius classes for \(k<D\), on the \(D\)-row board. Step 1 then kills these classes under the connecting map, so \(z\) is injective in degree \(k\) on the \(D\)-row board. lem:weak-row-reduction extends this to \(m\ge D\) rows. Replacing Step 3 by cover-freeness through \(D\), which gives the same consequence by items 1 to 3, proves the claim. \(\square\)

Consequences

  • The two open ends identified in the review are linked one way. conj:column-tensor-power-freeness at \(d=D\), \(t=D\), \(N=2D-1\) implies the \(p=3\) case of conj:weak-base-stability. Stability is not shown to imply cover-freeness. By prop:line-necessity, cover-freeness through \(D\) fails for \(N\le2D-2\). The stability conjecture's sharpness at \(D=4\), recorded for \(N=6\), is consistent with that failure, but a failure of cover-freeness does not by itself force a fall.
  • Over \(\mathbb F_3\), the recorded Hilbert-function equalities on the \(4\times7\) and \(5\times9\) boards now prove \(z\)-injectivity below \(D=4\) and \(D=5\) on those boards and, by row reduction, on every \(m\ge D\). ex:weak-base-stability-small already records these cases for every \(m\ge D\) by direct computation, so this route adds no new case there. It is consistent.
  • Over \(\mathbb F_3\), ex:column-tensor-power-thresholds gives cover-freeness through 3 for \((N,d)=(5,3)\) and \((6,3)\). So the weak base on \(m\ge3\) rows and \(N=5\) or \(6\) columns has no falls below 3. That lies below the quadratic theorem's range, \(N\ge(p-1)D^2=18\) at \(p=3\), \(D=3\).

Next: the graded Dade half of conj:column-tensor-power-freeness, which would give both linear stability and freeness over up to \(m\) generic forms. Try \(d=2\) directly: \(w_1\) acts on \(M_N\) with the Clebsch–Gordan decomposition. Compute the Jordan type of \(w_2\) on \(M_N/w_1M_N\), which is the 2-row algebra modulo its first row sum, and show it is free through \(\lceil N/2\rceil\). Then check that the iterative criterion holds through \(t\) in the truncated setting.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: thm:weak-base-stability-quadratic (Steps 1 to 3 and the proof), lem:weak-row-reduction, conj:weak-base-stability (scope: every \(p\)) and ex:weak-base-stability-small (every \(m\ge D\) at \((4,7)\) and \((5,9)\)), the openness lemma of thm:projection-freeness, and the tensor-power JSON. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed the resolution and its maps, the identification of \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^T\) with \(H_1\) modulo Frobenius classes, the Nakayama step, the degree bookkeeping of the replacement in the stability proof, and the JSON values at \((5,3)\) and \((6,3)\). It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the link between Hilbert-function equality and cover-freeness made explicit;
  • the "too pessimistic" remark rephrased, since the direct-sum sense is not refuted;
  • "coincide exactly" replaced by a one-way implication;

Tensor powers through degree 2: cover-free through degree 2 for every number of forms once N ≥ 3; chessboard connectivity has the conjectured threshold

24 September 2026 · Working proof (tensor powers through degree 2) · The "if" half of conj:column-tensor-power-freeness at t = 2; cycle odd-prime-two-form-dade. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. By the stability link, the "if" half of conj:column-tensor-power-freeness would give both linear base stability at \(p=3\) and freeness over up to \(m\) generic forms. Its "only if" half is prop:line-necessity. This cycle proves the first nontrivial case of the "if" half for every number of forms, and looks for a general mechanism.

General statement. prop:tensor-power-degree-two: over any field of characteristic \(\ne2\), the weak algebra without row sums on \(d\) rows and \(N\ge3\) columns, \(\tilde A=\mathbb F[x_{bj}]/(x_{bj}x_{b'j})\), has only Koszul relations among its row sums \(r_b=\sum_jx_{bj}\) in degrees \(\le2\). So in characteristic 3 it is cover-free through 2 over \(T=\mathbb F[R]/(R^3)\), for every \(d\). With prop:line-necessity, the threshold at \(t=2\) is exactly \(N\ge3=2t-1\), as conj:column-tensor-power-freeness predicts. For the general case, the content-graded Koszul complex of the row sums appears to be related to row-labelled chessboard complexes. The imported connectivity bound yields \((k-2)\)-connectivity of the \(k\times N\) chessboard complex for \(N\ge2k-1\), and only \((k-3)\) at \(N=2k-2\). That is the conjecture's threshold, a heuristic hint at a proof, not a proof.

Degree 2

Proof. By prop:stability-from-tensor-power, cover-freeness through 2 is the vanishing of \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^T(\mathbb F,\tilde A)\) in degrees 1 and 2. \(\tilde A\) is a \(T\)-module, since \(r_b^3=6\sum x\,x\,x=0\) in characteristic 3. \(\operatorname{Tor}_1\) vanishes in degree 0 because the \(e_b\) have degree 1. Frobenius classes start in degree 3, so the claim is that relations \(\sum_br_ba_b=0\) of degree \(\le2\) are Koszul.

  • Degree 1: \(a_b\) are constants, and \(\sum_b\beta_br_b=0\) forces \(\beta=0\), since the row sums involve disjoint variables.
  • Degree 2: write \(a_b=\sum_{c,k}\alpha_{bck}x_{ck}\). In \(\tilde A_2\), whose basis is the products \(x_{bj}x_{ck}\) with \(j\ne k\), the coefficient of \(x_{bj}x_{ck}\) is \(\alpha_{bck}+\alpha_{cbj}\). So \(\alpha_{bck}=-\alpha_{cbj}\) for all \(b,c\) and \(j\ne k\).
    • Fix \(b,c\) and two columns \(k\ne k'\). With \(N\ge3\) there is a column \(j\) different from both, and then \(\alpha_{bck}=-\alpha_{cbj}=\alpha_{bck'}\). So \(\alpha_{bck}=\beta_{bc}\) does not depend on \(k\), and \(\beta_{bc}=-\beta_{cb}\).
    • For \(b=c\) this gives \(\beta_{bb}=-\beta_{bb}\), so \(\beta_{bb}=0\) in characteristic \(\ne2\).
    Hence \(a_b=\sum_c\beta_{bc}r_c\) with \(\beta\) antisymmetric, the Koszul boundary of \(\sum_{b<c}\beta_{bc}\,e_b\wedge e_c\). \(\square\)

At \(N=2\) the argument fails, as prop:line-necessity requires. There is no third column, and for one row \(b\), \(a_b=x_{b1}-x_{b2}\) gives \(r_ba_b=x_{b1}^2-x_{b2}^2=0\) with \(a_b\) not in the Koszul span. Degree-2 boundaries have every \(a_b\) in the span of the \(r_c\), and there are no Frobenius classes in degree 2. So with \(a_c=0\) for \(c\ne b\) it is a relation of degree 2 that is not Koszul.

A general mechanism: chessboard complexes (heuristic, not a proof)

Grade \(\tilde A\) by row content \(c\in\mathbb N^d\): a monomial \(x_P\), \(P\) a column-injective cell set, has content \(c_b=\#\{\text{cells of }P\text{ in row }b\}\). The Koszul complex of the row sums respects this grading, with \(e_b\) of content \(e_b\). In content \(c\), the relevant spaces are spanned by column-injective placements of a multiset of row labels into the \(N\) columns. These are the faces of the \(|c|\times N\) chessboard complex, taken modulo permutations of equal labels, which is harmless in characteristic 3 when every \(c_b\le2\). Frobenius classes absorb labels of multiplicity 3 and more. The maps, however, carry no simplicial signs. For \(d=1\), multiplication by \(r\) on square-free monomials is the unsigned up-operator of the Boolean lattice, with \(r^2\ne0\). It is not a simplicial coboundary, which is why the Clebsch–Gordan decomposition over \(\mathbb F_3[r]/(r^3)\) applies there. The Clebsch–Gordan count gives the threshold \(N\ge2t-1\) at \(d=1\). The chessboard connectivity bound, \((k-2)\)-connectivity of the \(k\times N\) chessboard complex for \(N\ge2k-1\) (imported in lem:zero-marginal-chessboard-cycles), has the same threshold at \(k=t\). Its sharpness below \(2k-1\) is a separate result, not imported. The conjecture would follow if \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^T\) in content \(c\) embeds in the reduced homology of such a complex below its connectivity range. The degree-2 proof above is the case \(|c|=2\) done by hand.

Next: make the chessboard reduction precise, if it exists. First settle the sign issue: the Koszul complex over the commutative \(\tilde A\) has no simplicial signs, so any identification with a chessboard chain complex needs a sign twist or a different complex. Then identify the content-\(c\) strand of the Koszul complex of the row sums, modulo Frobenius classes, with a chain complex of the \(|c|\times N\) chessboard complex, symmetrized over equal labels. Then derive \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^T=0\) in degree \(k\) from the imported \((k-2)\)-connectivity for \(N\ge2k-1\). Check it against the degree-2 proof and the tensor-power data.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: prop:stability-from-tensor-power (Tor as Koszul homology modulo Frobenius classes), prop:line-necessity, and lem:zero-marginal-chessboard-cycles (the imported connectivity bound). A fresh-context reviewer confirmed the degree 1 and 2 argument, the case \(b=c\), the use of \(N\ge3\) and of characteristic \(\ne2\), and the \(N=2\) counterexample. It found one false statement, the claim that for \(d=1\) the complex is a simplex boundary map, since multiplication by \(r\) is unsigned. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • degree 0 and the module structure stated;
  • the boundary form of the Koszul relation and the reason the counterexample is not a boundary;
  • the connectivity statement worded as what the imported bound gives, with sharpness named as not imported;
  • the false \(d=1\) remark replaced, and the sign issue flagged as the first question of the next step;
  • the chessboard paragraph marked as heuristic;
  • the title made precise.

The changes correct or weaken, so no further pass was made.

Chessboard link: the row sums' Koszul complex is the chessboard cochain complex, and tensor powers are free through degree 5 for every number of forms

24 September 2026 · Working proof (chessboard link and heavy-core reduction) · Tensor-power conjecture through t = 5; cycle odd-prime-chessboard-link. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The degree-two entry proved the "if" half of conj:column-tensor-power-freeness at \(t=2\). It suggested chessboard complexes as a general mechanism, with a sign issue to settle first. The missing implication is: for \(N\ge2t-1\), \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^T(\mathbb F,\tilde A)\) vanishes in every degree \(k\le t\). This cycle settles the sign issue, proves the implication for every content with at most one entry \(\ge p\), and reduces the rest to contents whose every nonzero entry is \(\ge p\).

General statement. Setting: \(\tilde A=\mathbb F[x_{bj}]/(x_{bj}x_{b'j})\) on \(d\) rows and \(N\) columns, row sums \(r_b=\sum_jx_{bj}\), graded by row content \(c\in\mathbb N^d\). The all-parameter statements are thm:chessboard-link, thm:heavy-core-reduction and thm:one-heavy-row.

  • thm:chessboard-link, over any field. (i) The content-\((1^k)\) strand of the Koszul complex of the row sums on \(\tilde A\) is, after a sign twist, the augmented cochain complex of the \(k\times N\) chessboard complex \(\Delta_{k,N}\), so \(H_i(r;\tilde A)_{(1^k)}\cong\widetilde H^{k-i-1}(\Delta_{k,N};\mathbb F)\). (ii) For every content \(c\) with \(\prod_bc_b!\ne0\) in \(\mathbb F\) (the light contents), \(H_i(r;\tilde A)_c\) is a retract of the multilinear strand on \(|c|\) rows. (iii) Hence \(H_i(r;\tilde A)_c=0\) for all \(i\ge1\) and all light \(c\) with \(N\ge2|c|-1\).
  • thm:heavy-core-reduction, over \(\mathbb F_3\) with \(T=\mathbb F_3[R]/(R^3)\). For \(N\ge2|c|-1\), \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^T(\mathbb F_3,\tilde A)\) vanishes in content \(c\) if it vanishes in the pure heavy part of \(c\): the entries \(\ge3\), on their own rows, with \(|c|-|c_H|\) fewer columns. The light rows are handled by chessboard homology with coefficients in an FI-module, whose generation and regularity degrees are bounded by Church and Ellenberg.
  • thm:one-heavy-row, over \(\mathbb F_3\). \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^T(\mathbb F_3,\tilde A)_c=0\) for every content \(c\) with at most one entry \(\ge3\) and \(N\ge2|c|-1\). Every content of total at most 5 has at most one entry \(\ge3\). So conj:column-tensor-power-freeness holds for every \(t\le5\) and every \(d\), and by prop:stability-from-tensor-power the \(p=3\) case of conj:weak-base-stability holds for \(D\le5\), \(N\ge2D-1\). The first content the theorem does not cover is \((3,3)\), in degree 6.

One result is imported. The FI-module regularity theorem of Church and Ellenberg is used in the form of the regularity theorem and its kernel-generation corollary in Homology of FI-modules (Geom. Topol. 21 (2017)), whose statements were read for this cycle. The chessboard connectivity bound is the record's star-cover proof, ported to any field in (iii). Part (i) contains lem:zero-marginal-chessboard-cycles as its top degree: at \(i=0\), dualized, it identifies the zero-marginal arrays on a fixed set of \(k\) rows with the top cycles of \(\Delta_{k,N}\). The functions \(Z_{c_H}\) below are the analogue for rows used several times, which that lemma does not treat.

(i) The multilinear strand is the chessboard complex

Take \(d=k\) rows and content \((1^k)\). \(K_i\) has basis \(e_U\otimes x_f\): \(U\subseteq[k]\) with \(|U|=i\), and \(f:[k]\setminus U\to[N]\) injective, \(x_f=\prod_sx_{s,f(s)}\). The differential is \(e_U\otimes x_f\mapsto\sum_l(-1)^{l+1}e_{U\setminus u_l}\otimes\sum_{j\notin\operatorname{im}f}x_{f\cup(u_l\mapsto j)}\), with \(U=\{u_1<\dots<u_i\}\). The partial injections \(f\) are the faces of \(\Delta_{k,N}\). Order a face's rooks by row. The simplicial coboundary gives the added rook \((u,j)\) the sign \((-1)^{\#\{s\in\operatorname{dom}f:s<u\}}\). The Koszul sign is \((-1)^{\#\{u'\in U:u'<u\}}\). The two exponents add up to \(u-1\), since \(U\sqcup\operatorname{dom}f=[k]\). So \(\Phi(e_U\otimes x_f)=\varepsilon(f)\,f^*\) with \(\varepsilon(f)=\prod_{s\in\operatorname{dom}f}(-1)^{s-1}\) is a chain isomorphism \(K_i\to\widetilde C^{k-i-1}(\Delta_{k,N})\), with the empty face in degree \(-1\). This resolves the sign issue of the degree-two entry. Signs are missing only in contents that use a row twice, and those are handled in (ii) without comparing signs.

(ii) Light contents are retracts

Work over an infinite extension \(K\supseteq\mathbb F\), since Koszul homology commutes with field extension. Write \(\tilde A(W)=\bigotimes_{j=1}^N(K\oplus W)\), each factor with \(W^2=0\), and \(\ell(w)=\sum_jw^{(j)}\). A linear map \(g:W\to W'\) induces an algebra map \(\tilde A(g)\) with \(\ell(gw)=\tilde A(g)\ell(w)\), and \(\Lambda(g)\otimes\tilde A(g)\) is a chain map of Koszul complexes. So \(H_i(W)_k:=H_i(r;\tilde A(W))_k\) is a functor of \(W\) under all linear maps. It is a subquotient of \(\Lambda^iW\otimes\tilde A(W)_{k-i}\), which is homogeneous polynomial of degree \(k\). So a diagonal \(t\) acts on its content-\(c\) part by \(t^c\), for every \(t\in K^d\).

Let \(|c|=k\) and \(W'=K^k\), with slots split into blocks \(B_b\) of sizes \(c_b\). Let \(\varphi:W'\to W\) send \(e_s\mapsto e_b\) for \(s\in B_b\), \(\psi:W\to W'\) send \(e_b\mapsto\sum_{s\in B_b}e_s\), and \(\tau_t=\operatorname{diag}(t)\) on \(W'\). For \(v\in H_i(W)_c\), \(\varphi\tau_t\psi=\operatorname{diag}(\sum_{s\in B_b}t_s)\), so \(\sum_{c'}t^{c'}H(\varphi)\pi_{c'}H(\psi)v=\prod_b(\sum_{s\in B_b}t_s)^{c_b}\,v\), with \(\pi_{c'}\) the projection to content \(c'\). Comparing the coefficients of \(t_1\cdots t_k\) gives \(H(\varphi)\pi_{(1^k)}H(\psi)v=\prod_bc_b!\,v\). So when \(\prod c_b!\ne0\), \(H_i(W)_c\) is a retract of \(H_i(W')_{(1^k)}\). For heavy contents the coefficient vanishes, which is why they need a separate argument.

(iii) Vanishing

By the chessboard bound, \(\Delta_{k,N}\) is \((\nu-2)\)-acyclic with \(\nu=\min\{k,N,\lfloor(k+N+1)/3\rfloor\}\). For \(N\ge2k-1\), \(\nu=k\). Over a field, reduced cohomology then vanishes in degrees \(\le k-2\), which are the degrees \(k-i-1\) with \(i\ge1\). The record proves this bound by the star cover over \(\mathbb F_2\) (homological chessboard bound). The only characteristic-two step is that \(d_h+d_v\) squares to zero in the cover lemma's double complex. Take \(d_h\) to be the alternating Čech differential, \(\sum_m(-1)^m\) times omitting the \(m\)-th cover index. It commutes with \(d_v\), so the total differential \(d_h+(-1)^ad_v\) squares to zero, and the argument is unchanged over any field: horizontal exactness uses the augmented chain complex of a simplex, and the nerve and intersection conditions do not involve coefficients. So the bound used here does not rest on the unverified import. Frobenius classes have content \(\ge pe_b\), so light contents have none, and \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^T=H_1\) there. With \(p=3\), this gives the degree-two proposition as the case \(t=2\).

Heavy-core reduction

Take \(p=3\), and split a content \(c=(c_H,c_L)\) into its heavy rows \(H=\{b:c_b\ge3\}\) and its light rows \(L\), with \(|c_L|=l\) and \(N\ge2|c|-1\). Write \(W_H\), \(W_L\) for the corresponding spans of rows, and \(\tilde A_S(W_H)\) for the weak algebra without row sums on the rows \(H\) and the columns \(S\).

  1. Peeling the heavy rows. \(u(W)=u(W_H)\otimes u(W_L)\), so there is a content-graded spectral sequence \(E^2_{ij}=\operatorname{Tor}_i^{u(W_L)}(\mathbb F,\operatorname{Tor}_j^{u(W_H)}(\mathbb F,\tilde A))\Rightarrow\operatorname{Tor}_{i+j}^{u(W)}(\mathbb F,\tilde A)\). In content \((\cdot,c_L)\), \(\tilde A\) is, as a \(u(W_H)\)-module, \(\bigoplus_{P_L}\tilde A_{[N]\setminus\operatorname{cols}P_L}(W_H)\) over the placements \(P_L\) of \(c_L\). So \(E^2_{0,1}\) in content \(c\) is a quotient of \(\bigoplus_{P_L}\operatorname{Tor}_1^{u(W_H)}(\mathbb F,\tilde A_{[N]\setminus\operatorname{cols}P_L}(W_H))_{c_H}\). This is the pure heavy content \(c_H\) on \(N-l\ge2|c_H|-1\) columns. \(E_{1,0}\) receives and emits no differentials. With no light rows (\(l=0\)), \(E_{1,0}=0\) and the reduction is (H) itself, so assume \(l\ge1\) below, as steps 2 to 4 need. Hence, if the pure heavy content vanishes (hypothesis (H)), then \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^{u(W)}(\mathbb F,\tilde A)_c\cong\operatorname{Tor}_1^{u(W_L)}(\mathbb F,\tilde A/\mathfrak m_H\tilde A)_c\), with \(\mathfrak m_H=(r_b:b\in H)\).
  2. Light rows. The content \(c_L\) is light, so it has no Frobenius classes, and the right side equals \(H_1(r_L;\tilde A/\mathfrak m_H\tilde A)_c\). Over the infinite extension \(K\), this is a functor of \(W_L\) under maps \(\mathrm{id}\oplus g\), which fix the heavy row sums, and it is polynomial of degree \(|c_L|\) in \(W_L\). So the retract of (ii) reduces it to \(c_L=(1^l)\). Heavy content \(c_H\) of \(\tilde A/\mathfrak m_H\) over a light placement \(f\) is \(Q_{c_H}([N]\setminus\operatorname{im}f)\). Here \(Q_{c_H}(S)=B_{c_H}(S)/\sum_{b\in H}r_bB_{c_H-e_b}(S)\), and \(B_\gamma(S)\) is spanned by the placements of content \(\gamma\) into \(S\). The light row \(u\) acts by adding a rook at column \(j\) and applying \(\rho_j\), which kills heavy cells in column \(j\). With the sign twist of (i), the strand is the augmented chessboard cochain complex of \(\Delta_{l,N}\) with coefficients \(\mathcal Q(\sigma)=Q_{c_H}([N]\setminus\operatorname{cols}\sigma)\). So the group is \(\widetilde H^{l-2}(\Delta_{l,N};\mathcal Q)\cong\widetilde H_{l-2}(\Delta_{l,N};\mathcal Z)^*\). Here \(\mathcal Z(\sigma)=Z_{c_H}([N]\setminus\operatorname{cols}\sigma)\), and \(Z_{c_H}(S)=Q_{c_H}(S)^*\) is the space of functions on placements of \(c_H\) whose marginals all vanish. The maps are extension by zero, dual to \(\rho_j\).
  3. \(Z_{c_H}\) as an FI-module. Write \(h=|c_H|\). \(Z_{c_H}=\ker\bigl(\partial:B_{c_H}\to\bigoplus_{b\in H}B_{c_H-e_b}\bigr)\), with \(\partial\varphi(P')=\sum_{j\notin\operatorname{cols}P'}\varphi(P'\cup(j,b))\) on placements \(P'\) of content \(c_H-e_b\). This is a map of FI-modules under extension by zero. \(B_\gamma\) is the free FI-module \(M(V)\) with \(V\) the placements on exactly \(|\gamma|\) columns, since each placement has a unique column set. So \(B_\gamma\) is free in Church–Ellenberg's sense (their Section 2.1 and footnote 3) and \(H_0\)-acyclic (their Lemma 2.3). An \(\mathbb F_3\)-valued FI-module is a \(\mathbb Z\)-valued one with the same \(H_0\), and the \(\mathbb F_3\)-free modules \(M(V)\) are free in their sense. So their acyclicity lemma (Lemma 2.3), regularity theorem and kernel-generation corollary apply to FI-homology as stated. The kernel-generation corollary gives that \(Z_{c_H}\) is generated in degree \(\le(h-1)+h+1=2h\). Moreover \(H_i(Z_{c_H})\cong H_{i+2}(Q')\) with \(Q'=\operatorname{coker}\partial\), which is generated in degree \(\le h-1\) and related in degree \(\le h\). The case \(i=0\) uses that \(H_0(B_{c_H})\to H_0(\operatorname{im}\partial)\) is injective: on placements that use all \(h\) columns of a set, removing the cell in column \(j\) determines the placement, because the missing row is forced by the content. The regularity theorem then gives \(\deg H_i(Z_{c_H})\le2h+i\) for all \(i\ge0\).
  4. Resolution. Resolve \(Z_{c_H}\) by free FI-modules \(F_\bullet\), taking \(F_j=M((K_j)_{\le g_j})\) at each stage, with \(K_0=Z_{c_H}\) and \(K_{j+1}=\ker(F_j\to K_j)\). \(F_j\) is not a minimal cover, so \(H_0(F_j)\to H_0(K_j)\) need not be injective. The long exact sequence of \(0\to K_{j+1}\to F_j\to K_j\to0\), with \(F_j\) acyclic, gives \(\deg H_0(K_{j+1})\le\max(g_j,\deg H_1(K_j))\) and \(H_i(K_{j+1})\cong H_{i+1}(K_j)\) for \(i\ge1\). So \(\deg H_1(K_j)=\deg H_{j+1}(Z_{c_H})\le2h+j+1\), and by induction \(g_j=\deg H_0(K_j)\le2h+j\). Chessboard chains are exact in the coefficient module, so \(\widetilde H_{l-2}(\Delta;\mathcal Z)\) is the hyperhomology of the double complex \(\widetilde C_q(\Delta;F_j)\). A free module \(M(V)\) has \(M(V)(S)=\bigoplus_{J\subseteq S}V_J\) with inclusions as maps, so \(\widetilde C_\bullet(\Delta_{l,N};M(V))=\bigoplus_JV_J\otimes\widetilde C_\bullet(\Delta_{l,[N]\setminus J})\). In total degree \(l-2\), with \(q=l-2-j\ge-1\), the boards have \(M=N-|J|\ge2l-1-j\ge l\) columns. There \(\lfloor(l+M+1)/3\rfloor\ge l-\lceil j/3\rceil\ge l-j\), so \(\nu\ge l-j\) and \(\widetilde H_{l-2-j}=0\). Every \(E^1\) entry of total degree \(l-2\) vanishes, so \(\widetilde H_{l-2}(\Delta_{l,N};\mathcal Z)=0\). \(\square\)

So conj:column-tensor-power-freeness reduces to pure heavy contents: those whose every nonzero entry is at least 3, on their own rows. With one heavy row, (H) is the Clebsch–Gordan freeness of \(J_2^{\otimes n}\) through \(\lceil n/2\rceil\) (prop:line-necessity), with \(n=N-l\ge2h-1\). With no heavy row, the reduction is (iii). This proves thm:one-heavy-row. For \(l=1\), step 4 is simply this: \(Z_{c_H}(N)\) is spanned by functions with vanishing marginals that avoid some column, which holds once \(N\ge2h+1\). The threshold \(N\ge2|c|-1\) enters twice, as \(N-l\ge2h-1\) in (H) and as \(N-2h\ge2l-1\) on the boards. Both are exactly the conjectured threshold.

Checks

  • chessboard_link.py (check.json) computes, exactly over \(\mathbb F_3\), all Koszul homology of the row sums in content \((1^k)\) for \(k\le4\), \(k\le N\le7\). It compares them with the reduced homology of \(\Delta_{k,N}\), computed separately with simplicial signs. All 22 pairs agree in every degree, including the nonzero cases below the threshold: \((k,N)=(2,2),(3,3),(3,4),(4,4),(4,5),(4,6)\), with \(H_1\) of dimension 1, 4, 2, 15, 20, 5. \(\Delta_{3,4}\) is the torus. For the light contents \((2),(2,1),(2,2),(2,1,1)\), \(H_{\ge1}\) vanishes at \(N\ge2|c|-1\) and is bounded by the multilinear value below it. There were no failures.
  • n9.json reruns tensor_power.py at \((N,d)=(9,2)\). Freeness holds through exactly 5, as the theorem and prop:line-necessity predict, with \(\mathrm{HF}=217\) against a predicted 135 in degree 6. That covers the mixed heavy contents \((4,1)\) and \((3,2)\).

What remains

  • Pure heavy contents with two or more rows. The first is \((3,3)\), which needs \(N\ge11\). No light row is left to carry the chessboard argument, and the retract of (ii) is not available. One possible route peels one heavy row by Clebsch–Gordan, as in the one-heavy-row case. Then \(\tilde A/r_1\) over the other heavy rows is needed, as a module whose freeness is what (H) asks for.
  • For the goal, stability is needed at logarithmic \(D\), so heavy contents with many heavy rows matter. The case \(D\le5\) proved here is a check of the mechanism, not a use.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the degree-two entry and prop:tensor-power-degree-two; prop:stability-from-tensor-power (Tor as Koszul \(H_1\) modulo Frobenius classes); prop:line-necessity (the Clebsch–Gordan freeness of \(J_2^{\otimes n}\)); lem:zero-marginal-chessboard-cycles and the record's star-cover proof; Church–Ellenberg, the regularity theorem, the kernel-generation corollary, Lemma 2.3, Definition 2.1 and footnote 3, from the arXiv version. The claim searches for chessboard, Koszul and polarization found no earlier result on this module. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed (i) with its sign twist and degrees, the retract and its coefficient, step 1 and the stability of \(E_{1,0}\), the duality in step 2, the freeness of the \(B_\gamma\), the injectivity behind \(H_i(Z)\cong H_{i+2}(Q')\), the arithmetic of step 4 including \(q=-1\), and the count behind the corollary. Its own scripts recomputed the six nonzero chessboard values over \(\mathbb F_3\). They also found \(H_0(Z_h)\ne0\) in degree exactly \(2h\) for \(h=2,3\), so the generation bound is attained. It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the alternating Čech differential stated in the port of the star cover;
  • in step 2, the identification with Koszul \(H_1\) placed before the retract;
  • a sentence on FI-modules over \(\mathbb F_3\) in Church–Ellenberg's setting;
  • the induction for \(g_j\) written out, since the cover is not minimal;
  • the case \(l=0\) stated;
  • the import statement made consistent, the status line shortened, and the relation to lem:zero-marginal-chessboard-cycles stated.

Tensor-power freeness: peeling one row at a time proves the column tensor power conjecture at p = 3, and with it linear base stability

24 September 2026 · Working proof (tensor-power freeness), with an imported FI-module bound · Settles conj:column-tensor-power-freeness; cycle odd-prime-pure-heavy. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The chessboard-link entry reduced conj:column-tensor-power-freeness to its pure heavy contents, those with every nonzero entry at least 3, and proved the case of one heavy row. The first open content was \((3,3)\) at \(N\ge11\). The missing implication is \(\operatorname{Tor}_1\) vanishing for contents with several heavy rows.

General statement. thm:tensor-power-freeness: over \(\mathbb F_3\), let \(\tilde A=\mathbb F_3[x_{bj}]/(x_{bj}x_{b'j})\) on \(d\) rows and \(N\) columns be a module over \(u(W)=\mathbb F_3[R_1,\dots,R_d]/(R_b^3)\) through its row sums, graded by row content \(c\). For every \(d\), every content \(c\), and every \(i\ge1\), \(\operatorname{Tor}_i^{u(W)}(\mathbb F_3,\tilde A)_c=0\) whenever \(N\ge2|c|-i\). At \(i=1\), \(\tilde A\) is cover-free through \(t\) whenever \(N\ge2t-1\). With prop:line-necessity, this proves conj:column-tensor-power-freeness: cover-free through \(t\) if and only if \(N\ge2t-1\), for every \(d\). It has three consequences:

  • By prop:stability-from-tensor-power, the \(p=3\) case of conj:weak-base-stability holds. The homogenized weak unary base on \(m\ge D\) rows and \(N\ge2D-1\) columns has no falls below \(D\), that is, it is \(z\)-injective below \(D\).
  • By prop:generic-forms-as-row-sums, the weak algebra without row sums is free through \(t\) over any \(d\le m\) forms with injective column maps if and only if \(N\ge2t-1\). A summand on \(N-s\) columns, shifted by \(s\), needs \(N-s\ge2(t-s)-1\), which \(N\ge2t-1\) implies. The summand \(s=0\) gives the "only if".
  • It supersedes thm:one-heavy-row, and makes the hypothesis of thm:heavy-core-reduction, which is an implication, always true.

The previous cycle's attempt stalled because it used \(\operatorname{Tor}_1\) alone. The whole family of higher Tor groups is what makes the induction close.

Proof

Induction on the number \(m\) of rows in the support of \(c\), for all \(d\), \(N\), \(i\ge1\) at once. If \(m=0\), \(\operatorname{Tor}_i(\mathbb F,\tilde A)_0=\operatorname{Tor}_i(\mathbb F,\mathbb F)_0=0\). Otherwise let row 1 have \(h=c_1\ge1\), write \(c=(h,c')\), and let \(W'\) be the span of the other rows, so \(u(W)=u(r_1)\otimes u(W')\). Two degree facts are used throughout:

  • (D) The minimal resolution of \(\mathbb F\) over \(u(W')\) has its \(a\)-th generators in contents \(e\) with \(|e|\ge a\). So \(\operatorname{Tor}_a^{u(W')}(\mathbb F,X)_{c'}\) is a subquotient of \(\bigoplus_{|e|\ge a}X_{c'-e}\). It vanishes when \(X\) vanishes in all contents \(c''\le c'\) with \(|c''|\le|c'|-a\), and in particular when \(a>|c'|\) and \(X\) is in nonnegative contents.
  • (CG) By the graded Clebsch–Gordan rule of prop:line-necessity, \(J_2^{\otimes n}\) over \(\mathbb F_3[r]/(r^3)\) is free plus \(J_1(-n/2)\) for even \(n\), or free plus \(J_2(-(n-1)/2)\) for odd \(n\). The minimal resolutions of \(J_1\) and \(J_2\) have generators in degrees \(\lfloor3b/2\rfloor\) and \(\lceil3b/2\rceil\). So \(\operatorname{Tor}_b(J_2^{\otimes n})\) sits in the single degree \(n/2+\lfloor3b/2\rfloor\) or \((n-1)/2+\lceil3b/2\rceil\), which is at least \(h+b-\tfrac12\) once \(n\ge2h-b\). Hence \(\operatorname{Tor}_b(J_2^{\otimes n})_h=0\) for \(b\ge1\) and \(n\ge2h-b\).

The content-graded spectral sequence \(E^2_{a,b}=\operatorname{Tor}_a^{u(W')}(\mathbb F,\operatorname{Tor}_b^{u(r_1)}(\mathbb F,\tilde A))\Rightarrow\operatorname{Tor}_{a+b}^{u(W)}(\mathbb F,\tilde A)\) shows that \(\operatorname{Tor}_i\) vanishes in content \(c\) once every \(E^2_{a,b}\) with \(a+b=i\) does.

  1. Terms with \(b\ge1\). In content \((\cdot,c'')\), \(\tilde A\) is \(\bigoplus_{P''}J_2^{\otimes([N]\setminus\operatorname{cols}P'')}\) as a \(u(r_1)\)-module, over the placements \(P''\) of \(c''\). By (D) only \(|c''|\le|c'|-a\) matters, where \(n=N-|c''|\ge N-|c'|+a\ge2h+|c'|-i+a=2h+|c'|-b\ge2h-b\). By (CG), \(E^2_{a,b}=0\) in content \(c\).
  2. The term \(b=0\). \(E^2_{i,0}=\operatorname{Tor}_i^{u(W')}(\mathbb F,Y)_{c'}\) with \(Y=(\tilde A/r_1\tilde A)_{(h,\cdot)}\). As in the chessboard-link entry, \(Y=\bigoplus_{P'}Q_h([N]\setminus\operatorname{cols}P')\), with \(Q_h(S)=B_h(S)/rB_{h-1}(S)\). The row sum \(r_b\), for \(b\ge2\), adds a row-\(b\) cell at a free column \(j\) and applies the restriction \(\rho_j\). Call this construction \(\mathfrak B(Q)\) for any presheaf \(Q\) on the subsets of \([N]\), that is, with commuting restrictions \(\rho_j\rho_{j'}=\rho_{j'}\rho_j\). Commuting restrictions make the \(r_b\) commute. \(r_b^3=0\), because each unordered triple of columns occurs \(3!\equiv0\) times. So \(\mathfrak B(Q)\) is a \(u(W')\)-module, and \(\mathfrak B\) is exact in \(Q\). \(Q_h\) is such a presheaf, since \(\rho_j\) preserves \(rB_{h-1}\). For the dual of a free FI-module, \(Q=M(V)^*\) with \(Q(S)=\bigoplus_{K\subseteq S}V_K^*\) and \(\rho_j\) the projection onto the summands with \(j\notin K\). Then \(\mathfrak B(M(V)^*)=\bigoplus_KV_K^*\otimes\tilde A_{[N]\setminus K}(W')\), a sum of weak algebras on the other rows and \(N-|K|\) columns.
  3. A coresolution. \(Q_h=Z_h^*\) with \(Z_h=\ker(\partial:B_h\to B_{h-1})\). The FI-module steps of the chessboard-link entry never use heaviness, so they apply to \(Z_h\) for every \(h\ge1\). They consist of the kernel-generation corollary with generation degrees \(h-1\) and \(h\), the bound \(\deg H_1(Q')\le h\) because the image of \(\partial\) is a quotient of \(B_h\), the regularity theorem applied to \(Q'\), and the induction for a non-minimal cover. So \(Z_h\) has a resolution \(F_\bullet\to Z_h\) by free FI-modules \(F_s=M(V_s)\), with \(V_s\) in degrees \(\le2h+s\). The \(\rho_j\) on \(Q_h\) are dual to extension by zero on \(Z_h\), so the dualized resolution consists of maps of presheaves. Dualizing at each subset of \([N]\) and applying \(\mathfrak B\) gives an exact sequence \(0\to Y\to X^0\to X^1\to\cdots\) with \(X^s=\bigoplus_{|K|\le2h+s}V_{s,K}^*\otimes\tilde A_{[N]\setminus K}(W')\).
  4. Dimension shifting. With \(Y^0=Y\) and \(0\to Y^s\to X^s\to Y^{s+1}\to0\), the long exact sequences give \(\operatorname{Tor}_{k+1}(Y^{s+1})\to\operatorname{Tor}_k(Y^s)\to\operatorname{Tor}_k(X^s)\). So \(\operatorname{Tor}_i(Y)_{c'}=0\) if \(\operatorname{Tor}_{i+s}^{u(W')}(\mathbb F,X^s)_{c'}=0\) for all \(s\ge0\). The chain stops once \(i+s>|c'|\), by (D). Each summand of \(X^s\) is a weak algebra on \(m-1\) support rows and \(n=N-|K|\ge N-2h-s\ge2|c'|-(i+s)\) columns. The induction hypothesis at index \(i+s\) makes its \(\operatorname{Tor}_{i+s}\) vanish in content \(c'\). \(\square\)

The chessboard-link entry's route by chessboard homology is not needed here. In content \((1^k)\), \(\operatorname{Tor}_i^{u(W)}\) equals Koszul \(H_i\), because the resolution generators of row-degree \(\ge2\) do not occur in contents \(\le(1^k)\). So, through the chessboard-link entry's part (i), the multilinear case gives \(\widetilde H^{k-i-1}(\Delta_{k,N};\mathbb F_3)=0\) for \(N\ge2k-i\), consistent with the chessboard bound.

Check

tor_contents.py (tor.json) computes \(\dim\operatorname{Tor}_i^{u(W)}(\mathbb F_3,\tilde A)_c\) directly for \(i\le3\). It uses the complex of the tensor product of periodic resolutions, with exact ranks from the new OpenMP kernel research/tools/rank_modp.cpp, which matched the Python reference on 40 random matrices.

  • Validation. All 111 rows agree:
    • for \(d=1\), \(N\le7\), \(i\le3\), the exact Clebsch–Gordan prediction, including its 11 nonzero values;
    • for content \((1,1,1)\), the chessboard values of the chessboard-link check.
  • Test. Contents \((3,1)\), \((3,2)\), \((4,1)\), \((3,1,1)\) and \((3,3)\) near their thresholds, the last for \(7\le N\le11\): 75 values in all, 33 of them claimed zero. All 33 are zero, including \((3,3)\) at \(N=11\) for \(i=1,2,3\).
  • Sharpness at \(i=1\). In each of these contents \(\dim\operatorname{Tor}_1=1\) at \(N=2|c|-2\). For \(i\ge2\) the bound \(N\ge2|c|-i\) is not sharp in these data: the values are already zero one column lower.

What this means for the route

  • Base stability (a) is linear at \(p=3\): no falls below \(D\) when \(N\ge2D-1\), against the quadratic range \(N\ge2D^2\) of thm:weak-base-stability-quadratic. The goal's logarithmic degree was already inside the quadratic range, so for (a) the gain is the constant, not a new case.
  • Freeness over up to \(m\) generic forms holds at the same threshold.
  • Not covered:
    • odd primes \(p\ge5\), where (CG) and the resolution degrees change;
    • more forms than rows, \(d>m\);
    • row sums together with further forms;
    • the ENS blocks and adversarial forms named in the tensor-power review.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: the chessboard-link entry (the FI-module steps and the coresolution data), prop:line-necessity (the graded Clebsch–Gordan rule), prop:stability-from-tensor-power, prop:generic-forms-as-row-sums, conj:weak-base-stability (stated over \(\mathbb F_p\), so only its \(p=3\) case follows), and Church–Ellenberg's statements as recorded there. Claim searches for FI-module regularity and for higher Tor of the row sums found only this line's own entries. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed:

  • (CG), including \(n=0\), and the arithmetic of the \(b\ge1\) terms;
  • the decomposition of \(\mathfrak B(M(V)^*)\) and the exactness of the coresolution;
  • the degree bound on \(V_s\), the direction and termination of the dimension shifting, and the column bound;
  • the base case and the induction on support size.

Its own independent code reproduced recorded values. It found zero at 11 further points at or above the threshold, among them \((3,2,1)\) at \(N=11\), \(i=1\), and \((3,3,3)\) at \(N=12\), \(i=6\). It also found \(\dim\operatorname{Tor}_1=1\) for \((3,2,1)\) at \(N=10\). Those values are from its report, not from a result file. It found no gap in the argument, and required these changes, all adopted:

  • (D) restated as a vanishing criterion;
  • the presheaf condition and the module check for \(\mathfrak B\);
  • the FI-module steps stated for every \(h\ge1\);
  • the Koszul identification in multilinear contents;
  • the wording of the consequences, the summands of the generic-forms corollary, and the "no falls" wording of the stability corollary.

The changes restate or justify without adding claims, so no further pass was made.

Generic forms: grouped row sums show that the top algebra is free over m(⌊N/(2t−1)⌋−1) generic forms, so the one-count link's freeness hypothesis holds on a nonempty open set of inventories

24 September 2026 · Working proof (row-sum absorption; general-forms freeness) · Generic forms, p = 3; cycle odd-prime-kernel-forms. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The tensor-power freeness entry covers up to \(m\) forms with injective column maps. prop:one-count-by-freeness needs the weak top algebra to be free through \(D\) over about \(nh\) forms, together with the row sums. So the forms outnumber the rows, and their column maps have kernels. The proposed next step was a threshold for \(d>m\) forms. The record already treats the naive version. The criterion "every direction meets at least \(2t-1\) columns" is necessary, by the restriction lemma of prop:line-necessity. It is not sufficient in special position: ex:pencil-worst-direction finds exceptions for two forms in the column model, and ex:truncated-dade-special-position finds one for a general column tensor. So this cycle asks what holds for forms in general position, and how many there can be.

General statement. Over \(\mathbb F_3\), let \(\tilde A\) be the weak algebra without row sums on \(m\) rows and \(N\) columns, \(R\) the span of its row sums, and \(A=\tilde A/R\tilde A\) the weak top algebra. Let \(g=\lfloor N/(2t-1)\rfloor\). The all-parameter statements are lem:row-sum-absorption and thm:general-forms-freeness.

  • lem:row-sum-absorption. Let \(N\ge2t-1\), and let \(G\) be linear forms independent modulo \(R\). Then \(\operatorname{Tor}_i^{u(R\oplus G)}(\mathbb F,\tilde A)\cong\operatorname{Tor}_i^{u(G)}(\mathbb F,A)\) in degrees \(\le t\), for all \(i\). So \(\tilde A\) is free through \(t\) over the row sums together with \(G\) exactly when \(A\) is free through \(t\) over \(G\).
  • thm:general-forms-freeness. Let \(g\ge1\). For every \(d\le mg\), the \(d\)-tuples of forms over which \(\tilde A\) is free through \(t\) form a nonempty Zariski-open set of the space of \(d\)-tuples over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\). The set is defined over \(\mathbb F_3\) and has \(\mathbb F_3\)-rational points, among them the grouped row sums. For every \(e\le m(g-1)\), the same holds for the \(e\)-tuples \(G\) over which \(A\) is free through \(t\). That condition depends only on the classes of \(G\) modulo \(R\), and it forces those classes to be independent. So freeness holds for generic forms over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\).

For prop:one-count-by-freeness, take the stability range \(m\ge D\), \(N\ge2D-1\), where thm:tensor-power-freeness gives base stability at \(p=3\). Its freeness hypothesis is then satisfied by a nonempty Zariski-open set of inventories, generic over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\) and with \(\mathbb F_3\)-rational members, whenever \(1\le nh\le m(\lfloor N/(2D-1)\rfloor-1)\). The lower bound on \(nh\) forces \(g\ge2\), so \(N\ge2D-1\) holds automatically, but \(m\ge D\) is an assumption. The same open set also gives the independence of the \(nh\) forms. It does not say that a given \(\mathbb F_3\)-rational inventory lies in it. Remark: with \(m=N+1\) and \(N\ge2(2D-1)\), the count is of order \(N^2/(2D-1)\), against about \(N/(2(D+1))\) for the seed methods.

Row-sum absorption

Proof. \(u(R\oplus G)=u(R)\otimes u(G)\), so there is a spectral sequence \(E^2_{a,b}=\operatorname{Tor}_a^{u(G)}(\mathbb F,\operatorname{Tor}_b^{u(R)}(\mathbb F,\tilde A))\Rightarrow\operatorname{Tor}_{a+b}^{u(R\oplus G)}(\mathbb F,\tilde A)\). By thm:tensor-power-freeness, \(\operatorname{Tor}_b^{u(R)}(\mathbb F,\tilde A)\) vanishes in every degree \(k\) with \(N\ge2k-b\). That includes every \(k\le t\) when \(b\ge1\), since \(N\ge2t-1\). \(\operatorname{Tor}_a^{u(G)}(\mathbb F,X)\) in degree \(k\) is a subquotient of \(X\) in degrees \(\le k-a\). So in degrees \(\le t\) only the row \(b=0\) survives, where \(E^2_{a,0}=\operatorname{Tor}_a^{u(G)}(\mathbb F,A)\). No differential reaches or leaves it in those degrees. \(\square\)

General-forms freeness

  1. Grouped row sums. Split \([N]\) into \(g\) groups of at least \(2t-1\) columns. Let \(W_{\mathrm{grp}}\) be spanned by the \(mg\) forms \(\ell_{b,G}=\sum_{j\in G}x_{bj}\). Then \(\tilde A=\bigotimes_G\tilde A(G)\) and \(u(W_{\mathrm{grp}})=\bigotimes_Gu(W_G)\), with each factor acting on its own group. By the Künneth formula over a field, \(\operatorname{Tor}_1\) of the product is \(\bigoplus_G\operatorname{Tor}_1(\tilde A(G))\otimes\bigotimes_{G'\ne G}\operatorname{Tor}_0(\tilde A(G'))\). The \(\operatorname{Tor}_0\) factors start in degree 0. So the product is free through \(t\) if and only if each factor is, which thm:tensor-power-freeness gives for \(|G|\ge2t-1\).
  2. Sub-spans. \(u(W)\) is free over \(u(W_0)\) for \(W_0\subseteq W\). So freeness through \(t\) over \(u(W)\) restricts to \(u(W_0)\), by the argument of the restriction lemma of prop:line-necessity, with \(W_0\) in place of a line. Hence \(\tilde A\) is free through \(t\) over every sub-span of \(W_{\mathrm{grp}}\), of any dimension \(d\le mg\).
  3. Top algebra. \(R\subseteq W_{\mathrm{grp}}\), since \(r_b=\sum_G\ell_{b,G}\). Take a complement \(G_0\) of \(R\) in \(W_{\mathrm{grp}}\), of dimension \(m(g-1)\), and any \(G_1\subseteq G_0\). \(\tilde A\) is free over \(R\oplus G_1\) by step 2, so \(A\) is free over \(G_1\) by lem:row-sum-absorption.
  4. Openness. Fix the number of forms. By the openness lemma of thm:projection-freeness, freeness through \(t\) is the equality \(\mathrm{HF}(M/(\text{forms})M)_k=\mathrm{pred}_k:=[q^k]\,\mathrm{HS}_M/(1+q+q^2)^{\#\text{forms}}\) for \(k\le t\). It is also the inequality \(\le\). The minimal cover is onto, with kernel \(K\), so \(\mathrm{HF}(M/(\text{forms})M)_k=\mathrm{pred}_k+[q^k]\,\mathrm{HS}_K/\mathrm{HS}_T\). At the lowest degree \(s\) of \(K\) this exceeds \(\mathrm{pred}_s\) by \(\dim K_s>0\), so "\(\le\) through \(t\)" already forces \(K\) to start above \(t\). The Hilbert function of the quotient is upper semicontinuous in the forms' coefficients, because it is a corank of a matrix linear in them. So the tuples satisfying it form a Zariski-open set defined over \(\mathbb F_3\), and steps 2 and 3 show it is nonempty. For \(A\), the tuples are \(e\)-tuples \(G\) with \(\tilde A\) free over \(R\oplus G\). A tuple dependent modulo \(R\) fails already in degree 1, so the open set consists of independent tuples, where absorption applies. \(\square\)

Limits. The line argument of prop:line-necessity gives a necessary condition, stated here as an observation. Each kernel of a column map has codimension \(\le m\). So for every tuple, and exactly for general ones, some direction lies in the kernels of \(s\) column maps once \(d-sm\ge1\). Restricted to that direction, \(\tilde A\) has only \(N-s\) columns of type \(J_2\). So freeness through \(t\) needs \(N-\lfloor(d-1)/m\rfloor\ge2t-1\), that is, roughly \(d\le m(N-2t+2)\). The theorem's count is smaller by a factor of about \(2t-1\). Positivity of the prediction gives a second bound, and the two bounds are compared in the check below. The theorem reaches \(m\lfloor N/(2t-1)\rfloor\). How close that is to the positivity bound for large \(N\) is not established here. General position is a statement over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\). The inventory's forms are \(\mathbb F_3\)-rational, and uniformly random \(\mathbb F_3\) forms are not known to avoid the closed set.

Check

forms_freeness.py (forms.json) computes \(\mathrm{HF}(\tilde A/(\text{forms}))\) exactly over \(\mathbb F_3\) with the rank kernel research/tools/rank_modp.cpp.

  • Grouped row sums: 7 configurations, \((m,N,t)\in\{(1,6,2),(2,6,2),(3,6,2),(1,10,3),(2,10,3),(1,9,2),(2,9,2)\}\) with \(d=mg\). All are free through \(t\), with the Hilbert function equal to the prediction.
  • Seeded random \(\mathbb F_3\) forms on \(\tilde A\), for the \(d\le mg\) statement, with one draw per \(d\), for comparison. The largest free \(d\) found was 6, 9, 11, 5, 2 and 8, against theorem values 4, 6, 6, 2, 2, 4 and positivity bounds 6, 10, 11, 7, 4, 8, at \((m,N,t)=(2,6,2),(3,6,2),(2,9,2),(2,9,3),(1,10,3),(2,10,3)\). Random forms usually go beyond the theorem, reaching the positivity bound in 3 of 6 cases. This is consistent with conj:maximal-generic-freeness but does not test it, since one draw per \(d\) is not a Zariski-general point.

What remains for the one-count problem

  • Generic forms over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\) versus random \(\mathbb F_3\)-rational forms. A probabilistic version for random \(\mathbb F_3\) inventories is needed, or a structural reason why the inventory's forms avoid the closed set.
  • The ENS blocks of the compiler as members in their input forms, which is still unverified.
  • Adversarial inventories, which are not in general position.

Verification gate

Verification gate. Re-read: prop:one-count-by-freeness and its entry (the weak top algebra and the freeness hypothesis over the joint span), thm:tensor-power-freeness, prop:line-necessity (its restriction lemma), the openness lemma of thm:projection-freeness, conj:maximal-generic-freeness, ex:pencil-worst-direction, ex:truncated-dade-special-position and ex:worst-direction-tests. The claim searches for code distance, worst direction and Dade found those records. They show that the distance criterion is not sufficient in special position, so this entry claims only a nonempty open set. The weak top algebra is \(\tilde A/(r_1,\dots,r_m)\), as defined in the weak-base stability entry. A fresh-context reviewer confirmed:

  • the absorption, including the translation from content to total degree and the vanishing differentials;
  • the Künneth "iff", with a larger last group allowed;
  • the restriction to sub-spans;
  • the direction of semicontinuity, and the degree-1 failure of dependent tuples;
  • the table values.

It required these changes, all adopted:

  • the step from equality to the open inequality;
  • the theorem restated as a nonempty open set rather than a count for "general position", with the title matched;
  • the stability-range hypothesis and the independence stated for the one-count link;
  • the order-\(N^2\) count made a remark with its conditions;
  • "matching" dropped from the limits, with the necessary condition stated for every tuple;
  • the attributions in the question corrected, and the random comparison said to concern \(\tilde A\).

The changes weaken or justify, so no further pass was made.

Route review: the freeness side of the one-count link is settled for generic forms; the open core is whether an ENS block's degree-D shadow is a member

24 September 2026 · Route review · The (b), (c) and one-count line after the tensor-power review; cycle odd-prime-freeness-route-review. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. Five research entries have followed the tensor-power review, and two conjectures were settled at \(p=3\). This review states the line's claim and what the goal needs, tries to falsify the newest result, assesses the line, and names the highest-risk item.

General statement. The line's general claim is that the one-count problem of the restriction-mixture line has a degree-\(D\) PC design, for the weak base plus \(n\) random blocks with \(h\) input forms each. prop:one-count-by-freeness reduces this to three hypotheses: stability of the base, blocks that are satisfiable members in their input forms, and freeness of the weak top algebra over the joint span of the \(nh\) forms. The freeness hypothesis now holds on a nonempty open set of inventories, and base stability now holds at the linear threshold. The member hypothesis is untouched.

What happened since the last review

  • Stability from tensor powers: cover-freeness of the column tensor power through \(D\) is what the base's stability proof uses (stability link).
  • The tensor-power conjecture was proved in three steps.
    • Degree 2 (degree two).
    • Contents with every entry below \(p\), through the chessboard complex, and every content with at most one heavy row (chessboard link).
    • All contents, by peeling rows with an FI-module coresolution (tensor-power freeness). With it, \(p=3\) base stability holds at \(N\ge2D-1\).
  • The row sums absorb into the top algebra. Grouped row sums give freeness through \(t\) on a nonempty open set of up to \(m(\lfloor N/(2t-1)\rfloor-1)\) forms (generic forms). With \(m=N+1\) and \(D=11\), that is about \(N^2/21\) forms. The one-count problem needs about \(N^2/(4.4\times10^7)\), under the one-count entry's assumptions \(n\approx N\) and \(L\) of order \(N\). So the count is no longer the obstruction.

What the goal needs from this line

  1. Blocks as members. The compiler's blocks are ENS blocks. Their companions \(g_iP\), with \(P=\prod_\ell(1-\sum_ir_{i\ell}g_i)\), use fresh coefficient variables with field equations. Semantically such a block constrains its inputs not at all: if some \(g_i(x)\ne0\), a choice of \(r\) makes \(P=0\). What it contributes is proof power: its degree-\(D\) shadow, the polynomials in \(x\) that PC derives with it at degree \(D\) beyond the base. prop:one-count-by-freeness needs each shadow to be a satisfiable member in the block's input forms, and the shadows of \(n\) blocks to act as the union of these members. The record refutes fresh-block conservativity in every exact form (refutation, completeness). So shadows are nontrivial, and any statement about them must use the number of blocks, since exponentially many blocks refute PHP.
  2. Rational forms. The freeness result covers a nonempty open set. The inventory's forms are fixed \(\mathbb F_3\) forms from random blocks.
  3. The rest of the reduction. The top-size lemma's typicality, and the assumptions \(n\approx N\) and \(L\) of order \(N\). Also \(p\ge5\), where the Clebsch–Gordan input changes.

Falsification attempt

thm:general-forms-freeness is weakest where it meets the actual inventory, which consists of \(\mathbb F_3\)-rational forms rather than generic ones. random_within_count.py (random_within_count.json) drew uniformly random \(\mathbb F_3\) tuples \(G\) at the theorem's largest count \(e=m(\lfloor N/(2t-1)\rfloor-1)\). It tested the top algebra's freeness through \(t\), that is, \(\tilde A\) over the row sums plus \(G\).

  • Sizes: \((m,N,t,e)=(3,6,2,3),(4,6,2,4),(2,9,2,4),(3,9,2,6),(2,10,3,2),(3,10,3,3)\), with 40, 40, 40, 30, 30 and 20 draws.
  • Free: 198 of 200. The 2 failures, both at \((3,6,2,3)\), are exactly the draws where some rational direction meets fewer than \(2t-1\) columns. prop:line-necessity forces non-freeness there.
  • No draw satisfied that line condition and still failed.

So, at these sizes, the rational gap is the line condition and nothing more. The line condition asks that no nonzero \(\gamma\in G\) has \(N-2t+2\) or more of its column vectors equal to one \(r\in\mathbb F_3^m\). For random forms it fails with probability at most \(3^{m+e}\Pr[\mathrm{Bin}(N,3^{-m})\ge N-2t+2]\), which vanishes as \(N\) grows. The test did not falsify the line. It does not reach the special-position failures of ex:truncated-dade-special-position or ex:pencil-worst-direction, which lie outside the count.

Assessment of this line

The algebraic side of the line is in good shape at \(p=3\), and the evidence for that is proofs, not data. Base stability is linear. The column tensor powers are free at the sharp threshold with all higher Tor. The row sums absorb. Freeness over order \(N^2/D\) generic forms holds on a nonempty open set, and at small sizes random \(\mathbb F_3\) forms fail only through the line condition. What these results do not touch is item 1, the question the line depends on. There the record's evidence points the other way: conservativity fails in exact forms, and the loss comes from PC reuse (NS test). The freeness results make the rest of the chain ready to use once members are available. They give no evidence that members are available. Item 1 is therefore the highest-risk item, and the line should not produce further freeness refinements until it is tested.

Next step

On odd-prime-clause-transfer: the shadow of one ENS block. Take the weak base on a small board plus one complete accuracy-one ENS block with random input forms. Compute, with the exact \(\mathbb F_3\) PC-closure tester, its degree-\(D\) shadow in \(x\) beyond the base's own degree-\(D\) closure. Decide whether the shadow is generated by polynomials in the block's input forms, that is, whether it is a member. Then do the same for two blocks on independent inputs, and ask whether the joint shadow is the sum of the single shadows. Reuse is exactly the failure of that additivity. A statement that survives must depend on the number of blocks, since exponentially many blocks refute PHP. Use the recorded conservativity refutations as controls.
